title: Hadith on Worship: Remembrance after Fajr fully rewarded like a Hajj pilgrim
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever performs the dawn prayer in congregation, then remains seated remembering Allah until the sun rises, and then prays two units of prayer, they will receive a reward like that of a Hajj and an ‘Umrah pilgrimage.” The Prophet said, “Complete, complete, complete!”
q: Whoever performs the dawn prayer in congregation, then remains seated remembering Allah until the sun rises, and then prays two units of prayer, they will receive a reward like that of a Hajj and an ‘Umrah pilgrimage … Complete, complete, complete!

title: Ibn Abbas on Barsisa: Shaytan misleads pious monk into adultery, murder, and idolatry
t: ‘Atiyyah ibn Sa’d reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, stated in regards to His words, “They are like Satan when he lures someone to disbelieve. Then after they have done so, he will say, I have absolutely nothing to do with you. I truly fear Allah—the Lord of all worlds!’ So they will both end up in the Fire, staying there forever. That is the reward of the wrongdoers,” (59:16-17) saying, “There was a monk among the Israelites who worshiped Allah and excelled in his worship. People would come to him from every land to ask him questions about religious knowledge, for he was a learned man. Three brothers had a beautiful sister, one of the most beautiful among the people. They wished to travel, but it weighed heavily upon them to leave her without protection. They went to the monk and said, ‘We intend to travel, and we know no one whom we trust more, nor anyone who seems safer to us than you. If you agree, we would like to leave our sister with you. She is severely ill. If she dies, then take care of her affairs, and if she lives, then look after her until we return’ He said, ‘I will take care of her for you, Allah willing.’ So he cared for her and treated her until she recovered and her beauty returned. One day he looked upon her and found her adorned. Satan continued tempting him until he slept with her, and she became pregnant. Then Satan filled him with remorse and made it seem good to him that he should kill her. When her brothers returned, they asked him, ‘What happened?’ He said, ‘She died, and I buried her.’ They said, ‘You did the right thing.’ Then they began seeing dreams and being informed that the monk had killed her and that she was buried beneath a certain tree. They went to the tree and found that she had indeed been murdered, so they seized the monk. Then Satan came to him and said, ‘I am the one who made adultery seem attractive to you, and I am the one who made killing her seem good. Will you give me what I ask, and I will save you?’ He said yes. Satan said, ‘Prostrate to me once.’ So he prostrated to him, but then he was executed anyway. Such is the word of Allah, ‘They are like Satan when he lures someone to disbelieve…’”
q: They are like Satan when he lures someone to disbelieve. Then after they have done so, he will say, I have absolutely nothing to do with you. I truly fear Allah—the Lord of all worlds!’ So they will both end up in the Fire, staying there forever. That is the reward of the wrongdoers … They are like Satan when he lures someone to disbelieve

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Hadith: Wisdom in preventing narrations from misuse
t: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdillah reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “No one narrates a hadith to people who cannot comprehend it except that it will be a tribulation for some of them.”

title: Hadith on Travel: Be fair to fellow travelers, riding animals and their owners
t: Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you are in fertile land, allow the riding animals to benefit from it and do not pass beyond the rest areas. When you are in barren land, hasten across it. Travel during the night, for the earth is traversed more easily at night.”
q: When you are in fertile land, allow the riding animals to benefit from it and do not pass beyond the rest areas. When you are in barren land, hasten across it. Travel during the night, for the earth is traversed more easily at night
gf: Sahih li gharyihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Travel: Be kind to roadway companions, human or animal
t:
Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the land is fertile, travel at a moderate pace and give the riding animals their due rights, for Allah is gentle and He loves gentleness. When the land is barren, move quickly across it. Travel during the night, for the earth is traversed more easily at night. Beware of resting upon the roadway, for it is the refuge of snakes and the pathway of wild beasts.”

Imam Ibn ‘Abdul Barr commented, “Allah Almighty is gentle and He loves gentleness in all matters, and this meaning is general and includes riding animals, travelers, and others.”
q: When the land is fertile, travel at a moderate pace and give the riding animals their due rights, for Allah is gentle and He loves gentleness. When the land is barren, move quickly across it. Travel during the night, for the earth is traversed more easily at night. Beware of resting upon the roadway, for it is the refuge of snakes and the pathway of wild beasts

title: Hadith on Roads: Help everyone lost or in distress, even unbelievers
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to us while we were sitting by the roadside. The Prophet said, “Beware of sitting in these roads, for they are the gathering places of Satan. If you must do so, then give the road its due rights.” Then the Prophet went on his way. I said to myself, “The Messenger of Allah told us to give the road its due rights, but I did not ask him what they are.” So I caught up with him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, you said such-and-such, but what are the rights of the road?” The Prophet said, “The rights of the road are that you return greetings of peace, lower your gaze, refrain from causing harm, guide the one who has lost his way, and rescue those in distress.”
q: Beware of sitting in these roads, for they are the gathering places of Satan. If you must do so, then give the road its due rights. … The rights of the road are that you return greetings of peace, lower your gaze, refrain from causing harm, guide the one who has lost his way, and rescue those in distress.

title: Hadith on Roads: Fourteen civic duties on public highways
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade sitting in the courtyards and roadsides. The Muslims said, “We cannot avoid it, we cannot do without it.” The Prophet said, “If you cannot, then give the road its due rights.” They said, “What are its rights?” The Prophet said, “Lowering the gaze, guiding the traveler, blessing one who sneezes when they praise Allah, and returning the greeting.”
q: If you cannot, then give the road its due rights … Lowering the gaze, guiding the traveler, blessing one who sneezes when they praise Allah, and returning the greeting

title: Hadith on Ummah: Muslim nation to serve humanity in mercy and grace, even in war
t: Abu Hazim: Abu Huraira, may Allah be pleased with him, stated in regards to His words, “You are the best nation ever raised for humanity—you enjoin good, forbid evil, and have faith in Allah,” (3:110) saying, “You are the best of people for the people. You bring them with chains on their neck until they embrace Islam.”
q: You are the best nation ever raised for humanity—you enjoin good, forbid evil, and have faith in Allah

title: Hadith on Roads: Be a good citizen on public highways
t: Al-Bara’ reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by some people from the Ansar while they were sitting in the road. The Prophet said, “If you insist on doing so, then return greetings of peace, support the oppressed, and guide the travelers.”
q: If you insist on doing so, then return greetings of peace, support the oppressed, and guide the travelers

title: Hadith on Animals: Give creatures their rights, unlike ruthless Satan
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you travel through fertile land, then give the riding animals their rights and proper share. If you travel through barren land, then move quickly for their sake. Travel during the night, for the earth is traversed more easily at night. And if you camp, do not camp upon the roadway, for it is the dwelling place of every wild creature.”
q: If you travel through fertile land, then give the riding animals their rights and proper share. If you travel through barren land, then move quickly for their sake. Travel during the night, for the earth is traversed more easily at night. And if you camp, do not camp upon the roadway, for it is the dwelling place of every wild creature.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Travel: Be kind to riding animals, take precautions
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you travel through fertile land, then give the camels their rightful share of the earth. If you travel during drought and scarcity, then hasten their pace. And if you camp at night, avoid the roadway, for it is the dwelling place of wild creatures during the night.”
q: If you travel through fertile land, then give the camels their rightful share of the earth. If you travel during drought and scarcity, then hasten their pace. And if you camp at night, avoid the roadway, for it is the dwelling place of wild creatures during the night.

title: Hadith on Roads: Kind words are a civic duty on public highways
t: Abu Talhah reported: We were sitting in the courtyards and open spaces, talking amongst ourselves, when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to us and stood over us. The Prophet said, “What is the matter with you and sitting in the roadways? Avoid sitting in the roadways.” We said, “We are only sitting here without causing trouble. We sit to discuss matters and talk.” The Prophet said, “If you must, then give the roadway its due rights: lowering the gaze, returning greetings of peace, and speaking kind words.”
q: What is the matter with you and sitting in the roadways? Avoid sitting in the roadways. … If you must, then give the roadway its due rights: lowering the gaze, returning greetings of peace, and speaking kind words.

title: Hadith on Evil: Worst Muslims seek misery upon innocent people
t: Abu Malik al-Ash’ari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among the best servants of Allah in this nation are those who, when they are seen, Allah Almighty is remembered. Among the worst servants of Allah in this nation are those who spread gossip, dividing loved ones and wishing misery upon the innocent.”
q: Verily, among the best servants of Allah in this nation are those who, when they are seen, Allah Almighty is remembered. Among the worst servants of Allah in this nation are those who spread gossip, dividing loved ones and wishing misery upon the innocent.

title: Hadith on Excellence: Best servants of Allah benefit the people
t: Al-Hasan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most beloved servants to Allah are those who are most beneficial to His dependents.”
q: The most beloved servants to Allah are those who are most beneficial to His dependents

title: Hadith on Creation: Allah loves for us to benefit His creatures
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “All creatures depend upon Allah, so the most beloved creatures to Allah are those who are most beneficial to His dependents.”
q: All creatures depend upon Allah, so the most beloved creatures to Allah are those who are most beneficial to His dependents.

title: Hadith on Benefitting: Allah loves those who help people
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “All creatures depend upon Allah, and the most beloved creatures to Allah are those who are most beneficial to His dependents.”
q: All creatures depend upon Allah, and the most beloved creatures to Allah are those who are most beneficial to His dependents

title: Hadith on Hajj: Stoning the Jamarat where Al-Baqarah was revealed
t: ‘Abdur Rahman ibn Yazid reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, stoned the pillar of al-‘Aqabah from within the valley with seven pebbles, declaring Allah is great with each pebble. It was said to him, “Some people are stoning it from above.” Abdullah said, “By the One besides whom there is no God, this is the place of the one upon whom Surat al-Baqarah was revealed.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hajj: Stoning the Jamarat, raising hands in supplication
t: Salim ibn ‘Abdillah reported: Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, would stone the nearest pillar with seven pebbles, declaring Allah is great after each pebble. Then he would go forward to an open area, stand facing the qiblah for a long time, supplicating and raising his hands. Then he would stone the middle pillar in the same way, then move to the left, go to an open area, stand facing the qiblah for a long time, supplicating and raising his hands. Then he would stone the pillar of al-‘Aqabah from within the valley, and he would not stop there. He would say, “This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, do it.”

title: Hadith on Hajj: Ibrahim stones the Devil at the Jamarat
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Abraham, the intimate friend of Allah, came to perform the rites, Satan appeared to him at the pillar of al-‘Aqabah, so he stoned him with seven pebbles until he sank into the earth. Then he appeared to him at the second pillar, so he stoned him with seven pebbles until he sank into the earth. Then he appeared to him at the third pillar, so he stoned him with seven pebbles until he sank into the earth.”
q: When Abraham, the intimate friend of Allah, came to perform the rites, Satan appeared to him at the pillar of al-‘Aqabah, so he stoned him with seven pebbles until he sank into the earth. Then he appeared to him at the second pillar, so he stoned him with seven pebbles until he sank into the earth. Then he appeared to him at the third pillar, so he stoned him with seven pebbles until he sank into the earth.

title: Hadith on Hajj: Light on Judgment Day for stoning the Jamarat
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you stone the pillars, you will have light on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: When you stone the pillars, you will have light on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Excuses: People ruined if making excuses, but have none
t: Abu al-Bakhtari reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “People will not be destroyed until they make excuses for themselves—or they make excuses against themselves.”
q: People will not be destroyed until they make excuses for themselves—or they make excuses against themselves

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Rulers fighting for politics, not Islam
t: ‘Ammar ibn Yasar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will be rulers after me who fight each other for the sake of kingship, killing one another.”
q: There will be rulers after me who fight each other for the sake of kingship, killing one another.

title: Abu Dharr on Nifaq: Hypocrites defame their Muslim rulers
t:
‘Ubadah ibn Nusayy reported: Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, stopped at the door of Mu’waiyah, but he remained unavailable due to being occupied by some matter. It is as if Abu Dharr felt displeasure in himself, so he said, “Whoever comes to the door of the authorities is made to stand and sit. Whoever finds the door closed will find another door besides him that hopefully opens. If he is asked, he is given. If he seeks refuge, he is protected. Verily, the beginning of a man’s hypocrisy is in defaming his leader.”

Imam Abu ‘Umar commented, “If it is not possible to give sincere advice to the authorities, then one must be patient and supplicate, for the predecessors have prohibited us from reviling the rulers.”

title: Hadith on Rulers: Support Muslim governments, not rebel or humiliate them
t: Mu’waiyah ibn Abi Sufyan reported: When Abu Dharr set out for al-Rabadah, he was met by riders from the people of Iraq. They said, “O Abu Dharr, we have heard what was done to you, so raise a banner and men will come to you in numbers as you wish!” Abu Dharr said, “Careful! Careful, O people of Islam! For I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: There will be authorities after me, so strengthen them. Whoever seeks to humiliate them has struck at the throat of Islam. His repentance will not be accepted until he retracts it as it had been.”
q: There will be authorities after me, so strengthen them. Whoever seeks to humiliate them has struck at the throat of Islam. His repentance will not be accepted until he retracts it as it had been

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Blind to truth, violent in speech
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will be a trial that makes people deaf, dumb, and blind. Whoever approaches it will be pulled into it. Unleashing the tongue during it is like striking with the sword.”
q: There will be a trial that makes people deaf, dumb, and blind. Whoever approaches it will be pulled into it. Unleashing the tongue during it is like striking with the sword.

title: Hadith on Ruwaybidah: Ignorant commentators on general affairs
t: ‘Awf ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, before the Hour will be years of deception in which liars are believed and the truthful are belied, the treacherous are trusted and the trustworthy are accused, and during such the disgraceful will comment.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, who are the disgraceful?” The Prophet said, “The trivial man speaking about the public affairs.”
q: “Verily, before the Hour will be years of deception in which liars are believed and the truthful are belied, the treacherous are trusted and the trustworthy are accused, and during such the disgraceful will comment … The trivial man speaking about the public affairs

title: Hadith on Fitnah: When Muslims fight a civil war
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said about tribulations, “Break your bows during it, cut their strings, stay in the depths of your homes, and be like the son of Adam.”
q: Break your bows during it, cut their strings, stay in the depths of your homes, and be like the son of Adam.

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Refusal to fight an unjust civil war
t:
Burs ibn Sa’id reported: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas said during the crisis of ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, “I witnessed the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: Verily, there will be a tribulation in which one sitting is better than one standing, and one standing is better than one walking, and one walking is better than one running.” Sa’d said, “What do you advise if someone invades my home and stretches forth his hand to kill me?” The Prophet said, “Be like the son of Adam.”

Yazid recited the verse, “If you raise your hand to kill me, I will not raise mine to kill you, because I fear Allah—the Lord of all worlds,” (5:28).
q: Verily, there will be a tribulation in which one sitting is better than one standing, and one standing is better than one walking, and one walking is better than one running. … Be like the son of Adam … If you raise your hand to kill me, I will not raise mine to kill you, because I fear Allah—the Lord of all worlds

title: Hadith on Hiddah: Occasional firmness in best of this Ummah
t: Duwayd ibn Nafi’ reported: Abu Mansur al-Farisi had a certain sharpness in his temperament. I mentioned it to him and he said, “I would not want to be without it, for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Sharpness may arise in the best of my nation.”
q: Sharpness may arise in the best of my nation

title: Hadith on Qiyamah: All people resurrected into their original body
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Between the two blasts of the Trumpet will be forty.” They said, “O Abu Huraira, forty days?” He said, “I cannot say.” They said, “Forty years?” He said, “I cannot say.” They said, “Forty months?” He said, “I cannot say.” And the Prophet said, “Everything of the human being will decay except for his coccyx tailbone, by which his creation is reconstructed.”
q: Between the two blasts of the Trumpet will be forty. … Everything of the human being will decay except for his coccyx tailbone, by which his creation is reconstructed.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Manhood: True masculinity is good character
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The nobility of a man is in his righteousness, his chivalry is in his character, and his worth is in his religion.”
q: The nobility of a man is in his righteousness, his chivalry is in his character, and his worth is in his religion.

title: Hadith on Sha’ban: Allah forgives all but malicious killers
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty looks over His creation on the middle night of Sha’ban, and He forgives His servants except for two: one carrying hostility and one who murdered an innocent soul.”
q: Allah Almighty looks over His creation on the middle night of Sha’ban, and He forgives His servants except for two: one carrying hostility and one who murdered an innocent soul.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Paradise covered by hardship, Hell by desires
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and Hellfire is surrounded by temptations.”
q: Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and Hellfire is surrounded by temptations

title: Salaf on Torah: The Ten Commandments in Islam
t:
Ibn Kathir reported: The Children of Israel heard the word of Allah, but they did not understand until it was explained by Moses, upon him be peace. Moses conveyed ten commandments to them from Allah; the command to worship Allah alone without associating partners with Him; the prohibition of falsely swearing an oath by Allah; the command to preserve the Sabbath, meaning to set aside one day of the week for worship, which is now achieved on Friday after Allah abrogated the Sabbath; to honor your father and your mother, that your life may be long in the land your Lord is giving to you; do not murder; do not commit adultery; do not steal; do not bear false witness against your neighbor; do not gaze upon your neighbor’s house, neither covet your neighbor’s wife, his slave, his maidservant, his ox, his donkey, nor anything else that he owns, meaning envy has been prohibited.

Imam Ibn Kathir commented, “Many of the righteous predecessors and others have said these ten commandments are contained in two verses of the Quran, in the saying of the Almighty: Say, O Prophet, ‘Come! Let me recite to you what your Lord has forbidden to you: do not associate others with Him in worship. Do not fail to honor your parents. Do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for you and for them. Do not come near indecencies, openly or secretly. Do not take a human life—made sacred by Allah—except with legal right. This is what He has commanded you, so perhaps you will understand. Do not come near the wealth of the orphan—unless intending to enhance it—until they attain maturity. Give full measure and weigh with justice. We never require of any soul more than what it can afford. Whenever you speak, maintain justice—even regarding a close relative. Fulfill your covenant with Allah. This is what He has commanded you, so perhaps you will be mindful. Indeed, that is My Path—perfectly straight. So follow it and do not follow other ways, for they will lead you away from His Way. This is what He has commanded you, so perhaps you will be conscious of Allah.’” (6:151-153)
q: Say, O Prophet, ‘Come! Let me recite to you what your Lord has forbidden to you: do not associate others with Him in worship. Do not fail to honor your parents. Do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for you and for them. Do not come near indecencies, openly or secretly. Do not take a human life—made sacred by Allah—except with legal right. This is what He has commanded you, so perhaps you will understand. Do not come near the wealth of the orphan—unless intending to enhance it—until they attain maturity. Give full measure and weigh with justice. We never require of any soul more than what it can afford. Whenever you speak, maintain justice—even regarding a close relative. Fulfill your covenant with Allah. This is what He has commanded you, so perhaps you will be mindful. Indeed, that is My Path—perfectly straight. So follow it and do not follow other ways, for they will lead you away from His Way. This is what He has commanded you, so perhaps you will be conscious of Allah.

title: Hadith on Mu’awiyah: The Prophet prays for his guidance
t: Ibn Abi ‘Amirah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed for Mu’awiyah, saying, “O Allah, make him a guide, who is guided himself, guiding others through him.”
q: O Allah, make him a guide, who is guided himself, guiding others through him.

title: Hadith on Mu’awiyah: Speak well of the Prophet’s Companions
t: Abi Idris reported: When Umar ibn al-Khattab removed ‘Umayr ibn Sa’d as governor of Hims, he appointed Mu’awiyah as a replacement. The people said, “He has removed ‘Umayr and appointed Mu’awiyah!” ‘Umayr said, “Do not mention Mu’awiyah unless in a good way, for I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: O Allah, guide others through him!”
q: O Allah, guide others through him
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Umar on Quran: Prohibition of asking modality of Unseen
t: Abu ‘Uthman reported: A man asked contentious questions of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, about the verses, “By those scattering,” (51:1) and, “By those stripping out,” (79:1) and, “By those sent forth,” (77:1). Umar said to him, “Uncover your head!” The man uncovered his head to reveal a mop of hair. Umar said, “If I had found your head shaved like the Khawarij rebels, I surely would have struck what is between your two eyes!” Then, Umar wrote to the people of Basrah, instructing them not to sit with him. Abu ‘Uthman said, “If the man sat with a hundred of us, we would all get up to leave.”
q: By those scattering … By those stripping out … By those sent forth

title: Hadith on Sha’ban: Believers forgiven except the malicious
t: Abu Tha’labah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “On the middle night of Sha’ban, Allah Almighty looks down upon His creation and He forgives the believers, but He abandons the people of grudges and malice to their malice.”
q: On the middle night of Sha’ban, Allah Almighty looks down upon His creation and He forgives the believers, but He abandons the people of grudges and malice to their malice.

title: Ali on Humility: Believers do not seek superiority over others
t: Abu Sallam reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “If a man likes for so much as the strap of his sandal to be of better quality than his companion, then he is included in the Almighty’s saying: That eternal Home in the Hereafter We reserve only for those who seek neither supremacy nor corruption on the earth. The ultimate outcome belongs only to the righteous.” (28:83)
q: That eternal Home in the Hereafter We reserve only for those who seek neither supremacy nor corruption on the earth. The ultimate outcome belongs only to the righteous.

title: Hadith on Gifts: Purify your heart by giving to others
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Give each other gifts, for gifts remove agitation within the chest.”
q: Give each other gifts, for gifts remove agitation within the chest.

title: Mujahid on Malice: Voluntary fasting to purify the heart
t: Abu Ishaq reported: Al-Harith al-Hamdani, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Fasting the month of patience, Ramadan, and fasting three days each month removes disorders within the chest.” Mujahid said, “It removes agitation within the chest.” It was said, “What is agitation in the chest?” Mujahid said, “His malevolence.”

title: Hadith on Malice: Testimony of malicious not accepted
t: Sulayman ibn Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is not permissible to accept testimony from a deceitful man or woman, an adulterer or an adulteress, or one with spite against his brother.”
q: It is not permissible to accept testimony from a deceitful man or woman, an adulterer or an adulteress, or one with spite against his brother.

title: Hasan on Hasad: Everyone must resist envy and jealousy
t:
Ibn ‘Abdul Barr reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “There is no one among the children of Adam who was created without envy. Whoever restrains it from passing into injustice and transgression, then no harm will come to him from it.”

Imam Ibn ‘Abdul Barr commented, “We have elaborated this meaning with reports from the righteous predecessors about the condemnation of envy and the virtue of those who do not envy people.”

title: Hadith on Purity: Best people have sounds hearts
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: It was said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “Who are the best of people?” The Prophet said, “Everyone with a heart swept clean and a truthful tongue.” They said, “We understand a truthful tongue, but what is a heart swept clean?” The Prophet said, “It is Godfearing and pure without sin inside it, neither aggression, nor rancor, nor envy.”
q: Everyone with a heart swept clean and a truthful tongue. … It is Godfearing and pure without sin inside it, neither aggression, nor rancor, nor envy.

title: Hadith on Malice: Three characteristics Allah does not forgive
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are three things: whoever does not possess any one of them, Allah will forgive whatever is besides that for whom He wills: a person who dies without associating anything with Allah, who is not a sorcerer the ways of black magic, and who does not harbor malice toward his brother.”
q: There are three things: whoever does not possess any one of them, Allah will forgive whatever is besides that for whom He wills: a person who dies without associating anything with Allah, who is not a sorcerer the ways of black magic, and who does not harbor malice toward his brother.

title: Hadith on Malice: Repentance not accepted until rancor rejected
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The deeds are presented on Monday and Thursday. Whoever seeks forgiveness will be forgiven, whoever repents will be accepted, but the people of grudges are turned away on account of their grudges until they repent.”
q: The deeds are presented on Monday and Thursday. Whoever seeks forgiveness will be forgiven, whoever repents will be accepted, but the people of grudges are turned away on account of their grudges until they repent.

title: Hadith on Parents: Kindness to unbelieving relatives
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The mother of Sa’d swore an oath not to speak to him ever again unless he renounced his religion, nor would she eat or drink. She said, “You claim that Allah has commanded you to be kind to your parents, yet I am your mother and I command you to do this!” She continued for three days until she fainted from the effort. One of her sons named ‘Umarah gave her water to drink, then she started praying against Sa’d. Allah Almighty revealed this verse in the Quran, “If they pressure you to associate with Me what you have no knowledge of, do not obey them. Still keep their company in this world courteously.” (31:15)
q: If they pressure you to associate with Me what you have no knowledge of, do not obey them. Still keep their company in this world courteously.

title: Hadith on Neighbors: What are the rights of your community?
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: We said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of neighbors?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If he asks you for a loan, lend it to him. If he asks for help, assist him. If he needs something, give it to him. If he falls ill, visit him. If he dies, follow his funeral. If goodness reaches him, feel happy for him and congratulate him. If a calamity afflicts him, feel sad for him and console him. Do not trouble him with an aroma from your cooking pot unless you leave some for him. Do not build so high as to overshadow him, nor block the breeze from him unless he gives you permission. If you buy fruits, give some of it to him as a gift or at least conceal it, lest your children go out with some of it and provoke his children.” Then, the Prophet said, “Do you comprehend what I am saying to you? No one will truly fulfill the rights of their neighbors except for the few upon whom Allah has mercy.”
q: If he asks you for a loan, lend it to him. If he asks for help, assist him. If he needs something, give it to him. If he falls ill, visit him. If he dies, follow his funeral. If goodness reaches him, feel happy for him and congratulate him. If a calamity afflicts him, feel sad for him and console him. Do not trouble him with an aroma from your cooking pot unless you leave some for him. Do not build so high as to overshadow him, nor block the breeze from him unless he gives you permission. If you buy fruits, give some of it to him as a gift or at least conceal it, lest your children go out with some of it and provoke his children. … Do you comprehend what I am saying to you? No one will truly fulfill the rights of their neighbors except for the few upon whom Allah has mercy.

title: Hadith on Fiqh: Allah grants comprehension of religion
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “To whomever Allah wills goodness, He allows them to comprehend.”
q: To whomever Allah wills goodness, He allows them to comprehend.
gf: Jayyid (very good) according to Ibn Kathir

title: Hadith on Charity: Reward for good deeds to all creatures
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “I draw water from my basin until I fill it for my family, and then a camel belonging to someone else comes to me and I give it water to drink. Do I have a reward for this?” The Prophet said, “In every living being with a warm liver is a reward for charity.”
q: In every living being with a warm liver is a reward for charity.

title: Hadith on Awliya: Harming Allah’s friends is war against Him
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: Whoever humiliates an ally of Mine, he has declared war upon Me. My servant does not draw closer to me with anything like fulfilling the obligations. The servant continues to grow closer to Me by recommended deeds until I love him. If he asks from Me, I will give it to him. If he calls upon Me, I will answer him. I do not hesitate in anything that I do as much as I am reluctant to make him pass away, for he hates death and I hate to distress him.”
q: Allah Almighty said: Whoever humiliates an ally of Mine, he has declared war upon Me. My servant does not draw closer to me with anything like fulfilling the obligations. The servant continues to grow closer to Me by recommended deeds until I love him. If he asks from Me, I will give it to him. If he calls upon Me, I will answer him. I do not hesitate in anything that I do as much as I am reluctant to make him pass away, for he hates death and I hate to distress him.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Awliya: Curse upon those who harm Allah’s friends
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty revealed to me: O brother of the Messengers! O brother of the warners! Warn your people not to enter one of My houses while one of them carries an injustice with him, for I curse whoever stands before Me in prayer until he makes amends with those he has wronged. I am surely their hearing with which they hear and their seeing with which they see, for they are My allies and chosen ones, and they will be My neighbors alongside the Prophets, the truthful, and the martyrs in Paradise.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty revealed to me: O brother of the Messengers! O brother of the warners! Warn your people not to enter one of My houses while one of them carries an injustice with him, for I curse whoever stands before Me in prayer until he makes amends with those he has wronged. I am surely their hearing with which they hear and their seeing with which they see, for they are My allies and chosen ones, and they will be My neighbors alongside the Prophets, the truthful, and the martyrs in Paradise.
gf: Jayyid (very good) according to Ibn Rajab

title: Hadith on Qiyamah: People resurrected in a new creation
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, delivered a sermon, saying, “Verily, all of you will be gathered before Allah barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “Just as We produced the first creation, so shall We reproduce it. That is a promise binding upon Us. Surely, We will do it!” (21:104)
q: Verily, all of you will be gathered before Allah barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. … Just as We produced the first creation, so shall We reproduce it. That is a promise binding upon Us. Surely, We will do it!
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Rahmah: The Prophet’s public display of mercy
t: Abu Huraira reported: Al-Tufayl ibn ‘Amr, from the tribe of Daws, met the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, the tribe of Daws has surely disobeyed you and rejected you, so pray to Allah against them.” The Messenger of Allah turned to the Qiblah and raised his hands, such that the people thought he would pray against them, but the Prophet said, “O Allah, guide the tribe of Daws and bring them closer to me.”
q: O Allah, guide the tribe of Daws and bring them closer to me.

title: Al-Shafi’ee on Sunnah: Leave my opinions contradicting the Prophet
t: Rabia’ ibn Sulayman reported: Imam al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on upon him, said, “If you find something in my writings that contradict the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, then speak with the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah and abandon what I have said.”

title: Ali on Khilfaha: Ali accepted the Caliphate of Abu Bakr
t: Al-Hasan reported: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “After the passing of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, we looked for what we were commanded and we found the Prophet had given preference to Abu Bakr for leading the prayer. So, we were pleased for our religion and we preferred Abu Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him.”

title: Ali on Khalifah: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman the best Caliphs
t: Abu Wa’il reported: It was said to Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, “Will you not appoint a successor upon us?” Ali said, “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, did not appoint a successor, so I will not appoint a successor, but if Allah intends good for people, then He will gather them after me upon the best of them, just as the He gathered them after their Prophet upon the best of them.”
gf: Jayyid (very good) according to Ibn Kathir

title: Harith on Mercy: Satan hopes for intercession on Judgment Day
t: Ibrahim ibn Yazid reported: Al-Harith ibn Suwayd al-Taymi, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “People will continue being granted intercession on the Day of Resurrection until even the chief of devils, Iblees himself, will crane his neck in hope that it might reach him.”

title: Hadith on Divorce: Prohibition of discarding elderly wives
t:
Al-Miqdam ibn Ma’di reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stood up for the people and praised Allah as is due to Him, saying, “Verily, Allah Almighty instructs you to treat women well, again Allah instructs you to treat women well, and again Allah instructs you to treat women well. Verily, Allah enjoins goodness for your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, and your aunts. A man of the churches would stay married to a woman, not knowing if there was any good in her for him, neither of them finding their spouse attractive until they died together in old age.”

Al-‘Ala’ ibn Sufyan said, “I was told that among the immoralities forbidden by Allah, which are obscure and not clearly stated in the Quran, is that a man will marry a woman, so they spend a lot of time together until she exhausts what is in her womb, then he divorces here without any misgiving.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty instructs you to treat women well, again Allah instructs you to treat women well, and again Allah instructs you to treat women well. Verily, Allah enjoins goodness for your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, and your aunts. A man of the churches would stay married to a woman, not knowing if there was any good in her for him, neither of them finding their spouse attractive until they died together in old age.

title: Ahmad on Dua: Prayer against oppressors allowed, but forgiveness better
t:
Ibn Muflih reported: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Supplication is a proportional punishment. Whoever supplicates against the one who wronged him, he has not been patient.”

Imam Ibn Muflih commented, “By that he means the supplicant has retaliated. Retaliation is permissible, but the Almighty said: Whoever endures patiently and forgives, surely this is a resolve to aspire to, (42:23)… If one supplicates against the wrongdoer to be hurt by the same amount with which he was hurt by him, that is justice.”
q: Whoever endures patiently and forgives, surely this is a resolve to aspire to

title: Sufyan on Ihsan: Be good to sinners, not only the righteous
t: Al-Tha’labi reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Excellence is that you are good to the one who is evil to you, for only doing good to a good-doer is merely a transaction like currency in the marketplace. Take from me and give back.”

title: Sa’id on Curses: Do not wish evil upon believers
t: ‘Ata’ ibn Dinar reported: Sa’id ibn Jubayr, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Do not supplicate for evil against the believing men and women, asking Allah to disgrace them and curse them and so on, for that is transgression in the saying of Allah Almighty: Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly. Surely, He does not like the transgressors.” (7:55)
q: Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly. Surely, He does not like the transgressors.

title: Hadith on Dua: Prohibition of prayer against people by name
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to supplicate against four people until Allah Almighty revealed the verse, “You have no say in the matter. It is up to Allah to turn to them in mercy or punish them, for they are surely wrongdoers,” (3:128). Then, Allah guided them to Islam.
q: You have no say in the matter. It is up to Allah to turn to them in mercy or punish them, for they are surely wrongdoers

title: Nuh on Patience: Forgive my people for they do not know
t: ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Umayr reported: They used to beat and strangle Noah, upon him be peace, until he fainted. When he woke up, Noah said, “O Allah, forgive my people for they do not know.”

title: Ahmad on Curses: Disapproval of praying against people by name
t: Salih reported: A man mentioned Al-Hajjaj or others to his father, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him, saying, “Let him be cursed!” Ahmad said, “I do not like for it to be uttered.” Then, Ahmad said, “Surely, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.” (11:18)
q: Surely, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.

title: Hadith on Rahmah: The Prophet sent as gift of mercy
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I have only been sent as mercy and an offering of guidance.”
q: Verily, I have only been sent as mercy and an offering of guidance.

title: Hadith on Justice: Most concise verse on Halal and Haram
t: Abu al-Duha’ reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “There is no verse in the Quran more comprehensive for the lawful and the unlawful, the commanding and the forbidding, than this verse: Verily, Allah commands justice, grace, as well as generosity to close relatives. He forbids indecency, wickedness, and aggression. He instructs you so perhaps you will be mindful.” (16:90)
q: Verily, Allah commands justice, grace, as well as generosity to close relatives. He forbids indecency, wickedness, and aggression. He instructs you so perhaps you will be mindful.

title: Fudayl on Ihsan: Be good to all creatures, even animals
t: Muhammad ibn Thabit reported: Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Know that if the servant treated everyone well, but he was evil to his chickens, he would not be recorded among the good-doers.”

title: Jesus on Excellence: Be good to the evildoer
t: Al-Sha’bi reported: Jesus the son of Mary, upon him be peace, would say, “Verily, goodness is not that you are good to the one who is good to you, for that is only a charitable recompense. Rather, goodness is that you are good to the one who is evil to you.”

title: Hadith on Nikah: No forced marriages in Islam
t: Aisha reported: A young woman entered her home and she said, “My father married me off to his brother’s son to raise his status, but I was unwilling.” Aisha said, “Sit here until the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, comes.” The Messenger of Allah came and she told him about it, so he sent for her father, who gave her the decision. She said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have allowed what my father did, but I rejected it so I could know if women have any say in the matter.”

title: Hadith on Marriage: Serving husbands is equal to Jihad
t: Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah reported: While we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, a woman came to him, saying, “Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah! I am from the women’s delegation to you. Allah is the Lord of men and women. Adam is the father of men and women. Allah has sent you to men and women. When men go out campaigning in the way of Allah and are killed, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision and rejoicing in what Allah has given them. When they go out, they have the reward as they have learned, while we serve them and stay in place, so what is our reward?” The Prophet said to her, “Give my greetings of peace to the women and tell them that obeying their husbands is equal to all of that, yet few of you do it. The right of a man is to have his wife.”
q: Give my greetings of peace to the women and tell them that obeying their husbands is equal to all of that, yet few of you do it. The right of a man is to have his wife.

title: Hadith on Ikhlas: Man saved by the word of Tawhid
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The angel of death attended to a man who was dying. He examined his heart and found nothing there, so he untied his jaws and found the tip of his tongue sticking to the roof of his mouth, saying: There is no God but Allah. He was forgiven due to the word of sincerity.”
q: The angel of death attended to a man who was dying. He examined his heart and found nothing there, so he untied his jaws and found the tip of his tongue sticking to the roof of his mouth, saying: There is no God but Allah. He was forgiven due to the word of sincerity.

title: Hadith on Sahaba: The Companions are blessing for Ummah
t: Abu Burdah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The stars are safety for the sky, so when the stars are taken away, what is promised will come to the sky. I am safety for my companions, so when I am taken away, what is promised will come to my companions. My companions are safety for my nation, so when my companions are taken away, what is promised will come to my nation.”
q: The stars are safety for the sky, so when the stars are taken away, what is promised will come to the sky. I am safety for my companions, so when I am taken away, what is promised will come to my companions. My companions are safety for my nation, so when my companions are taken away, what is promised will come to my nation.

title: Hadith on Mut’ah: Ali corrects a fatwa of Ibn Abbas
t: Al-Hasan reported: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, heard Ibn Abbas being lenient with temporary marriage to women. Ali said, “Do not be hasty, Ibn Abbas! For the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited it on the day of Khaybar!”

title: Hadith on Dhul-Hijjah: Greatest ten days of all time
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best days in the world are the ten days of the month of Dhul-Hijjah.”
q: The best days in the world are the ten days of the month of Dhul-Hijjah.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Caliphs: Best of Ummah are Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman
t: Ibn Umar reported: In the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while his companions were numerous, we preferred Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman, then we would remain silent.

title: Hadith on Caliphs: The Prophet always with Abu Bakr and Umar
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Umar was placed upon his bier as the people surrounded him, supplicated for him, and performed the funeral prayer over him before he was taken away. I was there, and nothing else held my attention but a man putting his hand on my shoulder. It was Ali, invoking the mercy of Allah upon Umar. Ali said, “You have not left anyone behind so beloved to me that I should meet Allah with the likes of their good deeds other than you, Umar! By Allah, I always thought Allah would place you alongside your two companions, for I often heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: I went with Abu Bakr and Umar, I came with Abu Bakr and Umar, I left with Abu Bakr and Umar.”
q: I went with Abu Bakr and Umar, I came with Abu Bakr and Umar, I left with Abu Bakr and Umar.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Caliphs: Abu Bakr and Umar honored in Ummah
t: Abdullah ibn Hantab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saw Abu Bakr and Umar, saying, “These two are the hearing and the sight.”
q: These two are the hearing and the sight.

title: Hadith on Dua: Etiquette of order for supplications
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: I prayed with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while Abu Bakr and Umar were with him. When I sat down, I began by praising Allah, then sending blessings upon the Prophet, then supplicating for myself. The Prophet said, “Ask and you will be given. Ask and you will be given.”
q: Ask and you will be given. Ask and you will be given.

title: Hadith on Charity: Four types of Sadaqah Jariyah
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Four people continue to be rewarded after death: a soldier guarding the frontier in the way of Allah, one teaching a good deed to others is rewarded like them as they act upon it, a man offering charity is rewarded for it as it is ongoing, and a man leaving behind a righteous child who supplicates for him.”
q: Four people continue to be rewarded after death: a soldier guarding the frontier in the way of Allah, one teaching a good deed to others is rewarded like them as they act upon it, a man offering charity is rewarded for it as it is ongoing, and a man leaving behind a righteous child who supplicates for him.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Nowruz: Prohibition of joining idolatrous celebrations
t: Al-Walid reported: Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever passes through foreign lands and participates in their new years and their festivals, imitating them and dying upon that way, then he will be gathered with them on the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Hadith on Fiqh: Understanding Islam key to all good
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “To whomever Allah wills goodness, He grants them understanding of the religion.”
q: To whomever Allah wills goodness, He grants them understanding of the religion.

title: Abu Darda on Knowledge: Learn Islam before scholars die off
t: Mu’awiyah ibn Qurrah reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Learn sacred knowledge before it is taken away, for knowledge is taken away by the disappearance of the scholars. The scholar and the student surely have the same reward. Verily, there are only two kinds of men in the world: the scholar and the student. There is no goodness in anything besides that.”

title: Hadith on Fiqh: Understanding Islam a light unto the nations
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whomever Allah intends goodness for, He grants him understanding of the religion.”
q: Whomever Allah intends goodness for, He grants him understanding of the religion.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Ignorance: Islam weakened by lack of scholars
t: Abu Wa’il reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Do you know how Islam is weakened?” They said, “Just as the dye of a garment fades, or as an animal gets tired, or as a coin is rusted by the passage of time.” Abdullah said, “That is surely part of it, but even worse than that is the death or disappearance of the scholars.”

title: Hasan on Knowledge: Charity to learn and teach Islam
t: ‘Awf ibn Abi Jamilah reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It is part of charity to learn sacred knowledge, and then teach it to the people.”

title: Ibn Ka’b on Quran: Book of Allah is direct address to you
t: Abu Ma’shar reported: Muhammad ibn Ka’b, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whomever the Quran reaches, it is as if Allah is speaking to him.”

title: Thabit on Quran: Struggle with recitation first, then enjoy it
t: Abu Talib al-Makki reported: Thabit al-Bunani, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I suffered with the Quran for twenty years, then I enjoyed it for twenty years.”

title: ‘Utbah on Worship: Struggle with prayer first, then love it
t: Zaydan reported: ‘Utabah al-Ghulam, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I suffered with prayer for twenty years, then I enjoyed it for twenty years.”

title: Hadith on Polygamy: Warning against injustice to multiple wives
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever has two wives and he inclines to one of them over the other, he will come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides collapsed.”
q: Whoever has two wives and he inclines to one of them over the other, he will come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides collapsed.

title: Abu Qilabah on Bid’ah: Heresy leads to unlawful violence
t: Ayyub reported: Abu Qilabah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “People never innovate a heresy except that they make the sword lawful by it.”

title: Hadith on Dishonesty: Telling white lies or necessary lies
t: Asma’ bint Yazid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is not allowed to lie except in three cases: a man conversing with his wife to please her, to lie in warfare, and to lie in order to reconcile people.”
q: It is not allowed to lie except in three cases: a man conversing with his wife to please her, to lie in warfare, and to lie in order to reconcile people.

title: Umar om Marriage: Telling white lies to your spouse
t: Ibn Abi ‘Azrah reported: A man in the time of Umar said to his wife, “I adjure you by Allah, do you love me?” She said, “As you adjured me by Allah, I do not.” The man went out until he came to Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, so he sent for her. Umar said to her, “Are you the one who told her husband you did not love him?” She said, “O commander of the faithful, he adjured me by Allah. Should I fib?” Umar said, “Yes, you should fib. Not all households are built upon love, but rather people get along by Islam and good manners.”

title: Umar on Murder: Groups executed for conspiring to kill
t: Ibn Umar reported: A young boy was murdered in an act of treachery. Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “If the people of San’a’ had conspired to do this, I would execute all of them.”

title: Dahhak on Khilafah: The Prophet tells his wives about Caliphs
t: Abu Salih reported: Regarding the Almighty’s statement, “Remember when the Prophet had once confided something to one of his wives” (66:3), Al-Dahhak said, “He had secretly confided in Hafsah, the daughter of Umar, that the Caliphate after him would be with Abu Bakr, and Umar would succeed him.”
q: Remember when the Prophet had once confided something to one of his wives

title: Hadith on Khilafah: The Prophet foretells Four Righteous Caliphs
t:
Safinah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Caliphate after me will last for thirty years, then there will be kingship.”

Sa’id said to Safinah, “Count the Caliphates of Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman?” Then, Safinah said, “You must count the Caliphate of Ali.” Sa’id said, “We found them to total thirty years.”
q: The Caliphate after me will last for thirty years, then there will be kingship.

title: Hadith on Peacemaking: Allah and His Messenger pleased by reconciliation
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Abu Ayyub! Shall I not tell you of a deed most pleasing to Allah and His Messenger?” He said, “Of course!” The Prophet said, “That you reconcile people when there is resentment between them, and you bring together those who were estranged from each other.”
q: O Abu Ayyub! Shall I not tell you of a deed most pleasing to Allah and His Messenger? … That you reconcile people when there is resentment between them, and you bring together those who were estranged from each other.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Sidq: Cannot be cursing and truthful simultaneously
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You cannot be in the habit of cursing and among the truthful at the same time.”
q: You cannot be in the habit of cursing and among the truthful at the same time.

title: Hadith on Forbearance: Keep your reward from the insulter
t: Jabir ibn Sulaym reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a man insults you and reviles you for something he knows about you, do not disparage him for something you know about him. You will have his reward and he will have his sin, so do not insult anyone.”
q: If a man insults you and reviles you for something he knows about you, do not disparage him for something you know about him. You will have his reward and he will have his sin, so do not insult anyone.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Paradise: Chambers for feeding poor, gentle speech, night prayer
t: Abu Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, in Paradise, are rooms whose outside can be seen from the inside, and whose interior can be seen from the outside. Allah has prepared them for those who feed the hungry, speak mildly, regularly perform prayer, and stand at night while people sleep.”
q: Verily, in Paradise, are rooms whose outside can be seen from the inside, and whose interior can be seen from the outside. Allah has prepared them for those who feed the hungry, speak mildly, regularly perform prayer, and stand at night while people sleep.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Greed: Faith does not coexist with avarice
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Greed and faith are never combined within the heart of a servant.”
q: Greed and faith are never combined within the heart of a servant.

title: Hadith on Euphrates: Trial over treasure before the Hour
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Soon the Euphrates River will disclose a treasure of gold. Whoever witnesses it, let him not take anything from it.”
q: Soon the Euphrates River will disclose a treasure of gold. Whoever witnesses it, let him not take anything from it.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Travel: The Prophet helps his fellow travelers
t: Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would stay behind the caravan, encouraging the weak to catch up, letting them ride with him, and supplicating for them.

title: Hadith on Travel: Appoint leader for traveling group
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khurdi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whenever three people set out on a journey, let one of them be appointed as their leader.”
q: Whenever three people set out on a journey, let one of them be appointed as their leader.

title: Hadith on Gathering: Not allowed to separate sitting people
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is not permissible for a man to separate two people in a gathering without both their permission.”
q: It is not permissible for a man to separate two people in a gathering without both their permission.

title: Hadith on Silk: Prohibition of men wearing silk
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not wear silk, for whoever wears silk in the world will not wear it in the Hereafter.”
q: Do not wear silk, for whoever wears silk in the world will not wear it in the Hereafter.

title: Hadith on Clothing: Concession for women to lower garments
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever trails their garment in pride, Allah will never look at them on the Day of Resurrection.” Umm Salamah said, “What should women do with their hems?” The Prophet said, “Slacken them by a handspan.” She said, “Then their feet would be exposed.” The Prophet said, “Then slacken them by a forearms’ length and no more.”
q: Whoever trails their garment in pride, Allah will never look at them on the Day of Resurrection. … Slacken them by a handspan … Then slacken them by a forearms’ length and no more.

title: Hadith on Clothing: Recommendation for garment in middle of shins
t: Ibn Umar reported: I passed by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while my garment was falling. The Prophet said, “O Abdullah, raise your garment.” I raised it up, then the Prophet said, “More.” I raised it again and I kept pulling it up until some people said, “To where?” The Prophet said, “Halfway between the shins.”
q: O Abdullah, raise your garment. … More … Halfway between the shins.

title: Hadith on Pride: Punishment for proudful trailing clothes
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Draping is in regards to the robe, shirt, and turban. Whoever trails any of them in pride, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Draping is in regards to the robe, shirt, and turban. Whoever trails any of them in pride, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Vanity: Arrogant trailing garment in Hellfire
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whatever part of the garment is below the two ankles is in the Hellfire.”
q: Whatever part of the garment is below the two ankles is in the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Vanity: Allah will not look at proud, boastful
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah will not look on the Day of Resurrection at one who trailed his garment in vanity.”
q: Allah will not look on the Day of Resurrection at one who trailed his garment in vanity.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Rahmah: How misguided to restrict Allah’s mercy!
t: Jundub reported: A bedouin came, dismounted his camel, and tied it, then he prayed behind the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. Afterwards, he called out, “O Allah, have mercy upon me and Muhammad and do not share Your mercy with anyone else!” The Prophet said, “Do you say he is more astray or is his camel? Did you not hear what he said?” They said, “Of course.” The Prophet said, “The mercy of Allah before you is vast. Verily, Allah created one hundred portions of mercy and He sent down a single portion, by which the creation is compassionate to one another, its jinn, its people, and its animals. He has ninety-nine portions left. So do you say he is more astray or is his camel?”
q: Do you say he is more astray or is his camel? Did you not hear what he said? … The mercy of Allah before you is vast. Verily, Allah created one hundred portions of mercy and He sent down a single portion, by which the creation is compassionate to one another, its jinn, its people, and its animals. He has ninety-nine portions left. So do you say he is more astray or is his camel?

title: Hadith on Usury: Humiliation upon Ummah until repentance
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you engage in usurious transactions, hold on to the tails of cows, being pleased with agriculture, and abandon jihad, Allah will appoint disgrace as an authority over you and it will not be removed until you return to your religion.”
q: When you engage in usurious transactions, hold on to the tails of cows, being pleased with agriculture, and abandon jihad, Allah will appoint disgrace as an authority over you and it will not be removed until you return to your religion.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Salaam: Youth greeting adults with peace
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The young should greet elders with peace, the passerby should greet those sitting, and the small group should greet the large group.”
q: The young should greet elders with peace, the passerby should greet those sitting, and the small group should greet the large group.

title: Hadith on Salaam: Greeting with peace, living or dead
t: Jabir ibn Sulaym reported: I saw a man whose opinions the people took seriously. He would not say anything but that they accepted it. I said, “Who is this?” They said, “This is the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.” I said twice, “Upon you be peace, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “Do not say, ‘Upon you be peace,’ as such is the greeting for the deceased. Say, ‘Peace be upon you.’”
q: Do not say, ‘Upon you be peace,’ as such is the greeting for the deceased. Say, ‘Peace be upon you.’

title: Hadith on Dreams: Truest visions for honest believers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most truthful of your dreams come to the most truthful of you in speech.”
q: The most truthful of your dreams come to the most truthful of you in speech

title: Hadith on Nubuwwa: No prophecy left except good dreams
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Nothing remains of prophecy but glad tidings.” They said, “What are glad tidings?” The Prophet said, “Good dreams.”
q: Nothing remains of prophecy but glad tidings. … Good dreams.

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: The Prophet’s night-time routine
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would pray eleven cycles in the night. When dawn arrived, he would pray two brief cycles, then lie on his right side until the caller came to announce the prayer.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Clothes: Description of the Prophet’s turban
t: ‘Amr ibn Hurayth reported: I remember looking at the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was upon the pulpit. The Prophet had a black turban on his head with the two ends hanging between his shoulders.

title: Hadith on Clothes: The Prophet wears a red-striped mantle
t: Abu Juhayfah reported: I came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in Mecca while he was at al-Abtah in a red leather tent. Bilal came out with his leftover water from ablution, and some of them took it and rubbed themselves with it. The Prophet came out wearing a red mantle and I caught a glance at the skin of his shins.

title: Hadith on Clothes: Prefer white garments, living or deceased
t:
Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Clothe yourselves in white garments, for they are the best of garments, and shroud your deceased in them.”

Ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The most beloved to me is to shroud oneself with a white garment in which one prays.”
q: Clothe yourselves in white garments, for they are the best of garments, and shroud your deceased in them.

title: Hadith on Salah: Reciting Al-Fatihah in prayer is obligatory
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A prayer performed by one who has not recited ‘the foundation of the Quran’ during it is deficient, deficient, deficient, incomplete.”
q: A prayer performed by one who has not recited ‘the foundation of the Quran’ during it is deficient, deficient, deficient, incomplete.

title: Hadith on Duha: Best time for forenoon prayer
t: Zayd ibn Arqam reported: He saw some people performing the forenoon prayer, and he said, “They already know that prayer at a different time is better.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The forenoon prayer of the penitent is when young camels can feel the heat of the sun.”
q: The forenoon prayer of the penitent is when young camels can feel the heat of the sun.

title: Hadith on Siyam: All good deeds multiplied, but fasting is special
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Every good deed of the son of Adam is multiplied by ten like it, up to seven hundred more. Allah said: Except for fasting, for it is Mine and I will reward it.”
q: Every good deed of the son of Adam is multiplied by ten like it, up to seven hundred more. Allah said: Except for fasting, for it is Mine and I will reward it

title: Hadith on Siyam: Fasting person’s breath sweeter than musk
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, the odor coming from the mouth of a fasting person is more pleasant to Allah Almighty than the scent of musk. Allah said: He leaves his food, his drink, and his passions for My sake. The fast is for Me and I will reward him for it with a good deed ten times like it.”
q: By the One in whose hand is my soul, the odor coming from the mouth of a fasting person is more pleasant to Allah Almighty than the scent of musk. Allah said: He leaves his food, his drink, and his passions for My sake. The fast is for Me and I will reward him for it with a good deed ten times like it.

title: Hadith on Promises: Abu Bakr keeps the Prophet’s pledge
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If the goods come from Bahrain, I will give you such and such amount.” The goods from Bahrain did not arrive until after the Prophet passed away. When the goods arrived, Abu Bakr ordered an announcement, “Whoever has a promise or a debt from the Prophet, let him come to us and we will give it to him.” I said, “Indeed, the Prophet told me I could have such and such amount.” Abu Bakr gave me a handful of coins and I counted it as five hundred. Abu Bakr said, “Take twice what you have been promised.”
q: If the goods come from Bahrain, I will give you such and such amount
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Zakariya: Prophet Zechariah was a carpenter
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Zechariah, upon him be peace, worked as a carpenter.”
q: Zechariah, upon him be peace, worked as a carpenter

title: Hadith on Work: Any employment better than begging people
t: Al-Zubayr ibn al-’Awwam reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “For one of you to carry a rope and bring firewood upon his back to sell, by which Allah saves his face, is better for you than asking from people who might give to you or withhold from you.”
q: For one of you to carry a rope and bring firewood upon his back to sell, by which Allah saves his face, is better for you than asking from people who might give to you or withhold from you

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Upper hand giving better than lower hand taking
t: Hakim ibn Hizam reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The upper hand is better than the lower hand. Begin by giving to your dependents. The best charity is given by the rich. Whoever seeks to abstain from begging, Allah will make him abstain. Whoever seeks to be independent of others, Allah will make him independent.”
q: The upper hand is better than the lower hand. Begin by giving to your dependents. The best charity is given by the rich. Whoever seeks to abstain from begging, Allah will make him abstain. Whoever seeks to be independent of others, Allah will make him independent.

title: Hadith on Miskin: Truly poor rely upon Allah, not begging people
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The truly poor man is not the one who goes around people and is dismissed by a morsel, two morsels, or one or two dates.” They said, “Then who is the poor man, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “The one who does not find enough to satisfy himself, nor is he considered such that charity would be given to him, nor does he beg people for anything.”
q: The truly poor man is not the one who goes around people and is dismissed by a morsel, two morsels, or one or two dates. … The one who does not find enough to satisfy himself, nor is he considered such that charity would be given to him, nor does he beg people for anything.

title: Hadith on Heraclius: What does this Prophet really teach?
t: Abu Sufyan reported: In his lengthy narration regarding the story of the Roman Emperor, Heraclius, that he asked him, “What does he command you to do?” Abu Sufyan said, “The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, orders us to worship Allah alone without associating partners with Him, to abandon the sayings of our forefathers, to perform prayer, to be truthful, to practice abstinence, and to maintain relations.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Mercy: Believers show mercy even to birds
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever shows mercy, even in the slaughter of a sparrow, Allah will be merciful to him on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever shows mercy, even in the slaughter of a sparrow, Allah will be merciful to him on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: If you really knew Allah’s mercy or punishment
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you knew the measure of Allah’s mercy, you would take it for granted and only perform a few good deeds. If you knew the measure of Allah’s wrath, you would think there is no way you could be saved.”
q: If you knew the measure of Allah’s mercy, you would take it for granted and only perform a few good deeds. If you knew the measure of Allah’s wrath, you would think there is no way you could be saved.

title: Hadith on Kaba’ir: Despairing of Allah’s mercy a major sin
t: Ibn Abbas reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, what are the major sins?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him said, “Idolatry with Allah, losing hope in relief from Allah, and despair in the mercy of Allah.”
q: Idolatry with Allah, losing hope in relief from Allah, and despair in the mercy of Allah.

title: Hadith on Awliya: Ninety-nine mercies reserved for Allah’s allies
t: Mu’awiyah ibn Haydah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty created one hundred portions of mercy, so one portion of mercy between His creation is that they are merciful to each other by it, and ninety-nine portions are reserved for His allies.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty created one hundred portions of mercy, so one portion of mercy between His creation is that they are merciful to each other by it, and ninety-nine portions are reserved for His allies.

title: Hadith on Rahmah: One mercy for world, ninety-nine for Hereafter
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty created one hundred portions of mercy. One portion of mercy was distributed between the creation, and ninety-nine are reserved until the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty created one hundred portions of mercy. One portion of mercy was distributed between the creation, and ninety-nine are reserved until the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Mercy: Allah rewards compassion to animals
t: Ma’qil ibn Yasar reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, I had taken the goat to slaughter it, but I had mercy on it.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you had mercy on it, Allah will have mercy on you.”
q: If you had mercy on it, Allah will have mercy on you.

title: Hadith on Family: The Prophet is most merciful to his dependents
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was the most merciful of people to his dependents. He had his son suckled in part of Madina, and the husband of his wet-nurse was a blacksmith. We used to go to him and the house would be full of smoke from the bellows. He would kiss the child and take him in his lap.

title: Hadith on Mercy: Be merciful, forgiving, and penitent
