t: Jarir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is not merciful will not receive mercy. Whoever does not forgive will not be forgiven. Whoever does not repent, Allah will not turn to him.”
q: Whoever is not merciful will not receive mercy. Whoever does not forgive will not be forgiven. Whoever does not repent, Allah will not turn to him

title: Hadith on Rifq: Be gentle in speech, not harsh or profane
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must be gentle, and beware of harshness and obscenity.”
q: You must be gentle, and beware of harshness and obscenity.

title: Abu Rawwad on Ramadan: Supplication to start month of fasting
t: Al-Walid ibn Muslim reported: Abu Rawwad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The Muslims would supplicate at the arrival of Ramadan: O Allah, the month of Ramadan has come. Grant it to me, secure me in it, and accept it from me. O Allah, provide me with its fasting, its standing in prayer patiently and expecting reward, and provide me within it due diligence, effort, strength, and vitality. Protect me within it from weariness, weakness, laziness, and fatigue. Guide me within it to the Night of Decree and make it better for me than a thousand months.”

title: Hadith on Masjid: Allah counted every step as a reward
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: There was a man who lived the furthest from the mosque, as far as I know. He never missed a congregational prayer. It was said to him, “If you buy a donkey, you can ride it during the dark nights and hot days.” The man said, “I do not like for my house to be so close to the mosque. I want my walking towards the mosque, as well as returning to my home and family, to be recorded as good deeds for me.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah has gathered all of that for you.”
q: Allah has gathered all of that for you.

title: Hadith on Istighatha: I cannot help sinners on Judgment Day
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stood up one day and mentioned stealing from the spoils, emphasizing the severity of the matter. The Prophet said, “Let me not find one of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with a growling camel mounted upon his neck and he says, ‘O Messenger of Allah, rescue me!’ Then I will say, ‘I have no power to rescue you, for I already delivered the message.’ Let me not find one of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with a neighing horse mounted upon his neck and he says, ‘O Messenger of Allah, rescue me!’ Then I will say, ‘I have no power to rescue you, for I already delivered the message.’ Let me not find one of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with a bleating sheep mounted upon his neck and he says, ‘O Messenger of Allah, rescue me!’ Then I will say, ‘I have no power to rescue you, for I already delivered the message.’ Let me not find one of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with a crying soul mounted upon his neck and he says, ‘O Messenger of Allah, rescue me!’ Then I will say, ‘I have no power to rescue you, for I already delivered the message.’ Let me not find one of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with fluttering garments mounted upon his neck and he says, ‘O Messenger of Allah, rescue me!’ Then I will say, ‘I have no power to rescue you, for I already delivered the message.’ Let me not find one of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with gold and silver mounted upon his neck and he says, ‘O Messenger of Allah, rescue me!’ Then I will say, ‘I have no power to rescue you, for I already delivered the message.’”
q: Let me not find one of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with a growling camel mounted upon his neck and he says, ‘O Messenger of Allah, rescue me!’ Then I will say, ‘I have no power to rescue you, for I already delivered the message.’ Let me not find one of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with a neighing horse mounted upon his neck and he says, ‘O Messenger of Allah, rescue me!’ Then I will say, ‘I have no power to rescue you, for I already delivered the message.’ Let me not find one of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with a bleating sheep mounted upon his neck and he says, ‘O Messenger of Allah, rescue me!’ Then I will say, ‘I have no power to rescue you, for I already delivered the message.’ Let me not find one of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with a crying soul mounted upon his neck and he says, ‘O Messenger of Allah, rescue me!’ Then I will say, ‘I have no power to rescue you, for I already delivered the message.’ Let me not find one of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with fluttering garments mounted upon his neck and he says, ‘O Messenger of Allah, rescue me!’ Then I will say, ‘I have no power to rescue you, for I already delivered the message.’ Let me not find one of you on the Day of Resurrection coming with gold and silver mounted upon his neck and he says, ‘O Messenger of Allah, rescue me!’ Then I will say, ‘I have no power to rescue you, for I already delivered the message.’
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Medina: Do not take Prophet’s grave as celebration
t: ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn reported: He saw a man coming to the opening by the grave of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he entered it to supplicate. ‘Ali called for him and he said, “Shall I not narrate to you a tradition I heard from my father and my grandfather? The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Do not take my grave as a place of festival, nor take your houses as graves. Send blessings upon me, for your blessings reach me wherever you are.”
q: Do not take my grave as a place of festival, nor take your houses as graves. Send blessings upon me, for your blessings reach me wherever you are

title: Hadith on Shirk: You make me a partner with Allah?
t: Ibn Abbas reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “What Allah wills and what you will.” The Prophet said, “Have you made me a partner with Allah? Rather, what Allah wills alone.”
q: Have you made me a partner with Allah? Rather, what Allah wills alone.

title: Hadith on Siffin: Reconciliation between Ali and Mu’awiyah
t: Yazid ibn al-‘Asamm reported: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about the slain at the battle of Siffin. Ali said, “Our slain and their slain are in Paradise, and the matter will be referred to myself and Mu’awiyah at the Reckoning.”
gf: Sahih (authentic) according to Abu Habib al-Shithri

title: Hadith on Salah: Best deed to pray on time
t: Umm Farwah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked, “Which deeds are best?” The Prophet said, “Prayer at the beginning of its time.”
q: Prayer at the beginning of its time.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on ‘Ilm: Companions seeking the Prophet’s knowledge
t: Safwan ibn ‘Assal reported: I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was reclining in the mosque on his cloak. I said to him, “O Messenger of Allah, I have come to you seeking knowledge.” The Prophet said, “Welcome, seeker of knowledge! The seeker of knowledge is surrounded by the angels and shaded under their wings, then some of them ride upward until they reach the lowest heaven due to their love for what he is seeking. What have you come to learn?” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, we will continue to travel between Mecca and Medina, so what is the ruling on wiping over the socks?” The Prophet said, “It is three days for the traveler, and one day and one night for the resident.”
q: Welcome, seeker of knowledge! The seeker of knowledge is surrounded by the angels and shaded under their wings, then some of them ride upward until they reach the lowest heaven due to their love for what he is seeking. What have you come to learn? … It is three days for the traveler, and one day and one night for the resident.

title: Hadith on Dajjal: The Prophet fears Imams of Misguidance
t: Abu Dharr reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you fear for your nation more than the False Messiah?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Imams of misguidance.”
q: The Imams of misguidance.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Farming: Charity to cultivate a dead land
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever revives a barren land will be rewarded for it. Whatever is eaten from it in good health, he will be rewarded for it.”
q: Whoever revives a barren land will be rewarded for it. Whatever is eaten from it in good health, he will be rewarded for it.

title: Abu Bakr on Ijtihad: If my opinion is right, it is from Allah
t: Ibn Sirin reported: No one after the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was as cautious with what he did not know than Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and no one after Abu Bakr was as cautious with what he did not know than Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. Abu Bakr would be presented with a case for which he found no source in the Book, nor a report in the Sunnah, so he would strive to form an opinion, then he would say, “This is my opinion. If it is correct, it is from Allah. If it is wrong, it is from myself, and I seek forgiveness from Allah.”

title: Hadith on Charity: Spending pairs in the way of Allah
t: Sa’sa’ah ibn Mu’awiyah reported: I met Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, and I said, “Narrate a saying to me.” Abu Dharr said, “Yes. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: No Muslim servant spends a pair of any kind of wealth in the way of Allah but that the keepers of Paradise, all of them, will invite him to what they have.” I said, “How so?” Abu Dharr said, “If it is camels, he spends two camels. If it is cows, he spends two cows.”
q: No Muslim servant spends a pair of any kind of wealth in the way of Allah but that the keepers of Paradise, all of them, will invite him to what they have.

title: Hadith on Humility: The Prophet says, ‘I do not know’
t: Ibn Umar reported: A man asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “Which places are worst?” The Prophet said, “I will not know until I ask Gabriel.” Then he asked Gabriel, and he said, “I will not know until I ask Michael.” Michael came, and he said, “The best places are the mosques, and the worst places are the markets.”
q: I will not know until I ask Gabriel.

title: Hadith on Knowledge: Learning better than voluntary worship
t: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The virtue of knowledge is better than the virtue of worship, and the best of your religion is conscientious piety.”
q: The virtue of knowledge is better than the virtue of worship, and the best of your religion is conscientious piety.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Israiliyyat: Umar brings the Torah
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: When Umar came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, he said, “We have heard wonderous stories from the Jews. Shall we write them down?” The Prophet said, “Will you fall into an abyss like the Jews and Christians? I have come to you with a clear, pure path. If Moses were alive today, he would have no choice but to follow me.”
q: Will you fall into an abyss like the Jews and Christians? I have come to you with a clear, pure path. If Moses were alive today, he would have no choice but to follow me.

title: Hadith on Sunnah: Knowledge preserved by Hadith narrators
t: Ibrahim al-‘Udhri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “This knowledge will be carried in the following centuries by its trustworthy caretakers, refuting the distortions of the ignorant, the excuses of the falsifiers, and the misinterpretations of the exaggerators.”
q: This knowledge will be carried in the following centuries by its trustworthy caretakers, refuting the distortions of the ignorant, the excuses of the falsifiers, and the misinterpretations of the exaggerators.
gf: Sahih (authentic) according to Ahmad ibn Hanbal

title: Hadith on Eyesight: Reward for believers when blinded
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty says: Whoever has his two dear eyes taken away by Me and he patiently awaits his compensation, I am not pleased to reward him with anything except Paradise.”
q: Allah Almighty says: Whoever has his two dear eyes taken away by Me and he patiently awaits his compensation, I am not pleased to reward him with anything except Paradise.

title: Hadith on Strength: The Prophet’s walk displays his vitality
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would walk with such vigor that it would be known he was neither weak, nor lazy.

title: Hadith on Hellfire: The Prophet’s desperate warning to us
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I warn you of the Hellfire! I warn you of the Hellfire!” so loudly that if a man were in the furthest part of the market, he would hear it. The people in the market would hear his voice when he was on the pulpit.
q: I warn you of the Hellfire! I warn you of the Hellfire!

title: Hadith on Haram: Prophet holds us back from the Fire
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has not forbidden any deed but that He knew some of you would commit it. I am surely holding you back from swarming into the Hellfire as if you were moths or flies.”
q: Verily, Allah has not forbidden any deed but that He knew some of you would commit it. I am surely holding you back from swarming into the Hellfire as if you were moths or flies.

title: Hadith on Reciprocity: Reward and supplicate for good-doers
t: Al-Hakim ibn ‘Umayr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever does a good deed for you, then compensate him. If you cannot do so, then pray for him.”
q: Whoever does a good deed for you, then compensate him. If you cannot do so, then pray for him.

title: Hadith on Salat: Prayer washes away your sins
t: Uthman ibn Affan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the five prayers get rid of sins just as water gets rid of dirt.”
q: Verily, the five prayers get rid of sins just as water gets rid of dirt.

title: Hadith on Hawd: Heretics prevented from Prophet’s Fountain
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I am holding you back from the Fire. I say: Beware of Hell! Beware the limits of Allah! When I pass away, I will precede you and meet you at the Fountain. Whoever makes it there has succeeded, but some people will come and be driven to the left side. I will say: O Lord, my nation! It will be said: You do not know what they invented after you, turning away on their heels!”
q: I am holding you back from the Fire. I say: Beware of Hell! Beware the limits of Allah! When I pass away, I will precede you and meet you at the Fountain. Whoever makes it there has succeeded, but some people will come and be driven to the left side. I will say: O Lord, my nation! It will be said: You do not know what they invented after you, turning away on their heels!
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Wills: Warning to be fair with inheritance
t:
Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, a man might act like the people of virtue for seventy years, but he enjoins injustice in his will, sealing his life with evil and entering the Hellfire. Verily, a man might act like the people of vice for seventy years, but he enjoins justice in his will, sealing his life with virtue and entering Paradise.”

Abu Huraira said, “Recite the verse if you wish, ‘Such are the limits of Allah. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will enter gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the greatest victory!’” (4:13)
q: Verily, a man might act like the people of virtue for seventy years, but he enjoins injustice in his will, sealing his life with evil and entering the Hellfire. Verily, a man might act like the people of vice for seventy years, but he enjoins justice in his will, sealing his life with virtue and entering Paradise. … Such are the limits of Allah. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will enter gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the greatest victory!

title: Hadith on Hereafter: People asleep while Afterlife approaches
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have not seen the likes of the Fire by which one sleeps while he should flee from it, nor the likes of the Garden by which one sleeps while he should strive for it.”
q: I have not seen the likes of the Fire by which one sleeps while he should flee from it, nor the likes of the Garden by which one sleeps while he should strive for it.

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: Listening to the Prophet’s night prayer
t: Rabi’ah ibn Ka’b reported: I stayed the night by the door of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to give him water for ablution. I heard him saying throughout the night, “Allah hears those who praise Him,” and I heard him saying, “Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.”
q: Allah hears those who praise Him … Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds

title: Hadith on Precedents: Initiating good or evil practices
t: Abu Juhayfah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever establishes a good practice that is acted upon after him, he will have a reward like the others without decreasing their rewards at all. Whoever establishes an evil practice that is acted upon after him, he will have the burden of sin like the others without decreasing their burdens at all.”
q: Whoever establishes a good practice that is acted upon after him, he will have a reward like the others without decreasing their rewards at all. Whoever establishes an evil practice that is acted upon after him, he will have the burden of sin like the others without decreasing their burdens at all.

title: Hadith on Precedents: Reward or sin of those who follow you
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he encouraged others to give charity to him. One man said, “I have something,” and no man remained in the gathering without giving him some charity, great or small. The Prophet said, “Whoever establishes a good precedent for others will earn its reward completely as well as the rewards of those who followed it, without decreasing any of their rewards at all. Whoever establishes an evil precedent for others will earn its burden of sin completely as well as the burdens of those who followed it, without decreasing any of their burdens at all.”
q: Whoever establishes a good precedent for others will earn its reward completely as well as the rewards of those who followed it, without decreasing any of their rewards at all. Whoever establishes an evil precedent for others will earn its burden of sin completely as well as the burdens of those who followed it, without decreasing any of their burdens at all.

title: Hadith on Muhammad: Love for the Prophet is true faith
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, none of you have faith until I am more beloved to him than his parents and his children.”
q: By the One in whose hand is my soul, none of you have faith until I am more beloved to him than his parents and his children.

title: Hadith on Shahada: Testimony of faith leads to Paradise
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Know that whoever testifies ‘there is no God but Allah’ will enter Paradise.”
q: Know that whoever testifies ‘there is no God but Allah’ will enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Tawhid: ‘Allah is One’ leads to Paradise
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Give glad tidings to the people that whoever declares there is no God but Allah, he will have Paradise.”
q: Give glad tidings to the people that whoever declares there is no God but Allah, he will have Paradise.

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Take not Allah’s promise for granted
t: Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded to announce among the people, “Whoever sincerely testifies there is no God but Allah alone, without any partner, he will have Paradise.” Umar said, “What if they take it for granted?” The Prophet said, “Then leave them be.”
q: Whoever sincerely testifies there is no God but Allah alone, without any partner, he will have Paradise. … Then leave them be.

title: Hadith on Faith: Paradise if believers avoid major sins
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever comes worshiping Allah without associating anything with Him, performing the prayer, giving the charity, and avoiding the major sins, he will have Paradise.” They asked him about the major sins, and the Prophet said, “Idolatry against Allah, taking a Muslim life, and fleeing on the day of battle.”
q: Whoever comes worshiping Allah without associating anything with Him, performing the prayer, giving the charity, and avoiding the major sins, he will have Paradise. … Idolatry against Allah, taking a Muslim life, and fleeing on the day of battle.

title: Hadith on Islam: Must follow Sunnah to be true Muslim
t: Ibn Abbas reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, liberated Mecca, he said, “Verily, Allah Almighty and His Messenger have forbidden wine and its sale for you, and have forbidden carrion and its sale for you, and have forbidden you from eating the flesh of swine or selling it. Trim your mustaches, let your beards grow, and do not walk in the markets unless you are properly clothed. Verily, he is not one of us who acts upon another way from ours.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty and His Messenger have forbidden wine and its sale for you, and have forbidden carrion and its sale for you, and have forbidden you from eating the flesh of swine or selling it. Trim your mustaches, let your beards grow, and do not walk in the markets unless you are properly clothed. Verily, he is not one of us who acts upon another way from ours.

title: Hadith on Jama’ah: Rewards for ablution, then congregation
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you performs ablution in the best manner, then leaves from his house to the mosque, he does not depart but in a state of prayer. His left foot continues to expiate sins, while his right foot earns good deeds until he enters the mosque. If people knew what was contained in the evening and morning prayers, they would surely come even if they had to crawl.”
q: When one of you performs ablution in the best manner, then leaves from his house to the mosque, he does not depart but in a state of prayer. His left foot continues to expiate sins, while his right foot earns good deeds until he enters the mosque. If people knew what was contained in the evening and morning prayers, they would surely come even if they had to crawl.

title: Hadith on Islam: Signposts on the Straight Path
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Islam has milestones, lamps like the lamps on the road. Among them are that you worship Allah without associating anything with Him, you perform the prayer, you give charity, you perform the Hajj pilgrimage to the House, you fast in the month of Ramadan, and you enjoin good and forbid evil. It is your greeting of peace when you enter your household and your greeting of peace to the children of Adam when you meet them. If they return it to you, the angels return it to them. If they do not return it, the angels return it to you, or curse them, or stay silent over them. Whoever belittles any of these, it is a sign of Islam he has abandoned. Whoever casts them all aside has thrown Islam behind his back.”
q: Verily, Islam has milestones, lamps like the lamps on the road. Among them are that you worship Allah without associating anything with Him, you perform the prayer, you give charity, you perform the Hajj pilgrimage to the House, you fast in the month of Ramadan, and you enjoin good and forbid evil. It is your greeting of peace when you enter your household and your greeting of peace to the children of Adam when you meet them. If they return it to you, the angels return it to them. If they do not return it, the angels return it to you, or curse them, or stay silent over them. Whoever belittles any of these, it is a sign of Islam he has abandoned. Whoever casts them all aside has thrown Islam behind his back.

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Glad tidings for true monotheists
t: Zayd ibn Khalid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent me forth, saying, “Give glad tidings to the people that whoever declares there is no God but Allah alone, without any partners, he will have Paradise.”
q: Give glad tidings to the people that whoever declares there is no God but Allah alone, without any partners, he will have Paradise.

title: Hadith on Kufr: Warning against ingratitude for gifts
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever receives a donation and mentions it has shown gratitude, but if he hides it, he has been ungrateful.”
q: Whoever receives a donation and mentions it has shown gratitude, but if he hides it, he has been ungrateful.

title: Hadith on Da’wah: Guidance to Islam better than whole world
t: Abu Rafi’ reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “For Allah to guide a man by your hand is better for you than everything over which the sun rises and sets.”
q: For Allah to guide a man by your hand is better for you than everything over which the sun rises and sets.

title: Hadith on Tawhid: It reaches the Throne if major sins avoided
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Never does a servant sincerely say, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ but that the gates of heaven open for it, even leading to the Throne itself, as long as he avoids major sins.”
q: Never does a servant sincerely say, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ but that the gates of heaven open for it, even leading to the Throne itself, as long as he avoids major sins.

title: Hadith on Striving: Believer keeps working until agonies of death
t: Buraydah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believer dies with sweat upon his brow.”
q: The believer dies with sweat upon his brow.

title: Hadith on Friendliness: Believers are good mannered and kind
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believer is friendly, for there is no good in one who is not friendly or befriended.”
q: The believer is friendly, for there is no good in one who is not friendly or befriended.

title: Hadith on Iman: No faith in adulterer, thief, drunkard, or killer
t:
Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The servant does not commit adultery while he is a believer. He does not steal while he is a believer. He does not drink wine while he is a believer. He does not murder while he is a believer.”

‘Ikramah said, “I said to Ibn Abbas: How is faith taken from him?” Ibn Abbas said, “Like so,” and he clasped his fingers together and separated them, “If he repents, it returns like so,” and he clasped his fingers together.
q: The servant does not commit adultery while he is a believer. He does not steal while he is a believer. He does not drink wine while he is a believer. He does not murder while he is a believer.

title: Hadith on Gheerah: Allah and believers have honor
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believer has a sense of honor, and Allah has an even greater sense of honor.”
q: The believer has a sense of honor, and Allah has an even greater sense of honor.

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: Believers are mirrors of each other
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believer is the mirror of another believer.”
q: The believer is the mirror of another believer.

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Practicing Sunnah like holding a hot ember
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One holding fast to my Sunnah while my nation is in conflict is like one grasping a hot coal.”
q: One holding fast to my Sunnah while my nation is in conflict is like one grasping a hot coal.

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet straightens their prayer rows
t: Abu Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to touch our shoulders in the prayer rows, saying, “Be straight and not disjointed, lest your hearts conflict. Let the people of wisdom and prudence be next to me, then those after them, then those after them.” Abu Mas’ud said, “Yet, today you have become most severe in conflict.”
q: Be straight and not disjointed, lest your hearts conflict. Let the people of wisdom and prudence be next to me, then those after them, then those after them

title: Hadith on Salat: Angels bless the front prayer rows
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to pass through the prayer rows from one side to the other, setting their chests and shoulders in order. The Prophet would say, “Let not your hearts conflict,” and the Prophet would say, “Verily, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the first rows.”
q: Let not your hearts conflict … Verily, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the first rows.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Doubt: Ask the scholars, if you can find them
t: Abu Wa’il reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, one of you will remain good as long as he fears Allah. If you find doubt within yourself about something, ask a man to cure you from it, but soon you will not be able to find such a person.”

title: Hadith on Sunnah: Hold fast to Ahl al-Bayt
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, during Hajj on the day of Arafat while he was riding his camel, Qaswa. I heard the Prophet address them, “O people! Verily, I have left with you what will never lead you astray as long as you hold onto them: the Book of Allah, my family, and the people of my household.”
q: O people! Verily, I have left with you what will never lead you astray as long as you hold onto them: the Book of Allah, my family, and the people of my household.

title: Hadith on Intimidation: Angels curse threatening Muslims
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever points an iron weapon at his brother, the angels surely curse him until he backs down, even if they were brothers from the same parents.”
q: Whoever points an iron weapon at his brother, the angels surely curse him until he backs down, even if they were brothers from the same parents.

title: Hadith on Employees: Pay workers fairly in a timely manner
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Pay the worker his wages before the sweat dries from his brow, and inform him of his wages as he is working.”
q: Pay the worker his wages before the sweat dries from his brow, and inform him of his wages as he is working
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Wealth: What is better than gold and silver?
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Destruction is in gold and silver coins.” Umar said, “O Messenger of Allah, you said destruction is in gold and silver coins, so what do you instruct us or what should we work for?” The Prophet said, “A tongue of remembrance, a grateful heart, and a spouse to help you with your Hereafter.”
q: Destruction is in gold and silver coins. … A tongue of remembrance, a grateful heart, and a spouse to help you with your Hereafter.

title: Al-Qasim on Pictures: Concession to hang menial images, but not honor them
t: Ibn ‘Awn reported: I entered the home of Al-Qasim, may Allah be pleased with him, at the upper part of Mecca in his house, and I saw a canopy inside with pictures of a beaver and a phoenix.

title: Hadith on Punishment: Believers punished in world, sinners in Hereafter
t: Abdullah ibn Mughaffal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If Allah wills to bless a servant, He hastens the punishment for his sins. If Allah wills to harm a servant, He withholds the punishment for his sins until he is brought forth on the Day of Resurrection as if he were a wild ass.”
q: If Allah wills to bless a servant, He hastens the punishment for his sins. If Allah wills to harm a servant, He withholds the punishment for his sins until he is brought forth on the Day of Resurrection as if he were a wild ass.

title: Abu Darda on Muslims: We know who is wicked or righteous
t: Jubayr ibn Nufayr reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say about people, “We know you better than a veterinarian knows his animals. We surely know the best of you from the worst of you. As for the best of you, goodness is expected from them and you feel safe from their evil. As for the worst of you, goodness is not expected from them, none are safe from their evil, and they do not emancipate slaves.”

title: Hadith on Nasihah: Allah pleased with sincere advice to rulers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is pleased with three things for you, and He is displeased with three things for you. He is pleased for you to worship Him without associating anything with Him, to hold fast to the rope of Allah altogether, and to give sincere advice to those in charge of your affairs. He is displeased for you to gossip, to waste wealth, and to ask many frivolous questions.”
q: Verily, Allah is pleased with three things for you, and He is displeased with three things for you. He is pleased for you to worship Him without associating anything with Him, to hold fast to the rope of Allah altogether, and to give sincere advice to those in charge of your affairs. He is displeased for you to gossip, to waste wealth, and to ask many frivolous questions.

title: Hadith on Manliness: Slow to be angry, fast to reconcile
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the best of men are slow to anger and quick to be appeased, and the most evil of men are quick to anger and slow to be appeased.”
q: Verily, the best of men are slow to anger and quick to be appeased, and the most evil of men are quick to anger and slow to be appeased

title: Hadith on Celebrity: Wealth and status dangerous like wolves
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two ferocious wolves in a pen of sheep, devouring and destroying, are not as harmful than the love of high status and wealth are to the religion of a Muslim.”
q: Two ferocious wolves in a pen of sheep, devouring and destroying, are not as harmful than the love of high status and wealth are to the religion of a Muslim

title: Hadith on Sneezing: Praise Allah in all situations
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you sneezes, let him say: All praise is due to Allah in every circumstance. Let those respond to him by saying: May Allah have mercy upon you. Let him respond to them by saying: May Allah guide you and amend your affairs.”
q: When one of you sneezes, let him say: All praise is due to Allah in every circumstance. Let those respond to him by saying: May Allah have mercy upon you. Let him respond to them by saying: May Allah guide you and amend your affairs.

title: Hadith on Optimism: The Prophet loves words of optimism
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I am delighted by optimism, the good word, the kind word.”
q: I am delighted by optimism, the good word, the kind word.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Cleansed of minor sins by ablution
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a Muslim man performs ablution, his sins are removed from his hearing, his sight, his hands, and his legs. If he sits down, he will sit down forgiven.”
q: When a Muslim man performs ablution, his sins are removed from his hearing, his sight, his hands, and his legs. If he sits down, he will sit down forgiven.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Books: Recommendation to write down knowledge
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Bind the knowledge.” I said, “How to bind it?” The Prophet said, “Books.”
q: Bind the knowledge. … Books
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Purity: Allah is clean and loves cleanliness
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah is pure and He loves purity, He is clean and He loves cleanliness, He is noble and He loves nobility, and He is generous and He loves generosity, so clean your homes.”
q: Allah is pure and He loves purity, He is clean and He loves cleanliness, He is noble and He loves nobility, and He is generous and He loves generosity, so clean your homes.

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Noble status of sincere monotheism
t: ‘Iyad al-Ansari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the declaration, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ has a noble status with Allah. It is a word that whoever says it honestly, Allah will admit him into Paradise. Whoever says it falsely, his life is protected and his property is safeguarded, but He will meet Allah tomorrow to be held accountable.”
q: Verily, the declaration, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ has a noble status with Allah. It is a word that whoever says it honestly, Allah will admit him into Paradise. Whoever says it falsely, his life is protected and his property is safeguarded, but He will meet Allah tomorrow to be held accountable.

title: Hadith on Salvation: Believers saved from touch of Hellfire
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The arrival of the Hellfire, neither the righteous nor the wicked will be spared from passing through it, but it will be cool and peaceful for the believers just as it was for Abraham, until even the fires of Hell will clamor due to its coolness. Then, Allah ‘will save those who feared Him and bring the wrongdoers to their knees therein’ (19:72).”
q: The arrival of the Hellfire, neither the righteous nor the wicked will be spared from passing through it, but it will be cool and peaceful for the believers just as it was for Abraham, until even the fires of Hell will clamor due to its coolness. Then, Allah ‘will save those who feared Him and bring the wrongdoers to their knees therein’

title: Hadith on Shirk: Lesser idolatry to love injustice, hate justice
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Idolatry is more hidden in my nation than an ant crawling over a smooth rock in the dark of night, the least of which is to love something unjust or to hate something just. Is the religion not but to love for the sake of Allah and hate for the sake of Allah? Allah said, ‘Say: If you love Allah, follow me and He will love you’ (3:31).”
q: Idolatry is more hidden in my nation than an ant crawling over a smooth rock in the dark of night, the least of which is to love something unjust or to hate something just. Is the religion not but to love for the sake of Allah and hate for the sake of Allah? Allah said, ‘Say: If you love Allah, follow me and He will love you’

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Insincere testimony of faith rejected
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The declaration of ‘there is no God but Allah’ protects the servants from the displeasure of Allah as long as they do not prefer the promise of their worldly life over their religion, for if they prefer the promise of their worldly life over their religion and then say, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ it will be rejected from them, and Allah Almighty will say, ‘You have lied!’”
q: The declaration of ‘there is no God but Allah’ protects the servants from the displeasure of Allah as long as they do not prefer the promise of their worldly life over their religion, for if they prefer the promise of their worldly life over their religion and then say, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ it will be rejected from them, and Allah Almighty will say, ‘You have lied!’

title: Ibn Sireen on Conscience: Allah makes his heart admonish him
t: Habib reported: Ibn Sirin, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If Allah wills good for a servant, He appoints a preacher from his heart to command and prohibit him.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Seek refuge from harming another Muslim
t: Abu Rashid reported: I came to Abdullah ibn Amr, and I said, “Narrate to me what you have heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.” Abdullah set out a scroll, and he said, “This is what the Messenger of Allah has written for me.” I saw on it that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me what to say when I enter morning and evening.” The Prophet said, “O Abu Bakr! Say: O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the seen and unseen, there is no God but You, Lord and Sovereign of all things. I seek refuge in You from the evil in myself, the evil of Satan and his idolatry, and that I perpetrate evil upon myself or bring it upon another Muslim.”
q: O Abu Bakr! Say: O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the seen and unseen, there is no God but You, Lord and Sovereign of all things. I seek refuge in You from the evil in myself, the evil of Satan and his idolatry, and that I perpetrate evil upon myself or bring it upon another Muslim.

title: Hadith on Sawm: Lies and backbiting damage shield of fasting
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Fasting is a shield as long as you do not damage it.” It was said, “How does one damage it?” The Prophet said, “By dishonesty or backbiting.”
q: Fasting is a shield as long as you do not damage it. … By dishonesty or backbiting.

title: Hadith on Sickness: Expiation of sins for enduring illness
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when the Muslim falls ill, Allah Almighty inspires the angels, saying: O angels, I have detained My servant with My confinement. If I take his soul, he will be forgiven. If I heal his body, he will be forgiven as if he had no sins.”
q: Verily, when the Muslim falls ill, Allah Almighty inspires the angels, saying: O angels, I have detained My servant with My confinement. If I take his soul, he will be forgiven. If I heal his body, he will be forgiven as if he had no sins.

title: Salaf on Nifaq: Companions fear they will become hypocrites
t: Al-Bukhari reported: Ibn Abi Mulaykah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I met thirty companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and each one of them feared hypocrisy for himself. None of them said they had faith like the Angel Gabriel or the Angel Michael.”

title: Hadith on Trials: Signs of the Hour like beads on a thread
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The signs of the Hour will emerge in quick succession, one after another, just like the beads of a string.”
q: The signs of the Hour will emerge in quick succession, one after another, just like the beads of a string.

title: Hadith on Dua: Be ambitious in our supplications
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you asks from his Lord, let him ask for even more. Verily, he is asking from his Lord Almighty.”
q: When one of you asks from his Lord, let him ask for even more. Verily, he is asking from his Lord Almighty

title: Salaf on Moderation: Devil pleased with either extremism or leniency
t: Sa’id ibn Dawud reported: Makhlad ibn al-Husyan, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Allah never recommends something to His servants but that Satan interferes with it in one of two ways. He does not care which of them succeeds. Either he makes them exaggerate in it, or he makes them belittle it.”

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Best remembrance of Allah by day and night
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, once passed by him while he was moving his lips. The Prophet said, “O Abu Umamah, what are you saying?” Abu Umamah said, “I am remembering my Lord.” The Prophet said, “Shall I not tell you what is the greatest and best of your remembrance by night and day, and by day and night? It is that you say: Glory be to Allah by the number of what He created. Glory be to Allah by the fill of what He has created. Glory be to Allah by the number on the earth and in the heavens. Glory be to Allah by the fill of the earth and the heavens. Glory be to Allah by the number He counted in His book. Glory be to Allah by the number of all things. Glory be to Allah by the fill of all things. And that you say: All praise be to Allah likewise.”
q: O Abu Umamah, what are you saying? … Shall I not tell you what is the greatest and best of your remembrance by night and day, and by day and night? It is that you say: Glory be to Allah by the number of what He created. Glory be to Allah by the fill of what He has created. Glory be to Allah by the number on the earth and in the heavens. Glory be to Allah by the fill of the earth and the heavens. Glory be to Allah by the number He counted in His book. Glory be to Allah by the number of all things. Glory be to Allah by the fill of all things. And that you say: All praise be to Allah likewise.

title: Hadith on Muhammad: The Prophet leads humanity on Judgment Day
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and it is no boast. The banner of praise will be placed in my hand, and it is no boast. There is no Prophet from the time of Adam or otherwise but that he is under my banner. I am the first for whom the earth will cleft open, and it is no boast.”
q: I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and it is no boast. The banner of praise will be placed in my hand, and it is no boast. There is no Prophet from the time of Adam or otherwise but that he is under my banner. I am the first for whom the earth will cleft open, and it is no boast.

title: Hadith on Cruelty: Woman enters Hell for torturing a cat
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A woman entered the Hellfire because of a cat or kitten she had imprisoned. She did not let it eat, nor release it to eat the vermin of the earth, until it died emaciated.”
q: A woman entered the Hellfire because of a cat or kitten she had imprisoned. She did not let it eat, nor release it to eat the vermin of the earth, until it died emaciated.

title: Hadith on Cruelty: Prohibition of branding and striking the face
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by an animal who had been branded on the face and its nostrils were smoking. The Prophet said, “Allah has cursed whoever has done this. Do not brand anyone on the face, nor strike it.”
q: Allah has cursed whoever has done this. Do not brand anyone on the face, nor strike it.

title: Hadith on Siesta: Take a midday nap, unlike Shaytan
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Take a siesta, for Satan does not sleep in the midday.”
q: Take a siesta, for Satan does not sleep in the midday.

title: Hadith on Kaba’ir: Avoid major sins, share good news of Islam
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Avoid the major sins, follow the right course, and give glad tidings.”
q: Avoid the major sins, follow the right course, and give glad tidings.

title: Hadith on Silence: Allah has mercy on those who speak no evil
t: Khalid ibn Abi ‘Imran reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would hold his tongue for a long time. Then, the Prophet said, “I fear for you because of this. May Allah have mercy on a servant who speaks goodness and is rewarded, or he refrains from speaking evil and is safe.”
q: I fear for you because of this. May Allah have mercy on a servant who speaks goodness and is rewarded, or he refrains from speaking evil and is safe.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Fahsha: Allah does not love vulgarity and obscenity
t: Usamah ibn Zayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah does not love anyone vulgar and obscene.”
q: Verily, Allah does not love anyone vulgar and obscene.

title: Hadith on Salaam: Spread peace, do not be impudent
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Spread peace and you will be safe. Impudence is evil!” Abu Mu’awiyah said, “Impudence is frivolity.”
q: Spread peace and you will be safe. Impudence is evil!

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: All Muslims are brothers to another
t: Suwayd ibn Hanzalah reported: We went out intending to meet the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and with us was Wa’il ibn Hujr. Then, one of his enemies seized him, and the people resisted swearing an oath, but I swore an oath, saying, “He is my brother!” They let him go on his way, and we came to the Messenger of Allah. I told him that the people resisted swearing an oath, but I swore an oath that he was my brother. The Prophet said, “You spoke the truth. The Muslim is the brother of another Muslim.”
q: You spoke the truth. The Muslim is the brother of another Muslim.

title: Hadith on Vanity: Proud man sinking into earth until Judgment Day
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man among those before you went out haughtily in his fine garment, so Allah ordered the earth to seize him. He is sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection.”
q: A man among those before you went out haughtily in his fine garment, so Allah ordered the earth to seize him. He is sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection

title: Hadith on Kibr: Hellfire full of arrogant, miserly people
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said upon mention of the inhabitants of Hellfire, “It is everyone cruel, haughty, arrogant, a hoarder of possessions, and a withholder of good.”
q: It is everyone cruel, haughty, arrogant, a hoarder of possessions, and a withholder of good.

title: Hadith on Kibr: Religious leaders slaughtered by their arrogance
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of these slaughterhouses,” meaning the inner sanctums.
q: Beware of these slaughterhouses,
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Shawkani

title: Hadith on Cursing: I advise you not to curse others
t: Jurmuz al-Hujaymi reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, advise me.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I advise you not to curse others.”
q: I advise you not to curse others.

title: Hadith on Cursing: The Prophet not sent to invoke curses
t: Kariz ibn Samah reported: He was part of a delegation sent to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and it was said, “O Messenger of Allah, pray against the tribe of ‘Amir.” The Prophet said, “I was not sent to invoke curses.”
q: I was not sent to invoke curses.

title: Hadith on Cursing: Companions fear a wrongful curse backfiring
t: Abu ‘Umayr reported: He was friends with Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and Ibn Mas’ud visited his household but did not find him, so he sought permission to enter, greeted them with peace, and requested a drink. They dispatched a servant girl to bring him a drink from the neighbors, but she was slow to return. The people cursed her, so Ibn Mas’ud left them. Abu ‘Umayr came after him, and he said, “O Abu Abdur Rahman, no one makes a foray like you! Would that you greet my brother’s people, sit with them, and let them pour you a drink?” Ibn Mas’ud said, “I had done so. They sent the servant, but she was slow to return so they cursed her. I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: Verily, when a curse is directed at its target, it either strikes it on the way or finds another path, or else it says, ‘O Lord, I was directed at such a person, but I did not find a way or another path.’ It will be said to it, ‘Return from where you came.’” Ibn Mas’ud continued, “I was afraid that the servant had an excuse, then the curse would return to its people, and it would be my fault.”
q: Verily, when a curse is directed at its target, it either strikes it on the way or finds another path, or else it says, ‘O Lord, I was directed at such a person, but I did not find a way or another path.’ It will be said to it, ‘Return from where you came.’

title: Hadith on Anger: Honor in the Hereafter for suppressing rage
t: Mu’adh ibn Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever suppresses his rage, even though he could unleash it, Allah will summon him on the Day of Resurrection before the heads of all creation to choose whichever maiden he wishes.”
q: Whoever suppresses his rage, even though he could unleash it, Allah will summon him on the Day of Resurrection before the heads of all creation to choose whichever maiden he wishes.

title: Hadith on Ummah: Muhammad’s nation a majority in Paradise
t: Buraydah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people of Paradise are lined up in one hundred and twenty rows. Eighty of them are from this nation, and forty are from the rest of the nations.”
q: The people of Paradise are lined up in one hundred and twenty rows. Eighty of them are from this nation, and forty are from the rest of the nations.

title: Hadith on Tashahhud: Testifying to faith in prayer and in need
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, taught us to bear witness to faith in prayer and to bear witness to faith in times of need. Bearing witness in prayer is to say, “Greetings are for Allah, as are prayers and pure things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I testify there is no God but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger.” Bearing witness in times of need is to say, “Verily, all praise is due to Allah. We seek His help and His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Him from the evil of our own selves and our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, there is none to lead him astray. Whomever Allah leads astray, there is none to guide him. I testify there is no God but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger.”
q: Greetings are for Allah, as are prayers and pure things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I testify there is no God but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger. … Verily, all praise is due to Allah. We seek His help and His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Him from the evil of our own selves and our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, there is none to lead him astray. Whomever Allah leads astray, there is none to guide him. I testify there is no God but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger.

title: Jesus on Paradise: Store up your treasures in heaven
t: Ibrahim al-Taymi reported: Jesus, upon him be peace, said, “Place your treasures in heaven, for the heart of a man is with his treasure.”

title: Hadith on Ummah: Allah tells Jesus about Muhammad’s nation
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: O Jesus, I will raise a nation after you who will praise Me and be grateful to Me when I bestow what they love, and they will expect reward and be patient when I afflict them with what they hate, although they had no forbearance or knowledge. Jesus said: O Lord, how can this be if they had no forbearance or knowledge? Allah said: I will give them from My forbearance and My knowledge.”
q: Allah Almighty said: O Jesus, I will raise a nation after you who will praise Me and be grateful to Me when I bestow what they love, and they will expect reward and be patient when I afflict them with what they hate, although they had no forbearance or knowledge. Jesus said: O Lord, how can this be if they had no forbearance or knowledge? Allah said: I will give them from My forbearance and My knowledge.

title: Hadith on Heraclius: Roman emperor rejects Islam, fearing his army
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Who will depart with this letter of mine to Caesar and thus he will have Paradise?” A man among the people said, “Even if I am not killed?” The Prophet said, “Even if you are not killed.” The man departed with it and met Caesar as he came to the Sacred House. When Caesar finished the letter, he took it and summoned the heads of the priesthood. He read it and commanded the palace doors to be locked, and then he commanded someone to announce, “Caesar has surely followed Muhammad and abandoned Christianity!” His soldiers confronted him with arms until they surrounded his palace. Caesar said of the Messenger of Allah, “Do you see I am fearful of my kingdom?” Then, he commanded someone to announce, “Surely, Caesar is pleased with you, for he only told you that he might examine how perseverant you are in your religion, so turn back!” The soldiers withdrew, and Caesar wrote to the Messenger of Allah, saying, “Indeed, I am a Muslim,” and he sent him some gold coins. When he read the letter, the Prophet said, “The enemy of Allah has lied. He is not a Muslim, but he is upon Christianity.”
q: Who will depart with this letter of mine to Caesar and thus he will have Paradise? … Even if you are not killed. … The enemy of Allah has lied. He is not a Muslim, but he is upon Christianity.

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: The Prophet seeks refuge from evil character
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would supplicate, saying, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from discord, hypocrisy, and evil character.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from discord, hypocrisy, and evil character.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Dua: Refuge in Allah from all kinds of evil
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would say in his supplications, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disability and sloth, cowardice and senility, hardness of heart and negligence, dependence and humiliation and misery. I seek refuge in You from poverty and unbelief, wickedness and discord, hypocrisy and fame-seeking and ostentation. I seek refuge in You from deafness and dumbness, insanity and contagion, leprosy and evil ailments.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disability and sloth, cowardice and senility, hardness of heart and negligence, dependence and humiliation and misery. I seek refuge in You from poverty and unbelief, wickedness and discord, hypocrisy and fame-seeking and ostentation. I seek refuge in You from deafness and dumbness, insanity and contagion, leprosy and evil ailments.

title: Hadith on Shuhada: Martyrs of Allah entrusted with creation’s welfare
t: Abu ‘Inabah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the martyrs of Allah on the earth are the trustees of Allah on earth among His creation. They are killed, or they die.”
q: Verily, the martyrs of Allah on the earth are the trustees of Allah on earth among His creation. They are killed, or they die.

title: Hadith on Ruqyah: Calling upon Allah alone to remove pain
t: Abd al-Aziz reported: Thabit and I entered the home of Anas ibn Malik, and Thabit said, “O Abu Hamzah, I am complaining of pain.” Anas said, “Shall I not invoke over you with the incantation of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him?” Thabit said, “Of course.” Anas said, “O Allah, the Lord of the people, the Banisher of pain, heal it for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no trace of illness.”

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet calls upon Allah for the ill
t: Ali reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say when he visited the sick, “Take away the pain, O Lord of the people, and heal it, for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no trace of illness.”
q: Take away the pain, O Lord of the people, and heal it, for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no trace of illness.

title: Hadith on Ruqyah: No healing without Allah’s power
t: Ibn al-Sa’ib reported: Maymunah said to him, “O my nephew, shall I not invoke over you with the incantation of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him?” I said, “Of course.” Maymunah said, “In the name of Allah I invoke over you. May Allah heal you from every ailment. Take away the pain, O Lord of the people, and heal it for You are the Healer. There is no healing without You.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Dua: Calling upon Allah, Al-Shafi, for healing
t: Muhammad ibn Hatib reported: A boiling pot was spilled on my hand, so my mother went with me to the residence of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet spoke these words over it, “Take away the pain, O Lord of the people. Heal it, for You are the Healer.”
q: Take away the pain, O Lord of the people. Heal it, for You are the Healer.

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Moral degeneracy to precede the Hour
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the Hour will not be established until obscenity and miserliness prevail, the trustworthy are discredited, the treacherous are trusted, the mountain goats are destroyed, and the underlings ascend.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, who are the mountain goats and the underlings?” The Prophet said, “The mountain goats are the distinguished people and the most noble of them. The underlings are beneath people’s feet and unknown to them.”
q: By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the Hour will not be established until obscenity and miserliness prevail, the trustworthy are discredited, the treacherous are trusted, the mountain goats are destroyed, and the underlings ascend. … The mountain goats are the distinguished people and the most noble of them. The underlings are beneath people’s feet and unknown to them.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Umar on Bid’ah: Warning against innovated worship
t: Al-Ma’mur ibn Suwayd reported: We were with Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, between Mecca and Medina, and we performed the dawn prayer. Then, he saw people descending to pray in a mosque. Umar asked about them, and they said, “It is a mosque in which the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, performed prayer.” Umar said, “Verily, those before you were destroyed for taking the footprints of their Prophets as a transaction! Whoever passes by any mosque while it is time to pray, let him pray there, or if not, let him move on.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Allah eases our sadness as He wills
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, nothing is easy but what You make easy, for You ease the grief of whomever You will.”
q: O Allah, nothing is easy but what You make easy, for You ease the grief of whomever You will.

title: Hadith on Salah: No voluntary prayers after Fajr and ‘Asr
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no prayer after the morning prayer until the sun has risen, and there is no prayer after the afternoon prayer until the sun has set.”
q: There is no prayer after the morning prayer until the sun has risen, and there is no prayer after the afternoon prayer until the sun has set.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salah: Warning against missing congregational ‘Asr prayer
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever misses the afternoon prayer, it is as if he had lost his family and his property.”
q: Whoever misses the afternoon prayer, it is as if he had lost his family and his property.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet prays sitting down
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, did not pass away until most of his prayers were performed sitting down, except for the obligatory prayers.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Salat: Performing make-up prayers after ‘Asr
t: Aisha reported: By the One who took the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, he never left praying two missed cycles after the afternoon prayer until he met Allah Almighty, even when prayer became difficult for him. He used to perform many of his prayers while sitting down. The Prophet would perform them at home and not in the mosque, fearing it would be heavy upon his nation as he loved for matters to be lightened for them.

title: Umar on Abu Bakr: He was our master, the best of us
t: Aisha reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Abu Bakr was the most beloved of us to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, as he was the best of us and our master.”

title: Hadith on Disasters: Death and earthquakes just before the Hour
t: Salamah ibn Nufayl reported: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, as a man said, “O Messenger of Allah, were you given food from the heavens?” The Prophet said, “Yes.” The man said, “And with what?” The Prophet said, “A cooking pot.” The man said, “Did you have any leftovers?” The Prophet said, “Yes.” The man said, “What was done with it?” The Prophet said, “It was taken up as it was revealed to me that I will soon be buried, not to remain with you, and you will not remain after me but for a short time. Rather, you will remain until you say, ‘He has died.’ There will be factions annihilating each other and right before the Hour, there will be a great amount of death, followed by years of earthquakes.”
q: Yes … A cooking pot … Yes … It was taken up as it was revealed to me that I will soon be buried, not to remain with you, and you will not remain after me but for a short time. Rather, you will remain until you say, ‘He has died.’ There will be factions annihilating each other and right before the Hour, there will be a great amount of death, followed by years of earthquakes.

title: Ahmad on Dunya: The Great Imam never speaks of worldly matters
t: Abu Dawud al-Sijistani reported: The circle of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him, was a circle of the Hereafter, as he would not mention the affairs of the world therein. I never once saw Ahmad ibn Hanbal mentioning the world.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Golden combs and aloe incense in Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The combs of the people of Paradise are made of gold, and their censers are full of aloe vera.”
q: The combs of the people of Paradise are made of gold, and their censers are full of aloe vera.

title: Umar on Ummah: Best nation must adhere to its conditions
t: Qatadah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, saw some people with bad form during the Hajj pilgrimage, and he recited this verse, “You are the best nation produced for humanity. You enjoin good, you forbid evil, and you believe in Allah,” (3:110). Then, Umar said, “O people, whoever is pleased to be part of this nation, let him fulfill the conditions of Allah for it!”
q: You are the best nation produced for humanity. You enjoin good, you forbid evil, and you believe in Allah

title: Hadith on Qadr: Allah facilitates deeds for the final destination
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: A man asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, upon what shall we act? Are things already gone and past, or are they happening now?” The Prophet said, “Verily, the people of Paradise are facilitated for the deeds of Paradise, and the people of Hellfire are facilitated for the deeds of Hellfire.”
q: Verily, the people of Paradise are facilitated for the deeds of Paradise, and the people of Hellfire are facilitated for the deeds of Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Qadr: Righteous and wicked facilitated for their fate
t: Hisham ibn Hakim reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, shall we start acting or has fate already been decreed?” The Prophet said, “Verily, Allah Almighty took the progeny of Adam from their backs and made them bear witness against themselves. Then, He announced to them in His palms, saying: These are in Paradise, and these are in Hellfire. Thus, the people of Paradise are facilitated for the deeds of Paradise, and the people of Hellfire are facilitated for the deeds of Hellfire.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty took the progeny of Adam from their backs and made them bear witness against themselves. Then, He announced to them in His palms, saying: These are in Paradise, and these are in Hellfire. Thus, the people of Paradise are facilitated for the deeds of Paradise, and the people of Hellfire are facilitated for the deeds of Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Jama’ah: Reward for intending congregational prayer, even if missed
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever performs ablution in the best manner, then sets out but finds that the people had already prayed, then Allah Almighty will give him the reward of its prayer and its attendance without detracting from their reward at all.”
q: Whoever performs ablution in the best manner, then sets out but finds that the people had already prayed, then Allah Almighty will give him the reward of its prayer and its attendance without detracting from their reward at all.

title: Hadith on Masajid: Mecca, Jerusalem, then earth
t: Abu Dharr reported: I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about the first mosque placed on the earth. The Prophet said, “It was the Sacred Mosque.” I asked, “Then which one?” The Prophet said, “The furthest mosque in Jerusalem.” I said, “How long was between them?” The Prophet said, “Forty years, then the earth was made a mosque for you. Wherever the time for prayer reaches you, then pray there.”
q: It was the Sacred Mosque. … The furthest mosque in Jerusalem. … Forty years, then the earth was made a mosque for you. Wherever the time for prayer reaches you, then pray there.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Zubayr on Sincerity: Keep some of your good deeds private
t: Qays reported: Al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever among you can keep some of his good deeds hidden, let him do so.”

title: Hadith on Jumu’ah: Special hour of prayer on Friday
t: Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The day of Friday is made of twelve hours. No Muslim finds himself supplicating to Allah Almighty during one of them but that Allah will give it to him. Thus, seek it out in the last hour after the afternoon prayer.”
q: The day of Friday is made of twelve hours. No Muslim finds himself supplicating to Allah Almighty during one of them but that Allah will give it to him. Thus, seek it out in the last hour after the afternoon prayer.

title: Hadith on Quran: Last two verses of al-Baqarah from the Throne
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have been given these last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah from the treasures beneath the Throne. No prophet has been given the likes of them before me.”
q: I have been given these last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah from the treasures beneath the Throne. No prophet has been given the likes of them before me.

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: Allah slowly comes close during the night
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty slowly draws near until the first half of the night has passed. Then, He orders a heavenly caller to say: Is anyone calling out that he may be answered? Is anyone seeking forgiveness that he may be forgiven? Is anyone asking that he may be given?”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty slowly draws near until the first half of the night has passed. Then, He orders a heavenly caller to say: Is anyone calling out that he may be answered? Is anyone seeking forgiveness that he may be forgiven? Is anyone asking that he may be given?

title: Hadith on Funerals: Cries of the dead as they are carried away
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the body is placed in the bier, and men carry it on their shoulders, if the deceased was a righteous man, he says, ‘Go with me!’ If the deceased was something else, he says to his people, ‘Woe to it! Where are you taking me?’ Everything but human beings hears his voice. If someone had heard it, he would faint.”
q: When the body is placed in the bier, and men carry it on their shoulders, if the deceased was a righteous man, he says, ‘Go with me!’ If the deceased was something else, he says to his people, ‘Woe to it! Where are you taking me?’ Everything but human beings hears his voice. If someone had heard it, he would faint.

title: Hadith on Funerals: Abu Huraira requests a swift, modest procession
t: ‘Abdur Rahman ibn Mihran reported: When death approached Abu Huraira, he said, “Do not set up a special canopy over me and do not follow me with burning incense. Carry me quickly, for I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: When a righteous man is placed in his coffin, he says, ‘Go with me! Go with me!’ but when an evil man is placed in his coffin, he says, ‘Woe to him! Where are you taking me?’”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Worship: Until a prostration is greater than the world
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hour will not be established until a single prostration is better than the world and everything in it.”
q: The Hour will not be established until a single prostration is better than the world and everything in it.

title: Hadith on Virtues: Quran, Taqwa, enjoining good, and family
t: Dhurrah bint Abi Lahab reported: A man stood for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was upon the pulpit, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, who among people are best?” The Prophet said, “The best of people are the most to recite the Quran, the most fearful of Allah, the most enjoining of good, the most forbidding of evil, and the most to maintain family relations.”
q: The best of people are the most to recite the Quran, the most fearful of Allah, the most enjoining of good, the most forbidding of evil, and the most to maintain family relations.

title: Hadith on Luxury: Warning against extravagant decorations
t: Safinah reported: A man prepared food for Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who was his guest. Fatimah said, “If only we had invited the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, to eat with us!” They called for him, and he came, then he placed his hands on the door frame. When the Prophet saw the engraved curtain in the back of the house, he turned back. Fatimah told Ali, “Catch up to him and see what turned him back.” Ali followed him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, what made you return?” The Prophet said, “It is not for myself, or a prophet, to enter a decorated house.”
q: It is not for myself, or a prophet, to enter a decorated house

title: Hadith on Celibacy: Prohibition of abandoning marriage entirely
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, rejected ‘Uthman ibn Maz’un from vowing celibacy, and had he given him permission, we would have castrated ourselves.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jihad: Forgiveness for acts of cowardice
t: ‘Abdur Rahman reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “No man says three times, ‘I seek forgiveness from Allah, besides whom there is no God, the Living, the Sustainer, and I repent to Him,’ except that he will be forgiven, even if he fled from battle.”

title: Hadith on Jihad: Protection inside places of worship during war
t: Ibn Abbas reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, dispatched his armies, he would say, “Go forth in the name of Allah and fight in the way of Allah those who deny Allah. Do not be treacherous, do not embezzle the spoils, do not mutilate, and do not kill children, nor the monks in their monasteries.”
q: Go forth in the name of Allah and fight in the way of Allah those who deny Allah. Do not be treacherous, do not embezzle the spoils, do not mutilate, and do not kill children, nor the monks in their monasteries.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Animals: Be merciful even as you slaughter for food
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is merciful, even as he slaughters his animal, then Allah will be merciful to him on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever is merciful, even as he slaughters his animal, then Allah will be merciful to him on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Contentment: I am pleased with Allah as Lord
