t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever says, ‘I am pleased with Allah as a Lord, with Islam as a religion, and with Muhammad as a messenger,’ he must be given Paradise.”
q: Whoever says, ‘I am pleased with Allah as a Lord, with Islam as a religion, and with Muhammad as a messenger,’ he must be given Paradise.

title: Hadith on Unity: Separation and division is from the devil
t: Abu Tha’labah reported: The people would set up camp and disperse into the trails and valleys. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “This scattering of yours into the trails and valleys is from Satan.” They never set up camp afterward unless they were close to each other, so much so that it was said a single blanket could be spread over them all.
q: This scattering of yours into the trails and valleys is from Satan.

title: Hadith on Rage: True wrestler struggles against his anger
t: Abu Hasbah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Who is the true wrestler?” They said, “One who throws his opponent down.” The Prophet said, “The wrestler of all wrestlers is a man who is intensely angry, whose face turns red, and whose hair bristles, then he wrestles against his anger.”
q: Who is the true wrestler? … The wrestler of all wrestlers is a man who is intensely angry, whose face turns red, and whose hair bristles, then he wrestles against his anger.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Anger: Sit down when you are angry
t: ‘Imran ibn Husayn reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you are angry, then sit down.”
q: If you are angry, then sit down.

title: Hadith on Dreams: Three types of vision during sleep
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most truthful of you are those with the truest dreams. There are three kinds of vision: a righteous vision, which is good news from Allah, a distressful vision from Satan, and a vision arising from oneself. If one of you sees something he dislikes, let him stand to pray and not speak to people about it.”
q: The most truthful of you are those with the truest dreams. There are three kinds of vision: a righteous vision, which is good news from Allah, a distressful vision from Satan, and a vision arising from oneself. If one of you sees something he dislikes, let him stand to pray and not speak to people about it.

title: Hadith on Nifaq: Dishonesty and treachery among hypocrites
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Three are in the hypocrite: when he speaks, he lies, when he promises, he breaks it, and when he is trusted, he betrays.”
q: Three are in the hypocrite: when he speaks, he lies, when he promises, he breaks it, and when he is trusted, he betrays.

title: Hadith on Amanah: Loss of trust and honesty in the Ummah
t: Shaddad ibn Aws reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the first thing you will lose in your religion is the trust.”
q: Verily, the first thing you will lose in your religion is the trust.

title: Hadith on Takfir: Accusing a believer of kufr is like murdering him
t: Hisham ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever accuses a believer of unbelief, it is as if he has killed him.”
q: Whoever accuses a believer of unbelief, it is as if he has killed him.

title: Hadith on Hajj: No blame for mistakes, unless defaming a Muslim
t: Usamah ibn Sharik reported: I went out with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to perform the Hajj pilgrimage, and the people would come to him. One would say, “O Messenger of Allah, I ran between the two mounts before circling the Ka’bah, or I did some things before or after I should have.” The Prophet would say, “There is no blame. There is no blame, except upon a man who wrongfully defames another Muslim man’s reputation, for that is blameworthy and ruinous.”
q: There is no blame. There is no blame, except upon a man who wrongfully defames another Muslim man’s reputation, for that is blameworthy and ruinous.

title: Hadith on Dua: Do not pray against yourself or your family
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not supplicate against yourselves, do not supplicate against your children, and do not supplicate against your property, lest it coincides with an hour in which Allah is asked for something and He answers you.”
q: Do not supplicate against yourselves, do not supplicate against your children, and do not supplicate against your property, lest it coincides with an hour in which Allah is asked for something and He answers you.

title: Hadith on Funerals: Do not insult Muslim family, even if unbelievers
t: Sa’id ibn Zayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not harm a Muslim by insulting a deceased unbelieving relative.”
q: Do not harm a Muslim by insulting a deceased unbelieving relative.

title: Hadith on Moderation: Best of your religion is the easiest
t: Mihjan ibn al-Adra’ reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said three times, “Verily, the best of your religion is the easiest of it.”
q: Verily, the best of your religion is the easiest of it.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Balance: You must take the way of moderation
t: Buraydah al-Aslami reported: I went out one day to fulfill a need, and there was the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, walking before me. The Prophet took my hand, and we set out walking together. A man was praying before us who was performing many bowings and prostrations. The Prophet said, “Do you think he is being ostentatious?” I said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Prophet let go of my hand, then put his hands together and directed them upwards, saying, “You must take the way of moderation. You must take the way of moderation. You must take the way of moderation, for whoever is severe in this religion will be overwhelmed.”
q: Do you think he is being ostentatious? … You must take the way of moderation. You must take the way of moderation. You must take the way of moderation, for whoever is severe in this religion will be overwhelmed.

title: Hadith on Recitation: Warning not to exaggerate with the Quran
t: Mihjan ibn al-Adra’ reported: I was eager to meet the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, one night, and he came out to fulfill one of his needs. The Prophet saw me, took my hand, and we set out. We passed by a man who was praying loudly with the Quran. The Prophet said, “Perhaps he is being ostentatious.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, you recite the Quran aloud.” The Prophet raised his hands, then he said, “Verily, you will never achieve this matter by exaggeration.” Then, he came out another night, and we passed by a man praying with the Quran. I said, “Perhaps he is being ostentatious.” The Prophet said, “Nay, rather he is penitent.”
q: Perhaps he is being ostentatious. … Verily, you will never achieve this matter by exaggeration … Nay, rather he is penitent

title: Hadith on Gentleness: Hellfire forbidden for kind people
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you upon whom the Hellfire is forbidden tomorrow? It is everyone gentle, lenient, accessible, and easy-going.”
q: Shall I not tell you upon whom the Hellfire is forbidden tomorrow? It is everyone gentle, lenient, accessible, and easy-going.

title: Hadith on Rifq: Allah blesses beloved households with kindness
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when Allah loves the people of a household, He allows gentleness to enter with them.”
q: Verily, when Allah loves the people of a household, He allows gentleness to enter with them.

title: Hadith on Shirk: The Prophet warns his kindred of idolatry
t: Qabisah ibn al-Mukhariq reported: When the verse was revealed, “Warn your closest kindred,” (26:214) the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, set out to the mountain cliffs and ascended to the highest rock. Then, the Prophet called out, “O sons of ‘Abd Manafah! I am warning you! Verily, the parable of myself is that of a man who saw the enemy and set out to guard his people, but he feared they might reach them first, so he shouted: Prepare yourselves!”
q: Warn your closest kindred … O sons of ‘Abd Manafah! I am warning you! Verily, the parable of myself is that of a man who saw the enemy and set out to guard his people, but he feared they might reach them first, so he shouted: Prepare yourselves!

title: Hadith on Nifaq: Hypocrites are lost wandering in unbelief
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the hypocrite is that of a sheep wandering from flock to flock. It wanders to this at times and to another at times.”
q: The parable of the hypocrite is that of a sheep wandering from flock to flock. It wanders to this at times and to another at times.

title: Hadith on Hellfire: The Prophet tries his best to save believers
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of myself and all of you is that of a man who kindled a fire and tried to stop insects and moths from falling into it. I keep holding you back from the fire, yet you slip from my hand.”
q: The parable of myself and all of you is that of a man who kindled a fire and tried to stop insects and moths from falling into it. I keep holding you back from the fire, yet you slip from my hand.

title: Hadith on Faith: Believers endure trials, unlike hypocrites
t: Ka’b reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the believer is that of a tender plant. The wind sways it at times, and it returns to balance at times. The parable of the hypocrite is that of a cedar tree. It continues to be rigid until it is suddenly uprooted in a single moment.”
q: The parable of the believer is that of a tender plant. The wind sways it at times, and it returns to balance at times. The parable of the hypocrite is that of a cedar tree. It continues to be rigid until it is suddenly uprooted in a single moment.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Qiyamah: The Prophet is a sign the Hour is at hand
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of myself and the Hour is like these two,” and he separated between his middle and index fingers. Then, the Prophet said, “The parable of myself and the Hour is like a man dispatched to this people at the forefront of it, and when it is feared the glimmer of his shirt might arrive first, it comes upon you! It comes upon you!”
q: The parable of myself and the Hour is like these two … The parable of myself and the Hour is like a man dispatched to this people at the forefront of it, and when it is feared the glimmer of his shirt might arrive first, it comes upon you! It comes upon you!

title: Hadith on Tawakkul: Tie your camel and rely upon Allah
t: ‘Amr ibn Umayyah reported: A man said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “Shall I release my camel and trust in Allah?” The Prophet said, “Tie her and trust in Allah.”
q: Tie her and trust in Allah.

title: Hadith on Kufr: Unbelievers stay rigid until they break
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the believer is that of a planted stalk. It stays rigid in one moment and bends down in another moment. The parable of the unbeliever is that of a cedar tree. It continues to stay rigid until it falls down without realizing it.”
q: The parable of the believer is that of a planted stalk. It stays rigid in one moment and bends down in another moment. The parable of the unbeliever is that of a cedar tree. It continues to stay rigid until it falls down without realizing it.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Parables: Believers bend sometimes, upright sometimes
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the believer is that of a planted stalk. It bends at times, and it stays upright at times.”
q: The parable of the believer is that of a planted stalk. It bends at times, and it stays upright at times.

title: Hadith on Tayyib: Believers eat pure good, produce pure good
t: Abu Razin reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the believer is that of a bee. It only consumes what is purely good, and it only produces what is purely good.”
q: The parable of the believer is that of a bee. It only consumes what is purely good, and it only produces what is purely good.

title: Hadith on Faith: Believers like a date palm benefitting everyone
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the believer is that of a palm tree. Whatever you take from it will benefit you.”
q: The parable of the believer is that of a palm tree. Whatever you take from it will benefit you.

title: Hadith on Relief: Salvation for relieving difficulties of others
t: Abu Qatadah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is pleased for Allah to save him from distress on the Day of Resurrection, let him relieve one in hardship or lift his burden.”
q: Whoever is pleased for Allah to save him from distress on the Day of Resurrection, let him relieve one in hardship or lift his burden.

title: Hadith on Seeing: Turn your eyes away from unlawful images
t: Jarir reported: I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about the accidental glance. The Prophet said, “Redirect your sight.”
q: Redirect your sight.

title: Hadith on Zina: Staring with lust is committing adultery
t: ‘Alqamah ibn al-Huwayrith reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The adultery of the two eyes is the lustful gaze.”
q: The adultery of the two eyes is the lustful gaze.

title: Hadith on Zina: All of the limbs can commit adultery
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The two eyes commit adultery, the two hands commit adultery, the two legs commit adultery, and the genitals commit adultery.”
q: The two eyes commit adultery, the two hands commit adultery, the two legs commit adultery, and the genitals commit adultery.

title: Hadith on Harm: Not hurting others is obligatory charity
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Refrain from harming people, for it is your charity due upon yourself.”
q: Refrain from harming people, for it is your charity due upon yourself.

title: Hadith on Roads: Hurting Muslims in streets worthy of curses
t: Hudhayfah ibn Asid reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever harms the Muslims in their roads, he deserves to be cursed by them.”
q: Whoever harms the Muslims in their roads, he deserves to be cursed by them.

title: Hadith on Khulwah: Prohibition of men visiting married women alone
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of entering the homes of women alone.” A man from the Ansar said, “What about sisters-in-law?” The Prophet said, “Entering upon them is deadly serious.”
q: Beware of entering the homes of women alone … What about sisters-in-law … Entering upon them is deadly serious.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Khulwah: Prohibition of a man and woman alone
t: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, climbed the pulpit and he said, “After this day, certainly no man may enter the home of a woman whose husband is absent unless he has with him another man or two.”
q: After this day, certainly no man may enter the home of a woman whose husband is absent unless he has with him another man or two.

title: Hadith on Najwa: Do not harm believers by excluding them
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Let not two privately converse to the exclusion of a third, for that will hurt the believer and Allah Almighty hates for the believer to be hurt.”
q: Let not two privately converse to the exclusion of a third, for that will hurt the believer and Allah Almighty hates for the believer to be hurt.

title: Hadith on Modesty: Women prohibited from nudity in bathhouses
t: Abu al-Malih reported: Women from Hims or Syria entered the dwelling of Aisha, and she said, “Are you those women who enter the bathhouses? I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: No woman puts down her clothes in a place other than her husband’s home but that the barrier between her sin and her Lord will be torn to shreds.”
q: No woman puts down her clothes in a place other than her husband’s home but that the barrier between her sin and her Lord will be torn to shreds.

title: Hadith on Zina: Adultery exposed in this life or the next
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whenever a woman removes her clothes in a place outside of her home, Allah will tear open the veil hiding her sin.”
q: Whenever a woman removes her clothes in a place outside of her home, Allah will tear open the veil hiding her sin.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Bells: Satan plays his music with bells
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The bell is an instrument of Satan.”
q: The bell is an instrument of Satan.

title: Hadith on Bells: Angels keep away from musical instruments
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The angels do not enter a home in which is a jingle or a bell, and the angels do not accompany a gathering in which is a bell.”
q: The angels do not enter a home in which is a jingle or a bell, and the angels do not accompany a gathering in which is a bell.

title: Hadith on Noise: Prohibited musical instruments and screaming
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two voices are cursed in this world and in the Hereafter: a flute at a time of celebration, and wailing at a time of calamity.”
q: Two voices are cursed in this world and in the Hereafter: a flute at a time of celebration, and wailing at a time of calamity.

title: Hadith on Reputation: Testimony of your people a sign to Allah
t: Al-Dahhak ibn Qays reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a man comes to his people and they warmly welcome him, then he will be welcomed warmly on the Day he meets his Lord. If a man comes to his people and they coldly welcome him, then he will be welcomed coldly on the Day he meets his Lord.”
q: If a man comes to his people and they warmly welcome him, then he will be welcomed warmly on the Day he meets his Lord. If a man comes to his people and they coldly welcome him, then he will be welcomed coldly on the Day he meets his Lord.

title: Hadith on Neighbors: Testimony of others a sign of character
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you hear your neighbors saying you have been good, then you have been good. If you hear them saying you have been evil, then you have been evil.”
q: If you hear your neighbors saying you have been good, then you have been good. If you hear them saying you have been evil, then you have been evil.

title: Hadith on Praise: People’s reputations are a sign
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people of Paradise are those whose ears are filled with the praise of people for his virtue, and he hears it. The people of Hellfire are those whose ears are filled with the condemnation of people for his evil, and he hears it.”
q: The people of Paradise are those whose ears are filled with the praise of people for his virtue, and he hears it. The people of Hellfire are those whose ears are filled with the condemnation of people for his evil, and he hears it.

title: Hadith on Reputation: On earth as it is in heaven
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no servant but that he has a reputation in heaven. If his reputation is good, it will be placed upon the earth. If his reputation is evil, it will be placed upon the earth.”
q: There is no servant but that he has a reputation in heaven. If his reputation is good, it will be placed upon the earth. If his reputation is evil, it will be placed upon the earth

title: Hadith on Witness: Believers testify to righteousness and sin
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believers are the witnesses of Allah on the earth.”
q: The believers are the witnesses of Allah on the earth

title: Hadith on Nasihah: Goodwill is the essence of Islam
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The religion is sincere goodwill.”
q: The religion is sincere goodwill

title: Hadith on Nasihah: Do not interfere with business, but give advice if asked
t: Abu al-Sa’ib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allow people to barter amongst themselves, but if one of your brothers seeks advice, then let him offer advice.”
q: Allow people to barter amongst themselves, but if one of your brothers seeks advice, then let him offer advice
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Mockery: Prohibition of laughing at someone’s farts
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited us from laughing at someone who passes wind.

title: Hadith on Illness: Do not curse fever as it purifies from sin
t: Abu Huraira reported: Fever was mentioned in front of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and a man cursed it. The Prophet said, “Do not curse fever, for it cleanses sins just as fire cleanses iron from impurities.”
q: Do not curse fever, for it cleanses sins just as fire cleanses iron from impurities.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Modesty: Husband’s permission to enter women’s homes
t: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited us from requesting entrance into the homes of women unless their husbands give permission.

title: Hadith on Siyam: Wives need permission from husbands to fast
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited wives from fasting unless their husbands gave permission.

title: Hadith on Wealthy: Richest are lowest on Judgment Day, unless charitable
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Those who live to accumulate riches will be the lowest, except for one who gives away such wealth, but those are few.”
q: Those who live to accumulate riches will be the lowest, except for one who gives away such wealth, but those are few.

title: Hadith on Gratitude: Allah asks about even the smallest blessings
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, among the blessing you will be questioned about on the Day of Resurrection are the cool shade, fresh dates, and cold water.”
q: By the One in whose hand is my soul, among the blessing you will be questioned about on the Day of Resurrection are the cool shade, fresh dates, and cold water.

title: Hadith on Beef: Permission to eat cow’s meat in moderation
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, slaughtered a single cow for the house of Muhammad during his farewell pilgrimage.

title: Hadith on Menses: Women performing Hajj will menstruating
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, enter my dwelling at Sarif while I was crying. The Prophet said, “What is the matter? Are you menstruating?” I said yes. The Prophet said, “This is a matter that Allah has decreed for the daughters of Adam, so complete the rites of Hajj pilgrimage as other pilgrims do, but do not circle around the House.” And the Prophet sacrificed a cow for his wives.
q: What is the matter? Are you menstruating? … This is a matter that Allah has decreed for the daughters of Adam, so complete the rites of Hajj pilgrimage as other pilgrims do, but do not circle around the House.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Qiyamah: Two trumpet blasts to end the world
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stood up after a third of the night passed, and he said, “O people! Remember Allah! Remember Allah! The first trumpet blast will come, followed by the second (79:6-7). Death will come with it, death will come with it!”
q: O people! Remember Allah! Remember Allah! The first trumpet blast will come, followed by the second … Death will come with it, death will come with it!

title: Hadith on Repentance: Allah brings the earth full of forgiveness
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: O son of Adam, whenever you worship Me and place your hopes in Me, without associating any partners with Me, I will forgive whatever you have done. If you turn to Me with the likes of the heavens and the earth full of sins and shortcomings, I will turn to you with the same amount of forgiveness, and I do not mind.”
q: Allah Almighty said: O son of Adam, whenever you worship Me and place your hopes in Me, without associating any partners with Me, I will forgive whatever you have done. If you turn to Me with the likes of the heavens and the earth full of sins and shortcomings, I will turn to you with the same amount of forgiveness, and I do not mind.

title: Hadith on Maghfirah: Allah is surely swift in forgiveness
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah said: O son of Adam, if you remember Me within yourself, I will remember you within Myself. If you remember Me in a gathering, I will remember you in a gathering of angels. If you come near to Me by a handspan, I will come near to you by an arm’s length. If you come near to Me by an arm’s length, I will come near to you by the length of a fathom. If you come to Me walking, I will come to you running.” Qatadah said, “Surely, Allah Almighty is the quickest to forgive.”
q: Allah said: O son of Adam, if you remember Me within yourself, I will remember you within Myself. If you remember Me in a gathering, I will remember you in a gathering of angels. If you come near to Me by a handspan, I will come near to you by an arm’s length. If you come near to Me by an arm’s length, I will come near to you by the length of a fathom. If you come to Me walking, I will come to you running.

title: Hadith on Death: Only those forgiven rest in peace
t: Aisha reported: Bilal stood for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “This person has died and now is resting in peace.” The Prophet was upset by that, and he said, “Verily, only those forgiven rest in peace.”
q: . … Verily, only those forgiven rest in peace.

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: Allah descends in last third of night
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a third of the night remains, Allah Almighty descends to the lowest heavens, then the gates of heaven are opened, and He reaches out, saying: Are there any asking that might give them what they request? It continues as such until the rise of dawn.”
q: When a third of the night remains, Allah Almighty descends to the lowest heavens, then the gates of heaven are opened, and He reaches out, saying: Are there any asking that might give them what they request? It continues as such until the rise of dawn.

title: Hadith on Worship: Allah comes even closer as we worship Him
t: Salman al-Farisi reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty says: If My servant comes near to Me by a handspan, I come near to him by an arm’s length. If he comes near to Me by an arm’s length, I come near to him by the length of a fathom. If he comes to Me walking, I come to him running.”
q: Allah Almighty says: If My servant comes near to Me by a handspan, I come near to him by an arm’s length. If he comes near to Me by an arm’s length, I come near to him by the length of a fathom. If he comes to Me walking, I come to him running.

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: Allah descends to accept our night prayers
t: Jubayr ibn Mut’im reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty descends every night to the lowest heaven, and He says: Are there any asking that I may give them? Are there any seeking forgiveness that I may forgive them? This continues until the rise of dawn.”
q: Allah Almighty descends every night to the lowest heaven, and He says: Are there any asking that I may give them? Are there any seeking forgiveness that I may forgive them? This continues until the rise of dawn.

title: Hadith on Worship: Allah draws even closer as we approach
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: I am as My servant expects of Me, and I am with him as He remembers Me. By Allah, Allah is more joyful by the repentance of His servant than if one of you found his lost camel in the desert. Whoever comes near to Me by a handspan, I come near to him by an arm’s length. Whoever comes near to Me by an arm’s length, I come near to him by the length of a fathom. If he turns walking to Me, I turn running to Him.”
q: Allah Almighty said: I am as My servant expects of Me, and I am with him as He remembers Me. By Allah, Allah is more joyful by the repentance of His servant than if one of you found his lost camel in the desert. Whoever comes near to Me by a handspan, I come near to him by an arm’s length. Whoever comes near to Me by an arm’s length, I come near to him by the length of a fathom. If he turns walking to Me, I turn running to Him.

title: Hadith on Worship: Walk to Allah, He come running
t: Shurayh reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: O son of Adam, stand for Me, and I will walk to you. Walk to Me, and I will come running to you.”
q: Allah Almighty said: O son of Adam, stand for Me, and I will walk to you. Walk to Me, and I will come running to you.

title: Hadith on Hijrah: Emigration does not end until repentance ends
t: Mu’awiyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Emigration will not end until repentance ends, and repentance will not end until the sun rises from the west.”
q: Emigration will not end until repentance ends, and repentance will not end until the sun rises from the west.

title: Hadith on Mercy: Allah created you to forgive you
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The expiation of sin is regret. If you never sinned, Allah Almighty would surely come with people who would sin, and He would forgive them.”
q: The expiation of sin is regret. If you never sinned, Allah Almighty would surely come with people who would sin, and He would forgive them.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Repentance open until sun rises from west
t: Safwan ibn ‘Assal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has placed a gate for repentance in the west, the width of which is like seventy years of travel. It will not close until the sun rises in its direction. That is the word of Allah Almighty: The Day that some of the signs of your Lord will come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had earned some good by its faith.” (6:158)
q: Verily, Allah has placed a gate for repentance in the west, the width of which is like seventy years of travel. It will not close until the sun rises in its direction. That is the word of Allah Almighty: The Day that some of the signs of your Lord will come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had earned some good by its faith.

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: Allah descends for those praying at night
t: Rifa’ah ibn ‘Arabah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a half or third of the night has passed, Allah descends to the lowest heaven, and He says, ‘My servants do not ask from anyone but Me. Who is asking Me that I might give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness that I might forgive him? Who is calling upon Me that I might answer him?’ This continues until the dawn rises.”
q: When a half or third of the night has passed, Allah descends to the lowest heaven, and He says, ‘My servants do not ask from anyone but Me. Who is asking Me that I might give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness that I might forgive him? Who is calling upon Me that I might answer him?’ This continues until the dawn rises.

title: Hadith on Wealth: Allah provides for charity, not indulgence
t: Abu Waqid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah said: Verily, We have sent down wealth for the performance of prayer and offering charity. If the son of Adam owned a valley, he would like to have a second. If he had two valleys, he would like to add a third. Nothing satisfies the belly of the son of Adam but the dust of the grave, yet Allah will relent to whoever repents.”
q: Allah said: Verily, We have sent down wealth for the performance of prayer and offering charity. If the son of Adam owned a valley, he would like to have a second. If he had two valleys, he would like to add a third. Nothing satisfies the belly of the son of Adam but the dust of the grave, yet Allah will relent to whoever repents.

title: Hadith on Sins: Who has not fallen short of Allah’s commands?
t: Ibn Abbas reported: He recited the verse, “Those who avoid the major sins and obscenities, except for the shortcomings,” (53:32). Then, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If You forgive, O Allah, Your forgiveness is vast, yet who among Your servants has not fallen short?”
q: Those who avoid the major sins and obscenities, except for the shortcomings, … If You forgive, O Allah, Your forgiveness is vast, yet who among Your servants has not fallen short

title: Hadith on Tawbah: The Prophet repents seventy times a day
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I certainly repent to Allah seventy times in each day.”
q: I certainly repent to Allah seventy times in each day.

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Allah accepts repentance until death is imminent
t: Abdur Rahman al-Baylamani reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever repents before he utters the death rattle, Allah will accept it from him.”
q: Whoever repents before he utters the death rattle, Allah will accept it from him.

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Allah more pleased with our repentance than us
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah is more intensely joyful by the repentance of His servant than a man who sets out on a journey with his provisions upon his camel. Then, he marched until he reached a waterless desert and was overtaken by sleepiness. He descended to lie under a tree, but his camel ran away as he slept. When he woke up, he ran to the nearest hill but did not see anything, then he ran to another hill but did see anything, then he ran to a third hill but did not see anything, so he returned to his original place. While he was sitting, his camel came walking back until it placed his rein in his hand. Thus, Allah is more intensely joyful by the repentance of the servant than this man who finds his camel in this situation.”
q: Allah is more intensely joyful by the repentance of His servant than a man who sets out on a journey with his provisions upon his camel. Then, he marched until he reached a waterless desert and was overtaken by sleepiness. He descended to lie under a tree, but his camel ran away as he slept. When he woke up, he ran to the nearest hill but did not see anything, then he ran to another hill but did see anything, then he ran to a third hill but did not see anything, so he returned to his original place. While he was sitting, his camel came walking back until it placed his rein in his hand. Thus, Allah is more intensely joyful by the repentance of the servant than this man who finds his camel in this situation.

title: Hadith on Wealth: Greatest losers are super rich unless charitable
t: Abu Dharr reported: I arrived at the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who was sitting in the shade of the Ka’bah and saying, “They have the greatest loss, by the Lord of the Ka’bah, they have the greatest loss, by the Lord of the Ka’bah.” I said, “Who are they? May my mother and father be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah!” The Prophet said, “The greatest in wealth, except for those who spend like this, or this, or this.”
q: They have the greatest loss, by the Lord of the Ka’bah, they have the greatest loss, by the Lord of the Ka’bah … The greatest in wealth, except for those who spend like this, or this, or this.

title: Hadith on Takathur: Competition for worldly goods misleads you
t: Ibn al-Zubayr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If the son of Adam had two valleys full of wealth, he would desire a third. Nothing satisfies his belly but the dust of the grave, yet Allah relents to those who repent.” Ubayy said, “We thought this was from the Quran until the verse was revealed, ‘Rivalry for worldly goods distracts you…’” (102:1)
q: If the son of Adam had two valleys full of wealth, he would desire a third. Nothing satisfies his belly but the dust of the grave, yet Allah relents to those who repent. … Rivalry for worldly goods distracts you…’

title: Hadith on Greed: Humans insatiably desire wealth
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If the son of Adam had two valleys full of wealth, he would desire a third. Nothing will fill his belly but the dust of the grave, yet Allah relents to those who repent.”
q: If the son of Adam had two valleys full of wealth, he would desire a third. Nothing will fill his belly but the dust of the grave, yet Allah relents to those who repent.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Allah hates to meet His haters
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him. Whoever hates to meet Allah, Allah is averse to meet him.”
q: Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him. Whoever hates to meet Allah, Allah is averse to meet him.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Whoever loves or hates to meet Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah said: If My servant loves to meet Me, I love to meet him. If my servant hates to meet Me, I hate to meet him.”
q: Allah said: If My servant loves to meet Me, I love to meet him. If my servant hates to meet Me, I hate to meet him.

title: Hadith on Wealth: Umar asks for the riches of Persia and Rome
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab said, “O Messenger of Allah, call upon Allah to send abundance upon your nation, for the Persians and Romans enjoy abundance and have been given the world, yet they do not worship Allah as they recline on their couches!” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Are you in doubt, O Umar ibn al-Khattab? These people have only been given their pleasure in the life of this world.” Umar said, “O Messenger of Allah, seek forgiveness for me.”
q: Are you in doubt, O Umar ibn al-Khattab? These people have only been given their pleasure in the life of this world.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Deeds: If the inward is good, the outward is good
t: Mu’awiyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the deeds are only like vessels. If the bottom is clean, the top will be clean. If the bottom is spoiled, the top will be spoiled.”
q: Verily, the deeds are only like vessels. If the bottom is clean, the top will be clean. If the bottom is spoiled, the top will be spoiled

title: Hadith on Dunya: Time remaining for the world is short
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty made the world for a short time, and what remains is but the shortest of it. The parable of what remains is like the pure mountaintop water already drank while what is leftover is its murkiness.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty made the world for a short time, and what remains is but the shortest of it. The parable of what remains is like the pure mountaintop water already drank while what is leftover is its murkiness

title: Hadith on Dunya: Beware sinful temptations of worldly life
t: Mus’ab ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of the worldly life, for it is green and sweet.”
q: Beware of the worldly life, for it is green and sweet

title: Hadith on Trials: Better to be punished in world than Hereafter
t: Al-Hasan reported: A man saw a woman he recognized from the time of ignorance, so he talked to her and then left her. He turned back to look at her, and as he was walking, a wall collapsed on him, leaving scars upon his face. He went to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and told him about it. The Prophet said, “If Allah intends goodness for His servant, He hastens his punishment in the world.”
q: If Allah intends goodness for His servant, He hastens his punishment in the world.

title: Hadith on Trials: Allah punishes a man out of mercy
t: Abdullah ibn Mughaffal reported: A man met a woman who was a prostitute in the time of ignorance and he played with her until he wanted to touch her. The woman said, “Stop, for Allah has taken away idolatry and come to us with Islam.” The man turned away and was later struck in the face by a wall, fracturing his head. He went to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and told him about it. The Prophet said, “You are a servant, and Allah intends good for you. If Allah intends goodness for a servant, He hastens the punishment for his sins. If Allah intends harm for a servant, He withholds the punishment for his sins until he arrives on the Day of Resurrection as if he were a wild donkey.”
q: You are a servant, and Allah intends good for you. If Allah intends goodness for a servant, He hastens the punishment for his sins. If Allah intends harm for a servant, He withholds the punishment for his sins until he arrives on the Day of Resurrection as if he were a wild donkey.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Trials: Allah tests His beloved servants
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Allah loves a people, He afflicts them with trials.”
q: When Allah loves a people, He afflicts them with trials.

title: Hadith on Seerah: Remember the Prophet’s patience for strength
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you is struck by a calamity, let him remember my affliction, for it was among the greatest of calamities.”
q: If one of you is struck by a calamity, let him remember my affliction, for it was among the greatest of calamities.

title: Hadith on Seerah: Seek strength in the Prophet’s biography
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O people, whenever a calamity afflicts one of the people or the believers, let them be strengthened by remembering the calamity that afflicted me, with which no one was struck besides me. Verily, no one from my nation will be struck by a calamity more severe than my affliction.”
q: O people, whenever a calamity afflicts one of the people or the believers, let them be strengthened by remembering the calamity that afflicted me, with which no one was struck besides me. Verily, no one from my nation will be struck by a calamity more severe than my affliction.

title: Hadith on Masajid: Believers are pillars in the mosque
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the mosques have pillars with whom the angels sit. If they are absent, the angels miss their presence. If they are sick, the angels visit them. If they are in need, the angels support them.”
q: Verily, the mosques have pillars with whom the angels sit. If they are absent, the angels miss their presence. If they are sick, the angels visit them. If they are in need, the angels support them.

title: Hadith on Da’wah: Three men meet the Prophet
t: Abu Waqid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was sitting in the mosque with some people when he received three men. Two of them faced the Messenger of Allah and the third left. The two men continued standing before the Messenger of Allah until one saw an opening in the circle and sat down, the other sat behind them, and the third turned his back. When the Messenger of Allah finished speaking, he said, “Shall I not tell you about these three men? The first sought refuge in Allah, thus Allah granted him refuge. The other was shy before Allah, thus Allah was shy to blame him. The last turned away, thus Allah turned away from him.”
q: Shall I not tell you about these three men? The first sought refuge in Allah, thus Allah granted him refuge. The other was shy before Allah, thus Allah was shy to blame him. The last turned away, thus Allah turned away from him.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ijtihad: The Prophet has opinions, but never lies about Allah
t: Talhah reported: I passed by some people with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, who were on top of palm trees. The Prophet said, “What are you doing?” They said, “They are grafting them, mixing the male and female to produce more yield.” The Prophet said, “I do not expect it will amount to anything.” They were informed about that and abandoned the practice, but the yield was lower. The Prophet was told about it later and he said, “If that is beneficial, let them do it. Verily, I only had an opinion, so do not take my opinion. Rather, if I narrate to you anything from Allah, then take it. I do not lie against Allah Almighty.”
q: What are you doing? … If that is beneficial, let them do it. Verily, I only had an opinion, so do not take my opinion. Rather, if I narrate to you anything from Allah, then take it. I do not lie against Allah Almighty.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: All people in shade of their charity
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Everyone will be in the shade of their charity until judgment is carried out between the people.”
q: Everyone will be in the shade of their charity until judgment is carried out between the people.

title: Hadith on Zakat: Unpaid charity appears as a fearsome snake
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The unpaid alms of one of you will come on the Day of Resurrection as a white-headed, venomous serpent. Its owner will flee from it, but it will pursue him, saying: I am your treasure! By Allah, the serpent will not stop chasing him until he puts up his hand and the serpent devours it whole.”
q: The unpaid alms of one of you will come on the Day of Resurrection as a white-headed, venomous serpent. Its owner will flee from it, but it will pursue him, saying: I am your treasure! By Allah, the serpent will not stop chasing him until he puts up his hand and the serpent devours it whole.

title: Ibn Umar on Qadr: Allah’s decision is better than ours
t: Makhul reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, a man will seek the decision of Allah Almighty, and He chooses for him, yet he is displeased with his Almighty Lord. If he only waited to see the final result, he would find it is better for him.”

title: Hadith on Shirk: Idolaters forbidden from entering Paradise
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man will take his father’s hand on the Day of Resurrection and want to enter Paradise with him. It will be announced: An idolater will not enter Paradise! Allah has forbidden Paradise for the idolaters! He will say: O Lord, my father! O Lord, my father! Then, his father’s form will be made ugly and his scent repulsive, so he abandons him.”
q: A man will take his father’s hand on the Day of Resurrection and want to enter Paradise with him. It will be announced: An idolater will not enter Paradise! Allah has forbidden Paradise for the idolaters! He will say: O Lord, my father! O Lord, my father! Then, his father’s form will be made ugly and his scent repulsive, so he abandons him.

title: Hadith on Freedom: Emancipating slaves on behalf of another
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As said, “O Messenger of Allah, my idolatrous father ordered in his will to emancipate one hundred slaves. Hisham has emancipated fifty of them, and another fifty remain. Shall I emancipate them on his behalf?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If he had been a Muslim and you emancipated them on his behalf, or given charity on his behalf, or performed pilgrimage on his behalf, that good would have surely reached him.”
q: If he had been a Muslim and you emancipated them on his behalf, or given charity on his behalf, or performed pilgrimage on his behalf, that good would have surely reached him.

title: Hadith on Quran: Recite Allah’s Book sincerely, not for wealth
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Shibl reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Recite the Quran and do not exaggerate in it, do not abandon it, do not earn your livelihood from it, and do not accumulate wealth from it.”
q: Recite the Quran and do not exaggerate in it, do not abandon it, do not earn your livelihood from it, and do not accumulate wealth from it.

title: Hadith on Quran: Reward for listening and reciting a verse
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever listens to a verse from the Book of Allah Almighty will have a multiplied reward. Whoever recites a verse will have a light on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever listens to a verse from the Book of Allah Almighty will have a multiplied reward. Whoever recites a verse will have a light on the Day of Resurrection

title: Hadith on Quran: Teacher rewarded every time a verse recited
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever teaches a verse from the Book of Allah will have its reward as it is recited.”
q: Whoever teaches a verse from the Book of Allah will have its reward as it is recited.

title: Hadith on Death: Every worldly attachment is eventually gone
t: Ali bin Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Gabriel, upon him be peace, said to me: O Muhammad, love whom you wish for you will surely part with them, act as you wish for you will surely see its results, and live as you wish for you will surely die.” The Prophet said, “Gabriel had been concise with me in his discourse.”
q: Gabriel, upon him be peace, said to me: O Muhammad, love whom you wish for you will surely part with them, act as you wish for you will surely see its results, and live as you wish for you will surely die. … Gabriel had been concise with me in his discourse.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: Tell him that he is loved for Allah
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you loves your companion, let him go to his home and inform him that he loves him for the sake of Allah.”
q: When one of you loves your companion, let him go to his home and inform him that he loves him for the sake of Allah

title: Hadith on Love: Friendship endures, affection takes root
t: Mujahid ibn Jabr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you loves your brother for the sake of Allah, let him tell him, for through it friendship will endure and affection take root.”
q: When one of you loves your brother for the sake of Allah, let him tell him, for through it friendship will endure and affection take root.

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: Tell them you love them for Allah
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you loves his brother, let him tell him, for he will find that he feels the same way.”
q: When one of you loves his brother, let him tell him, for he will find that he feels the same way.

title: Hadith on Shirk: Recite Surat al-Kafirun before bed
t: Nawfal al-Ashja’i reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Recite the chapter, ‘Say: O disbelievers…’ (109:1) then sleep after finishing it, for it is a declaration of innocence from idolatry.”
q: Recite the chapter, ‘Say: O disbelievers…’ … then sleep after finishing it, for it is a declaration of innocence from idolatry.

title: Hadith on Nile: Earthly rivers flowing from Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Ceyhan, the Oxus, the Euphrates, and the Nile are all from the rivers of Paradise.”
q: The Ceyhan, the Oxus, the Euphrates, and the Nile are all from the rivers of Paradise.

title: Hadith on Salaam: Spread peace of Allah on the earth
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, peace is one of the names of Allah Exalted that He has placed upon the earth, so spread peace between yourselves.”
q: Verily, peace is one of the names of Allah Exalted that He has placed upon the earth, so spread peace between yourselves.

title: Hadith on Ease: Difficulty decreed along with two reliefs
t: Qatadah ibn Di’amatah reported: It has been mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gave glad tidings to his companions about this verse, “Verily, with the hardship comes an ease, with the hardship comes an ease,” (94:5-6) and the Prophet said, “A hardship will never defeat two eases.”
q: Verily, with the hardship comes an ease, with the hardship comes an ease, … A hardship will never defeat two eases.
gf: Jayyid (very good) according to Ibn Hajar

title: Hadith on Ease: Difficulty certain to be followed by relief
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was once standing over a hole and he said, “If hardship were to enter this hole, ease would surely follow it, go inside, and take it out.” Then, Allah Almighty revealed the verse, “Verily, with the hardship comes an ease, with the hardship comes an ease.” (94:5-6)
q: If hardship were to enter this hole, ease would surely follow it, go inside, and take it out. … Verily, with the hardship comes an ease, with the hardship comes an ease.

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Faith is completed by excellent character
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the people with the most complete faith have the best character, for good character reaches the level of regular fasting and prayer.”
q: Verily, the people with the most complete faith have the best character, for good character reaches the level of regular fasting and prayer.

title: Hadith on Ingratitude: Be grateful to both Allah and people
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is never thankful to people is never thankful to Allah.”
q: Whoever is never thankful to people is never thankful to Allah.

title: Hadith on Humility: Believers must be humble to each other
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has revealed to me that you be humble to one another and not transgress against each other.”
q: Verily, Allah has revealed to me that you be humble to one another and not transgress against each other.

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: The best of you, the worst of you
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of you are those with the most excellent character and are careful of those around them. The worst of you are the pompous, the braggarts, and the pretentious.”
q: The best of you are those with the most excellent character and are careful of those around them. The worst of you are the pompous, the braggarts, and the pretentious.

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Adorn yourself with good character and reflection
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must have good character and observe long periods of silence. By the One in whose hand is my soul, no behaviors are as beautifying as these two.”
q: You must have good character and observe long periods of silence. By the One in whose hand is my soul, no behaviors are as beautifying as these two.

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Good character nearest to the Prophet
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, those of you in the closest position to me on the Day of Resurrection are those of you with the best character in the world.”
q: Verily, those of you in the closest position to me on the Day of Resurrection are those of you with the best character in the world.

title: Hadith on Zuhd: Give up worldly life for Allah’s love
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Renounce the worldly life and Allah will love you. As for people, leave this to them and they will love you.”
q: Renounce the worldly life and Allah will love you. As for people, leave this to them and they will love you.

title: Hadith on Neighbors: No Paradise for an evil neighbor
t: Talq ibn ‘Ali reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He will not enter Paradise whose neighbor is not secure from his harm.”
q: He will not enter Paradise whose neighbor is not secure from his harm.

title: Hadith on Blindness: Paradise for patience with losing eyesight
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah says: If I take the two noble eyes of My servant in this world, there is no reward for him with Me but Paradise.”
q: Allah says: If I take the two noble eyes of My servant in this world, there is no reward for him with Me but Paradise.

title: Hadith on Trials: Expiation of sins for not complaining to people
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: If I put My servant to trial and he does not complain of Me to his visitors, I will release him from his captivity, then I will replace his flesh and blood with what is better, then he will resume his record of deeds anew.”
q: Allah Almighty said: If I put My servant to trial and he does not complain of Me to his visitors, I will release him from his captivity, then I will replace his flesh and blood with what is better, then he will resume his record of deeds anew.

title: Hadith on Sabr: Patience is best provision from Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A servant is not provided with anything better and vaster than patience.”
q: A servant is not provided with anything better and vaster than patience.

title: Hadith on Rizq: Allah provides help, patience as needed
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty sends down support in proportion to the need, and He sends down patience in proportion to the trial.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty sends down support in proportion to the need, and He sends down patience in proportion to the trial.

title: Hadith on Love: Believers shaded on Judgment Day by their love
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: My love is the right of those who loved each other for My sake. They will be under the shade of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection when there is no shade but Mine.”
q: Allah Almighty said: My love is the right of those who loved each other for My sake. They will be under the shade of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection when there is no shade but Mine.

title: Hadith on Jibreel: Gabriel advises the Prophet on living
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Gabriel, upon him be peace, said to me: O Muhammad, live as you wish for you will surely die, love whom you wish for you will surely part with them, and act as you wish for you will surely see its results.”
q: Gabriel, upon him be peace, said to me: O Muhammad, live as you wish for you will surely die, love whom you wish for you will surely part with them, and act as you wish for you will surely see its results.

title: Hadith on Safety: Believers are not harmful to neighbors
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He is not a believer whose neighbor is not safe from his calamities.”
q: He is not a believer whose neighbor is not safe from his calamities.

title: Hadith on Akhirah: Hereafter is the only life worth living
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: We were in the trench with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was digging and we were carrying the dirt away. The Prophet passed by us and he said, “O Allah, there is no life worth living but the life of the Hereafter, so forgive the Ansar and the Muhajirun.”
q: O Allah, there is no life worth living but the life of the Hereafter, so forgive the Ansar and the Muhajirun
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Gratitude: What kind of wealth should we acquire?
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said three times, “Destruction is in the desire for gold and silver.” Umar said, “O Messenger of Allah, what kind of wealth should we seek?” The Prophet said, “A tongue of remembrance, a grateful heart, and a believing wife.”
q: Destruction is in the desire for gold and silver. … A tongue of remembrance, a grateful heart, and a believing wife.

title: Hadith on Funerals: Paradise for patience with lost loved ones
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is not satisfied for His believing servant to be rewarded with anything but Paradise if his loved ones on earth pass away, he remains patient, hopes for reward, and says what he has been commanded.”
q: Verily, Allah is not satisfied for His believing servant to be rewarded with anything but Paradise if his loved ones on earth pass away, he remains patient, hopes for reward, and says what he has been commanded.

title: Hadith on Trials: Praise Allah even if you become blind
t: Al-‘Irbad ibn Sariyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: When I deprive My servant of his two noble eyes, although he was reluctant to lose them, I am not satisfied with any reward for him but Paradise if he praises Me for them.”
q: Allah Almighty said: When I deprive My servant of his two noble eyes, although he was reluctant to lose them, I am not satisfied with any reward for him but Paradise if he praises Me for them.

title: Hadith on Trials: Allah expiates all sins with sickness
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah will put His servant to trial with illness until that expiates every one of his sins.”
q: Verily, Allah will put His servant to trial with illness until that expiates every one of his sins.

title: Hadith on Seerah: Seek strength in the life of the Prophet
t: Abdur Rahman al-Qasim reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Let the Muslims be strengthened in their calamities by remembering the misfortunes that befell me.”
q: Let the Muslims be strengthened in their calamities by remembering the misfortunes that befell me.

title: Hadith on Quran: Study the Book for Allah, not the world
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Learn the Quran and use it to ask Allah for Paradise before people learn it to ask for the world. Verily, the Quran is learned for three reasons: a man who uses it to boast, a man who uses it for his livelihood, and a man who recites it for Allah.”
q: Learn the Quran and use it to ask Allah for Paradise before people learn it to ask for the world. Verily, the Quran is learned for three reasons: a man who uses it to boast, a man who uses it for his livelihood, and a man who recites it for Allah.

title: Hadith on Charity: Spending in the way of Allah multiplied
t: Khuraym ibn Fatik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever donates charity in the way of Allah, it will be multiplied up to seven hundred times in his record.”
q: Whoever donates charity in the way of Allah, it will be multiplied up to seven hundred times in his record.

title: Hadith on Guests: Warning not to overstay your welcome
t: Abu Shurayh reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Hospitality for the guest is no more than three days, and it is courteous to host for one day and night. It is not lawful for a Muslim man to reside with his brother until he tempts him to sin.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, how does he tempt him to sin?” The Prophet said, “He stays with him until he has nothing left to entertain him.”
q: Hospitality for the guest is no more than three days, and it is courteous to host for one day and night. It is not lawful for a Muslim man to reside with his brother until he tempts him to sin. … He stays with him until he has nothing left to entertain him.

title: Hadith on Alcohol: Intoxicants are poisonous, not medicine
t: Wa’il al-Hadrami reported: Tariq ibn Suwayd asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, about wine and the Prophet prohibited him from preparing it. Tariq said, “I only prepare it as medicine.” The Prophet said, “Verily, it is not a cure, but rather it is a sickness.”
q: Verily, it is not a cure, but rather it is a sickness.

title: Hadith on Revolt: No excuse with Allah for unlawful rebellion
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever pulls his hand away from lawful obedience to the ruler, he will meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection without any argument in his favor. Whoever dies without any ties of allegiance, he will have died a death of ignorance.”
q: Whoever pulls his hand away from lawful obedience to the ruler, he will meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection without any argument in his favor. Whoever dies without any ties of allegiance, he will have died a death of ignorance.

title: Hadith on Kufr: Allah may forgive anything but murder and disbelief
t: Mu’awiyah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah might forgive any sin except for a man who kills a believer on purpose or a man who dies as an unbeliever.”
q: Allah might forgive any sin except for a man who kills a believer on purpose or a man who dies as an unbeliever.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Da’wah: Whoever hears of Muhammad must believe
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever hears of me among my nation, the Jews, or the Christians but does not have faith in me, he will enter Hellfire.”
q: Whoever hears of me among my nation, the Jews, or the Christians but does not have faith in me, he will enter Hellfire.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Unity: All ethnicities gather to recite the Quran
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us while we were reciting the Quran. The Prophet said, “All praise is due to Allah! The Book of Allah is one, but among you are those with brown skin, white skin, or black skin. Continue reciting it before some people come who merely sharpen its outer form as if they were sharpening an arrow.”
q: All praise is due to Allah! The Book of Allah is one, but among you are those with brown skin, white skin, or black skin. Continue reciting it before some people come who merely sharpen its outer form as if they were sharpening an arrow.

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication against anxiety and depression
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Never is a servant struck by worry or grief but let him say, ‘O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant, the son of Your maidservant. My forelock is in Your hand, Your decision over me has passed, and Your decree upon me is in justice. I ask You by every name with which You have named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to one of Your creatures, or kept hidden in the Unseen with You, that You make the Quran the spring of my heart, the light of my insight, the banisher of my depression, and the expeller of my anxiety,’ then Allah will expel his worry and replace his grief with joy.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, should we study these words?” The Prophet said, “Of course, whoever hears them should study them.”
q: Never is a servant struck by worry or grief but let him say, ‘O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant, the son of Your maidservant. My forelock is in Your hand, Your decision over me has passed, and Your decree upon me is in justice. I ask You by every name with which You have named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to one of Your creatures, or kept hidden in the Unseen with You, that You make the Quran the spring of my heart, the light of my insight, the banisher of my depression, and the expeller of my anxiety,’ then Allah will expel his worry and replace his grief with joy. … Of course, whoever hears them should study them.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Angels strike parable of Allah’s invitation
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: While I was sitting and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was resting beside me, I beheld men around him in white garments. Allah knows best how handsome they were! They stopped near me and a group sat by the head of the Prophet, while another sat by his feet. They said among themselves, “We have never seen a servant given the likes of this prophet! His eyes sleep while his heart remains awake. Strike for him a parable of a master who built a palace, then placed a feast within and invited the people to eat and drink. Whoever answered him ate from his food and drank from his drinks, but whoever did not answer him was punished!” Then, they departed and the Messenger of Allah was awakened by that. The Prophet said, “I heard what they were saying. Do you know who they were?” I said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Prophet said, “They were angels. The parable they struck is that of the Most Merciful, Blessed and Exalted, who built Paradise and invites His servants to it. Whoever does not accept Him will be punished or tormented.”
q: I heard what they were saying. Do you know who they were? … They were angels. The parable they struck is that of the Most Merciful, Blessed and Exalted, who built Paradise and invites His servants to it. Whoever does not accept Him will be punished or tormented.

title: Hadith on Jama’ah: All sects in Hellfire but united community
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the children of Israel split into seventy-one sects and this nation will surely split into seventy-two sects. All of them are in the Hellfire except one: the united community.”
q: Verily, the children of Israel split into seventy-one sects and this nation will surely split into seventy-two sects. All of them are in the Hellfire except one: the united community.

title: Hadith on Jama’ah: Unity is mercy, division is punishment
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The united community is mercy and sectarianism is torment.”
q: The united community is mercy and sectarianism is torment.

title: Hadith on Jama’ah: Devil with one abandoning the community
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever desires the best place in Paradise must stick closely to the united community, for Satan is with the loner.”
q: Whoever desires the best place in Paradise must stick closely to the united community, for Satan is with the loner

title: Hadith on Jama’ah: Hand of Allah with Muslims united on truth
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hand of Allah is with the united community.”
q: The Hand of Allah is with the united community

title: Hadith on Consensus: Ummah will not collectively accept misguidance
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has protected my nation from agreeing entirely upon misguidance.”

title: Hadith on Death: The Prophet hears them punished in the grave
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered a palm garden of the tribe of Al-Najjar one day, and he heard the voices of men from the tribe who had died in the time of ignorance being punished in their graves. The Prophet went out startled and he commanded his companions, saying, “Seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the grave.”
q: Seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the grave.

title: Hadith on Kufr: Good deeds to be praised no benefit
t: Umm Salamah reported: She said, “O Messenger of Allah, Hisham ibn al-Mughirah used to feed the hungry, entertain the guest, uphold family ties, and free captives. Were Islam to have reached him, he would have embraced it. Will he be rewarded for any of it?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, your uncle used to give charity for the sake of the world and to be remembered fondly therein. He did not say for even a single day: Forgive me on the Day of Judgment.”
q: Verily, your uncle used to give charity for the sake of the world and to be remembered fondly therein. He did not say for even a single day: Forgive me on the Day of Judgment

title: Hadith on Forgiveness: Let them not take Allah’s mercy for granted
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever meets Allah without associating any partners with Him, performs the five prayers, and fasts the month of Ramadan, then he will be forgiven.” I said, “Shall I not give them glad tidings, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Leave them to work.”
q: Whoever meets Allah without associating any partners with Him, performs the five prayers, and fasts the month of Ramadan, then he will be forgiven. … Leave them to work.

title: Hadith on Salawat: Paradise for performing the five daily prayers
t: Anas reported: A man asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, how many prayers does Allah Almighty impose upon His servants?” The Prophet said, “Allah has obligated five prayers upon His servants.” The man said, “O Messenger of Allah, is there anything before or after them?” The Prophet said, “Allah has obligated five prayers upon His servants.” The man swore an oath that he would not add or lessen anything of them. The Prophet said, “If he is truthful, he will surely enter Paradise.”
q: Allah has obligated five prayers upon His servants. … Allah has obligated five prayers upon His servants. … If he is truthful, he will surely enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Waswas: Rejection of evil thoughts a sign of sincere faith
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: We asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about a man who finds thoughts within himself such that it would be more beloved for him to fall from the sky and be plucked by the birds than to speak openly of them. The Prophet said, “That is pure faith.”
q: That is pure faith

title: Hadith on Satan: Turn away the devil by renewing faith
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, one of you will be confronted by Satan and he will say: Who created you? Then he says: Allah. Satan says: Who created Allah? If one of you feels that, let him recite: I have faith in Allah and His Messengers. This will take him away.”
q: Verily, one of you will be confronted by Satan and he will say: Who created you? Then he says: Allah. Satan says: Who created Allah? If one of you feels that, let him recite: I have faith in Allah and His Messengers. This will take him away.

title: Hadith on Shaytan: Devil sows doubts by whispering false questions
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Satan will come to one of you and say: Who created the heavens? Then he says: Allah. Satan says: Who created the earth? Then he says: Allah. Satan says: Who created Allah? If one of you feels that, let him say: I have faith in Allah and His Messenger.”
q: Verily, Satan will come to one of you and say: Who created the heavens? Then he says: Allah. Satan says: Who created the earth? Then he says: Allah. Satan says: Who created Allah? If one of you feels that, let him say: I have faith in Allah and His Messenger.

title: Hadith on Deeds: Good definitely rewarded, evil maybe punished
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whomever Allah promises to reward for a good deed, He will surely bring it about. Whomever Allah warns to punish for an evil deed, He has the choice to carry it out or not.”
q: Whomever Allah promises to reward for a good deed, He will surely bring it about. Whomever Allah warns to punish for an evil deed, He has the choice to carry it out or not.

title: Hadith on Adultery: Faith leaves with major sin, returns with repentance
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a man commits adultery, faith departs from him as if it were a cloud overhead. When he stops what he is doing, faith returns to him.”
