q: Whoever says ten times before departing the sunset and dawn prayers or moving his feet, ‘There is no God but Allah alone, without any partners, to Him belong the dominion and all praise, all goodness is in His hand, He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things,’ then ten good deeds will be recorded for him each time, ten bad deeds will be erased, he will be raised by ten degrees, he will be fortified from everything he dislikes and from the accursed Satan. No sin will be allowed to harm him but idolatry. He will be the best of people in deeds except for a man who surpasses him by saying it more often than him.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Fajr: Rewards for supplication after dawn prayer
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever says one hundred times after dawn prayer before moving his feet, ‘There is no God but Allah, without any partners. He owns the dominion and to Him is all praise, He gives life and He causes death, and all goodness is in His hand for He has power over all things,’ he will be the best of those upon earth on that day except one who said likewise or even more.”
q: Whoever says one hundred times after dawn prayer before moving his feet, ‘There is no God but Allah, without any partners. He owns the dominion and to Him is all praise, He gives life and He causes death, and all goodness is in His hand for He has power over all things,’ he will be the best of those upon earth on that day except one who said likewise or even more.

title: Hadith on Courage: The Prophet fights on the frontlines
t: Ali reported: When the danger intensified and the people met each other in battle, we would seek protection by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. None of us would be closer to the enemy than him.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Allah loves to meet His beloved
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him. Whoever hates to meet Allah, Allah hates to meet him.”
q: Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him. Whoever hates to meet Allah, Allah hates to meet him.

title: Hadith on Bravery: The Prophet was the bravest in battle
t: Abu Ishaq reported: Al-Bara’, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “We would, by Allah, seek protection by the side of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when the battle was fierce. Verily, he was the most courageous among us who confronted the onslaught.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Powerful supplication to Allah, morning and evening
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever says ten times when he awakens in the morning, ‘There is no God but Allah, alone without any partners to Him. He owns the dominion and for Him is all praise. He gives life and causes death, for He has power over all things,’ then Allah will record ten good times for each time he said it, Allah will erase ten sins by it, he will be raised by Allah ten degrees, it will be as if he has freed ten slaves, he will be guarded from the beginning of the day until its end, and he will not act on that day with anything else to overcome it. If he says it in the evening, then he will have the same.”

title: Mujahid on Quran: Mercy descends upon finishing the Quran
t: Al-Hakam reported: Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Mercy descends at the time of completing the entire Quran.”

title: Anas on Dua: Praying for family after finishing the Quran
t: Thabit reported: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, when he completed reading the entire Quran, he would gather his children and his household and supplicate to Allah for them.

title: Hadith on Islam: Three truths about Allah Almighty
t: Ali reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Three are the truth: Allah does not make one with a portion of Islam like one without it, Allah will not entrust the servant to another if he takes Him as an ally, and a man does not love a people but that he will be resurrected with them.”
q: Three are the truth: Allah does not make one with a portion of Islam like one without it, Allah will not entrust the servant to another if he takes Him as an ally, … and a man does not love a people but that he will be resurrected with them.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Crops: Allah alone causes plants to grow
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Let not one of you say: I have grown crops. Rather, let him say: I have sown crops.” Abu Huraira said, “Have you not heard the saying of Allah Almighty: Do you not see what you have sown? Are you the growers or is it We who have grown them?” (56:63)
q: Let not one of you say: I have grown crops. Rather, let him say: I have sown crops. … : Do you not see what you have sown? Are you the growers or is it We who have grown them?

title: Ibn Umar on Creation: Allah created four things with His hand
t: Mujahid reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Allah Almighty created four things with His hand: Adam, upon him be peace, the Throne, the Pen, and the Gardens of Eden. Then, He said to the rest of creation, ‘Be’ and it was.”

title: Hadith on Poverty: Poor enter Paradise long before the rich
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The poor emigrants complained to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, because Allah favored the rich over them. The Prophet said, “O you in poverty, I bring you glad tidings that the poor believers will enter Paradise before the rich by half of a day, the length of which is like five hundred years.” Musa ibn ‘Ubaydah recited the verse, “Verily, a day to your Lord is like a thousand years in your count.” (22:47)
q: O you in poverty, I bring you glad tidings that the poor believers will enter Paradise before the rich by half of a day, the length of which is like five hundred years. … Verily, a day to your Lord is like a thousand years in your count.

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Allah promises to forgive the monotheists
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty says: O My servant, as long as you worship Me and place your hopes in Me, I will forgive you despite what you have done. O My servant, if you meet Me with enough sins to fill the earth, I will meet you with as much forgiveness as long as You do not associate anything with Me.”
q: Allah Almighty says: O My servant, as long as you worship Me and place your hopes in Me, I will forgive you despite what you have done. O My servant, if you meet Me with enough sins to fill the earth, I will meet you with as much forgiveness as long as You do not associate anything with Me.

title: Hadith on Poverty: Charity from the poor surpasses the rich
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One silver coin is ahead of one hundred thousand others.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, how is it so?” The Prophet said, “A man has only two coins, so he takes one and gives it in charity. Another man has abundant wealth, so he takes one hundred thousand coins from a mere portion of it and gives it in charity.”
q: One silver coin is ahead of one hundred thousand others. … A man has only two coins, so he takes one and gives it in charity. Another man has abundant wealth, so he takes one hundred thousand coins from a mere portion of it and gives it in charity.

title: Hadith on Honor: Nobility in night prayer, honor in independence
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The nobility of a believer is in his prayer at night, and his honor is in his independence from what belongs to people.”
q: The nobility of a believer is in his prayer at night, and his honor is in his independence from what belongs to people.

title: Hadith on Ghaflah: Allah forgets him as he has forgotten Him
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and Allah will say to him: Did I not make your hearing, your seeing, your wealth, and your children? Did I not subordinate the cattle and the harvest for you? Did I not leave you in charge of people and you were taken as their leader? Did you not expect to meet Me on this Day of yours? He will say no. Allah will say to him: Today, I have forgotten you as you had forgotten Me.”
q: A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and Allah will say to him: Did I not make your hearing, your seeing, your wealth, and your children? Did I not subordinate the cattle and the harvest for you? Did I not leave you in charge of people and you were taken as their leader? Did you not expect to meet Me on this Day of yours? He will say no. Allah will say to him: Today, I have forgotten you as you had forgotten Me.

title: Umar on Dua: O Allah, let me die among the righteous
t: ‘Amr ibn Maymun reported: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, would supplicate, “O Allah, let me die among the righteous, do not leave me among the wicked, and join me with the virtuous.”

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet seeks refuge from committing injustice
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from poverty, scarcity, and humiliation. I seek refuge in You from committing wrong or being wronged.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from poverty, scarcity, and humiliation. I seek refuge in You from committing wrong or being wronged.

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet seeks refuge from many evil trials
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the trials and punishment of the Hellfire, from the trials and punishment of the grave, from the evil of the trials of wealth, and from the evil of the trials of poverty. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of the trials of the False Messiah. O Allah, cleanse my heart with the water of snow and hail and purify my heart from sins, just as the white garment is purified from grime, and distance me from my sins, just as You have distanced the east from the west. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from sloth, sinfulness, and indebtedness.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the trials and punishment of the Hellfire, from the trials and punishment of the grave, from the evil of the trials of wealth, and from the evil of the trials of poverty. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of the trials of the False Messiah. O Allah, cleanse my heart with the water of snow and hail and purify my heart from sins, just as the white garment is purified from grime, and distance me from my sins, just as You have distanced the east from the west. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from sloth, sinfulness, and indebtedness.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Easy way to Paradise, but Satan distracts them
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are two practices no Muslim man preserves but that he will enter Paradise. Surely, they are both easy yet few act upon them. Glorify Allah at the end of every prayer ten times, praise Him ten times, and exalt Him ten times. These are one hundred and fifty upon the tongue, but one thousand and five hundred upon the Scale. When you retire to your bed, glorify Him, exalt Him, and praise Him one hundred times. These are one hundred upon the tongue, but one thousand upon the Scale. Which one of you would commit two thousand and five hundred sins in a day and night?” They said, “How could we not preserve them?” The Prophet said, “Satan comes to one of you while he is praying and he whispers for him to remember this and that until he turns away and, perhaps, he does not do it. While in his bed, Satan continues to lure him to sleep until he falls asleep.”
q: There are two practices no Muslim man preserves but that he will enter Paradise. Surely, they are both easy yet few act upon them. Glorify Allah at the end of every prayer ten times, praise Him ten times, and exalt Him ten times. These are one hundred and fifty upon the tongue, but one thousand and five hundred upon the Scale. When you retire to your bed, glorify Him, exalt Him, and praise Him one hundred times. These are one hundred upon the tongue, but one thousand upon the Scale. Which one of you would commit two thousand and five hundred sins in a day and night? … “Satan comes to one of you while he is praying and he whispers for him to remember this and that until he turns away and, perhaps, he does not do it. While in his bed, Satan continues to lure him to sleep until he falls asleep.

title: Hadith on Hajj: Pilgrimage purifies from sins and poverty
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Perform the Hajj and ‘Umrah pilgrimages, one after another, for they both erase poverty and sins just as the furnace removes impurity from iron, gold, and silver. There is no reward for an accepted Hajj but Paradise.”
q: Perform the Hajj and ‘Umrah pilgrimages, one after another, for they both erase poverty and sins just as the furnace removes impurity from iron, gold, and silver. There is no reward for an accepted Hajj but Paradise.

title: Hadith on Begging: Prohibition of persistently asking without need
t: Ja’far reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever would abstain from asking people, Allah will make him abstinent. Whoever would be independent, Allah will make him independent. Whoever begs people while he owns an amount of five ounces of silver, he has asked importunately.”
q: Whoever would abstain from asking people, Allah will make him abstinent. Whoever would be independent, Allah will make him independent. Whoever begs people while he owns an amount of five ounces of silver, he has asked importunately.

title: Hadith on Independence: Allah’s aid in self-sufficiency from begging
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever would be independent, Allah Almighty will make him independent. Whoever would abstain from asking people, Allah Almighty will make him abstinent. Whoever is content with sufficiency, Allah Almighty will suffice him.”
q: Whoever would be independent, Allah Almighty will make him independent. Whoever would abstain from asking people, Allah Almighty will make him abstinent. Whoever is content with sufficiency, Allah Almighty will suffice him.

title: Hadith on Truths: Three universal facts to swear upon
t: Abdur Rahman ibn ‘Awf reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, there are three I would swear an oath upon. Charity does not decrease wealth, so give in charity. No servant forgives wrongdoing, by which he seeks the countenance of Allah, but that Allah will increase his honor on the Day of Resurrection. And no servant opens the door of begging but that Allah will open the door of poverty.”
q: By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, there are three I would swear an oath upon. Charity does not decrease wealth, so give in charity. No servant forgives wrongdoing, by which he seeks the countenance of Allah, but that Allah will increase his honor on the Day of Resurrection. And no servant opens the door of begging but that Allah will open the door of poverty.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Charity: Three kinds of hands
t: Malik ibn Nadlah: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The hands are three types: the Hand of Allah is the highest, the hand of the giver is next to it, and the hand of the beggar is the lowest. Give from your surplus wealth and do not be weakened by your ego.”
q: The hands are three types: the Hand of Allah is the highest, the hand of the giver is next to it, and the hand of the beggar is the lowest. Give from your surplus wealth and do not be weakened by your ego.

title: Hadith on Independence: Working for a living far better than begging
t: Al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “For one of you to take his rope and carry a bundle of wood to sell, by which Allah preserves his dignity, is better than begging from people who may give or withhold.”
q: For one of you to take his rope and carry a bundle of wood to sell, by which Allah preserves his dignity, is better than begging from people who may give or withhold.

title: Hadith on Qadr: The Prophet never blamed his servants
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: I served the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, for ten years. He never blamed me if he ordered me to do something and I missed it or lost it. If someone in the household blamed me, the Prophet would say, “Leave him alone, for if it has been decreed, it is as it should be.”
q: Leave him alone, for if it has been decreed, it is as it should be.

title: Hadith on Dua: Ask Allah for faith with good character
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, I ask You for the health of my faith, such faith with good character, and salvation followed by success, Your mercy, Your wellness, Your forgiveness, and Your pleasure.”
q: O Allah, I ask You for the health of my faith, such faith with good character, and salvation followed by success, Your mercy, Your wellness, Your forgiveness, and Your pleasure.

title: Hadith on Qadr: Happiness in being pleased with Allah’s decrees
t: Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among the happiness of the son of Adam is to be satisfied with what Allah has decreed for him. Among the misery of the son of Adam is to abandon asking Allah for guidance, and among the misery of the son of Adam is displeasure with what Allah has decreed for him.”
q: Among the happiness of the son of Adam is to be satisfied with what Allah has decreed for him. Among the misery of the son of Adam is to abandon asking Allah for guidance, and among the misery of the son of Adam is displeasure with what Allah has decreed for him.

title: Hadith on Contentment: Allah blesses those pleased with His decrees
t: Abu al-‘Ala’ reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah will put His servants to trial in what He gives them. Whoever is pleased with what Allah has apportioned for him, then Allah will bless him in it and expand it. Whoever is not pleased, he will never be blessed in it.”
q: Verily, Allah will put His servants to trial in what He gives them. Whoever is pleased with what Allah has apportioned for him, then Allah will bless him in it and expand it. Whoever is not pleased, he will never be blessed in it.

title: Hadith on Hidayah: The Prophet completes guidance for the Ummah
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Nothing remains to bring you closer to Paradise and further from the Hellfire but that I have made it clear to you.”
q: Nothing remains to bring you closer to Paradise and further from the Hellfire but that I have made it clear to you.

title: Hadith on Shaytan: Satan lies in wait for you to enter the mosque
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, one of you enters the mosque, and Satan mounts him just as a man mounts his animal. If Satan becomes settled, he will collar him or bridle him.” Abu Huraira said, “You can witness this. As for the collar, it is that you see him filled with thoughts of whatever such that he does not remember Allah. As for the bridle, his mouth will open, but he does not remember Allah.”
q: Verily, one of you enters the mosque, and Satan mounts him just as a man mounts his animal. If Satan becomes settled, he will collar him or bridle him.

title: Hadith on Parents: Blessed is one who treats parents well
t: Mu’adh ibn Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Blessed is one who is good to his parents. Allah Almighty will extend his lifespan.”
q: Blessed is one who is good to his parents. Allah Almighty will extend his lifespan

title: Hadith on Haram: The Prophet warning us of tempting sins
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has not forbidden matters but that He knows you will be tempted towards them. Thus, I have taken it upon myself to prohibit you lest you fall into the Hellfire just like the falling of a moth or fly.”
q: Verily, Allah has not forbidden matters but that He knows you will be tempted towards them. Thus, I have taken it upon myself to prohibit you lest you fall into the Hellfire just like the falling of a moth or fly.

title: Fudayl on Music: Singing tempts people to commit adultery
t: Al-Husayn ibn Abdur Rahman reported: Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Singing is the invocation of adulterers.”

title: Urwah on Patience: ‘Urwah’s leg is amputated, he praises Allah
t: Al-Zuhri reported: When ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah have mercy on him, was afflicted with gangrene in his leg, it was said, “Shall we not call a doctor for you?” ‘Urawh said, “If you wish.” A doctor arrived and he said, “Drink this substance. It will ease your mind.” ‘Urwah said, “Go away with your drink. I do not think anyone could drink such a substance but to lose their mind until they no longer know their Lord.” Al-Zuhri said, “A saw was placed over his left leg and while we around him, we do not even hear him wince.” When the leg had been amputated, it made ‘Urwah say, “O Lord, You have taken from me, yet You have still left more to remain. If You have put me to trial, You have still granted me health.” Al-Zuhri said, “’Urwah still recited his portion of the Qur’an that night.”
s: al-Maraḍ wa al-kaffārāt li-Ibn Abī al-Dunyā 135

title: Hadith on Islam: Best Muslims have good character, patience, tolerance
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: It was said to the Prophet, “O Messenger of Allah, whose Islam is best?” The Prophet said, “The patient and tolerant.” It was said, “Which believers have the most complete faith?” The Prophet said, “Those with the best character.”
q: The patient and tolerant. … Those with the best character.

title: Hadith on Beauty: Islam beautified by patient and tolerance
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Islam is beautified by two qualities: modesty and tolerance for the sake of Allah, and not for anyone else.”
q: Islam is beautified by two qualities: modesty and tolerance for the sake of Allah, and not for anyone else

title: Hasan on Dunya: Love of worldly life is root of all evil
t: Hisham reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Love of the worldly life is the head of every sin.”

title: Ali on Ignorance: When to say Allah knows best
t: Razin Abi al-Nu’man reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “When you are asked about what you do not know, then flee.” It was said, “O leader of the faithful, how does one flee?” Ali said, “That you say: Allah knows best.”

title: Hadith on Greed: Seek refuge in Allah from avarice, covetousness
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Seek refuge in Allah from avarice that leads to disgrace, from avarice that leads to what should not be coveted, and from avarice where there is nothing to covet.”
q: Seek refuge in Allah from avarice that leads to disgrace, from avarice that leads to what should not be coveted, and from avarice where there is nothing to covet.

title: Hadith on Tawakkul: Trust in Allah, but do not store to excess
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered the room of Bilal and he found a pile of dates with him. The Prophet said, “What is this, O Bilal?” Bilal said, “They are dates I have stored for you.” The Prophet said, “Woe to you, O Bilal! Are you not afraid they will become your fumes in the Hellfire? Spend them in charity, O Bilal, and do not fear that the One upon the Throne will leave you bereft.”
q: What is this, O Bilal? … Woe to you, O Bilal! Are you not afraid they will become your fumes in the Hellfire? Spend them in charity, O Bilal, and do not fear that the One upon the Throne will leave you bereft.

title: Hadith on Desires: Be careful what you wish for
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you has a desire, let him be careful what he wishes for. He does not know which of his desires will be decreed for him.”
q: If one of you has a desire, let him be careful what he wishes for. He does not know which of his desires will be decreed for him.

title: Hadith on Hearts: Good and evil do not combine in the heart
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Faith and unbelief cannot be combined together in the heart of a man, nor can dishonesty and truthfulness be combined together, nor can treachery and trustworthiness be combined together.”
q: Faith and unbelief cannot be combined together in the heart of a man, nor can dishonesty and truthfulness be combined together, nor can treachery and trustworthiness be combined together.

title: Hadith on Halal: Seeking lawful is an obligation on all Muslims
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Seeking the lawful is a duty upon every Muslim.”
q: Seeking the lawful is a duty upon every Muslim.

title: Hadith on Haram: Charity from unlawful wealth not accepted
t: Al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymirah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever acquires wealth by sinning to serve his family, or give in charity, or spend in the way of Allah, then Allah will gather all of it together and cast it into Hell.”
q: Whoever acquires wealth by sinning to serve his family, or give in charity, or spend in the way of Allah, then Allah will gather all of it together and cast it into Hell.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Faith: Honor the guest, guard the neighbor
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him protect his neighbor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak goodness or remain silent.”
q: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him protect his neighbor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak goodness or remain silent.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Umar on Taqwa: Fear Allah, control anger and desires
t: Abu Abdullah al-Khurasani reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever fears Allah does not vent his anger, and whoever is mindful of Allah does not do whatever he desires.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Optimism: Best virtue to have good assumptions about Allah
t: Khaythamah reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “By the One besides whom there is no God, a believing servant is not given anything better than good thoughts about Allah Almighty. By the One besides whom there is no God, a servant does not improve his opinion of Allah Almighty except that Allah will give him what he assumes. That is because all good is in His hands.”

title: Hadith on Rifq: Allah loves gentleness in all things
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is gentle and He loves gentleness in all matters.”
q: Verily, Allah is gentle and He loves gentleness in all matters.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplicate even if you have debt like mountains
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not teach you a prayer which, if you supplicated by it, Allah would discharge your debt from you even if it were like the size of a mountain? Say: O Allah, the Absolute Sovereign, You grant sovereignty to whomever You will and deny sovereignty to whomever You will. You empower whomever You will and subjugate whomever You will. All goodness is in Your hand, for You alone have power over all things. The Most Merciful of the world and the Hereafter, You give from them both to whomever You will and withhold from them both to whomever You will. Have mercy upon me with such mercy that will free me from anyone else besides You.”
q: Shall I not teach you a prayer which, if you supplicated by it, Allah would discharge your debt from you even if it were like the size of a mountain? Say: O Allah, the Absolute Sovereign, You grant sovereignty to whomever You will and deny sovereignty to whomever You will. You empower whomever You will and subjugate whomever You will. All goodness is in Your hand, for You alone have power over all things. The Most Merciful of the world and the Hereafter, You give from them both to whomever You will and withhold from them both to whomever You will. Have mercy upon me with such mercy that will free me from anyone else besides You.

title: Khazzaz on Waqt: Ruminating on the past wastes precious time
t: Muhammad al-Kattani reported: Abu Sa’id al-Khazzaz, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Ruminating on a past moment is to lose a second moment.”

title: Hadith on Salat: Set prayer rows in order, close the gaps
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Establish the rows for prayer, stand shoulder to shoulder, close the gaps, accommodate your brethren, and do not leave any breaches for Satan. Whoever connects a row, Allah will connect with him. Whoever breaks a row, Allah will break from him.”
q: Establish the rows for prayer, stand shoulder to shoulder, close the gaps, accommodate your brethren, and do not leave any breaches for Satan. Whoever connects a row, Allah will connect with him. Whoever breaks a row, Allah will break from him.

title: Hadith on Tasbih: Earning a thousand good deeds in a single day
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Is one of you unable to earn one thousand good deeds each day? Let him glorify Allah one hundred times. Thus, it will be recorded for him as one thousand good deeds, or one thousand bad deeds will be erased.”
q: Is one of you unable to earn one thousand good deeds each day? Let him glorify Allah one hundred times. Thus, it will be recorded for him as one thousand good deeds, or one thousand bad deeds will be erased.

title: Hadith on Trials: Ranks in Paradise elevated by hardship, if not deeds
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, a man may have a rank with Allah that he does not achieve by his good deeds. Thus, Allah continues to put him to trial with what he hates until he reaches the rank destined for him.”
q: Verily, a man may have a rank with Allah that he does not achieve by his good deeds. Thus, Allah continues to put him to trial with what he hates until he reaches the rank destined for him.

title: Hadith on Quran: Recite and ascend in Paradise with every verse
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It will be said to the companion of the Quran when he enters Paradise: Recite and ascend! Thus, he will recite and ascend one level for each verse until he recites the last one with him.”
q: It will be said to the companion of the Quran when he enters Paradise: Recite and ascend! Thus, he will recite and ascend one level for each verse until he recites the last one with him.

title: Hadith on Relief: Prayer of Yunus to relieve worldly distress
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Shall I not tell you of something by which a man among you can supplicate to relieve the hardships or trials of the world when they descend?” They said, “Of course!” The Prophet said, “It is the prayer of Jonah, Dhul Nun: There is no God but You, glory be to You for I have certainly been among the wrongdoers.” (21:87)
q: Shall I not tell you of something by which a man among you can supplicate to relieve the hardships or trials of the world when they descend? … It is the prayer of Jonah, Dhul Nun: There is no God but You, glory be to You for I have certainly been among the wrongdoers.

title: Hadith on Mercy: Compassion Allah placed within His servants
t: Usamah ibn Zayd reported: One of the daughters of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent a messenger calling for him and telling him that her child or son was on the verge of death. The Prophet said to the messenger, “Return to her and tell her that it is for Allah Almighty to take and to give, for all things have an appointed term with Him. Enjoin her to be patient and hope for reward from Allah.” She sent the messenger again, swearing by Allah that he must come. When the child was presented to him, his breath quivered as if it were within a water-skin. The Prophet’s eyes were overcome with tears. Sa’d said, “O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “This is mercy which Allah has placed in the hearts of His servants. Verily, Allah is only merciful to His merciful servants.”
q: Return to her and tell her that it is for Allah Almighty to take and to give, for all things have an appointed term with Him. Enjoin her to be patient and hope for reward from Allah. … This is mercy which Allah has placed in the hearts of His servants. Verily, Allah is only merciful to His merciful servants.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Oaths: Warning against violating rights by false testimony
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No man misappropriates the right of another Muslim using a false oath but that Allah will obligate his entrance into Hellfire and forbid his entrance into Paradise.” A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, even if it is something insignificant?” The Prophet said, “Even if it is a twig of an Arak tree.”
q: No man misappropriates the right of another Muslim using a false oath but that Allah will obligate his entrance into Hellfire and forbid his entrance into Paradise. … Even if it is a twig of an Arak tree.

title: Hadith on Jihad: Supporting family and oneself in the way of Allah
t: Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah reported: A man passed by the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the companions of the Messenger of Allah saw his endurance and vigor. They said, “O Messenger of Allah, if only this man was acting in the way of Allah!” The Prophet said, “If he goes out striving for his small children, he is in the way of Allah. If he goes out striving for his elderly parents, he is in the way of Allah. If he goes out striving for himself to abstain from wrongdoing, he is in the way of Allah. If he goes out vainly and boasting, he is in the way of Satan.”
q: If he goes out striving for his small children, he is in the way of Allah. If he goes out striving for his elderly parents, he is in the way of Allah. If he goes out striving for himself to abstain from wrongdoing, he is in the way of Allah. If he goes out vainly and boasting, he is in the way of Satan.

title: ‘Amir on Salat: Do you talk to your Nafs in prayer?
t: Abu al-Husayn reported: It was said to ‘Amir ibn Abdul Qays, may Allah have mercy on him, “Do you talk to yourself in prayer?” ‘Amir said, “Yes. I tell myself to stand in front of the Lord Almighty and to turn away from what is in front of Him.”

title: Wahb on Time: Four moments of the day to not neglect
t: Sufyan reported: Wahb ibn Munabbih, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, in the wisdom of the household of David it is written that it is a duty upon a wise person to not neglect four moments: a time in which to privately converse with one’s Lord Almighty, a time to hold oneself accountable, a time to come to his brothers who tell him about his faults and tell him the truth about himself, and a time for himself to spend in recreation, lawfully and appropriately.”

title: Hadith on Sins: Believers recompensed in the world for their sins
t: Abu Bakr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Afflictions, diseases, and sadness in the world are a recompense for sins.”
q: Afflictions, diseases, and sadness in the world are a recompense for sins.

title: Ma’ruf on Dua: O Allah, guide sinners to repentance
t:
Ibrahim ibn al-Utrush reported: Ma’ruf al-Karkhi, may Allah have mercy on him, was upon the Tigris river, and we were with him as we passed by some people on a boat misbehaving, singing and beating drums. We said to Ma’ruf, “O Abu Mahfuz, do you not see these people on the water disobeying Allah Almighty? Pray to Allah against them!” Ma’ruf raised his hands to the sky, saying, “O Allah, my God, my Master! O Allah, I ask You to bring them joy in the Hereafter as You have brought them joy in the world!” One of his companions said, “We asked you to pray against them! We did not ask you to pray for them!” Ma’ruf said, “If Allah brings them joy in the Hereafter, then He has accepted their repentance. It will not harm you at all!”

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “From this topic is the saying of Allah Almighty: O believers! Do not let some ridicule others, they may be better than them, nor let some women ridicule other women, they may be better than them. Do not defame one another, nor call each other by offensive nicknames. How evil it is to act rebelliously after having faith! And whoever does not repent, it is they who are the true wrongdoers. O believers! Avoid many suspicions, for indeed, some suspicions are sinful. And do not spy, nor backbite one another. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of their dead brother? You would despise that! And fear Allah. Surely, Allah is the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful.” (49:11-12)
q: O believers! Do not let some ridicule others, they may be better than them, nor let some women ridicule other women, they may be better than them. Do not defame one another, nor call each other by offensive nicknames. How evil it is to act rebelliously after having faith! And whoever does not repent, it is they who are the true wrongdoers. O believers! Avoid many suspicions, for indeed, some suspicions are sinful. And do not spy, nor backbite one another. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of their dead brother? You would despise that! And fear Allah. Surely, Allah is the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful.

title: Wahb on Iblees: Satan plays with anger like a child with a ball
t: Mundhir reported: Wahb ibn Munabbih, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Satan, upon whom is the curse of Allah, said: Verily, we lie in wait among the people of impatience and fury, then we play with them as children play with a ball.”

title: Malik on Patience: A good deed accomplished brings relief and comfort
t: Rabah ibn ‘Amr reported: Malik ibn Dinar, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “There is no righteous deed but that an obstacle is in front of it. If one is patient, he will break through to comfort, but if he is intimidated, he will turn back.”

title: Hadith on Dua: A supplication beneath the Throne of Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not direct you to a word among the treasures of Paradise beneath the Throne? There is no movement or might but in Allah. Allah says: My servant has completely surrendered to Me.”
q: Shall I not direct you to a word among the treasures of Paradise beneath the Throne? There is no movement or might but in Allah. Allah says: My servant has completely surrendered to Me.

title: Hadith on Riba: Usury increases wealth, decreases rewards in Hereafter
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one increases his wealth by usury except that his result will be little.”
q: No one increases his wealth by usury except that his result will be little.

title: Hadith on Dunya: Leave the worldly life for its people
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Leave the world to its people. Whoever takes from the world more than what suffices him, he has taken a portion of his ruin while he is unaware.”
q: Leave the world to its people. Whoever takes from the world more than what suffices him, he has taken a portion of his ruin while he is unaware.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-San’ani

title: Hadith on Halal: Lawful food is clear, unspoken matters are pardoned
t: Salman al-Farisi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about eating ghee, cheese, and wild donkeys. The Prophet said, “The lawful is what Allah has made lawful in His Book and the unlawful is what Allah has made unlawful in His book. Whatever He has been silent over has been pardoned.”
q: The lawful is what Allah has made lawful in His Book and the unlawful is what Allah has made unlawful in His book. Whatever He has been silent over has been pardoned

title: Hadith on Halal: Lawful and unlawful are clear, leave doubtful matters
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear. Thus, leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.”
q: The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear. Thus, leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Seeking protection from Hellfire
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No servant seeks protection from the Hellfire seven times in a day but that the Hellfire says: O Lord, Your servant has sought Your protection from me, so protect him! No servant asks Allah for Paradise seven times in a day but that Paradise says: O Lord, Your servant has asked for me, so admit him!”
q: No servant seeks protection from the Hellfire seven times in a day but that the Hellfire says: O Lord, Your servant has sought Your protection from me, so protect him! No servant asks Allah for Paradise seven times in a day but that Paradise says: O Lord, Your servant has asked for me, so admit him!

title: Hadith on Sunnah: The Prophet speaks as if to say farewell
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us one day as if to say farewell. The Prophet said, “I am Muhammad, the unlettered prophet. There is no prophet after me. I have been given words that are eloquent, comprehensive, and decisive. I know how many angels guard the Hellfire and carry the Throne. Leniency came through me and I was pardoned along with my nation. Thus, listen and obey me as long as I am among you. When I am taken away, then you must adhere to the Book of Allah. Make lawful what it declares to be lawful and forbid what it declares to be forbidden.”
q: I am Muhammad, the unlettered prophet. There is no prophet after me. I have been given words that are eloquent, comprehensive, and decisive. I know how many angels guard the Hellfire and carry the Throne. Leniency came through me and I was pardoned along with my nation. Thus, listen and obey me as long as I am among you. When I am taken away, then you must adhere to the Book of Allah. Make lawful what it declares to be lawful and forbid what it declares to be forbidden.

title: Hadith on Dua: Words of prayer better than gold and silver
t: Shaddad ibn Aws reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you see people amassing gold and silver, then amass these words: O Allah, I ask You for firmness in the matter and determination upon guidance. I ask You for gratitude over Your blessings, I ask You to help me worship You in the best manner, I ask You for a pure heart, and I ask You for a truthful tongue. I ask You for the goodness that You know, I seek refuge in You from the evil that You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know. Verily, You alone are All-Knowing of the Unseen.”
q: When you see people amassing gold and silver, then amass these words: O Allah, I ask You for firmness in the matter and determination upon guidance. I ask You for gratitude over Your blessings, I ask You to help me worship You in the best manner, I ask You for a pure heart, and I ask You for a truthful tongue. I ask You for the goodness that You know, I seek refuge in You from the evil that You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know. Verily, You alone are All-Knowing of the Unseen.

title: Hadith on Explotation: Warning of profit at a Muslim’s expense
t: Al-Mustawrid reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever eats so much as a morsel at the expense of a Muslim’s reputation, then Allah will feed him the likes of it in Hell. Whoever clothes himself with a garment at the expense of a Muslim’s reputation, then Allah will clothe him with the likes of it in Hell. Whoever stands in a position of repute and fame at the expense of a man, then Allah will make him stand in a position of dishonor and infamy on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever eats so much as a morsel at the expense of a Muslim’s reputation, then Allah will feed him the likes of it in Hell. Whoever clothes himself with a garment at the expense of a Muslim’s reputation, then Allah will clothe him with the likes of it in Hell. Whoever stands in a position of repute and fame at the expense of a man, then Allah will make him stand in a position of dishonor and infamy on the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Hearts: True wealth is not outward, rather in the heart
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Richness does not exist outwardly. Verily, true richness is the richness of the soul. If Allah wills goodness for a servant, He places richness in his soul and righteousness in his heart. If Allah wills harm for a servant, He places poverty between his eyes.”
q: Richness does not exist outwardly. Verily, true richness is the richness of the soul. If Allah wills goodness for a servant, He places richness in his soul and righteousness in his heart. If Allah wills harm for a servant, He places poverty between his eyes.

title: Hadith on Firdaws: One hundred levels in Paradise beneath the Throne
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever fasts the month of Ramadan, performs the prayers, and makes the Hajj pilgrimage to the House, it is a duty upon Allah to forgive him whether he emigrates in the path of Allah or remains in the land of his birth.” Mu’adh said, “Shall I not tell the people?” The Prophet said, “Leave them to work. Verily, there are one hundred levels in Paradise, the distance between them like the heavens and the earth. Al-Firdaws is the highest and most ideal level, for above that is the Throne of the Most Merciful and from it flow the rivers of Paradise. When you ask from Allah, ask for Al-Firdaws.”
q: Whoever fasts the month of Ramadan, performs the prayers, and makes the Hajj pilgrimage to the House, it is a duty upon Allah to forgive him whether he emigrates in the path of Allah or remains in the land of his birth. … Leave them to work. Verily, there are one hundred levels in Paradise, the distance between them like the heavens and the earth. Al-Firdaws is the highest and most ideal level, for above that is the Throne of the Most Merciful and from it flow the rivers of Paradise. When you ask from Allah, ask for Al-Firdaws.

title: Dawud on Taqwa: Faith is richness in your heart without wealth
t: Muhammad ibn Yahya reported: Dawud al-Ta’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A servant does not leave the disgrace of disobedience to the honor of righteousness except that he will be enriched without wealth, he will be strengthened without a tribe, and he will be entertained without company.”

title: Hadith on Ma’ruf: Good deeds protect from ruin in the Hereafter
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Good works done for people protect those who did them from evil fates, harm, and destruction. The people of goodness in the world will be the people of goodness in the Hereafter.”
q: Good works done for people protect those who did them from evil fates, harm, and destruction. The people of goodness in the world will be the people of goodness in the Hereafter.

title: Hadith on Privacy: Be obedient to Allah even when you are alone
t: Usamah ibn Sharik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whatever Allah hates for you to do, then do not do it in private.”
q: Whatever Allah hates for you to do, then do not do it in private.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Islam: Parable of straight path, open doors, and curtains
t: Al-Nawwas ibn Sam’an reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah strikes a parable of the straight path. On either side of the path are walls with open doors over which are hanging curtains. Upon the gate of the path is a caller, saying, ‘O people! Enter the straight path altogether and do not divert to the side!’ A caller is placed above the path and when anyone intends to open those doors in the slightest, he says, ‘Woe to you! Do not open it or else you will enter it!’ The path is Islam, the curtains are the limits of Allah, and the open doors are the prohibitions of Allah. The caller at the head of the path is the Book of Allah, and the caller above the path is an admonition from Allah in the heart of every Muslim.”
q: Allah strikes a parable of the straight path. On either side of the path are walls with open doors over which are hanging curtains. Upon the gate of the path is a caller, saying, ‘O people! Enter the straight path altogether and do not divert to the side!’ A caller is placed above the path and when anyone intends to open those doors in the slightest, he says, ‘Woe to you! Do not open it or else you will enter it!’ The path is Islam, the curtains are the limits of Allah, and the open doors are the prohibitions of Allah. The caller at the head of the path is the Book of Allah, and the caller above the path is an admonition from Allah in the heart of every Muslim.

title: Hadith on Sunnah: No permission to violate rights of Ahl al-Kitab
t: Al-‘Irbad ibn Sariyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No doubt, by Allah, I have admonished you, commanded you, and prohibited you from things like those in the Quran or even more. Verily, Allah Almighty has not made it lawful for you to enter the houses of the People of the Book without their permission, nor strike their women, nor eat from their fruits if they give you what is due upon them.”
q: No doubt, by Allah, I have admonished you, commanded you, and prohibited you from things like those in the Quran or even more. Verily, Allah Almighty has not made it lawful for you to enter the houses of the People of the Book without their permission, nor strike their women, nor eat from their fruits if they give you what is due upon them.

title: Hadith on Faith: Virtue of believers who never saw the Prophet
t: Abu Jumu’ah reported: We ate a meal with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and Abu ‘Ubadah al-Jarrah was with us. Abu ‘Ubadah said, “O Messenger of Allah, is there anyone better than us? We embraced Islam and waged jihad with you.” The Prophet said, “Yes, people will come after you who have faith in me but never saw me.”
q: Yes, people will come after you who have faith in me but never saw me.

title: Hadith on Ummah: Allah protects the Muslims from three disasters
t: Abu Malik al-Ash’ari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has protected you from three calamities: that your Prophet supplicate against you and thus you all perish, that the people of falsehood prevail over the people of truth, and that you would unite upon misguidance.”
q: Verily, Allah has protected you from three calamities: that your Prophet supplicate against you and thus you all perish, that the people of falsehood prevail over the people of truth, and that you would unite upon misguidance.

title: Hadith on Sincerity: Three virtues to protect from malice
t: Zayd ibn Thabit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are three qualities by which malice cannot enter the heart of a Muslim: sincere deeds for Allah, goodwill to the leaders of the Muslims, and keeping to the united community. Verily, their call to Islam is protected behind them.”
q: There are three qualities by which malice cannot enter the heart of a Muslim: sincere deeds for Allah, goodwill to the leaders of the Muslims, and keeping to the united community. Verily, their call to Islam is protected behind them.

title: Hassan on Bid’ah: Every religious innovation replaces a Sunnah like it
t: Al-Awza’i reported: Hassan ibn ‘Atiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “No people fabricate an innovation in their religion but that Allah will remove a Sunnah from like it, then it will never come back to them until the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Hadith on Bid’ah: Warning against glorifying innovators in religion
t: Ibrahim ibn Maysarah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever honors a heretical innovator has aided in the destruction of Islam.”
q: Whoever honors a heretical innovator has aided in the destruction of Islam.

title: Hadith on Islam: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As pledges allegiance to the Prophet
t: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As reported: I came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and I said, “Stretch out your hand that I may pledge allegiance to you.” The Prophet reached out but I clenched my hand. The Prophet said, “What is the matter with you, O ‘Amr?” I said, “I wish to make a condition.” The Prophet said, “What is your condition?” I said, “That I will be forgiven.” The Prophet said, “Did you not know that Islam demolishes the sins before it? And that emigration demolishes the sins before it? And that the Hajj pilgrimage demolishes the sins before it?”
q: What is the matter with you, O ‘Amr? … What is your condition? … Did you not know that Islam demolishes the sins before it? And that emigration demolishes the sins before it? And that the Hajj pilgrimage demolishes the sins before it?

title: Hadith on Islam: Believers obedient to commands of Allah
t: Makhul reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believers are easy-going and gentle, like a camel tethered by its nose. If he is restricted, he is submissive. If he is made to kneel upon a rock, he will comply.”
q: The believers are easy-going and gentle, like a camel tethered by its nose. If he is restricted, he is submissive. If he is made to kneel upon a rock, he will comply.

title: Hadith on Believers: Amazing faith of those who never saw Prophets
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Who in creation has the most astonishing faith?” They said, “The angels.” The Prophet said, “But how could the angels not believe?” They said, “The prophets.” The Prophet said, “But the prophets were given divine revelation, so how could they not believe?” They said, “Their companions.” The Prophet said, “The companions were with their prophets, so how could they not believe? Rather, the people with the most astonishing faith are those who come after you and they find a book of divine revelation, thus they believe in it and follow it. They are the people with the most astonishing faith.”
q: Who in creation has the most astonishing faith? … But how could the angels not believe? … But the prophets were given divine revelation, so how could they not believe? … The companions were with their prophets, so how could they not believe? Rather, the people with the most astonishing faith are those who come after you and they find a book of divine revelation, thus they believe in it and follow it. They are the people with the most astonishing faith.

title: Hadith on Doubt: Recite the verses of Allah if you are in doubt
t: Abu Zumayl reported: I asked Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, saying, “What is this I find in my chest?” Ibn Abbas said, “If you find any doubt within yourself, then recite the verse: He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He has knowledge of all things.” (57:3)
q: He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He has knowledge of all things.

title: Hadith on Salvation: Every believer is eventually taken out of Hell
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever has the weight of an atom of faith in his heart will be taken out of the Hellfire.” Abu Sa’id said, “Thus, whoever is in doubt, let him recite the verse: Verily, Allah does no wrong even the weight of an atom.” (4:40)
q: Whoever has the weight of an atom of faith in his heart will be taken out of the Hellfire. … : Verily, Allah does no wrong even the weight of an atom.

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Faith leaves until repentance of major sins
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The adulterer is not a believer while he commits adultery. The thief is not a believer while he is stealing. The drinker of wine is not a believer while he is drinking, yet repentance is possible thereafter.”
q: The adulterer is not a believer while he commits adultery. The thief is not a believer while he is stealing. The drinker of wine is not a believer while he is drinking, yet repentance is possible thereafter.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Declaring Allah’s oneness protects from Hell
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever testified that there is no God but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, then Allah will forbid him from the Hellfire.”
q: Whoever testified that there is no God but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, then Allah will forbid him from the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Tasbih: Glorifying Allah daily erases many sins
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever declares the glory of Allah and His praises one hundred times in a day, his sins will be diminished even if they are like the foam of the sea.”
q: Whoever declares the glory of Allah and His praises one hundred times in a day, his sins will be diminished even if they are like the foam of the sea.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jannah: The Prophet takes them by the hand into Paradise
t: Al-Munaydhir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever says when he awakens in the morning, ‘I am pleased with Allah as a Lord, with Islam as a religion, and with Muhammad as a prophet,’ then I am responsible for him and I will surely take him by the hand until he enters Paradise.”
q: Whoever says when he awakens in the morning, ‘I am pleased with Allah as a Lord, with Islam as a religion, and with Muhammad as a prophet,’ then I am responsible for him and I will surely take him by the hand until he enters Paradise.

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for forgiveness before sleeping
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever says when he retires to his bed, ‘There is no God but Allah alone without any partners, to Him belong the dominion and praise and He is powerful over all things, there is no movement or might but in Allah, glory be to Allah and all praise is due to Allah, there is not God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest,’ then Allah will forgive his sins even if they were like the foam of the sea.”
q: Whoever says when he retires to his bed, ‘There is no God but Allah alone without any partners, to Him belong the dominion and praise and He is powerful over all things, there is no movement or might but in Allah, glory be to Allah and all praise is due to Allah, there is not God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest,’ then Allah will forgive his sins even if they were like the foam of the sea.

title: Aisha on Istighfar: Blessed to ask Allah’s forgiveness many times
t: Safiyyah reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “Blessed is one who finds many prayers for forgiveness on their record.”

title: Hasan on Arguing: They were bored with worship, so they argued
t: Ahmad ibn Hanbal reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, heard some people arguing and he said, “By Allah! These are not but people who are bored with worship and they found speaking easier upon them than acting. Their piety diminished and thus they speak.”

title: Hadith on Family: Paradise forbidden for those who cut off family ties
t: Sa’id ibn Zayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, this womb is derived from the name of the Most Merciful. Whoever severs its relations, Allah will forbid him from entering Paradise.”
q: Verily, this womb is derived from the name of the Most Merciful. Whoever severs its relations, Allah will forbid him from entering Paradise.

title: Hadith on Family: The womb testifies on the Day of Judgment
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The womb will be presented on the Day of Resurrection. It will have a staff like a spindle and it will speak with a clear and articulate tongue. It will maintain whoever maintained its relations, and it will cut off whoever cut off its relations.”
q: The womb will be presented on the Day of Resurrection. It will have a staff like a spindle and it will speak with a clear and articulate tongue. It will maintain whoever maintained its relations, and it will cut off whoever cut off its relations.

title: Hadith on Family: Allah maintains relations if family ties are respected
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the womb is a branch derived from the name of the Most Merciful. He will maintain whoever maintains its relations, and He will cut off whoever cuts off its relations.”
q: Verily, the womb is a branch derived from the name of the Most Merciful. He will maintain whoever maintains its relations, and He will cut off whoever cuts off its relations.

title: Hadith on Parents: Respect your father’s loved ones
t: Ibn Umar reported: He passed by a bedouin on a journey and the bedouin’s father had been a friend of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Umar said to the bedouin, “Are you not his son?” The bedouin said, “Of course.” Ibn Umar ordered that he be given a donkey from his entourage, and he took off his turban and gave it to him. Those who were with him said, “Would it not have been enough only to give him two coins?” Ibn Umar said, “The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Respect the loved ones of your father and do not cut them off, lest Allah extinguish your light.”
q: Respect the loved ones of your father and do not cut them off, lest Allah extinguish your light.

title: ‘Urwah on Ibrahim: Abraham never cursed anyone, his heart was pure
t: Hisham reported: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “O my son, do not fall into the habit of cursing others. Have you not seen that Abraham never cursed anyone? As Allah said: When he came to his Lord with a pure heart.” (37:84)
q: When he came to his Lord with a pure heart.

title: Hadith on Drinks: The Prophet loved cold, sweet drinks
t: Aisha reported: The most beloved drink to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was sweetened and cold.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Two inescapable consequences in Afterlife
t: Khuraym ibn Fatik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are two inevitabilities: The one who declares there is no God but Allah, or who is a believer in Allah, will enter Paradise, and the one who dies while associating partners with Allah will enter Hellfire.”
q: There are two inevitabilities: The one who declares there is no God but Allah, or who is a believer in Allah, will enter Paradise, and the one who dies while associating partners with Allah will enter Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Rivers of water, milk, honey, and wine in Paradise
t: Mu’awiyah ibn Haydah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, in Paradise there is a sea of water, a sea of honey, a sea of milk, and a sea of wine, and thereafter they branch into rivers.”
q: Verily, in Paradise there is a sea of water, a sea of honey, a sea of milk, and a sea of wine, and thereafter they branch into rivers.

title: Hadith on Meals: The Prophet ate a portion of dates every day
t: Aisha reported: The household of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, never ate two meals in a day but that one of them consisted of dates.

title: Hadith on Hajj: No unruly behavior when performing the pilgrimage
t: Qudamah ibn Abdullah reported: I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, upon a she-camel stoning the pillar at Hajj. There was no hitting, nor crowding, nor shouts to make way.

title: Hadith on Majlis: Supplication for forgiveness after leaving assembly
t: Abu al-‘Aliyah reported: They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what are the words we just heard you say?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “They are words that the Angel Gabriel, upon him be peace, taught me as an expiation for gatherings: Glory be to You, O Allah, with Your Praises. I bear witness there is no God but You, I seek Your forgiveness, and I repent to You.”
q: They are words that the Angel Gabriel, upon him be peace, taught me as an expiation for gatherings: Glory be to You, O Allah, with Your Praises. I bear witness there is no God but You, I seek Your forgiveness, and I repent to You.

title: Hadith on Generosity: The Prophet donates all of his money before sundown
t: Abdullah al-Hawzani reported: I met Bilal, the caller of prayer for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, at Aleppo and I said, “O Bilal, tell us about the spending of the Prophet.” Bilal said, “He would not have anything left. I was the one to manage it for him since Allah sent him until the day he died. If a Muslim came to him and he saw him naked, he would order me to depart, borrow money, and purchase a cloak for him, then I would clothe him and feed him.”

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: O Allah, make my character excellent
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, You have made my creation beautiful, thus make my character beautiful.”
q: O Allah, You have made my creation beautiful, thus make my character beautiful.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Abu ‘Awn on Salaf: Three statements of the righteous predecessors
t: Abu ‘Awn reported: Whenever the people of virtue would meet, they would enjoin each other with three sayings, and if they departed one another, they would write to each other with three sayings, “Whoever works for his Hereafter, Allah will suffice him in his worldly life. Whoever sets right what is between Allah and himself, Allah will suffice him among the people. Whoever sets right his inner-self, Allah will set right his outer-self.”

title: Umm Darda on Tafakkur: Abu Darda’s habit of contemplation
t: ‘Awn ibn Abdullah reported: I said to Umm Darda, may Allah be pleased with her, “What act of worship did Abu Darda perform most often?” Umm Darda said, “Reflection and consideration.”

title: Hadith on Leadership: Intense regret of sinful leaders on Judgment Day
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Woe to the rulers! Woe to the authorities! Woe to the trustees! Some people will wish their forelocks were hanging from the star of Pleiades on the Day of Resurrection, rather than had done anything they did.”
q: Woe to the rulers! Woe to the authorities! Woe to the trustees! Some people will wish their forelocks were hanging from the star of Pleiades on the Day of Resurrection, rather than had done anything they did.

title: Hadith on Leadership: Sinful leaders to meet Allah in chains
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No man is given authority over ten people or more but that he will come to Allah on the Day of Resurrection with his hands in shackles up to his neck. His freedom is his righteousness, or his imprisonment is his sin. The first of it is blame, the middle of it is regret, and the last of it is disgrace on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: No man is given authority over ten people or more but that he will come to Allah on the Day of Resurrection with his hands in shackles up to his neck. His freedom is his righteousness, or his imprisonment is his sin. The first of it is blame, the middle of it is regret, and the last of it is disgrace on the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Jannah: The Prophet with those who care for women
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever has three daughters, or three sisters, and he fears Allah regarding them and cares for them, he will be with me in Paradise like this,” and he held up his two fingers.
q: Whoever has three daughters, or three sisters, and he fears Allah regarding them and cares for them, he will be with me in Paradise like this,

title: Hadith on Wellness: Success is well-being in this life and the next
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, which supplication is best?” The Prophet said, “Ask your Lord for health and wellness in the world and in the Hereafter. If you are given wellness in the world and in the Hereafter, you have succeeded.”
q: Ask your Lord for health and wellness in the world and in the Hereafter. If you are given wellness in the world and in the Hereafter, you have succeeded.

title: Hadith on ‘Afiyah: Ask Allah for wellness in this life and next
t: Al-‘Abbas reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me something to ask Allah Almighty.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Ask Allah for wellness.” I waited for some days, then I came back, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me something.” The Prophet said to me, “O ‘Abbas! O uncle of the Messenger of Allah! Ask Allah for wellness in the world and the Hereafter.”
q: Ask Allah for wellness. … O ‘Abbas! O uncle of the Messenger of Allah! Ask Allah for wellness in the world and the Hereafter.

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Whoever worships Allah sincerely enters Paradise
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever says there is no God but Allah sincerely, he will be admitted into Paradise.”
q: Whoever says there is no God but Allah sincerely, he will be admitted into Paradise.

title: Hadith on Oaths: Swear by Allah and tell the truth
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Swear your oaths by Allah, be righteous, and tell the truth. Verily, Allah Almighty loves for oaths to be sworn by Him.”
q: Swear your oaths by Allah, be righteous, and tell the truth. Verily, Allah Almighty loves for oaths to be sworn by Him.

title: Hadith on Sahaba: Honor for the Companions and the Salaf
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Respect me in regards to my companions, then those who come after them, then those after them. Then, falsehood will spread until a man offers his testimony without being asked, and swears an oath without being asked.”
q: Respect me in regards to my companions, then those who come after them, then those after them. Then, falsehood will spread until a man offers his testimony without being asked, and swears an oath without being asked.

title: Hadith on Jumu’ah: Have presence at sermon, be near to Imam
t: Samurah ibn Jundub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be present at the sermon and come close to the Imam. Verily, a man continues to distance himself until he is delayed from Paradise, even though he will eventually enter it.”
q: Be present at the sermon and come close to the Imam. Verily, a man continues to distance himself until he is delayed from Paradise, even though he will eventually enter it.

title: Hadith on Honesty: The Prophet loves truthful speech
t: Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most beloved speech to me is the most truthful.”
q: The most beloved speech to me is the most truthful.

title: Hadith on Moderation: Do not excessively seek from the world
t: Abu Humayd al-Sa’idi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be moderate in seeking from the world, for everyone will be facilitated towards what has been decreed for him in it.”
q: Be moderate in seeking from the world, for everyone will be facilitated towards what has been decreed for him in it.

title: Hadith on Hudud: Avoid legal punishment unless it becomes public
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Avoid these filthy crimes that Allah has prohibited. Whoever commits one, let him seek concealment from Allah and repent to Allah. Verily, whoever shows us his deed, we will retaliate according to the Book of Allah.”
q: Avoid these filthy crimes that Allah has prohibited. Whoever commits one, let him seek concealment from Allah and repent to Allah. Verily, whoever shows us his deed, we will retaliate according to the Book of Allah.

title: Hadith on Intoxication: Avoid every intoxicating substance
t: Buraydah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Avoid all intoxicants.”
q: Avoid all intoxicants.

title: Hadith on Patience: Avoid being angry, avoid being angry
t: Humayd ibn Abdur Rahman reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “Tell me of a word I can live by but not so much that I forget.” The Prophet said, “Avoid being angry.” The man repeated his question, and the Prophet said, “Avoid being angry.”
q: Avoid being angry. … Avoid being angry.

title: Hadith on Ma’ruf: Never consider any good deed insignificant
t: Jabir ibn Sulaym reported: I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and I said, “O Messenger of Allah, instruct me.” The Prophet said, “Fear Allah and do not belittle any good deed, not even emptying your bucket in a cup for someone to drink or speaking to your brother with a cheerful face.”
q: Fear Allah and do not belittle any good deed, not even emptying your bucket in a cup for someone to drink or speaking to your brother with a cheerful face.

title: Hadith on Prayer: Gabriel delivers the promise of Allah
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Angel Gabriel, upon him be peace, came to me from my Lord and he said, ‘O Muhammad, Allah Almighty says: Verily, I have obligated five prayers upon your nation. Whoever fulfils them with their ablution, their timings, their bowings, and their prostrations, then he has a promise from Me that he will enter Paradise. But whoever meets Me with any shortcomings in them, he does not have a promise from Me. If I wish, I will punish him, and if I wish, I will have mercy upon him.”
q: The Angel Gabriel, upon him be peace, came to me from my Lord and he said, ‘O Muhammad, Allah Almighty says: Verily, I have obligated five prayers upon your nation. Whoever fulfils them with their ablution, their timings, their bowings, and their prostrations, then he has a promise from Me that he will enter Paradise. But whoever meets Me with any shortcomings in them, he does not have a promise from Me. If I wish, I will punish him, and if I wish, I will have mercy upon him.

title: Hadith on Qiyamah: The Prophet chooses intercession on Judgment Day
t: ‘Awf ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A visitor came to me from my Lord and gave me the choice between half of my nation entering Paradise or the intercession in the Hereafter. I chose the intercession, and it is for whoever dies without associating partners with Allah.”
q: A visitor came to me from my Lord and gave me the choice between half of my nation entering Paradise or the intercession in the Hereafter. I chose the intercession, and it is for whoever dies without associating partners with Allah.

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Charity due on every joint of the human being
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The son of Adam has three hundred and sixty joints, and charity is due upon each one of them every day. A kind word that a man speaks is charity. A man helping his brother with something is charity. Giving someone a drink of water is charity. Removing harmful things from the road is charity.”
q: The son of Adam has three hundred and sixty joints, and charity is due upon each one of them every day. A kind word that a man speaks is charity. A man helping his brother with something is charity. Giving someone a drink of water is charity. Removing harmful things from the road is charity.

title: Hadith on Salat: Allah boasts to angels for those waiting in mosque
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: We performed the sunset prayer with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. Some people left and some people stayed. The Prophet came back in a hurry, out of breath and holding his cloak above his shins. The Prophet said, “Rejoice! Your Lord has opened a gate to the heavens and He boasts to the angels, saying: Look at My servants! They have completed a prescribed prayer and they are waiting for another!”
q: Rejoice! Your Lord has opened a gate to the heavens and He boasts to the angels, saying: Look at My servants! They have completed a prescribed prayer and they are waiting for another!

title: Hadith on Jannah: Enter Paradise from whichever gate you desire
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Rejoice! Rejoice! Verily, whoever performs the five prayers and avoids the major sins will enter Paradise from whichever gate he wishes.”
q: Rejoice! Rejoice! Verily, whoever performs the five prayers and avoids the major sins will enter Paradise from whichever gate he wishes.

title: Hadith on Bay’ah: Companions pledge their loyalty to Islam
