t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, along with a group of people. The Prophet said, “I take your pledge that you will not associate partners with Allah, you will not steal, you will not commit adultery, you will not kill your children, you will not bring forth slander that you have fabricated, and you will not disobey me in good conduct. Whoever among you fulfills his pledge, his reward is with Allah. Whoever commits any of these sins, it will be taken from him in the world as his expiation and purification. Whoever has his crime concealed by Allah, then the matter belongs to Allah. If He wills, He will punish him, or if He wills, He will forgive him.”
q: I take your pledge that you will not associate partners with Allah, you will not steal, you will not commit adultery, you will not kill your children, you will not bring forth slander that you have fabricated, and you will not disobey me in good conduct. Whoever among you fulfills his pledge, his reward is with Allah. Whoever commits any of these sins, it will be taken from him in the world as his expiation and purification. Whoever has his crime concealed by Allah, then the matter belongs to Allah. If He wills, He will punish him, or if He wills, He will forgive him.

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Set up a barrier against Hell with charity
t: Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Set up a barrier between yourself and the Hellfire, even with half of a date in charity.”
q: Set up a barrier between yourself and the Hellfire, even with half of a date in charity

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Guard yourself from Hell with even half a date
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Protect yourself against the Hellfire, even with half of a date in charity.”
q: Protect yourself against the Hellfire, even with half of a date in charity.

title: Hadith on Salat: Proceed to prayer with dignity and tranquility
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you proceed to prayer, then go with dignity and calm. Pray whatever you have reached and make up whatever you have missed.”
q: When you proceed to prayer, then go with dignity and calm. Pray whatever you have reached and make up whatever you have missed.

title: Ka’b on Ramadan: Whoever fasts intending to sin after Ramadan
t: Ibn Rajab reported: Ka’b ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever fasts the month of Ramadan and he says to himself that he will return to sinful disobedience when Ramadan is over, his fasting is rejected.”

title: Hadith on Trials: Expiation of sins due to sickness
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No believing man or woman, nor Muslim man or woman, is afflicted with illness but that Allah will curtail some of their sins by it.”
q: No believing man or woman, nor Muslim man or woman, is afflicted with illness but that Allah will curtail some of their sins by it.

title: Hadith on Zuhd: Enough of the world on journey to Hereafter
t: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, it is enough for you to have in the world the likes of a traveler’s provision.”
q: Verily, it is enough for you to have in the world the likes of a traveler’s provision.

title: Hadith on Sajdah: Prostration is the repentance of a prophet
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, prostration is the repentance of a prophet.”
q: Verily, prostration is the repentance of a prophet.

title: Hadith on Barakah: Blessings in community, healthy food, and Suhur
t: Salman al-Farisi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are blessings in three: the united community, tharid stew, and the pre-fasting meal.”

title: Hadith on Sajdah: The Prophet prostrates to thank Allah
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, if he received good news or something pleasing, he would fall down in prostration from gratitude to Allah.

title: Hadith on Gratitude: Thankfulness to Allah rewarded like patience
t: Sinan ibn Sannah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The one who eats gratefully has a reward similar to one who fasts patiently.”

title: Hadith on Trials: Prophets rejoice at hardship, seeking reward
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most severely tested are the Prophets, and then the righteous. One of them would be tested with poverty until he could find nothing to cover himself but a cloak. One of them would rejoice in a trial just as one of you rejoices in prosperity.”
q: The most severely tested are the Prophets, and then the righteous. One of them would be tested with poverty until he could find nothing to cover himself but a cloak. One of them would rejoice in a trial just as one of you rejoices in prosperity.

title: Hadith on Dua: Seeking refuge from debt and oppression
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety, sorrow, disability, laziness, cowardice, miserliness, the burdens of debt, and the repression of men.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety, sorrow, disability, laziness, cowardice, miserliness, the burdens of debt, and the repression of men.

title: Hadith on Ummah: Virtue of the first and last Muslims
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of my nation is like the rain. One does not know if the first part is the best or the last.”
q: The parable of my nation is like the rain. One does not know if the first part is the best or the last.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Malik on Tawbah: Malik ibn Dinar’s story of repentance
t: Ibn Qudamah reported: Malik ibn Dinar, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about the reason for his repentance and he said: I was an officer and I was given to drinking wine. When half the night had passed in the month of Sha’ban, which was Friday night, I became drunk from wine and I failed to perform the last evening prayer. I saw in a dream as if the Resurrection had begun, the trumpet was blown, the graves were overturned, and the creatures were gathered, and I was among them. I heard a sound behind me and I turned around to behold a great dragon, nothing more dark and blue, its mouth open and rushing towards me. I passed in front of it, fleeing in panic and terror, then an old man passed by my way. He had pure, clean clothes and a wonderful fragrance. I greeted him with peace and he returned it. I said, “Old man! Protect me from this dragon! I adjure you by Allah!” The old man wept and he said to me, “I am weak and this dragon is stronger than me. I have no power over it, but you must keep running, for perhaps Allah will grant you what can save you from it.” Then, I continued to flee in the other direction and I ascended the cliffs of the Resurrection until I came upon the plains of fire. I looked upon its horrors and I nearly passed away from the terror of the dragon. A voice called out, “Get back, for you are not one of its people!” I was put at rest by this voice and I turned back. The dragon turned back to pursue me and the old man came to me again. I said, “Old man! I asked you to protect me from this dragon and you were unable.” The old man wept and he said, “I am weak but retreat to this mountain, for within it are the lodgings of the Muslims. If it is for you, within it is a lodging and you will be helped.” I looked to the mountain and it was covered in silver, within which were open niches, curtains hanging upon every alley, and skylights fitted with red gold, separated by rubies, the constellation of each skylight was draped with pure silk. When I looked upon the mountain, I turned fleeing towards it and the dragon chased me from behind, until he came close to me and the voice of some angels cried out, “Pull aside the drapes, open the windows, and go inside! Perhaps for this danger among you is a lodging to protect one from his enemy!” Behold, the curtains were lifted, the windows were opened, and children emerged from these niches with faces like moons. The dragon drew closer to me and I was disheartened by my affair. Some of the children called out, “Woe to you! Enter, all of you, for one’s enemy is approaching him!” They entered, group after group, and I beheld my daughter who had died. She entered along with them. When she saw me, she wept and she said, “My father, by Allah!” She darted to me upon a cradle of light until she appeared before me. She reached with her left hand towards my right hand and held onto it, then she stretched forth her right hand towards the dragon and he turned to flee. Then, she gave me a seat and sat upon my lap. She struck my beard with her right hand and she said, “O father, is it not time for those with faith that their hearts be humbled by the remembrance of Allah?” (57:16). I wept and I said, “O my daughter, all of you know the Quran too?” She said, “O father, we know it better than you!” I said, “Tell me about the dragon that wanted to destroy me.” She said, “That was the strength of your evil deeds, so it wanted to consume you in the fire of Hell.” I said, “Tell me about the old man who passed by me.” She said, “O father, that was your righteous deeds, which had been weakened until they could no longer overpower your evil deeds.” I said, “O my daughter, what do you do in this mountain?” She said, “We are the children of the Muslims. We have settled therein until the Hour is established, waiting for it to come to pass such that we intercede for you.” I took this frightening experience to heart and I awoke sober, I broke my vessels, and I repented to Allah Almighty. That is the reason for my repentance.

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication upon monotheism, morning and evening
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, taught us to say when we entered the morning, “We have entered the morning upon the pure nature of Islam, the word of sincerity, the Sunnah of our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the religion of our father Abraham, the monotheist, the Muslim who was not one of the idolaters.” We would say the same when we entered the evening.
q: We have entered the morning upon the pure nature of Islam, the word of sincerity, the Sunnah of our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the religion of our father Abraham, the monotheist, the Muslim who was not one of the idolaters.

title: Hadith on Nobility: Poor believers better than the wealthy and famous
t: Sahl reported: A man passed by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Prophet said, “What do you say about this man?” They said, “If he proposes in marriage, it should be accepted. If he intercedes, it should be granted. If he speaks, he should be listened to.” The Prophet was silent and then a poor man among the Muslims passed by. The Prophet said, “What do you say about this man?” They said, “If he proposes in marriage, it should not be accepted. If he intercedes, it should not be granted. If he speaks, he should not be listened to.” The Prophet said, “This man is better than the entire earth filled with the likes of the other.”
q: What do you say about this man? … What do you say about this man? … This man is better than the entire earth filled with the likes of the other.

title: Hadith on Killing: The Prophet disavows himself from treachery, murder
t: ‘Amr ibn al-Hamiq reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whenever a man promises safety for another man’s life and then kills him, I disavow myself from him even if the victim was an unbeliever.”
q: Whenever a man promises safety for another man’s life and then kills him, I disavow myself from him even if the victim was an unbeliever.

title: Hadith on Visions: Encouragement to interpret dreams optimistically
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, a dream will come to pass in the manner it is interpreted. The parable of this is a man who raises his foot until he places it down. Thus, if one of you sees a dream, let him not speak about it unless with one who wishes him well or with a scholar.”
q: Verily, a dream will come to pass in the manner it is interpreted. The parable of this is a man who raises his foot until he places it down. Thus, if one of you sees a dream, let him not speak about it unless with one who wishes him well or with a scholar.

title: Hadith on Modesty: Let him be modest and bathe in private
t: Ya’la reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saw a man bathing in public, so he ascended the pulpit and then praised and extoled Allah. The Prophet said, “Verily, Allah Almighty is forbearing, modest, and protective. He loves modesty and protection. Thus, if one of you washes himself, let him protect himself with a screen.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty is forbearing, modest, and protective. He loves modesty and protection. Thus, if one of you washes himself, let him protect himself with a screen.

title: Hadith on Prayer: The Prophet spends all night reciting one verse
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed at night reciting a single verse until morning, by which he would bow and prostrate, “If You punish them, they are Your servants. If You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the Wise,” (5:118). When the Prophet awoke in the morning, I said, “O Messenger of Allah, you continued to recite this verse until morning, bowing and prostrating by it.” The Prophet said, “Verily, I asked my Lord for the intercession of my nation and He gave it to me. It will be granted, if Allah wills, to whoever does not associate anything with Allah.”
q: If You punish them, they are Your servants. If You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the Wise, … Verily, I asked my Lord for the intercession of my nation and He gave it to me. It will be granted, if Allah wills, to whoever does not associate anything with Allah.

title: Zayd on Quran: Recitation for contemplation better than for completion
t: Yahya ibn Sa’id reported: A man came to Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said, “How do you view reciting the entire Quran in seven days?” Zayd said, “That is good, but to recite it in half a month or ten days is more beloved to me. Ask me why that is.” The man said, “Indeed, I ask you.” Zayd said, “That I reflect upon it and pause over it.”
gf: Sahih (authentic) according to Ibn Abdul Barr

title: Hadith on Jama’ah: Imams should supplicate for their congregants too
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The one who leads others in prayer should not supplicate only for himself to the exclusion of them. If he does so, he has betrayed them.”
q: The one who leads others in prayer should not supplicate only for himself to the exclusion of them. If he does so, he has betrayed them.

title: Hadith on Sajdah: The Prophet prostrates with body above ground
t: Maymunah reported: If a calf wanted to pass beneath the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when he prostrated, it could certainly pass through.

title: Hadith on Salat: Alternate opening supplications for prayer
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, performed prayer at night, he would exalt Allah and then say, “Glory be to You, O Allah, with Your praises, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no God besides You.” Then, he would say, “Allah is the greatest of the great.” Then, he would say, “I seek refuge in Allah, the Hearing, the Knowing, from the accursed Satan, his madness, his pride, and his poetry.”
q: Glory be to You, O Allah, with Your praises, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no God besides You. … Allah is the greatest of the great. … I seek refuge in Allah, the Hearing, the Knowing, from the accursed Satan, his madness, his pride, and his poetry.

title: Hadith on Salat: Men covering shoulders during prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None of you should perform prayer in a single garment that does not cover any part of the shoulders.”
q: None of you should perform prayer in a single garment that does not cover any part of the shoulders.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on ‘Isha: Delay evening prayer for half the night if not hardship
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, held back the evening prayer one night until most people had retired for the night. Then, the Prophet came out and performed the prayer, saying, “Verily, this is the proper time were it not hardship upon my nation.”
q: Verily, this is the proper time were it not hardship upon my nation.

title: Hadith on Islam: Last virtue to lose in your religion is prayer
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The first thing you will lose in your religion is trust, and the final thing you will lose is prayer.”
q: The first thing you will lose in your religion is trust, and the final thing you will lose is prayer.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Umar on Salat: No share of Islam for one who leaves prayer
t: Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “There is no share of Islam for one who abandons the prayer.”

title: Hadith on Sajdah: Prostration raises a degree, erases a sin
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must perform many prostrations to Allah, for you do not prostrate to Allah but that Allah will raise you one degree for it and erase one sin for it.”
q: You must perform many prostrations to Allah, for you do not prostrate to Allah but that Allah will raise you one degree for it and erase one sin for it.

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet stresses the greatness of prayer
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he asked him about the best of deeds. The Prophet said, “Prayer.” The man said, “Then what?” The Prophet said, “Then prayer.” The man said, “Then what?” The Prophet said, “Then prayer.” He said it three times. The man said, “Then what?” The Prophet said, “Then jihad in the way of Allah.”
q: Prayer … Then prayer … Then prayer … Then jihad in the way of Allah

title: Hadith on Shaytan: How to repel the devil’s whispering in prayer
t: Abu al-‘Ala’ reported: Uthman ibn al-‘As came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, Satan interferes between me, my prayer, and my recitation, confusing me.” The Prophet said, “Such is Satan, who is called rotten. When you sense him, then seek refuge in Allah from him and puff to your left three times.” Uthman said, “I did so and Allah took him away from me.”
q: Such is Satan, who is called rotten. When you sense him, then seek refuge in Allah from him and puff to your left three times.

title: Fudayl on Truth: Do not feel lonely on the path of guidance
t: Al-Nawawi reported: Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Do not feel lonely on the paths of guidance because their people are few, and do not be deceived by the great many who are ruined.”

title: Hadith on Fitnah: When practicing Islam is like grasping thorns
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Woe to the Arabs for an evil tribulation approaching like darkest part of the night! A man will wake up as believer but by evening will become an unbeliever. People will sell their religion for some pitiful gains in the world. The one who adheres to his religion on that day will be as if he were grasping a hot coal or a bundle of thorns.”
q: Woe to the Arabs for an evil tribulation approaching like darkest part of the night! A man will wake up as believer but by evening will become an unbeliever. People will sell their religion for some pitiful gains in the world. The one who adheres to his religion on that day will be as if he were grasping a hot coal or a bundle of thorns.

title: Hadith on Debates: The Prophet prohibits arguing over the Quran
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A group was sitting by the door of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and some of them said, “Did Allah not say this?” Others said, “Did Allah not say this?” The Prophet heard that and he came out, his face red with anger like a pomegranate seed. The Prophet said, “With this I commanded you? Or with this I was sent you? For you to dispute parts of the Book of Allah by others? Verily, the nations before you were led astray by the likes of this. You are doing nothing good here. Look at what I have commanded you and act by it. What you have been prohibited, then do not do it.”
q: With this I commanded you? Or with this I was sent you? For you to dispute parts of the Book of Allah by others? Verily, the nations before you were led astray by the likes of this. You are doing nothing good here. Look at what I have commanded you and act by it. What you have been prohibited, then do not do it.

title: Hasan on Debate: Scholars do argue with fools or heretics
t: Al-Ajurri reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I have never seen a jurist indulge argumentation. The believer does not debate with the foolish, not does he argue. He spreads the wisdom of Allah. If it is accepted, he praises Allah. If it is rejected, he praises Allah.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Jama’ah: Strong encouragement to pray in congregation
t: Abu al-Ahwas reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever would be pleased to meet Allah tomorrow as a Muslim, let him guard over these prayers when they are announced. Verily, Allah has instituted for His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, practices of guidance, for they are indeed practices of guidance. If you were to pray in your houses like one who keeps to his house, you would have abandoned the practice of your Prophet, and if you were to abandon a practice of your Prophet, you have been misguided. No man purifies himself in the best manner and then proceeds to one of these mosques but that Allah records a good deed for every step he takes, raises him by a degree, and erases a sin. We have seen a time when no one leaves it but a hypocrite whose hypocrisy is known, whereas a weak man would come being carried by two men until he was placed within the rows.”

title: Hadith on Ziyarah: Peace be on the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar
t: Nafi’ reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, when he arrived on his journey, he would enter the mosque of Medina and then go to the graves. Ibn Umar would say, “Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Abu Bakr. Peace be upon you, O my father.”

title: Hadith on Salat: Whoever abandons the prayer commits unbelief
t: Buraydah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The covenant between us and them is the prayer, so whoever abandons it has committed unbelief.”
q: The covenant between us and them is the prayer, so whoever abandons it has committed unbelief.

title: Hadith on Sunnah: The Prophet’s commands are like Allah’s commands
t: Al-Miqdam ibn Ma’dikarib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, what the Messenger of Allah has forbidden is like what Allah has forbidden.”
q: Verily, what the Messenger of Allah has forbidden is like what Allah has forbidden.

title: Hadith on Janazah: Four takbirat in the funeral prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings upon him, announced the news to people on the day the Negus died. The Prophet went out with them to the place of prayer, they stood in rows, and he exalted Allah with four exaltations.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Qadr: All that happens is by Allah’s will
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Know that whatever happens to you could never miss you, and whatever misses you could never reach you.”
q: Know that whatever happens to you could never miss you, and whatever misses you could never reach you.

title: Hadith on Jannah: The Prophet hopes they join families in Paradise
t: Rifa’ah al-Juhani reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no servant has faith and then follows right direction but that he will be admitted into Paradise. I hope they will not enter it unless all of you and your righteous offspring settle in the residences of Paradise together. I have been promised by my Lord Almighty that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without reckoning.”
q: By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no servant has faith and then follows right direction but that he will be admitted into Paradise. I hope they will not enter it unless all of you and your righteous offspring settle in the residences of Paradise together. I have been promised by my Lord Almighty that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without reckoning.

title: Hadith on Tafsir: The Prophet explains the Quran with Quran
t: Umm Mubashir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said in front of Hafsah, “No one among my companions will enter the Hellfire, if Allah wills, those who pledged beneath the tree.” She said, “Why not, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet admonished her and Hafsah recited the verse, “There are none of you but that he will come to it,” (19:71). The Prophet said, “Allah Almighty said: Then, We will save those who were righteous and and leave the wrongdoers within it upon their knees.” (19:72)
q: No one among my companions will enter the Hellfire, if Allah wills, those who pledged beneath the tree. … There are none of you but that he will come to it, … Allah Almighty said: Then, We will save those who were righteous and and leave the wrongdoers within it upon their knees

title: Ibn Sirin on Quran: Angels attend houses to hear verses of Allah
t: ‘Abbad reported: Ibn Sirin, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The house in which the Quran is recited is attended by the angels, the devils leave it, its people will be enriched and their goodness increased. The house in which the Quran is not recited is attended by the devils, the angels leave it, its people will be impoverished and their goodness will decrease.”

title: Hadith on Graves: Permission to set up a humble tombstone
t: Al-Mutallib reported: When Uthman ibn Madh’un died, he was brought out for his funeral and he was buried. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered a man to bring a rock but he was unable to carry it. The Prophet went to it and rolled up his sleeves, then he carried it and placed it at the head of the grave. The Prophet said, “I am making the grave of my brother known and I will bury my family members who die next to him.”
q: I am making the grave of my brother known and I will bury my family members who die next to him.

title: Ibn Abbas on Akhirah: Angels say one of three things upon death
t: Al-Barbahari reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Know that there are three tidings at the time of death. It will be said: Receive glad tings of the pleasure of Allah, O beloved of Allah, and Paradise! And it will be said: Receive tidings of the anger of Allah, O enemy of Allah, and the Hellfire! And it will be said: Receive tidings, O servant of Allah, of Paradise after retribution!”

title: Hadith on Kawthar: The Prophet is given the Abundance in Paradise
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A chapter was just revealed to me.” The Prophet recited, “In the name of Allah, the Gracious, the Merciful. Verily, We have given you the Abundance,” (108:1) until he finished it. The Prophet said, “Do you know what is the Abundance?” They said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Prophet said, “Verily, it is a river that my Lord Almighty has promised me in Paradise.”
q: A chapter was just revealed to me. … In the name of Allah, the Gracious, the Merciful. Verily, We have given you the Abundance, … Do you know what is the Abundance? … Verily, it is a river that my Lord Almighty has promised me in Paradise.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Wonders of Paradise for the believers
t: Abdullah ibn Qays reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, in Paradise is a tent made of a hollowed pearl sixty miles wide, in each corner are families who do not see each other. The believers will roam freely between them. There are two gardens of silver, their utensils and whatever is in them, and two gardens of gold, their utensils and whatever is in them. Nothing will come between its people and looking upon their Lord but a curtain of majesty over His face in the Garden of Eden.”
q: Verily, in Paradise is a tent made of a hollowed pearl sixty miles wide, in each corner are families who do not see each other. The believers will roam freely between them. There are two gardens of silver, their utensils and whatever is in them, and two gardens of gold, their utensils and whatever is in them. Nothing will come between its people and looking upon their Lord but a curtain of majesty over His face in the Garden of Eden.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sirat: Believers purified by justice before entering Paradise
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believers will be saved from the Hellfire and they will be stopped at a bridge between Paradise and Hellfire. Then, they will justly retaliate against each other for wrongs committed between them in the world, until they are cleansed and purified for admittance into Paradise. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of you will know his residence in Paradise better than his residence in the world.”
q: The believers will be saved from the Hellfire and they will be stopped at a bridge between Paradise and Hellfire. Then, they will justly retaliate against each other for wrongs committed between them in the world, until they are cleansed and purified for admittance into Paradise. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of you will know his residence in Paradise better than his residence in the world.

title: Hadith on Jannah: What is Paradise made out of?
t: Abu Huraira reported: I said, “What is Paradise built from?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Bricks of silver and gold, its mortar is musk of strong fragrance, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will enjoy bliss without despair and eternity without death. Their clothes will not fade, nor will their youth expire.”
q: Bricks of silver and gold, its mortar is musk of strong fragrance, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will enjoy bliss without despair and eternity without death. Their clothes will not fade, nor will their youth expire.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Jahannam: Hellfire carried by billions of angels
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Hell will be brought on that day with seventy thousand reins, each rein carried by seventy thousand angels.”
q: Hell will be brought on that day with seventy thousand reins, each rein carried by seventy thousand angels.”
gf: Sahih (authentic agreed upon) according to Muslim

title: Hadith on Jahannam: Hellfire seventy times stronger than earthly fire
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Your fire, which the son of Adam ignites, is only one of seventy parts from the fire of Hell.” They said, “By Allah, that would be enough, O Messenger of Allah!” The Prophet said, “Verily, it exceeds it by sixty nine parts, each of which are like its heat.”
q: Your fire, which the son of Adam ignites, is only one of seventy parts from the fire of Hell. … Verily, it exceeds it by sixty nine parts, each of which are like its heat.
gf: Sahih (authentic agreed upon) according to Muslim

title: Hadith on Sirat: People pass over Hell by their good deeds
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Fulfilling the trust and maintaining family ties will be sent to stand on the sides of the bridge over Hell, left and right, then the first of you will pass over it like lightning.” I said, “May my father and mother be ransomed for you, what passes like lightning?” The Prophet said, “Have you not seen how lightning comes and goes like the blink of an eye? Then, they will pass like the wind, then like a bird, then like a strong man running, by the measure of their deeds. Your Prophet will stand over the bridge, saying, ‘O Lord, save them, save them,’ until the deeds of the servants are so weak such that a man can only cross it by crawling.”
q: Fulfilling the trust and maintaining family ties will be sent to stand on the sides of the bridge over Hell, left and right, then the first of you will pass over it like lightning. … Have you not seen how lightning comes and goes like the blink of an eye? Then, they will pass like the wind, then like a bird, then like a strong man running, by the measure of their deeds. Your Prophet will stand over the bridge, saying, ‘O Lord, save them, save them,’ until the deeds of the servants are so weak such that a man can only cross it by crawling.
gf: Sahih (authentic agreed upon) according to Muslim

title: Hadith on Sirat: Passing of people over Hellfire’s bridge
t: Abu Sai’d al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A bridge will come and be placed across Hell.” We said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is the bridge?” The Prophet said, “It is shaky and slippery, over which are claws, pincers, and broad spikes with curved thorns like the seed found in Najd known as al-Sa’dan. The believer will cross over it like the blink of an eye, or like lightning, or like wind, or like powerful horses, or like camels. Thus, one will be unharmed, another will be lacerated, and another will plunge into the fires of Hell, until the last one will be dragged across it.”
q: A bridge will come and be placed across Hell. … It is shaky and slippery, over which are claws, pincers, and broad spikes with curved thorns like the seed found in Najd known as al-Sa’dan. The believer will cross over it like the blink of an eye, or like lightning, or like wind, or like powerful horses, or like camels. Thus, one will be unharmed, another will be lacerated, and another will plunge into the fires of Hell, until the last one will be dragged across it.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Graves: Angels come to ask about Muhammad
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the servant is placed in his grave, his companions turn and leave until he hears the scuffing of their sandals. Two angels come to him and sit by his head, saying to him: What do you say about this man, Muhammad? He says: I testify that he is the servant of Allah and His Messenger. It will be said: Look at your seat in Hellfire, for Allah has replaced it with a seat in Paradise. He will see them both together. As for the unbeliever or hypocrite, he says: I do not know, as I only said what people said! It will be said: You did not know, nor did you recite! Then he will be struck between his two ears with an iron hammer and he will cry out such that whoever is near him will hear it except humans and jinn.”
q: When the servant is placed in his grave, his companions turn and leave until he hears the scuffing of their sandals. Two angels come to him and sit by his head, saying to him: What do you say about this man, Muhammad? He says: I testify that he is the servant of Allah and His Messenger. It will be said: Look at your seat in Hellfire, for Allah has replaced it with a seat in Paradise. He will see them both together. As for the unbeliever or hypocrite, he says: I do not know, as I only said what people said! It will be said: You did not know, nor did you recite! Then he will be struck between his two ears with an iron hammer and he will cry out such that whoever is near him will hear it except humans and jinn.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Abu Darda on Muhasabah: Hold yourself accountable first
t: Abu al-Haytham reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Do not hold people responsible for what they cannot do, and do not get even with people to the exclusion of their Lord. O son of Adam, you must be concerned with yourself, for whoever pursues what he sees in people, his grief will be prolonged and it will not heal his anger.”

title: Umar II on Death: The Caliph trembles remembering the Hereafter
t: Al-Qaddah reported: Whenever death was mentioned in front of Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, he would tremble like a bird and weep until his tears ran through his beard.

title: Hadith on Marriage: Reward for spouses giving each other drinks
t: Al-‘Irbad ibn Sariyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when a man gives his wife something to drink, he is rewarded.”
q: Verily, when a man gives his wife something to drink, he is rewarded.

title: Hadith on Dishonesty: Plots and deception are in Hell
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Conspiracy and treachery are in the Hellfire.”
q: Conspiracy and treachery are in the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Hisab: O Allah, grant me an easy reckoning
t: Aisha reported: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say in some of his prayers, “O Allah, bring me to account with an easy reckoning.”
q: O Allah, bring me to account with an easy reckoning.

title: Hadith on Travel: Shortening prayer in times of safety
t: Ya’la ibn Umayyah reported: I said to Umar ibn al-Khattab about the verse, “There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear persecution from those who disbelieve,” (4:101). I said, “The people are now safe.” Umar said, “I wondered about it as you did, so I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about that. He said: It is charity Allah has given to you, so accept His charity.”
q: There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear persecution from those who disbelieve … It is charity Allah has given to you, so accept His charity.

title: Hadith on Salat: Sunnah to shorten prayer during travel
t: Muwarriq al-‘Ijli reported: He asked Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, about prayer during travel. Ibn Umar said, “Two cycles, two cycles. Whoever opposes the Sunnah has disbelieved.”

title: Hadith on Mercy: I will find Muhammad forgiving and generous
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: On the day Mecca was liberated, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, granted general amnesty to all of the people except for four men and two women. They were ‘Ikramah ibn Abi Jahl, Abdullah ibn Khatal, Maqis ibn Subabah, and Abdullah ibn Sa’d. As for ‘Ikramah, he fled to the sea and they were hit by a storm. The crew of the ship said, “Turn sincerely to Allah, for your gods can do nothing for you here!” ‘Ikramah said, “By Allah, if nothing can save me on the sea but sincerity to Allah, nothing can save me on land but Him! O Allah, I promise You that if You deliver me from my situation, I will go to Muhammad and put my hand in his hand and I will surely find him forgiving and generous!” Then, ‘Ikramah came and he accepted Islam.

title: Hadith on Hawd: Every Prophet has a fountain in the Hereafter
t: Samurah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, every prophet has a fountain and they compete with each other to see who will have the most followers arrive. I hope I will have the most followers arrive.”
q: Verily, every prophet has a fountain and they compete with each other to see who will have the most followers arrive. I hope I will have the most followers arrive.

title: Salaf on Fatwa: Hesitancy in legal verdicts unless necessary
t: Al-Mu’afa ibn ‘Imran reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I met the jurists and they disliked to answer a question or a request for a legal verdict. They would not issue a legal verdict unless no one else could be found, then they would give their judgment.”

title: Hadith on ‘Ilm: Islamic knowledge not for worldly gain
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not acquire knowledge to impress the scholars, nor to argue with the fools, and do not seek the best seat in the gatherings through it. Whoever does so, then to the Hellfire, to the Hellfire!”
q: Do not acquire knowledge to impress the scholars, nor to argue with the fools, and do not seek the best seat in the gatherings through it. Whoever does so, then to the Hellfire, to the Hellfire!

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Bad character spoils good deeds
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, bad character spoils deeds just as vinegar spoils honey.”
q: Verily, bad character spoils deeds just as vinegar spoils honey.

title: Hadith on Iman: Best of faith is patience and tolerance
t: Ma’qil ibn Yasar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of faith is patience and tolerance.”
q: The best of faith is patience and tolerance.

title: Hadith on Speeches: Allah hates excessive, exaggerated speaking
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah despises an extravagant speaker among men, who flaps his tongue about like the flapping of a cow.”
q: Verily, Allah despises an extravagant speaker among men, who flaps his tongue about like the flapping of a cow.

title: Ibn Mubarak on Parenting: Be gentle with your children
t: Al-Ghazali reported: A man came to Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him, and he complained about disrespect from his son. Ibn al-Mubarak said, “Have you supplicated against him?” The man said yes. Ibn al-Mubarak said, “You have corrupted him.” Al-Ghazali said, “It is recommended to be gentle with children.”

title: Umar on Sunnah: No excuse for misguidance after clear proof
t: Al-Awza’i reported: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O people, we do not find any excuse after the Sunnah for anyone to be in misguidance, embarking upon it and considering it guidance, nor to be in guidance, embarking upon it and considering it misguidance. The matters have been explained, the proof has been established, and the excuses have ended.”

title: Ali on Haqq: Know the truth, you will know its people
t: Al-‘Utbi reported: Al-Harith ibn Hut came to Ali and he said to him, “Do you see that I think Talhah, Al-Zubayr, and Aisha have united upon falsehood?” Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O rebel, you are confused! Verily, truth and falsehood are not known by the statures of men. Know the truth and you will recognize its people. Know falsehood and you will recognize the one who brings it.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Jama’ah: You are Ahl al-Sunnah even if you are alone
t: ‘Amr ibn Maymun reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, the majority of groups have left the united community. The united community is only the one that conforms to the obedience of Allah, even if you are by yourself.”
s: Sharḥ Uṣūl I’tiqād Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jamā’ah 160

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Remembering Allah loudly or softly after prayer
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The people would raise their voices in remembrance as they left the obligatory prayers in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Ibn Abbas said, “I used to know when they were leaving as I heard them.”
gf: Mutaffaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Remembering Allah as a private conversation
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, retreated within the mosque and he heard them raising their voices in recitation. The Prophet lifted the curtain and he said, “Are not all of you in private conversation with his Lord? Do not bother each other and do not raise your voices over each other with recitation or prayer.”
q: Are not all of you in private conversation with his Lord? Do not bother each other and do not raise your voices over each other with recitation or prayer.

title: Hadith on Salat: Prayer is a private conversation with Allah
t: Al-Bayadi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to the people while they were praying and they were raising their voices in recitation. The Prophet said, “Verily, the one in prayer is in an intimate conversation with his Lord Almighty, so let one look at how he converses with Him. Do not raise your voices above each other with the Quran.”
q: Verily, the one in prayer is in an intimate conversation with his Lord Almighty, so let one look at how he converses with Him. Do not raise your voices above each other with the Quran.

title: Hadith on Status: Love of worldly life dangerous to faith
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two ravenous, hungry wolves spending the night in a pen of sheep while its owners are negligent, bloodthirsty and eating, are not faster to wreak havoc than the love of wealth and high status are to the religion of a Muslim.”
q: Two ravenous, hungry wolves spending the night in a pen of sheep while its owners are negligent, bloodthirsty and eating, are not faster to wreak havoc than the love of wealth and high status are to the religion of a Muslim.

title: Abdullah on Bid’ah: Rejection of apparently good or small innovations
t: Salamah al-Hamdani reported: We used to sit by the door of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, before dawn prayer. When he came out, we would walk with him to the mosque. Abu Musa al-Ash’ari came to us and he said to him, “O Abu Abdur Rahman, I recently saw something in the mosque that I detested and yet, praise be to Allah, I saw nothing but good.” Ibn Mas’ud said, “What was it?” Abu Musa said, “If you wait long enough, you will see it. I saw people sitting in the mosque in circles waiting for prayer. A man in each circle had pebbles and he would tell them to exalt Allah one hundred times and they would do so, then declare there is no God but Allah one hundred times and they would do so, then glorify Allah one hundred times and they would do so.” Ibn Mas’ud said, “What did you say to them?” Abu Musa said, “I did not say anything to them. I was waiting for your opinion or order.” Ibn Mas’ud said, “Would you not order them to count their sins and guarantee for them that their good deeds would not be wasted?” We went along with him until he reached one of these circles and he stood over it, saying, “What is this I see you doing?” They said, “O Abu Abdur Rahman, they are pebbles by which we count the exaltation of Allah, declaration of His oneness, and His glorification.” Ibn Mas’ud said, “Count your sins, for I guarantee that none of your good deeds will be wasted. Woe to you, nation of Muhammad! How quickly do you run to your destruction! Here are his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, numerous around you, these are his clothes yet to fade, these are his utensils yet to break. By the One in whose hand is my soul, perhaps you are upon a religion better guided than the religion of Muhammad? Or have you opened the door of misguidance?” They said, “By Allah, O Abu Abdur Rahman, we intended nothing but good.” Ibn Mas’ud said, “How many intend good but are not right! The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, informed us that people would recite the Quran and it would not reach beyond their throats. By Allah, I do not know that perhaps many of them are among you!” Then he turned away from them. ‘Amr ibn Salamah said, “We saw most of them in these circles attacking us on the day of Nahrawan with the Khawarij.”

title: Malik on Bid’ah: What is worse than contradicting the Messenger?
t: Muhammad ibn al-Dahhak reported: A man came to Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, and he said, “Where should I put on my clothes for pilgrimage?” Malik said, “At the places designated by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.” The man said, “I will do it from a further place.” Malik said, “I do not agree with that.” The man said, “What do you dislike about that?” Malik said, “I dislike for you to be put to trial.” The man said, “What trial is there in doing more good?” Malik said, “Allah Almighty says, ‘So let them beware who contradict his order lest they be struck by a trial or a painful punishment,’ (24:63) and what trial is greater than that you assign a deed for yourself that was not chosen by the Messenger of Allah?”
q: So let them beware who contradict his order lest they be struck by a trial or a painful punishment

title: Sufyan on Bid’ah: Innovations more beloved to Satan than major sins
t: Ibn al-Yaman reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Religious innovations are more beloved to Satan than sinful disobedience to Allah. Disobedience is repented from, but innovations are not repented from.”

title: Abu Darda on Bid’ah: Anger at seeing innovations in the religion
t: Umm Darda reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, entered upon me while he was furious. I said, “Why are you angry?” Abu Darda said, “By Allah, I do not recognize any of the affairs of Muhammad among them except that they pray in congregation.”

title: Abu Bakr on Muhammad: The Prophet will never die twice
t: Aisha reported: Abu Bakr came riding on his horse from his dwelling in al-Sunuh until he arrived and entered the mosque. He did not speak to people until he entered the home of Aisha while the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was covered with a shroud. Abu Bakr lifted the shroud from his face and knelt down and kissed him, then he wept. Abu Bakr said, “May my father be ransomed for you. By Allah, Allah will never make you die twice. As for the death Allah has decreed for you, it has come to pass.”

title: Hadith on Trials: Allah tests a blind man, bald man, and leper
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, there were three among the children of Israel whom Allah Almighty intended to test: a leper, a bald man, and a blind man. He sent an angel to them and he came to the leper, saying: What would you love most? The leper said: I want a beautiful color and beautiful skin, for people have shunned me. The angel wiped over him and it had gone away, then he was given a beautiful color and beautiful skin. The angel said: Which property would you love most? The man said: Camels. Thus, he was given a pregnant camel. The angel said: May Allah bless you in it. The angel came to the bald man, saying: What would you love most? The bald man said: Beautiful hair and to be rid of this, for people have shunned me. The angel wiped over him and it had gone away, then he was given beautiful hair. The angel said: Which property would you love most? The man said: Cows. Thus, he was given a pregnant cow. The angel said: May Allah bless you in it. The angel came to the blind man, saying: What would you love most? The blind man said: For Allah to return my sight so I can see people. The angel wiped over him, then Allah returned his sight. The angel said: Which property would you love most? The man said: Sheep. Thus, he was given a pregnant sheep. The animals had grown and given birth such that one man had a valley of camels, another had a valley of cows, and another had a valley of sheep. Then, the angel came to the former leper while disguised in the shape and appearance of a leper, saying: I am a poor man, bereft of my livelihood while on a journey, none can take care of my needs today but Allah and then you, so I ask by the One who gave you beautiful color and beautiful skin and a wealth of camels to help me reach my destination! The man said: I have many duties. The angel said to him: It is as if I recognize you, were you not a leper shunned by people, in poverty, but Allah gave this to you? The man said: I have inherited it from my forefathers. The angel said: If you are lying, then may Allah return you to what you were before! The angel came to the former bald man in a similar appearance, saying the same as he had said to the leper and the man responded the same way. The angel said: If you are lying, then may Allah return you to what you were before! The angel came to the blind man in a similar form, saying: I am a poor man and wayfarer, bereft of my livelihood while on a journey, none can take care of my needs today but Allah and then you, so I ask by the One who returned your sight and gave you sheep to help me reach my destination! The man said: I was once a blind man and Allah returned my sight, I was poor and He enriched me, so take whatever you wish for, by Allah, I will not dispute you today in whatever you take for Allah’s sake. The angel said: Keep your property, for I was only sent to test you and Allah is pleased with you but angry with your two companions.”
q: Verily, there were three among the children of Israel whom Allah Almighty intended to test: a leper, a bald man, and a blind man. He sent an angel to them and he came to the leper, saying: What would you love most? The leper said: I want a beautiful color and beautiful skin, for people have shunned me. The angel wiped over him and it had gone away, then he was given a beautiful color and beautiful skin. The angel said: Which property would you love most? The man said: Camels. Thus, he was given a pregnant camel. The angel said: May Allah bless you in it. The angel came to the bald man, saying: What would you love most? The bald man said: Beautiful hair and to be rid of this, for people have shunned me. The angel wiped over him and it had gone away, then he was given beautiful hair. The angel said: Which property would you love most? The man said: Cows. Thus, he was given a pregnant cow. The angel said: May Allah bless you in it. The angel came to the blind man, saying: What would you love most? The blind man said: For Allah to return my sight so I can see people. The angel wiped over him, then Allah returned his sight. The angel said: Which property would you love most? The man said: Sheep. Thus, he was given a pregnant sheep. The animals had grown and given birth such that one man had a valley of camels, another had a valley of cows, and another had a valley of sheep. Then, the angel came to the former leper while disguised in the shape and appearance of a leper, saying: I am a poor man, bereft of my livelihood while on a journey, none can take care of my needs today but Allah and then you, so I ask by the One who gave you beautiful color and beautiful skin and a wealth of camels to help me reach my destination! The man said: I have many duties. The angel said to him: It is as if I recognize you, were you not a leper shunned by people, in poverty, but Allah gave this to you? The man said: I have inherited it from my forefathers. The angel said: If you are lying, then may Allah return you to what you were before! The angel came to the former bald man in a similar appearance, saying the same as he had said to the leper and the man responded the same way. The angel said: If you are lying, then may Allah return you to what you were before! The angel came to the blind man in a similar form, saying: I am a poor man and wayfarer, bereft of my livelihood while on a journey, none can take care of my needs today but Allah and then you, so I ask by the One who returned your sight and gave you sheep to help me reach my destination! The man said: I was once a blind man and Allah returned my sight, I was poor and He enriched me, so take whatever you wish for, by Allah, I will not dispute you today in whatever you take for Allah’s sake. The angel said: Keep your property, for I was only sent to test you and Allah is pleased with you but angry with your two companions.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Abbas on Patience: Enemies become friends by forgiveness
t: Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Allah has commanded patience at a time of anger, and forbearance and forgiveness at a time of being wronged. If they do so, Allah will protect them from Satan and subdue their enemies such that they become like dear friends.”

title: Hadith on Marriage: Sweetness of faith to fulfill marital duties
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If I were to order anyone to prostrate to another, I would have ordered the wife to prostrate to her husband due to his rights over her. A woman will not taste the sweetness of faith until she fulfills the rights of her husband, even if he were to call for her while she is upon a camel’s saddle.”
q: If I were to order anyone to prostrate to another, I would have ordered the wife to prostrate to her husband due to his rights over her. A woman will not taste the sweetness of faith until she fulfills the rights of her husband, even if he were to call for her while she is upon a camel’s saddle.

title: Hadith on Dua: No movement or might but in Allah, treasure of Paradise
t: Abu Musa al-Ash’ari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “Shall I not tell you about a word among the treasures of Paradise?” I said, “Of course.” The Prophet said, “There is no movement or might but in Allah.”
q: Shall I not tell you about a word among the treasures of Paradise? … There is no movement or might but in Allah.

title: Hadith on Kunya: Changing names to safeguard monotheism
t: Shurayh reported: His father, Hani, attended the delegation with his people to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Prophet heard them calling him by his nickname Abu al-Hakam, father of judgement. The Prophet called him and he said, “Verily, Allah is the Judge, to Him belongs judgment, so why are you called father of judgement?” Hani said, “When my people disagree over something, they come to me and I judge between them and both parties are pleased.” The Prophet said, “How excellent is this! Do you have children?” Hani said, “I have Shurayh, Muslim, and Abdullah.” The Prophet said, “Who is the oldest of them?” Hani said, “Shurayh.” The Prophet said, “Then you are now Abu Shurayh, father of Shurayh.”
q: Verily, Allah is the Judge, to Him belongs judgment, so why are you called father of judgement? … How excellent is this! Do you have children? … Who is the oldest of them? … Then you are now Abu Shurayh, father of Shurayh.

title: Hadith on Shirk: Safeguarding words from lesser idolatry
t: Qutaylah reported: A Jewish man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Indeed, you are setting up rivals with Allah and associating partners with Him when you say, ‘What Allah wills and you will,’ and when you swear by the Ka’bah!” Then the Prophet ordered them to say if they intend to swear an oath, “By the Lord of the Ka’bah,” and for them to say instead, “What Allah wills and then what you will.”

title: Hadith on Kaba’ir: Idolatry, losing hope, not fearing Allah
t: Ibn Abbas reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “What are the major sins?” The Prophet said, “To associate partners with Allah, to despair of relief from Allah, and to feel safe from the plan of Allah. These are the worst of enormities.”
q: To associate partners with Allah, to despair of relief from Allah, and to feel safe from the plan of Allah. These are the worst of enormities.

title: Hadith on Sihr: Prohibition of using magic to counter magic
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about seeking a cure from magic (al-nushrah). The Prophet said, “They are among the works of Satan.”
q: They are among the works of Satan.

title: Hadith on Sihr: Fortunetellers and magicians are not Muslims
t: ‘Imran ibn Husayn reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He is not one of us who reads omens or has them read for him, or who performs soothsaying or has it performed for him, or who practices magic or has it practiced for him.”
q: He is not one of us who reads omens or has them read for him, or who performs soothsaying or has it performed for him, or who practices magic or has it practiced for him.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Kahin: Warning against belief in soothsayers or sodomy
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever goes to a fortuneteller and believes in what he says, or approaches his wife for intercourse while she is menstruating, or approaches his wife for intercourse from her backside, he was nothing to do with what has been revealed to Muhammad.”
q: Whoever goes to a fortuneteller and believes in what he says, or approaches his wife for intercourse while she is menstruating, or approaches his wife for intercourse from her backside, he was nothing to do with what has been revealed to Muhammad.

title: Hadith on Amulets: The Prophet prohibits charms and filth
t: Ruwayfah ibn Thabit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Ruwayfah, perhaps you will live for a long time after me. Tell the people that whoever ties knots in his beard, or hangs a string around his neck, or cleans himself with dung or bones, then Muhammad has disavowed him.”
q: O Ruwayfah, perhaps you will live for a long time after me. Tell the people that whoever ties knots in his beard, or hangs a string around his neck, or cleans himself with dung or bones, then Muhammad has disavowed him.

title: Hadith on Wasilah: Ask Allah to bring the Prophet near to Him
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Ask Allah to grant me the means of approach. Verily, a servant does not ask for it in the world but that I will be a witness for him or intercede for him on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Ask Allah to grant me the means of approach. Verily, a servant does not ask for it in the world but that I will be a witness for him or intercede for him on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication to guarantee the Prophet’s intercession
t: Ruwayfah ibn Thabit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever sends blessings upon Muhammad by saying, ‘O Allah, grant him the seat near You on the Day of Resurrection,’ then my intercession is ensured for him.”
q: Whoever sends blessings upon Muhammad by saying, ‘O Allah, grant him the seat near You on the Day of Resurrection,’ then my intercession is ensured for him.

title: Hadith on Talismans: The Prophet orders all charms removed
t: Abu Bashir reported: He was with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in one of his travels. The Prophet sent a messenger, saying, “Do not leave a stringed necklace upon a camel, or any necklace, but that you cut it off.” Malik said, “I think they were for protection from the evil eye.”
q: Do not leave a stringed necklace upon a camel, or any necklace, but that you cut it off.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hudayfah on Shirk: Wearing good luck charms is lesser idolatry
t: Ghazrah reported: Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, entered the home of a sick man and he saw him wearing a luck charm on his arm. Hudhayfah cut it off or removed it, then he recited the verse, “Most of them do not believe in Allah but that they associate with Him.” (12:106)
q: Most of them do not believe in Allah but that they associate with Him.

title: Umar on Dua: Supplication held back until the Prophet is blessed
t: Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, the supplication is suspended between the heavens and the earth. Nothing ascends from it until you send blessings upon your Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Name of Allah greater than all sins
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah will single out a man from my nation before all of creation on the Day of Resurrection. Ninety-nine scrolls will be unrolled before him, each scroll as far as the eye can see. Allah will say: Do you deny any of this? Have my recording angels wronged you? He will say: No, O Lord. Allah will say: Do you have any excuse? He will say: No, O Lord. Allah will say: No, rather you have a good deed with us and you will not be wronged today. A card will be brought upon which is written the testimony that there is no God but Allah and Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. Allah will say: Bring forth your scale. He will say: O Lord, this card along with these scrolls? Allah will say: Verily, you will not be wronged.” The Prophet said, “Then, the scrolls will be placed upon one side of the scale and the card upon the other. The scrolls will be lifted up and the card will weigh it down. Thus, nothing is heavier with the name of Allah.”
q: Verily, Allah will single out a man from my nation before all of creation on the Day of Resurrection. Ninety-nine scrolls will be unrolled before him, each scroll as far as the eye can see. Allah will say: Do you deny any of this? Have my recording angels wronged you? He will say: No, O Lord. Allah will say: Do you have any excuse? He will say: No, O Lord. Allah will say: No, rather you have a good deed with us and you will not be wronged today. A card will be brought upon which is written the testimony that there is no God but Allah and Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. Allah will say: Bring forth your scale. He will say: O Lord, this card along with these scrolls? Allah will say: Verily, you will not be wronged. … Then, the scrolls will be placed upon one side of the scale and the card upon the other. The scrolls will be lifted up and the card will weigh it down. Thus, nothing is heavier with the name of Allah.

title: Hadith on Muhammad: Satan exaggerates status of the Prophet
t: Abdullah ibn Shikhir reported: I proceeded with the delegation of the tribe of ‘Amir to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. We said, “You are our master.” The Prophet said, “The Master is Allah Almighty.” We said, “You are the best and greatest among us.” The Prophet said, “Say what you have to say, or part of it, but do not take Satan as a guardian.”
q: The Master is Allah Almighty. … Say what you have to say, or part of it, but do not take Satan as a guardian.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Akhlaq: Vulgarity worst character trait of a believer
t: Abu al-Ahwas reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The most blameworthy characteristic in a believer is obscenity.”

title: Hadith on Resurrection: Each resurrected with their religion
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Every servant in his grave will be resurrected upon the way he died, the believer upon his faith and the hypocrite upon his hypocrisy.”
q: Every servant in his grave will be resurrected upon the way he died, the believer upon his faith and the hypocrite upon his hypocrisy.

title: Ibn Abbas on Quran: Following Quran protects from misguidance, damnation
t: ‘Ikramah reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Allah has guaranteed for one who follows the Quran that he will not be led astray in the world, nor be damned in the Hereafter.” Then, he recited the verse, “Thus, whoever follows My guidance will not be led astray or damned.” (20:123)
q: Thus, whoever follows My guidance will not be led astray or damned.

title: Hadith on Hudaybiyyah: Peace treaty with idolaters a victory for the Prophet
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: When the verse was revealed, “Verily, We have given you a clear victory,” (48:1), they had returned from Al-Hudaybiyyah mixed with grief and despair. They slaughtered their sacrificial animals at Hudaybiyyah, then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A verse has been revealed to me that is more beloved to me than the entire world.”
q: Verily, We have given you a clear victory, … A verse has been revealed to me that is more beloved to me than the entire world.

title: Hadith on Hudaybiyyah: All who pledged under the tree in Paradise
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None of the companions who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter Hellfire.”
q: None of the companions who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Imamate: Regret for eagerness to rule on Judgment Day
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, you will crave leadership, and it will be a source of regret on the Day of Resurrection. How nice is the wet nurse, yet how evil is the weaning!”
q: Verily, you will crave leadership, and it will be a source of regret on the Day of Resurrection. How nice is the wet nurse, yet how evil is the weaning!

title: Hadith on Mursalin: Messengers sent to give glad tidings and warn
t: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one has a greater sense of honor than Allah. No one loves to allow excuses more than Allah. For this reason, He sent the Messengers to give glad tidings and warnings. No one loves to be praised more than Allah on account of what Allah has promised of Paradise.”
q: No one has a greater sense of honor than Allah. No one loves to allow excuses more than Allah. For this reason, He sent the Messengers to give glad tidings and warnings. No one loves to be praised more than Allah on account of what Allah has promised of Paradise.

title: Ibn Abbas on Shirk: Creation fears associating partners with Allah
t: Al-Tabari reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, idolatry terrifies the heavens, the earth, the mountains, and all of creation except for the worlds of men and jinn. They nearly quake from the greatness of Allah, as goodness with idolatry will not benefit the idolater. Thus, we hope that Allah will forgive the sins of the monotheists.”

title: Hadith on Qubur: Making graves levelled flat with the earth
t: Thamamah ibn Shufayy reported: We were with Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd in the land of the Romans by a place known as Rudis. One of our companions passed away, so Fadalah ordered his grave to be levelled flat. Then, Fadalah said, “I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordering them to be leveled.”

title: Hadith on Graves: Visiting the dead softens the heart
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I had prohibited you from visiting the graves, but it occurred to me that now you may visit them. Verily, they soften the heart, shed tears in the eyes, and remind of the Hereafter. Thus, visit them and do not say anything obscene.”

title: Mu’awiyah on Tawassul: Supplications of living righteous people
t: Sulaym ibn ‘Amir reported: The sky withheld rain, so Mu’awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and the people of Damascus sought prayers for rain. When Mu’awiyah sat upon the pulpit, he said, “Where is Yazid ibn al-Aswad al-Jurashi?” Then, the people called for him and he came forward cutting through the crowd. Mu’awiyah ordered him to ascend the pulpit and Yazid sat by his feet. Mu’awiyah said, “O Allah, we seek intercession with You today by the best of us and most virtuous of us! O Allah, we seek intercession with You today by Yazid ibn al-Aswad al-Jurashi! O Yazid, raise your hands to Allah!” Yazid raised his hands and the people raised their hands. The clouds in the west soon began to stir, a wind began to rush, and we were given rain until the people almost could not pray but in their houses.

title: Hadith on Dua: Declaring glory of Allah expiates sins
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no one on earth who declares there is no God but Allah, Allah is the greatest, and there is no movement or might except in Allah, but that it will expiate his sins even if they were like foam on the sea.”
q: There is no one on earth who declares there is no God but Allah, Allah is the greatest, and there is no movement or might except in Allah, but that it will expiate his sins even if they were like foam on the sea.

title: ‘Ata’ on Graves: Prohibition of mosques pointing to a graveyard
t:
Ibn Jurayj reported: I said to ‘Ata’, may Allah have mercy on him, “Do you disapprove of us praying in the midst of graves or in a mosque pointing towards a grave?” ‘Ata’ said, “Yes, that has been prohibited.” I said, “What do you think if there is a small space between me and it, or in a mosque elevated by a cubit?” ‘Ata’ said, “It is hateful to pray in the midst of graves.”

Tawus said, “I do not know anything about it but that prayer in the midst of graves is severely disapproved.”

title: Hadith on Masajid: Prohibition of building mosques in graveyards
t: Qatadah reported: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by a graveyard of Ramad while they were building a mosque over it. Anas said, “It is hated to build a mosque in the midst of graves.”

title: Umar on Idolatry: The Caliph hides the grave of Prophet Daniel
t: Anas reported: When they liberated Tustar, they found a man with a long nose in a coffin. The people were seeking victory and seeking rain through him. Abu Musa wrote to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, about that. Umar wrote back, saying, “Indeed, this man is one of the prophets. Fire and earth do not consume the bodies of the prophets.” Umar wrote further, “Look for him, you and your companion, and bury him in a place no one knows but the two of you.” Anas said, “Then I went with Abu Musa and we reburied him.”

title: Hadith on Shirk: Effacing graven images, leveling high graves
t: Abu al-Hayyaj reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib said to me, “Shall I not send you upon the mission with which the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent me? Do not leave a graven image but that you efface it, and do not leave a built over grave but that you level it.”

title: Hadith on Qubur: Forbidden to build, sit, or pray over graves
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited building over graves, sitting upon them, or praying over them.

title: Hadith on Salat: Ritual prayer forbidden at graveyards
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited praying amongst the graves.

title: Hadith on Meals: The Prophet eats sitting upright
t: Abu Juhayfah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I do not eat while reclining.”
q: I do not eat while reclining.

title: Abu Dharr on Bathrooms: Supplication for exiting the toilet
t: Abu Ali al-Sayqal reported: Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, when he left the washroom, he would say, “All praise is due to Allah, who has removed harm from me and granted me wellness.”

title: Hadith on Bathrooms: Refuge in Allah before relieving oneself
t: Zayd ibn Arqam reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, these washrooms are inhabited by jinn. When one of you enters his place of relief, let him say: I seek refuge in Allah from foul and noxious things.”
q: Verily, these washrooms are inhabited by jinn. When one of you enters his place of relief, let him say: I seek refuge in Allah from foul and noxious things.

title: Hadith on Bathrooms: Bismillah before entering the toilet
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A screen will be placed between the eyes of the Jinn and the nakedness of the children of Adam if one of them says as he enters the washroom: In the name of Allah.”
q: A screen will be placed between the eyes of the Jinn and the nakedness of the children of Adam if one of them says as he enters the washroom: In the name of Allah.

title: Abu Hurairah on Qulub: Heart is king, body is the soldier
t: Abu Salih reported: Abu Huraira, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The heart is king and its soldiers are the limbs. If the king is set right, his soldiers will be set right. If the king is corrupted, his soldiers will be corrupted.”

title: Hasan on Self-Talk: Hearts of believers speak with wisdom
t: Abu Maryam al-Salt reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, the people of understanding continue to alternate from remembrance to reflection, and reflection to remembrance, until their hearts awaken and speak with wisdom.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Answered unless impatient or asking for sin
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The servant will continue to have his supplications answered as long as he does not ask for sin or cutting family ties, and he is not impatient.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is its impatience?” The Prophet said, “He says: I have supplicated again and again, but I have not seen an answer. He becomes frustrated with that and gives up supplicating.”
q: The servant will continue to have his supplications answered as long as he does not ask for sin or cutting family ties, and he is not impatient … He says: I have supplicated again and again, but I have not seen an answer. He becomes frustrated with that and gives up supplicating

title: Hadith on Badr: Allah supports the Prophet with angels
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: On the day of Badr, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, looked upon the idolaters and they were a thousand in number, while his companions were only three hundred and nineteen men. The Prophet faced the direction of prayer, then he raised his hands and supplicated aloud to his Lord, “O Allah, accomplish what You have promised me! O Allah, bring about what You have promised me!
