O Allah, if this band among the people of Islam is destroyed, You will not be worshipped on the earth!” The Prophet continued to call out to his Lord with his hands raised and facing the direction of prayer until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Abu Bakr came, picked up his cloak, and placed it on his shoulders, then he embraced him from behind, saying, “O Prophet of Allah, your supplication to your Lord will suffice, for He will accomplish what He has promised you.” Allah Almighty revealed the verse, “When you sought deliverance from your Lord and He answered you: Verily, I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, rank after rank,” (8:9). Thus, Allah reinforced him with the angels.
q: O Allah, accomplish what You have promised me! O Allah, bring about what You have promised me! O Allah, if this band among the people of Islam is destroyed, You will not be worshipped on the earth! … When you sought deliverance from your Lord and He answered you: Verily, I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, rank after rank,

title: Hadith on Trials: Seek refuge from tribulations, torment of grave
t: Zayd ibn Thabit reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, this nation will be put to trial in their graves. Were it not that you would stop burying each other, I would have called upon Allah to make you hear the punishment of the grave as I hear it.” Then, the Prophet turned to face us, saying, “Seek refuge in Allah from the torment of the Hellfire.” They said, “We seek refuge in Allah from the torment of the Hellfire.” The Prophet said, “Seek refuge in Allah from the torment of the grave.” They said, “We seek refuge in Allah from the torment of the grave.” The Prophet said, “Seek refuge in Allah from tribulations, the evident of them and the hidden.” They said, “We seek refuge in Allah from tribulations, the evident of them and the hidden.” The Prophet said, “Seek refuge in Allah from the tribulation of the False Messiah.” They said, “We seek refuge in Allah from the tribulation of the False Messiah.”
q: Verily, this nation will be put to trial in their graves. Were it not that you would stop burying each other, I would have called upon Allah to make you hear the punishment of the grave as I hear it. … Seek refuge in Allah from the torment of the Hellfire. … Seek refuge in Allah from the torment of the grave. … Seek refuge in Allah from tribulations, the evident of them and the hidden. … Seek refuge in Allah from the tribulation of the False Messiah.

title: Sahaba on Salat: Abandoning the prayer completely is unbelief
t: Abdullah ibn Shaqiq reported: The companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, did not consider leaving any deed to be unbelief except for the prayer.

title: Hadith on Vows: Permission only to vow in righteousness
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever vows to obey Allah, let him obey Him. Whoever vows to disobey Allah, he must not disobey Him.”
q: Whoever vows to obey Allah, let him obey Him. Whoever vows to disobey Allah, he must not disobey Him.

title: Hadith on Shirk: Paradise for one neither an idolater, nor murderer
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever meets Allah without associating anything with Him, nor spilling sacred blood, he will enter Paradise.”
q: Whoever meets Allah without associating anything with Him, nor spilling sacred blood, he will enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Intercession: Sinful Muslims enter Hell before Paradise
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, some people will be taken out of the Hellfire. The outsides of their faces will be burned therein, until they enter Paradise.”
q: Verily, some people will be taken out of the Hellfire. The outsides of their faces will be burned therein, until they enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Shirk: Allah curses those who sacrifice to other gods
t: Abi ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah has cursed one who sacrifices to other than Allah. Allah has cursed one who harbors a heretic. Allah has cursed one who curses his own parents. Allah has cursed one who manipulates the boundaries of a land.”
q: Allah has cursed one who sacrifices to other than Allah. Allah has cursed one who harbors a heretic. Allah has cursed one who curses his own parents. Allah has cursed one who manipulates the boundaries of a land.

title: Hadith on Shafa’ah: Believers intercede for each other on Judgment Day
t: Abdullah ibn Shaqiq reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “More people than the tribe of Tamim will enter Paradise by the intercession of a single man from my nation.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, someone besides you?” The Prophet said, “Someone besides me.”
q: More people than the tribe of Tamim will enter Paradise by the intercession of a single man from my nation. … Someone besides me.

title: Hadith on Shirk: Idolaters believe Allah is Lord, but do not worship Him alone
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The idolaters would say, “O Allah, at Your service! You have no partners!” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would say, “Woe to you! Stop here! Stop here!” Then they would say, “Except for partners You own and do not own You.” They would say this as they circled the House.
q: Woe to you! Stop here! Stop here!

title: Hadith on Shirk: First man to bring idolatry into Arabia
t:
Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I saw ‘Amra ibn ‘Amr ibn Luhayy al-Khuza’i dragging his intestines in the Hellfire. He introduced the custom of releasing animals on behalf of false gods.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “He was the first to change the religion of Ishmael and set up idols.”
q: I saw ‘Amra ibn ‘Amr ibn Luhayy al-Khuza’i dragging his intestines in the Hellfire. He introduced the custom of releasing animals on behalf of false gods. … He was the first to change the religion of Ishmael and set up idols.

title: Hadith on Shirk: The Prophet victorious over idolatry in Mecca
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered Mecca on the day of its liberation and there were three hundred and sixty idols around the House. The Prophet thrust his staff at them, saying, “The truth has come and falsehood has passed away. Verily, falsehood will ever pass away (17:81). The truth has come and falsehood can neither create, nor resurrect.” (34:49)
q: The truth has come and falsehood has passed away. Verily, falsehood will ever pass away … The truth has come and falsehood can neither create, nor resurrect.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Shirk: No worship in places where idols were worshipped
t: Thabit ibn al-Dahhak reported: A man in the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, made a vow to sacrifice a camel at a placed called Buwanah. He came to the Prophet and he said, “I have made a vow to sacrifice a camel at Buwanah.” The Prophet said, “Were there any idols worshipped there in the time of ignorance?” They said no. The Prophet said, “Were any of their idolatrous festivals celebrated there?” They said no. The Prophet said, “Fulfill your vow, for a vow in disobedience to Allah must not be fulfilled, nor a vow over which the son of Adam has not control.”
q: Were there any idols worshipped there in the time of ignorance? … Were any of their idolatrous festivals celebrated there? … Fulfill your vow, for a vow in disobedience to Allah must not be fulfilled, nor a vow over which the son of Adam has not control.

title: Hadith on Hayd: Menstruating women make up fasts, but not prayers
t: Mu’adhah reported: I asked Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, saying, “Why do menstruating women make up missed fasts but not missed prayers?” Aisha said, “We endured those menses and we were ordered to make up missed fasts, but we were not ordered to make up missed prayers.”

title: Hadith on Ghusl: Description of the Prophet’s ritual bath
t: Maymunah reported: I brought water to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, for his ritual bath from major impurity. He washed his hands two or three times, then he put his right hand in the vessel and poured it over his private parts, washing it with his left hand. Then, he struck the ground with his left hand and rubbed it hard, and performed ablution as for prayer. Then, he poured three handfuls of water over his head and washed the rest of his body. Then, he moved away from that place and washed his feet. I brought him a towel but he turned it away.

title: Abu Sa’ud on Wudu: Seeking forgiveness after ablution
t: Qays ibn ‘Ubad reported: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever performed ablution, let him say: Glory be to You, O Allah, and Your praise. I testify there is no God but You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.”

title: Hadith on War: Whoever fights or deceives believers is not true Muslim
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever raises arms against us is not one of us. Whoever deceives us is not one of us.”
q: Whoever raises arms against us is not one of us. Whoever deceives us is not one of us.

title: Hadith on Khawatim: Final deeds determine fate in Hereafter
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the deeds are only judged by their endings.”
q: Verily, the deeds are only judged by their endings.

title: Hadith on Hidayah: The Prophet leaves behind complete religious guidance
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, there is nothing to bring you closer to Paradise and distance you from Hellfire but that I have commanded you to do it, and there is nothing to bring you closer to Hellfire and distance you from Paradise but that I have forbidden you from doing it.”
q: Verily, there is nothing to bring you closer to Paradise and distance you from Hellfire but that I have commanded you to do it, and there is nothing to bring you closer to Hellfire and distance you from Paradise but that I have forbidden you from doing it.

title: Hadith on Travel: Supplication for righteous farewell journey
t: Qatadah ibn ‘Ayyash reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, concluded a meeting with my people, I took his hand and I bid him farewell. The Prophet said, “May Allah make fear of Him your provision, may He forgive your sins, and may He turn your face to goodness wherever you are.”
q: May Allah make fear of Him your provision, may He forgive your sins, and may He turn your face to goodness wherever you are.

title: Hadith on Taqwa: Best provision for travel is fear of Allah
t: Anas reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, I intend to travel, so supplicate for my provision.” The Prophet said, “May Allah provide you with fear of Him.” The man said, “Give me more.” The Prophet said, “May He forgive your sins.” The man said, “Give me more, may my father and my mother be ransomed for you!” The Prophet said, “May He make goodness easy for you wherever you are.”
q: May Allah provide you with fear of Him. … May He forgive your sins. … May He make goodness easy for you wherever you are.

title: Hadith on Taqwa: Godfearing pious are closest to the Prophet
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, dispatched him to Yemen, he went out with him to instruct Mu’adh as he was riding. When he finished, the Prophet said, “O Mu’adh, perhaps you will not see me after this year, perhaps you will pass by my mosque and my grave.” Mu’adh wept respectfully at the parting of the Messenger of Allah, then the Prophet turned to face Medina and he said, “Verily, the people of this house of mine view themselves as the nearest to me, but the nearest of people to me are the Godfearing, whoever they are and wherever they are. O Allah, I have not made lawful for them the wickedness You have corrected! I swear by Allah, my nation will turn away from its religion just as a vessel is poured into a basin.”
q: O Mu’adh, perhaps you will not see me after this year, perhaps you will pass by my mosque and my grave. … Verily, the people of this house of mine view themselves as the nearest to me, but the nearest of people to me are the Godfearing, whoever they are and wherever they are. O Allah, I have not made lawful for them the wickedness You have corrected! I swear by Allah, my nation will turn away from its religion just as a vessel is poured into a basin.

title: Uthman on Qisas: The Caliph lets his servant take retribution on himself
t: Abu al-Malih reported: Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, entered his house to find his servant boy playing in the trough of a camel. Uthman took him by the ear and twisted it, but he later regretted what he did. He said to him, “Take my ear and twist it.” Uthman made him do it, telling him to pull harder and harder, until he thought what had been done to himself was the same as he did. Uthman said, “How easy is retribution in the world before retribution in the Hereafter!”

title: Hadith on Family: Duties to household more important than voluntary worship
t: Wahb ibn Jabir reported: The client of Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him, “I intend to reside this month by the Sacred House in Jerusalem.” Abdullah said to him, “Have you left your family with enough to sustain themselves?” He said no. Abdullah said, “Return to your family and leave them with enough to sustain themselves, for I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: It is enough sin for a man to neglect those under his care.”
q: It is enough sin for a man to neglect those under his care.

title: Junayd on Tasawwuf: True Sufism based on Quran, Sunnah, and Fiqh
t: Abu al-Hasan ‘Ali reported: Al-Junayd ibn Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Our knowledge of Tasawwuf is defined by the Book and the Sunnah. Whoever does not memorize the Quran, nor write the prophetic teachings, nor study their understanding, he is not to be followed in it.”

title: Hadith on Moderation: Do not be hard on yourself in worship
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not be hard upon yourselves, lest the matter be made severe upon you. Verily, if people are hard upon themselves, Allah will be hard upon them. Their remnants are in the monasteries and abbeys.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “The monasticism they innovated, We did not prescribe it upon them.” (57:27)
q: Do not be hard upon yourselves, lest the matter be made severe upon you. Verily, if people are hard upon themselves, Allah will be hard upon them. Their remnants are in the monasteries and abbeys. … The monasticism they innovated, We did not prescribe it upon them.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Shirk: Origins of idolatry in grave worship, graven images
t: Aisha reported: Umm Habibah and Umm Salamah mentioned a church they saw in Abyssinia that had graven images in it. They mentioned it to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Verily, when a righteous man among them would die, they would build a place of worship over his grave and carve these images within it. They will be the worst to Allah on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Verily, when a righteous man among them would die, they would build a place of worship over his grave and carve these images within it. They will be the worst to Allah on the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salat: Angels descend to watch, record your prayers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A group of angels stay with you by night and another group of angels by day. They meet together at the time of afternoon prayer and dawn prayer, then those who stayed with you ascend to the heavens. Allah asks them, although He knows better than them: How did you leave My servants? The angels say: We left them while they were praying, and we came to them while they were praying.”
q: A group of angels stay with you by night and another group of angels by day. They meet together at the time of afternoon prayer and dawn prayer, then those who stayed with you ascend to the heavens. Allah asks them, although He knows better than them: How did you leave My servants? The angels say: We left them while they were praying, and we came to them while they were praying.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Abdullah on Munkar: Destruction for one not rejecting evil in his heart
t: Tariq ibn Shihab reported: A man said to Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, “The one who does not enjoin good or forbid evil has been ruined!” Abdullah said, “Rather, the one who does not recognize good in his heart or reject evil in his heart has been ruined.”

title: Hadith on Da’wah: The Prophet arises to warn his family
t: Abu Huraira reported: When the verse, “Warn your closest relatives,” (26:214) was revealed to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, he said, “O assembly of Quraysh! Purchase your souls from Allah, for I cannot avail you from Allah at all. O tribe of Abdul Muttalib, I cannot avail you from Allah at all. O ‘Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib, I cannot avail you from Allah at all. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, I cannot avail you from Allah at all. O Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah, ask from me whatever you wish, but I cannot avail you from Allah at all.”
q: Warn your closest relatives … O assembly of Quraysh! Purchase your souls from Allah, for I cannot avail you from Allah at all. O tribe of Abdul Muttalib, I cannot avail you from Allah at all. O ‘Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib, I cannot avail you from Allah at all. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, I cannot avail you from Allah at all. O Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah, ask from me whatever you wish, but I cannot avail you from Allah at all.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Graves: Supplication for visiting graveyards
t: Buraydah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to teach them as they went to visit the graves, saying to their inhabitants, “Peace be upon you, O people of this abode, from the believers and the Muslims. We will soon, if Allah wills, be joining you. I ask Allah to grant well-being to us and to you.”
q: Peace be upon you, O people of this abode, from the believers and the Muslims. We will soon, if Allah wills, be joining you. I ask Allah to grant well-being to us and to you.

title: Hadith on Signs: Time passes quickly before the Hour
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hour will not be established until time passes rapidly, such that a year is like a month, a month is like a week, a week is like a day, a day is like an hour, and an hour is like the flicker of a flame.”
q: The Hour will not be established until time passes rapidly, such that a year is like a month, a month is like a week, a week is like a day, a day is like an hour, and an hour is like the flicker of a flame.

title: Hadith on Shirk: How to protect from lesser idolatry?
t: Abu Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O people, beware of this idolatry, for it is more hidden than a crawling ant!” It was said, “Whomever Allah wills to say! How do we protect ourselves from it while it is more hidden than a crawling ant?” The Prophet said, “Say: O Allah, we seek refuge in You from associating any partners with You while we know, and we seek Your forgiveness for what we do not know.”
q: O people, beware of this idolatry, for it is more hidden than a crawling ant! … Say: O Allah, we seek refuge in You from associating any partners with You while we know, and we seek Your forgiveness for what we do not know.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Istighfar: Allah marvels at believer seeking forgiveness
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is astonished at a servant when he says: There is no God but You, I have wronged myself so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You. Allah says: My servant acknowledges that he has a Lord who forgives and punishes.”
q: Verily, Allah is astonished at a servant when he says: There is no God but You, I have wronged myself so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You. Allah says: My servant acknowledges that he has a Lord who forgives and punishes.

title: Hadith on Salat: Timings of the five prayers
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you perform the dawn prayer, its time is until the first rising of the sun. Then, when you perform noon prayer, its time is until the presence of afternoon. When you perform the afternoon prayer, its time is until the sun turns yellow. When you perform the sunset prayer, its time is until the twilight has disappeared. When you perform the evening prayer, its time is until midnight.”
q: When you perform the dawn prayer, its time is until the first rising of the sun. Then, when you perform noon prayer, its time is until the presence of afternoon. When you perform the afternoon prayer, its time is until the sun turns yellow. When you perform the sunset prayer, its time is until the twilight has disappeared. When you perform the evening prayer, its time is until midnight.

title: Hadith on Salat: Praying with and for every Muslim
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Perform funeral prayer over whoever says there is no God but Allah. Perform prayer behind whoever says there is no God but Allah.”
q: Perform funeral prayer over whoever says there is no God but Allah. Perform prayer behind whoever says there is no God but Allah.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Ibn Abdul Barr

title: Hadith on Mithaq: Allah takes covenant from children of Adam
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah took the covenant from the loins of Adam at Arafat, bringing forth from his backbone every seed that he would sow. He scattered them before him and then He spoke to them as they stood before Him, saying: Am I not your Lord? They said: Of course, we bear witness. Lest you say on the Day of Resurrection: We were unaware of this.” (7:172)
q: Allah took the covenant from the loins of Adam at Arafat, bringing forth from his backbone every seed that he would sow. He scattered them before him and then He spoke to them as they stood before Him, saying: Am I not your Lord? They said: Of course, we bear witness. Lest you say on the Day of Resurrection: We were unaware of this.

title: Hadith on Pardon: The Prophet lets an enemy combatant go free
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, fought against the tribe of Muharib ibn Khasafah, and a man among them named Ghawrath ibn al-Harith came until he was standing over the Messenger of Allah with a sword. The man said, “Who will protect you from me?” The Prophet said, “Allah.” The sword fell from his hand, and the Prophet picked it up, saying, “Who will protect you from me?” The man said, “Be better than the offender!” The Prophet said, “Will you testify that there is no God but Allah, and I am the Messenger of Allah?” The man said, “No, but I promise not to fight you, nor will I join anyone fighting you.” The Prophet let him go, and the man returned to his people, saying, “I have just come to you from the best of people!”
q: Allah … Who will protect you from me? … Will you testify that there is no God but Allah, and I am the Messenger of Allah?

title: Hadith on Zuhd: The simple living of the Prophet
t: Aisha reported: She said to ‘Urwah, “O my nephew, we used to sight three crescent moons in two months without having any fire to cook in the house of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.” ‘Urwah said, “How did you live?” Aisha said, “With the two dark things, dates and water, except that the Messenger of Allah had neighbors among the Ansar who had some milking animals. They would give the Messenger of Allah some milk from their animals and he would give it to us to drink.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Funerals: Supplicating benefits believers in grave
t: Uthman ibn Affan reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when he finished burying the deceased, he would stand over them and say, “Seek forgiveness for your brothers and ask Allah to keep them firm, for they are being questioned now.”
q: Seek forgiveness for your brothers and ask Allah to keep them firm, for they are being questioned now.

title: Malik on Knowledge: When to say I do not know
t:
Abdur Rahman ibn Mahdi reported: I was with Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, as a man came and he said, “O Abu Abdullah, I have come from a distance of six months travel. The people of my land have an issue to ask you about.” Malik said, “Then ask.” The man asked him about the issue and Malik said, “I do not know it.” The man was speechless, as if he had thought he came to someone who knew everything. The man said, “So what do I say to my people when I return to them?” Malik said, “Say to them that Malik said: I do not know.”

Ibn Wahb said, “I heard him many times saying: I do not know.”

title: Hadith on Nubuwwa: The Prophet is given five unique blessings
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have been given five that were given to no one before me: every prophet was sent specifically to his people but I have been sent to every white and black person, spoils are made lawful for me and they were not lawful for anyone before me, the entire earth has been made pure and clean and a place of prayer for me such that a man can pray anywhere he is at the time of prayer, I have been supported by the dread of my enemies even as far as a month of marching, and I have been granted the Intercession.”
q: I have been given five that were given to no one before me: every prophet was sent specifically to his people but I have been sent to every white and black person, spoils are made lawful for me and they were not lawful for anyone before me, the entire earth has been made pure and clean and a place of prayer for me such that a man can pray anywhere he is at the time of prayer, I have been supported by the dread of my enemies even as far as a month of marching, and I have been granted the Intercession.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Mubarak on Sins: Calamity to not care about your faults
t: Al-Husayn reported: Ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Among the greatest of calamities is that a man knows his own shortcomings, but he does not care about them, nor does he grieve over them.”

title: Ali on Tawbah: Repentance is by deeds, not merely words
t: Musa ibn Abi Habib reported: Ali ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, repentance is only by action and turning away from the matter. Repentance is not by speech alone.”

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet’s supplication after prayer
t: Al-Mughirah reported: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saying after the prayer, “There is no God but Allah alone without any partners. O Allah, none can withhold what You give and none can give what You withhold. The might of the mighty is no benefit against You.”
q: There is no God but Allah alone without any partners. O Allah, none can withhold what You give and none can give what You withhold. The might of the mighty is no benefit against You.

title: Hadith on Salawat: Great rewards for blessing the Prophet
t: Abu Talhah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A visitor came to me from my Lord Almighty and he said: Whoever among your nation blesses you, Allah will record for him ten good deeds, He will erase ten bad deeds, He will raise him ten degrees, and the angel will respond with the same.”
q: A visitor came to me from my Lord Almighty and he said: Whoever among your nation blesses you, Allah will record for him ten good deeds, He will erase ten bad deeds, He will raise him ten degrees, and the angel will respond with the same.

title: Hudhayfah on Fitnah: Who are the dead among the living?
t: Abu al-Tufayl reported: It was said to Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, “Who are the dead among the living?” Hudhayfah said, “Those who do not recognize good in their hearts and do not reject evil in their hearts.”

title: Mu’adh on Haqq: Accept truth even from unbelievers
t: Ibn Taymiyyah reported: Mu’adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, would say, “Accept the truth from whoever brings it, even if he is an unbeliever or a sinner.”

title: Hadith on Mercy: Allah loves praise, forgiving His servants
t: Al-Aswad ibn Sari’ reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one loves to be praised more than Allah Almighty, and no one accepts more excuses than Allah Almighty.”
q: No one loves to be praised more than Allah Almighty, and no one accepts more excuses than Allah Almighty.

title: Hadith on Qiyamah: All are resurrected as they had died
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Every servant will be resurrected upon the way that they died.”
q: Every servant will be resurrected upon the way that they died.

title: Hadith on Salawat: Forgetting to send blessings on the Prophet
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever forgets to send blessings upon me, he has missed the path to Paradise.”
q: Whoever forgets to send blessings upon me, he has missed the path to Paradise.

title: Hadith on Sneezing: Response to a non-Muslim who sneezes
t: Abu Musa reported: The Jews used to sneeze in front of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, hoping that he would say, “May Allah have mercy on you.” The Prophet would say, “May Allah guide you and amend your affairs.”
q: May Allah guide you and amend your affairs.

title: Hadith on Manners: Sneezing and its proper etiquette
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you sneezes, let him say: All praise is due to Allah. Let his brother or companion say: May Allah have mercy on you. When he invokes the mercy of Allah upon him, let him say: May Allah guide you and amend your affairs.”
q: When one of you sneezes, let him say: All praise is due to Allah. Let his brother or companion say: May Allah have mercy on you. When he invokes the mercy of Allah upon him, let him say: May Allah guide you and amend your affairs.

title: Hadith on Qunut: The Prophet prays for reforming hardship
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when he said, “Allah listened to those who praise Him,” in the last cycle of evening prayer, he stood to supplicate, “O Allah, save ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabiah. O Allah, save Al-Walid ibn al-Walid. O Allah, save Salamah ibn Hisham. O Allah, save the oppressed among the believers. O Allah, be hard on the tribe of Mudar. O Allah, place drought in their years like the years of Joseph.”
q: Allah listened to those who praise Him … O Allah, save ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabiah. O Allah, save Al-Walid ibn al-Walid. O Allah, save Salamah ibn Hisham. O Allah, save the oppressed among the believers. O Allah, be hard on the tribe of Mudar. O Allah, place drought in their years like the years of Joseph.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salawat: The Prophet shown supplications for him
t: Abu Mas’ud al-Ansari reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Increase your blessings upon me on Friday, for no one blesses me on Friday but that his prayer is presented to me.”
q: Increase your blessings upon me on Friday, for no one blesses me on Friday but that his prayer is presented to me.

title: Mu’adh on Silence: Speak to people little, but to Allah often
t: Al-Qushayri reported: Mu’adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Talk to people a little and talk to your Almighty Lord often, for perhaps your heart will see Allah Almighty.”

title: Ahnaf on Anger: Beware political rage leading to bloodshed
t: Al-‘Ala’ ibn Jarir reported: Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “It is not appropriate for the leader to be angry, for anger with power is a source of the sword and regret.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Brotherhood: Treat him as you like to be treated
t: Mujahid reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be please with him, said, “Mention your brother when he is absent in the way you would love to be mentioned by him. Forgive him as you would love to be forgiven by him.”

title: Ibrahim on Dua: No harm in asking Allah to guide non-Muslims
t: Mansur reported: Ibrahim al-Nakhi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “There is nothing wrong if one says to a Jew or a Christian: May Allah guide you.”

title: Hadith on Istighfar: Seeking forgiveness from Allah all day long
t: Abu Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I never start a new day but that I seek forgiveness from Allah one hundred times during it.”
q: I never start a new day but that I seek forgiveness from Allah one hundred times during it.

title: Umar on Tawbah: The meaning of sincere repentance
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: I asked Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, about His saying, “Repent to Allah with sincere repentance,” (66:8). Umar said, “It is a servant who repents from a sin and never commits it again.”
q: Repent to Allah with sincere repentance,

title: Hadith on Friday: A caravan arrives in Medina, Muslims distracted
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: We were praying with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as a caravan arrived carrying food. They turned their attention to it until none remained with the Prophet but twelve men. Thus, the verse was revealed, “When they saw trade or diversion, they rushed to it and left you standing.” (62:11)
q: When they saw trade or diversion, they rushed to it and left you standing.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Sufyan on Dunya: Leave the worldly life for the rulers
t: Yahya ibn Abdil Malik reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, the kings have left the Hereafter to you, so leave the world to them.”

title: Hadith on Shukr: Sin of ingratitude to husbands who provide
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah will not look at a woman who is ungrateful to her husband while she cannot take care of herself without him.”
q: Allah will not look at a woman who is ungrateful to her husband while she cannot take care of herself without him.

title: Hadith on Parents: Transgression, disobedience swiftly punished
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two deeds are quickly punished in the world: transgression and disrespect to parents.”
q: Two deeds are quickly punished in the world: transgression and disrespect to parents

title: Malik on Salaf: Way of righteous predecessors our only option
t: Malik ibn Anas reported: Wahb ibn Kaysan, may Allah have mercy on him, would sit with us and he would not stand to leave until he said to us, “Nothing will reform the latter of this nation except what reformed the beginning of it.”

title: Hadith on Children: They are the delight of your eyes
t: Al-Ash’ath ibn Qays reported: I approached the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, during the delegation of Kindah. The Prophet said to me, “Do you have any children?” I said, “A boy was born to me as I was coming out to you, from a daughter of Jamd. I wish in his place I could provide food for my impoverished people instead.” The Prophet said, “Do not say this, for they are the delight of your eyes and you will be rewarded if they pass away. If you say this, they will surely turn you into a coward and be a source of grief, they will surely turn you into a coward and be a source of grief.”
q: Do you have any children? … Do not say this, for they are the delight of your eyes and you will be rewarded if they pass away. If you say this, they will surely turn you into a coward and be a source of grief, they will surely turn you into a coward and be a source of grief

title: ‘Amr on Fitnah: Tyranny a better situation than lengthy tribulation
t: Ibn ‘Asakir reported: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As, may Allah be pleased with him, said to his son, “My son, memorize what I instruct you: a just leader is better than abundant rain, a predatory lion is better than an oppressive leader, and an oppressive and tyrannical leader is better than an everlasting tribulation.”

title: Hadith on Rulers: Advising the Muslim leader in private
t: Abu Wa’il reported: It was said to Usamah ibn Yazid, may Allah be pleased with him, “Have you not spoken to Uthman?” Usamah said, “You think I have not spoken to him unless you heard it? I have certainly spoken to him in the matter between us without bringing it up. I do not like to be the first to bring it up.”

title: Hadith on Rulers: Fear Allah, listen, and obey lawful orders
t: ‘Adi ibn Hatim reported: We said, “O Messenger of Allah, we do not ask you about obedience to Godfearing rulers, but rather those who do this and that,” and he mentioned their evil. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Fear Allah, listen, and obey.”
q: Fear Allah, listen, and obey.

title: Hadith on Rulers: Patience with tyranny but no obedience in sin
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Listen and obey authorities in hardship, in ease, and in what you dislike, even if they give undue preference over you, even if they consume your property and they strike your back, unless they order flagrant disobedience to Allah.”
q: Listen and obey authorities in hardship, in ease, and in what you dislike, even if they give undue preference over you, even if they consume your property and they strike your back, unless they order flagrant disobedience to Allah.

title: Hadith on Rulers: What if they do not give us our rights?
t: Wa’il al-Hadrami reported: Salamah ibn Yazid asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “O Prophet of Allah, what do you think if rulers are charged over us who demand their rights and prevent us from our rights? What do you command us to do?” The Prophet turned away from him, then he asked a second or third time, so Al-Ash’ath ibn Qays pulled him to the side. The Prophet said, “Listen and obey, for their burdens are upon them and your burdens are upon you.”
q: Listen and obey, for their burdens are upon them and your burdens are upon you.

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Tribulations coming one after another
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, no prophet came before me but that it was a duty upon him to guide his nation to what he knew was good for them and to warn them of what he knew was evil for them. This nation of yours has been granted well-being in its beginning, but the latter generations will be afflicted with trials and affairs you will recognize as evil. Tribulations will come one after another, and a tribulation will come in which the believer says: This will destroy me! Then it will pass and another tribulation will come in which the believer says: This one, this one! Thus, whoever would love to be delivered from Hellfire and admitted into Paradise, let him meet his end with faith in Allah and the Last Day, and let him treat people as he would love to be treated. Whoever pledges allegiance to a leader should give him the contract of his hand and sincerity of his heart, so let him obey as much as he can. If another leads comes to start rebellion, strike the neck of the other.”
q: Verily, no prophet came before me but that it was a duty upon him to guide his nation to what he knew was good for them and to warn them of what he knew was evil for them. This nation of yours has been granted well-being in its beginning, but the latter generations will be afflicted with trials and affairs you will recognize as evil. Tribulations will come one after another, and a tribulation will come in which the believer says: This will destroy me! Then it will pass and another tribulation will come in which the believer says: This one, this one! Thus, whoever would love to be delivered from Hellfire and admitted into Paradise, let him meet his end with faith in Allah and the Last Day, and let him treat people as he would love to be treated. Whoever pledges allegiance to a leader should give him the contract of his hand and sincerity of his heart, so let him obey as much as he can. If another leads comes to start rebellion, strike the neck of the other.

title: Hadith on Obedience: Obey the Prophet as much as you can
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: When we pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on condition of listening and obeying, he said to us, “As much as you are able.”
q: As much as you are able.

title: Hadith on Sultan: Obey authorities in prosperity and adversity
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must listen and obey authorities in hardship and ease, what you are eager for and what you dislike, even if they give undue preference over you.”
q: You must listen and obey authorities in hardship and ease, what you are eager for and what you dislike, even if they give undue preference over you.

title: Malik on Rulers: Do not curse kings, rather repent to Allah
t: Salih al-Murri reported: Malik ibn Dinar, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I have found in the Wisdom that Allah says: I am Allah, the King of kings. The hearts of the kings are in My hand. Whoever obeys Me, I will make them merciful to him, and whoever disobeys Me, I will make them malicious to him. Do not be preoccupied with cursing the kings, but rather repent to Me and I will make them compassionate to you.”

title: Hadith on Khuruj: Rebels have rejected guidance of Islam
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever secedes from the community as much as a handspan has thrown the yoke of Islam off of his neck.”
q: Whoever secedes from the community as much as a handspan has thrown the yoke of Islam off of his neck.

title: Hadith on Khuruj: Violent rebellion against Muslim ruler is ignorance
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None of the people rebel against the ruler by as much as a handspan and die but that he will have died a death of ignorance.”
q: None of the people rebel against the ruler by as much as a handspan and die but that he will have died a death of ignorance.

title: Hadith on Sultan: Sincerely advising Muslims rulers and authorities
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is pleased for you to sincerely advise those to whom Allah has given authority over your affairs.”
q: Verily, Allah is pleased for you to sincerely advise those to whom Allah has given authority over your affairs.

title: Hadith on Trade: Business dealings with unbelievers, idolaters
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Bakr reported: We were with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when a tall man from the idolaters came driving sheep. The Prophet said, “Are they for sale, gift, or donation?” The man said, “No, they are for sale.” The Prophet purchased one sheep from him.
q: Are they for sale, gift, or donation?

title: Hadith on Imarah: Every leader has good and evil advisors
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A Caliph is never appointed but that he has two advisors: one advisor orders him to do good and encourages him, and another advisor orders him to do evil and encourages him. The unscathed are only those whom Allah has protected.”
q: A Caliph is never appointed but that he has two advisors: one advisor orders him to do good and encourages him, and another advisor orders him to do evil and encourages him. The unscathed are only those whom Allah has protected.

title: Hadith on Hajj: Jihad for women without fighting
t: Aisha reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, is jihad a duty upon women?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Yes, jihad is a duty upon them in which there is no fighting: the Hajj and ‘Umrah pilgrimages.”
q: Yes, jihad is a duty upon them in which there is no fighting: the Hajj and ‘Umrah pilgrimages.

title: Hadith on Jud: Allah is generous, magnanimous, righteous
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty is magnanimous and He loves magnanimity. He loves the highest morals and He detests pettiness.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty is magnanimous and He loves magnanimity. He loves the highest morals and He detests pettiness.

title: Hadith on Dhulm: Allah angry with helpers of injustice
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever supports a disputant in wrongdoing, or helps in wrongdoing, he will be subject to the wrath of Allah until he removes himself.”
q: Whoever supports a disputant in wrongdoing, or helps in wrongdoing, he will be subject to the wrath of Allah until he removes himself.

title: Hadith on Evil: Three sinners will not enter Paradise
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Three will not enter Paradise: the stubborn drunkard, the one who severs family ties, and the believer in magic.”
q: Three will not enter Paradise: the stubborn drunkard, the one who severs family ties, and the believer in magic.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Rahim: Deeds not accepted from estranged relatives
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the deeds of the children of Adam are presented every Thursday, when night turns into Friday. The deeds are not accepted from one who severed his family ties.”
q: Verily, the deeds of the children of Adam are presented every Thursday, when night turns into Friday. The deeds are not accepted from one who severed his family ties.

title: Hadith on Rahim: Benefits of good relationships with family
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the quickest act of obedience to be rewarded is to maintain family ties, even if the people of the household are wicked, such that it will grow their wealth and increase their numbers if they maintain family ties. No people of a household maintain family ties and remain in need.”
q: Verily, the quickest act of obedience to be rewarded is to maintain family ties, even if the people of the household are wicked, such that it will grow their wealth and increase their numbers if they maintain family ties. No people of a household maintain family ties and remain in need.

title: Hadith on Rahim: Increase your lifespan, expand provision
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Surely, whoever wants to extend his lifespan and expand his provision, let him uphold his family ties.”
q: “Surely, whoever wants to extend his lifespan and expand his provision, let him uphold his family ties.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Rahim: The womb pleads to the Most Merciful
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the womb has an iron hook attached firmly to the Throne, speaking with a penetrating tongue: O Allah, keep relations with whoever keeps relations with me, and sever relations with whoever severs them with me. Allah Almighty says: I am the Gracious, the Merciful. I derived the womb from My name. Whoever keeps relations with it, I keep relations with him. Whoever cuts off relations with it, I cut off relations with him.”
q: Verily, the womb has an iron hook attached firmly to the Throne, speaking with a penetrating tongue: O Allah, keep relations with whoever keeps relations with me, and sever relations with whoever severs them with me. Allah Almighty says: I am the Gracious, the Merciful. I derived the womb from My name. Whoever keeps relations with it, I keep relations with him. Whoever cuts off relations with it, I cut off relations with him.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Rahim: Allah has mercy on close families
t: Abdur Rahman ibn ‘Awf reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah said: I am Allah and I am the Merciful. I created the womb and I derived it from My name. Whoever upholds it, I will uphold him. Whoever severs it, I will deprive him of My mercy.”
q: Allah said: I am Allah and I am the Merciful. I created the womb and I derived it from My name. Whoever upholds it, I will uphold him. Whoever severs it, I will deprive him of My mercy.

title: Hadith on Advice: The Prophet’s virtuous instructions to Abu Dharr
t: Abu Dharr reported: My dear friend, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, instructed me with virtuous traits. He instructed me not to look at those above me and to look at those below me. He instructed me to love the poor and be close to them. He instructed me to maintain my family ties even if they turn their backs. He instructed me not to fear the blame of the blamer in the matter of Allah. He instructed me to speak the truth even if it is bitter. He instructed me to increase in declaring there is no movement or might but in Allah, for it is a treasure among the treasures of Paradise.

title: Hadith on Dua: Do not help criminals by cursing them
t: Aisha reported: Something was stolen from her, so she began to supplicate against the thief. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not lighten his sin.”
q: Do not lighten his sin.

title: Hadith on Pardon: Expiation for forgiving harmful injuries
t: Al-Muharrir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever suffers injury to his body by someone, in any way, and he leaves it for the sake of Allah, it will be an expiation for him.”
q: Whoever suffers injury to his body by someone, in any way, and he leaves it for the sake of Allah, it will be an expiation for him.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Witr: Allah added Witr prayer, so perform it
t: Abu Basrah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty has added one to your prayers, so perform it between the evening and dawn prayers: the Witr prayer, the Witr prayer.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty has added one to your prayers, so perform it between the evening and dawn prayers: the Witr prayer, the Witr prayer.

title: Hadith on Witr: Allah loves what is odd in number
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is numerically odd, and He loves what is odd in number.”
q: Verily, Allah is numerically odd, and He loves what is odd in number.

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Voluntary raka’at after Isha prayer
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, never performed the evening prayer and entered my home but that he would then pray four or six cycles.

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Continuous praying between Maghrib and Isha
t: Hudhayfah reported: I came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and I performed the evening prayer with him. The Prophet continued to pray until the evening prayer.

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Voluntary prayer between Maghrib and Isha
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: In regards to the verse, “They arise from their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and in hope, spending from what We have provided them,” (32:16). Anas said, “They are those who are awake to pray between sunset and evening prayer.”
q: They arise from their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and in hope, spending from what We have provided them

title: Hadith on Nawafil: The Prophet’s beautiful prayer before Dhuhur
t: Abu Qabus reported: My father sent word to Aisha, asking, “Which prayer did the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, most love to perform regularly?” Aisha said, “The Prophet would perform four cycles before noon prayer, lengthening their standing, bowing and prostrating in the best manner.”
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Four raka’at before Dhuhur ascend to heaven
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would pray four cycles before noon prayer. It was said to him, “You are always performing this prayer.” The Prophet said, “Verily, gates of heavens are opened when the sun begins to decline. They do not begin to close until the noon prayer is completed. Thus, I love for my good deeds to ascend to the heavens.”
q: Verily, gates of heavens are opened when the sun begins to decline. They do not begin to close until the noon prayer is completed. Thus, I love for my good deeds to ascend to the heavens.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Salat al-Duha is prayer of repentant
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None preserve the forenoon prayer but the penitent. It is the prayer of the penitent.”
q: None preserve the forenoon prayer but the penitent. It is the prayer of the penitent.

title: Hadith on Salat: Prayer rewarded like pilgrimage
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever leaves his house with ritual purification for a prescribed prayer, his reward will be like one performing a Hajj pilgrimage in a state of sanctity. Whoever leaves to glorify Allah in the forenoon, laboring only for this purpose, his reward will be like one performing the Umrah pilgrimage.”
q: Whoever leaves his house with ritual purification for a prescribed prayer, his reward will be like one performing a Hajj pilgrimage in a state of sanctity. Whoever leaves to glorify Allah in the forenoon, laboring only for this purpose, his reward will be like one performing the Umrah pilgrimage.

title: Hadith on Salat: Prayer after prayer recorded in heaven
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Prayer followed by another prayer, without any vain talk in between, is written in the heavenly record.” (83:18)
q: Prayer followed by another prayer, without any vain talk in between, is written in the heavenly record

title: Hadith on Prayer: Salat al-Duha, Allah will be enough
t: Nu’aym ibn Hammar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty says: O son of Adam, do not be frustrated to perform four cycles of prayer for me at the beginning of your day. I will suffice you for the rest of it.”
q: Allah Almighty says: O son of Adam, do not be frustrated to perform four cycles of prayer for me at the beginning of your day. I will suffice you for the rest of it.

title: Hadith on Duha: Four raka’at for Allah, He will suffice your day
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty says: O son of Adam, suffice Me with four cycles of prayer at the beginning of the morning and by them I will suffice you for the rest of your day.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty says: O son of Adam, suffice Me with four cycles of prayer at the beginning of the morning and by them I will suffice you for the rest of your day.

title: Hadith on Spoils: Remembrance in mosque better than booty
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, dispatched a company to Najd and they acquired many spoils and rushed back. A man who did not go with them said, “We have not seen a company return more swiftly and with better spoils than this one!” The Prophet said, “Shall I not tell you about a people with better spoils and a swifter return? People who attend the dawn prayer, then sit remembering Allah until the sun rises. These have a swifter return and better spoils.”
q: Shall I not tell you about a people with better spoils and a swifter return? People who attend the dawn prayer, then sit remembering Allah until the sun rises. These have a swifter return and better spoils.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Salat: Two raka’at of mindful prayer, sins forgiven
t: Zayd ibn Khalid reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever performs ablution in the best manner, then prays two cycles, without being unmindful in either of them, his previous sins will be forgiven.”
q: Whoever performs ablution in the best manner, then prays two cycles, without being unmindful in either of them, his previous sins will be forgiven
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Duha: Forenoon prayer is better than spoils
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, dispatched a company that acquired a great amount of spoils and returned quickly. A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, we have not had a company of our people return more quickly with greater spoils!” The Prophet said, “Shall I not tell you of a swifter return and greater spoils than this company? A man who performs ablution in the best manner, then sets out to the mosque to pray in it in the morning and ends with forenoon prayer. He has a swifter return and greater spoils.”
q: Shall I not tell you of a swifter return and greater spoils than this company? A man who performs ablution in the best manner, then sets out to the mosque to pray in it in the morning and ends with forenoon prayer. He has a swifter return and greater spoils.

title: Hadith on Salat: Duha prayer better than spoils of war
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, once dispatched a company. They acquired spoils and rushed back to tell people how close their battle was, how many their spoils were, and how quickly they returned. The Prophet said, “Shall I not tell you what is closer than a battle, more plentiful than spoils, and a swifter return? One who performs ablution, then goes to the mosque in the morning to glorify Allah in the forenoon. It is a closer battle, more plentiful spoils, and a swifter return.”
q: Shall I not tell you what is closer than a battle, more plentiful than spoils, and a swifter return? One who performs ablution, then goes to the mosque in the morning to glorify Allah in the forenoon. It is a closer battle, more plentiful spoils, and a swifter return.

title: Hadith on Advice: Fasting, Salat al-Duha, Witr prayer
t: Abu Darda reported: My beloved friend, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, instructed me with three deeds I will never leave for as long as I live: fasting three days a month, performing forenoon prayer, and not sleeping until performing Witr prayer.

title: Hadith on Dua: Allah angry when He is not asked
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever never asks from Allah, He will be angry with him.”
q: Whoever never asks from Allah, He will be angry with him

title: Hadith on Love: Visit each other, love each other
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported; The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Visit each other periodically. It will increase your love.”
q: Visit each other periodically. It will increase your love.

title: Hadith on Visiting: The Prophet visits to comfort a blind man
t: Jubayr ibn Mut’im reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Come with us to the tribe of Waqif. We, who can see, will visit a man whose eyes cannot.”
q: Come with us to the tribe of Waqif. We, who can see, will visit a man whose eyes cannot.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Prophets, martyrs, children in Paradise
t: Hasna’ bint Mu’awiyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Prophet is in Paradise, the martyrs are in Paradise, the young children who die are in Paradise, and the infant buried alive is in Paradise.”
q: The Prophet is in Paradise, the martyrs are in Paradise, the young children who die are in Paradise, and the infant buried alive is in Paradise.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Who is in Paradise?
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you about your men in Paradise?” We said, “Of course, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “The Prophet is in Paradise, the truthful are in Paradise, the martyrs are in Paradise, the child who dies is in Paradise, and a man who visits his brother in a faraway land, only visiting him for the sake of Allah, is in Paradise.”
q: Shall I not tell you about your men in Paradise? … The Prophet is in Paradise, the truthful are in Paradise, the martyrs are in Paradise, the child who dies is in Paradise, and a man who visits his brother in a faraway land, only visiting him for the sake of Allah, is in Paradise.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Visiting: Paradise rewarded for visiting fellow Muslims
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No Muslim servant visits his brother for the sake of Allah but that a caller from the heavens announces: You are purified and Paradise is purified for you! Otherwise, Allah says in the realms of His throne: My servant has visited Me and his guest for My sake, so I am not pleased for him to have any reward other than Paradise.”
q: No Muslim servant visits his brother for the sake of Allah but that a caller from the heavens announces: You are purified and Paradise is purified for you! Otherwise, Allah says in the realms of His throne: My servant has visited Me and his guest for My sake, so I am not pleased for him to have any reward other than Paradise.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Akhirah: No death in Hereafter, only eternity
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the people of Paradise will be sent to Paradise, and the people of Hellfire will be sent to Hellfire, until they are separated between them. Then, death will be slaughtered and a heavenly caller will announce: O people of Paradise, there is no death! O people of Hellfire, there is no death! For the people of Paradise, it will add joy to their joy, and for the people of Hellfire, it will add grief to their grief.”
q: When the people of Paradise will be sent to Paradise, and the people of Hellfire will be sent to Hellfire, until they are separated between them. Then, death will be slaughtered and a heavenly caller will announce: O people of Paradise, there is no death! O people of Hellfire, there is no death! For the people of Paradise, it will add joy to their joy, and for the people of Hellfire, it will add grief to their grief.

title: Hadith on Zaynab: The generosity of the Prophet’s wife
t: Aisha reported: Some of the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him, “Which of us will be the quickest to meet you?” The Prophet said, “The one with the longest hand.” They measured their hands with sticks and Sawdah had the longest of them, yet Zaynab was the first to die. Then, we knew that the length of her hand meant her charity. She was the quickest to meet him and she loved to give charity.
q: The one with the longest hand.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Trials: Nations gather to dominate weak Ummah
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Soon the nations will be summoned to you just like one is invited to a feast.” It was said, “Will we be few in that day?” The Prophet said, “No, rather you will be many in that day, but you will be scum like such flowing down a torrent. Allah will remove your esteem from the chests of your enemies, and Allah will insert feebleness in your own hearts.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is this feebleness?” The Prophet said, “Love for the worldly life and hatred of death.”
q: Soon the nations will be summoned to you just like one is invited to a feast. … No, rather you will be many in that day, but you will be scum like such flowing down a torrent. Allah will remove your esteem from the chests of your enemies, and Allah will insert feebleness in your own hearts. … Love for the worldly life and hatred of death.

title: Hadith on Life: Long living always good for a believer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Let none of you wish for death, nor call for it before its time comes. When one of you dies, his deeds come to an end. Verily, the life of a believer only increases in good.”
q: Let none of you wish for death, nor call for it before its time comes. When one of you dies, his deeds come to an end. Verily, the life of a believer only increases in good.

title: Hadith on Despair: Never wish for death, only improvement
t: Umm al-Fadl reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered the home of Al-‘Abbas while he was complaining and wishing for death. The Prophet said, “O ‘Abbas, O uncle of the Messenger of Allah, do not wish for death. If you are a good-doer, your goodness will be added to your goodness, and it will be good for you. If you are an evil-doer, you will be given time to make amends for your evil, and it will be good for you.”
q: O ‘Abbas, O uncle of the Messenger of Allah, do not wish for death. If you are a good-doer, your goodness will be added to your goodness, and it will be good for you. If you are an evil-doer, you will be given time to make amends for your evil, and it will be good for you.

title: Hadith on Life: Best believers live long to glorify Allah
t: Talhah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no one better to Allah than a believer who lives long in Islam to glorify Him, exalt Him, and declare His oneness.”
q: There is no one better to Allah than a believer who lives long in Islam to glorify Him, exalt Him, and declare His oneness.

title: Hadith on Life: Best Muslims live long, greatest deeds
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you about the best of you?” They said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “The best of you are those with the longest lives and best deeds.”
q: Shall I not tell you about the best of you? … The best of you are those with the longest lives and best deeds.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Caution: Deliberating all things except actions of Hereafter
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is careful hesitation in everything but the deeds of the Hereafter.”
q: There is careful hesitation in everything but the deeds of the Hereafter.

title: Hadith on Jama’ah: Come to Isha and Fajr, even if crawling
t: Abu Darda reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Worship Allah as if you can see Him, for if you do not see Him, He surely sees you. Prepare yourself for death and beware of the supplication of the oppressed, for it will be answered. If one of you can attend the evening and dawn prayers, even if you must crawl, then do so.”
q: Worship Allah as if you can see Him, for if you do not see Him, He surely sees you. Prepare yourself for death and beware of the supplication of the oppressed, for it will be answered. If one of you can attend the evening and dawn prayers, even if you must crawl, then do so.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Salat: Pray as if you are saying farewell
t: Ibn Umar reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, give me a teaching and make it concise.” The Prophet said, “Pray your prayers as if they were your last, for if you do not see Him, He surely sees you. Give up trying to acquire what people have and you will be wealthy. Beware of doing anything for which you must apologize.”
q: Pray your prayers as if they were your last, for if you do not see Him, He surely sees you. Give up trying to acquire what people have and you will be wealthy. Beware of doing anything for which you must apologize.

title: Hadith on Hour: Hereafter approaching, people forgetful
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hour is approaching people, yet it does not increase but in distance from their minds.”
q: The Hour is approaching people, yet it does not increase but in distance from their minds.

title: Hadith on Aml: Your worldly hopes exceed your lifespan
t: Buraydah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do you know what these are?” The Prophet threw down two pebbles. They said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Prophet said, “This further one is your worldly hope and this closer one is your lifespan.”
q: Do you know what these are? … This further one is your worldly hope and this closer one is your lifespan.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Death: Man’s hopes extend beyond his lifespan
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “This is the son of Adam and this is his lifespan,” and he placed his hands on the back of his neck and then extended them outwardly, saying, “And from there he hopes in the world, from there he hopes in the world.”
q: This is the son of Adam and this is his lifespan … And from there he hopes in the world, from there he hopes in the world.

title: Hadith on Mawt: Death will come quicker than expected
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by me while I was plastering a wall belonging to me and my mother. The Prophet said, “What is this, O Abdullah?” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, it is something I am repairing.” The Prophet said, “The matter of death will come quicker than the ruin of this wall.”
q: What is this, O Abdullah? … The matter of death will come quicker than the ruin of this wall.

title: Hadith on Bukhl: Corruption of Ummah by miserliness, worldly hopes
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The beginning of righteousness in this nation is by conviction and temperance, and the beginning of its corruption by is miserliness and vain hopes.”
q: The beginning of righteousness in this nation is by conviction and temperance, and the beginning of its corruption by is miserliness and vain hopes.

title: Hadith on Death: Remembering death balances fear and hope in Allah
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Remember often the destroyer of pleasures: death. Verily, no one living a hard life remembers it but that it expands his contentment, nor one living in prosperity but that it constricts his vain hopes.”
q: Remember often the destroyer of pleasures: death. Verily, no one living a hard life remembers it but that it expands his contentment, nor one living in prosperity but that it constricts his vain hopes.

title: Hadith on Badr: The Prophet prays and weeps under a tree
t: Ali reported: None among us was upon a horse on the day of Badr other than Al-Miqdad. We saw, although everyone else was sleeping, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, under a tree praying and weeping until dawn.

title: Hadith on Footsteps: Allah loves two drops, two footsteps
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Nothing is more beloved to Allah than two drops and two footsteps: a teardrop from fear of Allah and a drop of blood shed in the way of Allah. As for two footsteps, a footstep in the way of Allah and a footstep in one of the obligations of Allah.”
q: Nothing is more beloved to Allah than two drops and two footsteps: a teardrop from fear of Allah and a drop of blood shed in the way of Allah. As for two footsteps, a footstep in the way of Allah and a footstep in one of the obligations of Allah.

title: Hadith on Eyes: Guarding, weeping, and lowering gaze
t: Mu’awiyah ibn Jaydah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Three eyes will never see the Hellfire, an eye standing guard in the way of Allah, an eye weeping from the fear of Allah, and an eye lowering its gaze from what Allah has forbidden.”
q: Three eyes will never see the Hellfire, an eye standing guard in the way of Allah, an eye weeping from the fear of Allah, and an eye lowering its gaze from what Allah has forbidden.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Eyes: Vigilance and fear of Allah never enter Hell
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two eyes will never be touched by the Hellfire: an eye staying vigilant for the Muslims in the way of Allah, and an eye weeping from the fear of Allah.”
q: Two eyes will never be touched by the Hellfire: an eye staying vigilant for the Muslims in the way of Allah, and an eye weeping from the fear of Allah.

title: Hadith on Jihad: Dust in jihad and smoke of Hell never combine
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man who weeps from the fear of Allah will never enter Hellfire, unless milk could return to its udder. The dust in the way of Allah will never combine with the smoke of Hell.”
q: A man who weeps from the fear of Allah will never enter Hellfire, unless milk could return to its udder. The dust in the way of Allah will never combine with the smoke of Hell.

title: Hadith on Eyes: Hell never harms eyes fearing Allah, standing guard
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two eyes are forbidden from being consumed by the Hellfire: an eye weeping from the fear of Allah, and an eye standing guard for Islam and its people against unbelief.”
q: Two eyes are forbidden from being consumed by the Hellfire: an eye weeping from the fear of Allah, and an eye standing guard for Islam and its people against unbelief.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Weeping: Two eyes never touched by Hellfire
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two eyes will never touch the Hellfire: an eye weeping from the fear of Allah, and an eye standing guard in the way of Allah.”
q: Two eyes will never touch the Hellfire: an eye weeping from the fear of Allah, and an eye standing guard in the way of Allah.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Eyes: Three eyes will never enter the Hellfire
t: Abu Rayhanah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hellfire is forbidden for the eye weeping from the fear of Allah. The Hellfire is forbidden for the eye vigilant in the way of Allah. The Hellfire is forbidden for the eye that lowers its gaze from what Allah has forbidden.”
q: The Hellfire is forbidden for the eye weeping from the fear of Allah. The Hellfire is forbidden for the eye vigilant in the way of Allah. The Hellfire is forbidden for the eye that lowers its gaze from what Allah has forbidden.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Ummah: A group of Muslims always victorious
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A group of my nation will continue to be victorious upon the religion, overpowering their enemies. None who oppose them will harm them, except what afflicts them of difficult circumstances, until Allah brings his command while they are like so.”
q: A group of my nation will continue to be victorious upon the religion, overpowering their enemies. None who oppose them will harm them, except what afflicts them of difficult circumstances, until Allah brings his command while they are like so.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Embracing Islam plus good deeds
t: Abu Tawil reported: He came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “What do you think of a man who commits every sin, leaving nothing of them. Is there repentance for him?” The Prophet said, “Have you embraced Islam?” He said, “As for me, I testify there is no God but Allah, along without any partners, and that you are the Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “Yes, perform good deeds and leave evil deeds, then Allah will turn all of them into good deeds for you.” He said, “And my treachery and wickedness?” The Prophet said, “Yes.” He said, “Allah is the greatest!” He continued exalting Allah until he disappeared from view.
q: Have you embraced Islam? … Yes, perform good deeds and leave evil deeds, then Allah will turn all of them into good deeds for you … Yes

title: Hadith on Expiation: Parable of one who does good after evil
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the parable of one who commits a sin and then performs a good deed is that of a man wearing a tightened iron chain choking his neck. Then, he performs a good deed and one of its rings loosens, then he performs another good deed and one of its rings loosens again, until he is set free to walk the earth.”
q: Verily, the parable of one who commits a sin and then performs a good deed is that of a man wearing a tightened iron chain choking his neck. Then, he performs a good deed and one of its rings loosens, then he performs another good deed and one of its rings loosens again, until he is set free to walk the earth.

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Good deeds expiate past sins in life
