t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever does good in what remains of his life, he will be forgiven for what has passed. Whoever does evil in what remains of his life, he will be taken to account for what has passed and what remains.”
q: Whoever does good in what remains of his life, he will be forgiven for what has passed. Whoever does evil in what remains of his life, he will be taken to account for what has passed and what remains.

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Son of Adam, rise and walk to Me
t: Shurayh reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: O Son of Adam, stand for Me and I will walk to you, walk to Me and I will run to you.”
q: Allah Almighty said: O Son of Adam, stand for Me and I will walk to you, walk to Me and I will run to you.

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Great repentance of the adulteress
t: ‘Imran ibn Husayn reported: A woman of Juhaynah came to the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while she was pregnant from adultery. She said, “O Prophet of Allah, I have committed a legal offense, so impose it upon me.” The Prophet called for her guardian and he said, “Be kind to her and when she gives birth, bring her to me.” He did so and the Prophet ordered for her shroud to be wrapped over her, then her ordered her to be stoned and he prayed over her. Umar said, “Do you pray over one who committed adultery?” The Prophet said, “She had repented with such repentance that, if it had been divided between seventy people of Medina, it would have reached beyond them. Have you found any repentance better than this, that she gave up her life for Allah Almighty?”
q: Be kind to her and when she gives birth, bring her to me. … She had repented with such repentance that, if it had been divided between seventy people of Medina, it would have reached beyond them. Have you found any repentance better than this, that she gave up her life for Allah Almighty?

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Remember Allah by every rock and tree
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, instruct me.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Worship Allah as if you can see Him and prepare yourself for death. Remember Allah by every rock and tree. If you commit a bad deed, accompany it with a good deed, secretly for a secret deed and publicly for a public deed.”
q: Worship Allah as if you can see Him and prepare yourself for death. Remember Allah by every rock and tree. If you commit a bad deed, accompany it with a good deed, secretly for a secret deed and publicly for a public deed.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Repentance open until sun rises in West
t: Safwan ibn ‘Assal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, towards the Western sun is an open gate the length of which is seventy years of travel. It will remain open for repentance until the sun rises from there. When the sun rises from the West, the faith of any soul will not benefit it if it had not had faith earlier or earned goodness from its faith.”
q: Verily, towards the Western sun is an open gate the length of which is seventy years of travel. It will remain open for repentance until the sun rises from there. When the sun rises from the West, the faith of any soul will not benefit it if it had not had faith earlier or earned goodness from its faith.

title: Hadith on Fajr: The Prophet committed to Sunan of dawn prayer
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was not as strongly committed to any voluntary prayers as he was to the two cycles before dawn.

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Voluntary prayers greater at home
t: Damrah ibn Habib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The voluntary prayer of a man in his house is greater than his voluntary prayer in front of people, just as the congregational prayer is better than the prayer of a man alone.”
q: The voluntary prayer of a man in his house is greater than his voluntary prayer in front of people, just as the congregational prayer is better than the prayer of a man alone.

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Voluntary prayers better at home
t: Suhayb ibn al-Nu’man reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The voluntary prayer of a man in his house is better than his prayer where people can see him, just as the prescribed prayers are better than the voluntary prayers.”
q: The voluntary prayer of a man in his house is better than his prayer where people can see him, just as the prescribed prayers are better than the voluntary prayers.

title: Hadith on Da’wah: Pillars of Islam, all else voluntary
t: Talhah ibn ‘Ubayd reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, from the people of Najd. His hair was unkempt and his loud voice was heard, which could not be understood until he came closer. He was asking about Islam. The Prophet said, “There are five prayers in a day and night.” The man said, “Is there anything else I must do?” The Prophet said, “No, unless you do so voluntarily.” The Prophet said, “And fasting the month of Ramadan.” The man said, “Is there anything else I must do?” The Prophet said, “No, unless you do so voluntarily.” The Prophet mentioned Zakat and the man said, “Is there anything else I must do?” The Prophet said, “No, unless you do so voluntarily.” The man turned back and he was saying, “By Allah, I will never add to this or lessen it.” The Prophet said, “He has succeeded if he is truthful.”
q: There are five prayers in a day and night. … No, unless you do so voluntarily. … And fasting the month of Ramadan. … No, unless you do so voluntarily. … No, unless you do so voluntarily. … He has succeeded if he is truthful.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Kusuf: The Prophet prays during an eclipse
t: Aisha reported: The sun eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, so he sent a caller to announce a congregational prayer. They gathered and arrived, then they exalted Allah and performed two cycles with four bowings and four prostrations.

title: Hadith on Istisqa: Raising hands to supplicate for rain
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would not raise his hands for any supplication except to pray for rain. He would raise them until we saw the skin of his armpits.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Istisqa: The Prophet prays and supplicates for rain
t: Abdullah ibn Zayd reported: I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, one day go out to prayer for rain. He turned his back to the people and faced the Qiblah and supplicated, then he turns his cloak inside out, then he prayed two cycles for us while reciting aloud.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Witr: Separating raka’at of Witr from previous prayers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not perform Witr prayer with three cycles, rather perform it with five or seven. Do not make it resemble sunset prayer.”
q: Do not perform Witr prayer with three cycles, rather perform it with five or seven. Do not make it resemble sunset prayer.

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: Reciting in moderate voice in night prayer
t: Abu Qatadah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came out at night and he saw Abu Bakr who was praying with a low voice, and he passed by Umar ibn al-Khattab who was praying with a raised voice. When they met together, the Prophet said, “O Abu Bakr, I passed by you and you were praying with a low voice.” Abu Bakr said, “I made Him hear with whom I was having an intimate conversation, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said to Umar, “I passed by you and you were praying with a raised voice.” Umar said, “O Messenger of Allah, I was awakening the drowsy and driving away Satan.” The Prophet said, “O Abu Bakr, raise your voice a little.” And the Prophet said to Umar, “Lower your voice a little.”
q: O Abu Bakr, I passed by you and you were praying with a low voice. … I passed by you and you were praying with a raised voice. … O Abu Bakr, raise your voice a little. … Lower your voice a little.

title: Ali on Eid: Every day obeying Allah is a celebration
t: Al-Ghazali reported: Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, when he saw the decorations of the Nabataeans in Iraq on the day of Eid, he said, “What is this they are showing?” They said, “O commander of the faithful, this is their day of celebration.” Ali said, “Every day in which Allah Almighty is not disobeyed is our celebration.”

title: Hasan on Eid: Every day without sin is a celebration
t: Abdullah ibn Shawdhab reported: We were with Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, and he heard a man speaking during Eid. Al-Hasan said, “Every day in which Allah Almighty is not disobeyed is a celebration.”

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Recommended voluntary prayer before Maghrib
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: We used to prayer two cycles after the sun set before sunset prayer in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. It was said to him, “Did the Messenger of Allah pray both of them?” Anas said, “The Prophet saw us praying then but he did not command us, nor prohibit us from doing so.”

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Perform Sunan prayers in your home
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Perform your voluntary prayers in your houses, and do not take your houses as graves.”
q: Perform your voluntary prayers in your houses, and do not take your houses as graves.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jerusalem: Virtue of prayers in Masjid al-Aqsa
t: Abu Darda reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The virtue of prayer in Masjid al-Haram is one hundred thousand times better than prayer elsewhere, prayer in this mosque of mine is one thousand times better than prayer elsewhere, and prayer in Bayt al-Maqdis is better than five hundred prayers elsewhere.”
q: The virtue of prayer in Masjid al-Haram is one hundred thousand times better than prayer elsewhere, prayer in this mosque of mine is one thousand times better than prayer elsewhere, and prayer in Bayt al-Maqdis is better than five hundred prayers elsewhere.

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Seek Laylat al-Qadr on last night of Ramadan
t: Mu’awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Seek the Night of Decree on the last night of Ramadan.”
q: Seek the Night of Decree on the last night of Ramadan.

title: Ali on Dua: Three supplications are never rejected
t: Ibn al-Hanba’ reported: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Three supplications are never turned away: a just leader for his subjects, a parent over his child, and the supplication of the oppressed.”

title: Hadith on Dua: No screen to block supplication of oppressed
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no veil between it and Allah.”
q: Beware the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no veil between it and Allah.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Sahaba on Eid: May Allah accept from us and you
t: Jubayr ibn Nufayr reported: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when they met each other on the day of Eid, they would say to each other, “May Allah accept good deeds from us and from you.”

title: Hasan on Eid: May Allah accept from us and from you
t: Hawshab ibn ‘Aqil reported: I met Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, on the day of Eid and I said, “May Allah accept good deeds from us and from you.” Al-Hasan said, “Yes, may Allah accept good deeds from us and from you.”

title: Umar II on Eid: May Allah accept from us and from you
t: Adham reported: We would say to Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, on the two Eids, “May Allah accept good deeds from us and from you, O commander of the faithful.” He would return it to us and he did not reject that from us.

title: Hadith on Iqtisas: No heavenly entry until wrongs are righted
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah will gather the servants naked, uncircumcised, and destitute.” We said, “What is destitute?” The Prophet said, “They will have nothing with them. They will be addressed with a voice heard from afar: I am the King! It is not befitting for any of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise while any of the people of Hellfire seek redress for injustice. It is not befitting for any of the people of Hellfire to enter Hellfire while any of the people of Paradise seek redress from injustice.” I said, “How is it so? We only come to Allah naked and destitute.” The Prophet said, “It is by their good and evil deeds.”
q: Allah will gather the servants naked, uncircumcised, and destitute. … They will have nothing with them. They will be addressed with a voice heard from afar: I am the King! It is not befitting for any of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise while any of the people of Hellfire seek redress for injustice. It is not befitting for any of the people of Hellfire to enter Hellfire while any of the people of Paradise seek redress from injustice. … It is by their good and evil deeds.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Salat: Catching up with the Imam in prayer
t: Abu al-Ahwas reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever does not catch the Imam while bowing, he has not caught that raka’ah.”

title: Hadith on Decree: Angels obey Allah’s word in heavens
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Allah decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submissive obedience to His word, as if it were a chain dragging over rock, and ‘when fright is removed from their hearts, they say: What has your Lord said? They say: It is the truth, for He is the Exalted, the Greatest.” (34:23)
q: When Allah decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submissive obedience to His word, as if it were a chain dragging over rock, and ‘when fright is removed from their hearts, they say: What has your Lord said? They say: It is the truth, for He is the Exalted, the Greatest.

title: Hadith on Ignorance: Sins excused if one genuinely does not know
t: Abdullah ibn Abbas reported: A man presented a water-skin filled with wine to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet said, “Do you know that Allah has forbidden it?”
q: Do you know that Allah has forbidden it?

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplications of parent, fasting person, traveler
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The supplications of three are not turned back: the supplication of a parent, the supplication of a fasting person, and the supplication of a traveler.”
q: The supplications of three are not turned back: the supplication of a parent, the supplication of a fasting person, and the supplication of a traveler.

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: Last third of night best for prayer
t: Uthman ibn al-‘As reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A heavenly caller announces every night: Who is supplicating that he may be answered? Who is asking that he may be given? Who is seeking forgiveness that he may be forgiven? It is so until the appearance of dawn.”
q: A heavenly caller announces every night: Who is supplicating that he may be answered? Who is asking that he may be given? Who is seeking forgiveness that he may be forgiven? It is so until the appearance of dawn.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Akhirah: Make the Hereafter your only concern
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever makes his concerns only one concern, the Hereafter, Allah will be enough for his concerns in the world. Whoever scatters his concerns, it does not matter to Allah in which valley of the world he meets his demise.”
q: Whoever makes his concerns only one concern, the Hereafter, Allah will be enough for his concerns in the world. Whoever scatters his concerns, it does not matter to Allah in which valley of the world he meets his demise.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on ‘Ibadah: Use free time to worship Allah, enrich the heart
t: Ma’qil ibn Yasar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Your Lord Almighty said: Son of Adam, be free for My worship. I will fill your heart with richness and fill your hands with provision. Son of Adam, do not distance yourself from Me, or else I will fill your heart with poverty and fill your hands with worthless distractions.”
q: Your Lord Almighty said: Son of Adam, be free for My worship. I will fill your heart with richness and fill your hands with provision. Son of Adam, do not distance yourself from Me, or else I will fill your heart with poverty and fill your hands with worthless distractions.

title: Hadith on Quran: Revelation of last verses of Ali ‘Imran
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon, said to me on one of my nights, “O Aisha, leave me to worship my Lord tonight.” I said, “By Allah, I love to be close to you and I love what pleases you.” The Prophet stood up and performed ablution, then stood in prayer. He did not stop weeping until it was moist around his eyes. Then, he wept and he did not stop weeping until his beard was moist. Then, he wept and he did not stop weeping until the ground was moist. Bilal came and announced the call to prayer. When he saw the Prophet weeping, he said, “O Messenger of Allah, why are you weeping when Allah has forgiven you for what you have done and what you will do?” The Prophet said, “Shall I not be a grateful servant? A verse has been revealed to me tonight and woe to one who reads it without reflecting upon it: Verily, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and day, are signs for those of understanding.” (3:190)
q: O Aisha, leave me to worship my Lord tonight. … Shall I not be a grateful servant? A verse has been revealed to me tonight and woe to one who reads it without reflecting upon it: Verily, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and day, are signs for those of understanding.

title: Hadith on Quran: Parable of Surat al-Baqarah and Ali ‘Imran
t: Buraydah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Learn Surat al-Baqarah, for adhering to it is blessed, leaving it is sorrow, and the sorcerers cannot defeat it. Learn al-Baqarah and Ali ‘Imran, for they are both the brightly illuminated chapters coming on the Day of Resurrection as if they were two clouds, or two canopies of shade, or as If they are a decisive wall of birds in ranks, arguing on behalf of their reciters.”
q: Learn Surat al-Baqarah, for adhering to it is blessed, leaving it is sorrow, and the sorcerers cannot defeat it. Learn al-Baqarah and Ali ‘Imran, for they are both the brightly illuminated chapters coming on the Day of Resurrection as if they were two clouds, or two canopies of shade, or as If they are a decisive wall of birds in ranks, arguing on behalf of their reciters.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Shaytan: Satan does not enter with Surat al-Baqarah recited
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Recite Surat al-Baqarah in your houses, for Satan does not enter a house in which Surat al-Baqarah is recited.”
q: Recite Surat al-Baqarah in your houses, for Satan does not enter a house in which Surat al-Baqarah is recited.

title: Hadith on Quran: Surat al-Baqarah keeps Satan out of home
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, everything has a summit and the summit of the Quran is Surat al-Baqarah. Whoever recites it in his house at night, Satan will not enter his house for three nights. Whoever recites it during the day, Satan will not enter his house for three days.”
q: Verily, everything has a summit and the summit of the Quran is Surat al-Baqarah. Whoever recites it in his house at night, Satan will not enter his house for three nights. Whoever recites it during the day, Satan will not enter his house for three days.

title: Hadith on Quran: Al-Baqarah is peak of the Book of Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Everything has a summit, and the summit of the Quran is Surat al-Baqarah. It contains a verse which is the chief of the Quran, the verse of the Throne.”
q: Everything has a summit, and the summit of the Quran is Surat al-Baqarah. It contains a verse which is the chief of the Quran, the verse of the Throne.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Quran: Al-Fatihah and al-Baqarah descend from heaven
t: Ibn Abbas reported: While the Angel Gabriel was sitting with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, he heard a creaking noise above him. Gabriel raised his head and he said, “This is a door of heaven that has been opened today and it has never been opened before today.” Then an angel descended from it, and Gabriel said, “This angel descended to the earth today and he has never descended until today.” The angel greeted him with peace and he said, “Rejoice in two lights you have been given, which were not given to any prophet before you: the opening of the Book, Surat al-Fatihah, and the last verses of Surat al-Baqarah. You will never recite a letter from them but that you will be given.”

title: Hadith on al-Fatihah: The greatest chapter of the Quran
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was on a journey and he descended from his riding animal as a man among his companions was walking by his side. The Prophet turned to him and he said, “Shall I not tell you of the greatest of the Quran?” The Prophet recited to him, “All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds,” (1:1) meaning Surat al-Fatihah.
q: Shall I not tell you of the greatest of the Quran? … All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds,

title: Hadith on Quran: Surat al-Fatihah unlike any revealed scripture
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him, “How do you recite in prayer?” Ubayy said, “I recite the foundation of the Book, Surat al-Fatihah.” The Prophet said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, nothing like it has been revealed in the Torah, nor the Gospel, nor the Psalms, nor the Furqan. Verily, they are the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Quran given to me.”
q: How do you recite in prayer? … By the One in whose hand is my soul, nothing like it has been revealed in the Torah, nor the Gospel, nor the Psalms, nor the Furqan. Verily, they are the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Quran given to me.

title: Hadith on Quran: Best recitations inspire fear and awe of Allah
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among the people who recite the Quran with the best voice are those who, when you hear them, you consider them in awe of Allah.”
q: Verily, among the people who recite the Quran with the best voice are those who, when you hear them, you consider them in awe of Allah.

title: Hadith on Sajdah: Supplication to be like David upon prostrating
t: Ibn Abbas reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, I saw while I was sleeping night as if I were praying behind a tree. I prostrated and the tree prostrated along with me. I heard it saying: O Allah, write a reward for me with You, remove my burdens, store it for me with You, and accept it from me as You accepted it from your servant David.” Then, the Prophet recited a verse of prostration and prostrated.

title: Hadith on Quran: Ten verses at night, not among heedless
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever recites ten verses in the night will never be recorded among the negligent.”
q: Whoever recites ten verses in the night will never be recorded among the negligent.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Recitation: Angels descend to listen to the Quran
t: Usayd ibn Hudayr reported: He said, “O Messenger of Allah, while I was reciting Surat al-Baqarah in the night, I heard a loud noise behind me and I thought my horse had escaped.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Recite, O Abu ‘Atik.” Then, I turned to behold the likeness of a lamp hanging between the heavens and the earth, as the Prophet was saying, “Recite, O Abu ‘Atik.” He said, “O Messenger of Allah, how can I keep going?” The Prophet said, “These angels descended for your recitation of Surat al-Baqarah. If you had continued, you would have seen wonders.”
q: Recite, O Abu ‘Atik. … Recite, O Abu ‘Atik. … These angels descended for your recitation of Surat al-Baqarah. If you had continued, you would have seen wonders.

title: Hadith on Quran: Learning verses of Quran better than all worldly goods
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us while we were in the shelter. The Prophet said, “Which of you would love to go out in the morning each day to Buthan or ‘Aqiq and bring with him two mature she-camels, without sinning or severing family ties?” We said, “O Messenger of Allah, we would love that.” The Prophet said, “Does not one of you go out in the morning to the mosque to learn or recite two verses from the Book of Allah Almighty? It is better for him than two camels, three is better than three, four is better than four and whatever number of camels.”
q: Which of you would love to go out in the morning each day to Buthan or ‘Aqiq and bring with him two mature she-camels, without sinning or severing family ties? … Does not one of you go out in the morning to the mosque to learn or recite two verses from the Book of Allah Almighty? It is better for him than two camels, three is better than three, four is better than four and whatever number of camels.

title: Hadith on Charity: Best deeds to bring happiness, fulfill needs
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked, “Which deeds are best?” The Prophet said, “To bring happiness to a believer, to satisfy his hunger, to clothe his nakedness, or to fulfill his needs.”
q: To bring happiness to a believer, to satisfy his hunger, to clothe his nakedness, or to fulfill his needs.

title: Hadith on Charity: Blessings will vanish if not used for good
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None among the servants are bestowed a blessing from Allah and He makes it abundant upon him but that He will appoint to him something of the needs of people. If he is irritated with them, he risks the disappearance of that blessing.”
q: None among the servants are bestowed a blessing from Allah and He makes it abundant upon him but that He will appoint to him something of the needs of people. If he is irritated with them, he risks the disappearance of that blessing.

title: Hadith on Greed: Faith and miserliness never combined in heart
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The dust in the way of Allah and the smoke of Hell can never be combined on the face of a man. Greed and faith can never be combined in the heart.”
q: The dust in the way of Allah and the smoke of Hell can never be combined on the face of a man. Greed and faith can never be combined in the heart.

title: Ali on Ramadan: Sermon given at the arrival of Ramadan
t: Al-Sha’bi reported: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, would deliver a sermon when the month of Ramadan arrived, saying, “This is the blessed month in which Allah has obligated fasting and not obligated night prayers. Certainly, fasting is not merely from food and drink, but rather from lying, falsehood, and vain talk.” Al-Sha’bi said, “Ali would say this after the dawn prayer and afternoon prayer.”

title: Hadith on Qadr: Allah can never be unjust to His servants
t: Zayd ibn Thabit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If Allah were to punish the inhabitants of His heavens and His earth, He would punish them without being unjust to them. If He were to have mercy on them, His mercy is better for them than their deeds. If you were to spend the likes of mount Uhud in gold in the way of Allah, He would not accept it from you until you had faith in all of divine providence, such that you know what you acquire could never miss you, and what you missed you could never acquire, and that if you die upon something other than this, you will enter the Hellfire.”
q: If Allah were to punish the inhabitants of His heavens and His earth, He would punish them without being unjust to them. If He were to have mercy on them, His mercy is better for them than their deeds. If you were to spend the likes of mount Uhud in gold in the way of Allah, He would not accept it from you until you had faith in all of divine providence, such that you know what you acquire could never miss you, and what you missed you could never acquire, and that if you die upon something other than this, you will enter the Hellfire.

title: Adam on Rizq: Why people are not given equal provision?
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: In regards to the saying of Allah Almighty, “As your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their progeny and He made them testify against themselves: Am I not your Lord?” (7:172). Adam, upon him be peace, looked at his progeny and he saw the rich and the poor, those with a beautiful appearance and otherwise. Adam said, “O Lord, why did You not provide the same to all Your servants?” Allah said, “Verily, I love to be thanked.”
q: As your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their progeny and He made them testify against themselves: Am I not your Lord?

title: Hadith on Dua: All righteous supplication answered, sooner or later
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No Muslim sets his face towards Allah Almighty in some matter but that he will be given a response, whether it comes quickly or is stored for later.”
q: No Muslim sets his face towards Allah Almighty in some matter but that he will be given a response, whether it comes quickly or is stored for later.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Dua: Allah shy to not answer supplication
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is merciful, conscientious, and generous. He would be shy for His servant to raise his hands to Him and then not place any goodness in either of them.”
q: Verily, Allah is merciful, conscientious, and generous. He would be shy for His servant to raise his hands to Him and then not place any goodness in either of them.

title: Hadith on Dua: Allah with those who supplicate to Him
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah says: I am as My servant expects of Me, and I am with him when he calls upon Me.”
q: Allah says: I am as My servant expects of Me, and I am with him when he calls upon Me.

title: Bara’ on Hope: To destruction if he despairs of Allah’s mercy
t: Al-Bara’ reported: A man said to him, “O Abu ‘Umarah, the verse: Do not throw yourself to destructions by your own hands (2:195). Is it a man who meets the enemy in battle and he fights until he is killed?” Al-Bara’ said, “No, rather it is that a man commits a sin and he says: Allah will not forgive me.”
q: Do not throw yourself to destructions by your own hands
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Istighfar: Increase seeking forgiveness on one’s record
t: Al-Zubayr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever would love to be pleased with his record, let him increase seeking forgiveness on it.”
q: Whoever would love to be pleased with his record, let him increase seeking forgiveness on it.

title: Hadith on Ruqyah: Blowing over illness with Surat al-Falaq, al-Nas
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when anyone from his family was sick, he would blow over them with the two chapters of refuge. When he was sick with the illness in which he died, I blew over him and wiped himself with his hands, as they had greater blessings than my hand.

title: Hadith on ‘Ayn: Perform ruqyah to cure the evil eye
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saw a servant girl in her house whose face has become discolored. The Prophet said, “Treat her with protective recitations, as she has been afflicted by an evil stare.”
q: Treat her with protective recitations, as she has been afflicted by an evil stare.

title: Hadith on Ruqyah: Treat your sick ones with the Quran
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered upon her as a woman was treating her illness or performing recitations over her. The Prophet said, “Treat her with the book of Allah.”
q: Treat her with the book of Allah.

title: Hadith on Ruqyah: Gabriel invokes Allah to heal the Prophet
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The angel Gabriel came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Muhammad, do you have a complaint of illness?” The Prophet said, “Yes.” Gabriel said, “In the name of Allah, I perform protective recitations over you from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul or envious eye. May Allah heal you. In the name of Allah, I perform recitations over you.”
q: Yes

title: Hadith on Wisdom: Parable of one who only shares bad news
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of one who hears wisdom in a gathering, but then only reports evil from its speaker, is the likeness of one who visits a shepherd. He says: O shepherd, shear off the wool of a sheep for me from your flock. The shepherd says: Go and take the best of them by the ear. So he goes and take the shepherd’s dog by the ear.”
q: The parable of one who hears wisdom in a gathering, but then only reports evil from its speaker, is the likeness of one who visits a shepherd. He says: O shepherd, shear off the wool of a sheep for me from your flock. The shepherd says: Go and take the best of them by the ear. So he goes and take the shepherd’s dog by the ear.

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Say my Lord is Allah, until you are killed
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will be a civil war in which the one asleep is better than one lying down, the one lying down is better than the one sitting, the one sitting is better than the one standing, the one standing is better than the one walking, the one walking is better than the one riding, and the one riding is better than the one running. All of those killed on both sides are in the Hellfire.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, when will that happen?” The Prophet said, “Those are the days of slaughter.” I said, “When are the days of slaughter?” The Prophet said, “When a man is not safe in his own gathering.” I said, “What do you order me to do if I witness that?” The Prophet said, “Restrain yourself and your hands, and stay in your building.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you say if a man breaks into my building?” The Prophet said, “Go into your home.” I said, “What do you say if he invades my home?” The Prophet said, “Go into your prayer room and do like this,” and he grasped his elbow with his right hand, “And say ‘my Lord is Allah’ until you die upon that.”
q: There will be a civil war in which the one asleep is better than one lying down, the one lying down is better than the one sitting, the one sitting is better than the one standing, the one standing is better than the one walking, the one walking is better than the one riding, and the one riding is better than the one running. All of those killed on both sides are in the Hellfire. … Those are the days of slaughter. … When a man is not safe in his own gathering. … Restrain yourself and your hands, and stay in your building. … Go into your home. … Go into your prayer room and do like this, … And say ‘my Lord is Allah’ until you die upon that.

title: Hadith on Asiyah: Courageous martyrdom of Pharaoh’s wife
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Pharaoh pinned down his wife with four spikes in her hands and feet. When they left her, the angels provided her with shade. She said, “O Lord, build me a house in Paradise with You, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the oppressive people,” (66:11). Thus, her house in Paradise was revealed to her.
q: O Lord, build me a house in Paradise with You, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the oppressive people,

title: Ibn Umar on Husayn: Ibn Umar weeps for the Prophet’s grandson
t: Ibn Umar reported: He heard that Al-Husayn ibn ‘Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, had set out to Iraq, so he met up with him three days out. Ibn Umar said, “What do you intend?” Al-Husayn said, “Iraq.” Ibn Umar said, “While you have papers and letters with you?” Al-Husayn said, “These letters are their pledges of allegiance.” Ibn Umar said, “Do not go to them.” Al-Husayn refused, so Ibn Umar said, “I will share a narration with you. Gabriel came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he offered him the choice between the world and the Hereafter. The Prophet choose the Hereafter and he did not want the world. Indeed, you are part of the Messenger of Allah. No one like you will come again amongst you all. Allah will not turn it away from you but that it will be better for all of you.” Al-Husayn refused to turn back, so Ibn Umar embraced him and wept, saying, “I ask Allah to protect you from being killed.”

title: Hadith on Wudu: Washing limbs three times in ablution
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, how does one perform purification?” The Prophet called for a vessel of water, then he washed his hands three times, then he washed his face three times, then he washed his arms to the elbow three times, then he wiped his head, then he put his fingers around his earlobes, wiping the back with his thumbs and the interior with his index fingers, then he washed his feet three times, each three by three. Then, the Prophet said, “Such is the ablution. Whoever adds to this has sinned and done wrong.”
q: Such is the ablution. Whoever adds to this has sinned and done wrong.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Cleanliness: The Prophet always uses water after call of nature
t: Aisha reported: I never saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, come out from the toilet but that he cleansed with water.

title: Hadith on ‘Ayn: Many Muslims die by the evil eye
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A great many from my nation who die, after the judgment, decree, and providence of Allah, die by the evil eye.”
q: A great many from my nation who die, after the judgment, decree, and providence of Allah, die by the evil eye.

title: Abdullah on Medicine: Use the Quran and honey for healing
t: Abu al-Ahwas reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “You must make use of two healers: the Quran and honey.”

title: Hadith on Passions: The Prophet seeks intimacy in a lawful way
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saw a woman and then he went to his wife Zaynab as she was tanning leather, and he satisfied his needs with her. Then, the Prophet came out to his companions and he said, “Verily, a woman might advance in the form of a devil and withdraw in the form of a devil. If one of you sees a woman, let him return to his home, for that will turn back the lust within himself.”
q: Verily, a woman might advance in the form of a devil and withdraw in the form of a devil. If one of you sees a woman, let him return to his home, for that will turn back the lust within himself.

title: Hadith on Quran: The Prophet weeps as Quran is recited
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “Recite to me.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, I recite to you while it was revealed to you?” The Prophet said, “Yes.” I recited Surat al-Nisa until I reached this verse, “How will it be when We bring a witness from every nation and We bring you as a witness over these?” (4.:41). The Prophet said, “Enough for now!” I turned to him and saw his eyes welling with tears.
q: Recite to me. … Yes … How will it be when We bring a witness from every nation and We bring you as a witness over these? … Enough for now!
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Uthman on Quran: If we were pure, never bored of Quran
t: Sufyan reported: Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “If our hearts were pure, we would never be tired of the speech of Allah.”

title: Umar on Wudu: The Caliph’s ablution from Christian water
t: Zayd ibn Aslam reported: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, performed ablution using the water of a Christian woman, in the jar of a Christian woman.

title: Uthman on Martyrdom: Killed while fasting, breaks fast in Paradise
t: Nafi’ reported: Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in his dream on the night he was killed the following morning. The Prophet said, “O Uthman, break your fast with us tonight.” Then, he was killed while he was fasting.

title: Ibn Abbas on Ramadan: Old people may break fast, feed poor instead
t: ‘Ikramah reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Elders have been given a concession to break their fast in Ramadan and to feed a poor person for each day, without a need to make it up later.”

title: Hadith on ‘Ayn: Evil eye can drive a man insane, suicidal
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the evil eye might attach itself to a man by permission of Allah, until he climbs a tall mountain and then throws himself off it.”
q: Verily, the evil eye might attach itself to a man by permission of Allah, until he climbs a tall mountain and then throws himself off it
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Ali on Sujud: Beloved to Allah to ask forgiveness in prostration
t: Zirr reported: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The most beloved word to Allah Almighty is that one says while prostrating: O Lord, I have done wrong. My Lord, forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.”

title: Hadith on Resurrection: Standing on the Day for 50,000 years
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people will stand before the Lord of the worlds for the length of half of a day, which is like fifty thousand years. That day will be made easy for the believer like the sun lowering itself until it has set.”
q: The people will stand before the Lord of the worlds for the length of half of a day, which is like fifty thousand years. That day will be made easy for the believer like the sun lowering itself until it has set.

title: Hadith on Hell: Unbelievers stand for years before thrown into Fire
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The unbeliever will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection for a length of fifty thousand years. Verily, the unbeliever will see Hell and think he will be falling into it for a distance of forty years of travel.”
q: The unbeliever will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection for a length of fifty thousand years. Verily, the unbeliever will see Hell and think he will be falling into it for a distance of forty years of travel.

title: Hadith on Deen: O Allah, make me firmly grounded upon Islam
t: Shaddad ibn Aws reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say in his prayer, “O Allah, I ask You to make me firmly grounded in the matter and determined upon right guidance. I ask You to make me grateful for Your blessings and to help me worship You in the best manner. I ask You for a pure heart and a truthful tongue. I ask You for the good You know, I seek refuge in You from the evil You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know.”
q: O Allah, I ask You to make me firmly grounded in the matter and determined upon right guidance. I ask You to make me grateful for Your blessings and to help me worship You in the best manner. I ask You for a pure heart and a truthful tongue. I ask You for the good You know, I seek refuge in You from the evil You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Quran: Reciting a surah before sleeping, angel comes
t: Shaddad ibn Aws reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No Muslim retires to his bed, reciting a chapter from the Book of Allah, but that Allah entrusts him to the care of an angel. Nothing will approach to harm him until he awakens, whenever he awakens.”
q: No Muslim retires to his bed, reciting a chapter from the Book of Allah, but that Allah entrusts him to the care of an angel. Nothing will approach to harm him until he awakens, whenever he awakens.

title: Hadith on Sujud: Ask Allah’s forgiveness in prostration
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say in his prostration, “O Allah, forgive all of my sins, the small and large, the first and last, the public and private.”
q: O Allah, forgive all of my sins, the small and large, the first and last, the public and private.

title: Hadith on Death: Angels receive the souls of righteous or wicked
t:
Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when the believer is ready to depart the world and is facing the Hereafter, angels from heaven descend with bright faces, as if their faces were the sun, with them are the shrouds and perfumes of Paradise, until they sit from him a distance as far as the eye can see. Then, the angel of death, upon him be peace, comes until he sits by his head and he says: O pure soul, come out to the forgiveness of Allah and His pleasure! He takes it out like a drop from a water-skin and holds it, never to leave his hand for the blink of an eye until he places it in that shroud and perfume. The scent coming from it is more pleasant than any musk you would find on the face of the earth. He ascends and passes by no gathering of angels but that they say: What a pure spirit! They say he is this person, son of this person, calling him by the best names by which he was known in the world, until he stops at the lowest heaven and seeks entry and it will be opened for him. The company of each heaven bring him closer to the heaven following it until he stops at the seventh heaven. Allah Almighty will say: Write the record of My servant in the righteous register and return him to the earth, for from it I created them, to it I return them, and from it I will take them out once again. His spirit will be returned to his body and two angels will come to sit by him, saying to him: Who is your Lord? He will say: My Lord is Allah. They will say: What is your religion? He will say: My religion is Islam. They will say: Who is this man sent you? He will say: He is the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. They will say: How did you know? He will say: I read the Book of Allah, had faith in it, and believed in it. A heavenly announcement will be made: My servant has spoken the truth! Spread out carpets for him in Paradise, clothe him for Paradise, and open a gate for him to Paradise! Its comforts and fragrances will come to him and his grave will become spacious as far as his eye can see. A handsome man, with fine clothes and wonderful fragrance, will come and say: Glad tidings of what pleases you, for this was your Day you were promised! He will say: Who are you with such a handsome face? He will say: I am your righteous deeds! He will say: O Lord, begin the Hour that I may return to my family and property!”

The Prophet continued, “Verily, when the unbeliever is ready to depart the world and is facing the Hereafter, angels descend from heaven with darkened faces and with them sack-cloth. They will sit away from his as far as the eye can see. Then, the angel of death approaches until he sits by his head and he says: O filthy soul, come out to the displeasure of Allah and His wrath! He will be separated from his body like the tearing of skewers from wet wool and he holds it in his hand, never to leave it for the blink of an eye, until he places it in this sack-cloth. The scent coming from it is like the most foul corpse found upon the face of the earth. They will ascend with him and not pass by a gathering of angels but that they say: What a filthy spirit! They say he is this person, son of this person, calling him by the ugliest names by which he was known in the world, until he stops at the lowest heaven. They will request it to be opened for him but it will not open.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “The gates of heaven will never open for them, nor will they enter Paradise, until the camel goes through the eye of the needle,” (7:40). The Prophet said, “Allah Almighty will say: Write his record in the wicked register in the lowest earth. His spirit will be thrown down,” then the Prophet recited the verse, “It is as though he had fallen from the sky and was snatched by the birds or the wind carried him down into a remote place,” (22:31). The Prophet said, “His spirit will return to his body and two angels will come to sit by him, saying to him: Who is your Lord? He will say: Uh, uh, I do not know! They will say: What is your religion? He will say: Uh, uh, I do not know! They will say: Who is this man sent to you? He will say: Uh, uh, I do not know! A heavenly announcement will be made: He has lied! Spread carpets for him in Hellfire and open a gate for him to Hellfire! Its heat and its flames will approach him, and he will be squeezed in his grave until his ribs press together. An ugly man, with hideous clothing and a foul stench, will approach him and say: Glad tidings of what despairs you, for this is your Day you were promised! He will say: Who are with your evil face? He will say: I am your wicked deeds! He will say: O Lord, do not begin the Hour!”
q: Verily, when the believer is ready to depart the world and is facing the Hereafter, angels from heaven descend with bright faces, as if their faces were the sun, with them are the shrouds and perfumes of Paradise, until they sit from him a distance as far as the eye can see. Then, the angel of death, upon him be peace, comes until he sits by his head and he says: O pure soul, come out to the forgiveness of Allah and His pleasure! He takes it out like a drop from a water-skin and holds it, never to leave his hand for the blink of an eye until he places it in that shroud and perfume. The scent coming from it is more pleasant than any musk you would find on the face of the earth. He ascends and passes by no gathering of angels but that they say: What a pure spirit! They say he is this person, son of this person, calling him by the best names by which he was known in the world, until he stops at the lowest heaven and seeks entry and it will be opened for him. The company of each heaven bring him closer to the heaven following it until he stops at the seventh heaven. Allah Almighty will say: Write the record of My servant in the righteous register and return him to the earth, for from it I created them, to it I return them, and from it I will take them out once again. His spirit will be returned to his body and two angels will come to sit by him, saying to him: Who is your Lord? He will say: My Lord is Allah. They will say: What is your religion? He will say: My religion is Islam. They will say: Who is this man sent you? He will say: He is the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. They will say: How did you know? He will say: I read the Book of Allah, had faith in it, and believed in it. A heavenly announcement will be made: My servant has spoken the truth! Spread out carpets for him in Paradise, clothe him for Paradise, and open a gate for him to Paradise! Its comforts and fragrances will come to him and his grave will become spacious as far as his eye can see. A handsome man, with fine clothes and wonderful fragrance, will come and say: Glad tidings of what pleases you, for this was your Day you were promised! He will say: Who are you with such a handsome face? He will say: I am your righteous deeds! He will say: O Lord, begin the Hour that I may return to my family and property! … Verily, when the unbeliever is ready to depart the world and is facing the Hereafter, angels descend from heaven with darkened faces and with them sack-cloth. They will sit away from his as far as the eye can see. Then, the angel of death approaches until he sits by his head and he says: O filthy soul, come out to the displeasure of Allah and His wrath! He will be separated from his body like the tearing of skewers from wet wool and he holds it in his hand, never to leave it for the blink of an eye, until he places it in this sack-cloth. The scent coming from it is like the most foul corpse found upon the face of the earth. They will ascend with him and not pass by a gathering of angels but that they say: What a filthy spirit! They say he is this person, son of this person, calling him by the ugliest names by which he was known in the world, until he stops at the lowest heaven. They will request it to be opened for him but it will not open. … The gates of heaven will never open for them, nor will they enter Paradise, until the camel goes through the eye of the needle … Allah Almighty will say: Write his record in the wicked register in the lowest earth. His spirit will be thrown down, … It is as though he had fallen from the sky and was snatched by the birds or the wind carried him down into a remote place … His spirit will return to his body and two angels will come to sit by him, saying to him: Who is your Lord? He will say: Uh, uh, I do not know! They will say: What is your religion? He will say: Uh, uh, I do not know! They will say: Who is this man sent to you? He will say: Uh, uh, I do not know! A heavenly announcement will be made: He has lied! Spread carpets for him in Hellfire and open a gate for him to Hellfire! Its heat and its flames will approach him, and he will be squeezed in his grave until his ribs press together. An ugly man, with hideous clothing and a foul stench, will approach him and say: Glad tidings of what despairs you, for this is your Day you were promised! He will say: Who are with your evil face? He will say: I am your wicked deeds! He will say: O Lord, do not begin the Hour!

title: Wahb on Shahwah: Satan flees from one who overcomes his desires
t: Muhammad ibn Ziyad reported: Wahb ibn Munabbih, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whoever places his lusts beneath his feet, Satan will flee from his shadow. Whoever overcomes his whims by his forbearance, that one is among the victorious scholars.”

title: Hadith on Shaytan: Parable of the Prophet as warning of enemies
t: Buraydah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came out and called out to us three times, “O people! Do you know the parable between you and myself?” They said, “Allah and His messenger know best.” The Prophet said, “Verily, the parable between you and myself is that of a people who feared an enemy approaching them, so they dispatched a man to keep watch for them. While they were doing so, he saw the enemy and returned to warn them, afraid that the enemy would reach them before he could warn his people.” The Prophet threw up his garment and he said three times, “O people, you have been encroached!”
q: O people! Do you know the parable between you and myself? … Verily, the parable between you and myself is that of a people who feared an enemy approaching them, so they dispatched a man … to keep watch for them. While they were doing so, he saw the enemy and returned to warn them, afraid that the enemy would reach them before he could warn his people. … O people, you have been encroached!
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Hereafter: If you could only see the Day of Resurrection…
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I see what you do not see and I hear what you do not hear. The heavens groan, and rightly so. There is no place a span of four fingers but that an angel is placing his forehead in prostration to Allah. By Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep often. You would not feel any pleasure in the beds of women, and you would go out to the highest hills to loudly beg to Allah.”
q: Verily, I see what you do not see and I hear what you do not hear. The heavens groan, and rightly so. There is no place a span of four fingers but that an angel is placing his forehead in prostration to Allah. By Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep often. You would not feel any pleasure in the beds of women, and you would go out to the highest hills to loudly beg to Allah.

title: Hadith on Funerals: Glorify and exalt Allah upon burial of deceased
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: We went out with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on the day Sa’d ibn Mu’adh passed away. When the Prophet prayer over him, placed him the grave, and covered it over, he glorified Allah and so we glorified Allah for a long time. Then, the Prophet exalted Allah and so we exalted Him. It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, why did you glorify Allah and then exalt Him?” The Prophet said, “The grave had constricted over this righteous servant until Allah expanded it for him.”
q: The grave had constricted over this righteous servant until Allah expanded it for him.

title: Hadith on Dua: Regularly call out, Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be constant in saying: O Majestic and Noble!”
q: Be constant in saying: O Majestic and Noble!

title: Hadith on Recompense: Eat only healthy Halal food, shed no blood
t: Jundub reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the first organ the human being to rot is his stomach. Whoever can eat nothing but wholesome food, let him do so. Whoever can let nothing obstruct him from Paradise, even as much as a handful of bloodshed, let him do so.”
q: Verily, the first organ the human being to rot is his stomach. Whoever can eat nothing but wholesome food, let him do so. Whoever can let nothing obstruct him from Paradise, even as much as a handful of bloodshed, let him do so.

title: Hadith on Dua: Seek help by the Merciful, the Living
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, whenever he encountered a difficult matter, he would say, “O Living, O Sustaining! By Your mercy, I seek deliverance!”
q: O Living, O Sustaining! By Your mercy, I seek deliverance!

title: Hadith on Murder: Is there any repentance for the killer?
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The one murdered will come with the scalp and head of his killer in his hand on the Day of Resurrection, his jugular vein flowing with blood and saying: O Lord! This one has killed me! And he will draw near to the Throne.” They mentioned repentance to Ibn Abbas and he recited this verse, “Whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell,” (4:93). Ibn Abbas said, “This verse has not been abrogated or replaced, so where is his repentance?”
q: The one murdered will come with the scalp and head of his killer in his hand on the Day of Resurrection, his jugular vein flowing with blood and saying: O Lord! This one has killed me! And he will draw near to the Throne. … Whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell,

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Greatest name of Allah in these two verses
t: Asma’ bint Yazid reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The greatest name of Allah is in these two verses: Your God is one God, there is no God but Him, the Gracious, the Merciful (2:163). As well as the opening of Surat Ali ‘Imran: Allah, there is no God but Him, the Living, the Sustainer.” (3:2)
q: The greatest name of Allah is in these two verses: Your God is one God, there is no God but Him, the Gracious, the Merciful … As well as the opening of Surat Ali ‘Imran: Allah, there is no God but Him, the Living, the Sustainer

title: Hadith on Mikaeel: Michael has not laughed since Hell created
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to the Angel Gabriel, “Why do I never see the angel Michael laughing?” Gabriel said, “Michael has not laughed since Hellfire was created.”
q: Why do I never see the angel Michael laughing?
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Death: Prepare to die and experience the grave
t: Al-Bara’ reported: We were with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, at a funeral and he was sitting beside the edge of the grave, weeping until the ground became wet. The Prophet said, “O my brethren, prepare for the likes of this.”
q: O my brethren, prepare for the likes of this.

title: Hadith on Qiyamah: Sun draws nearer, hotter on Judgment Day
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The sun will be lowered on the Day of Resurrection to the distance of a mile and its heat will be increased by as much. It will boil skulls just like the boiling of pots. They will sweat by the measure of their sins. Among them are those to whom it will reach their ankles, among them are those to whom it will reach their shins, among them are those to whom it will reach their midsections, and among them are those who are subsumed in sweat.”
q: The sun will be lowered on the Day of Resurrection to the distance of a mile and its heat will be increased by as much. It will boil skulls just like the boiling of pots. They will sweat by the measure of their sins. Among them are those to whom it will reach their ankles, among them are those to whom it will reach their shins, among them are those to whom it will reach their midsections, and among them are those who are subsumed in sweat.

title: Hadith on Sirat: The Prophets pass over the bridge of Hell
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I will be the first to cross the bridge over Hell. The supplication of the Messengers on that day will be: O Allah, keep us safe! O Allah, keep us safe! There will be hooks on the sides like the thorns of al-Sa’dan, except their enormity is only known to Allah. People will be seized by them according to their deeds. Among them are those who are ruined by their deeds. Among them are those who are cut into pieces and later saved, until Allah has finished judging between His servants and He intends to take out of the Hellfire whomever He wills to take out. For whomever testified there is no God but Allah, the angels will be ordered to take them out and they will be known by their trace marks of prostration. Allah has forbidden the Hellfire from consuming any children of Adam with traces of prostration. They will be taken out after they had been burned, then dipped into a water called the water of life. They will spring forth like seeds on a streaming river.”
q: I will be the first to cross the bridge over Hell. The supplication of the Messengers on that day will be: O Allah, keep us safe! O Allah, keep us safe! There will be hooks on the sides like the thorns of al-Sa’dan, except their enormity is only known to Allah. People will be seized by them according to their deeds. Among them are those who are ruined by their deeds. Among them are those who are cut into pieces and later saved, until Allah has finished judging between His servants and He intends to take out of the Hellfire whomever He wills to take out. For whomever testified there is no God but Allah, the angels will be ordered to take them out and they will be known by their trace marks of prostration. Allah has forbidden the Hellfire from consuming any children of Adam with traces of prostration. They will be taken out after they had been burned, then dipped into a water called the water of life. They will spring forth like seeds on a streaming river.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hasan on Jihad: Fighting in jihad for Allah without weapons
t: Abu Bashir reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, the servant may wage jihad for the sake of Allah, jihad as is due to Him, without ever striking anything with a sword.”

title: Ali on Akhirah: Be children of the Hereafter, not of the world
t: Al-Bukhari reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Set out with the world at your back and the Hereafter at your front. Each of them both has their children. Be children of the Hereafter and not children of the world, for today is for action and not reckoning, while tomorrow is for reckoning and not action.”

title: Hadith on Sins: Entire nation punished if disobedient gain upper hand
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the disobedient gain ascendancy in my nation, Allah Almighty will send down His punishment upon all of them.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, will there be righteous among them on that day?” The Prophet said, “Of course.” I said, “How will they be treated?” The Prophet said, “They will be afflicted as the people are afflicted, then they will be taken away to forgiveness from Allah and His pleasure.”
q: When the disobedient gain ascendancy in my nation, Allah Almighty will send down His punishment upon all of them. … Of course … They will be afflicted as the people are afflicted, then they will be taken away to forgiveness from Allah and His pleasure.

title: Fudayl on Sultan: Ignorant rulers ascend when believers disobey Allah
t: Ibrahim ibn al-Ash’ath reported: Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Allah Almighty revealed to some of His Prophets: When those who know Me disobey Me, I will make them be ruled by those who do not know Me.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication not answered unless enjoining good
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Enjoin good and forbid evil before you call upon Allah and He does not answer you.”
q: Enjoin good and forbid evil before you call upon Allah and He does not answer you.

title: Malik on Honor: Man punished for not honoring Allah’s commands
t: Malik ibn Dinar reported: A rabbi among the tribes of Israel would be visited in his house by men and women, whom he would admonish and remind them of the days of Allah. One day, he saw some of his sons harassing women, so he said: Easy, my sons! Easy, my sons! He later fell from his bed and broke his spine, his wife miscarried, and his son was killed in the army. Allah Almighty revealed to His Prophet to tell this rabbi: I will never take you out of your hardship as a truthful one. Your anger for My sake was nothing more than to say, easy my sons!

title: Hudhayfah on Sins: Gradual disobedience led Israelites to unbelief
t: Tariq ibn Shihab reported: It was said to Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, “Was it in one day that the tribes of Israel abandoned their religion?” Hudhayfah said, “No, rather when they were given a command, they would leave it, and when they were given a prohibition, they would commit it, until they slid out of their religion just as a man slides out of his shirt.”

title: Umar on Ikhlaas: Make all my deeds sincere for Your sake
t: Al-Hasan reported: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say, “O Allah, make my deeds righteous, make them purely for Your sake, and do not let anyone else have a share of them.”

title: Hadith on Funerals: The Prophet prays for a humble mosque servant
t: Abu Huraira reported: A black woman, or a young man, used to maintain the mosque and one day the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, missed her and asked about her. They said, “She has died.” The Prophet said, “You would not announce it to me?” It was as if they considered her insignificant. The Prophet said, “Show me to her grave.” They led him to it and he prayed over her, then the Prophet said, “Verily, these graves are filled with darkness over their inhabitants. Allah Almighty illuminates them by my prayers over them.”
q: You would not announce it to me? … Show me to her grave. … Verily, these graves are filled with darkness over their inhabitants. Allah Almighty illuminates them by my prayers over them.

title: Fudayl on Sins: Degree of sinning depends on perception of it
t: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim reported: Fudyal ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah gave mercy on him, said, “By the measure of how small a sin seems to you, such is it enormous to Allah. By the measure of how enormous it seems to you, such is it small to Allah.”

title: Ja’far on ‘Izzah: O Allah, honor us with obeying Your commands
t: Abu Mu’awiyah reported: Ja’far ibn Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, used to supplicate, “O Allah, honor us by obedience to You and do not disgrace by disobedience to You.”

title: Hadith on Charity: The Prophet gives everything away before he dies
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was in the severe agony of his final illness and he had seven or nine gold coins. The Prophet said, “O Aisha, what have you done with this gold?” I said, “It is with me.” The Prophet said, “Give it away in charity.” But I was busy caring for him, and then he said, “O Aisha, what have you done with this gold?” I said, “It is with me.” The Prophet said, “Give it to me.” I brought them and placed them in his hands, then the Prophet said, “What is Muhammad thinking if he were to meet Allah while holding onto these?”
q: O Aisha, what have you done with this gold? … Give it away in charity. … O Aisha, what have you done with this gold? … Give it to me. … What is Muhammad thinking if he were to meet Allah while holding onto these?

title: Hadith on Judgment: Angel of Horn waiting to start Resurrection
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “How can I be comfortable while the holder of the trumpet is holding it to his lips, his head lowered and waiting for the order to blow it?” The Muslims said, “What should we say, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Say: Allah is enough for us, and excellent is the Caretaker. We trust in Allah, our Lord.”
q: How can I be comfortable while the holder of the trumpet is holding it to his lips, his head lowered and waiting for the order to blow it? … Say: Allah is enough for us, and excellent is the Caretaker. We trust in Allah, our Lord.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Deceased in grave shown their fate at Judgment
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when one of you dies, he is shown his place morning and evening. If he is among the inhabitants of Paradise, then he is among the inhabitants of Paradise. If he is among the inhabitants of the Hellfire, then he is among the inhabitants of the Hellfire. It will be said: This is your place until you are raised on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Verily, when one of you dies, he is shown his place morning and evening. If he is among the inhabitants of Paradise, then he is among the inhabitants of Paradise. If he is among the inhabitants of the Hellfire, then he is among the inhabitants of the Hellfire. It will be said: This is your place until you are raised on the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Alcohol: Wine-drinker’s prayer not accepted until he repents
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever drinks wine, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty mornings, but if he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he does it again, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty mornings, but if he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he does it again, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty mornings, but if he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he does it again a fourth time, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty mornings and if he repents, Allah will not accept his repentance. He will drink from a river of pus in Hell.”
q: Whoever drinks wine, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty mornings, but if he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he does it again, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty mornings, but if he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he does it again, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty mornings, but if he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he does it again a fourth time, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty mornings and if he repents, Allah will not accept his repentance. He will drink from a river of pus in Hell.

title: Hadith on Jannah: The precious merchandise of Allah is Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the merchandise of Allah is valuable, surely the merchandise of Allah is Paradise.”
q: Verily, the merchandise of Allah is valuable, surely the merchandise of Allah is Paradise.

title: Bilal on Sin: Minors sins against the Lord are no small matter
t: Al-Awza’i reported: Bilal ibn Sa’d, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Do not look at the smallness of the sin, but rather look at the One you have disobeyed.”

title: Hadith on Iman: Allah only bestows faith upon those He loves
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has distributed your characters among you just as He has distributed your provision. Allah gives the world to those He loves and to those He does not love, but He only gives faith to those He loves. Whoever is too stingy with wealth to spend it, too fearful of the enemy to fight them, or too worried to pray at night that he might suffer, then let him increase his declarations of the glory of Allah, that there is no God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest.”
q: Verily, Allah has distributed your characters among you just as He has distributed your provision. Allah gives the world to those He loves and to those He does not love, but He only gives faith to those He loves. Whoever is too stingy with wealth to spend it, too fearful of the enemy to fight them, or too worried to pray at night that he might suffer, then let him increase his declarations of the glory of Allah, that there is no God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest.

title: Ma’ruf on Delusion: Foolish to rely on Allah’s mercy while disobeying Him
t: Ibn al-Jawzi reported: Ma’ruf al-Karkhi, may Alla have mercy on him, said, “Your hope in the mercy of the One you refuse to obey is nothing but delusion and foolishness.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Tasbih: Prophets seek help of Allah by glorifying Him
t: Abu ‘Ubaydah reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “No prophet among the prophets experienced distress but that they would seek aid with the glorification of Allah.”

title: Hadith on Tawakkul: Relying on Allah they enter Paradise without reckoning
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Seventy thousand from my nation will enter Paradise without reckoning. They are those who do not rely on incantations, nor believe in omens, but rather they trust in their Lord.”
q: Seventy thousand from my nation will enter Paradise without reckoning. … They are those who do not rely on incantations, nor believe in omens, but rather they trust in their Lord.

title: Hadith on Tawakkul: Paradise without reckoning, they relied on Allah
t: ‘Imran ibn Husayn reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Seventy thousand from my nation will enter Paradise without reckoning.” They said, “Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “They are those who do not rely on incantations, nor believe in omens, nor use cauterization, but rather they trust in their Lord.”
q: Seventy thousand from my nation will enter Paradise without reckoning.

title: Hadith on Tilawah: Best worship is recitation of the Quran
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best act of worship for my nation is reciting the Quran.”
q: The best act of worship for my nation is reciting the Quran.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Safirini

title: Malik on Tawbah: Crying in repentance removes sins like wind
t: Khazim ibn Husayn reported: Malik ibn Dinar, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “To weep over a mistake will dispel sins just as the wind dispels dry leaves.”

title: Hadith on Quran: Dwellers of heaven view recitations of Quran
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when the Quran is recited in a house, it appears to the inhabitants of the heavens just as the stars appear to the inhabitants of the earth.”
q: Verily, when the Quran is recited in a house, it appears to the inhabitants of the heavens just as the stars appear to the inhabitants of the earth.

title: Hadith on Joy: Allah presents Himself laughing to believers
t: Abu Musa al-Ashari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Our Lord will present Himself to us laughing on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Our Lord will present Himself to us laughing on the Day of Resurrection

title: Sufyan on Self-Talk: Negative voluntary thoughts are blameworthy
t: Abu Talib al-Makki reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I was deprived of the night prayer for five months because of a sin I committed.” It was said, “What was it?” Sufyan said, “I saw a man weeping and I said to myself: This one is showing off.”

title: Hatim on Rizq: No worries about what Allah has guaranteed
