t: Abu Turab reported: Hatim al-Asamm, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I saw all people doubting the matter of their provision and I relied upon Allah Almighty: There is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision (11:6). I realized that I am one among these creatures, so I do not preoccupy myself with anything that my Lord has already guaranteed for me.”
q: There is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: Tell your brothers that you love them
t: Al-Miqdam ibn Ma’di reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a man loves his brother, let him tell him that he loves him.”
q: When a man loves his brother, let him tell him that he loves him.

title: Hadith on Dunya: Love of world accompanied by three vices
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever absorbs his heart in love of the world will be entangled by three things: misery that will not cease to discomfort him, greed that will not achieve his independence, and vain hopes that will never reach their end. For the world is seeking and is sought. Whoever seeks the world, the Hereafter will pursue him until death comes to him and it seizes him. Whoever seeks the Hereafter, the world will pursue him until he exhausts his provision from it.”
q: Whoever absorbs his heart in love of the world will be entangled by three things: misery that will not cease to discomfort him, greed that will not achieve his independence, and vain hopes that will never reach their end. For the world is seeking and is sought. Whoever seeks the world, the Hereafter will pursue him until death comes to him and it seizes him. Whoever seeks the Hereafter, the world will pursue him until he exhausts his provision from it.

title: Abu Darda on Patience: Be forbearing in the face of insults, curses
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Jubayr reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Give up your reputation for the sake of Allah. Whoever abuses you, insults you, or fights you, leave him to Allah. If you do a bad deed, then ask forgiveness from Allah.”

title: Umar on Muhasabah: Hold yourselves accountable before the Reckoning
t: Thabit ibn al-Hajjaj reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Hold yourselves accountable before you are held accountable and evaluate yourselves before you are evaluated, for the Reckoning will be easier upon you tomorrow if you hold yourselves accountable today.”

title: Umar on Humility: Playful with family, but a man when needed
t: Abu Najih reported: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “I am certainly amazed that a man can be with his family like a child, but if he is called forth, he is found to be a true man.”

title: Hadith on Silence: Speak good and be rewarded, be silent and safe
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Speak what is good and acquire gains, or refrain from speaking evil and be safe.”

title: Hadith on Birth: Praise Allah whether the baby is a boy or girl
t: Kathir ibn ‘Ubayd reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, if a child was born to anyone from her family, she would not ask if it was a boy or a girl. Aisha would say, “Was it created healthy?” If the answer was yes, she would say, “All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.”

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Glad tidings of Paradise for professing monotheism
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him, “O Abu Huraira, go forth and whomever you meet who testifies with conviction in his heart that there is no God but Allah, give him the glad tidings of Paradise.”
q: O Abu Huraira, go forth and whomever you meet who testifies with conviction in his heart that there is no God but Allah, give him the glad tidings of Paradise.

title: Hadith on Repentance: Allah created people to forgive them
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you were not to sin, Allah would surely create people who would sin and He would forgive them.”
q: If you were not to sin, Allah would surely create people who would sin and He would forgive them.

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Sincere Muslims never barred from Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I bear witness there is no God but Allah and I am the Messenger of Allah. A servant who meets Allah testifying to these two statements, without any doubt, will not be barred from Paradise.”
q: I bear witness there is no God but Allah and I am the Messenger of Allah. A servant who meets Allah testifying to these two statements, without any doubt, will not be barred from Paradise.

title: Hadith on Dunya: Worldly life is pleasant, then becomes foul
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the food of the son of Adam presents a parable for the worldly life in what the son of Adam defecates. He garnishes the food and seasons it, yet look at what it becomes.”
q: Verily, the food of the son of Adam presents a parable for the worldly life in what the son of Adam defecates. He garnishes the food and seasons it, yet look at what it becomes.

title: Hadith on Dunya: Worldly life is like good food becoming excrement
t: Al-Dahhak ibn Sufyan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him, “O Dahhak, what are you eating?” He said, “Meat and milk.” The Prophet said, “Then what will it become?” He said, “You know what it will become.” The Prophet said, “Verily, Allah Almighty presents what the son of Adam defecates as a parable for the worldly life.”
q: O Dahhak, what are you eating? … Then what will it become? … Verily, Allah Almighty presents what the son of Adam defecates as a parable for the worldly life.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Dhikr: If you remember Me, I will remember you
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: O son of Adam, if you remember Me in solitude, I will remember you in solitude. If you remember Me in a gathering, I will remember you in a gathering greater than the one in which you remembered Me.”
q: Allah Almighty said: O son of Adam, if you remember Me in solitude, I will remember you in solitude. If you remember Me in a gathering, I will remember you in a gathering greater than the one in which you remembered Me.

title: Hadith on Mahabbah: Love Allah, His Messenger, and Ahl al-Bayt
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Love Allah for the blessings by which He nourishes you, love me for the love of Allah, and love the people of my house for the love of me.”
q: Love Allah for the blessings by which He nourishes you, love me for the love of Allah, and love the people of my house for the love of me.

title: Hadith on Dishonesty: Sin to promise payment without intending to
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever marries a woman on the condition of a dowry he does not intend to pay to her, he is an adulterer. Whoever takes on a debt he does not intend to pay back to its owner, he is a thief.”
q: Whoever marries a woman on the condition of a dowry he does not intend to pay to her, he is an adulterer. Whoever takes on a debt he does not intend to pay back to its owner, he is a thief.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Umar II on Qadr: O Allah, make me satisfied with the Decree
t: Yahya ibn Sa’id reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say, “O Allah, make me content with Your providence and bless me in Your decree, such that I would not like to hasten what has been delayed, nor delay what has been hastened.”

title: Hadith on Sincerity: Make my heart better than my appearance
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, make what is within me better than my outward appearance and make my outward appearance righteous. O Allah, I ask You for the righteousness of what You give to people of property, family, and children without myself being misguided or misguiding others.”
q: O Allah, make what is within me better than my outward appearance and make my outward appearance righteous. O Allah, I ask You for the righteousness of what You give to people of property, family, and children without myself being misguided or misguiding others.

title: Hadith on Congregation: Concession to stay home in extreme weather
t: Nu’aym ibn al-Nahham reported: The call to dawn prayer was announced on a cold day while I was in bed with my wife. I said, “If only the caller said: There is no blame upon whoever stays home.” Then the caller of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said at the end of his announcement, “There is no blame upon whoever stays home.”
q: There is no blame upon whoever stays home.

title: Hadith on Hypocrisy: Believers, hypocrites, and evildoers recite Quran
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will be successors after sixty years ‘who waste the prayer and follow their lusts, so they will soon meet an evil ending’ (19:59). Then, there will be successors who recite the Quran, but it does not go beyond their throats. There are three who recite the Quran: a believer, a hypocrite, and an evildoer.” Al-Walid said, “The hypocrite disbelieves in it, the evildoer earns his livelihood from it, and the believer has faith in it.”
q: There will be successors after sixty years ‘who waste the prayer and follow their lusts, so they will soon meet an evil ending’ … Then, there will be successors who recite the Quran, but it does not go beyond their throats. There are three who recite the Quran: a believer, a hypocrite, and an evildoer.

title: Hadith on Virtues: Fasting half of patience, purification half of faith
t: Jurayy al-Nahdi reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Glorification of Allah is half of the Scale, the praise of Allah fills it, and the exaltation of Allah fills what is between the heavens and the earth. Fasting is half of patience, and purification is half of faith.”
q: Glorification of Allah is half of the Scale, the praise of Allah fills it, and the exaltation of Allah fills what is between the heavens and the earth. Fasting is half of patience, and purification is half of faith.

title: Hadith on Jahiliyyah: Four traits remain from pre-Islamic ignorance
t: Abu Malik al-Ash’ari reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Four traits in my nation are among the affairs of ignorance that they have not abandoned: boasting over status, disparaging over lineage, seeking rain by the stars, and wailing over the dead.”
q: Four traits in my nation are among the affairs of ignorance that they have not abandoned: boasting over status, disparaging over lineage, seeking rain by the stars, and wailing over the dead.

title: Hadith on Ostentation: Special place in Hell for reciters showing off
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Seek refuge in Allah from the pit of sorrow.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is the pit of sorrow?” The Prophet said, “It is a valley in Hell from which Hell itself seeks refuge one hundred times a day.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, who will enter it?” The Prophet said, “The reciters who only acted to be seen.”
q: Seek refuge in Allah from the pit of sorrow. … It is a valley in Hell from which Hell itself seeks refuge one hundred times a day. … The reciters who only acted to be seen.

title: Hadith on Hypocrisy: People will be arrogant with the Quran
t: Al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Abdul Muttalib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The religion will be victorious until you pass beyond the seas and fight upon the seas in the way of Allah, then after you will come people who recite the Quran. They will say: We recite the Quran, so who is better at reciting than us? Who has more understanding than us? Who has more knowledge than us?” Then the Prophet turned to his companions and he said, “Is there any good in these people?” They said no. The Prophet said, “These people are among you from this nation. These are fuel for the Hellfire.”
q: The religion will be victorious until you pass beyond the seas and fight upon the seas in the way of Allah, then after you will come people who recite the Quran. They will say: We recite the Quran, so who is better at reciting than us? Who has more understanding than us? Who has more knowledge than us? … Is there any good in these people? … These people are among you from this nation. These are fuel for the Hellfire.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Kibr: Pride is to reject truth, belittle people
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Arrogance is one who disregards the truth and looks down upon people.”
q: Arrogance is one who disregards the truth and looks down upon people.

title: Hadith on Halal: Lawful wealth is excellent for a righteous man
t: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent for me and he ordered me to put on my armor and weapons, then come to him. I did so and came to him while he was performing ablution. The Prophet raised his eyes to me, then lowered them and he said, “O ‘Amr, I intend to send you at the head of an army and Allah will award you with spoils. I will give you an appropriate portion of the property.” ‘Amr said, “I did not embrace Islam in hopes of earning spoils, but rather I submitted in hopes of Islam and to be with the Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “O ‘Amr, lawful wealth is excellent for a righteous man.”
q: O ‘Amr, I intend to send you at the head of an army and Allah will award you with spoils. I will give you an appropriate portion of the property. … O ‘Amr, lawful wealth is excellent for a righteous man.

title: Hadith on Lies: Beware of small acts of dishonesty
t: Asma’ bint Yazid reported: Food was brought to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and it was presented before us. We said, “We do not have an appetite for it.” The Prophet said, “Do not combine hunger with lies.”
q: Do not combine hunger with lies

title: Hasan on Backbiting: Permission to mention evil of three people
t: ‘Aqil reported: Al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “It is not backbiting to speak against three people: a follower of whims, an obstinate sinner who publicizes his sins, and a tyrannical ruler.”

title: Dawud Ta’i on Self-talk: Talking to yourself as a means of discipline
t: Hammad ibn Abi Hanifah reported: I came to Dawud al-Ta’i, may Allah have mercy on him, and his door was fastened shut. I could hear him saying: You lusted after carrots so I fed you carrots, then you lusted after carrots and dates together and I will never let you eat them again! I entered and greeted him with peace only to find that he was censuring himself.

title: Hadith on Zuhd: The Prophet chooses humility over great wealth
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “My Lord presented me with the valley of Mecca that He might turn it into gold for me. I said: No, O Lord, rather I will be satiated some days and hungry some days. When I am hungry, I will humble myself before You and remember You. When I am satiated, I will be grateful to You and praise You.”
q: My Lord presented me with the valley of Mecca that He might turn it into gold for me. I said: No, O Lord, rather I will be satiated some days and hungry some days. When I am hungry, I will humble myself before You and remember You. When I am satiated, I will be grateful to You and praise You.

title: Hadith on Dishonesty: Beware of telling lies about small things
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: My mother called me one day while the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was seated in our house. She said, “Come here and I will give you something.” The Prophet asked her, “What do you want to give him?” She said, “I will give him a date.” The Prophet said, “If you had not given him anything, it would have been recorded against you as a lie.”
q: What do you want to give him? … If you had not given him anything, it would have been recorded against you as a lie.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hudhayfah on Nifaq: Beware of taking hypocrisy too lightly
t: Abu al-Ruqad reported: Hudhayfah said, “A man used to speak a word in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, by which he would become a hypocrite. Indeed, I hear one of you say it now in your gatherings ten times a day!”

title: Ali on Iman: Faith is a light in the heart, hypocrisy is darkness
t: Abdullah ibn Hind reported: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, faith begins like a fragment of white in the heart. Each time faith increases in magnitude, it increases that brightness. When he completes his faith, the entire heart is brightened. Verily, hypocrisy begins like a fragment in the heart. Each time hypocrisy increases in magnitude, it increases that darkness. When he completes his hypocrisy, the entire heart is darkened. I swear by Allah, if you were to split open the heart of a believer, you would find brightness and if you were to split open the heart of a hypocrite, you would find darkness.”

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Best remembrance is hidden from people
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best remembrance is in private and the best provision is sufficient.”
q: The best remembrance is in private and the best provision is sufficient.

title: Hadith on Miracles: The Prophet performs signs for his companions
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: We were on a journey with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and we ran short of water. The Prophet said, “Bring the remaining water.” They brought a vessel with a little water in it. The Prophet placed his hands in the vessel, then he said, “Come to the blessed purification, a blessing from Allah.” I saw the water emanating from between the Prophet’s fingers, and we heard his food glorifying Allah as he ate it.
q: Bring the remaining water. … Come to the blessed purification, a blessing from Allah

title: Hadith on Sirat: Traverse over Hell thinner than a hair
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: We said, “O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do you have trouble seeing the sun on a day without clouds?” Abu Sa’id said, “I have come to know that the bridge over Hell is thinner than a hair and sharper than a sword.”
q: Do you have trouble seeing the sun on a day without clouds?

title: Hadith on Sujud: Verses of prostration recommended, not obligatory
t:
Rabia’ reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, recited Surat al-Nahl on the pulpit on Friday until he reached the verse of prostration, then he descended and prostrated and the people prostrated with him. On the following Friday, Umar recited the same chapter until he came to the verse of prostration. Umar said, “O people, we have passed by a verse of prostration. Whoever prostrates has acted correctly, but whoever does not prostrate is not sinful,” and Umar did not prostrate.

Ibn Umar said, “Indeed, Allah has not obligated the prostration unless we wish to do so.”

title: Hadith on Quran: The Prophet supplicates between verses
t: Hudhayfah reported: I prayed one night with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he recited in a relaxed manner. If he passed by a verse glorifying Allah, he would glorify Him. If he passed by a verse of petition, he would ask Him. If he passed by a verse of refuge, he would seek refuge in Him.

title: Hadith on Tawassul: Story of three men in the cave
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “While three men were walking, they were overcome by rain and took refuge in a cave in a mountain. A boulder fell over the mouth of their cave, blocking them inside. One of them said to the others, ‘Look at the good deeds you have done for Allah that you may call upon Allah Almighty by them, for perhaps He will relieve you.’ One of them said, ‘O Allah, I had two old parents with my wife and young child. I tended to a flock and when evening came, I milked them and served my parents first before my child. One day I went in search of fodder and I did not come back until it was evening. I found them both sleeping, so I milked as I had done before. I brought the milk and stood by their heads, for I hated to disrupt their sleep or to serve my child before both of them. My child was crying at my feet, yet I continued standing over them until the approach of dawn. If You know I had done that seeking Your countenance, then relieve us of this distress that we might see the sky!’ Allah shifted the boulder until they could see the sky. Another man said, ‘O Allah, I had a cousin whom I loved more than any man could love women. I presented myself to her and she refused unless I could give her one hundred coins. I worked hard until I gathered one hundred coins and brought them to her. When I prepared myself between her legs, she said: O servant of Allah, fear Allah and do not break the hymen without right to do so! I stood and left her. If You know I had done that seeking your Face, then relieve us of this distress!’ The boulder was again shifted for them. The last man said, ‘O Allah, I employed a worker for a portion of rice. When he finished his work, he said: Give me what I deserve! I offered his share to him but he did not accept it. I continued planting his share until I had amassed cows and flocks. Then he came to me and he said: Fear Allah and do not violate my rights! I said: Go to this cow and its flocks and take them. He said: Fear Allah and do not mock me! I said: I do not mock you, take that cow and its flocks. So he took them and he left. If You know I had done that seeking Your face, then relieve us of what remains!’ Then Allah relieved them of what remained.”
q: While three men were walking, they were overcome by rain and took refuge in a cave in a mountain. A boulder fell over the mouth of their cave, blocking them inside. One of them said to the others, ‘Look at the good deeds you have done for Allah that you may call upon Allah Almighty by them, for perhaps He will relieve you.’ One of them said, ‘O Allah, I had two old parents with my wife and young child. I tended to a flock and when evening came, I milked them and served my parents first before my child. One day I went in search of fodder and I did not come back until it was evening. I found them both sleeping, so I milked as I had done before. I brought the milk and stood by their heads, for I hated to disrupt their sleep or to serve my child before both of them. My child was crying at my feet, yet I continued standing over them until the approach of dawn. If You know I had done that seeking Your countenance, then relieve us of this distress that we might see the sky!’ Allah shifted the boulder until they could see the sky. Another man said, ‘O Allah, I had a cousin whom I loved more than any man could love women. I presented myself to her and she refused unless I could give her one hundred coins. I worked hard until I gathered one hundred coins and brought them to her. When I prepared myself between her legs, she said: O servant of Allah, fear Allah and do not break the hymen without right to do so! I stood and left her. If You know I had done that seeking your Face, then relieve us of this distress!’ The boulder was again shifted for them. The last man said, ‘O Allah, I employed a worker for a portion of rice. When he finished his work, he said: Give me what I deserve! I offered his share to him but he did not accept it. I continued planting his share until I had amassed cows and flocks. Then he came to me and he said: Fear Allah and do not violate my rights! I said: Go to this cow and its flocks and take them. He said: Fear Allah and do not mock me! I said: I do not mock you, take that cow and its flocks. So he took them and he left. If You know I had done that seeking Your face, then relieve us of what remains!’ Then Allah relieved them of what remained.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salat: Moving lips for silent recitation in prayer
t: Abu Ma’mar reported: I said to Khabbab, “Did the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, recite in the noon and afternoon prayers?” Khabbab said yes. We said, “How do you know?” Khabbab said, “By the movement of his beard.”

title: Hadith on Quran: Recommendation to recite distinctly, not too quickly
t: Shaqiq reported: A man from the tribe of Bahilah named Nahik ibn Sinan came to Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said, “I recite the chapters of al-Mufassal in one cycle of prayer.” Abdullah said, “This is like the recitation of poetry. I know the manner in which the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, recited them: two chapters in one cycle of prayer.”

title: Hadith on Tilawah: Recite the Quran pleasantly, then cry over it
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, this Quran has descended with sadness. If you recite it, then weep. If you cannot weep, then feign weeping. Recite in a melodious tone, for whoever does not use a pleasant voice is not one of us.”
q: Verily, this Quran has descended with sadness. If you recite it, then weep. If you cannot weep, then feign weeping. Recite in a melodious tone, for whoever does not use a pleasant voice is not one of us.

title: Hadith on Tilawah: Companions recite Quran pleasantly to each other
t: Abu Huraira reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said to Abu Musa while he was sitting in a gathering, “Remind us of our Lord.” Abu Musa would recite to him in a melodious tone as he sat in the gathering.

title: Hadith on Hifz: Tremendous rewards for memorizing Quran
t: Buraydah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the Quran will meet its companion on the Day of Resurrection, when his grave is cleaved open, as a pale man, saying: Do you recognize me? He will say: I do not recognize you. The pale man will say: I am your companion, the Quran, who made you thirsty in the midday heat and sleepless at night, for every trader is beyond his trade, and today you are beyond every transaction. He will be given the dominion in his right hand and eternal life in his left hand. A crown of dignity will be placed on his head and his parents will be clothed in two garments, which no people from the world could ever afford. They will say: Why have you dressed us with this? It will be said: Your child held to the Quran. Then it will be said to him: Recite and ascend the levels of Paradise and its chambers! He will continue to ascend as long as he recites, whether slowly or quickly.”
q: Verily, the Quran will meet its companion on the Day of Resurrection, when his grave is cleaved open, as a pale man, saying: Do you recognize me? He will say: I do not recognize you. The pale man will say: I am your companion, the Quran, who made you thirsty in the midday heat and sleepless at night, for every trader is beyond his trade, and today you are beyond every transaction. He will be given the dominion in his right hand and eternal life in his left hand. A crown of dignity will be placed on his head and his parents will be clothed in two garments, which no people from the world could ever afford. They will say: Why have you dressed us with this? It will be said: Your child held to the Quran. Then it will be said to him: Recite and ascend the levels of Paradise and its chambers! He will continue to ascend as long as he recites, whether slowly or quickly.

title: Hadith on Leaders: Honoring elders, scholars, righteous rulers
t: Abu Musa al-Ash’ari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, part of glorifying Allah is to honor the gray-haired Muslim and the bearer of the Quran, who is neither extravagant nor neglectful of it, and to honor the just ruler.”
q: Verily, part of glorifying Allah is to honor the gray-haired Muslim and the bearer of the Quran, who is neither extravagant nor neglectful of it, and to honor the just ruler.

title: Hadith on Miracles: The rocks and trees greet the Prophet
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: I was with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in Mecca and we went out to one of its neighborhoods. He did not face any mountain or tree but that it would say, “Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Qira’ah: Allah attentively listens to recitation of Quran
t: Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah listens more intently to a man reciting the Quran aloud in a beautiful voice than an employer of singers listens to his singers.”
q: Allah listens more intently to a man reciting the Quran aloud in a beautiful voice than an employer of singers listens to his singers.

title: Hadith on Qira’ah: Description of the Prophet’s recitation of Quran
t: Abdullah ibn al-Mughaffal reported: I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, reciting upon his camel while he was traveling with it. He was reciting Surat al-Fath, or a part of it, in a soft tone while his voice was quivering.

title: Hadith on Qira’ah: The Prophet beautifies his recitation of Quran
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, reciting in the evening prayer, “By the fig and the olive,” (95:1). I have not heard a voice more beautiful than his.
q: By the fig and the olive
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Quran: Every verse has a deeper meaning than is obvious
t:
Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Quran was revealed in seven modes. Each verse among them has an outward and an inward, and each limit has a horizon.”

Abu Ja’far said, “We contemplated this tradition and the best of possible interpretations to come is that there is the outward of it, the meaning of which is obvious, and the inward of it, the meaning of which is subtle. This shows that people must seek its inward meanings just as they seek its outward meanings.”
q: The Quran was revealed in seven modes. Each verse among them has an outward and an inward, and each limit has a horizon

title: Hadith on Evil: When to abandon enjoining good?
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, when should we give up enjoining good and forbidding evil?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When there appears among you the same as the nations which came before you.” We said, “O Messenger of Allah, what appeared among the nations before us?” The Prophet said, “Kingship among your youths, obscenity among your elders, and knowledge among your most vile.”
q: When there appears among you the same as the nations which came before you … Kingship among your youths, obscenity among your elders, and knowledge among your most vile.

title: Hadith on Nifaq: Islam may be supported by sinners and hypocrites
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty might support this religion by the hands of people who have no share in the Hereafter.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty might support this religion by the hands of people who have no share in the Hereafter.

title: Hadith on Trials: Allah expiates sins with disease
t: Jubayr ibn Mut’im reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty will put His servant to trial by illness until his every sin is expiated.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty will put His servant to trial by illness until his every sin is expiated.

title: Hadith on Cleanliness: The Prophet teaches his companions like a father
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I am only like a father to you in the way that I teach you. When one of you goes to relieve himself, he should not face the direction of prayer or turn his back to it completely, and he should not cleanse himself with his right hand.”
q: Verily, I am only like a father to you in the way that I teach you. When one of you goes to relieve himself, he should not face the direction of prayer or turn his back to it completely, and he should not cleanse himself with his right hand.

title: Mu’adh on ‘Ilm: No reward for divine knowledge until acted upon
t: Yazid ibn Jabir reported: Mu’adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Act as you wish after you have learned, for Allah Almighty will never reward you for knowledge until you act upon it.”

title: Hadith on Dishonesty: Plotters and liars are punished in Hell
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever deceives us is not one of us. Conspiracy and deception are in the Hellfire.”
q: Whoever deceives us is not one of us. Conspiracy and deception are in the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Trials afflict those with good words, corrupt hearts
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty said: I have created My creatures with tongues as sweet as honey and hearts as bitter as aloes. I swear by Myself, I will surely decree a tribulation for them that will leave even the forbearing among them deranged. Do they try to delude Me or conspire against Me?”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty said: I have created My creatures with tongues as sweet as honey and hearts as bitter as aloes. I swear by Myself, I will surely decree a tribulation for them that will leave even the forbearing among them deranged. Do they try to delude Me or conspire against Me?

title: Hadith on Fame: Allah gives no weight to worldly status
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, a prominent and obese man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection who does not weigh as much as a gnat’s wing to Allah. Recite the verse: Thus, We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection.” (18:105)
q: Verily, a prominent and obese man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection who does not weigh as much as a gnat’s wing to Allah. Recite the verse: Thus, We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Sha’bi on ‘Ilm: Knowing one’s own ignorance is half of knowledge
t: Mughirah reported: Al-Sha’bi, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The statement ‘I do not know’ is one half of knowledge.”

title: Hadith on Signs: Hurry to good before six signs of the Hour
t: ‘Abis al-Ghifari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Hasten to do good deeds before six signs: foolish leaders, proliferation of enforcement, bribery in judgment, bloodshed is taken lightly, family ties are severed, and a generation are brought up treating the Quran as musical instruments; they put forth one of them to sing for them, though he is the least of them in understanding.”
q: Hasten to do good deeds before six signs: foolish leaders, proliferation of enforcement, bribery in judgment, bloodshed is taken lightly, family ties are severed, and a generation are brought up treating the Quran as musical instruments; they put forth one of them to sing for them, though he is the least of them in understanding.

title: Hadith on Humility: Blessed is one busy with self-improvement
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Blessed is he whose own faults preoccupy him from the faults of people.”
q: Blessed is he whose own faults preoccupy him from the faults of people.

title: Hadith on Ghuraba: Blessed are strangers who revive the Sunnah
t: ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the religion began as something strange and it will return to being strange, so blessed are the strangers who restore my Sunnah which the people after me had distorted.”
q: Verily, the religion began as something strange and it will return to being strange, so blessed are the strangers who restore my Sunnah which the people after me had distorted.

title: Ali on Fiqh: True jurist preaches wisdom, knowledge, understanding
t: Yahya ibn ‘Abbad reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, the jurist is truly one of understanding, who never lets people despair of the mercy of Allah, who never grants them a concession to disobey Allah, who never lets them feel secure from the punishment of Allah, and who never abandons the Quran seeking anything else. Verily, there is no good in worship without knowledge, nor in knowledge without understanding, nor in recitation without reflection.”

title: Hasan on Fiqh: Who is the true Faqih in Islam?
t: ‘Imran al-Minqari reported: I said one day to Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah be pleased with him, about something he claimed, “O Abu Sa’id, this is not as the jurists say!” Al-Hasan said, “Woe to you! Do you think of yourself as merely a jurist? Surely, the true jurist is only one who renounces the world by seeking the Hereafter, insightful in the matters of his religion, and constantly worshiping his Lord.”

title: Hadith on ‘Ilm: Knowledge is Quran, Sunnah, and justice
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Knowledge is three types and anything else is a surplus: a decisive verse, or an established Sunnah, or an obligation of justice.”
q: Knowledge is three types and anything else is a surplus: a decisive verse, or an established Sunnah, or an obligation of justice

title: Sa’id on Cleanliness: Allah is pure, clean, generous, magnanimous
t: Salih ibn Abi Hassan reported: Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, Allah is pure and He loves purity. He is clean and He loves cleanliness. He is generous and He loves generosity. He is magnanimous and He loves magnanimity.”

title: Hadith on Pets: The Prophet comforts a boy whose pet bird died
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would come to us and I had a little brother whose nickname was Abu ‘Umayr. He had a pet sparrow he used to play with and it died. The Prophet entered one day and saw him grieving, so he said, “What is the matter with him?” They said, “His sparrow has died.” The Prophet said, “O Abu ‘Umayr, what happened to the little sparrow?”
q: What is the matter with him? … O Abu ‘Umayr, what happened to the little sparrow?

title: Hadith on Pardon: Allah commands the Prophet to forgive bad manners
t: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah reported: When the verse was revealed, “Hold to forgiveness, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant,” (7:199), the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Gabriel, what is this?” Gabriel said, “I do not know until I ask the All-Knowing.” Then Gabriel said, “O Muhammad, Allah commands you to keep relations with those who cut you off, to give to those who deprive you, and to forgive those who wrong you.”
q: Hold to forgiveness, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant, … O Gabriel, what is this

title: Ibn Zubayr on Character: Commandment to tolerate people’s bad manners
t: Wahb ibn Kaysan reported: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, said upon the pulpit, “Hold to forgiveness, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant (7:199). By Allah, we have not been commanded but to endure the bad character of people. By Allah, I will endure it from them as long as I accompany them.”
q: Hold to forgiveness, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant

title: Hadith on Adversity: Be grateful in prosperity, Allah helps in hardship
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Acknowledge Allah in prosperity, and He will acknowledge you in adversity.”
q: Acknowledge Allah in prosperity, and He will acknowledge you in adversity.

title: Hadith on Rizq: Be certain the provision of Allah will reach you
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Were the son of Adam to flee from his provision as he flees from death, his provision would surely reach him just as death will reach him.”
q: Were the son of Adam to flee from his provision as he flees from death, his provision would surely reach him just as death will reach him.

title: Shafi’i on Satiety: I never ate to my fill for sixteen years
t: Al-Rabia’ ibn Sulayman reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I have not satiated myself for sixteen years, as I have cast fullness aside. For satiety puts heaviness in the body, hardens the heart, causes loss of intelligence, induces sleepiness, and weakens the performance of the worshiper.”

title: Hadith on Faqr: Prepare for poverty if you love the Prophet
t: Abu Dharr reported: He came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Indeed, I love the people of your house!” The Prophet said to him, “By Allah? Then prepare to endure poverty, for poverty quickly approaches those who love us faster than a torrent flows from the highest hillock to its lowest part.”
q: By Allah? Then prepare to endure poverty, for poverty quickly approaches those who love us faster than a torrent flows from the highest hillock to its lowest part.

title: Hadith on Torture: Worst punishment in Hell for torturing people
t: Khalid ibn al-Walid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the people most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are those who most severely tortured people in the world.”
q: Verily, the people most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are those who most severely tortured people in the world.

title: Hasan on Dua: Goodness is knowledge in world, Paradise in Hereafter
t: Hisham ibn Hassan reported: Al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said in regards to His saying, “O Lord, give us good in the world and good in the Hereafter,” (2:201) that good in the world is knowledge and worship, and good in the Hereafter is Paradise.
q: O Lord, give us good in the world and good in the Hereafter

title: Hadith on Hellfire: Severe punishment for prophet-killers, idol-makers
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people punished most severely on the Day of Resurrection are a man who was killed by a prophet or who killed a prophet, an Imam of misguidance, and a sculptor of graven images.”

title: Hadith on Ulama’: Scholars are distinguished, forgiven in Hereafter
t: Abu Musa al-Ash’ari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah will raise His servants on the Day of Resurrection, then He will distinguish the scholars, saying: O company of scholars, I would never waste My knowledge among you that I might punish you, so go now for I have forgiven you.”
q: Allah will raise His servants on the Day of Resurrection, then He will distinguish the scholars, saying: O company of scholars, I would never waste My knowledge among you that I might punish you, so go now for I have forgiven you.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Ibn al-Qayyim

title: Abu Darda on ‘Ilm: Seeking knowledge is an act of jihad
t: Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever does not consider coming and going for the sake of knowledge to be an act of jihad, he has a shortcoming in his mind and his opinion.”

title: Sufyan on Lust: Extreme condemnation of child sexual abuse
t: Salm ibn Qutaybah reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If a man were even to play with the two toes of a boy seeking lustful pleasure, he would be a sodomite.”

title: Ibn Sirin on Hasad: How can I envy anyone in the world?
t: Yunus ibn ‘Ubayd reported: Ibn Sirin, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I have never envied anyone for something they had in the world. If he was among the people of Paradise, how could I envy him for something in the world while he will be sent to Paradise? If he was among the people of Hellfire, how could I envy him for something in the world while he will be sent to Hellfire?”

title: Hadith on Judges: Three types of judges, only one in Paradise
t: Buraydah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The judges are three kinds: two judges are in Hellfire and one judge is in Paradise. A man who judges without the truth while he knows it, he is in Hellfire. A judge who has no knowledge and violates the rights of people, he is in Hellfire. A judge who judges with the truth, he is in Paradise.”
q: The judges are three kinds: two judges are in Hellfire and one judge is in Paradise. A man who judges without the truth while he knows it, he is in Hellfire. A judge who has no knowledge and violates the rights of people, he is in Hellfire. A judge who judges with the truth, he is in Paradise.

title: Abu Uthman on Suhbah: Friend to Allah, His Messenger, believers, and fools
t: Abu al-Husayn reported: Abu Uthman al-Hiri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Companionship with Allah Almighty is to have good manners, to always be reverent, and to be mindful. Companionship with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, is to follow his Sunnah and adhere to the outward rulings. Companionship with the allies of Allah is to respect and to serve them. Companionship with one’s family and children is to have good character. Companionship with one’s brethren is to always be joyful and cheerful, unless there is sin. Companionship with the foolish is to supplicate for them, to be merciful to them, and to appreciate the blessings of Allah upon you as you have been kept safe from their trials.”

title: Sahl on Presence: Believers relieved by living the present moment
t:
Al-Sulami reported: It was asked of Sahl ibn Abdullah, may Allah have mercy on him, “When will the soul of the impoverished find rest?” Sahl said, “When the soul does not see a moment other than the present moment in which it is.”

Al-Sulami said, “It is part of virtue that the servant not be concerned with any moment but his present moment.”

title: Yahya on Wara’: True piety is inwardly and outwardly
t: Ibn ‘Alawiyyah reported: Yahya ibn Mu’adh, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Piety has two types: outward piety and inward piety. As for the external, it is to not make any movement but for the sake of Allah. As for the internal, it is to not allow anything into the heart besides Allah Almighty.”

title: Abu Khayr on Qulub: Hearts of believers merciful, hypocrites malicious
t: Isma’il ibn Nujayd reported: Abu al-Khayr, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Hearts are containers. A heart filled with faith has signs of compassion for all Muslims, concern for their concerns, and is cooperative in their welfare. A heart filled with hypocrisy has signs of malice, rancor, dishonesty, and envy.”

title: Sufyan on Zuhd: Definition of asceticism is being thankful, patient
t: Ali ibn al-Madini reported: It was said to Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, “What is the definition of temperance?” Sufayn said, “It is that you are grateful in prosperity and patient in adversity. If one is like that, he is temperate.” It was said, “What is gratitude?” Sufyan said, “It is that you avoid what Allah has prohibited.”

title: Hadith on Adhan: Pronouncing call to prayer in baby newborn’s ear
t: Abu Rafi’ reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, pronounce the call to prayer in the ear of Hasan ibn Ali after Fatimah gave birth to him.

title: Hadith on Luxury: Worst Muslims extravagant in food, clothing, speech
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will be men from my nation who eat a variety of foods, drink a variety of drinks, wear a variety of clothes, and are boastful in their speech. These are the worst of my nation.”
q: There will be men from my nation who eat a variety of foods, drink a variety of drinks, wear a variety of clothes, and are boastful in their speech. These are the worst of my nation

title: Hadith on Extravagance: Worst Muslims are addicted to luxury
t: Fatimah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The worst of my nation are those who are nourished by pleasure, eating a variety of foods, wearing a variety of clothes, and being pompous in their speech.”
q: The worst of my nation are those who are nourished by pleasure, eating a variety of foods, wearing a variety of clothes, and being pompous in their speech.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Hunger: The Prophet does not feed his family to their fill
t: Abu Huraira reported: By the One in whose hand is my soul, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, did not satiate his family with wheat bread for three consecutive nights until he departed from this world.

title: Hadith on Satiety: Those who overeat are hungriest in Hereafter
t: Ibn Umar reported: A man belched in the presence of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet said, “Restrain your belching, for those who were most satiated in the world will be the most hungry on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Restrain your belching, for those who were most satiated in the world will be the most hungry on the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Islam: Good deeds before conversion to Islam rewarded
t: Hakim ibn Hizam reported: He said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “What do you think of the acts of worship I did in the time of ignorance. Will I get anything from them?” The Prophet said, “You have embraced Islam with the good you previously did.”
q: You have embraced Islam with the good you previously did

title: Hadith on Qubur: Great rewards or punishments in the grave
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the believer in his grave is within a green meadow. His grave welcomes him with seventy cubits of space and it is illuminated for him like the full moon on a clear night. Do you know why this verse was revealed: He will have a confined life and We will raise him blind on the Day of Resurrection (20:124)? Do you know what is a confined life?” They said, “Allah and His messenger know best.” The Prophet said, “It is the punishment of an unbeliever in his grave. By the One in whose hand is my soul, ninety-nine dragons will be given authority over him. Do you know what is a dragon? It is seventy serpents, each serpent with seven heads stinging him and maiming him until the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Verily, the believer in his grave is within a green meadow. His grave welcomes him with seventy cubits of space and it is illuminated for him like the full moon on a clear night. Do you know why this verse was revealed: He will have a confined life and We will raise him blind on the Day of Resurrection … Do you know what is a confined life … It is the punishment of an unbeliever in his grave. By the One in whose hand is my soul, ninety-nine dragons will be given authority over him. Do you know what is a dragon? It is seventy serpents, each serpent with seven heads stinging him and maiming him until the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Death: Aisha’s Godfearing humility on her deathbed
t: Ibn Abi Mulaykah reported: Ibn Abbas asked permission to see Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, before her death while she was overcome with suffering. Aisha said, “I am afraid he will praise me.” It was said, “He is the cousin of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and a prominent Muslim.” Aisha said, “Give him permission.” Ibn Abbas said, “How do you find yourself?” Aisha said, “I am good, if I fear Allah.” Ibn Abbas said, “You are good, if Allah wills. You are the wife of the Messenger of Allah. He married no virgin besides you. Your innocence was revealed from heaven.” Ibn al-Zubayr entered after him and Aisha said, “Ibn Abbas visited and praised me. I wish I was a thing forgotten!”

title: Hadith on Jannah: Wives of Paradise sing for their husbands
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the wives of Paradise will sing for their husbands with the most beautiful voices no one has ever heard. Among their singing is: We are fine and beautiful women, wives of a noble people looked upon with the eyes of comfort! And among their singing is: We are women everlasting never to die, we are women in safety never to fear, we are women here to stay never to leave!”
q: Verily, the wives of Paradise will sing for their husbands with the most beautiful voices no one has ever heard. Among their singing is: We are fine and beautiful women, wives of a noble people looked upon with the eyes of comfort! And among their singing is: We are women everlasting never to die, we are women in safety never to fear, we are women here to stay never to leave!

title: Ibrahim on Character: Asking Allah to give Paradise to the wrongdoer
t: Al-Qushayri reported: Ibrahim ibn Adham, may Allah have mercy on him, went out to one of the prairies and he was confronted by a soldier. The soldier said, “Where are the residents?” Ibrahim pointed to the graveyard, so the soldier struck his head and wounded him. When the soldier passed by later, it was said to him, “He is Ibrahim ibn Adham, the ascetic of Khorasan!” The soldier came to him apologizing, and Ibrahim said, “When you struck me, I asked Allah Almighty to give you Paradise.” The soldier said, “Why?” Ibrahim said, “I knew I would be rewarded for it, so I did not want my share from you to be good and your share from me to be evil.”

title: Hadith on Janazah: Virtue of many believers performing funeral prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is prayed over by a hundred Muslims at his funeral, he will be forgiven.”
q: Whoever is prayed over by a hundred Muslims at his funeral, he will be forgiven.”

title: Hatim on Leadership: Believers seek good governance, hypocrites seek power
t: Al-Ghazali reported: Hatim al-Asamm, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The believer commands and prohibits for the sake of governance and he sets things right. The hypocrite commands and prohibits for the sake of power and he causes corruption.”

title: Hadith on Hypocrisy: No reward for worshipping with worldly motives
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Give glad tidings to this nation of honor, victory, and stability. Yet, whoever does a deed of the Hereafter for the sake of the world, he will have no share of it in the Hereafter.”
q: Give glad tidings to this nation of honor, victory, and stability. Yet, whoever does a deed of the Hereafter for the sake of the world, he will have no share of it in the Hereafter.

title: Hadith on Greed: Human nature remains greedy
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The son of Adam grows old but remains young in two matters: greed for wealth and greed for long life.”
q: The son of Adam grows old but remains young in two matters: greed for wealth and greed for long life.

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: O Allah, guide me to the best of character
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, You are the King. There is no God but You. You are my Lord, and I am Your servant. I have wronged myself and acknowledged my sins, so forgive all of my sins. Verily, none forgives sins but You. Guide me to the best of character, for none guides to it but You.”
q: O Allah, You are the King. There is no God but You. You are my Lord, and I am Your servant. I have wronged myself and acknowledged my sins, so forgive all of my sins. Verily, none forgives sins but You. Guide me to the best of character, for none guides to it but You.

title: Hadith on Death: The Prophet suffers painful throes of death
t: Aisha reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, as he was dying and he had a cup of water, which he would dip his hand into and wipe his face with water, then he was saying, “O Allah, help me with the agonies of death!”
q: O Allah, help me with the agonies of death!

title: Hadith on Death: Munkar and Nakir questions souls in the grave
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the deceased is buried in his grave, two black and blue angels come to him. One of them is called Munkar and the other is called Nakir. They will both say: What do you say about this man? He will say what he said before: He is the servant of Allah and His messenger, I bear witness there is no God but Allah and Muhammad is His servant and His messenger. They will both say: We knew you would say this! Then his grave is expanded by seventy cubits on each side, it is illuminated for him, and it is said to him: Sleep! He will say: May I return to my family to tell them? They will both say: Sleep like a bridegroom, whom none awakens but the most beloved of his family, until Allah resurrects him from his place of rest. If he was a hypocrite, he will say to the angels: I heard people saying something, so I said the same as them, for I do not know! They will both say: We knew you would say that! It will be said to the earth to constrict him, so it will constrict him by squeezing his ribs together. He will continue being punished until Allah resurrects him from that place of his.”
q: When the deceased is buried in his grave, two black and blue angels come to him. One of them is called Munkar and the other is called Nakir. They will both say: What do you say about this man? He will say what he said before: He is the servant of Allah and His messenger, I bear witness there is no God but Allah and Muhammad is His servant and His messenger. They will both say: We knew you would say this! Then his grave is expanded by seventy cubits on each side, it is illuminated for him, and it is said to him: Sleep! He will say: May I return to my family to tell them? They will both say: Sleep like a bridegroom, whom none awakens but the most beloved of his family, until Allah resurrects him from his place of rest. If he was a hypocrite, he will say to the angels: I heard people saying something, so I said the same as them, for I do not know! They will both say: We knew you would say that! It will be said to the earth to constrict him, so it will constrict him by squeezing his ribs together. He will continue being punished until Allah resurrects him from that place of his.

title: Hadith on Death: Angels taking souls of believers and unbelievers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When death approaches the believer, angels of mercy come to him with white silk, saying: Come out satisfied and well-pleasing to the rest and comfort of Allah and to a Lord who is not angry! So it comes out like the best fragrance of musk until they pass him between themselves and reach the gate of heaven, saying: How pleasant is this fragrance you have brought from the earth! The souls of believers come to him more joyful than one of you whose loved ones return home. They ask him: What happened to this person? What happened to this person? They will say: Let him be, for he was in the distress of the world. When he is asked if such person has come to you, they say: He was taken away to his mother, the abyss. Verily, when death approaches the unbeliever, angels of punishment come to him with sackcloth, saying: Come out displeased and displeasing to the punishment of Allah Almighty! So it comes out like the foulest stench of a corpse until they take it to the gate of the earth, saying how foul is this stench until the souls of unbelievers are brought to him.”
q: When death approaches the believer, angels of mercy come to him with white silk, saying: Come out satisfied and well-pleasing to the rest and comfort of Allah and to a Lord who is not angry! So it comes out like the best fragrance of musk until they pass him between themselves and reach the gate of heaven, saying: How pleasant is this fragrance you have brought from the earth! The souls of believers come to him more joyful than one of you whose loved ones return home. They ask him: What happened to this person? What happened to this person? They will say: Let him be, for he was in the distress of the world. When he is asked if such person has come to you, they say: He was taken away to his mother, the abyss. Verily, when death approaches the unbeliever, angels of punishment come to him with sackcloth, saying: Come out displeased and displeasing to the punishment of Allah Almighty! So it comes out like the foulest stench of a corpse until they take it to the gate of the earth, saying how foul is this stench until the souls of unbelievers are brought to him.

title: Hadith on Funerals: Only remember the dead in a good way
t: Aisha reported: A person who passed away was mentioned in an evil way in front of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, so he said, “Do not mention your deceased unless it is good.”
q: Do not mention your deceased unless it is good

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Allah’s dominion not decreased by spending
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The hand of Allah is full and it is not diminished by continuous spending night and day. Do you not see that He has been spending since the creation of the heavens and the earth, and it has not decreased anything in His hand?”
q: The hand of Allah is full and it is not diminished by continuous spending night and day. Do you not see that He has been spending since the creation of the heavens and the earth, and it has not decreased anything in His hand?
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Faith: Let him maintain his family relations
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him uphold his family ties.”
q: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him uphold his family ties.

title: Hadith on Salat: Paradise rewarded for praying with presence of heart
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No Muslim performs ablution well and then prays two cycles with his heart and direction focused, except that Paradise will be necessary for him.”
q: No Muslim performs ablution well and then prays two cycles with his heart and direction focused, except that Paradise will be necessary for him.

title: Hasan on Mindfulness: Presence of heart required in every prayer
t: Rabia’ ibn Subayh reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Every prayer in which your heart is not present may more quickly be punished than rewarded.”

title: Sufyan on Salat: Reverence is required for sound prayer
t: Bishr ibn al-Harith reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whoever does not have reverence has spoiled his prayer.”

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Glory be to Allah by the number of His creations
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: He entered the house of a woman along with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while she had date-stones or pebbles in her hand by which she counted her glorifications of Allah. The Prophet said, “Shall I not tell you what is easier or better than this? Glory be to Allah by the number of His creations in the heavens. Glory be to Allah by the number of His creations on the earth. Glory be to Allah by the number of His creations between them. Glory be to Allah by the number of what He has created. Then say Allah is the greatest similarly, all praise is due to Allah similarly, there is no God but Allah similarly, and there is no movement or might but in Allah similarly.”
q: Shall I not tell you what is easier or better than this? Glory be to Allah by the number of His creations in the heavens. Glory be to Allah by the number of His creations on the earth. Glory be to Allah by the number of His creations between them. Glory be to Allah by the number of what He has created. Then say Allah is the greatest similarly, all praise is due to Allah similarly, there is no God but Allah similarly, and there is no movement or might but in Allah similarly.

title: Hadith on Salat: Supplication after bowing, between prostrations
t: Hudhayfah reported: He prayed one night with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he heard him when he announced the opening exaltation, “Allah is the greatest, O possessor of power, dominion, grandeur, and might.” The Prophet said in his bowing, “Glory be to Allah the Almighty.” When he raised his head from bowing, he said, “To my Lord is all praise. To my Lord is all praise,” and in his prostration, “Glory be to Allah the Exalted,” and between the two prostrations, “Lord, forgive me. Lord, forgive me.” The Prophet’s standing, bowing, when he raised his head from bowing, his prostrations, and between his prostrations were nearly the same length.
q: Allah is the greatest, O possessor of power, dominion, grandeur, and might. … Glory be to Allah the Almighty. … To my Lord is all praise. To my Lord is all praise … Glory be to Allah the Exalted … Lord, forgive me. Lord, forgive me.

title: Hadith Shayatin: Devils come out to roam when darkness settles
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the night lowers its wings or you enter evening, hold back your children, for the devils spread out at that time. When a while has passed, you may let them go. Lock your doors and mention the name of Allah, for Satan cannot open a locked door. Tie your water-skins and mention the name of Allah, cover your vessels with whatever you have and mention the name of Allah, and put out your lamps.”
q: When the night lowers its wings or you enter evening, hold back your children, for the devils spread out at that time. When a while has passed, you may let them go. Lock your doors and mention the name of Allah, for Satan cannot open a locked door. Tie your water-skins and mention the name of Allah, cover your vessels with whatever you have and mention the name of Allah, and put out your lamps.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Khutbah al-Hajah: How the Prophet began his sermons
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gave us the combination of all good things and their endings, for he taught us the statements of prayer and the statements of need. The statements of prayer are, “All greetings, prayers, and good things are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I testify there is no God but Allah, and I testify Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.” The statements of need are, “All praise is due to Allah. We praise him, we seek His help, we seek His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Allah from the evil within ourselves and our evil deeds. Whomever Allah guides, there is none to misguide him. Whomever Allah leads astray, there is none to guide him. I testify there is no God but Allah alone, without any partners, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.” Then, he would add to his statement with three verses from the Book of Allah, “O believers! Fear Allah in the way He deserves, and do not die except in as Muslims,” (3:102) and, “Fear Allah, in Whose Name you appeal to one another, and honor family ties. Surely, Allah is ever Watchful over you,” (4:1) and, “Fear Allah and say what is right. He will bless your deeds for you, and forgive your sins. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has truly achieved a great triumph.” (33:70-71)
q: All greetings, prayers, and good things are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I testify there is no God but Allah, and I testify Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. … All praise is due to Allah. We praise him, we seek His help, we seek His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Allah from the evil within ourselves and our evil deeds. Whomever Allah guides, there is none to misguide him. Whomever Allah leads astray, there is none to guide him. I testify there is no God but Allah alone, without any partners, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger … O believers! Fear Allah in the way He deserves, and do not die except in as Muslims, … Fear Allah, in Whose Name you appeal to one another, and honor family ties. Surely, Allah is ever Watchful over you … Fear Allah and say what is right. He will bless your deeds for you, and forgive your sins. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has truly achieved a great triumph.

title: Hadith on Dua: Allah affirms truthfulness of their supplications
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever says, ‘There is no God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest,’ his Lord affirms his truthfulness. Allah says, ‘There is no God but Me, and I am the greatest.’ When he says, ‘There is no God but Allah alone,’ Allah says, ‘There is no God but Me alone.’ When he says, ‘There is no God but Allah alone, without any partners,’ Allah says, ‘There is no God but Me alone, and I have no partners.’ When he says, ‘There is no God but Allah, to whom belongs the dominion and all praise,’ Allah says, ‘There is no God but Me alone, to Me belongs the dominion and all praise.’ When he says, ‘There is no God but Allah, and there is no power or might but in Allah,’ Allah says, ‘There is no God but Me, and there is no power or might but in Me.’ Whoever says them in his illness and then dies, he will never be consumed by the Hellfire.”
q: Whoever says, ‘There is no God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest,’ his Lord affirms his truthfulness. Allah says, ‘There is no God but Me, and I am the greatest.’ When he says, ‘There is no God but Allah alone,’ Allah says, ‘There is no God but Me alone.’ When he says, ‘There is no God but Allah alone, without any partners,’ Allah says, ‘There is no God but Me alone, and I have no partners.’ When he says, ‘There is no God but Allah, to whom belongs the dominion and all praise,’ Allah says, ‘There is no God but Me alone, to Me belongs the dominion and all praise.’ When he says, ‘There is no God but Allah, and there is no power or might but in Allah,’ Allah says, ‘There is no God but Me, and there is no power or might but in Me.’ Whoever says them in his illness and then dies, he will never be consumed by the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Salat: Parable of one who rushes through prayer
t: Abu ‘Abdillah al-Ash’ari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saw a man who did not complete his bowings and rushed through his prostrations while praying. The Prophet said, “If he were to die in this state, he would have died upon other than the way of Muhammad. The parable of one who does not complete his bowings and rushes through his prostrations is that of a starving person, who eats only a morsel or two that does not suffice him at all.”
q: If he were to die in this state, he would have died upon other than the way of Muhammad. The parable of one who does not complete his bowings and rushes through his prostrations is that of a starving person, who eats only a morsel or two that does not suffice him at all.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Quran: The Book of Allah is His feast, so take it
t: Abu al-Ahwas reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, this Quran is the banquet of Allah, so take as much of it as you can, for I do not know of anything more bereft of good than a house in which there is nothing from the Book of Allah. Verily, the heart which does not contain anything from the Book of Allah is ruined, like a dilapidated house in which no one lives.”

title: Hadith on Qabr: Animals hear punishment of people in the grave
t: Abdullah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the dead are surely punished in their graves, such that even the beasts can hear their cries.”
q: Verily, the dead are surely punished in their graves, such that even the beasts can hear their cries

title: Talq on Taqwa: Godfearing righteousness is to obey Allah by His light
t: Bakr ibn Abdullah reported: Talq ibn Habib, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Godfearing righteousness is to act in obedience to Allah upon a light from Allah, hoping in the mercy of Allah. Godfearing righteousness is to abandon disobedience to Allah upon a light from Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah.”

title: Hadith on Adhan: Responding to come to prayer, come to salvation
t: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir reported: Some of our brethren narrated to me that when the caller to prayer says, “Come to the prayer,” one says, “There is no movement or might but in Allah.” Mu’awiyah said, “I heard it said likewise by your Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.”
q: There is no movement or might but in Allah

title: Hadith on Adhan: Sunan of responding to the call to prayer
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the caller to prayer says, ‘Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest,’ then let one of you say, ‘Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest.’ Then he says, ‘I testify there is no God but Allah,’ one says, ‘I testify there is no God but Allah.’ Then he says, ‘I testify Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,’ one says, ‘I testify Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.’ Then he says, ‘Come to prayer,’ one says, ‘There is no movement or might but in Allah.’ Then he says, ‘Come to salvation,’ one says, ‘There is no movement or might but in Allah.’ Then he says, ‘Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest,’ one says, ‘Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest.’ Then he says, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ one says, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ from his heart and he will enter Paradise.”
q: When the caller to prayer says, ‘Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest,’ then let one of you say, ‘Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest.’ Then he says, ‘I testify there is no God but Allah,’ one says, ‘I testify there is no God but Allah.’ Then he says, ‘I testify Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,’ one says, ‘I testify Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.’ Then he says, ‘Come to prayer,’ one says, ‘There is no movement or might but in Allah.’ Then he says, ‘Come to salvation,’ one says, ‘There is no movement or might but in Allah.’ Then he says, ‘Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest,’ one says, ‘Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest.’ Then he says, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ one says, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ from his heart and he will enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Dua: Seek refuge in Allah from darkness as it settles
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, looked at the moon and he said, “O Aisha, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, for this is ‘the darkness when it settles.’” (113:3)
q: O Aisha, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, for this is ‘the darkness when it settles.’

title: Hadith on Salat: Recite al-Falaq and al-Nas after prayer
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded me to recite the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and al-Nas, at the end of every prayer.

title: Hadith on Dua: A man calls upon Allah by His greatest name
t: Anas reported: He was sitting with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while a man was praying, and then he supplicated, “O Allah, I ask You by virtue of all praise belonging to You. There is no God but You, the Beneficent, the Originator of the heavens and the earth. O Majestic and Generous, O Living, O Sustainer!” The Prophet said, “He has called upon Allah by His greatest name, by which He will answer when called and give when asked.”
q: He has called upon Allah by His greatest name, by which He will answer when called and give when asked.

title: Hadith on Quran: Earth testifies to what people did on its surface
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, recited this verse, “On that day the earth will tell its stories,” (99:4) and he said, “Do you know what are its stories?” They said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Prophet said, “Verily, its stories are that it will bear witness against every servant and maidservant to what they did on its surface, saying this person did such on such day. These are its stories.”
q: On that day the earth will tell its stories … Do you know what are its stories? … Verily, its stories are that it will bear witness against every servant and maidservant to what they did on its surface, saying this person did such on such day. These are its stories.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Plant your trees in Paradise with remembrance
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Increase your plantings in Paradise, for its water is sweet and its soil is clean. Its plantings are to say: there is no movement or might but in Allah.”
q: Increase your plantings in Paradise, for its water is sweet and its soil is clean. Its plantings are to say: there is no movement or might but in Allah.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Burdens are lifted by solitary remembrance of Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Those in solitude have raced ahead, who are absorbed in the remembrance of Allah. Remembrance has lifted their burdens and they will come on the Day of Resurrection weightless.”
q: Those in solitude have raced ahead, who are absorbed in the remembrance of Allah. Remembrance has lifted their burdens and they will come on the Day of Resurrection weightless.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Remember Allah for strength to keep working
t: Ali reported: Fatimah complained about blisters on her hands from working the millstone and she asked for a servant. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you what is better than you ask for? When both of you lay down to sleep, exalt Allah thirty-four times, glorify Allah thirty-three times, and praise Allah thirty-three times. This is better for you both than a servant.”
