q: Shall I not tell you what is better than you ask for? When both of you lay down to sleep, exalt Allah thirty-four times, glorify Allah thirty-three times, and praise Allah thirty-three times. This is better for you both than a servant.

title: Hadith on Manasik: Rites of Hajj are only to remember Allah
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, stoning the pillar and running between Al-Safa and Al-Marwah is only to establish the remembrance of Allah.”
q: Verily, stoning the pillar and running between Al-Safa and Al-Marwah is only to establish the remembrance of Allah.

title: Ibn Abbas on Dhikr: Remembrance of Allah is the greatest deed
t: ‘Antarah reported: I asked Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, “Which deed is best?” Ibn Abbas said, “The remembrance of Allah is greatest, (29:45). No people sit in a house, in which they are occupied with the Book of Allah among them and they study it together, except that the angels will shade them in their wings. They will be the guests of Allah as long as they remain there, until they enter into another conversation.”
q: The remembrance of Allah is greatest

title: Abu Darda on Dhikr: Those who remember Allah enter Paradise laughing
t: Jubary ibn Nufayr reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, one who keeps his tongue moist with the remembrance of Allah Almighty, those will enter Paradise laughing.”

title: Hadith on Akhirah: The Prophet’s astonishing dream of the Hereafter
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Samurah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us and he said, “Verily, I saw something wondrous last night. I saw a man of my nation as angels were holding him back, and his ablution came to save him from that. I saw a man of my nation surrounded by devils, and the remembrance of Allah came to free him from them. I saw a man of my nation suffering from extreme thirst, and his fasting in Ramadan came to give him drink. I saw a man of my nation with darkness before him, darkness behind him, darkness to his right, darkness to his left, darkness above him, and darkness below him, and his pilgrimages came to bring him out of darkness. I saw a man of my nation to whom the angel of death came to take his soul, and his righteousness to his parents came and turned the angel back. I saw a man of my nation to whom the believers would not speak, and his maintenance of family ties came and it said, ‘Verily, he is one who has maintained family ties, so speak to him,’ and he became one of them. I saw a man of my nation come to people sitting in circles and every circle he came to drove him away, and his ritual bath from major impurity led him by the hand and seated him next to them. I saw a man of my nation shielding his face from the heat of the Hellfire, and his charity came to give him shade and cover his face. I saw a man of my nation to whom the angels of punishment came, and his enjoining good and forbidding evil came to save him from that. I saw a man of my nation falling into the Hellfire, and the tears which he shed for reverence of Allah came to pull him out of the Fire. I saw a man of my nation whose scroll fell into his left hand, and his fear of Allah came to place his scroll in his right hand. I saw a man of my nation swaying in the wind like a palm tree, and his good thoughts of Allah came to calm his shaking. I saw a man of my nation crawling across the bridge over Hell, at times kneeling, at times clinging to it, and his blessings over me came to take him by the hand and stand him up upon the bridge until he passed over it. I saw a man of my nation who was stopped at the gates of Paradise and every gate was locked for him, and his testimony that there is no God but Allah came to take him by the hand and lead him into Paradise.”
q: Verily, I saw something wondrous last night. I saw a man of my nation as angels were holding him back, and his ablution came to save him from that. I saw a man of my nation surrounded by devils, and the remembrance of Allah came to free him from them. I saw a man of my nation suffering from extreme thirst, and his fasting in Ramadan came to give him drink. I saw a man of my nation with darkness before him, darkness behind him, darkness to his right, darkness to his left, darkness above him, and darkness below him, and his pilgrimages came to bring him out of darkness. I saw a man of my nation to whom the angel of death came to take his soul, and his righteousness to his parents came and turned the angel back. I saw a man of my nation to whom the believers would not speak, and his maintenance of family ties came and it said, ‘Verily, he is one who has maintained family ties, so speak to him,’ and he became one of them. I saw a man of my nation come to people sitting in circles and every circle he came to drove him away, and his ritual bath from major impurity led him by the hand and seated him next to them. I saw a man of my nation shielding his face from the heat of the Hellfire, and his charity came to give him shade and cover his face. I saw a man of my nation to whom the angels of punishment came, and his enjoining good and forbidding evil came to save him from that. I saw a man of my nation falling into the Hellfire, and the tears which he shed for reverence of Allah came to pull him out of the Fire. I saw a man of my nation whose scroll fell into his left hand, and his fear of Allah came to place his scroll in his right hand. I saw a man of my nation swaying in the wind like a palm tree, and his good thoughts of Allah came to calm his shaking. I saw a man of my nation crawling across the bridge over Hell, at times kneeling, at times clinging to it, and his blessings over me came to take him by the hand and stand him up upon the bridge until he passed over it. I saw a man of my nation who was stopped at the gates of Paradise and every gate was locked for him, and his testimony that there is no God but Allah came to take him by the hand and lead him into Paradise.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Ibn Taymiyyah

title: Hadith on Dhikr: If good deeds are too difficult, remember Allah often
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is too weak among you to pray at night that he might fall down, too miserly with his wealth that he might spend it, or too fearful of the enemy that he might fight them, then let him remember Allah often.”
q: Whoever is too weak among you to pray at night that he might fall down, too miserly with his wealth that he might spend it, or too fearful of the enemy that he might fight them, then let him remember Allah often.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Dhikr: Remembrance over spending in Jihad
t: Hilal ibn Yasaf reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “That I declare the glory of Allah many times is more beloved to me than spending the same number of coins in the cause of Allah.”

title: Abu Muslim on Dhikr: Remembrance is the cure for madness
t: Abu Muslim al-Khawlani reported: A man came to him and he said, “Instruct me, O Abu Muslim.” Abu Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Remember Allah under every tree and hillside.” The man said, “Tell me more.” Abu Muslim said, “Remember Allah until people think you have gone mad with the remembrance of Allah.” Abu Muslim used to frequently mention Allah. A man saw him mentioning Allah and he said, “Has this companion of yours gone mad?” Abu Muslim heard him and he said, “This is not madness, O son of my brother, rather this is the cure for madness.”

title: Hudhayl on Dhikr: Mention Allah at all times, except in the bathroom
t: Abu Sinan reported: Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, Allah loves to be remembered in the market, and He loves to be mentioned in every circumstance except when relieving oneself.”

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Angels send mercy, calm upon remembrance
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No people gather to remember Allah Almighty but that the angels surround them, cover them with mercy, send tranquility upon them, and Allah mentions them to those with Him.”
q: No people gather to remember Allah Almighty but that the angels surround them, cover them with mercy, send tranquility upon them, and Allah mentions them to those with Him

title: Hadith on Dhikr: The spoils of remembrance is Paradise
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what are the spoils of gathering to remember Allah?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The spoils of the gatherings of remembrance is Paradise.”
q: The spoils of the gatherings of remembrance is Paradise.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Angels declare forgiveness for circles of remembrance
t: Sahl ibn Hanzalah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No people sit together to remember Allah Almighty and stand to leave until a heavenly caller says to them: Stand and your sins are forgiven by Allah! Your bad deeds have been replaced with good deeds!”
q: No people sit together to remember Allah Almighty and stand to leave until a heavenly caller says to them: Stand and your sins are forgiven by Allah! Your bad deeds have been replaced with good deeds!
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for entering the marketplace
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever enters the market and he says, ‘There is no God but Allah, alone without any partners. To Him belong the dominion and all praise, He causes life and death. He lives and does not die, all good is in His hand, and He is powerful over all things,’ Allah will record for him thousands of good deeds, erase thousands of bad deeds, and raise him by thousands of degrees.”
q: Whoever enters the market and he says, ‘There is no God but Allah, alone without any partners. To Him belong the dominion and all praise, He causes life and death. He lives and does not die, all good is in His hand, and He is powerful over all things,’ Allah will record for him thousands of good deeds, erase thousands of bad deeds, and raise him by thousands of degrees.

title: Hadith on Quran: Allah’s words better than all other speech
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The superiority of the words of Allah over all other words is like the superiority of Allah over His creation.”
q: The superiority of the words of Allah over all other words is like the superiority of Allah over His creation.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Remembrance of Allah by the Throne
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among what you mention of the majesty of Allah, His glorification, declaration of His oneness, and His praise circle around the Throne, buzzing like bees in reminder of who said them. Would one of you not like to have or continue to be remembered this way?”
q: Verily, among what you mention of the majesty of Allah, His glorification, declaration of His oneness, and His praise circle around the Throne, buzzing like bees in reminder of who said them. Would one of you not like to have or continue to be remembered this way?

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Their only regret is not remembering Allah more
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people of Paradise will have no regrets, except for moments that passed by them in which they did not remember Allah.”
q: The people of Paradise will have no regrets, except for moments that passed by them in which they did not remember Allah.

title: Wahb on Khalil: Ibrahim was Allah’s best friend for his humility
t: Wahb ibn Munabbih reported: I read in some of the books revealed from heaven, “Verily, Allah Almighty said to Abraham, upon him be peace: Do you know why I have taken you as an intimate friend? Ibrahim said: No, O Lord. Allah said: For your humility in standing before Me in prayer.”

title: Yusuf on Khalil: Ibrahim was Allah’s best friend for his generosity
t: Tahir reported: Yusuf ibn Asbat, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It reached me that Allah Almighty revealed to Abraham, upon him be peace: Do you know why I have taken you as an intimate friend? It is because you give to people and take nothing in return.”

title: Hadith on Anger: Real strength is one who can control his anger
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whom do you consider to be a fighter among you?” We said, “One whom men cannot wrestle down.” The Prophet said, “It is not so. Rather, it is one who controls himself when angry.”
q: Whom do you consider to be a fighter among you? … It is not so. Rather, it is one who controls himself when angry.

title: Hadith on Istighfar: The Prophet supplicates for Allah’s forgiveness
t: Abu Musa al-Ash’ari reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to supplicate with these words, “O Allah, forgive my faults, my ignorance, and my excesses in my affairs, for You know better than me. O Allah, forgive my serious and frivolous errors, whether mistakenly or deliberately, for all of that is within me. O Allah, forgive me for what I have done and what I will do, privately and publicly, for You know better than me. You are the First, You are the Last, and You have power over all things.”
q: O Allah, forgive my faults, my ignorance, and my excesses in my affairs, for You know better than me. O Allah, forgive my serious and frivolous errors, whether mistakenly or deliberately, for all of that is within me. O Allah, forgive me for what I have done and what I will do, privately and publicly, for You know better than me. You are the First, You are the Last, and You have power over all things.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Fudayl on Mercy: A pious man weeps out of pity for the thief
t: Al-Ghazali reported: Al-Fudayl, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I never saw anyone more pious than a man of Khorasan. He was sitting by me at the Sacred Mosque, then he stood to perform circumambulation. Some coins with him were stolen and it made him weep. I said: Is it over some coins you weep? The man said: No, rather I imagined him and myself before Allah Almighty. My mind envisioned the rejection of his excuse, so I wept out of mercy for him.”

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet asks Allah for light in his heart
t: Ibn Abbas reported: He spent the night with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet woke up, cleansed his teeth, performed ablution, the call to prayer was announced, and he went out for the prayer while he was saying, “O Allah, place light in my heart and light on my tongue. Place light in my hearing and light in my seeing. Place light behind me and light in front of me. Place light above me and light below me. O Allah, grant me light!”
q: O Allah, place light in my heart and light on my tongue. Place light in my hearing and light in my seeing. Place light behind me and light in front of me. Place light above me and light below me. O Allah, grant me light!
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet seeks refuge at the end of prayer
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to seek refuge from these at the end of prayer, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from cowardice. I seek refuge in You from returning to the feebleness of old age. I seek refuge in You from the trials of the world, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from cowardice. I seek refuge in You from returning to the feebleness of old age. I seek refuge in You from the trials of the world, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave.

title: Hadith on Yahya: John’s five commands to the Children of Israel
t:
Al-Harith ibn al-Ash’ari reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah commanded John, the son of Zechariah, with five words to practice and to command the Children of Israel to practice. He was nearly slow to act, so Jesus said: Verily, Allah has commanded you with five words to practice and to command the Children of Israel to practice, either command them or I will. John said: I am afraid if you precede me with them, I will be swallowed by the earth or punished! So he gathered the people in the sacred house and the mosque filled as they sat upon the balcony. John said: Verily, Allah has commanded me with five words for me to practice and I command you to practice them. First, that you worship Allah without associating any partners with Him, for the parable of one who associates with Allah is that of a man who purchases a servant with his own gold or currency and he says, ‘This is my house and this is my business, so get to work and send me the profits.’ The servant gets to work, but he gives the profits to another master. Which of you would be pleased to have a servant like that? Second, Allah commands you to pray. If you pray, then do not fidget, for Allah set His face towards His servant in his prayer as long as he does not fidget. Third, I command you to fast, for the parable of that is a man amongst others with a satchel of musk. All of them are pleased and enjoy its scent, for the scent of a fasting person is more pleasant to Allah than musk. Fourth, I command you to give charity, for the parable of that is a man whose enemy has captured him and tied his hands to his neck. As they approach to strike his neck, he says, ‘I will ransom myself for a little or a lot!’ So he ransoms himself from them. Fifth, I command you to remember Allah, for the parable of that is a man who goes out with his enemy quickly following his steps, until he comes to a protected fortress and barricades himself from them. Such a servant cannot barricade himself from Satan but by remembering Allah.”

The Prophet said, “And I command you with five words with which Allah commanded me: to listen, to obey, to perform jihad, to perform emigration, and to unite with the community. For whoever splits away from the community as much as a hand span has cast off the yoke of Islam from his neck until he returns. Whoever calls to the ways of ignorance will surely be among the rubble of Hell.” A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, even if he prays and fasts?” The Prophet said, “Even if he prays and fasts, so call to the ways of Allah who has named you the Muslims, the believers, the servants of Allah.”
q: Verily, Allah commanded John, the son of Zechariah, with five words to practice and to command the Children of Israel to practice. He was nearly slow to act, so Jesus said: Verily, Allah has commanded you with five words to practice and to command the Children of Israel to practice, either command them or I will. John said: I am afraid if you precede me with them, I will be swallowed by the earth or punished! So he gathered the people in the sacred house and the mosque filled as they sat upon the balcony. John said: Verily, Allah has commanded me with five words for me to practice and I command you to practice them. First, that you worship Allah without associating any partners with Him, for the parable of one who associates with Allah is that of a man who purchases a servant with his own gold or currency and he says, ‘This is my house and this is my business, so get to work and send me the profits.’ The servant gets to work, but he gives the profits to another master. Which of you would be pleased to have a servant like that? Second, Allah commands you to pray. If you pray, then do not fidget, for Allah set His face towards His servant in his prayer as long as he does not fidget. Third, I command you to fast, for the parable of that is a man amongst others with a satchel of musk. All of them are pleased and enjoy its scent, for the scent of a fasting person is more pleasant to Allah than musk. Fourth, I command you to give charity, for the parable of that is a man whose enemy has captured him and tied his hands to his neck. As they approach to strike his neck, he says, ‘I will ransom myself for a little or a lot!’ So he ransoms himself from them. Fifth, I command you to remember Allah, for the parable of that is a man who goes out with his enemy quickly following his steps, until he comes to a protected fortress and barricades himself from them. Such a servant cannot barricade himself from Satan but by remembering Allah. … And I command you with five words with which Allah commanded me: to listen, to obey, to perform jihad, to perform emigration, and to unite with the community. For whoever splits away from the community as much as a hand span has cast off the yoke of Islam from his neck until he returns. Whoever calls to the ways of ignorance will surely be among the rubble of Hell. … Even if he prays and fasts, so call to the ways of Allah who has named you the Muslims, the believers, the servants of Allah.

title: Hadith on Negligence: Satan steals from an unmindful prayer
t: Aisha reported: I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about fidgeting in the prayer. The Prophet said, “It is theft by which Satan steals from the prayer of a servant.”
q: It is theft by which Satan steals from the prayer of a servant.

title: Hadith on Restraint: Controlling speech, anger, and apologizing
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever restrains his tongue, Allah Almighty will cover his faults. Whoever controls his anger, Allah Almighty will protect him from His punishment. Whoever apologizes to Allah Almighty, He will accept his apology.”
q: Whoever restrains his tongue, Allah Almighty will cover his faults. Whoever controls his anger, Allah Almighty will protect him from His punishment. Whoever apologizes to Allah Almighty, He will accept his apology.

title: Hadith on Dua: Take refuge in Allah from an evil heart
t: Shakal ibn Humayd reported: I came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me a prayer for refuge that I may say.” The Prophet took hold of my shoulder, saying, “Say: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing, from the evil of my seeing, from the evil of my tongue, from the evil in my heart, and from the evil of my seed,” meaning his passions.
q: Say: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing, from the evil of my seeing, from the evil of my tongue, from the evil in my heart, and from the evil of my seed,

title: Hadith on Dua: Ending a supplication with Ameen
t: Abu Zuhayr reported: We went out one night with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and a man came to us who was earnestly supplicating to Allah for some matter. The Prophet stopped and listened to him, then he said, “It must be so if he seals it.” A man among the people said, “With what does he seal it?” The Prophet said, “Amin, for if he ends it with amin, it will be so.” The man who questioned the Prophet departed and came to the other man and he said, “Seal it with amin, O sir, and rejoice!”
q: It must be so if he seals it. … Amin, for if he ends it with amin, it will be so.

title: Hadith on Dua: Seeking refuge from harmful things
t: Abu al-Yasar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to supplicate, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from being crushed under rubble. I seek refuge in You from falling into an abyss. I seek refuge in You from drowning, burning, and senility. I seek refuge in You from Satan striking me at the time of death. I seek refuge in You from dying in Your path while retreating. I seek refuge in You from dying by a poisonous sting.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from being crushed under rubble. I seek refuge in You from falling into an abyss. I seek refuge in You from drowning, burning, and senility. I seek refuge in You from Satan striking me at the time of death. I seek refuge in You from dying in Your path while retreating. I seek refuge in You from dying by a poisonous sting.

title: Hadith on Qadr: I ask for Your every decree to be good
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, taught her among the comprehensive supplications, “O Allah, I ask You for Your every decree upon me to be good.”
q: O Allah, I ask You for Your every decree upon me to be good.

title: Hadith on Anger: Ibn Umar asks the Prophet for pithy advice
t: Ibn Umar reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, give me a word and make it short that I might understand it.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not be angry.” I repeated my question twice and each time the Prophet responded, “Do not be angry.”
q: Do not be angry. … Do not be angry.

title: Hadith on Salat: The prayer responds to good or poor performance
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a man prays, performs ablution well, and perfects its bowing and prostration, the prayer says: May Allah preserve you as you have preserved me! When he performs his bowing poorly, neither perfecting its bowing nor its prostration, the prayer says: May Allah waste you as you have wasted me!”
q: When a man prays, performs ablution well, and perfects its bowing and prostration, … the prayer says: May Allah preserve you as you have preserved me! When he performs his bowing poorly, neither perfecting its bowing nor its prostration, the prayer says: May Allah waste you as you have wasted me!

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet’s daily instruction for Fatimah
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Fatimah, “I instruct you to say in the morning and evening: O Living, O Sustainer, by Your mercy I seek deliverance. Take care of all my affairs and do not leave me to the care of myself even for the blink of an eye.”
q: I instruct you to say in the morning and evening: O Living, O Sustainer, by Your mercy I seek deliverance. Take care of all my affairs and do not leave me to the care of myself even for the blink of an eye.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Tawbah: Two verses to seek forgiveness from Allah
t: ‘Alqamah reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, there are two verses in the Book of Allah, never does a servant commit a sin, recite them both, and seek forgiveness from Allah but that Allah will forgive him. His saying: Those who, if they behave obscenely or wrong themselves, they remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins. Who forgives sins besides Allah? (3:135), and His saying: Whoever does an evil deed or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness from Allah, he will surely find Allah to be forgiving and merciful.” (4:110)
q: Those who, if they behave obscenely or wrong themselves, they remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins. Who forgives sins besides Allah? … Whoever does an evil deed or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness from Allah, he will surely find Allah to be forgiving and merciful.
gf: Rijal al-Sahih (narrators are reliable) according to Al-Haythami

title: Hadith on Dua: O Allah, make me content with what I have
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to supplicate, “O Allah, make me content with what You have provided for me, bless me in it, and replace everything I do not have with something better.”
q: O Allah, make me content with what You have provided for me, bless me in it, and replace everything I do not have with something better.

title: Hadith on Speech: All words recorded against people except good
t: Umm Habibah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Every word of the son of Adam is against him, not for him, except for enjoining good, forbidding evil, or the remembrance of Allah.”
q: Every word of the son of Adam is against him, not for him, except for enjoining good, forbidding evil, or the remembrance of Allah.”

title: Hadith on Hope: Be ambitious in supplication, ask for best things
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you calls upon Allah, let him hope for the greatest of things. Verily, nothing has any greatness over Allah.”
q: When one of you calls upon Allah, let him hope for the greatest of things. Verily, nothing has any greatness over Allah.

title: Hadith on Dua: Best worship to wait patiently for relief
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Ask Allah for His favor as Allah Almighty loves to be asked. Among the best acts of worship is to patiently wait in expectation of relief.”
q: Ask Allah for His favor as Allah Almighty loves to be asked. Among the best acts of worship is to patiently wait in expectation of relief.

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication is the essence of worship
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Supplication is the essence of worship.”
q: Supplication is the essence of worship.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Funerals: The Prophet respectfully buries a hypocrite
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to the hypocrite Abdullah ibn ‘Ubayy after he was placed in his grave. The Prophet ordered him to be taken out, he placed him on his knees, he blew his blessed breath over him, and he wrapped him in his own shirt. And Allah knows best.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet supplicates and asks three times
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when he would supplicate, he would supplicate three times, and when he would ask Allah, he would ask three times.

title: Abu Dharr on Dua: Supplication needs good deeds like food needs salt
t: Bakr al-Muzanni reported: Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Supplication is in need of enough righteousness as food is in need of enough salt.”

title: ‘Ata’ on Anger: Terrible consequences for a careless angry word
t: Ibn Rajab reported: ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, a man might speak a word in anger by which his good deeds of sixty or seventy years are destroyed.”

title: Sufyan on Hearts: Time will come when dead hearts are in live bodies
t: Al-Harith ibn Mansur reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A time will come to people in which the hearts are dead even as the bodies are alive.”

title: Hadith on Hereafter: All enter Paradise but those who stray like camels
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will all surely enter Paradise except one who refuses and wanders away from Allah like a stray camel.” It was said, “Who would refuse to enter Paradise?” The Prophet said, “Whoever obeys me will enter Paradise, and whoever disobeys me will enter Hellfire.”
q: By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will all surely enter Paradise except one who refuses and wanders away from Allah like a stray camel. … Whoever obeys me will enter Paradise, and whoever disobeys me will enter Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Independence: The Prophet orders Abu Bakr not to ask people
t: Ibn Abi Mulaykah reported: Abu Bakr the truthful, may Allah be pleased with him, might drop the rein from his hand, so he would strike the leg of his camel to make it kneel and he would pick it up. They said to him, “Why did you not order us to take care of it?” Abu Bakr said, “My beloved Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded me not to ask people for anything.”
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Bunan on Greed: True freedom is contentment, greed is slavery
t: Al-Zubayr ibn Abdul Wahid reported: Abu al-Hasan Bunan, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The freeman is a slave as long as he is greedy, and the slave is free as long as he is content.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Be certain with mindfulness that Allah will answer
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The hearts are vessels and some have greater capacity than others. When you ask from Allah Almighty, O people, then ask Him while you are convinced He will answer. Verily, Allah does not answer the supplication of a servant from behind an unmindful heart.”
q: The hearts are vessels and some have greater capacity than others. When you ask from Allah Almighty, O people, then ask Him while you are convinced He will answer. Verily, Allah does not answer the supplication of a servant from behind an unmindful heart.

title: Umar on Greed: Greed is poverty and slavery to materialism
t: ‘Urwah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, would say in his sermons, “You know that greed is poverty and renunciation is independence. Verily, whoever renounces his desire for what people have, he will be independent of them.”

title: Hadith on Masajid: Mosques are the home of every righteous person
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The mosque is the home of every righteous person. Allah Almighty has guaranteed those who have their home in the mosques with the spirit, mercy, and safe passage over the bridge of Hell unto the pleasure of Allah Almighty.”
q: The mosque is the home of every righteous person. Allah Almighty has guaranteed those who have their home in the mosques with the spirit, mercy, and safe passage over the bridge of Hell unto the pleasure of Allah Almighty.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Angels praise gatherings to remember Allah
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No people gather to remember Allah, only desiring by that His countenance, except that it will be announced for them in the heavens: Stand forgiven! Your bad deeds have been replaced with good deeds!”
q: No people gather to remember Allah, only desiring by that His countenance, except that it will be announced for them in the heavens: Stand forgiven! Your bad deeds have been replaced with good deeds!
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Death: Best deed to die while remembering Allah
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among which deeds are most beloved to Allah?” The Prophet said, “That you die while your tongue is moist with the remembrance of Allah.”
q: That you die while your tongue is moist with the remembrance of Allah.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Allah with one mentioning Him verbally
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty says: I am with My servant while he remembers Me and his two lips are moving for My sake.”
q: Allah Almighty says: I am with My servant while he remembers Me and his two lips are moving for My sake.

title: Ali on Dua: Every supplication to include blessing the Prophet
t: Al-Harith reported: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Every supplication is veiled until one sends blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.”
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Consequences: Three people get what they deserve
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are three persons who will get what they deserve. No servant is wronged, and he withholds retaliation for the sake of Allah Almighty, but that Allah will strengthen him with His support. A man does not open the door of charity to strengthen family ties, but that Allah will increase his wealth. And a man does not open the door of begging to usurp wealth but that Allah will increase his poverty.”
q: There are three persons who will get what they deserve. No servant is wronged, and he withholds retaliation for the sake of Allah Almighty, but that Allah will strengthen him with His support. A man does not open the door of charity to strengthen family ties, but that Allah will increase his wealth. And a man does not open the door of begging to usurp wealth but that Allah will increase his poverty.

title: Hadith on ‘Ujb: The Prophet fears self-admiration for Muslims
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Were you not to sin, I would fear for you what is even worse: vanity.”
q: Were you not to sin, I would fear for you what is even worse: vanity.

title: Aisha on Arrogance: When does a man become a villain?
t: Al-Muhasibi reported: It was said to Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, “When does a man become villainous?” Aisha said, “When he thinks of himself as virtuous.”

title: Umar II on Frugality: Moderation in abundance, forgiveness in strength
t: Sa’id ibn Suwayd reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The best frugality is at a time of abundance, and the best forgiveness is at a time of power.”

title: Ibn Umar on Humility: Ibn Umar eats with lepers and outcasts
t: Abu Bakr ibn Hafs reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, while travelling between Mecca and Medina would not withhold his food from a leper, nor an outcast, nor anyone afflicted, even letting them sit with him at his table.

title: Umar II on Humility: Best Muslims are humble with Allah
t: Al-Ghazali reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The best people are those who are humble before Allah.”

title: Hadith on Arrogance: The Prophet seeks refuge from Satan’s pride
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the accursed Satan, his madness, his pride, and his poetry.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the accursed Satan, his madness, his pride, and his poetry

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Taqwa: Sinful to show anger when told to fear Allah
t: Zayd ibn Wahb reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “It is enough sin for a man to get angry when he is told to fear Allah.”
gf: Rijal al-Sahih (narrators are reliable) according to Al-Haythami

title: Hadith on Arrogance: Tyrants are trampled on the Day of Resurrection
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The arrogant and the tyrants will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection as tiny particles. The people will trample upon them due to their disgrace before Allah Almighty.”
q: The arrogant and the tyrants will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection as tiny particles. The people will trample upon them due to their disgrace before Allah Almighty.

title: Hadith on Nuh: Noah’s commands on his deathbed
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When death approached Noah, upon him be peace, he called his sons and he said: Verily, my time is short and you must receive instruction. I command you with two and prohibit you with two. I forbid you from committing idolatry and being arrogant. I command you to declare there is no God but Allah, for if the heavens and the earth and everything between them were placed on one side of the scale and the declaration of no God but Allah were placed on the other, it would surely outweigh it. Were the heavens and the earth a ring of solid iron and the declaration of no God but Allah was placed upon it, it would shatter them to pieces. I command you to declare the glory of Allah and His praises, for it is the prayer of all things, and by it all things are given provision.”
q: When death approached Noah, upon him be peace, he called his sons and he said: Verily, my time is short and you must receive instruction. I command you with two and prohibit you with two. I forbid you from committing idolatry and being arrogant. I command you to declare there is no God but Allah, for if the heavens and the earth and everything between them were placed on one side of the scale and the declaration of no God but Allah were placed on the other, it would surely outweigh it. Were the heavens and the earth a ring of solid iron and the declaration of no God but Allah was placed upon it, it would shatter them to pieces. I command you to declare the glory of Allah and His praises, for it is the prayer of all things, and by it all things are given provision.

title: Hadith on Hell: The Fire declares its ownership of tyrants and idolaters
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A neck will emerge from the Hellfire on the Day of Resurrection, with two eyes to see, two ears to hear, and a tongue to speak. It will say: Verily, I am in charge of three persons, every stubborn tyrant, everyone who called upon another god alongside Allah, and every maker of images.”
q: A neck will emerge from the Hellfire on the Day of Resurrection, with two eyes to see, two ears to hear, and a tongue to speak. It will say: Verily, I am in charge of three persons, every stubborn tyrant, everyone who called upon another god alongside Allah, and every maker of images.

title: Hadith on Virtues: Blessed are the humble, charitable, merciful
t: Rakb al-Misri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Blessed is he who has humility without debasing himself, who lowers himself without humiliating himself, who spends wealth in charity and accumulates it without sinning, who is merciful to the lowly and downtrodden, and who accompanies the people of understanding and wisdom.”
q: Blessed is he who has humility without debasing himself, who lowers himself without humiliating himself, who spends wealth in charity and accumulates it without sinning, who is merciful to the lowly and downtrodden, and who accompanies the people of understanding and wisdom.

title: Abu Bakr on Humility: Let no Muslim belittle or despise another
t: Al-Ghazali reported: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Let no one look down upon another among the Muslims, for even the smallest of Muslims is great to Allah.”

title: Hasan on Humility: Don’t think you’re better than any other Muslim
t: Salih al-Murri reported: Al-Hasan, Yunus, and Ayyub, may Allah have mercy on them, were outside discussing humility. Al-Hasan said, “Do you know what is humility? Humility is that you leave your house and you do not meet any Muslim but that you view him as better than yourself.”

title: Hasan on Tazkiyyah: Allah commands you to have a pure heart
t: Khalid ibn Abi Bakr reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Cure your heart, for Allah Almighty requires the servants to have sound hearts.”

title: Malik on Akhirah: Biggest loser sells his Hereafter for the world
t: Ibn Wahb reported: Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said to me, “The greatest loser among people is one who sold his Hereafter for his share of the world, and an even greater loser is one who sold his Hereafter for someone else’s share of the world.”

title: Umar on Sermons: Umar warns against greed, anger, and dishonesty
t: Abu Huraira reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say to people in his sermons, “Those among you have succeeded who are protected from whims, greed, and anger. There is no good in anything less than truthful speech.”

title: Abu Yazid on Humility: He is not humble until he lowers his ego
t: Al-Ghazali reported: Abu Yazid, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “As long as a servant thinks there is someone in the creation more evil than himself, he is arrogant.” It was said, “When will he be humble?” Abu Yazid said, “When he views himself as having no special station or status. The humility of every human being is by the measure of his knowledge of his Lord Almighty and knowledge of himself.”

title: Ja’far on Rage: Anger is the key to every evil deed
t: Al-Ghazali reported: Ja’far ibn Muhammad, may Allah be pleased with them both, said, “Anger is the key to every evil.”

title: Hudhayfah on Fitnah: Worst tribulation to not know good or evil
t: ‘Amir reported: Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked, “Which trial is the worst?” Hudhayfah said, “It is when good and evil are before you and you do not know which of them to follow.”

title: Hadith on Sleep: Supplications for waking and going to bed
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you gets up from his bed and then returns to it, let him brush it off with the end of his garment three times, for he does not know what came to it after him. When he lies down, let him say: In the name of my Lord, I lay down my side and by You I make it rise, and if You take my soul, have mercy upon it, and if you release it, grant it protection the same as given to Your righteous servants. When he awakens, let him say: All praise is due to Allah who granted wellness to my body, returned my spirit, and allowed me to remember Him.”
q: When one of you gets up from his bed and then returns to it, let him brush it off with the end of his garment three times, for he does not know what came to it after him. When he lies down, let him say: In the name of my Lord, I lay down my side and by You I make it rise, and if You take my soul, have mercy upon it, and if you release it, grant it protection the same as given to Your righteous servants. When he awakens, let him say: All praise is due to Allah who granted wellness to my body, returned my spirit, and allowed me to remember Him.

title: Hadith on Lisan: Greatest good or evil in a person’s speech
t: ‘Adi ibn Hatim reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The greatest propensity for good or evil in a man lies between his two lips,” meaning his tongue.
q: The greatest propensity for good or evil in a man lies between his two lips

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet’s supplication for entering a new town
t: Ibn Umar reported: We were traveling with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and when he saw a town he wanted to enter, he would say three times, “O Allah, bless us in it. O Allah, provide us with its fruits, make us beloved to its people, and make the righteous of its people beloved to us.”
q: O Allah, bless us in it. O Allah, provide us with its fruits, make us beloved to its people, and make the righteous of its people beloved to us.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: The Prophet rushes to give gold in charity
t: ‘Uqbah ibn al-Harith reported: I prayed the afternoon prayer with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and when he ended by invoking peace, he quickly stood up and entered the house of some of his wives. Then, he came out and he saw wonder on the people’s faces at his haste. The Prophet said, “I remembered while I was praying that we had some gold and I disliked for our evening or night to pass while we still have it, so I ordered it to be distributed.”
q: I remembered while I was praying that we had some gold and I disliked for our evening or night to pass while we still have it, so I ordered it to be distributed.

title: Hadith on Fear: Only God-fearing will overcome the steep path
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, before you is a burdensome path to traverse. No one is saved from it except everyone who fears falling into sin.”
q: Verily, before you is a burdensome path to traverse. No one is saved from it except everyone who fears falling into sin.

title: Hadith on Chastity: The Prophet’s advice for unmarried young men
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O young men of Quraysh, do not commit adultery and guard your chastity. No doubt, whoever guards his chastity will certainly enter Paradise.”
q: O young men of Quraysh, do not commit adultery and guard your chastity. No doubt, whoever guards his chastity will certainly enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Hunger: The Prophet suffers in poverty with his companions
t: Abu Talhah reported: We complained about hunger to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and we lifted our garments to reveal stones tied to our stomachs, so the Messenger of Allah lifted his garment to reveal two stones.

title: Hadith on Faith: Believers are honest, sinners are treacherous
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believer is naively generous, and the wicked one is deceitfully malicious.”
q: The believer is naively generous, and the wicked one is deceitfully malicious.

title: Hadith on Vice: Evil within people lies in greed and cowardice
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The worst evil within a man is his restless greed and his utmost cowardice.”
q: The worst evil within a man is his restless greed and his utmost cowardice.

title: Hadith on Refuge: Gabriel teaches the Prophet to seek refuge
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Khanbash reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Gabriel came to me and he said: O Muhammad, speak! I said: What should I say? Gabriel said: Say, I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created, dispersed, and shaped, from the evil of what descends from the sky, from the evil of what ascends therein, from the evil of trials by night and day, and from the evil of every visitor by night except one who visits for good, O Most Merciful.”
q: Gabriel came to me and he said: O Muhammad, speak! I said: What should I say? Gabriel said: Say, I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created, dispersed, and shaped, from the evil of what descends from the sky, from the evil of what ascends therein, from the evil of trials by night and day, and from the evil of every visitor by night except one who visits for good, O Most Merciful.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Give whatever you can in charity, even small
t: Umm Bujayd reported: She said, “O Messenger of Allah, the poor come to my door and I cannot find anything to give them.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you can find nothing but a burnt trotter, hand it over to them.”
q: If you can find nothing but a burnt trotter, hand it over to them.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Best charity is given when little is available
t: Abu Huraira reported: He said, “O Messenger of Allah, which charity is best?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One with little property to give. Begin with your dependents.”
q: One with little property to give. Begin with your dependents.

title: Hadith on Haram: Unlawful wealth not accepted as charity
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever accumulates unlawful wealth and then gives it in charity, he will never be rewarded and the burden of sin will be upon him.”
q: Whoever accumulates unlawful wealth and then gives it in charity, he will never be rewarded and the burden of sin will be upon him

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Blameworthy to give low-quality charity
t: ‘Awf ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to us in the mosque and he had a staff in his hand. A man among us had hung a bundle of brittle dates, so the Prophet started striking that bundle with his staff and he said, “If he wished he could have given better charity than this. Verily, the one who gave this in charity will eat brittle dates on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: If he wished he could have given better charity than this. Verily, the one who gave this in charity will eat brittle dates on the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Charity shades believers on Judgment Day
t: Marthad ibn Abdullah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The shade of the believer on the Day of Resurrection is his charity.”
q: The shade of the believer on the Day of Resurrection is his charity.

title: Hadith on Tyranny: The Prophet disowns evil rulers, their supporters
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah, I seek refuge in Allah on your behalf from the leadership of fools, for they will become rulers. Whoever has an audience before them, supports them in their wrongdoing, and affirms their lies, then he is not part of me and I am not part of him. He will never meet me at the Fountain. Whoever does not have an audience before them, does not support them in their wrongdoing, and does not affirm their lies, then he is part of me and I am part of him. He will meet me at the Fountain. O Ka’b ibn ‘Urjah, prayer brings one closer to Allah, fasting is a shield, and charity extinguishes sins just as water extinguishes fire.”
q: O Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah, I seek refuge in Allah on your behalf from the leadership of fools, for they will become rulers. Whoever has an audience before them, supports them in their wrongdoing, and affirms their lies, then he is not part of me and I am not part of him. He will never meet me at the Fountain. Whoever does not have an audience before them, does not support them in their wrongdoing, and does not affirm their lies, then he is part of me and I am part of him. He will meet me at the Fountain. O Ka’b ibn ‘Urjah, prayer brings one closer to Allah, fasting is a shield, and charity extinguishes sins just as water extinguishes fire.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Set up a barrier from Hell with charity
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to her, “O Aisha, set up a barrier from the Hellfire, even with half of a date in charity, for it settles the hungry in place of the full.”
q: O Aisha, set up a barrier from the Hellfire, even with half of a date in charity, for it settles the hungry in place of the full.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Guard yourself from Hell, even with small charity
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Let one of you protect his face from the Hellfire, even with half of a date in charity.”
q: Let one of you protect his face from the Hellfire, even with half of a date in charity.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Acts of charity are true wealth in the Hereafter
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Which of you loves the wealth of his heirs more than his own wealth?” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, there are none of us but his own wealth is more beloved to him.” The Prophet said, “Verily, his true wealth is what he puts forward, and the wealth of his heirs is what is left behind.”
q: Which of you loves the wealth of his heirs more than his own wealth? … Verily, his true wealth is what he puts forward, and the wealth of his heirs is what is left behind.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Only charity stored for the Hereafter
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The servant says: My wealth, my wealth! Verily, he only gets three from his wealth: he eats and it perishes, or he wears clothes and they degrade, or he gives in charity and it is stored for him. Whatever is beyond this will depart him and be left behind for people.”
q: The servant says: My wealth, my wealth! Verily, he only gets three from his wealth: he eats and it perishes, or he wears clothes and they degrade, or he gives in charity and it is stored for him. Whatever is beyond this will depart him and be left behind for people.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: All of charity endures in the Hereafter
t: Aisha reported: They slaughtered a sheep and gave in charity from it. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “What remains of it?” Aisha said, “Nothing remains but its shoulder.” The Prophet said, “All of it endures but its shoulder.”
q: What remains of it? … All of it endures but its shoulder.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Allah multiplies charity until it is like a mountain
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah will raise up a date or a morsel in charity, just as one of you raises his mare or his young, until it becomes like the mountain of Uhud.”
q: Verily, Allah will raise up a date or a morsel in charity, just as one of you raises his mare or his young, until it becomes like the mountain of Uhud.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Islam: Which degree of the religion is best?
t: Zirr ibn Hubaysh reported: A man came to Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said, “O Abu Abdur Rahman, which degree of Islam is best?” Ibn Mas’ud said, “Prayer.” The man said, “Then what?” Ibn Mas’ud said, “Charity.” The man said, “Then what?” Ibn Mas’ud said, “Righteousness to parents.”

title: Hadith on Zakat: Eagerness to give charity is sweetness of faith
t: Abdullah ibn Mu’awiyyah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever does three deeds will taste the sweetness of faith: one who worships Allah alone, who declares there is no God but Allah, and who gives charity from his wealth each year with a cheerful and earnest soul.”
q: Whoever does three deeds will taste the sweetness of faith: one who worships Allah alone, who declares there is no God but Allah, and who gives charity from his wealth each year with a cheerful and earnest soul.

title: Ibn Umar on Zakat: Paid charity will never be lost or forgotten
t: Nafi’ reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Every piece of property on which alms is paid, even if it were beneath the seven earths, it will never be buried. Every piece of property on which alms is not paid is buried, even if it were to lie openly on the face of the earth.”

title: Hadith on Zakat: Paying obligatory charity removes his evil
t: Jabir reported: A man among his people said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if a man pays alms on his wealth?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever pays alms on his wealth, his evil will depart from him.”
q: Whoever pays alms on his wealth, his evil will depart from him.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Islam: The religion has eight types of good deeds
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Islam has eight shares: Islam is a share, prayer is a share, charity is a share, Hajj pilgrimage to the House is a share, fasting is a share, enjoining good is a share, forbidding evil is a share, and jihad in the way of Allah is a share. He has failed who has a share of none.”
q: Islam has eight shares: Islam is a share, prayer is a share, charity is a share, Hajj pilgrimage to the House is a share, fasting is a share, enjoining good is a share, forbidding evil is a share, and jihad in the way of Allah is a share. He has failed who has a share of none.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Islam: The Prophet swears upon four truths
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I swear an oath upon three truths. Allah Almighty does not make one with a share in Islam like one without. The shares of Islam are three: prayer, fasting, and charity. Allah Almighty will not take a servant as an ally in this world but entrust him to another on the Day of Resurrection. And a man does not love a people but that Allah will resurrect him with them. The fourth, if I were to swear upon it, I hope it would not be sinful: Allah Almighty does not conceal the sins of a servant in the world but that He will conceal them on the Day of Resurrection”
q: I swear an oath upon three truths. Allah Almighty does not make one with a share in Islam like one without. The shares of Islam are three: prayer, fasting, and charity. Allah Almighty will not take a servant as an ally in this world but entrust him to another on the Day of Resurrection. And a man does not love a people but that Allah will resurrect him with them. The fourth, if I were to swear upon it, I hope it would not be sinful: Allah Almighty does not conceal the sins of a servant in the world but that He will conceal them on the Day of Resurrection

title: Hadith on Tribalism: Two men share lineage, one man goes to Hellfire
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two men shared their lineages in the time of Moses, upon him be peace. One man boasted to the other: I am this person, son of this person, back for nine generations. Who are you? You have no mother? The other man said: I am this person, son of this person, son of Islam. Allah revealed to Moses in regards to these two who shared their lineages: As for you tribalist, you shared lineage back for nine generations in Hellfire and you are the tenth of them. As for you, you shared lineage back for two generations in Paradise and you are the third of them.”
q: Two men shared their lineages in the time of Moses, upon him be peace. One man boasted to the other: I am this person, son of this person, back for nine generations. Who are you? You have no mother? The other man said: I am this person, son of this person, son of Islam. Allah revealed to Moses in regards to these two who shared their lineages: As for you tribalist, you shared lineage back for nine generations in Hellfire and you are the tenth of them. As for you, you shared lineage back for two generations in Paradise and you are the third of them.

title: Hadith on Salat: Every prayer expiates your sins
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, every prayer makes the sins before you fall away.”
q: Verily, every prayer makes the sins before you fall away.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Prayer: Salat removes sins like leaves from a tree
t: Salman al-Farisi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the Muslim prays while his sins hang over his head. Every time he prostrates, some of them drop. When he finishes his prayer, his sins will have fallen away.”
q: Verily, the Muslim prays while his sins hang over his head. Every time he prostrates, some of them drop. When he finishes his prayer, his sins will have fallen away.

title: Hadith on Salat: Five prayers protect believers from the Fire
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You are exposed to fire, you are exposed to fire! If you perform the dawn prayer, it will cleanse you. Then, you are exposed to fire, you are exposed to fire! If you perform the noon prayer, it will cleanse you. Then, you are exposed to fire, you are exposed to fire! If you pray the mid-day prayer, it will cleanse you. Then, you are exposed to fire, you are exposed to fire! If you pray the sunset prayer, it will cleanse you. Then, you are exposed to fire, you are exposed to fire! If you pray the evening prayer, it will cleanse you. Then, when you sleep, nothing will be written against you until you wake up.”
q: You are exposed to fire, you are exposed to fire! If you perform the dawn prayer, it will cleanse you. Then, you are exposed to fire, you are exposed to fire! If you perform the noon prayer, it will cleanse you. Then, you are exposed to fire, you are exposed to fire! If you pray the mid-day prayer, it will cleanse you. Then, you are exposed to fire, you are exposed to fire! If you pray the sunset prayer, it will cleanse you. Then, you are exposed to fire, you are exposed to fire! If you pray the evening prayer, it will cleanse you. Then, when you sleep, nothing will be written against you until you wake up.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Salat: Five prayers expiate filthy sins like rivers
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The five prayers expiate the sins between them. You see that if there were five rivers between a working man’s house and his place of work, he would depart for work as much as Allah willed, covered in dirt or sweat. Every time he passed by a river, it would cleanse him of that stain. Likewise are the prayers. Each time he commits a sin or as much as Allah wills, then performs a prayer for forgiveness, he is forgiven for what came before it.”
q: The five prayers expiate the sins between them. You see that if there were five rivers between a working man’s house and his place of work, he would depart for work as much as Allah willed, covered in dirt or sweat. Every time he passed by a river, it would cleanse him of that stain. Likewise are the prayers. Each time he commits a sin or as much as Allah wills, then performs a prayer for forgiveness, he is forgiven for what came before it.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Adhan: Dua not rejected between Adhan and Iqamah
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the call to prayer is announced, the gates of heaven are opened and the supplication is answered. The supplication between the call to prayer and the commencement is never turned back.”
q: When the call to prayer is announced, the gates of heaven are opened and the supplication is answered. The supplication between the call to prayer and the commencement is never turned back.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Adhan: Supplication for forgiveness after call to prayer
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever says when he hears the call to prayer, ‘I testify there is no God but Allah alone, without any partner, and Muhammad is His servant and His messenger, I am pleased with Allah as a Lord, with Muhammad as a messenger, and with Islam as a religion,’ then his sins will be forgiven.”
q: Whoever says when he hears the call to prayer, ‘I testify there is no God but Allah alone, without any partner, and Muhammad is His servant and His messenger, I am pleased with Allah as a Lord, with Muhammad as a messenger, and with Islam as a religion,’ then his sins will be forgiven.

title: Hadith on Adhan: Call to prayer with conviction rewarded in Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: We were with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when Bilal stood to announce the prayer, then he was silent. The Prophet said, “Whoever says the likes of this with conviction, he will enter Paradise.”
q: Whoever says the likes of this with conviction, he will enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Adhan: Caller to prayer rewarded with those praying
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The caller to prayer is forgiven for as far as his voice reaches, and his reward is similar to those who pray with him.”
q: The caller to prayer is forgiven for as far as his voice reaches, and his reward is similar to those who pray with him.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Salat: Greater rewards for caller, congregational prayers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The caller to prayer is forgiven as far as his voice is heard. Every creature on land or sea will testify for him. Whoever is present at the prayer will have a reward multiplied by twenty five times and his sins will be expiated between two prayers.”
q: The caller to prayer is forgiven as far as his voice is heard. Every creature on land or sea will testify for him. Whoever is present at the prayer will have a reward multiplied by twenty five times and his sins will be expiated between two prayers.

title: Hadith on Adhan: Allah and His creatures forgive callers to prayer
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah forgives the callers to prayer when they end their call, and every creature on land or sea who hears his voice seeks forgiveness for him.”
q: Allah forgives the callers to prayer when they end their call, and every creature on land or sea who hears his voice seeks forgiveness for him.

title: Hadith on Virtue: Be fair, be merciful, and keep your promises
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you judge, be just. When you make a covenant, keep it. When your mercy is sought, be merciful. Whoever does not do any of that, the curse of Allah, His angels, and all people will be upon him.”
q: When you judge, be just. When you make a covenant, keep it. When your mercy is sought, be merciful. Whoever does not do any of that, the curse of Allah, His angels, and all people will be upon him.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Rahma: Inhabitants of heaven not merciful to the unmerciful
t: Jarir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is not merciful to those on the earth, those in the heavens will not be merciful to him.”
q: Whoever is not merciful to those on the earth, those in the heavens will not be merciful to him.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Caliphs: Uhud trembles for Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was climbing Mount Uhud with Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman when it began to quake because of them. The Prophet said, “Be still, Uhud! It is but a Prophet, a truthful man, and two martyrs upon you!”
q: Be still, Uhud! It is but a Prophet, a truthful man, and two martyrs upon you!

title: Hadith on Virtue: Reward for giving up wine, silk
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever abandons wine-drinking although he could drink it, he will be given drink within the holy sanctuary. Whoever abandons wearing silk although he could wear it, he will be clothed within the holy sanctuary.”
q: Whoever abandons wine-drinking although he could drink it, he will be given drink within the holy sanctuary. Whoever abandons wearing silk although he could wear it, he will be clothed within the holy sanctuary.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Vice: Ummah is endangered by five evil practices
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When my nation adopts five practices, their destruction is inevitable: when they curse each other openly, they wear silk, they take up musical instruments, they drink wine, and men are satisfied with men and women are satisfied with women.”
q: When my nation adopts five practices, their destruction is inevitable: when they curse each other openly, they wear silk, they take up musical instruments, they drink wine, and men are satisfied with men and women are satisfied with women.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Abortion: Discarding unborn is a sign of Judgment Day
t: ‘Umayr ibn Ishaq reported: Abu Huraira, may Allah be pleased with him, said in regards to signs before the Hour, “A woman will be taken and her stomach ripped open, then what is in her womb will be taken out and discarded for fear of giving birth.”

title: Hadith on Shuhada: Best martyrs stand up to oppressive rulers
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The master of the martyrs on the Day of Resurrection is Hamzah ibn ‘Abdul Muttalib, and a man who stands up to a tyrannical leader, prohibiting him from evil and enjoining good upon him, and he is killed for it.”
q: The master of the martyrs on the Day of Resurrection is Hamzah ibn ‘Abdul Muttalib, and a man who stands up to a tyrannical leader, prohibiting him from evil and enjoining good upon him, and he is killed for it.

title: Umar on Nifaq: I fear hypocrite scholars in the Ummah
t: Abu Uthman al-Hindi reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, what I fear most for this nation is a learned hypocrite.” It was said, “How is he a learned hypocrite?” Umar said, “He is learned with his tongue, but he is ignorant of the heart and good deeds.”

title: Yahya on Positivity: If you cannot benefit, at least do not harm
t: Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi reported: Yahya ibn Mu’adh, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you cannot benefit, then do not harm. If you cannot bring joy, then do not bring distress. If you cannot praise, then do not blame.”

title: Hadith on Humanity: All human beings are children of Adam
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “All of you are the children of Adam and Adam was created from dust, that people might stop boasting of their fathers lest they become more insignificant to Allah than the dung of a beetle.”
q: All of you are the children of Adam and Adam was created from dust, that people might stop boasting of their fathers lest they become more insignificant to Allah than the dung of a beetle.

title: Hadith on Nightmares: Supplication upon being scared by a dream
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you is frightened by a dream during sleep, let him say: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from His anger, His punishment, and the evil of His servants, from the insinuations of devils and their presence. Verily, they will never harm him.”
q: If one of you is frightened by a dream during sleep, let him say: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from His anger, His punishment, and the evil of His servants, from the insinuations of devils and their presence. Verily, they will never harm him.

title: Hadith on Poverty: If only you knew reward for patience
t: Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If only you knew the rewards you had with Allah, you would like to be increased in poverty and need.”
q: If only you knew the rewards you had with Allah, you would like to be increased in poverty and need.

title: Hadith on Relief: Supplication for worry, sadness, sickness, and difficulty
t: Asma’ bint ‘Umays reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is afflicted by anxiety, grief, illness, or hardship and he says, ‘Allah is my Lord without any partner,’ it will be lifted off him.”
q: Whoever is afflicted by anxiety, grief, illness, or hardship and he says, ‘Allah is my Lord without any partner,’ it will be lifted off him.

title: Shafi’i on Debate: Too much debating belittles status of knowledge
t:
Ibn ‘Abd al-Hakam reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Among the degradation of knowledge is that you debate everyone who debates you, or you argue with everyone who argues with you.”

And he said, “Knowledge is ignorance to the people of ignorance, just as ignorance is ignorance to the people of knowledge.”

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Sins forgiven for declaring oneness of Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest. There is no God but Allah, without any partner, there is no God but Allah. To Him belong dominion and praise, there is no God but Allah. There is no movement or might but in Allah. Whoever says these words in a day or a night or a month, then he dies in that day or night or month, his sins will be forgiven.”
q: There is no God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest. There is no God but Allah, without any partner, there is no God but Allah. To Him belong dominion and praise, there is no God but Allah. There is no movement or might but in Allah. Whoever says these words in a day or a night or a month, then he dies in that day or night or month, his sins will be forgiven.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Dhul-Hijjah: These ten days most pure to Allah
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No deeds are more pure to Allah Almighty, nor greater in reward, than good deeds performed in the ten days of the month of sacrificing.”
q: No deeds are more pure to Allah Almighty, nor greater in reward, than good deeds performed in the ten days of the month of sacrificing.

title: Hadith on Quran: Three Quls suffice against every evil
t: Abdullah ibn Khubayb reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Speak.” I said, “What should I say?” The Prophet said, “Say, ‘He is Allah, the One,’ (112:1) and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and al-Nas, every evening and morning three times. They will be enough for you against everything.”
q: Speak … Say, ‘He is Allah, the One,’ … and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and al-Nas, every evening and morning three times. They will be enough for you against everything.

title: Hadith on Quran: Surat al-Ikhlas makes Paradise obligatory
t: Abu Huraira reported: I met with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he heard a man reciting the verses, “Say: He is Allah, the One, the Eternal Refuge,” (112:1-2). The Prophet said, “It is necessary for him.” I said, “What is necessary?” The Prophet said, “Paradise.”
q: Say: He is Allah, the One, the Eternal Refuge, … It is necessary for him. … Paradise

title: Hadith on Mu’awwidhatayn: Best two chapters for seeking refuge in Allah
t: Ibn ‘Abis al-Juhani reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him, “O Ibn ‘Abis, shall I not tell you about the best way to seek refuge for those who seek it?” He said, “Of course, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “These two chapters, ‘Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak,’ (113:1) and, ‘Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of the people,’ (114:1).”
q: O Ibn ‘Abis, shall I not tell you about the best way to seek refuge for those who seek it? … These two chapters, ‘Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak,’ … and, ‘Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of the people,’

title: Hadith on Hamd: Reward of praising Allah during hardship
t: Shaddad ibn Aws reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty says: When I put one of my faithful servants to trial and he praises Me despite his trial, he will rise from his bed free of sin like the day he was born from his mother. The Almighty Lord says: I have confined My servant and put him to trial, so he will be rewarded the same as he used to do when he was healthy.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty says: When I put one of my faithful servants to trial and he praises Me despite his trial, he will rise from his bed free of sin like the day he was born from his mother.
