The Almighty Lord says: I have confined My servant and put him to trial, so he will be rewarded the same as he used to do when he was healthy.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Salat: Supplication between the two prostrations
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say between the two prostrations, “O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, restore me, guide me, and provide for me.”
q: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, restore me, guide me, and provide for me.

title: Hadith on Health: O Allah, grant me enduring wellness
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say, “O Allah, grant me wellness in my body, wellness in my sight, and make it lasting within me. There is no God but You, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, the Lord of the Great Throne. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.”
q: O Allah, grant me wellness in my body, wellness in my sight, and make it lasting within me. There is no God but You, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, the Lord of the Great Throne. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

title: Hadith on Adhkar: Supplication for physical wellness in the morning
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, grant me wellness in my body. O Allah, grant me wellness in my hearing. O Allah, grant me wellness in my seeing. There is no God but You.”
q: O Allah, grant me wellness in my body. O Allah, grant me wellness in my hearing. O Allah, grant me wellness in my seeing. There is no God but You

title: Hadith on Sleep: The Prophet’s supplication, manners before bed
t: Al-Bara’ reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, if he intended to sleep, he would put his right hand under his cheek and say, “O Lord, protect me from Your punishment on the day You resurrect Your servants.”
q: O Lord, protect me from Your punishment on the day You resurrect Your servants.

title: Jesus on Humility: Look at your sins like slaves, not lords
t: Malik ibn Anas reported: Jesus, the son of Mary, upon him be peace, used to say, “Do not speak too much without remembering Allah, for it will harden your hearts and a hard heart is the furthest from Allah, if only you knew. Do not look at the sins of people as if you were lords, but rather look at your own sins as if you were slaves. Verily, some people are put to trial while others are granted safety, so be merciful to those under trial and praise Allah for your safety.”

title: Hadith on Contentment: Satisfaction with Islam leads to Paradise
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is pleased with Allah as a Lord, with Islam as a religion, and with Muhammad as a prophet, he must enter Paradise.”
q: Whoever is pleased with Allah as a Lord, with Islam as a religion, and with Muhammad as a prophet, he must enter Paradise.

title: Ali on Blame: Do not excessively rebuke people
t: Abi al-Sa’ib reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Do not frequently scold others, for scolding leads to resentment and hatred and too much of it is bad manners.”

title: Abdullah on Faith: Believers have many temperaments, except dishonesty
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Yazid reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The believer may have all kinds of natural dispositions flowing throughout himself, except for treachery and dishonesty.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Opinions: If my claim is wrong, it is from me and Satan
t: Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “If my opinion is correct, it is from Allah. If it is mistaken, it is from myself and Satan. Allah and His Messenger are innocent of it.”

title: Hadith on Begging: Warning to self-sufficient beggars
t: Sahl ibn al-Hanzalah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever asks from people, while he is self-sufficient, only increases his share of the embers of Hellfire.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what amount of independence does not justify begging?” The Prophet said, “Enough to eat in the morning and evening.”
q: Whoever asks from people, while he is self-sufficient, only increases his share of the embers of Hellfire. … Enough to eat in the morning and evening.

title: Ibn Abbas on Shaytan: Devil withdraws if one remembers Allah
t: Sa’id ibn Jubayr reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Satan is perched over the heart of the son of Adam. If he is unmindful and he forgets, Satan whispers. If he remembers Allah, Satan withdraws.”

title: ‘Ata’ on Gentleness: Speak good words to all people
t: Al-Qurtubi reported: Talhah ibn Umar said to ‘Ata’, may Allah have mercy on him, “Indeed, you are a man whom people of various whims gather around and I am a man who has a temper. I would say harsh words to them.” ‘Ata’ said, “Do not do so! Allah Almighty said: Speak good words to people (2:83). This verse includes Jews and Christians, so how about the true monotheists?”
q: Speak good words to people

title: Hadith on Names: Allah forbids insulting by hateful nicknames
t: Abu Jabirah ibn al-Dahhak reported: A man used to have two or three names by which he was called. Perhaps he hated one of them, so Allah revealed the verse, “Do not insult each other with offensive nicknames.” (49:11)
q: Do not insult each other with offensive nicknames.

title: Hadith on Mockery: Man sinks into Hell because of bad joke
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, a man might speak a word to make those around him laugh, yet by it he plunges farther than the star of Pleiades.”
q: Verily, a man might speak a word to make those around him laugh, yet by it he plunges farther than the star of Pleiades.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Umar II on Mockery: Beware of making fun, causing malice
t:
Al-Mawardi reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Beware of mockery, for it is foolishness that produces grudges.”

Imam al-Mawardi commented, “Some of the wise men said mockery is a form of insult, unless it makes the recipient laugh, and it is said mockery is only named as such because it misdirects one from the truth.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Prayer of three people are always answered
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The supplications of three are never turned back: a fasting person until he breaks his fast, a just leader, and the supplication of the oppressed is raised above the clouds by Allah, the gates of heaven open for it and the Lord says: By My might, I will surely help you in due time.”
q: The supplications of three are never turned back: a fasting person until he breaks his fast, a just leader, and the supplication of the oppressed is raised above the clouds by Allah, the gates of heaven open for it and the Lord says: By My might, I will surely help you in due time.

title: Hadith on Sleep: Angel and devil approach you at bedtime
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a man retires to his bed, an angel and a devil rush to him. The angel says: End your day with good! The devil says: End your day with evil! If he remembers Allah and then falls sleep, the angel will spend the night to take care of him.”
q: When a man retires to his bed, an angel and a devil rush to him. The angel says: End your day with good! The devil says: End your day with evil! If he remembers Allah and then falls sleep, the angel will spend the night to take care of him.

title: Hadith on Worship: Acts of worship spoiled by insincerity and sins
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One who fasts might only acquire hunger and thirst from his fasting. One who stands for prayer might only acquire fatigue from his prayer.”
q: One who fasts might only acquire hunger and thirst from his fasting. One who stands for prayer might only acquire fatigue from his prayer.

title: Hadith on Siyam: Do not insult anyone while fasting
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not insult anyone while you are fasting. If anyone insults you, then say: Indeed, I am fasting. If you are standing, then sit down.”
q: Do not insult anyone while you are fasting. If anyone insults you, then say: Indeed, I am fasting. If you are standing, then sit down.

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Those who fasted among truthful and martyrs
t: ‘Amr ibn Murrah reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if I testify there is no God but Allah and you are the Messenger of Allah, I perform the five prayers, I pay the obligatory alms, and I fast the month of Ramadan and stand for prayer in it. Among whom will I be?” The Prophet said, “Among the truthful and the martyrs.”
q: Among the truthful and the martyrs.

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Every Muslim has an answered supplication
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has people He redeems in every day and night of Ramadan, and every servant among them has a supplication that will be answered.”
q: Verily, Allah has people He redeems in every day and night of Ramadan, and every servant among them has a supplication that will be answered.

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Laylat al-Qadar better than a thousand months
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said when the month of Ramadan began, “Verily, this month has presented itself to you. There is a night within it that is better than a thousand months. Whoever is deprived of it has been deprived of all good, and none is deprived of its good but that he is truly deprived.”
q: Verily, this month has presented itself to you. There is a night within it that is better than a thousand months. Whoever is deprived of it has been deprived of all good, and none is deprived of its good but that he is truly deprived.

title: Hadith on Siyam: Allah distances Hellfire from those who fast
t: ‘Amr ibn ‘Abasah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever fasts a day in the way of Allah, Allah will distance him from the Hellfire by a distance of one hundred years of travel.”
q: Whoever fasts a day in the way of Allah, Allah will distance him from the Hellfire by a distance of one hundred years of travel.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Siyam: Fasting is a shield from Hellfire
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, fasting is only a shield by which the servant seeks protection from the Hellfire.”
q: Verily, fasting is only a shield by which the servant seeks protection from the Hellfire.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Action: Allah purifies him by inspiring good deeds
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If Allah wills goodness for a servant, He purifies him before his death.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is the purification of the servant?” The Prophet said, “He inspires him to perform good deeds until his soul is taken.”
q: If Allah wills goodness for a servant, He purifies him before his death. … He inspires him to perform good deeds until his soul is taken.

title: Abdullah on Islam: O Allah, guide us to the path of Islam
t: Shaqiq reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say often in his supplications, “Our Lord, set things right between us and guide us to the path of Islam. Save us from darkness and bring us to the light. Keep obscenities away from us, the outward and inward among them. Bless us in our hearing, our seeing, our hearts, our wives, and our children. Accept our repentance for you are the Relenting, the Merciful. Make us grateful for your bounties, praising you for them and proclaiming them openly, and perfect them for us.”

title: Hadith on Meals: The Prophet accepts invitation from a Jew
t: Anas reported: A Jewish man invited the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to a meal of barley bread and stale meat, so the Prophet accepted his invitation.

title: Hadith on Charity: Many good deeds of Abu Bakr
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Who among you has woken up today fasting?” Abu Bakr said, “I have.” The Prophet said, “Who among you has followed a funeral procession?” Abu Bakr said, “I have.” The Prophet said, “Who among you has fed a needy person?” Abu Bakr said, “I have.” The Prophet said, “Who among you has visited a sick person?” Abu Bakr said, “I have.” The Prophet said, “These deeds are not combined in someone but that they will enter Paradise.”
q: Who among you has woken up today fasting? … Who among you has followed a funeral procession? … Who among you has fed a needy person? … Who among you has visited a sick person? … These deeds are not combined in someone but that they will enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication if afraid of bad people
t: Abu Musa reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, feared evil from people, he would say, “O Allah, we place You in front of them, and we seek refuge in You from their evil.”
q: O Allah, we place You in front of them, and we seek refuge in You from their evil.

title: Hadith on Food: Prohibition of eating predatory animals
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited eating any predatory beast with fangs or any bird with talons.

title: Hadith on Mercy: The Prophet is most kind to his family
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: I have never seen anyone more merciful to his dependents than the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.

title: Hadith on Rukhsa: Allah loves believers taking His concessions
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah loves for you to take His concessions, just as He loves you to fulfill His edicts.”

title: Hadith on Hoarding: Whoever refuses to share food is a sinner
t: Ma’mar ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever hoards food is a sinner.”
q: Whoever hoards food is a sinner.

title: Hadith on Salat: Prayer at home during heavy rain, bad weather
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to order the caller to say on a cold, rainy night, “Surely, pray in your homes.”
q: Surely, pray in your homes.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hamd: Believers praise Allah even as they die
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the believer is in good shape in every situation. He praises Allah Almighty even while his soul is taken out of his body.”
q: Verily, the believer is in good shape in every situation. He praises Allah Almighty even while his soul is taken out of his body.

title: Abu Bakr on Charity: The Caliph secretly cares for the old blind woman
t: Abu Salih reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was committed to an old, disabled blind woman who lived on the outskirts of Medina. At night he would draw water for her and manage her affairs. When he came to her one time, he found that someone else had preceded him and taken care of what she needed. So Umar came to her more than once, lest someone come to her before him, and he lied in wait. He found that it was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, who had already come to her; he was Caliph at the time.

title: Hadith on Quran: The Quran is an intercessor, truthful prosecutor
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Quran is an intercessor and a truthful prosecutor. Whoever puts it in front of himself, it will lead him to Paradise. Whoever throws it behind his back, it will drive him into the Hellfire.”
q: The Quran is an intercessor and a truthful prosecutor. Whoever puts it in front of himself, it will lead him to Paradise. Whoever throws it behind his back, it will drive him into the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Dunya: The worldly life is less than worthless to Allah
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed through the market from a higher part of the city and people were look at him from both sides. The Prophet passed by the carcass of a one-eared goat and he reached out to take its ear. The Prophet said, “Which one of you would like this for a coin?” They said, “Who among us would want it while it is worth nothing? What would we do with it?” The Prophet said three times, “Would you like to have it?” They said no each time and said, “No, by Allah, if it were alive it would be defective as it only has one ear. How so if it were dead?” The Prophet said, “By Allah, the worldly life is less important to Allah than this is to you.”
q: Which one of you would like this for a coin? … Would you like to have it? … By Allah, the worldly life is less important to Allah than this is to you.

title: Hadith on Trials: When Allah afflicts a Muslim in his body
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If Allah puts the Muslim servant to trial in his body, Allah says: Record his righteous deeds for him that he used to do. If he is healed, it is his cleansing and purification. If his soul is taken, he will be forgiven and shown mercy.”
q: If Allah puts the Muslim servant to trial in his body, Allah says: Record his righteous deeds for him that he used to do. If he is healed, it is his cleansing and purification. If his soul is taken, he will be forgiven and shown mercy.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Ali on Freedom: Ali ibn al-Husayn emancipates his slave girl
t: ‘Abd al-Razzaq reported: A slave girl belonging to Ali ibn al-Husyan, may Allah be pleased with him, poured out some water as he prepared to pray and she dropped the pitcher onto his face causing an injury. She said, “Allah Almighty says: Those who restrain their anger (3:134)!” Ali said, “I have restrained my anger.” She said, “And those who forgive people!” Ali said, “Allah has forgiven you.” She said, “And Allah loves those who do good!” Ali said, “Go, for you are now free.”
q: Allah Almighty says: Those who restrain their anger … And those who forgive people! … And Allah loves those who do good!

title: Hadith on Disease: Follow basic hygiene to stop spread of contagions
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Cover the vessels and close the water skins, for there will be night out of the year in which an epidemic descends. It will not pass over an uncovered vessel or an untied water skin but that some of this contagion will fall into it.”
q: Cover the vessels and close the water skins, for there will be night out of the year in which an epidemic descends. It will not pass over an uncovered vessel or an untied water skin but that some of this contagion will fall into it.

title: Hadith on Charity: Expiation of sins for forgiving injury
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No man suffers an injury to his body, and forgives it as charity, but that his sins will be expiated by the measure of his charity.”
q: No man suffers an injury to his body, and forgives it as charity, but that his sins will be expiated by the measure of his charity.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Hilm: Forbearance must be learned and cultivated
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, knowledge only comes by learning and forbearance only comes by cultivating forbearance. Whoever aims for good will receive goodness and whoever seeks to evade evil will be protected from it.”
q: Verily, knowledge only comes by learning and forbearance only comes by cultivating forbearance. Whoever aims for good will receive goodness and whoever seeks to evade evil will be protected from it.

title: Hadith on Courtesy: The Prophet accepts humble gifts and invitations
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If I were invited to a meal of a simple sheep’s hoof or shoulder, I would answer it. If I were given a gift of a simple sheep’s hoof or shoulder, I would accept it.”
q: If I were invited to a meal of a simple sheep’s hoof or shoulder, I would answer it. If I were given a gift of a simple sheep’s hoof or shoulder, I would accept it.

title: Hadith on Dua: I seek refuge from all things displeasing to You
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would supplicate, saying, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a decline in Your blessings, a change in the wellness You have provided, a sudden act of Your vengeance, and all things displeasing to You.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a decline in Your blessings, a change in the wellness You have provided, a sudden act of Your vengeance, and all things displeasing to You.

title: Hadith on Nikah: Looking at a prospective marriage candidate
t:
Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah reported: He proposed to a woman in marriage and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Look at her, for it is the best way to make lasting affection between you.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “Some of the people of knowledge adhered to this tradition. They said: There is nothing wrong with looking at her as long as he does not see parts of her forbidden to see.”
q: Look at her, for it is the best way to make lasting affection between you.

title: Hadith on Hygiene: The Prophet washes his hands before eating
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, if he wanted to sleep while he was in a state of major ritual impurity, he would perform ablution. If he wanted to eat or drink, he would first wash his hands and then eat or drink.

title: Hadith on Plague: Avoid the plague but do not spread it either
t: Sa’d reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you hear of a plague in a land, do not go into it. If it happens in land where you are, do not go out of it.”
q: If you hear of a plague in a land, do not go into it. If it happens in land where you are, do not go out of it.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Disease: Seek refuge in Allah from physical, mental illness
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say, “O Allah, I seek refuge in you from leprosy, madness, contagion, and evil ailments.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in you from leprosy, madness, contagion, and evil ailments.

title: Abu Huraira on Labor: Help workers and pay their fair wages
t: Abu Yunus reported: Abu Huraira, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Help the laborer with his work. Verily, one who works for Allah will never be disappointed.”

title: Hatim on Enmity: No one is a true enemy except for Satan
t: Abu Turab reported: Hatim al-Asamm, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I saw that everyone has an enemy, so I said I would find out who mine is. As for one who backbites me, he is not my enemy, or one who takes something from me, he is not my enemy. Rather, my enemy is one who commands me to disobey Allah when I am obeying Allah. Thus, I saw that in Satan and his soldiers, so I took them as my enemy, and I waged war between us. I darted my bow, drew my arrow, and never let him come near me.”

title: Hadith on Shaytan: Satan lies in wait to ambush the believers
t: Sabrah ibn Abi Fakih reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Satan lies in wait for the son of Adam along his paths. He sits on the path of Islam and he says: You will embrace Islam and abandon your religion and your forefather’s religion? He disobeys him and embraces Islam. Then, Satan lies in wait for him on the path of emigration and he says: You will emigrate and leave your land and sky? Indeed, an emigrant is like a tethered horse! He disobeys him and emigrates. Then, Satan lies in wait for him on the path of jihad and he says: You will wage jihad at great cost to your life and wealth? You will fight and be killed, your wife will remarry, and your wealth distributed as spoils! He disobeys him and he wages jihad. Whoever does that has a right upon Allah Almighty that he will enter Paradise.”
q: Verily, Satan lies in wait for the son of Adam along his paths. He sits on the path of Islam and he says: You will embrace Islam and abandon your religion and your forefather’s religion? He disobeys him and embraces Islam. Then, Satan lies in wait for him on the path of emigration and he says: You will emigrate and leave your land and sky? Indeed, an emigrant is like a tethered horse! He disobeys him and emigrates. Then, Satan lies in wait for him on the path of jihad and he says: You will wage jihad at great cost to your life and wealth? You will fight and be killed, your wife will remarry, and your wealth distributed as spoils! He disobeys him and he wages jihad. Whoever does that has a right upon Allah Almighty that he will enter Paradise.

title: Abu Yazid on Will: I want not to want anything in the world
t:
Ibn al-Qayyim reported: It was said to Abu Yazid, may Allah have mercy on him, “What do you want?” Abu Yazid said, “I want not to want.”

Ibn al-Qayyim said, “He wanted the lower-self to be cut off from its aims… so he guarded his will and restricted it from anything besides Allah Almighty.”

title: Hadith on Grief: Death of the Prophet’s son, Ibrahim
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: We entered the house of Abu Sayf along with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, who was the husband of Ibrahim’s wet-nurse, upon him be peace. The Prophet took hold of Ibrahim, kissed him, and smelled him. Then, we entered as Ibrahim was breathing his last breaths. It made the eyes of the Prophet shed tears. ‘Abdur Rahman ibn Awf said, “Even you, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “O son of Awf, this is mercy.” Then, the Prophet wept some more, saying, “Verily, the eyes shed tears and the heart is grieved, yet we will not say anything but what is pleasing to our Lord. We are saddened by your departure, O Ibrahim!”
q: O son of Awf, this is mercy. … Verily, the eyes shed tears and the heart is grieved, yet we will not say anything but what is pleasing to our Lord. We are saddened by your departure, O Ibrahim!

title: Hadith on Rain: The Prophet’s supplication for a windy storm
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, if there was a windy storm, he would say, “O Allah, I ask You for its good, the good within it, and the good for which it was sent. I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil within it, and the evil for which it was sent.” If the sky began to light up and thunder, the color of the Prophet’s face would change and he would anxiously come and go, back and forth. If it rained, he would be pleased with it and I could recognize the signs of that on his face. I asked him about it and the Prophet said, “O Aisha, perhaps it is as Allah said about the people of ‘Ad: When they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said this is a cloud bringing us rain!” (46:24)
q: O Allah, I ask You for its good, the good within it, and the good for which it was sent. I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil within it, and the evil for which it was sent. … O Aisha, perhaps it is as Allah said about the people of ‘Ad: When they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said this is a cloud bringing us rain!

title: Hadith on Ease: The Prophet rebukes Mu’adh for long prayers
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: Mu’adh ibn Jabal used to pray with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Then, he returned to his people and led them in prayer. Mu’adh prayed the evening prayer and recited Surat al-Baqarah, until a man left the prayer, and Mu’adh was critical of him. The news reached the Prophet and he said three times, “You put them to trial!” The Prophet ordered him to recite two medium chapters from the end of the Quran.
q: You put them to trial!

title: Hadith on Shaytan: The devil sends out troops to misguide believers
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Satan (Iblis) awakens in the morning, he dispatches his troops, saying: Whoever misguides a Muslim today, I will dress him with a crown. This one will go out and say: I did not leave him alone until he divorced his wife. Satan will say: A Muslim is about to get married. This one will come and say: I did not leave him alone until he disrespected his parents. Satan will say: A Muslim is about to be good to his parents. This one will come and say: I did not leave him alone until he committed idolatry. Satan will say: You, you! Another will come and say: I did not leave him alone until he committed adultery. Satan will say: You, you! This one will come and say: I did not leave him alone until he killed someone. Satan will say: You, you! Then he will dress him with a crown.”
q: When Satan … awakens in the morning, he dispatches his troops, saying: Whoever misguides a Muslim today, I will dress him with a crown. This one will go out and say: I did not leave him alone until he divorced his wife. Satan will say: A Muslim is about to get married. This one will come and say: I did not leave him alone until he disrespected his parents. Satan will say: A Muslim is about to be good to his parents. This one will come and say: I did not leave him alone until he committed idolatry. Satan will say: You, you! Another will come and say: I did not leave him alone until he committed adultery. Satan will say: You, you! This one will come and say: I did not leave him alone until he killed someone. Satan will say: You, you! Then he will dress him with a crown.

title: Hasan on ‘Ilm: Knowledge is two types, beneficial or hypocritical
t: Hisham reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Knowledge is two types: Knowledge in the heart is that which benefits. Knowledge on the tongue will be an indictment against the son of Adam.”

title: Hadith on Angels: Every person followed by an angel or devil
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one goes out from his house except there are two banners in hand: one in the hand of an angel and one in the hand of Satan. Verily, if he goes out for a reason Allah loves, the angel will follow him with his banner, and he will continue to be under the banner of the angel until he returns home. If he goes out for a reason displeasing to Allah, Satan will follow him with his banner, and he will continue to be under the banner of Satan until he returns home.”
q: No one goes out from his house except there are two banners in hand: one in the hand of an angel and one in the hand of Satan. Verily, if he goes out for a reason Allah loves, the angel will follow him with his banner, and he will continue to be under the banner of the angel until he returns home. If he goes out for a reason displeasing to Allah, Satan will follow him with his banner, and he will continue to be under the banner of Satan until he returns home.

title: Hasan on Quran: Book of Allah is a personal letter from Him
t: Al-Nawawi reported: Al-Hasan ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, those before you viewed the Quran as letters from their Lord, such that they would contemplate it by night and yearn for it by day.”

title: Sahl on Mindfulness: One who knows himself, knows his Lord
t:
Abu Nu’aym reported: Sahl ibn Abdullah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If one knows the enemy, one knows his Lord. If one knows himself, one knows his status with his Lord. If one knows his mind, one knows his state between him and his Lord. If one knows sacred knowledge, one knows his journey. If one knows the world, one knows the Hereafter.”

And Sahl was asked about the saying, “Whoever knows himself, knows his Lord.” Sahl said, “Whoever defines himself for the sake of his Lord, his Lord defines him for the sake of himself.”

title: Ibrahim on Ma’rifah: One who knows Allah is busy with nothing else
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Ibrahim ibn Adham, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, whoever knows himself will be busy with himself. Whoever knows his Lord will be busy with his Lord to the exclusion of anything else.”

title: Hadith on Kindness: Gentle and easy-going people are in Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is kind, affable, and easy-going, Allah will forbid him from entering Hellfire.”
q: Whoever is kind, affable, and easy-going, Allah will forbid him from entering Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Adhan: O Bilal, comfort us with the prayer
t: Abdullah ibn Muhammad reported: The time for prayer arrived, and he said to some of his relatives, “Young lady, bring me water for ablution that I might pray and be comforted.” We objected to that from him, but he said, “I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: Stand, O Bilal, and comfort us with the prayer.”
q: Stand, O Bilal, and comfort us with the prayer.

title: Umar on Zuhd: Incredible asceticism of Syrian governor Abu ‘Ubaydah
t: Abdullah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when he arrived in Syria, he said to Abu ‘Ubaydah, “Let us go to your house.” Abu ‘Ubaydah said, “You want nothing but to shed tears for me?” Umar entered his house and he saw nothing. Umar said, “Where are your provisions? I do not see anything but rags, a water-skin, and a dish. You are governor! Do you have food?” Abu ‘Ubaydah went to a bucket and took out some scraps, and Umar wept. Abu ‘Ubaydah said to him, “I told you that you would shed tears over me, O commander of the faithful. It is enough for you to have in the world what lets you reach the final place of rest.” Umar said, “The world has changed all of us except for you, O Abu ‘Ubaydah.”

title: Shafi’i on Malice: Forgiveness relieved my soul of anxiety
t: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote in his poetry, “When I forgave and stopped holding malice against anyone, I relieved my soul of the worries of enmity.”

title: Hadith on Jannah: Five deeds for the faithful to enter Paradise
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever comes with five deeds, along with faith, will enter Paradise: one who preserves the five prayers, their ablution, their bowings, their prostrations, and their timings, who fasts the month of Ramadan, who performs Hajj pilgrimage to the House if he can find the means, who gives charity with a cheerful soul, and one who fulfills the trust.”
q: Whoever comes with five deeds, along with faith, will enter Paradise: one who preserves the five prayers, their ablution, their bowings, their prostrations, and their timings, who fasts the month of Ramadan, who performs Hajj pilgrimage to the House if he can find the means, who gives charity with a cheerful soul, and one who fulfills the trust.

title: Hadith on Repentance: Time to regret sin before the angels records it
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the angel on the left side will raise his pen over the error or sin of a Muslim servant for six hours. If he sincerely regrets it and seeks forgiveness from Allah, the angel will throw it aside. Otherwise, he will record it as one sin.”
q: Verily, the angel on the left side will raise his pen over the error or sin of a Muslim servant for six hours. If he sincerely regrets it and seeks forgiveness from Allah, the angel will throw it aside. Otherwise, he will record it as one sin.

title: Ja’far on Muraqabah: Mindfulness is to be careful with every thought
t: Abu al-‘Abbas reported: I asked Ja’far ibn Nasir, may Allah have mercy on him, about mindfulness. Ja’far said, “It is to be watchful over one’s innermost being, due to awareness of the Almighty Lord, with every thought.”

title: Ahmad on Divorce: Not obligation to divorce upon parental request
t:
Sindi reported: A man asked Abu Abdullah, Imam Ahmad, “My father has ordered me to divorce my wife.” Ahmad said, “Do not divorce her.” He said, “Did not Umar command his son Abdullah to divorce his wife?” Ahmad said, “Is your father like Umar, may Allah be pleased with him?”

Imam Ibn Muflih commented, “If his father commands him to divorce his wife, it is not an obligation to do so as mentioned by most of our scholars.”

title: Shafi’i on Criticism: Delivering criticism in the best way, without hyperbole
t: Al-Muzanni reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, heard me one day as I said, “This narrator is a great liar!” Al-Shafi’i said to me, “O Abu Ibrahim, dress your words in the best manner. Do not say this narrator is a great liar, but rather say his narrations are of no importance.”

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet prays lightly, yet perfectly
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: I never prayed behind an Imam who prayed so lightly, yet so perfectly as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. He would hear a child crying and lighten the prayer, fearing it would put his mother to trial.

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet’s supplication rising from bowing
t: Ibn Abi Awfa reported: When the Messegner of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, raised his back from bowing, he would say, “Allah has heard one who praised Him. O Allah, our Lord, to You belong praise as fills the heavens, fills the earth, and fills anything You will after them.”
q: Allah has heard one who praised Him. O Allah, our Lord, to You belong praise as fills the heavens, fills the earth, and fills anything You will after them.

title: Hadith on Salat: Seeking forgiveness, supplicating after prayer
t: Thawban reported: When the Messenger of Allah peace and blessings be upon him, finished his prayer, he would seek forgiveness from Allah three times and he would say, “O Allah, You are peace and from You is peace. Blessed are You, Majestic and Generous.”
q: O Allah, You are peace and from You is peace. Blessed are You, Majestic and Generous.

title: Hadith on Salat: Listen to the Imam when he recites Quran
t: Abu Musa al-‘Ashari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the Imam recites the Quran, then listen quietly.”
q: When the Imam recites the Quran, then listen quietly.

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Charity on behalf of deceased parents rewarded
t: Aisha reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, my mother died suddenly without writing a will. I think if she could speak, she would give in charity. Will she have a reward if I give charity on her behalf?” The Prophet said, “Yes.”
q: Yes
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ali on Zuhd: People who abandon part of Islam harm themselves
t: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “People do not abandon something from their religion, intending to benefit their worldly affairs, except that Allah will expose them to what is even more harmful and more evil for them.”

title: Hadith on Hamd: Best servants of Allah always praise Him
t: ‘Imran ibn Husyan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the best servants of Allah on the Day of Resurrection are those who constantly praised Him.”
q: Verily, the best servants of Allah on the Day of Resurrection are those who constantly praised Him.

title: Hadith on Talaq: Prohibition of divorcing women during menstruation
t: Ibn Umar reported: He divorced his wife in the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while she menstruating. Umar ibn al-Khattab asked the Prophet about that and he said, “Order him to return her. Let him leave her alone until she becomes pure, then menstruates, and then is pure again. If he wishes, he may keep her or divorce her before he is intimate with her. That is the waiting period Allah has commanded for divorcing women.” (65:1)
q: Order him to return her. Let him leave her alone until she becomes pure, then menstruates, and then is pure again. If he wishes, he may keep her or divorce her before he is intimate with her. That is the waiting period Allah has commanded for divorcing women.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: The Prophet sends blessings on the charitable
t: Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa reported: When people came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to give charity, he would say, “O Allah, send blessings upon the household of these people.” My father came to him with charity and he said, “O Allah, send blessings upon the household of Abu Awfa.”
q: O Allah, send blessings upon the household of these people. … O Allah, send blessings upon the household of Abu Awfa.

title: Hadith on Zina: Nikah Halala is a form of adultery
t: Nafi’ reported: A man came to Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, and he asked about a man who divorces his wife three times, then he marries her to his brother, without any prior agreement from him, in order to make her lawful to him again. Does she become lawful to the first husband? Ibn Umar said, “No, unless it is a marriage she had desired. We used to consider this illegal fornication in the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.”

title: Umar on Talaq: The Caliph punishes men who triple divorce
t: Anas reported: Whenever a man was brought to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who had divorced his wife three times in one sitting, he would flog his back.

title: Hadith on Marriage: Condemnation of Nikah Halala
t:
Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, cursed the one who marries a woman to overturn an irrevocable divorce and the man for whom it is done.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “This tradition was acted upon by the people of knowledge among the companions of the Prophet, among them Umar ibn al-Khattab, Uthman ibn Affan, Abdullah ibn Umar, and others. It is the opinion of the jurists among the successors. It was said by Sufyan al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq.”

title: Hadith on Divorce: The Prophet is angered by triple talaq
t: Mahmud ibn Labid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was informed about a man who pronounced divorce to his wife three times at once. The Prophet stood in anger and he said, “Do they play with the Book of Allah while I am among you?”
q: Do they play with the Book of Allah while I am among you?

title: Hadith on Divorce: Evidence triple talaq only counts as one divorce
t: Yazid ibn Rukanah reported: Rukanah had divorced his wife irrevocably and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, only counted it as one divorce.

title: Hadith on Divorce: Triple talaq in the time of the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Triple divorce in the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, Abu Bakr, and two years of the Caliphate of Umar was considered to be only one revocable divorce. Umar ibn al-Khattab said, “Verily, the people have become hasty in a matter for which they should take care. If only we imposed it upon them.” Thus, Umar imposed it upon them.

title: Hadith on Nikah: Command to announce the marriage in public
t: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Announce the marriage.”
q: Announce the marriage

title: Hadith on Khula: Warning against initiating frivolous divorce
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a woman asks her husband for a divorce without a strong reason, the fragrance of Paradise becomes forbidden for her.”
q: If a woman asks her husband for a divorce without a strong reason, the fragrance of Paradise becomes forbidden for her.

title: Malik on Fatwa: Humility of Imam Malik’s independent judgments
t: Sa’id ibn Sulayman reported: I never heard Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, issue a religious verdict on anything but that he would recite this verse, “Verily, we only consider it speculation and we are not certain.” (45:32)
q: Verily, we only consider it speculation and we are not certain.

title: Hadith on Creation: Allah created angels, jinn, and humankind
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The angels were created from light, the jinn were created from a mixture of fire, and Adam was created as has been described for you.”
q: The angels were created from light, the jinn were created from a mixture of fire, and Adam was created as has been described for you.

title: Hadith on Jinn: Three forms of interdimensional beings
t: Abu Tha’labah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The jinn have three forms: one form like dogs and snakes, one form flies through the air, and one form comes and goes.”
q: The jinn have three forms: one form like dogs and snakes, one form flies through the air, and one form comes and goes.

title: Hadith on Ayat al-Kursi: Verse of Throne for protection from Satan
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entrusted me to protect the charity of Ramadan. Someone came to me and began taking from the food. I took hold of him, and I said, “I will certainly take you to the Messenger of Allah!” Abu Huraira told the story to the Prophet, saying, “The man told me that when I go to bed, I should recite the Verse of the Throne. Allah will appoint a protector over me, and no devil will come near me until morning.” The Prophet said, “He told you the truth, although he is a liar. That was Satan.”
q: He told you the truth, although he is a liar. That was Satan

title: Ahmad on Love: True love for Allah seeks no worldly benefits
t: Al-Maruwidhi reported: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about love for the sake of Allah and he said, “It is that you not love him for the sake of some worldly benefit.”

title: Hadith on Orphans: Be kind to orphans for a soft heart
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Bring the orphan close to you, pat his head, and feed him with the same food you eat. It will soften your heart and fulfill your need.”
q: Bring the orphan close to you, pat his head, and feed him with the same food you eat. It will soften your heart and fulfill your need.

title: Shabib on Silence: Better to ignore some evil speech than respond
t: Ibn ‘Asakir reported: Shabib ibn Shaybah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whoever hears a word he disapproves, he should be silent. What he disapproves will cease. If he answers it, he will hear more of what he disapproves.”

title: Umar on Silence: Some falsehood is defeated by ignoring it
t: Abu Yusuf reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Know that Allah has servants who cause some falsehood to die out by ignoring it and they give life to the truth by mentioning it.”

title: Hadith on Salat: An angel announces at the time of every prayer
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has an angel announce at the time of every prayer: O children of Adam, stand for your fires that you have put forward by your sins and extinguish them with prayer!”
q: Verily, Allah has an angel announce at the time of every prayer: O children of Adam, stand for your fires that you have put forward by your sins and extinguish them with prayer!
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Dajjal: False Messiah to come with fake miracles, power to revive
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The False Messiah will come and he will be forbidden from entering the boundary of Medina. He will descend upon some of the salty barren areas around Medina. On that day, a man among the best of the people will say come out and say: I testify that you are the same impostor whom the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, told us about. The False Messiah will say: Do you all think if I killed you and brought you back to life, would you have any doubt in the matter? The man will say no. Then, he will kill the man and bring him back to life and the man will say when he is alive again: By Allah, I have never seen so clearly as I do today! The False Messiah will intend to kill him, for he has not authority over him.”
q: The False Messiah will come and he will be forbidden from entering the boundary of Medina. He will descend upon some of the salty barren areas around Medina. On that day, a man among the best of the people will say come out and say: I testify that you are the same impostor whom the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, told us about. The False Messiah will say: Do you all think if I killed you and brought you back to life, would you have any doubt in the matter? The man will say no. Then, he will kill the man and bring him back to life and the man will say when he is alive again: By Allah, I have never seen so clearly as I do today! The False Messiah will intend to kill him, for he has not authority over him.

title: Fudayl on Forgiveness: Always recommend mercy and forbearance
t: ‘Abdu Samad reported: Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If a man comes to you complaining about another man, then say: O brother, forgive him, as forgiveness is closer to righteousness. If he says my heart cannot tolerate forgiveness, but rather retaliation as Allah Almighty has commanded me, then say: If you must, do so in the best manner and retaliate with the same measure which you were afflicted, or else return to the door of forgiveness. Surely, the door of forgiveness is wider. Whoever forgives and sets things right, his reward is with Allah. The one who forgives will sleep comfortably in his bed, but the one who avenges will toss and turn over his affairs.”

title: Hadith on Intimacy: Approach your spouse with kindness, gentleness
t: ‘Utbah ibn Abdu Sulami reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you comes to their spouse for intercourse, let them cover themselves and not approach each other like two wild mules.”
q: When one of you comes to their spouse for intercourse, let them cover themselves and not approach each other like two wild mules.

title: Hadith on Shafa’a: The Prophet chooses intercession as mercy
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I had a choice between the intercession and only half of my nation entering Paradise, so I chose the intercession as it is broader and more fulfilling. Do you think it is for the righteous and the pure? No, rather it is for the sinners and the defiled.”
q: I had a choice between the intercession and only half of my nation entering Paradise, so I chose the intercession as it is broader and more fulfilling. Do you think it is for the righteous and the pure? No, rather it is for the sinners and the defiled.

title: Hadith on Shafa’a: The Prophet intercedes for sinners of the Ummah
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “My intercession is for the people of major sins among my nation.”
q: My intercession is for the people of major sins among my nation.

title: Hadith on Secrecy: Be transparent and beware of secret activities
t: Ibn Umar reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, instruct me.” The Prophet said, “Worship Allah and associate none with Him, perform the prayer, give charity, fast the month of Ramadan, and perform the two pilgrimages. Listen to and obey your leaders. You must be transparent and beware of secrecy.”
q: Worship Allah and associate none with Him, perform the prayer, give charity, fast the month of Ramadan, and perform the two pilgrimages. Listen to and obey your leaders. You must be transparent and beware of secrecy

title: Hadith on Prophecy: The Prophet left us everything we need to know
t:
Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, left us behind and no bird flaps with its wings but that he had given us some knowledge about it.

Abu Hatim said, “It means by his commands, his prohibitions, his stories, his actions, and his permissions, peace and blessings be upon him.”

title: Hasan on Fear: He enters Paradise because he never forgot his sins
t: Hisham ibn Hassan reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, a man may commit a sin and he never forgets it, always fearing it, until he enters Paradise.”

title: Hadith on Dajjal: False Messiah preceded by years of treachery
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, preceding the False Messiah will be years of deception, in which the truthful are belied, the liars are believed, the trustworthy are discredited, the treacherous are trusted, and the disgraceful speak.” It was said, “Who are the disgraceful?” The Prophet said, “Little wicked men who speak about the general affairs.”
q: Verily, preceding the False Messiah will be years of deception, in which the truthful are belied, the liars are believed, the trustworthy are discredited, the treacherous are trusted, and the disgraceful speak. … Little wicked men who speak about the general affairs.

title: Tawus on Moderation: Tawus steers people towards a middle way
t: Layth reported: Tawus, may Allah have mercy on him, if the people became too strict in a matter, he would grant them a concessions in it. If the people became too permissive in a matter, he would make them be more strict in it. Layth said, “That is truly knowledge.”

title: Hadith on Lineage: Learn your family history to solidify familial ties
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Learn your lineages to solidify your family ties. Verily, keeping family ties causes love among the kinship, enriches the wealth, and increases the lifespan.”
q: Learn your lineages to solidify your family ties. Verily, keeping family ties causes love among the kinship, enriches the wealth, and increases the lifespan.

title: Hadith on Nikah: Minimum legal requirements for valid marriage
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no marriage unless with a guardian and two credible witnesses. Any marriage contracted with less than that is invalid. If there is a dispute, the ruler is the guardian for one without a guardian.”
q: There is no marriage unless with a guardian and two credible witnesses. Any marriage contracted with less than that is invalid. If there is a dispute, the ruler is the guardian for one without a guardian.

title: Umar on ‘Ilm: No gathering more noble than a scholar’s class
t: Al-Ghazali reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, a man might leave his house with sins like the mountain of Tihamah, but then he hears some knowledge and fear Allah, forsakes his sins and departs to his house without any sin upon him. Do not abandon the assemblies of the scholars, for Allah has not created any ground on the face of the earth more noble than the assemblies of scholars.”

title: Hadith on Believers: Truth-seekers among Persians find faith
t: Abu Huraira reported: We were sitting with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when Surat al-Jumu’ah was revealed. When he recited the verse, “And others who have yet to join them,” (62:3) a man said, “O Messenger of Allah, who are these?” Salman the Persian was among us and the Prophet placed his hand upon him, then he said, “Were faith to be found as far away as the star of Pleiades, men among these would reach it.”
q: And others who have yet to join them … Were faith to be found as far away as the star of Pleiades, men among these would reach it.

title: Hadith on Ahl Bayt: The Prophet leaves his household to guide us
t: Zayd ibn Arqam reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I have left behind what will never lead you astray if you hold fast to them. One of them is greater than the other: the Book of Allah is a rope extended from the heavens to the earth, and my family, the people of my household. They will not dissent until they return to me at the Fountain, so look at how you treat them after me.”
q: Verily, I have left behind what will never lead you astray if you hold fast to them. One of them is greater than the other: the Book of Allah is a rope extended from the heavens to the earth, and my family, the people of my household. They will not dissent until they return to me at the Fountain, so look at how you treat them after me.

title: Hadith on Ummah: Muslim nation honored for worship in three ways
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “We have been favored in three ways: Our prayer rows have been made like the rows of angels, the entire earth has been made a place of prayer for us, and its soil is purifying for ablution if one cannot find water.”
q: We have been favored in three ways: Our prayer rows have been made like the rows of angels, the entire earth has been made a place of prayer for us, and its soil is purifying for ablution if one cannot find water.

title: Hadith on Seduction: Women who are fully-clothed, but naked
t: Abu Salih reported: Abu Huraira, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Some women are clothed but naked, inclining to evil and seducing with it. They will not enter Paradise, nor smell its fragrance, even though it can be found from a distance of five hundred years of travel.”
gf: Sahih (authentic) according to Ibn Abdul Barr

title: Ahmad on Ummah: Imam Ahmad’s supplication for the Muslim nation
t: Al-Bayhaqi reported: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him, would supplicate in prostration, “O Allah, whomever among this nation is not upon the truth, but thinks he is upon the truth, bring him back to the truth that he may be among the people of truth.” And he would say, “O Allah, if you accept a ransom from the sinful among the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, then make me their ransom.”

title: Sufyan on Dua: Hardship with supplication better than ease
t: Abu Ruh reported: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “What a servant dislikes is better for him than what he likes, as what he dislikes compels him to supplicate and what he likes distracts him from it.”

title: Hadith on Ummah: Righteousness in temperance, destruction in worldly hope
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The rightness in the beginning of this nation was by renouncing the world and attaining conviction. The destruction in the end of it is by miserliness and vain hopes.”
q: The rightness in the beginning of this nation was by renouncing the world and attaining conviction. The destruction in the end of it is by miserliness and vain hopes.

title: Hadith on Wealth: Your true earnings are your acts of charity
t: Abu Mutarrif reported: I came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was reciting the verse, “Competition for wealth diverts you,” (102:1). The Prophet said, “The son of Adam boasts: My wealth! My wealth! O son of Adam, have you truly earned any wealth but what you ate and consumed, or clothes put on and wore out, or spent in charity so it remained?”
q: Competition for wealth diverts you, … The son of Adam boasts: My wealth! My wealth! O son of Adam, have you truly earned any wealth but what you ate and consumed, or clothes put on and wore out, or spent in charity so it remained?

title: Hadith on Ikhtilaf: Companions criticized leadership but remained united
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Yazid reported: Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, prayed four cycles at Mina. Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said, “I prayed it as two cycles with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as well as Abu Bakr and Umar.” Mu’awiyah ibn Qurrah added: Abdullah then prayed four cycles in Mina. It was said to him, “You faulted Uthman and then you prayed four?” Abdullah said, “Dissension is evil.”

title: Hadith on Kusuf: The Prophet frees slaves during an eclipse
t: Asma’ bint Abi Bakr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had ordered the emancipation of slaves during a solar eclipse.

title: Hadith on Modesty: Prohibition of verbally describing sexual features
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A woman should not touch another woman and then describe her figure to her husband as if he were gazing at her.”
q: A woman should not touch another woman and then describe her figure to her husband as if he were gazing at her.

title: Hadith on Maghfirah: Allah has power to forgive all sins
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: Whoever knows that I have the power to forgive all sins, I will forgive him and I will not hesitate as long as he does not associate any partner with Me.”
q: Allah Almighty said: Whoever knows that I have the power to forgive all sins, I will forgive him and I will not hesitate as long as he does not associate any partner with Me.

title: Hadith on Parents: Obligation to meet needs of your parents
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have some property and my father invades my property.” The Prophet said, “You and your property belong to your father. Verily, your children are the most wholesome of your earnings, so eat from what your children earn.”
q: You and your property belong to your father. Verily, your children are the most wholesome of your earnings, so eat from what your children earn.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Umar on Hamd: How are you? All praise is due to Allah
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A man greeted Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, with peace and Umar returned his greeting. Then, Umar said to the man, “How are you?” The man said, “I praise Allah to you.” Umar said, “This praise is what I wanted from you.”

title: Hadith on Hamd: I wanted you to praise Allah for me
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to a man, “How are you this morning?” The man said, “I praise Allah to you, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “This praise is what I wanted from you.”
q: How are you this morning? … This praise is what I wanted from you.

title: A’mash on Rulers: Corruption among masses leads to evil rulers
t: Mansur ibn Abi al-Aswad reported: I asked Al-A’mash, may Allah have mercy on him, about the saying of the Exalted, “’Thus, We appoint some oppress as allies of one another because of what they have earned,’ (6:129). What have you heard being said about it?” Al-A’mash said, “ I heard them say: If the people become corrupt, the worst of them will be appointed rulers over them.”
q: ’Thus, We appoint some oppress as allies of one another because of what they have earned,

title: Hadith on Earning: Best to eat from work of one’s own hands
t: Al-Miqdam ibn Ma’dikarib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No meal eaten by one of you is better than the meal he eats from the work of his own hands. Verily, the Prophet of Allah, David, upon him be peace, would eat from the work of his own hands.”
q: No meal eaten by one of you is better than the meal he eats from the work of his own hands. Verily, the Prophet of Allah, David, upon him be peace, would eat from the work of his own hands.

title: Sufyan on Fatwa: Granting proper concessions, not strictest opinion
t: Abu Usamah reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Indeed, knowledge in our view is granting a proper concession upon a reliable basis. As for giving the strictest opinion, anybody can do that well.”

title: Hadith on Da’wah: Former enemies, prisoners embrace Islam
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah marvels at people who enter Paradise in chains.”
q: Allah marvels at people who enter Paradise in chains.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Observing nature’s wonders to remember Allah
t: Ibn Abi Awfa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among the best servants of Allah are those who observe the sun, the moon, the stars, and the shades for the remembrance of Allah.”
q: Verily, among the best servants of Allah are those who observe the sun, the moon, the stars, and the shades for the remembrance of Allah.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Abu Bakr on Jihad: Abu Bakr’s ten commandments for just war
t: Yahya ibn Sa’id reported: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, dispatched armies to Syria and he said, “I give you ten instructions: Do not kill a woman, nor a child, nor an infirm elder. Do not cut down fruit-bearing trees, nor tear down inhabited buildings. Do not slaughter sheep or camels, except for food. Do not burn or drown bees nests. Do not steal from the spoils and do not act cowardly.”

title: Hadith on ‘Ilm: Parable of one not sharing Islamic knowledge
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of one who learns sacred knowledge and then does not share it is like one who stores up treasure and does not spend it.”
q: The parable of one who learns sacred knowledge and then does not share it is like one who stores up treasure and does not spend it.

title: Hadith on Mercy: Sinful believers eventually taken out of Hellfire
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One will be taken out of the Hellfire who said, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ and he had good in his heart like the weight of a grain of barley. Then, one will be taken out of Hellfire who said, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ and he had good in his heart like the weight of a grain of wheat. Then, one will be taken out of Hellfire who said, ‘there is no God but Allah,’ and he had good in his heart like the weight of a speck.”
q: One will be taken out of the Hellfire who said, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ and he had good in his heart like the weight of a grain of barley. Then, one will be taken out of Hellfire who said, ‘There is no God but Allah,’ and he had good in his heart like the weight of a grain of wheat. Then, one will be taken out of Hellfire who said, ‘there is no God but Allah,’ and he had good in his heart like the weight of a speck.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Defense: First verse revealed about fighting and jihad
t: Ibn Abbas reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was expelled from Mecca, Abu Bakr said, “They have expelled their Prophet. Verily, unto Allah we belong and unto him we will return. They will surely be ruined. Then, it was revealed: Permission is given to those who are being fought because they were wronged, for Allah has power to support them (22:39). I knew that there would be fighting.” Ibn Abbas said, “It was the first verse to be revealed about fighting.”
q: Permission is given to those who are being fought because they were wronged, for Allah has power to support them

title: Hadith on Sahaba: Virtues of Abu Bakr, Umar, ‘Ammar, and Ibn Mas’ud
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Follow these two men from my companions after me, Abu Bakr and Umar. Accept the guidance of ‘Ammar, and take the advice of Ibn Mas’ud.”
q: Follow these two men from my companions after me, Abu Bakr and Umar. Accept the guidance of ‘Ammar, and take the advice of Ibn Mas’ud.

title: Ibrahim on Greetings: Say as-Salaamu ‘Alaykum for the angels too
t: Al-A’mash reported: Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you greet a single person with peace, then say: Peace be upon you all. Verily, the angels are with him.”

title: Hadith on Akhirah: Umar weeps at the poverty of the Prophet
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: I entered the room of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was lying on his side over a mat. I sat down as he drew up his lower garment and he was not wearing anything else. The mat had left marks on his side. I looked at the Prophet’s cupboard and I saw a handful of barely in a small amount, the same of mimosa leaves in the corner, and a leather bag hanging to the side. My eyes started to tear up, and the Prophet said, “What makes you weep, son of Khattab?” I said, “O Prophet of Allah, why should I not cry that this mat has left marks on your side and I see little in this cupboard? Caesar and Khosrau live among fruits and springs, while you are the Messenger of Allah and His chosen, yet this is your cupboard.” The Prophet said, “O son of Khattab, are you not pleased that they are for us in the Hereafter and for them in the world?” I said, “Of course.”
q: What makes you weep, son of Khattab? … O son of Khattab, are you not pleased that they are for us in the Hereafter and for them in the world?

title: Aisha on Ignorance: People fast to criticize what they do not know
t: ‘Abbad ibn Abdullah reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her said, “How quick are people to fault what they have no knowledge about!”

title: Hadith on Sunnah: Twelve raka’at of al-Sunan al-Rawatib prayers
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever perseveres in performing twelve cycles of prayer from the Sunnah, Allah will build a house for him in Paradise. They are four cycles before noon prayer and two after it, two cycles after sunset prayer, two cycles after evening prayer, and two cycles before dawn prayer.”
q: Whoever perseveres in performing twelve cycles of prayer from the Sunnah, Allah will build a house for him in Paradise. They are four cycles before noon prayer and two after it, two cycles after sunset prayer, two cycles after evening prayer, and two cycles before dawn prayer.

title: Fudayl on Hikmah: Many scholars but few who have wisdom
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: A man said to Al-Fudayl, may Allah have mercy on him, “The scholars are many.” Al-Fudayl said, “But those with wisdom are few.”

title: Hadith on Anas: Here is your little servant, Anas ibn Malik
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered our home and it was only me, my mother, and my aunt Umm Haram. The Prophet said, “Stand that I may pray with you a voluntary prayer.” He prayed with us, then supplicated for the people of the household to have every good in the world and in the Hereafter. My mother said, “O Messenger of Allah, here is your little servant. Supplicate to Allah for him.” The Prophet supplicated for me to have every good and at the end of his supplication, he said, “O Allah, increase him in wealth, in children, and bless him in them.”
q: Stand that I may pray with you a voluntary prayer. … O Allah, increase him in wealth, in children, and bless him in them.

title: Artah on Revenge: Believers do not take revenge for their egos
t: Al-Khallal reported: Artah ibn al-Mundhir, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The believer does not seek vengeance for the sake of himself. The Quran and Sunnah have prevented him from that. He has been restrained.”

title: Hadith on Qulub: Most beloved of hearts to Allah are the softest
t: Abu ‘Inabah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has vessels among the people of the earth, and the vessels of your Lord are the hearts of His righteous servants. The most beloved of them to Him are the softest and most tender of them.”
q: Verily, Allah has vessels among the people of the earth, and the vessels of your Lord are the hearts of His righteous servants. The most beloved of them to Him are the softest and most tender of them.

title: Ahmad on Amr: Enjoin good, forbid evil with humble gentleness
t: Muhanna reported: I asked Abu Abdullah Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, about enjoining good and forbidding evil, “How should one enjoin it?” Ahmad said, “One should enjoin good with gentleness and humility. If they make him hear what he dislikes, he should not get angry such that he wants to avenge himself.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Rulers: Do not confront rulers if they will kill you
t: Sa’id ibn Jubayr reported: I asked Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, “Shall I enjoin good and forbid evil upon the ruler?” Ibn Abbas said, “If you fear he will kill you, then no.” Then, I asked him again and he said the same to me. Then, I asked him again and he said the same to me and also said, “If you must do so, then do it between you and him privately.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Mothers: Good to mothers best deed to draw near to Allah
t: ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar reported: A man came to Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said, “I proposed to a woman and she refused to marry me. Another man proposed to her and she was happy to marry him. I became jealous and I killed her. Is there any repentance for me?” Ibn Abbas said, “Is your mother alive?” The man said no. Ibn Abbas said, “Repent to Allah Almighty and draw close to him in worship as much as you can.” I went to Ibn Abbas and I asked him, “Why did you ask if his mother was alive?” Ibn Abbas said, “Verily, I do not know of any deed better to bring one closer to Allah Almighty than goodness to one’s mother.”

title: Hadith on Aunts: Be good to your mother and her sisters
t: Ibn Umar reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have committed a great sin. Is there any repentance for me?” The Prophet said, “Is your mother with you?” The man said no. The Prophet said, “Is your mother’s sister with you?” The man said yes. The Prophet said, “Be good to her.”
q: Is your mother with you? … Is your mother’s sister with you? … Be good to her.

title: Hadith on Salat: Recommended two raka’at before Maghrib
t: Abdullah ibn al-Muzanni reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Pray before the sunset prayer.” The Prophet said on the third time, “For whomever wishes,” as he disliked for people to consider it an obligatory tradition.
q: Pray before the sunset prayer. … For whomever wishes,

title: Hadith on Hadith: The Prophet’s miracle for Abu Huraira’s memory
t: Abu Huraira reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, I hear many traditions from you, but I forget them.” The Prophet said, “Spread open your garment.” I spread it and he placed something from his hand into it, saying, “Wrap it.” I wrapped it around me, and then I never forgot a tradition ever again.
q: Spread open your garment. … Wrap it.

title: Hadith on Sujud: Prostrate more to be with the Prophet in Paradise
t: Rabi’ah ibn Ka’b reported: I spent the night with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and I brought him water for his ablution and his needs. The Prophet said to me, “Ask.” I said, “I ask for your companionship in Paradise.” The Prophet said, “And anything else besides that?” I said, “That is all.” The Prophet said, “Then help me do it for you by prostrating often.”
q: Ask … And anything else besides that? … Then help me do it for you by prostrating often.

title: Hadith on Jokes: Not allowed to play about divorce, freedom
t: Fadallah ibn ‘Ubayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is not permissible to jest about three matters: divorce, marriage, and emancipation.”
q: It is not permissible to jest about three matters: divorce, marriage, and emancipation.

title: Hadith on Poverty: The Prophet’s family endures hardship, starvation
t: Aisha reported: We in the household of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, used to live for a whole month without cooking anything over a fire. We would have nothing to eat but dates and water.

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for purity after beginning prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, began the opening exaltation of prayer, he would remain silent for a short while before reciting. I said, “O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be ransomed for you! What do you say in the silent period between your exaltation and recitation?” The Prophet said, “I say: O Allah, make the distance between me and my sins like the distance between the east and the west. O Allah, purify me from my sins just as the white cloth is purified from filth. O Allah, cleanse me of my sins with the likes of snow, water, and ice.”
q: I say: O Allah, make the distance between me and my sins like the distance between the east and the west. O Allah, purify me from my sins just as the white cloth is purified from filth. O Allah, cleanse me of my sins with the likes of snow, water, and ice.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Haith on Jihad: No divine reward in fighting for spoils of war
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever joins a military campaign in the way of Allah with no intention but to acquire as much as a rope in spoils, he will only have what he intended.”
q: Whoever joins a military campaign in the way of Allah with no intention but to acquire as much as a rope in spoils, he will only have what he intended.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Idolatry: O Allah, do not make my grave an idol
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, do not turn my grave into an idol that is worshiped. Allah has cursed people who take the graves of their prophets as places of worship.”
q: O Allah, do not turn my grave into an idol that is worshiped. Allah has cursed people who take the graves of their prophets as places of worship.

title: Hadith on Faith: O Allah, make faith in Islam beloved in our hearts
t: Rifa’ah ibn Rafi’ reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, make faith beloved to us and beautify it in our hearts, and make unbelief, wickedness, and disobedience hateful to us, and make us among the rightly-guided. O Allah, let us pass away as Muslims, live as Muslims, and let us be joined with the righteous.”
