q: O Allah, make faith beloved to us and beautify it in our hearts, and make unbelief, wickedness, and disobedience hateful to us, and make us among the rightly-guided. O Allah, let us pass away as Muslims, live as Muslims, and let us be joined with the righteous.

title: Hadith on Gratitude: Praise be to Allah who fed us, sheltered us
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would say when he retired to his bed, “All praise is due to Allah who has fed us, given us drink, sufficed us, and sheltered us. How many are those who do not have enough and have no shelter?”
q: All praise is due to Allah who has fed us, given us drink, sufficed us, and sheltered us. How many are those who do not have enough and have no shelter?

title: Ibrahim on Backbiting: Fear of speaking about other’s faults, tested like them
t: Al-A’mash reported: Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, I will see something I dislike in someone, and nothing stops me from speaking about it except fear of being put to trial in the same way.”

title: Hadith on Qiyamah: Animals fear coming of the Hour, except humans and jinn
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no creature but that it is alert on Friday when it awakens until the sun sets, anxious of the Hour, except for humans and jinn.”
q: There is no creature but that it is alert on Friday when it awakens until the sun sets, anxious of the Hour, except for humans and jinn.

title: Hadith on Children: Kids climb over the Prophet’s back as he prays
t: Shidad ibn al-Had reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us for one of the evening prayers and he was carrying his grandson Hasan, or Husayn. The Prophet came forward and put him down, then began prayer with exaltation and prayed. He prostrated at the end of his prayer for a long time. I raised my head and the child was upon the Prophet’s back while he was prostrating, so I returned to my prostration. When the Prophet finished the prayer, people said, “O Messenger of Allah, you prostrated at the end of your prayer for a long time, until we thought something happened or you received a revelation.” The Prophet said, “None of that that happened. Rather, my grandson was riding on my back and I disliked to rush him before he met his needs.”
q: None of that that happened. Rather, my grandson was riding on my back and I disliked to rush him before he met his needs.

title: Hadith on Amulets: Wearing good luck charms an act of idolatry
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, received a group of men and he accepted the pledge of nine of them, while he refrained from one. They said, “O Messenger of Allah, you accepted the pledge of nine men and left this one out?” The Prophet said, “Verily, there is an amulet upon him.” The man took it in his hand and cut it, then the Prophet accepted his pledge and he said, “Whoever hangs an amulet around his neck has committed an act of idolatry.”
q: Verily, there is an amulet upon him. … Whoever hangs an amulet around his neck has committed an act of idolatry.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Amulets: Disapproval of Quranic talismans, necklaces
t:
Ibrahim al-Nakha’i reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, disapproved of hanging anything from the Quran around the neck.

Ibrahim said, “They disapproved of all types of amulets, whether it contained the Quran or not.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Why not ask for good in this life and the Hereafter?
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, visited a sick man among the Muslims and he was so emaciated that he was like thin bird. The Prophet said to him, “Have you supplicated for anything or asked from Allah?” The man said, “Yes. I said: O Allah, as long as I am safe in the Hereafter, hasten my punishment in this world.” The Prophet said, “Glory be to Allah! You cannot withstand it. Why did you not say: O Allah, give us goodness in the world and goodness in the Hereafter and save us from the punishment of the Hellfire (2:201)?” Then, the man supplicated to Allah for it and he was healed.
q: Have you supplicated for anything or asked from Allah? … Glory be to Allah! You cannot withstand it. Why did you not say: O Allah, give us goodness in the world and goodness in the Hereafter and save us from the punishment of the Hellfire

title: Hadith on Tuba: Blessed tree in Paradise to clothe the righteous
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: A man said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “What is Tuba (13:29)?” The Prophet said, “It is a tree in Paradise as wide as a hundred years of travel. The clothes of the people of Paradise will come from its leaves.”
q: It is a tree in Paradise as wide as a hundred years of travel. The clothes of the people of Paradise will come from its leaves.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Mushaf: Umar convinces Abu Bakr to collect the Quran
t: Zayd ibn Thabit reported: Abu Bak sent for me after the people of Al-Yamamah were killed and Umar ibn al-Khattab was with him. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Umar came to me and said that many reciters of the Quran were killed in the fighting at Al-Yamamah, saying: I am afraid more reciters will be killed in battles to come and much of the Quran will be lost, and I think you should order for the Quran to be compiled. I said to Umar: How can you do something that was not done by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him? Umar said: By Allah, this will be a good thing. Umar continued to appeal to me until Allah opened my heart to that and I saw the good in it that Umar saw.”

title: Hadith on Faith: Blessed is one who has faith without seeing him
t: Abdur Rahman al-Juhani reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of one who has faith in you, believes in you, and follows you, but never saw you?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He is blessed. Again, he is blessed. Again, he is blessed.”
q: He is blessed. Again, he is blessed. Again, he is blessed

title: Hadith on Salat: Aisha describes the Prophet’s prayer
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would begin his prayer by exalting Allah and reciting the verses, “All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds,” (1:1). When he bowed, he would not hold his head up or drop it down, but rather he would be between that. When he raised his head from bowing, he would not prostrate until he stood up completely. When he raised his head from prostration, he would not prostrate again until he sat up completely. He would supplicate with the greeting prayer (al-tahiyyah) at the end of every two cycles. He would lay down his left foot and prop up his right foot. He prohibited sitting on the heels like Satan, or spreading out one’s arms like a wild beast. He would end the prayer with the invocation of peace.
q: All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds

title: Hadith on Adhan: Uthman institutes third call to prayer on Friday
t: Al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid reported: The announcement of Friday prayer was first made when the Imam would sit upon the pulpit in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as well as Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them. In the time of Uthman, the number of people increased, so he added a third announcement at al-Zawra’, a place in the market of Medina.

title: Hadith on Dua: Gates of heaven opened for good supplication
t: Ibn Umar reported: We were praying with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and a man among the people said, “Allah is the Greatest of the Great. All abundant praise is due to Allah, glory be to Him, morning and evening.” The Prophet said after the prayer, “Who said these words?” A man said, “It was me, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “I was amazed at how the gates of heaven were opened for it.”
q: Who said these words? … I was amazed at how the gates of heaven were opened for it.

title: Hadith on Shaytan: Believers exhaust their devils by obeying Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the believer will wear down his devils by obedience to Allah, just as one of you wears down his camel on a journey.”
q: Verily, the believer will wear down his devils by obedience to Allah, just as one of you wears down his camel on a journey.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Scholars: Death of ‘Ulama an irreplaceable loss
t: Al-Hasan reported: Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The death of a scholar is a loss that cannot be replaced for as long as the day and night revolve.”

title: Hadith on Hypocrisy: He sees other’s faults but forgets his own
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One of you sees the speck in his brother’s eye while he forgets the log in his own eye.”
q: One of you sees the speck in his brother’s eye while he forgets the log in his own eye.

title: Aisha on Death: Sudden death is mercy for believers, regret for wicked
t: Abu al-Ahwas reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “A sudden death is mercy for the believer and regretful for the wicked.”

title: Hadith on Loans: Best of you are excellent in repaying debts
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sought a loan for a camel and he repaid it with a better camel, saying, “The best of you are excellent in repayment.”
q: The best of you are excellent in repayment.

title: Ibn Abbas on Death: This is how Islamic knowledge is lost
t: Al-Zuhri reported: When they lowered Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, into his grave, Ibn Abbas said, “Whoever would like to see how knowledge is lost, this here is the loss of knowledge.”

title: Hadith on Mahdi: Righteous believers force the Mahdi to be Caliph
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will be a conflict with the death of a Caliph and a man among the residents of Medina will go out fleeing to Mecca. Some people will come to pledge allegiance to him, although he is unwilling, and they will pledge allegiance to him between the corner of the Ka’bah and the station of Abraham. An army from Syria will be dispatched for him and they will be swallowed in the desert between Mecca and Medina. When the people see that, the saints of Syria and the strong tribes of Iraq will come to him and pledge allegiance to him between the corner and the station.”
q: There will be a conflict with the death of a Caliph and a man among the residents of Medina will go out fleeing to Mecca. Some people will come to pledge allegiance to him, although he is unwilling, and they will pledge allegiance to him between the corner of the Ka’bah and the station of Abraham. An army from Syria will be dispatched for him and they will be swallowed in the desert between Mecca and Medina. When the people see that, the saints of Syria and the strong tribes of Iraq will come to him and pledge allegiance to him between the corner and the station.

title: Hadith on Mahdi: The Ummah becomes great by the Mahdi
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Mahdi will appear in the latter part of my nation. Allah will grant him rain to bring produce from the earth. He will give out wealth appropriately, cattle will be plentiful, and the nation will become great. He will live as ruler for seven or eight years.”
q: The Mahdi will appear in the latter part of my nation. Allah will grant him rain to bring produce from the earth. He will give out wealth appropriately, cattle will be plentiful, and the nation will become great. He will live as ruler for seven or eight years.

title: Hadith on Mahdi: Earth to be filled with justice by the Mahdi
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Mahdi will be from my lineage, with a curved nose. He will fill the earth with justice and equity, just as it had been filled with tyranny and oppression. He will rule for seven years.”
q: The Mahdi will be from my lineage, with a curved nose. He will fill the earth with justice and equity, just as it had been filled with tyranny and oppression. He will rule for seven years.

title: Hadith on Mahdi: The Mahdi is a descendant of Fatimah bint Muhammad
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Mahdi will be from my offspring, among the descendants of Fatimah.”
q: The Mahdi will be from my offspring, among the descendants of Fatimah.

title: Hadith on Mahdi: Allah will raise up the Mahdi in a single night
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Mahdi is from us, the prophetic household. Allah will set right his affairs in a single night.”
q: The Mahdi is from us, the prophetic household. Allah will set right his affairs in a single night.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Mahdi: World will not end until appearance of the Mahdi
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The world will not pass away until the Arabs are ruled by a man from my household, whose name agrees with my name.”
q: The world will not pass away until the Arabs are ruled by a man from my household, whose name agrees with my name.

title: Hadith on ‘Ashura: Fasting 9th and 10th of Muharram
t:
Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered fasting on the day of ‘Ashura, the tenth of al-Muharram.

Imam al-Tirmidhi said, “It is reported from Ibn Abbas that he said to fast on the ninth and tenth of the month and to do so differently from the Jews, and this tradition is the same as was said by Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq.”

title: Dawud on Gratitude: Hidden blessings are in each breath day and night
t: Al-Qurtubi reported: David, upon him be peace, said, “O Lord, show me the hidden blessings upon me.” Allah Almighty said, “O David, breath,” so David took a breath. Allah said, “Who counts these blessings in each day and night?”

title: Hadith on Funerals: Make sincere supplication for the dead
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you have prayed over your deceased, offer a sincere supplication for him.”
q: When you have prayed over your deceased, offer a sincere supplication for him.

title: Hadith on Islam: Ibn Umar, why do you not go for jihad?
t: Tawus reported: A man said to Abdullah ibn Umar, “Why do you not join the military campaigns?” Ibn Umar said, “I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: Verily, Islam is built upon five: to testify there is no God but Allah, to establish prayer, to give charity, to fast the month of Ramadan, and to perform pilgrimage to the House.”
q: Verily, Islam is built upon five: to testify there is no God but Allah, to establish prayer, to give charity, to fast the month of Ramadan, and to perform pilgrimage to the House.

title: Ibn Sireen on Sahaba: Whoever degrades Abu Bakr and Umar
t: Ayyub reported: Muhammad ibn Sirin, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I suspect that a man who denigrates Abu Bakr and Umar does not love the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.”

title: Abdullah on Weeping: Cry from fear of Allah, or pretend to cry
t: Ibn Abi Mulaykah reported: I was sitting with Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with him, by the stone of the Ka’bah and he mentioned a prophetic tradition, then he said, “Weep! If you do not find yourself weeping, then feign weeping. By the one in whose hand is my soul, if you truly knew, one of you would cry out until his voice is hoarse and pray until his back is broken.”

title: Umar on Humility: Allah have mercy on one who corrects me
t: ‘Abbad ibn ‘Abbad reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “May Allah have mercy on the one who shows me my faults.”

title: Hadith on Tashahhud: Looking at the finger while pointing in prayer
t:
Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would sit in prayer, he would place his left foot between his thigh and shin, stretch his right foot, place his left hand on his left knee, place his right hand on his right thigh, and point with his finger.

In another narration, Abdullah said: The gaze of the Prophet would not go beyond his index finger.

title: Muslim on Sujud: Looking at place of prostration in prayer
t: Abu Qilabah reported: I asked Muslim ibn Yasar, may Allah have mercy on him, “Where should one fix his gaze in prayer?” Muslim said, “If it is where you prostrate, it is good.”

title: Hadith on Parents: How to maintain relations with deceased parents?
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever would like to maintain relations with his father in his grave, let him maintain relations with his father’s brothers after him.”
q: Whoever would like to maintain relations with his father in his grave, let him maintain relations with his father’s brothers after him.

title: Hadith on ‘Ashura: Fasting day of ‘Ashura with 9th of Muharram
t: Al-Hakam ibn al-A’raj reported: I went to Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and I said, “Tell me about fasting the day of ‘Ashura.” Ibn Abbas said, “When you see the crescent of the month of al-Muharram, count the days and wake up to fast on the ninth day.” I said, “Is this how the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, fasted it?” Ibn Abbas said, “Yes.”

title: Hadith on Jannah: You will have whatever you want in Paradise
t: Buraydah ibn al-Hasib reported: A man asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “O Messenger of Allah, will there be camels in Paradise?” The Prophet said, “If Allah admits you into Paradise, you will have therein whatever your soul desires and pleases your eyes.”
q: If Allah admits you into Paradise, you will have therein whatever your soul desires and pleases your eyes.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Tawhid: They have not justly estimated Allah
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: There was a Rabbi who came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “O Muhammad, Allah will place the heavens on a finger, the earth on a finger, the mountains on a finger, the trees and rivers on a finger, and the rest of creation on a finger, then he will say: I am the King.” The Prophet laughed, and he recited the verse, “They have not estimated Allah as is due to Him.” (39:67)
q: They have not estimated Allah as is due to Him.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Akhirah: Whoever makes the Hereafter a primary concern
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is concerned about the Hereafter, Allah will place richness in his heart, bring his affairs together, and the world will inevitably come to him. Whoever is concerned about the world, Allah will place poverty between his eyes, disorder his affairs, and he will get nothing of the world but what is decreed for him.”
q: Whoever is concerned about the Hereafter, Allah will place richness in his heart, bring his affairs together, and the world will inevitably come to him. Whoever is concerned about the world, Allah will place poverty between his eyes, disorder his affairs, and he will get nothing of the world but what is decreed for him.

title: Hadith on Salat: Allah reduces prayers from fifty to five daily
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: Fifty prayers were obligated upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when he was taken on his night journey. Then, it was reduced until it was set at five and an announcement was made, “O Muhammad, My word is never changed, so these five prayers will be counted as fifty.”
q: O Muhammad, My word is never changed, so these five prayers will be counted as fifty.

title: Ibn Mubarak on Blessings: Best things a human being is given from Allah
t: Habib al-Jallab reported: I asked Ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him, “What is the best thing a human being can be given?” He said, “Innate intelligence.” I said, “What if it is not so?” He said, “Good manners.” I said, “What if it is not so?” He said, “A kind brother he can consult.” I said, “What if it is not so?” He said, “Long periods of silence.” I said, “What if it is not so?” He said, “An early death.”

title: Hadith on Parents: Best of believers serve their noble parents
t: Ka’b ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked, “Which of the people is best?” The Prophet said, “A believer in service of two noble parents.”
q: A believer in service of two noble parents.

title: Hadith on Ikhlas: Idolaters ask for the lineage of Allah Almighty
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: The idolaters asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “Tell us the lineage of your Lord.” Then, Allah revealed the verse, “Say: He is Allah, the One, Allah the Eternal Refuge.” (112:1-2)
q: Say: He is Allah, the One, Allah the Eternal Refuge.

title: Hadith on Istighatha: Seek divine help from Allah, not the Prophet
t:
‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: Abu Bakr said, “Come, let us seek the aid of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, from this hypocrite.” The Prophet said, “That is not done for me. Verily, that is only done for Allah Almighty.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “Deliverance is not to be sought from me. Verily, deliverance is only sought from Allah.”
q: That is not done for me. Verily, that is only done for Allah Almighty. … Deliverance is not to be sought from me. Verily, deliverance is only sought from Allah.

title: Hadith on Shirk: Origin of idolatry in glorifying ancestors
t: ‘Ata’ reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “All of the idols among the people of Noah appeared among the Arabs later. They were the names of righteous men among the people of Noah. When they passed away, Satan inspired in their people to build statues in the places they used to sit and name them by their names. They did so and they were not worshiped until the first generation passed away and knowledge was lost; then they were worshiped.”

title: Hadith on Shirk: Whoever dies calling upon a partner with Allah
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, made a statement and I made another in his presence. The Prophet said, “Whoever dies while calling upon a partner besides Allah will enter the Hellfire.” I said, “Whoever dies without calling upon a partner besides Allah will enter Paradise.”
q: Whoever dies while calling upon a partner besides Allah will enter the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Huquq: Be fair and measured in seeking your rights
t:
Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever seeks a right, let him seek it with restraint, whether it is fulfilled or unfulfilled.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “Take your rights with restraint, whether it is fulfilled or unfulfilled.”
q: Whoever seeks a right, let him seek it with restraint, whether it is fulfilled or unfulfilled. … Take your rights with restraint, whether it is fulfilled or unfulfilled.

title: Hadith on Qubur: Believers in grave want to give family good news
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the believer sees how spacious his grave has become, he will say: Let me go back to my family to give the good news! It will be said to him: Reside where you are.”
q: When the believer sees how spacious his grave has become, he will say: Let me go back to my family to give the good news! It will be said to him: Reside where you are.

title: Hadith on Tawassul: Seeking the Prophet’s supplication in his lifetime
t: Uthman ibn Hunayf reported: A blind man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Supplicate for Allah to heal me.” The Prophet said, “I will supplicate for you if you wish, or it is better for you to be patient if you wish.” The man said, “Supplicate for me.” The Prophet ordered him to perform ablution in the best manner and to supplicate with these words, “O Allah, I ask You and turn to You by Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of Mercy. I turn by you to my Lord to fulfill this need of mine. O Allah, accept his intercession for me.”
q: I will supplicate for you if you wish, or it is better for you to be patient if you wish.

title: Hadith on Dua: No request better than for wellness in world, Hereafter
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No supplication a servant can say is better than this: O Allah, I ask You for wellness in the world and in the Hereafter.”
q: No supplication a servant can say is better than this: O Allah, I ask You for wellness in the world and in the Hereafter.

title: Hadith on Envy: Everyone blessed will be envied, so be cautious
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Seek help in the fulfillment of your needs by being discrete, for everyone who is given a blessing will be envied.”

title: Hadith on Akhirah: Death is only a relief if Allah forgives you
t: Aisha reported: It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, this woman has died and is relieved from suffering.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, became angry and he said, “Verily, one is only relieved from suffering if they are forgiven by Allah.”
q: Verily, one is only relieved from suffering if they are forgiven by Allah.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hudhayfah on Munkar: Dead among living are those who do not reject evil
t: Abu al-Tufayl reported: It was said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, “What do you mean by your statement: The dead person is not one relieved by death, but rather the truly dead person is dead among the living?” Hudhayfah said, “It is one who does not reject evil with his hand, nor his tongue, nor his heart.”

title: Hadith on Trade: No undermining the sales of each other
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no undermining the sales of one another, nor undermining the marriages of one another.”
q: There is no undermining the sales of one another, nor undermining the marriages of one another.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Nikah: Do not undermine each other’s marriage proposals
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man must not offer a marriage proposal to a woman if his brother has already done so, nor may he try to outbid the price of his brother. A woman must not be joined in marriage with her paternal aunt, nor her maternal aunt. A woman must not ask for her sister to be divorced to deprive her of what is rightfully hers. Rather, let her get married, for Allah she will only have what Allah has decreed for her.”
q: A man must not offer a marriage proposal to a woman if his brother has already done so, nor may he try to outbid the price of his brother. A woman must not be joined in marriage with her paternal aunt, nor her maternal aunt. A woman must not ask for her sister to be divorced to deprive her of what is rightfully hers. Rather, let her get married, for Allah she will only have what Allah has decreed for her.

title: Hadith on Tawhid: What are two inevitabilities of life?
t: Jabir reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, what are the two inevitabilities?” The Prophet said, “Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise, and whoever dies associating anything with Allah will enter Hellfire.”
q: Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise, and whoever dies associating anything with Allah will enter Hellfire.

title: Ali on Quran: Abu Bakr first to compile Quran into one book
t: ‘Abdu Khayr reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “May Allah have mercy on Abu Bakr. He was the first to compile the Quran between two covers.”

title: Awza’i on Sunnah: Brotherhood, Halal money, Sunnah to become rare
t: Al-Mu’afi ibn ‘Imran reported: Al-Awza’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A time will come to people in which the rarest thing of that era will be a friendly brother, or a lawfully-earned coin, or a practice from the Sunnah.”

title: Bishr on Blame: Do not give up on your principles, fearing criticism
t: Al-Qasim ibn Munabbih reported: Bishr ibn al-Harith, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Do not give into anything due to fear of being blamed by people.”

title: Hadith on Marriage: Get married, or fast to control your urges
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Marriage is part of my Sunnah. Whoever does not act upon my Sunnah is not part of me. Give each other in marriage, for I will boast of your great numbers before the nations. Whoever has the means, let him contract a marriage. Whoever does not have the means should fast, as fasting will restrain his impulses.”
q: Marriage is part of my Sunnah. Whoever does not act upon my Sunnah is not part of me. Give each other in marriage, for I will boast of your great numbers before the nations. Whoever has the means, let him contract a marriage. Whoever does not have the means should fast, as fasting will restrain his impulses.

title: Hadith on Praise: Creation glorifies Creator, except devils and fools
t: ‘Amr ibn ‘Abasah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The sun does not rise over any creation of Allah but that it glorifies Allah, except for the devils and the fools among the children of Adam.”
q: The sun does not rise over any creation of Allah but that it glorifies Allah, except for the devils and the fools among the children of Adam.

title: Hasan on Sunnah: O people of Sunnah, be gentle with each other
t: Mubarak reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “O followers of the Sunnah! Be gentle with each other, may Allah have mercy on you, for you are surely in the minority of people.”

title: Hadith on Sunnah: Whoever forsakes Sunnah is not part of Muhammad
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever does not desire my Sunnah is not a part of me.”
q: Whoever does not desire my Sunnah is not a part of me.

title: Hadith on Family: Best charity given to estranged relatives
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the best act of charity is one given to an estranged relative.”
q: Verily, the best act of charity is one given to an estranged relative.

title: Hadith on Family: Best charity given to reconcile family members
t: Hakim ibn Hizam reported: A man asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “What act of charity is best?” The Prophet said, “One given to an estranged relative.”
q: One given to an estranged relative.

title: Hadith on Family: The Prophet enjoins family ties on his deathbed
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said in his illness before he passed away, “Your family relations! Your family relations!”
q: Your family relations! Your family relations!

title: Abu Huraira on Taqwa: God-fearing piety like traveling a thorny path
t: Abu Salih reported: A man said to Abu Huraira, may Allah be pleased with him, “What is God-fearing mindfulness?” Abu Huraira said, “Have you ever taken a thorny path?” The man said yes. Abu Huraira said, “What did you do?” The man said, “If I saw thorns, I would avoid them, pass over them, or stop short of them.” Abu Huraira said, “That is God-fearing mindfulness.”

title: Hadith on Gratitude: Be thankful for little things, thankful to people
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is not grateful for small things will not be grateful for large things. Whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah Almighty.”
q: Whoever is not grateful for small things will not be grateful for large things. Whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah Almighty.

title: Hadith on Rahim: Allah loves family ties, hates separation
t: Qatadah reported: A man of Khath’am came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, asaying, “Are you the one who considers himself the Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Yes.” The man said, “O Messenger of Allah, which deeds are most beloved to Allah?” The Prophet said, “Faith in Allah.” The man said, “Then what?” The Prophet said, “To maintain family relationships.” The man said, “O Messenger of Allah, which deeds are most hateful to Allah?” The Prophet said, “To associate idols with Allah.” The man said, “Then what?” The Prophet said, “To sever family relationships.” The man said, “Then what?” The Prophet said, “To enjoin evil and forbid good.”
q: Yes … Faith in Allah. … To maintain family relationships. … To associate idols with Allah. … To sever family relationships. … To enjoin evil and forbid good.

title: Hadith on Repentance: Every believer is tested with a sinful habit
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no believing servant but that he has a sin he habitually commits from time to time, or a sin entrenched in him that he does not abandon until he departs the world. Verily, the believer was created to be tested, both repenting and forgetful. If he is reminded, he will remember.”
q: There is no believing servant but that he has a sin he habitually commits from time to time, or a sin entrenched in him that he does not abandon until he departs the world. Verily, the believer was created to be tested, both repenting and forgetful. If he is reminded, he will remember.

title: Hadith on Istighfar: O Allah, Your mercy is greater than my sins
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O my sins! O my sins!” The Prophet said to him, “Say: O Allah, your forgiveness is vaster than my sins, and your mercy is more hopeful to me than my deeds.” The man said it, then the Prophet said, “Repeat it.” The man repeated it, then the Prophet said, “Repeat it again.” The man repeated it, then the Prophet said, “Stand up, for Allah has forgiven you.”
q: Say: O Allah, your forgiveness is vaster than my sins, and your mercy is more hopeful to me than my deeds. … Repeat it. … Repeat it again. … Stand up, for Allah has forgiven you.

title: Hadith on Nikah: Supplication upon giving a marriage proposal
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Keep your marriage proposal secret. Then, perform ablution in the best manner, pray for as much as Allah has written for you, praise and glorify your Lord, and then say: O Allah, you decree and none can decree against you. You know best and I do not know, for you are the Knower of the unseen. If you see good for me in this woman – and mention her name – in my religion, my worldly affairs, and my Hereafter, or if you see one better than her in my religion, my worldly affairs, and my Hereafter, then decree it for me through her.”
q: Keep your marriage proposal secret. Then, perform ablution in the best manner, pray for as much as Allah has written for you, praise and glorify your Lord, and then say: O Allah, you decree and none can decree against you. You know best and I do not know, for you are the Knower of the unseen. If you see good for me in this woman – and mention her name – in my religion, my worldly affairs, and my Hereafter, or if you see one better than her in my religion, my worldly affairs, and my Hereafter, then decree it for me through her.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Warraq on Humility: We’d treat them well until disdain left our hearts
t: Al-Qushayri reported: Abu al-Husayn al-Warraq, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whomever we hated to meet, we would not take revenge for our own sake. Rather, we would excuse him and show humility towards him. If we felt disdain enter our hearts for anyone, we would commit ourselves to his service and good treatment until it disappeared.”

title: Hadith on Romans: Muslims rejoice at victory of Christians
t: Abu Sa’id reported: On the day of Badr, the Romans were victorious over the Persians and the believers were pleased by that, as Allah had revealed the verse, “The Romans have been defeated in a nearby land. Yet following their defeat, they will triumph within three to nine years. The matter rests with Allah before and after victory, and on that day, the believers will rejoice at the victory willed by Allah,” (30:1-4). Thus, the believers rejoiced at the victory of the Romans over the Persians.
q: The Romans have been defeated in a nearby land. Yet following their defeat, they will triumph within three to nine years. The matter rests with Allah before and after victory, and on that day, the believers will rejoice at the victory willed by Allah

title: Umar on Nepotism: Betrayal of Islam to favor relatives at expense of others
t: Abdul Malik ibn ‘Umayr reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever employs a man among his loved ones or relatives, employing him for no other reason besides that, then he has betrayed Allah, His messenger, and the believers.”

title: Hadith on Talbiyah: Raising voice in answering call to pilgrimage
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A pilgrim never raises his voice answering the call to Allah but that he is given glad tidings, and a pilgrim never raises his voice in exalting Allah but that he is given glad tidings.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, of Paradise?” The Prophet said, “Yes.”
q: A pilgrim never raises his voice answering the call to Allah … but that he is given glad tidings, and a pilgrim never raises his voice in exalting Allah … but that he is given glad tidings. … Yes

title: Hadith on Wills: Giving charity on behalf of deceased parents
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “My father has died and he left behind some property without drafting a will for it. While his sin be expiated if I give charity on his behalf?” The Prophet said, “Yes.”
q: Yes

title: Hadith on Deeds: Faith, Jihad, Hajj better than all other deeds
t: Ma’iz al-Tamimi reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked, “Which deeds are best?” The Prophet said, “Faith in Allah alone, then jihad, and then a blessed pilgrimage are better than all other deeds like the distance between the rising of the sun and its setting.”
q: Faith in Allah alone, then jihad, and then a blessed pilgrimage are better than all other deeds like the distance between the rising of the sun and its setting.

title: Hadith on Adha: The Prophet sacrifices an animal on Eid al-Adha
t:
Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: I was present with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, on Eid al-Adha at the place of prayer. When the Prophet finished his sermon, he came down from his pulpit and a ram was brought to him. The Prophet slaughtered it with his own hand, saying, “In the name of Allah and Allah is the greatest. This is from me and those of my nation who cannot offer a sacrifice.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “This was acted upon by the people of knowledge among the companions of the Prophet (ṣ) and others, that a man should say at the time of slaughtering: In the name of Allah, and Allah is the greatest. It is the opinion of Ibn al-Mubarak.”
q: In the name of Allah and Allah is the greatest. This is from me and those of my nation who cannot offer a sacrifice.

title: Hadith on Udhiyah: Supplication before sacrificing animals
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered for a ram to be brought as a sacrifice. The Prophet took the ram and laid it on its side to prepare for slaughtering, then he said, “In the name of Allah, O Allah, accept it from Muhammad, the house of Muhammad, and the nation of Muhammad.” Then, he sacrificed it.
q: In the name of Allah, O Allah, accept it from Muhammad, the house of Muhammad, and the nation of Muhammad.

title: Hadith on Salat: What the Imam and followers say in prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah heard those who praise him,” he would say, “O Allah, our Lord, for you is praise.” When the Prophet bowed and raised his head, he would declare the greatness of Allah. When he stood from the two prostrations, he would say, “Allah is the greatest.”
q: Allah heard those who praise him, … O Allah, our Lord, for you is praise. … Allah is the greatest.

title: Hadith on Salat: What to say when Imam rises in prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the Imam says, ‘Allah heard those who praise him,’ then say, ‘Our Lord, for you is praise.’ If one’s statement coincides with the statement of the angels, his previous sins will be forgiven.”
q: When the Imam says, ‘Allah heard those who praise him,’ then say, ‘Our Lord, for you is praise.’ If one’s statement coincides with the statement of the angels, his previous sins will be forgiven.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hadith: Distinguishing authentic or weak Hadith
t: Abu Humayd reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you hear a narration from me that your hearts recognize, settles your hair and skin, and you see it as close to you, then I am most deserving of it. If you hear a narration from me that your hearts reject, makes your hair stand and your skin crawl, and you see it as far from you, then I am the furthest from it.”
q: If you hear a narration from me that your hearts recognize, settles your hair and skin, and you see it as close to you, then I am most deserving of it. If you hear a narration from me that your hearts reject, makes your hair stand and your skin crawl, and you see it as far from you, then I am the furthest from it.

title: Umar on Inbreeding: Discouraging marriage within close bloodlines
t:
Ibn Abi Mulaykah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the house of Al-Sa’ib, “You have become frail, so marry intelligent people unrelated to you.”

Imam al-Shafi’i said, “Whenever the people of a household do not allow their women to marry men outside of their line, there will be fools among their children.”

title: Hadith on Dajjal: False Messiah targets women and families
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The False Messiah will come upon this marsh of Marriqanat. Most of those who go out to him will be women, to the extent that a man goes back to his wife, his mother, his daughter, his sister, and his aunt to shackle them tightly, fearing they would go out to him.”
q: The False Messiah will come upon this marsh of Marriqanat … . Most of those who go out to him will be women, to the extent that a man goes back to his wife, his mother, his daughter, his sister, and his aunt to shackle them tightly, fearing they would go out to him.

title: Hadith on Days: Friday, Day of Arafat, and Day of Resurrection
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witnessed day is the day of Arafat, and the witnessing day is Friday (85:2-3). The sun does not rise or set over a day better than it. In it is a moment in which a believing servant does not supplicate to Allah for good but that Allah will answer him, and he does not seek refuge from any evil thing but that Allah will grant him refuge.”
q: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witnessed day is the day of Arafat, and the witnessing day is Friday … The sun does not rise or set over a day better than it. In it is a moment in which a believing servant does not supplicate to Allah for good but that Allah will answer him, and he does not seek refuge from any evil thing but that Allah will grant him refuge.

title: Hadith on Hajj: Pilgrims not fasting on the day of Arafat
t: Maymunah reported: People had doubts about the fasting of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, on the day of Arafat. She sent him a cup of milk while he was standing on the plain and he drank from it while the people were looking at him.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Aisha on Arafat: No harm for pilgrims to fast Arafat if not too weak
t: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad reported: Aisha, mother of the believers, may Allah be pleased with her, fasted on the day of ‘Arafat as a pilgrim. Al-Qasim said, “I saw her in the evening on they day of Arafat as the Imam was departing. She stood until one could see the ground between her and the people, then she called for a drink and broke her fast.”

title: Hadith on Dunya: Endure harm in world for safety in Hereafter
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever seeks the world will be harmed in the Hereafter, and whoever seeks the Hereafter will be harmed in the world. Thus, be harmed by the ephemeral for the sake of the everlasting.”
q: Whoever seeks the world will be harmed in the Hereafter, and whoever seeks the Hereafter will be harmed in the world. Thus, be harmed by the ephemeral for the sake of the everlasting.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Three are guaranteed Paradise from Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Three people have a guarantee from Allah Almighty: a man who leaves his house to attend one of the mosques of Allah Almighty, a man who goes out waging a campaign in the way of Allah Almighty, and a man who goes out for the Hajj pilgrimage.”
q: Three people have a guarantee from Allah Almighty: a man who leaves his house to attend one of the mosques of Allah Almighty, a man who goes out waging a campaign in the way of Allah Almighty, and a man who goes out for the Hajj pilgrimage.

title: Hadith on Worship: Pray, give zakat, be upright to Allah
t: Samurah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Establish prayer, give charity, perform the Hajj and Umrah pilgrimages, and be upright; your affairs will be made upright.”
q: Establish prayer, give charity, perform the Hajj and Umrah pilgrimages, and be upright; your affairs will be made upright.

title: Hadith on Hajj: Allah boasts of the pilgrims at Arafat
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty boasts to His angels of the pilgrims on the afternoon of the day of Arafat, saying: Look at My servants, coming to Me disheveled and dusty!”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty boasts to His angels of the pilgrims on the afternoon of the day of Arafat, saying: Look at My servants, coming to Me disheveled and dusty!

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Best deed to declare no God but Allah
t: Abu Dharr reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, instruct me.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you do a bad deed, follow it with a good deed to wipe it out.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, is it a good deed to declare there is no God but Allah?” The Prophet said, “It is the best of good deeds.”
q: If you do a bad deed, follow it with a good deed to wipe it out. … It is the best of good deeds.

title: Hadith on Qadr: Better to ask Allah for salvation in Hereafter
t: Abdullah reported: Umm Habibah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, let me enjoy my husband, the Messenger of Allah, my father Abu Sufyan and my brother Mu’awiyyah.” The Prophet said, “You have asked Allah about terms already set, days already numbered, and provision already allocated. He does not speed up or delay anything from its appropriate time. If you were to ask Allah to grant you refuge from the punishment of Hellfire or punishment in the grave, it would have been better and preferable.”
q: You have asked Allah about terms already set, days already numbered, and provision already allocated. He does not speed up or delay anything from its appropriate time. If you were to ask Allah to grant you refuge from the punishment of Hellfire or punishment in the grave, it would have been better and preferable.

title: Hadith on Sahaba: Allah curses one who reviles the Companions
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The curse of Allah is upon the one who insults my companions.”
q: The curse of Allah is upon the one who insults my companions.

title: Hadith on Hypocrisy: This is the prayer of the hypocrites
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “This is the prayer of the hypocrites: He sits watching the sun decline until it is between the two horns of Satan, then he quickly pecks the ground four times while he only remembers Allah for a few moments.”
q: This is the prayer of the hypocrites: He sits watching the sun decline until it is between the two horns of Satan, then he quickly pecks the ground four times while he only remembers Allah for a few moments.

title: Hadith on Dunya: Bitterness of world is sweetness in Hereafter
t: Abu Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The sweetness of the world is bitterness in the Hereafter, and the bitterness of the world is sweetness in the Hereafter.”
q: The sweetness of the world is bitterness in the Hereafter, and the bitterness of the world is sweetness in the Hereafter.

title: Hadith on Siwak: Clean your mouth for the angels, the Quran
t: Ali reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when the servant uses the toothstick and then stands to pray, an angel stands behind him and listens to his recitation. The angel draws near until his mouth coincides with his and nothing of the Quran comes out of it but that it enters the heart of the angel. Thus, purify your mouths for the Quran.”
q: Verily, when the servant uses the toothstick and then stands to pray, an angel stands behind him and listens to his recitation. The angel draws near until his mouth coincides with his and nothing of the Quran comes out of it but that it enters the heart of the angel. Thus, purify your mouths for the Quran.

title: Hadith on Teeth: Until I feared my teeth would fall out
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I was ordered to use the toothstick so often that I was afraid my teeth might fall out.”
q: I was ordered to use the toothstick so often that I was afraid my teeth might fall out.

title: Hadith on Teeth: The Prophet uses the toothstick often
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I was ordered to use the toothstick so often that I thought something of it would be sent down to me in the Quran or revealed to me.”
q: I was ordered to use the toothstick so often that I thought something of it would be sent down to me in the Quran or revealed to me.

title: Hadith on Miswak: The Prophet brushes his teeth after night prayer
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would pray at night in cycles two by two, then he used the toothstick after he finished.

title: Hadith on Siwak: First thing the Prophet does at home
t: Shurayh reported: I asked Aisha, saying, “What was the first thing the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did when he entered his house?” Aisha said, “Use the toothstick.”

title: Hadith on Siwak: Clean mouth and teeth pleasing to the Lord
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must use the toothstick, as it is pleasant for the mouth and pleasing to the Lord.”
q: You must use the toothstick, as it is pleasant for the mouth and pleasing to the Lord.

title: Hadith on Teeth: You visit the Prophet with bad oral hygiene?
t: Al-‘Abbas reported: They entered upon the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, without having brushed their teeth. The Prophet said, “You enter upon me with unclean teeth? Go use the toothstick. Were it not hardship for my nation, I would have obligated them to use the toothstick at every prayer, just as I obligated them to perform ablution.”
q: You enter upon me with unclean teeth? Go use the toothstick. Were it not hardship for my nation, I would have obligated them to use the toothstick at every prayer, just as I obligated them to perform ablution.

title: Hadith on Siwak: Using Miswak with every ablution
t: Umm Habibah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Were it not hardship for my nation, I would have commanded them to use the toothstick with every prayer as they perform ablution.”
q: Were it not hardship for my nation, I would have commanded them to use the toothstick with every prayer as they perform ablution.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Wudu: Using the toothstick with every ablution
t: Ali reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Were it not hardship for my nation, I would have commanded them to use the toothstick with every ablution.”
q: Were it not hardship for my nation, I would have commanded them to use the toothstick with every ablution

title: Hadith on Punishment: Calamities afflict obedient, disobedient alike
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When evil appears on the earth, Allah sends down his punishment upon its inhabitants.” Aisha said, “Even if there are people who obey Allah Almighty among them?” The Prophet said, “Yes, then they will be sent back to the mercy of Allah Almighty.”
q: When evil appears on the earth, Allah sends down his punishment upon its inhabitants. … Yes, then they will be sent back to the mercy of Allah Almighty.

title: Hadith on Dhul-Hijjah: No better time for good deeds
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No good deeds can be done at a time better than these first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah.” It was said, “Not even jihad in the way of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Not even jihad in the way of Allah.”
q: No good deeds can be done at a time better than these first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. … Not even jihad in the way of Allah.

title: Sa’id on Dhul-Hijjah: Great striving in first ten days
t: Al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub reported: When Sa’id ibn Jubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, reached the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, he would exert himself in worship so greatly that he would nearly overwhelm himself.

title: Hadith on ‘Arafah: Blessings of Dhul-Hijjah, day of Arafat
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No days are better to Allah than the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah.” A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, are they better or time spent waging jihad in the way of Allah?” The Prophet said, “They are better than time spent waging jihad in the way of Allah. No day is better to Allah than the day of Arafat. Allah descends to the lowest heaven and He boasts to the inhabitants of the heavens about the inhabitants of the earth, saying: Look at My servants, appearing disheveled and dusty! They came from every mountain pass hoping for My mercy. They do not see My punishment, yet they do not see that on no day are more saved from Hellfire than the day of Arafat.”
q: No days are better to Allah than the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. … They are better than time spent waging jihad in the way of Allah. No day is better to Allah than the day of Arafat. Allah descends to the lowest heaven and He boasts to the inhabitants of the heavens about the inhabitants of the earth, saying: Look at My servants, appearing disheveled and dusty! They came from every mountain pass hoping for My mercy. They do not see My punishment, yet they do not see that on no day are more saved from Hellfire than the day of Arafat.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Guard your ablution, inwardly and outwardly
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Remain upright, as it is a blessing if you can do so. The best of your good deeds is prayer, and none can preserve his ablution but a believer.”
q: Remain upright, as it is a blessing if you can do so. The best of your good deeds is prayer, and none can preserve his ablution but a believer.
gf: Sahihli ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Salat: Know your best deed is the prayer
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Remain upright, though you cannot encompass it entirely. Know that the most favorable of your deeds is prayer and that none can preserve his ablution but a believer.”

title: Hadith on Sahaba: How Bilal ibn Rabah got into Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Bilal at the time of dawn prayer, “O Bilal, tell me of the most hopeful deed you practiced in Islam.  I heard the scuffle of your sandals before me in Paradise.” Bilal said, “The most hopeful deed to me is that I do not perform ablution by day or night but that I pray along with it as much as Allah has decreed me to pray.”
q: O Bilal, tell me of the most hopeful deed you practiced in Islam.  I heard the scuffle of your sandals before me in Paradise.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Remembrance of Allah heaviest on the Scale
t: Abu Salma reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Nothing is heavier on the Scale than to glorify Allah, to praise Allah, to declare there is no God but Allah, to declare Allah is the greatest, and for a Muslim parent whose righteous child passes away yet he bears it patiently for the sake of Allah.”
q: Nothing is heavier on the Scale than to glorify Allah, to praise Allah, to declare there is no God but Allah, to declare Allah is the greatest, and for a Muslim parent whose righteous child passes away yet he bears it patiently for the sake of Allah.

title: ‘Ammar on Faith: Justice, generosity, offering peace to the world
t: Silah reported: ‘Ammar ibn Yasir, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever has three qualities has completed the faith: a sense of fairness in yourself, spending in charity despite difficult circumstances, and offering peace to the world.”

title: Hadith on Oaths: Swear by Allah or keep quiet
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, found Umar ibn al-Khattab while he was upon his mount, swearing an oath by his father. The Prophet said, “Surely Allah prohibits you from swearing an oath by your fathers. Whoever swears an oath, let him swear by Allah or remain silent.”
q: Surely Allah prohibits you from swearing an oath by your fathers. Whoever swears an oath, let him swear by Allah or remain silent.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Abu Hatim on Hilm: Graceful patience to forgive without vengeance
t: Ibn Hibban reported: Abu Hatim, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Forbearance is most graceful when it is given despite having the power to take revenge.”

title: Hadith on Dhul-Hijjah: Fasting first nine days of Dhul-Hijjah
t: Hunaydah ibn Khalid reported: Some of the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said that he would fast the first nine days of the month of Dhul-Hijjah, the day of Ashura, and three days of every month, which would be the first Monday and Thursday of the month.

title: Hadith on Time: Take advantage of good moments Allah gives you
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do good deeds in the time that you have and take advantage of the moments of gentle breeze from the mercy of Allah. Verily, Allah has moments of gentle breeze from his mercy that he sends upon whomever he wills among his servants. Ask Allah to cover your faults and protect you from your anxieties.”
q: Do good deeds in the time that you have and take advantage of the moments of gentle breeze from the mercy of Allah. Verily, Allah has moments of gentle breeze from his mercy that he sends upon whomever he wills among his servants. Ask Allah to cover your faults and protect you from your anxieties.

title: Hadith on Salat: What to say when bowing, prostrating in prayer
t: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said three times while bowing in prayer, “Glory to my Lord, the Almighty,” and he said three times while prostrating in prayer, “Glory to my Lord, the Most High.”
q: Glory to my Lord, the Almighty, … Glory to my Lord, the Most High

title: Hadith on Sajdah: Supplication after reading a verse of prostration
t: Aisha reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prostrated after reading a verse of prostration in the Quran during the night prayer, he would say, “I prostrate my face to the One who created it and brought forth its hearing and its seeing by His ability and His might.”
q: I prostrate my face to the One who created it and brought forth its hearing and its seeing by His ability and His might.

title: Hadith on Dua: Seek refuge from Satan when entering mosque
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered the mosque, he would say, “I seek refuge in Allah Almighty, in his noble countenance, and in his everlasting authority from the accursed Satan.”
q: I seek refuge in Allah Almighty, in his noble countenance, and in his everlasting authority from the accursed Satan.

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet’s supplication in bowing, prostration
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say in his bowing and prostration, “Glory be to you, Allah our Lord, and your praises. Forgive me.”
q: Glory be to you, Allah our Lord, and your praises. Forgive me.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salat: Glorifying Allah minimum three times in bowing, prostrating
t:
Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you bows in prayer, let him say three times in his bowing: Glory be to my Lord, the Greatest. He will have completed his bowing and that is the least of it. Let him say three times in his prostration: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. He will have completed his prostration and that is the least of it.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “This was acted upon by the people of knowledge, that they preferred a man glorify Allah no less than three times in bowing and prostration.”
q: When one of you bows in prayer, let him say three times in his bowing: Glory be to my Lord, the Greatest. He will have completed his bowing and that is the least of it. Let him say three times in his prostration: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. He will have completed his prostration and that is the least of it.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet’s supplication after finishing prayer
t: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, finished the prayer and invoked peace, he would say, “There is no God but Allah, alone without partner. To him belongs the dominion, all praise, and he has power over all things. O Allah, none can prevent you from giving, and none can give to whomever you prevent. The riches of the rich are of no avail against you.”
q: There is no God but Allah, alone without partner. To him belongs the dominion, all praise, and he has power over all things. O Allah, none can prevent you from giving, and none can give to whomever you prevent. The riches of the rich are of no avail against you.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tashahhud: What to say at end of prayer
t: Ka’b ibn ‘Urjah reported: We asked, “O Messenger of Allah, how do we send blessings upon you and the people of the house? Allah has taught us how to send peace upon you.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Say: O Allah, send grace upon Muhammad and the house of Muhammad, just as You have sent grace upon Abraham and the house of Abraham. Verily, You are Praiseworthy and Majestic. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the house of Muhammad, just as You have blessed Abraham and the house of Abraham. Verily, You are Praiseworthy and Majestic.”
q: Say: O Allah, send grace upon Muhammad and the house of Muhammad, just as You have sent grace upon Abraham and the house of Abraham. Verily, You are Praiseworthy and Majestic. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the house of Muhammad, just as You have blessed Abraham and the house of Abraham. Verily, You are Praiseworthy and Majestic.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Shafi’i on Knowledge: No good in one who does not love knowledge
t: Ibn ‘Asakir reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whoever does not love knowledge, there is no good in him.”

title: Hadith on Salat: Performing ablution, prayer as Allah commanded
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever performs ablution and prayer as he has been commanded, he will be forgiven for his previous misdeeds.”
q: Whoever performs ablution and prayer as he has been commanded, he will be forgiven for his previous misdeeds.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Perfect ablution, five prayers expiation of sins
t: Uthman ibn Affan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever perfects his ablution as Allah Almighty has commanded him, the prescribed prayers will be an expiation for what occurs between them.”
q: Whoever perfects his ablution as Allah Almighty has commanded him, the prescribed prayers will be an expiation for what occurs between them.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Deeds to expiate sins, increase rewards
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you of that by which Allah expiates your sins and increases your good deeds?” They said, “Of course, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “Performing ablution thoroughly despite hardship, taking many steps to the mosque, and waiting for one prayer after another.”
q: Shall I not tell you of that by which Allah expiates your sins and increases your good deeds? … Performing ablution thoroughly despite hardship, taking many steps to the mosque, and waiting for one prayer after another.

title: Hadith on Masajid: Waiting in between congregational prayers expiates sins
t: Ali reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you of that by which Allah expiates sins? Thorough ablution despite hardship, working your feet in walking to the mosque, and waiting in between prayers will fully cleanse one of sins.”
q: Shall I not tell you of that by which Allah expiates sins? Thorough ablution despite hardship, working your feet in walking to the mosque, and waiting in between prayers will fully cleanse one of sins.

title: Hadith on Salat: Know what is being said in prayer
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No Muslim performs ablution and does so thoroughly, then stands for prayer while he knows what he is saying, but that he will return free of any fault like the day he was born from his mother. There will be no sin upon him.”
q: No Muslim performs ablution and does so thoroughly, then stands for prayer while he knows what he is saying, but that he will return free of any fault like the day he was born from his mother. There will be no sin upon him.

title: Hadith on Salat: Forgiveness for ablution, praying with excellence
t: ‘Abbad al-‘Abdi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No servant performs ablution in an excellent manner such that water covers his face, then he washes his arms until water covers his elbows, then he washes his feet until water covers his heels, and then he prays in an excellent manner, but that he will be forgiven for what he had done before.”
q: No servant performs ablution in an excellent manner such that water covers his face, then he washes his arms until water covers his elbows, then he washes his feet until water covers his heels, and then he prays in an excellent manner, but that he will be forgiven for what he had done before.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Wudu: Sins fall away by ablution and prayer
t: ‘Amr ibn ‘Abasah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None of you approach ablution and rinse his mouth and nose but that the sins of his face, mouth, and nose fall away. He does not wash his face as Allah commanded him but that the sins of his jaws fall away with the water. He does not wash his arms up to the elbows but that the sins of his hands to his fingertips fall away with the water. He does not wipe his head but that the sins of his head to his temples fall away with the water. He does not wash his feet to his ankles but that the sins of his feet to their tips fall away with the water. If he stands to pray, thanking, praising, and glorifying Allah as He deserves and devoting his heart only to Allah, his sins will depart from him like the day he was born from his mother.”
q: None of you approach ablution and rinse his mouth and nose but that the sins of his face, mouth, and nose fall away. He does not wash his face as Allah commanded him but that the sins of his jaws fall away with the water. He does not wash his arms up to the elbows but that the sins of his hands to his fingertips fall away with the water. He does not wipe his head but that the sins of his head to his temples fall away with the water. He does not wash his feet to his ankles but that the sins of his feet to their tips fall away with the water. If he stands to pray, thanking, praising, and glorifying Allah as He deserves and devoting his heart only to Allah, his sins will depart from him like the day he was born from his mother.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Prayer, walking to mosque an additional virtue
t: Abdullah al-Sunabihi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever performs ablution and rinses his mouth and nose, his sins committed with them are removed. When he washes his face, his sins committed with his face are removed even beneath his eyelids. When he washes his hands, his sins committed with his hands are removed. When he wipes his head, his sins committed with his head are removed even from his ears. When he washes his feet, his sins committed with his feet are removed even beneath his nails. His prayer and walking to the mosque are an extra merit.”
q: Whoever performs ablution and rinses his mouth and nose, his sins committed with them are removed. When he washes his face, his sins committed with his face are removed even beneath his eyelids. When he washes his hands, his sins committed with his hands are removed. When he wipes his head, his sins committed with his head are removed even from his ears. When he washes his feet, his sins committed with his feet are removed even beneath his nails. His prayer and walking to the mosque are an extra merit.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Will you ask me why I laughed?
t: Uthman ibn Affan reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, call for water and perform ablution, then he laughed. The Prophet said, “Will you not ask me what made me laugh?” They said, “What made you laugh, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Verily, when the servant performs ablution and washes his face, Allah removes every sin he committed with his face. Likewise, when he washes his arms, wipes his head, and cleanses his feet.”
q: Verily, when the servant performs ablution and washes his face, Allah removes every sin he committed with his face. Likewise, when he washes his arms, wipes his head, and cleanses his feet.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Allah forgives what one did between prayers
t: Uthman ibn Affan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A Muslim man does not perform ablution in an excellent manner and then performs prayer, but that Allah will forgive him for what occurred between his prayer and the next.”
q: A Muslim man does not perform ablution in an excellent manner and then performs prayer, but that Allah will forgive him for what occurred between his prayer and the next.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hereafter: The Prophet recognizes his Ummah on Judgment Day
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I will be the first to be called to prostrate on the Day of Resurrection. I will be the first to be called to raise his head and I will look in front of me. I will recognize my nation among the nations, from behind me, to my right and to my left.” A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize your nation among the nations from Noah until now?” The Prophet said, “They will have radiant streaks from the traces of ablution. No one will have that but them. I will recognize them when they are given their records in their right hands, and I will recognize them as their descendants run before them.”
q: I will be the first to be called to prostrate on the Day of Resurrection. I will be the first to be called to raise his head and I will look in front of me. I will recognize my nation among the nations, from behind me, to my right and to my left. … They will have radiant streaks from the traces of ablution. No one will have that but them. I will recognize them when they are given their records in their right hands, and I will recognize them as their descendants run before them.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Wudu: Sins washed away by first drop of ablution
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whenever a man performs his ablution intending to pray and he washes his hands, the sins of his hands fall down with the first drop. When he rinses his mouth and nose, the sins of his tongue and lips fall down with the first drop. When he washes his face, the sins of his hearing and sight fall down with the first drop. When he washes his arms to his elbows and his feet to his ankles, he is purified from every sin and fault, like the day he was born from his mother. If he stands for prayer, Allah will raise his status by a degree. If he sits, he will sit in peace.”
q: Whenever a man performs his ablution intending to pray and he washes his hands, the sins of his hands fall down with the first drop. When he rinses his mouth and nose, the sins of his tongue and lips fall down with the first drop. When he washes his face, the sins of his hearing and sight fall down with the first drop. When he washes his arms to his elbows and his feet to his ankles, he is purified from every sin and fault, like the day he was born from his mother. If he stands for prayer, Allah will raise his status by a degree. If he sits, he will sit in peace.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Wudu: How will you recognize Muslims in the Hereafter?
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize those you have never seen from your nation?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Radiant streaks upon their limbs from the traces of ablution.”
q: Radiant streaks upon their limbs from the traces of ablution.

title: Hasan on Reason: No benefit in narrations without using reason
t: Ibn Abi Dunya reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whoever is not governed by reason, he will not benefit by an abundance of reports from the scholars of narration.”

title: Hadith on Wudu: Islam includes ablution, ritual purification
t: Ibn Umar reported: Gabriel said, “O Muhammad, what is Islam?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Islam is to testify there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to pray, to give charity, to perform pilgrimage, to wash oneself of impurities, to perform ablution thoroughly, and to fast the month of Ramadan.”
q: Islam is to testify there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to pray, to give charity, to perform pilgrimage, to wash oneself of impurities, to perform ablution thoroughly, and to fast the month of Ramadan.

title: Hadith on Dua: Nothing to block two supplications
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two supplications have no barrier between them and Allah: the supplication of the oppressed, and the supplication of a man for his brother behind his back.”
q: Two supplications have no barrier between them and Allah: the supplication of the oppressed, and the supplication of a man for his brother behind his back.

title: Hadith on Arrogance: None can compete with grandeur of Allah
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty says that might is His garment and grandeur is His cloak: Whoever competes with Me, I will punish him.”
q: Allah Almighty says that might is His garment and grandeur is His cloak: Whoever competes with Me, I will punish him.

title: Hadith on Death: Expecting good from Allah at time of death
t: Hayyan Abi al-Nadrah reported: I went out to visit Yazid ibn al-Aswad as he was suffering a fatal illness, and I met Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ who also wanted to visit him. We entered Yazid’s home and Wathilah said, “What do you expect from Allah?” Yazid said, “By Allah, I expect good from Allah.” Wathilah said, “Rejoice! For I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say that Allah Almighty said: I am as my servant expects me. If he expects good, he will have it. If he expects evil, he will have it.”
q: I am as my servant expects me. If he expects good, he will have it. If he expects evil, he will have it.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Good thoughts about Allah, good results
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty says: I am as My servants expect of Me. If he thinks good of Me, he will have it. If he thinks evil of Me, he will have it.”
q: Allah Almighty says: I am as My servants expect of Me. If he thinks good of Me, he will have it. If he thinks evil of Me, he will have it.
