title: Hadith on Neighbors: Gabriel emphasizes good behavior to neighbors
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Gabriel did not stop instructing me to treat neighbors well until I thought he would make them my heirs.”
q: Gabriel did not stop instructing me to treat neighbors well until I thought he would make them my heirs.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Kindness: Allah loves gentleness, not harshness
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is gentle and He loves gentleness. He grants reward for gentleness what is not given for harshness.”
q: Verily, Allah is gentle and He loves gentleness. He grants reward for gentleness what is not given for harshness.

title: Hadith on Hellfire: Ships could sail on tears of people in Hell
t: Abdullah ibn Qays reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the people of Hellfire will weep so much that if ships tried to sail in their tears, they would sail. Then they will weep blood in place of their tears.”
q: Verily, the people of Hellfire will weep so much that if ships tried to sail in their tears, they would sail. Then they will weep blood in place of their tears.

title: Hadith on Jahannam: The least punished man in Hellfire
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most lightly punished of the people of Hellfire on the Day of Resurrection is a man under whose feet are placed two hot coals by which his brain boils.”
q: Verily, the most lightly punished of the people of Hellfire on the Day of Resurrection is a man under whose feet are placed two hot coals by which his brain boils.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Roads: Allah forgives man for clearing the street
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “While a man was walking in the road, he found a thorny branch in the road so he moved it aside. Allah appreciated his deed and forgave him.”
q: While a man was walking in the road, he found a thorny branch in the road so he moved it aside. Allah appreciated his deed and forgave him.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Most beloved to Allah have best character
t: Usamah ibn Sharik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most beloved people to Allah are those with the best character.”
q: The most beloved people to Allah are those with the best character.

title: Hadith on Chivalry: Masculine virtue in religion, reason, and character
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The nobility of a man is in his religion, his chivalry is in his reasoning, and his worth is in his character.”
q: The nobility of a man is in his religion, his chivalry is in his reasoning, and his worth is in his character.

title: Hadith on Duties: Mercy to children, respect to elders
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He is not one of us who is neither merciful to our young, nor respects the rights of our elders, nor enjoins good and forbids evil.”
q: He is not one of us who is neither merciful to our young, nor respects the rights of our elders, nor enjoins good and forbids evil.

title: Hadith on Kids: The Prophet is kind to his host’s children
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would visit the homes of the Ansar, greet their children with peace, pat their heads, and supplicate on their behalf.

title: Hadith on Zakat: Charity from unlawful wealth is not rewarded
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you pay alms on your property, you have fulfilled your obligation. Whoever accumulates wealth unlawfully and then spends it in charity, he will not have a reward and its burden of sin is upon him.”
q: If you pay alms on your property, you have fulfilled your obligation. Whoever accumulates wealth unlawfully and then spends it in charity, he will not have a reward and its burden of sin is upon him.

title: Hadith on Neighbors: Until I thought he would make them my heirs
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Gabriel kept advising me to be good to neighbors until I thought he would make them my heirs.”
q: Gabriel kept advising me to be good to neighbors until I thought he would make them my heirs.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: If last deeds are good, ending is good
t: Mu’awiyah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, nothing remains in the world but trials and tribulations. The parable of one of your deeds is that of a vessel. If the top of the vessel is pleasant, the rest of it will be pleasant. If the top is malignant, the rest of it will be malignant.”
q: Verily, nothing remains in the world but trials and tribulations. The parable of one of your deeds is that of a vessel. If the top of the vessel is pleasant, the rest of it will be pleasant. If the top is malignant, the rest of it will be malignant.

title: Hadith on Allah: Do you think Allah hears us talking?
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: Gathered by the House were two men of Quraysh and one or two men of Thaqif. The Qurayshi men had a lot of fat on their bellies and little understanding in their hearts. One of them said, “Do you think Allah hears what we say?” The other said, “He hears us if we are loud but does not hear us if we are quiet.” Another said, “If Allah hears us if we are loud, he also hears us if we are quiet.” Then, Allah Almighty revealed the verse, “You were not covering yourselves, lest your hearing, your sight, and your skins testify against you. Rather, you assumed that Allah does not know much of what you are doing.” (41:22)
q: You were not covering yourselves, lest your hearing, your sight, and your skins testify against you. Rather, you assumed that Allah does not know much of what you are doing.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Gaze: Allah knows men stare at women
t: Ibn Abbas reported: A woman would pray behind the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, who was the most beautiful of all people. Some men would come early to be in the first row, so as not to gaze at her. Some of them would come late to be in the last row. When they bowed, they would look at her between their limbs. Allah Almighty revealed the verse, “We surely know who comes first among you and We surely know who comes last.” (15:24)
q: We surely know who comes first among you and We surely know who comes last.

title: Hadith on Retaliation: Equal punishment permitted, forgiveness is better
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: On the day of the battle of Uhud, sixty-four of the Ansar and six of the Muhajirun had fallen, one of whom was Hamza, and the enemy mutilated their bodies. The Ansar said, “If we kill any of them in the future, we will do the same to them by twice as much.” On the day of Mecca’s liberation, Allah Almighty revealed the verse, “If you are afflicted, then afflict with the same as you were afflicted. If you are patient, it surely better for the patient,” (16:126). A man said, “The Quraysh will be wiped out today.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not harm anyone from the tribe, except four criminals.”
q: If you are afflicted, then afflict with the same as you were afflicted. If you are patient, it surely better for the patient, … Do not harm anyone from the tribe, except four criminals.

title: Hadith on Mistakes: Allah forgives errors, forgetfulness, compulsion
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has overlooked for my nation their honest mistakes, forgetfulness, and what they are forced into doing.”
q: Verily, Allah has overlooked for my nation their honest mistakes, forgetfulness, and what they are forced into doing.

title: Malik on Aqidah: Modality of divine attributes is inconceivable
t:
Yahya ibn Yahya reported: We were with Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, and a man came to him, saying, “O Abu Abdullah, ‘The Merciful rose above the Throne,’ (20:5). How is this rising?” Malik bowed his head silently until he raised it, dripping sweat, saying, “The rising is not unknown, its modality is inconceivable, faith in it is an obligation, and asking about it is an innovation. I do not see you as anything but a heretic.” Then, he ordered the man to be expelled.

Al-Bayhaqi said, “Most of our scholars followed this example in the issue of the divine attribute of ‘rising,’ as well as the issues of ‘coming,’ ‘going,’ and ‘descending.'”
q: The Merciful rose above the Throne

title: Hadith on Tazkiyah: What is purification of the soul?
t: Abdullah ibn Mu’awiyah reported: A man said, “What is purification of the soul?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “That one knows Allah Almighty is with him wherever he is.”
q: That one knows Allah Almighty is with him wherever he is.

title: Hadith on Fitnah: If trials get out of control, take care of yourself
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: We were gathered around the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he mentioned tribulations, saying, “If you see that people have disordered their commitments, diminished their trusts, and are as jumbled as this,” and he interlaced his fingers. I stood to come near him and I said, “How should I act if that happens?” The Prophet said, “Stay in your house, control your tongue, accept what you know is good, reject what you know is evil, take care of your affairs specifically and abandon the affairs of the common people.”
q: If you see that people have disordered their commitments, diminished their trusts, and are as jumbled as this, … Stay in your house, control your tongue, accept what you know is good, reject what you know is evil, take care of your affairs specifically and abandon the affairs of the common people.

title: Hadith on Virtue: Best strive in jihad and worship, worst are miserly
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you of the best of people? A man who clutches the reins of his horse in the way of Allah. Shall I not tell of the best after him? A man who withdraws with his flocks to fulfill the right of Allah therein. Shall I not tell you of the worst of people? A man who is asked by Allah and does not give in charity for His sake.”
q: Shall I not tell you of the best of people? A man who clutches the reins of his horse in the way of Allah. Shall I not tell of the best after him? A man who withdraws with his flocks to fulfill the right of Allah therein. Shall I not tell you of the worst of people? A man who is asked by Allah and does not give in charity for His sake.

title: Hadith on Jihad: Best people strive in jihad, worship in seclusion
t:
Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, which people are best?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A believer who strives in the way of Allah with his life and property.” They said, “Then who?” The Prophet said, “A believer in a narrow valley who fears his Lord and spares people from his evil.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “A man who withdraws into a narrow valley to worship his Lord.”
q: A believer who strives in the way of Allah with his life and property. … A believer in a narrow valley who fears his Lord and spares people from his evil.” … A man who withdraws into a narrow valley to worship his Lord.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Slander: Severe punishment for false accusations
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever accuses someone in his custodianship of a crime and he is innocent of the claim, the accuser will be flogged on the Day of Resurrection, unless it truly is as he claimed.”
q: Whoever accuses someone in his custodianship of a crime and he is innocent of the claim, the accuser will be flogged on the Day of Resurrection, unless it truly is as he claimed.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Eating: Praise be to Allah who fed me
t: Mu’adh ibn Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever eats a meal and says, ‘All praise is due to Allah, who fed me this from his provision without any capability or strength on my part,’ his previous minor sins will be forgiven.”
q: Whoever eats a meal and says, ‘All praise is due to Allah, who fed me this from his provision without any capability or strength on my part,’ his previous minor sins will be forgiven.

title: Hadith on Knowledge: Each generation refutes distortions against Islam
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “This knowledge will be carried by the trustworthy of every successive generation, refuting the corruption of extremists, the distortions of falsifiers, and the interpretations of the ignorant.”
q: This knowledge will be carried by the trustworthy of every successive generation, refuting the corruption of extremists, the distortions of falsifiers, and the interpretations of the ignorant.
gf: Sahih (authentic) according to Ahmad ibn Hanbal

title: Hadith on Tajassus: Only public sins punished, spying is forbidden
t: Zayd ibn Wahb reported: A man was brought to Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and it was said, “This man was found with wine dripping from his beard!” Ibn Mas’ud said, “Verily, we have been prohibited from spying, but if he shows it to us publicly, we will hold him accountable.”

title: Hadith on Kaba’ir: Three of the worst major sins
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said three times, “Shall I not tell you about the worst of major sins?” They said, “Of course, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “They are to associate partners with Allah and to be disrespectful to parents.” Then, the Prophet sat up after reclining, saying, “And surely to speak falsely.” The Prophet continued repeating it until we said to ourselves, “Would that he stop!”
q: Shall I not tell you about the worst of major sins? … They are to associate partners with Allah and to be disrespectful to parents. … And surely to speak falsely.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Waste: Allah does not love wasting money, gossip
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah does not like for you to waste wealth, nor ask many unnecessary questions, nor spread gossip.”
q: Allah does not like for you to waste wealth, nor ask many unnecessary questions, nor spread gossip.

title: Bishr on Fame: Love of being famous denies sweetness of faith
t: Ibn Abi Dunya reported: Bishr ibn al-Harith, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A man will not find the sweetness of the Hereafter if he loves to be known by people.”

title: Fudayl on Fame: If you can get by without being famous, do so
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you can get by without being known, do so. What is it against you if you are not praised? What is it against you that people blame you but to Allah you are praiseworthy?”

title: Fudayl on Manhood: Character flaws dishonor religion, masculinity
t: Ibn ‘Asakir reported: Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whoever has bad character has dishonored his religion, his reputation, and his chivalry.”

title: Hadith on Silence: You are safe as long as you stay silent
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, you will continue to be safe as long as you remain silent. If you speak, it will be recorded for you or against you.”
q: Verily, you will continue to be safe as long as you remain silent. If you speak, it will be recorded for you or against you.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Worship: The Prophet performs deeds consistently
t: ‘Alqamah reported: I asked Aisha, “O mother of the believers, how were the deeds of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him? Did he designate anything for certain days?” Aisha said, “No. The Prophet would performs deeds regularly, and who among you are capable of doing as he did?”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Shura: Consult your brothers when they ask you
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If your brother requests your consultation, let him give counsel.”
q: If your brother requests your consultation, let him give counsel.

title: Hadith on Muhammad: The Prophet more handsome than the moon
t: Jabir ibn Samurah reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on a clear night while he was wearing a red cloak. I turned my sight between him and the moon and, to me, he was more handsome and beautiful than the moon.

title: Hadith on Miscarriage: Deceased fetus will carry his mother into Paradise
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, the miscarried fetus will carry his mother by his umbilical cord into Paradise, if she was seeking its reward.”
q: By the One in whose hand is my soul, the miscarried fetus will carry his mother by his umbilical cord into Paradise, if she was seeking its reward.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: You would laugh less, cry often if you knew
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Paradise and Hellfire were shown to me and I have never seen such good or evil as I have today. If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep often.”
q: Paradise and Hellfire were shown to me and I have never seen such good or evil as I have today. If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep often.

title: Hadith on Dua: Believers in good shape if patient with supplication
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The servant will continue to be upon goodness as long as he is not impatient.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, how is he impatient?” The Prophet said, “He says: I have supplicated to my Lord and He did not answer me.”
q: The servant will continue to be upon goodness as long as he is not impatient. … He says: I have supplicated to my Lord and He did not answer me.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Dua: No one ever harmed by too much supplication
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not become frustrated with supplication, for no one was ever ruined by supplication.”
q: Do not become frustrated with supplication, for no one was ever ruined by supplication.

title: Hadith on Qadr: No precaution enough against providence but supplication
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No worldly precaution is enough against the divine decree. Supplication benefits by what is sent down and what is not sent down. Verily, a supplication will confront a trial and they both fight each other until the Day of Resurrection.”
q: No worldly precaution is enough against the divine decree. Supplication benefits by what is sent down and what is not sent down. Verily, a supplication will confront a trial and they both fight each other until the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet teaches Ali what to say in distress
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, taught me to say when I was afflicted with distress, “There is no God but Allah, the Forbearing, the Noble. Glory be to Allah, blessed is Allah the Lord of the Great Throne, and all praise is due to Allah the Lord of the worlds.”
q: There is no God but Allah, the Forbearing, the Noble. Glory be to Allah, blessed is Allah the Lord of the Great Throne, and all praise is due to Allah the Lord of the worlds.

title: Hadith on Miracles: Moon splits, the Prophet is accused of magic
t: Jubayr ibn Mu’tim reported: The moon was split in the lifetime of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, until it became two separate pieces over this mountain and this mountain. They said, “Muhammad has cast a spell on us!” Some of them said, “If he has bewitched us, he cannot bewitch all of the people.”

title: Hadith on Miracles: Bear witness to the splitting of the moon
t:
Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The moon split when we were with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and it became two separate pieces. The Prophet said to us, “Bear witness. Bear witness.”

In another narration, Ibn Mas’ud said, “A piece was behind the mountain and another piece was below it.”
q: Bear witness. Bear witness
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Miracles: The Quraysh ask the Prophet for a sign
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The people of Mecca asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, for a sign, so he showed them the splitting of the moon into two pieces until mount Hira’ could be seen between them.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sweets: The Prophet liked naturally sweet food
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to like sweets and honey.

title: Hadith on Dua: O Allah, I ask you for guidance and direction
t:
Ali reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “Say: O Allah, guide me and direct me.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “O Allah, I ask you for guidance and direction.”
q: Say: O Allah, guide me and direct me. … O Allah, I ask you for guidance and direction.

title: Umar on Apostasy: Apostates return peacefully or imprisoned
t:
Anas ibn Malik reported: I said, “O commander of the faithful, some people have turned renegade against Islam and joined the idolaters. What is to be done other than killing them?” Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “That I take hold of them on peaceful terms is more beloved to me than everything over which the sun rises, from the horizon to the zenith.” I said, “O commander of the faithful, what would you do if you seized them?” Umar said, “I would offer them the door through which they exited, that they would enter it again. If they did so, I would accept it from them; otherwise, I would keep them in prison.”

Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said about the apostate, “He is held for his repentance indefinitely,” and Sufyan al-Thawri said, “This is what we adhere to.”

title: Hadith on Quran: The Prophet’s love for Surat al-Fath
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A chapter has been revealed to me tonight that is more beloved to me than everything over which the sun rises.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “Verily, We have granted you a clear victory.” (48:1)
q: A chapter has been revealed to me tonight that is more beloved to me than everything over which the sun rises. … Verily, We have granted you a clear victory

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Four most beloved statements to Allah
t: Samurah ibn Jundab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most beloved words to Allah are four: glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the greatest. There is no harm in starting with any of them.”
q: The most beloved words to Allah are four: glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the greatest. There is no harm in starting with any of them.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Increase your righteous deeds everlasting
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Increase in ‘righteous deeds everlasting,’” (18:46). It was said, “What are they, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “To declare the greatness of Allah, the oneness of Allah, the glory of Allah, the praise of Allah, and that there is no movement or might but in Allah.”
q: Increase in ‘righteous deeds everlasting,’ … To declare the greatness of Allah, the oneness of Allah, the glory of Allah, the praise of Allah, and that there is no movement or might but in Allah.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Best four statements to remember Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best words are four: glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the greatest.”
q: The best words are four: glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the greatest.

title: Hadith on Islam: Disappearance of religious knowledge at end of time
t: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Islam will be taken apart just as a garment is taken apart, until fasting is not known, nor prayer, nor rites, nor charity. The Book of Allah Almighty will vanish in a single night, such that no verse of it is left on earth. There will only remain some sects among the people, old men and women who say: We heard our forefathers used to say ‘there is no God but Allah,’ so we say it as well.”
q: Islam will be taken apart just as a garment is taken apart, until fasting is not known, nor prayer, nor rites, nor charity. The Book of Allah Almighty will vanish in a single night, such that no verse of it is left on earth. There will only remain some sects among the people, old men and women who say: We heard our forefathers used to say ‘there is no God but Allah,’ so we say it as well.

title: Hadith on Quran: Encouragement to memorize, not only read Quran
t: Abu al-Qasim reported: Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Recite the Quran and do not be deceived by depending on the written copies. Verily, Allah will never punish a heart that has preserved the Quran.”

title: Hadith on Signs: Faith of no benefit after seeing three signs
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When three signs appear, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not already believe or earn good by its faith: the rising of the sun from the west, the False Messiah, and the beast from the earth.”
q: When three signs appear, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not already believe or earn good by its faith: the rising of the sun from the west, the False Messiah, and the beast from the earth.

title: Hadith on Quran: Sign of the Hour is disappearance of Quran
t: Zirr reported: Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The Quran will vanish in one night. No verse in the scripture or in the heart of anyone will be left behind.”

title: Hadith on Hawd: Description of first to drink from the Fountain
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “My fountain is like the distance between ‘Adan and ‘Amman, cooler than ice, sweeter than honey, its fragrance more pleasant than musk, its cups as numerous as stars in the sky. Whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty afterward forever. The first people to arrive at it are homeless among the emigrants.” Someone said, “Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Their hair is disheveled, their faces disfigured, and their clothes stained. The gates of the rulers are not opened for them and they are not favored in marriage, yet they fulfill every right over them and do not take any right belonging to them.”
q: My fountain is like the distance between ‘Adan and ‘Amman, cooler than ice, sweeter than honey, its fragrance more pleasant than musk, its cups as numerous as stars in the sky. Whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty afterward forever. The first people to arrive at it are homeless among the emigrants. … Their hair is disheveled, their faces disfigured, and their clothes stained. The gates of the rulers are not opened for them and they are not favored in marriage, yet they fulfill every right over them and do not take any right belonging to them.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: First to drink from the Fountain are poor, downtrodden
t: Thawban reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “My fountain is from ‘Adan to ‘Amman al-Balqa’. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Its cups are as numerous as the stars. Whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty afterwards forever. The first people to arrive at it will be the poor emigrants, their hair disheveled and their clothes stained, who are not favored in marriage and for whom the gates of rulers are not opened.”
q: My fountain is from ‘Adan to ‘Amman al-Balqa’. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Its cups are as numerous as the stars. Whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty afterwards forever. The first people to arrive at it will be the poor emigrants, their hair disheveled and their clothes stained, who are not favored in marriage and for whom the gates of rulers are not opened.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Gold, silver, and pearl wonders in Paradise
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, in Paradise are two gardens with silver vessels and two gardens with golden vessels. Nothing comes between its people looking upon their Lord but a curtain of majesty over His face in the Garden of Eden. In Paradise is a tent made of hollow pearls, the breadth of which is sixty miles. In each corner is a family and they do not see the others, while the believer roams freely among them.”
q: Verily, in Paradise are two gardens with silver vessels and two gardens with golden vessels. Nothing comes between its people looking upon their Lord but a curtain of majesty over His face in the Garden of Eden. In Paradise is a tent made of hollow pearls, the breadth of which is sixty miles. In each corner is a family and they do not see the others, while the believer roams freely among them.

title: Hadith on Hawd: Those who meet the Prophet at the Fountain
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “My fountain is like the distance between ‘Adan and ‘Uman, within which are cups as numerous as stars in the sky. Whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty again forever. Among those of my nation to arrive at it are the poor with disheveled hair and their clothing stained, not favored for marriage and not present in the courts of rulers, those who fulfill every right upon them yet are not given any of their rights.”
q: My fountain is like the distance between ‘Adan and ‘Uman, within which are cups as numerous as stars in the sky. Whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty again forever. Among those of my nation to arrive at it are the poor with disheveled hair and their clothing stained, not favored for marriage and not present in the courts of rulers, those who fulfill every right upon them yet are not given any of their rights.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Hawd: Never thirsty after drinking from Fountain
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I will precede you at the Fountain in the Hereafter. Whoever arrives at it and drinks from it will never feel thirsty ever again. Some people will come to me and we will recognize each other, but then a barrier will separate us.”
q: I will precede you at the Fountain in the Hereafter. Whoever arrives at it and drinks from it will never feel thirsty ever again. Some people will come to me and we will recognize each other, but then a barrier will separate us.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salat: Guarding five prayers, reciting Quran at night
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever guards these prescribed prayers, he will not be recorded as negligent. Whoever recites one hundred verses in the night, he will not be recorded as negligent.”
q: Whoever guards these prescribed prayers, he will not be recorded as negligent. Whoever recites one hundred verses in the night, he will not be recorded as negligent.”

title: Hadith on Quran: Reciting last ten verses of Surat Ali ‘Imran
t: Ibn Abbas reported: I spent the night with my aunt Maymunah and I said to myself that I will watch the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. She laid out a cushion for the Prophet and he slept on the direction of its long side. He awoke and wiped the sleep from his eyes, then recited the last ten verses of Surat Ali ‘Imran until its end.

title: Hadith on Rulers: Beware associating with tyrannical, unjust rulers
t: Abu al-‘Awar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of approaching the gates of the ruler, for they will become tyrants.”
q: Beware of approaching the gates of the ruler, for they will become tyrants.

title: Hadith on Ease: The Prophet fears making Islam more difficult
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would abstain from doing a deed he liked to perform, fearing that people would do it until it became an obligation upon them.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Rabia on Sins: Disease is sin, cure is seeking forgiveness
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Al-Rabia’ ibn Khuthaym, may Allah have mercy on him, said to his companions, “Do you know the disease, the cure, and the healing?” They said no. Al-Rabia’ said, “The disease is sin, the cure is to seek forgiveness from Allah, and the healing is to repent and then not repeat it.”

title: Hadith on Shahid: Seven types of martyrdom besides fighting
t: Jabir ibn ‘Atik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are seven martyrs besides one who is killed in the way of Allah: the victim of plague is a martyr, the one who drowns is a martyr, the one who dies of chest pain is a martyr, the one who dies of stomach infection is a martyr, the one who burns to death is a martyr, the one who dies under rubble is a martyr, and the pregnant woman who dies in labor is a martyr.”
q: There are seven martyrs besides one who is killed in the way of Allah: the victim of plague is a martyr, the one who drowns is a martyr, the one who dies of chest pain is a martyr, the one who dies of stomach infection is a martyr, the one who burns to death is a martyr, the one who dies under rubble is a martyr, and the pregnant woman who dies in labor is a martyr.

title: Hadith on Taqwa: Be mindful of Allah in public and private
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I instruct you to fear Allah in your private and public affairs. If you do a bad deed, then do a good deed. Do not ask anyone for anything, even if you drop your whip. Do not violate what is entrusted, and do not take a position as judge between two people.”
q: I instruct you to fear Allah in your private and public affairs. If you do a bad deed, then do a good deed. Do not ask anyone for anything, even if you drop your whip. Do not violate what is entrusted, and do not take a position as judge between two people.

title: Hadith on Taqwa: When he is told to fear Allah
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most beloved statement to Allah is for a servant to say, ‘Glory be to You, O Allah, and Your praises. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no God besides You.’ The most hateful statement to Allah is for a man to say to another man, ‘Fear Allah!’ and he replies, ‘Mind yourself!’”
q: Verily, the most beloved statement to Allah is for a servant to say, ‘Glory be to You, O Allah, and Your praises. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no God besides You.’ The most hateful statement to Allah is for a man to say to another man, ‘Fear Allah!’ and he replies, ‘Mind yourself!’

title: Hadith on Shahid: Martyrs protected from pain of death
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The martyr does not feel the pain of being killed except as one of you feels the pinch of an insect bite.”
q: The martyr does not feel the pain of being killed except as one of you feels the pinch of an insect bite.

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet’s supplication for distress and sorrow
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say at a time of distress, “There is no God but Allah, the Knowing, the Forbearing. There is no God but Allah, Lord of the Great Throne. There is no God but Allah, Lord of the heavens, the earth, and the Noble Throne.”
q: There is no God but Allah, the Knowing, the Forbearing. There is no God but Allah, Lord of the Great Throne. There is no God but Allah, Lord of the heavens, the earth, and the Noble Throne.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Healing: Cures for every physical, mental, spiritual disease
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah did not send down any disease but that he also sent down the cure.”
q: Allah did not send down any disease but that he also sent down the cure.

title: Hadith on Medicine: Allah placed cures for all diseases, except aging
t: Usamah ibn Sharik reported: A bedouin said, “O Messenger of Allah, shall we not seek treatment?” The Prophet said, “Yes, O servants of Allah, seek treatment. Verily, Allah did not place a disease but that he also placed its treatment or cure, except for one ailment.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is it?” The Prophet said, “Old age.”
q: Yes, O servants of Allah, seek treatment. Verily, Allah did not place a disease but that he also placed its treatment or cure, except for one ailment. … Old age.

title: Ali on Quran: Recite Ayat al-Kursi and two verses of Al-Baqarah before bed
t: Abu Ishaq reported: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “I have not seen anyone of intelligence go to sleep unless he had recited these three verses at the end of Surat al-Baqarah.”

title: Hadith on Quran: Al-Baqarah decree before heaven and earth
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah issued a decree two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. He sent down two verse for the end of Surat al-Baqarah. They are not recited in a house but that Satan will not come near it.”
q: Verily, Allah issued a decree two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. He sent down two verse for the end of Surat al-Baqarah. They are not recited in a house but that Satan will not come near it.

title: Hadith on Hypocrisy: The Prophet fears scholars with ignorant hearts
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among what I fear most for my nation is every hypocrite with a knowledgeable tongue.”
q: Verily, among what I fear most for my nation is every hypocrite with a knowledgeable tongue.

title: Hadith on Nifaq: The Prophet fears debates of eloquent hypocrites
t: ‘Imran ibn Husayn reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among what I fear most for you are the debates of hypocrites with a knowledgeable tongue.”
q: Among what I fear most for you are the debates of hypocrites with a knowledgeable tongue.

title: Hadith on Nifaq: Hypocritical teacher like a burning lamp
t: Jundub ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the scholar who teaches people virtue, but forgets it himself, is that of a lamp giving people light while it burns itself.”
q: The parable of the scholar who teaches people virtue, but forgets it himself, is that of a lamp giving people light while it burns itself.

title: Abu Darda on Judgment: Did you not act upon your knowledge?
t: Luqman reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, I fear from my Lord on the Day of Resurrection that I will be called in front of the heads of all creation, saying: O ‘Uwaymir! I will say: At your service, my Lord. He will say: Did you not act upon what you knew?”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Judgment: Asked about life, youth, earnings, knowledge
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The servant’s feet will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about four matters: his body and how he used it, his lifetime and how he exhausted it, his wealth and how he acquired it and spent it, and his knowledge and how he acted upon it.”
q: The servant’s feet will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about four matters: his body and how he used it, his lifetime and how he exhausted it, his wealth and how he acquired it and spent it, and his knowledge and how he acted upon it.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Judgement: Asked about life, knowledge, wealth, health
t: Abu Barzah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The feet of a servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about his lifetime and how he used it, his knowledge and how he acted upon it, his wealth and from where he acquired it and how he spent it, and his body and how he exhausted it.”
q: The feet of a servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about his lifetime and how he used it, his knowledge and how he acted upon it, his wealth and from where he acquired it and how he spent it, and his body and how he exhausted it.

title: Hadith on Janazah: The Prophet’s supplication at funerals
t: Abu Ibrahim al-Ash’hali reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, performed the funeral prayer, he would say, “O Allah, forgive our living and our deceased, those of us present and those of us absent, our young and our old, our men and our women. O Allah, for whomever you give life among us, give him life upon Islam. For whomever you take among us, take him upon faith.”
q: O Allah, forgive our living and our deceased, those of us present and those of us absent, our young and our old, our men and our women. … O Allah, for whomever you give life among us, give him life upon Islam. For whomever you take among us, take him upon faith

title: Hadith Ahruf: Quran revealed in seven readings, do not argue it
t: Abu Juhaym reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Quran is recited in seven ways. Do not argue over the Quran, for arguing over the Quran is an act of unbelief.”
q: The Quran is recited in seven ways. Do not argue over the Quran, for arguing over the Quran is an act of unbelief.

title: Hadith on Quran: Arguing over the Quran is unbelief
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Arguing over the Quran is an act of unbelief.”
q: Arguing over the Quran is an act of unbelief.

title: Hadith Debates: With this I commanded you? To argue?
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: We were sitting in front of the door of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and we were debating, bringing this verse and bringing this verse. The Prophet came out to us red with anger, as if a pomegranate seed had burst on his face. The Prophet said, “O these people! Is it with this I sent you? With this I commanded you? Do not return to unbelief after me by striking the necks of each other!”
q: O these people! Is it with this I sent you? With this I commanded you? Do not return to unbelief after me by striking the necks of each other!
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Character: House in Paradise for giving up arguments, lies
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I guarantee a house on the outskirts of Paradise, a house in the middle of Paradise, and a house in the highest part of Paradise for one who gives up arguing even if he is right, who gives up lying even while joking, and who makes his character excellent.”
q: I guarantee a house on the outskirts of Paradise, a house in the middle of Paradise, and a house in the highest part of Paradise for one who gives up arguing even if he is right, who gives up lying even while joking, and who makes his character excellent.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Knowledge: All creatures seek forgiveness for good teachers
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Everything seeks forgiveness for the teacher of virtue, even fish in the sea.”
q: Everything seeks forgiveness for the teacher of virtue, even fish in the sea.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Knowledge: They have reward of those who act on it
t: Mu’adh ibn Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever imparts knowledge will have the reward of whoever acted upon it, without detracting from the reward of one who acted.”
q: Whoever imparts knowledge will have the reward of whoever acted upon it, without detracting from the reward of one who acted.

title: Hadith on Charity: Three best things to leave behind after death
t: Abu Qatadah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of what a man leaves behind are three: a righteous child who supplicates for him, ongoing charity the reward of which reaches him, and knowledge that is acted upon after him.”
q: The best of what a man leaves behind are three: a righteous child who supplicates for him, ongoing charity the reward of which reaches him, and knowledge that is acted upon after him.

title: Hadith on Charity: Seven types of ongoing charity after death
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Seven deeds of a servant continue to be rewarded after his death while he is in his grave: knowledge to be learned, constructing a canal, digging a well, planting a date-palm tree, building a mosque, handing down a written copy of the Quran, and leaving a righteous child who seeks forgiveness for him after his death.”
q: Seven deeds of a servant continue to be rewarded after his death while he is in his grave: knowledge to be learned, constructing a canal, digging a well, planting a date-palm tree, building a mosque, handing down a written copy of the Quran, and leaving a righteous child who seeks forgiveness for him after his death.

title: Hadith on Knowledge: Cure for ignorance is to ask scholars
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the only cure for ignorance is to ask questions.”
q: Verily, the only cure for ignorance is to ask questions.

title: Hadith on Taqwa: Only people of knowledge fear Allah
t: Mu’awiyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O people, knowledge only comes by learning, and understanding only comes by seeking understanding. For whoever Allah wills goodness, He grants him understanding of the religion. Verily, only those with knowledge fear Allah among His servants.” (35:28)
q: O people, knowledge only comes by learning, and understanding only comes by seeking understanding. For whoever Allah wills goodness, He grants him understanding of the religion. Verily, only those with knowledge fear Allah among His servants.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Idolatry: How many gods do you worship now?
t: ‘Imran ibn Husayn reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to my father, “O Husayn, how many gods do you worship today?” My father said, “Seven. Six on earth and one in heaven.” The Prophet said, “In which of them do you depend for your most ardent hopes and concerns?” He said, “The one in heaven.” The Prophet said, “O Husayn, if you accept Islam, I will teach you two words to benefit you.” Later when Husayn had embraced Islam, he said, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me the two words you promised to me.” The Prophet said, “Say: O Allah, inspire me with guidance and protect me from the evil of my ego.”
q: O Husayn, how many gods do you worship today? … In which of them do you depend for your most ardent hopes and concerns? … O Husayn, if you accept Islam, I will teach you two words to benefit you. … Say: O Allah, inspire me with guidance and protect me from the evil of my ego.
gf: Jayyid (very good) according to Ibn Hajar

title: Hadith on Lut: May Allah have mercy on Prophet Lot
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “May Allah have mercy upon Lot. He had sought refuge in a strong pillar. If I had remained in prison for as long as Joseph, I would have accepted an offer of freedom.”
q: May Allah have mercy upon Lot. He had sought refuge in a strong pillar. If I had remained in prison for as long as Joseph, I would have accepted an offer of freedom.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Aisha on Dreams: O Allah, I ask you for good and true dreams
t: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr reported: Aisha, may Allah have pleased with her, would say when she intended to sleep, “O Allah, I ask you for good and true dreams, not false dreams, beneficial and not harmful.” When she said this, they knew that she would not say anything more until she awoke in the morning or in the middle of the night.

title: Awn on Trials: Allah sends trials as medicine, like doctors and parents
t: Qurrah reported: ‘Awn, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, Allah compels his servant into a trial in the same way as caretakers do to their sick and their children. They say: Drink this, for in the end it will be good for you.”

title: Hadith on Milk: Rinsing the mouth after drinking milk
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, drank some milk and rinsed his mouth. The Prophet said, “It contains fatty grease.”
q: It contains fatty grease
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Voluntary prayers separated from obligatory prayers
t: Mu’awiyyah reported: When you perform the Friday prayer, do not pray another prayer until you have spoken or left the mosque. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded us to do that, to not connect two prayers together unless we have spoken or we have left.

title: Ibn Dhakwan on Gender: Lowering the gaze for beardless young boys
t: Uthman ibn Salih reported: Al-Hasan ibn Dhakwan, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Do not sit with young boy singers, for their appearance is like that of women. They are an even greater temptation than young virgin girls.”

title: Hadith on Gender: Two types of effeminate men, sinful and not sinful
t: Umm Salamah reported: An effeminate man was with her and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in the house. He said to the brother of Umm Salamah, “O Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, if Allah opens up Al-Ta’if tomorrow, I will show you the daughter of Ghaylan. She has four rolls of belly fat on the front and eight on the back.” The Prophet heard him say this and he said, “Do not allow these men to enter your homes freely.”
q: Do not allow these men to enter your homes freely.

title: Hadith on Virtues: Six good qualities for Allah to guarantee Paradise
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No Muslim dies with one of six traits but that he has a guarantee from Allah he will be admitted into Paradise. A man who goes out for jihad; if he dies in this state, his guarantee is upon Allah. A man who follows a funeral procession; if he dies in this state, his guarantee is upon Allah. A man who visits a sick person; if he dies in this state, his guarantee is upon Allah. A man who performs ablution in the best manner and then goes out to the mosque for his prayer; if he dies in this state, his guarantee is upon Allah. A man who comes to a Muslim leader for no reason but to honor and respect him; if he dies in this state, his guarantee is upon Allah. A man in his house who does not backbite a Muslim and he does not bring displeasure or vengeance upon himself; if he dies in this state, his guarantee is upon Allah.”
q: No Muslim dies with one of six traits but that he has a guarantee from Allah he will be admitted into Paradise. A man who goes out for jihad; if he dies in this state, his guarantee is upon Allah. A man who follows a funeral procession; if he dies in this state, his guarantee is upon Allah. A man who visits a sick person; if he dies in this state, his guarantee is upon Allah. A man who performs ablution in the best manner and then goes out to the mosque for his prayer; if he dies in this state, his guarantee is upon Allah. A man who comes to a Muslim leader for no reason but to honor and respect him; if he dies in this state, his guarantee is upon Allah. A man in his house who does not backbite a Muslim and he does not bring displeasure or vengeance upon himself; if he dies in this state, his guarantee is upon Allah.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Virtues: Their security is guaranteed by Allah
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever wages jihad in the way of Allah, his safety is assured by Allah. Whoever visits a sick person, his safety is assured by Allah. Whoever visits the mosque in the morning or evening, his safety is assured by Allah. Whoever enters the dwelling of a prayer leader to honor him, his safety is assured by Allah. Whoever sits in his house and does not backbite any human being, his safety is assured by Allah.”
q: Whoever wages jihad in the way of Allah, his safety is assured by Allah. Whoever visits a sick person, his safety is assured by Allah. Whoever visits the mosque in the morning or evening, his safety is assured by Allah. Whoever enters the dwelling of a prayer leader to honor him, his safety is assured by Allah. Whoever sits in his house and does not backbite any human being, his safety is assured by Allah.

title: Hadith on Faith: Recompense for deeds is of the same genus
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “As one does not harvest thorns and grapes together, the wicked will not be in the position of the righteous. There are two paths, so whichever path you take will bring you to its outcome.”
q: As one does not harvest thorns and grapes together, the wicked will not be in the position of the righteous. There are two paths, so whichever path you take will bring you to its outcome.

title: Hadith on Recompense: Traverse the path you wish, good or evil
t: Yazid ibn Marthad reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “As one does not harvest thorns and grapes together, likewise the righteous will not be in the position of the wicked. Traverse the path you wish, for whichever path you travel will lead you back to its people.”
q: As one does not harvest thorns and grapes together, likewise the righteous will not be in the position of the wicked. Traverse the path you wish, for whichever path you travel will lead you back to its people

title: Hadith on Dua: Seek refuge from vices, trials, and oppression
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would say, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disability, sloth, cowardice, senility, and miserliness. I seek refuge in You from the torment of the grave and from the trials of life and death.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disability, sloth, cowardice, senility, and miserliness. I seek refuge in You from the torment of the grave and from the trials of life and death.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: A’mash on Hadith: Fiqh scholars are doctors, Hadith scholars pharmacists
t: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Amr reported: We were with Al-A’mash, may Allah have mercy on him, while he was asking Abu Hanifa about legal issues and Abu Hanifa answered him. Al-A’mash said to him, “From where did you get this?” Abu Hanifa said, “You narrated to us from Ibrahim as such. You narrated to us from Al-Sha’bi as such.” Al-A’mash said at that, “O scholars of Fiqh, you are the doctors and we are the pharmacists.”

title: Hadith on Ayat: Three verses in prayer better than worldly gains
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Would one of you like to find three fattened, pregnant she-camels when he returns to his family?” They said yes. The Prophet said, “Three verses recited in one of your prayers is better than three fattened, pregnant she-camels.”
q: Would one of you like to find three fattened, pregnant she-camels when he returns to his family? … Three verses recited in one of your prayers is better than three fattened, pregnant she-camels.

title: Muzanni on Abu Bakr: Righteous Caliph was favored by his pure heart
t: Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi reported: Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzanni said, “Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, was not favored over people because of abundant of fasting and prayer. Rather, he was only favored over them because of something that settled in his heart.”

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: Night prayer intention rewarded regardless
t: Abu Darda reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever comes to his carpet intending to stand for prayer at night, yet his eyes are overcome with sleep until morning, his intention is recorded for him, and his sleep is charity from his Lord Almighty to him.”
q: Whoever comes to his carpet intending to stand for prayer at night, yet his eyes are overcome with sleep until morning, his intention is recorded for him, and his sleep is charity from his Lord Almighty to him.

title: Hadith on Deeds: Allah instructs angels how to record deeds
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah says to the angels: If My servant intends to commit a sin, do not record it against him until he does it. If he does it, record it against him as one bad deed. If he leaves it for My sake, record it for him as one good deed. If he intends to do a good deed and he does not do it, record it for him as one good deed. If he does it, record it for him as ten good deeds up to seven hundred times as much.”
q: Allah says to the angels: If My servant intends to commit a sin, do not record it against him until he does it. If he does it, record it against him as one bad deed. If he leaves it for My sake, record it for him as one good deed. If he intends to do a good deed and he does not do it, record it for him as one good deed. If he does it, record it for him as ten good deeds up to seven hundred times as much.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Niyyah: Resurrected for judgment of intentions
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people will be gathered for judgment based upon their intentions.”
q: The people will be gathered for judgment based upon their intentions.

title: Hadith on Dunya: Entire world cursed but sincerity to Allah
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The world is cursed and everything in it is cursed, except whatever seeks the countenance of Allah Almighty.”
q: The world is cursed and everything in it is cursed, except whatever seeks the countenance of Allah Almighty
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Welfare: Muslims supported because of their weak
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah only supports this nation due to the supplications, the prayers, and the sincerity of their vulnerable.”
q: Verily, Allah only supports this nation due to the supplications, the prayers, and the sincerity of their vulnerable.

title: Hadith on Sunnah: I leave you upon a clear path
t: Al-‘Irbad ibn Sariyah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have left you upon a clear path, its clarity is the same by night or day. No one deviates from it after me but that he will be ruined.”
q: I have left you upon a clear path, its clarity is the same by night or day. No one deviates from it after me but that he will be ruined.

title: Hadith on Bid’ah: Repentance not accepted until heresy abandoned
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah veils repentance from the practitioner of any heresy.”
q: Verily, Allah veils repentance from the practitioner of any heresy.

title: Hadith on Deeds: Assure these six deeds to enter Paradise
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Assure six deeds for me, and I will assure for you Paradise. When you speak, do not lie. When you promise, do not break it. When you are trusted, do not betray it. Lower your gaze, guard your chastity, and restrain your hands from harming others.”
q: Assure six deeds for me, and I will assure for you Paradise. When you speak, do not lie. When you promise, do not break it. When you are trusted, do not betray it. Lower your gaze, guard your chastity, and restrain your hands from harming others.

title: Fudayl on Tawhid: Only Allah can truly bring benefit, cause harm
t: Sari ibn al-Mughallis reported: Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whoever fears Allah, no one can harm him. Whoever fears another besides Allah, no one can benefit him.”

title: Hadith on Faith: The Prophet explains Islam, Iman, and Yaqin
t: Abu Firas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Ask me about whatever you wish.” A man called out, “O Messenger of Allah, what is Islam?” The Prophet said, “To perform prayer and give charity.” The man said, “What is faith?” The Prophet said, “Sincerity.” The man said, “What is conviction?” The Prophet said, “Certainty in the truth of the Resurrection.”
q: Ask me about whatever you wish … To perform prayer and give charity … Sincerity … Certainty in the truth of the Resurrection

title: Hadith on Hereafter: His deeds seem small on Judgement Day
t: ‘Utbah ibn ‘Abdu Sullami reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Were a man to fall upon his face in prostration from the day he was born until the day he died as an old man, seeking the pleasure of Allah Almighty, he would still consider his good deeds to be insignificant on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Were a man to fall upon his face in prostration from the day he was born until the day he died as an old man, seeking the pleasure of Allah Almighty, he would still consider his good deeds to be insignificant on the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Sahih li ghayihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Society: Believers never abandon starving neighbors
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He is not a believer who spends the night satiated while the neighbor to his side is hungry.”
q: He is not a believer who spends the night satiated while the neighbor to his side is hungry
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Society: Not a believer if neighbors are starving
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He does not have faith in me who spends the night satiated while he knows that a neighbor to his side is hungry.”
q: He does not have faith in me who spends the night satiated while he knows that a neighbor to his side is hungry

title: Hadith on Faith: Believers are trusted, Muslims do not harm
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believer is one who is trusted by people. The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand Muslims are safe. The emigrant is one who emigrates away from evil. By the One in whose hand is my soul, a servant will not enter Paradise if his neighbor is not secure from his evil.”
q: The believer is one who is trusted by people. The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand Muslims are safe. The emigrant is one who emigrates away from evil. By the One in whose hand is my soul, a servant will not enter Paradise if his neighbor is not secure from his evil.

title: Hadith on Neighbors: Crimes against neighbors are magnified
t: Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to his companions, “What do you say about adultery?” They said, “Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it, so it is forbidden until the Day of Resurrection.” The Prophet said, “For a man to commit adultery with ten women is less against him than committing adultery with the wife of his neighbor. What do you say about theft?” They said, “Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it, so it is forbidden.” The Prophet said, “For a man to steal from ten houses is less against him than stealing from his neighbor.”
q: What do you say about adultery? … For a man to commit adultery with ten women is less against him than committing adultery with the wife of his neighbor. What do you say about theft? … For a man to steal from ten houses is less against him than stealing from his neighbor.

title: Ibn Umar on Sunnah: Ibn Umar naps as the Prophet napped
t: Nafi’ reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, would come to a tree between Mecca and Medina, and he would take a nap under it. He told people that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had done so.

title: Ibn Umar on Sunnah: Ibn Umar’s strict adherence to the Prophet’s actions
t: Mujahid reported: We were with Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, on a journey. We passed by a place and he kept to the side away from it. He was asked, “Why did you do that?” Ibn Umar said, “I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, do that, do I did that.”

title: Hadith on Quran: Hold fast to the verses of Allah
t: ‘Awf ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Obey me as long as I am here with you. You must hold firmly to the verses of Allah. Permit what they permit and forbid what they forbid.”
q: Obey me as long as I am here with you. You must hold firmly to the verses of Allah. Permit what they permit and forbid what they forbid.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Bid’ah: Moderate Sunnah better than effort for heresy
t: ‘Abdur Rahman ibn Yazid reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Moderation in the Sunnah is better than striving in innovation.”

title: Farewell Sermon: Final advice to follow Quran and Sunnah
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, addressed the people during the farewell sermon, saying, “Satan has despaired that he will ever be worshiped in your lands. Rather, he is pleased for you to obey him in other matters, among your deeds you consider insignificant. Beware, O people! I have surely left among you what you must firmly hold to, by which you will never be led astray again: the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet. Verily, the Muslim is a brother of another Muslim, the Muslims are brethren. It is not lawful for a man to take his brother’s wealth unless he gives it freely and willingly. You may not wrong each other. Do not turn back to the ways of unbelievers after me, striking the necks of each other.”
q: Satan has despaired that he will ever be worshiped in your lands. Rather, he is pleased for you to obey him in other matters, among your deeds you consider insignificant. Beware, O people! I have surely left among you what you must firmly hold to, by which you will never be led astray again: the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet. Verily, the Muslim is a brother of another Muslim, the Muslims are brethren. It is not lawful for a man to take his brother’s wealth unless he gives it freely and willingly. You may not wrong each other. Do not turn back to the ways of unbelievers after me, striking the necks of each other.

title: Hadith on Company: Parable of Quran reciters, righteous friends
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the believer who recites the Quran is that of citron, whose fragrance and taste are pleasant. The parable of the believer who does not recite the Quran is that of a date, whose taste is sweet and has no fragrance. The parable of the wicked who recites the Quran is that of basil, whose fragrance is pleasant and taste is bitter. The parable of the wicked who does not recite the Quran is that of a vine, whose taste is bitter and has no fragrance. The parable of good company is that of a seller of musk; he will smell its fragrance even if he does not buy anything. The parable of bad company is that of a blacksmith; he will smell its smoke even if he is not touched by its ashes.”
q: The parable of the believer who recites the Quran is that of citron, whose fragrance and taste are pleasant. The parable of the believer who does not recite the Quran is that of a date, whose taste is sweet and has no fragrance. The parable of the wicked who recites the Quran is that of basil, whose fragrance is pleasant and taste is bitter. The parable of the wicked who does not recite the Quran is that of a vine, whose taste is bitter and has no fragrance. The parable of good company is that of a seller of musk; he will smell its fragrance even if he does not buy anything. The parable of bad company is that of a blacksmith; he will smell its smoke even if he is not touched by its ashes.

title: Hadith on Honor: Allah frees him for defending his brother
t: Asma’ bint Yazid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever defends the flesh of his brother from backbiting, it will be a duty upon Allah to free him from the Hellfire.”
q: Whoever defends the flesh of his brother from backbiting, it will be a duty upon Allah to free him from the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Backbiting: Man punished in grave for eating flesh, backbiting
t: Ya’la ibn Siyabah reported: He lived in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and they came upon a grave whose occupant was being punished. The Prophet said, “Verily, this person used to eat the flesh of people.”
q: Verily, this person used to eat the flesh of people.
gf: Jayyid (very good) according to Ibn Hajar

title: Hadith on Graves: Two men punished for backbiting, uncleanliness
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by two graves and he said, “Verily, they are both being punished, but not for a sin difficult to avoid. As for one, he is punished for the habit of soiling himself with urine. As for the other, he is punished for the habit of backbiting.”
q: Verily, they are both being punished, but not for a sin difficult to avoid. As for one, he is punished for the habit of soiling himself with urine. As for the other, he is punished for the habit of backbiting

title: Amr on Gheebah: Backbiting worse than eating a dead carcass
t: Qays reported: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by the carcass of a dead mule and he said to his companions, “That one of you eat from this until his belly is full is better than to eat the flesh of his brother Muslim.”

title: Hadith on Gheebah: Enough sin to speak badly about your brothers
t:
Abdullah ibn Amr reported: They mentioned a man in front of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and they said, “He only eats if he is fed! He only moves if he is made to move!” The Prophet said, “You have backbitten him.” They said, “We only said what is true about him.” The Prophet said, “It is enough sin to mention bad things about your brother.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “If what you said about him were not true, you would have slandered him.”
q: You have backbitten him. … It is enough sin to mention bad things about your brother. … If what you said about him were not true, you would have slandered him.

title: Hadith on Mockery: Enormous sin to belittle a believer
t: Aisha reported: I said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “Safiyyah is enough for you as such,” making fun of her short stature. The Prophet said, “You have said a word that would pollute the sea if mixed with it!” She said, “I had caricatured someone before.” The Prophet said, “I do not like to caricature someone for any reason.”
q: You have said a word that would pollute the sea if mixed with it! … I do not like to caricature someone for any reason.

title: Hadith on Riba: Worst act of usury to backbite, slander a believer
t: Sa’id ibn Zayd reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the worst act of usury is to attack the reputation of a Muslim without a just cause.”
q: Verily, the worst act of usury is to attack the reputation of a Muslim without a just cause.

title: Hadith on Riba: Seventy-two doors of usury include backbiting, slander
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Usury has seventy-two doors, the least of which is like a man who goes into his mother. The worst act of usury is for a man to attack the reputation of his brother.”
q: Usury has seventy-two doors, the least of which is like a man who goes into his mother. The worst act of usury is for a man to attack the reputation of his brother.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Muslims: Lives, wealth, honor of believers made sacred
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said in the farewell sermon, “Verily, your lives, your property, and your reputations have been made sacred to you, just as the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours. Will not the witness inform the absent?”
q: Verily, your lives, your property, and your reputations have been made sacred to you, just as the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours. Will not the witness inform the absent?
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Nifaq: Hypocrites with forked-tongues punished in Fire
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever speaks with a forked-tongue in the world, Allah will make two tongues of fire for him on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever speaks with a forked-tongue in the world, Allah will make two tongues of fire for him on the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Two-Faces: Hypocrites with two-faces given tongues of Fire
t: ‘Ammar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever carries two faces in the world, he will have two tongues of fire on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever carries two faces in the world, he will have two tongues of fire on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Nifaq: Hypocrisy to speak two-faced in public and private
t: Muhammad ibn Zayd reported: Some people said to Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, “When we had an audience with a ruler, we would speak to them differently than what we said after we left them.” Ibn Umar said, “We used to consider that hypocrisy.”

title: Hadith on Ummah: Muslim nation ruled by evil if it is arrogant
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When my nation walks with a swagger and their servants are the sons of kings, Persians, and Romans, the worst of them will be given authority over the best of them.”
q: When my nation walks with a swagger and their servants are the sons of kings, Persians, and Romans, the worst of them will be given authority over the best of them.

title: Hadith on Boasts: Earth swallows man for boasting in fine clothes
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man before you left his house wearing two green mantles, boasting in them. Allah commanded the earth to take him. Verily, he will be buried in it until the Day of Resurrection.”
q: A man before you left his house wearing two green mantles, boasting in them. Allah commanded the earth to take him. Verily, he will be buried in it until the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Vanity: Earth swallows man dragging his garment
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “While a man was trailing his robe out of vanity, he was suddenly swallowed up, and he will be buried in the earth until the Day of Resurrection.”
q: While a man was trailing his robe out of vanity, he was suddenly swallowed up, and he will be buried in the earth until the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Bulas: Terrifying punishment of arrogant in Hellfire
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection as tiny particles in the form of men. Disgrace will be cast over them from every side. They will be dragged to a prison in Hell named ‘Despair,’ to be submerged in the fire of all fires, drinking the bile of the people of Hellfire and driving them into madness.”
q: The arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection as tiny particles in the form of men. Disgrace will be cast over them from every side. They will be dragged to a prison in Hell named ‘Despair,’ to be submerged in the fire of all fires, drinking the bile of the people of Hellfire and driving them into madness.

title: Hadith on Kibr: I want my soul to be pure of arrogance
t: Abdullah ibn Hanzalah reported: Abdullah ibn Salaam, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by the market carrying bundles of firewood. It was said to him, “What makes you do this? Allah does not need you to do this.” Abdullah said, “I want to be purged of arrogance. I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: One will not enter Paradise with the weight of a seed of arrogance in his heart.”
q: One will not enter Paradise with the weight of a seed of arrogance in his heart.

title: Hadith on Kibr: Allah throws down the arrogant in Hell
