t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever has the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance in his heart, Allah will throw him down on his face in Hellfire.”
q: Whoever has the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance in his heart, Allah will throw him down on his face in Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Sins: Four people who are hateful to Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are four people who are hateful to Allah Almighty: a merchant swearing false oaths, a conceited poor person, an elder who commits adultery, and an unjust leader.”
q: There are four people who are hateful to Allah Almighty: a merchant swearing false oaths, a conceited poor person, an elder who commits adultery, and an unjust leader.

title: Hadith on Akhirah: Paradise and Hellfire dispute with each other
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Paradise and Hellfire argued with each other. The Hellfire said: The tyrants and the arrogant are in me! Paradise said: The meek among people and their poor are in me! Allah judged between them: You, Paradise, are My mercy that I bestow upon whomever I will. You, Hellfire, are My punishment with which I punish whomever I will. You will both be filled.”
q: Paradise and Hellfire argued with each other. The Hellfire said: The tyrants and the arrogant are in me! Paradise said: The meek among people and their poor are in me! Allah judged between them: You, Paradise, are My mercy that I bestow upon whomever I will. You, Hellfire, are My punishment with which I punish whomever I will. You will both be filled.

title: Hadith on Servitude: Best and worst servants of Allah
t: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you about the worst servants of Allah? They are cruel and arrogant. Shall I not tell you about the best servants of Allah? They are weak, persecuted, and down-trodden, yet if they swear an oath by Allah, Allah will fulfill their oath.”
q: Shall I not tell you about the worst servants of Allah? They are cruel and arrogant. Shall I not tell you about the best servants of Allah? They are weak, persecuted, and down-trodden, yet if they swear an oath by Allah, Allah will fulfill their oath
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Cruelty: Hellfire filled with mean, arrogant sinners
t: Suraqah ibn Ju’shum reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Suraqah, shall I tell you about the people of Paradise and Hellfire?” Suraqah said, “Of course, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “As for the people of Hellfire, it is everyone hard-hearted, cruel, and arrogant. As for the people of Paradise, they are the meek and downtrodden.”
q: O Suraqah, shall I tell you about the people of Paradise and Hellfire? … As for the people of Hellfire, it is everyone hard-hearted, cruel, and arrogant. As for the people of Paradise, they are the meek and downtrodden
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Arrogance: Do not ask about three ruined people
t: Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not ask about three people: a man who competes for the robe of Allah Almighty, for His robe is grandeur and His garment is might, a man who doubts in the matter of Allah, and one who despairs of the mercy of Allah.”
q: Do not ask about three people: a man who competes for the robe of Allah Almighty, for His robe is grandeur and His garment is might, a man who doubts in the matter of Allah, and one who despairs of the mercy of Allah.

title: Hadith on Arrogance: Competing with Allah will end in disgrace
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty says: Grandeur is My cloak and pride is My garment. Whoever competes with Me in one of these two, I will throw him into the Hellfire.”
q: Allah Almighty says: Grandeur is My cloak and pride is My garment. Whoever competes with Me in one of these two, I will throw him into the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Angels: Guided by humility, humbled by arrogance
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no human being but that over his head are reins in the hands of an angel. If he is humble, it is said to the angel: Raise up his reins! If he is haughty, it is said to the angel: Lower his reins!”
q: “There is no human being but that over his head are reins in the hands of an angel. If he is humble, it is said to the angel: Raise up his reins! If he is haughty, it is said to the angel: Lower his reins!

title: Hadith on Debt: Paradise if he dies free of arrogance, theft, debt
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever dies innocent of these three, arrogance, embezzlement, and debt, he will enter Paradise.”
q: Whoever dies innocent of these three, arrogance, embezzlement, and debt, he will enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Humanity: All people go back equally to Adam and Eve
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, these lineages of yours cannot be used to disparage anyone. You are all the children of Adam, going back to him equally, and cannot be exceeded. No one is favored except by religion or good deeds. It is enough sin for a man to be vulgar, shameless, miserly, and cowardly.”
q: Verily, these lineages of yours cannot be used to disparage anyone. You are all the children of Adam, going back to him equally, and cannot be exceeded. No one is favored except by religion or good deeds. It is enough sin for a man to be vulgar, shameless, miserly, and cowardly.

title: Hadith on Bukhl: Never seen anyone as miserly as you!
t: Jabir reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Indeed, I share the wall of a cloister with someone who bothers me and makes things difficult for me.” The Prophet sent for the man and he said, “Sell me your cloister that is on the wall of your neighbor.” The man said no. The Prophet said, “Then give it to me.” The man said no. The Prophet said, “Then buy it from me for a cloister in Paradise.” The men said no. The Prophet said, “I have not seen anyone more miserly than you, except for those who are miserly with the greeting of peace.”
q: Sell me your cloister that is on the wall of your neighbor … Then give it to me … Then buy it from me for a cloister in Paradise. … I have not seen anyone more miserly than you, except for those who are miserly with the greeting of peace.

title: Hadith on Sins: Five major sins have no expiation, only full repentance
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Five sins cannot be expiated: idolatry with Allah, killing a soul without a just cause, slandering a believer, fleeing the battlefield, and bearing false witness to consume the wealth of another without right.”
q: Five sins cannot be expiated: idolatry with Allah, killing a soul without a just cause, slandering a believer, fleeing the battlefield, and bearing false witness to consume the wealth of another without right.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for a new convert to Islam
t: Tariq ibn al-Ashyam reported: Whenever a man embraced Islam, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would teach him the prayer. Then, the Prophet instructed him to supplicate with these words, “O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, grant me wellness, and provide for me.” The Prophet brought his fingers together, saying, “Verily, these words encompass your worldly life and your Hereafter.”
q: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, grant me wellness, and provide for me … Verily, these words encompass your worldly life and your Hereafter.

title: Hadith on Arrogance: Three sinful people will not enter Paradise
t: Salman reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Three people will not enter Paradise: an elderly person who commits adultery, a dishonest leader, and a conceited dependent.”
q: Three people will not enter Paradise: an elderly person who commits adultery, a dishonest leader, and a conceited dependent.

title: Hadith on Iman: No true faith until he stops arguing in religion
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the servant does not entirely have faith until he abandons lying even while joking, and he abandons arguing even if he is truthful.”
q: Verily, the servant does not entirely have faith until he abandons lying even while joking, and he abandons arguing even if he is truthful.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Nifaq: Hypocrisy of one who claims faith but lies
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever has three traits is a hypocrite, even if he fasts, prays, goes to Hajj and Umrah, and claims to be a Muslim. When he speaks, he lies. When he promises, he breaks it. When he is trusted, he betrays it.”
q: Whoever has three traits is a hypocrite, even if he fasts, prays, goes to Hajj and Umrah, and claims to be a Muslim. When he speaks, he lies. When he promises, he breaks it. When he is trusted, he betrays it.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Truth: You must be truthful, avoid dishonesty
t: Mu’awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must be truthful. Verily, it leads to righteousness and they are both in Paradise. Beware of dishonesty, for it leads to wickedness and they are both in the Hellfire.”
q: You must be truthful. Verily, it leads to righteousness and they are both in Paradise. Beware of dishonesty, for it leads to wickedness and they are both in the Hellfire
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Deeds: Six good deeds to assure entry into Paradise
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Accept six deeds from me and I assure your acceptance into Paradise. When one of you speaks, let him not lie. When one of you promises, let him not break it. When one of you is trusted, let him not betray it. Lower your gaze, restrain your hands from harming others, and guard your chastity.”
q: Accept six deeds from me and I assure your acceptance into Paradise. When one of you speaks, let him not lie. When one of you promises, let him not break it. When one of you is trusted, let him not betray it. Lower your gaze, restrain your hands from harming others, and guard your chastity.

title: Hadith on Gossip: Best servants remind of Allah, worst spread rumors
t: ‘Abdur Rahman ibn Ghanm reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best servants of Allah are those who remind you of Allah when they are seen. The worst servants of Allah are those who carry gossip, sowing discord between loved ones and wishing misery upon the innocent.”
q: The best servants of Allah are those who remind you of Allah when they are seen. The worst servants of Allah are those who carry gossip, sowing discord between loved ones and wishing misery upon the innocent
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Gossip: Punished in the grave for spreading gossip
t: Abu Huraira reported: We were walking with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when we passed by two graves. The Prophet stood over them and we stood with him. The color of his face changed until it was white like the sleeve of his shirt. We said, “What is wrong, O Prophet of Allah?” The Prophet said, “You cannot hear what I hear.” We said, “What is that, O Prophet of Allah?” The Prophet said, “These two men are being severely punished in their graves for a trivial matter.” We said, “What is that, O Prophet of Allah?” The Prophet said, “One of them did not take care to keep his garments clean of urine. The other harmed people with his tongue, carrying gossip between them.”
q: You cannot hear what I hear. … These two men are being severely punished in their graves for a trivial matter. … One of them did not take care to keep his garments clean of urine. The other harmed people with his tongue, carrying gossip between them.

title: Hadith on Thorns: Man enjoys Paradise for clearing out a thorny tree
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: There was a tree in the road that used to harm people, so a man came and cleared it from the road. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have seen him enjoying himself in its shade in Paradise.”
q: I have seen him enjoying himself in its shade in Paradise.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Every day 360 acts of charity are due
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, every human being among the children of Adam was created with three hundred and sixty joints. Whoever exalts Allah, praises Allah, declares Allah is one, glorifies Allah, removes a rock from the roads of people, or a thorn, or a bone from the roads of people, and enjoins good and forbids evil by the number of those joints, he will walk on that day delivering himself from the Hellfire.”
q: Verily, every human being among the children of Adam was created with three hundred and sixty joints. Whoever exalts Allah, praises Allah, declares Allah is one, glorifies Allah, removes a rock from the roads of people, or a thorn, or a bone from the roads of people, and enjoins good and forbids evil by the number of those joints, he will walk on that day delivering himself from the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Roads: Entry into Paradise by removing obstacles
t: Abu Darda reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever pulls something out of the roads of the Muslims that harms them, Allah will record a good deed for him. Whoever has a good deed written for him, Allah will admit him into Paradise by it.”
q: Whoever pulls something out of the roads of the Muslims that harms them, Allah will record a good deed for him. Whoever has a good deed written for him, Allah will admit him into Paradise by it.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Hasanat: Removing harm from roads leads to Paradise
t: Ma’qil ibn Yasar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever clears harmful things from the roads of the Muslims, a good deed will be recorded for him. Whoever is awarded a good deed, he will enter Paradise.”
q: Whoever clears harmful things from the roads of the Muslims, a good deed will be recorded for him. Whoever is awarded a good deed, he will enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Charity due upon joints of human being
t: Abu Buraydah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Inside the human being are three hundred and sixty joints, upon each of them charity is due.” They said, “Who can do that, O Prophet of Allah?” The Prophet said, “It is spittle in the mosque you clean, or something in the road you move to the side. If you cannot find anything, it is enough to perform two cycles of forenoon prayer.”
q: Inside the human being are three hundred and sixty joints, upon each of them charity is due. … It is spittle in the mosque you clean, or something in the road you move to the side. If you cannot find anything, it is enough to perform two cycles of forenoon prayer.

title: Hadith on Charity: Doors of virtuous good deeds are plentiful
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no soul in the son of Adam but that charity is due upon it on every day the sun rises.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, from what can we give in charity?” The Prophet said, “The doors of virtue are many: to glorify Allah, to praise Allah, to exalt Allah, to declare Allah is one, to enjoin good, to forbid evil, to clear harmful things from the road, to help a deaf person hear, to guide a blind person, to direct a person to meet his needs, to lend great effort to one worried and seeking aid, and to carry a heavy load in your hands on behalf of the weak. All of this is your charity, due upon your soul.”
q: There is no soul in the son of Adam but that charity is due upon it on every day the sun rises … The doors of virtue are many: to glorify Allah, to praise Allah, to exalt Allah, to declare Allah is one, to enjoin good, to forbid evil, to clear harmful things from the road, to help a deaf person hear, to guide a blind person, to direct a person to meet his needs, to lend great effort to one worried and seeking aid, and to carry a heavy load in your hands on behalf of the weak. All of this is your charity, due upon your soul.

title: Hadith on Faith: Abu Dharr loves Allah and His Messenger
t: Abu Dharr reported: He said, “O Messenger of Allah, a man loves a people, but he cannot do good deeds like they do.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You, O Abu Dharr, will be with those you love.” Abu Dharr said, “I love Allah and His Messenger.” The Prophet said, “Verily, you will be with those you love.”
q: You, O Abu Dharr, will be with those you love. … Verily, you will be with those you love.

title: Hadith on Love: Which handle of Islam is most reliable?
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: We were sitting with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Which handle of Islam is the most firm?” They said, “Prayer.” The Prophet said, “It is good, but that is not it.” They said, “Charity.” The Prophet said, “It is good, but that is not it.” They said, “Fasting the month of Ramadan.” The Prophet said, “It is good, but that is not it.” They said, “The Hajj pilgrimage.” The Prophet said, “It is good, but that is not it.” They said, “Jihad.” The Prophet said, “It is good, but that is not it. Verily, the most trustworthy handle of faith is to love and hatred for the sake of Allah.”
q: Which handle of Islam is the most firm? … It is good, but that is not it. … It is good, but that is not it … It is good, but that is not it … It is good, but that is not it. … It is good, but that is not it. Verily, the most trustworthy handle of faith is to love and hatred for the sake of Allah.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Love: Great honor bestowed on sincere loving believers
t: Abu Malik al-Ashari reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O people, listen, understand, and know that Allah Almighty has servants who are neither prophets, nor martyrs, yet the prophets and martyrs admire them for their position and closeness to Allah.” A man among the bedouins of a distant land came and he waved to the Prophet, saying, “O Prophet of Allah, describe them to us.” The Prophet was pleased by the bedouin’s question, and he said, “They are people from faraway lands and different tribes. They have no close familial relationship between them. They sincerely love each other for the sake of Allah. Allah will place them on pulpits of light on the Day of Resurrection and grant them an audience. He will place light on their faces and light on their garments. People will be terrified on the Day of Resurrection, yet they will not be terrified. They are the allies of Allah, upon whom there is no fear or grief.” (10:62)
q: O people, listen, understand, and know that Allah Almighty has servants who are neither prophets, nor martyrs, yet the prophets and martyrs admire them for their position and closeness to Allah. … They are people from faraway lands and different tribes. They have no close familial relationship between them. They sincerely love each other for the sake of Allah. Allah will place them on pulpits of light on the Day of Resurrection and grant them an audience. He will place light on their faces and light on their garments. People will be terrified on the Day of Resurrection, yet they will not be terrified. They are the allies of Allah, upon whom there is no fear or grief
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Love: Loving believers in the shade of the Throne
t: Al-‘Irbad ibn Sariyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: Those who loved each other for the sake of My glory will be in the shade of My throne, on a Day there is no shade but Mine.”
q: Allah Almighty said: Those who loved each other for the sake of My glory will be in the shade of My throne, on a Day there is no shade but Mine.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Jannah: Loving believers at right side of the Throne
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah will have an audience on the Day of Resurrection, sitting on the right side of His Throne, and both sides are honored as the right. They will be upon pulpits of light and there will be light upon their faces, yet they are not prophets, nor martyrs, nor disciples.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, who are they?” The Prophet said, “Those who loved each other for the glory of Allah Almighty.”
q: Verily, Allah will have an audience on the Day of Resurrection, sitting on the right side of His Throne, and both sides are honored as the right. They will be upon pulpits of light and there will be light upon their faces, yet they are not prophets, nor martyrs, nor disciples. … Those who loved each other for the glory of Allah Almighty

title: Hadith on Friendship: Allah’s love upon friends for His sake
t: ‘Amr ibn ‘Abasah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: My love is a right upon those who befriend each other for My sake, and My love is a right upon those who defend each other for My sake.”
q: Allah Almighty said: My love is a right upon those who befriend each other for My sake, and My love is a right upon those who defend each other for My sake.

title: Hadith on Love: Allah loves most those who love others
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No two men love each other for the sake of Allah, behind their backs, but that the most beloved of them to Allah has the strongest love for his companion.”
q: No two men love each other for the sake of Allah, behind their backs, but that the most beloved of them to Allah has the strongest love for his companion.

title: Hadith on Faith: Sweetness of faith to love for Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever would be pleased to taste the flavor of faith, let him love a person only for the sake of Allah Almighty.”
q: Whoever would be pleased to taste the flavor of faith, let him love a person only for the sake of Allah Almighty

title: Hadith on Dua: Travelers, parents, oppressed answered by Allah
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The supplications of three people are answered: the traveler, the parents, and the oppressed.”
q: The supplications of three people are answered: the traveler, the parents, and the oppressed.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Greetings: Sins expiated by shaking hands
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when the Muslim shakes hands with his brother, both of their sins fall away like the falling of leaves from a tree.”
q: Verily, when the Muslim shakes hands with his brother, both of their sins fall away like the falling of leaves from a tree.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Greetings: Shaking hands, hugging after long journey
t: Anas reported: If the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, met each other, they would shake hands. If they had returned from a journey, they would embrace each other.

title: Hadith on Arrogance: No pleasure to be received standing
t: Mu’awiyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is pleased to be received by men standing, let him take his seat in the Hellfire.”
q: Whoever is pleased to be received by men standing, let him take his seat in the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Salaam: Greet with peace arriving and leaving
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man passed by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was sitting in a gathering. The man said, “Peace be upon you.” The Prophet said, “Ten good deeds.” Another man passed by, saying, “Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah.” The Prophet said, “Twenty good deeds.” Another man passed by, saying, “Peace be upon you, the mercy of Allah, and His blessings.” The Prophet said, “Thirty good deeds.” A man stood up to leave the gathering and he did not offer salutations of peace. The Prophet said, “How quickly your companion forgets! If one of you comes to a gathering, let him greet them with peace. If there is room for him to sit, let him sit. If he stands to leave, let him offer salutations of peace. The former duty is no different than the latter.”
q: Ten good deeds … Twenty good deeds … Thirty good deeds … How quickly your companion forgets! If one of you comes to a gathering, let him greet them with peace. If there is room for him to sit, let him sit. If he stands to leave, let him offer salutations of peace. The former duty is no different than the latter

title: Hadith on Salaam: Thirty good deeds for peace, blessings, mercy
t: Sahl ibn Hunayf reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever greets with peace, ten goods are recorded for him. Whoever greets with peace and the mercy of Allah, twenty good deeds are recorded for him. Whoever greets with peace, the mercy of Allah, and His blessings, thirty good deeds are recorded for him.”
q: Whoever greets with peace, ten goods are recorded for him. Whoever greets with peace and the mercy of Allah, twenty good deeds are recorded for him. Whoever greets with peace, the mercy of Allah, and His blessings, thirty good deeds are recorded for him.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Salaam: Salutations of peace when coming and going
t: Mu’adh ibn Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is a duty upon one arriving at a gathering to offer greetings of peace to them. It is a duty upon one leaving a gathering to offer salutations of peace to them.”
q: It is a duty upon one arriving at a gathering to offer greetings of peace to them. It is a duty upon one leaving a gathering to offer salutations of peace to them.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Salaam: Greeting with peace after brief separation
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: We would be with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and if we were separated by a tree and we met again, we would greet each other with peace again.

title: Hadith on Salaam: Allah’s name is Peace, spread His Peace on earth
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, peace is among the names of Allah that He has placed on the earth, so spread it between yourselves. If a man greets people with peace and they answer him, he is favored by a degree over them as he has reminded them. If they do not answer him, he is answered by the angels who are better and purer than them.”
q: Verily, peace is among the names of Allah that He has placed on the earth, so spread it between yourselves. If a man greets people with peace and they answer him, he is favored by a degree over them as he has reminded them. If they do not answer him, he is answered by the angels who are better and purer than them.

title: Hadith on Hiqd: Allah leaves people of grudges to their malice
t: Abu Tha’labah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “On the middle night of Sha’ban, Allah looks down upon His creation and He forgives the believers, gives respite to the unbelievers, and He abandons the people of malice to their malice until they give it up.”
q: On the middle night of Sha’ban, Allah looks down upon His creation and He forgives the believers, gives respite to the unbelievers, and He abandons the people of malice to their malice until they give it up.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Sha’ban: Allah forgives believers in mid-Sha’ban
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah looks down at His creation on the middle night of Sha’ban and He forgives all of His creatures, except for an idolater or one carrying hostility.”
q: Allah looks down at His creation on the middle night of Sha’ban and He forgives all of His creatures, except for an idolater or one carrying hostility.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Boycott: He left Islam until he reconciles
t: Yazid ibn Wahb reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “No two men who have entered Islam boycott each other but that one of them has left it until he returns. His return to Islam is going to him and greeting him with peace.”

title: Hadith on Boycotts: Boycotter in Hell, unless Allah shows mercy
t: Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever boycotts his brother for more than three days, he is in the Hellfire unless the generosity of Allah reaches him.”
q: Whoever boycotts his brother for more than three days, he is in the Hellfire unless the generosity of Allah reaches him.

title: Hadith on Boycott: Fear of Muslims boycotting each other
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is not lawful to boycott for more than three days. If the two meet and one greets the other with peace and receives a response, they will share the reward. If the other refuses to return his greeting, he is free of sin and it backfires against the one boycotting. I fear that if the two die while boycotting each other, they will not be together in Paradise.”
q: It is not lawful to boycott for more than three days. If the two meet and one greets the other with peace and receives a response, they will share the reward. If the other refuses to return his greeting, he is free of sin and it backfires against the one boycotting. I fear that if the two die while boycotting each other, they will not be together in Paradise.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Boycott: After three days, sin backfires onto boycotter
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A Muslim may not boycott another Muslim for more than three days. Then, if he meets him, greets him with peace three times, and he receives no response, the sin falls back on the one still boycotting.”
q: A Muslim may not boycott another Muslim for more than three days. Then, if he meets him, greets him with peace three times, and he receives no response, the sin falls back on the one still boycotting.

title: Hadith on Boycott: Hellfire if he dies boycotting his brother
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is not lawful for a Muslim to boycott his brother for more than three days. Whoever boycotts for more than three days and dies, he will enter Hellfire.”
q: It is not lawful for a Muslim to boycott his brother for more than three days. Whoever boycotts for more than three days and dies, he will enter Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Sins: Avoid seven major sins, idolatry, killing
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Stay away from seven mortal sins.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what are they?” The Prophet said, “Idolatry with Allah, occult magic, killing a soul that Allah has sanctified except for a just cause, consuming usury, usurping the property of an orphan, fleeing the battlefield, and accusing chaste but unwary believing women.”
q: Stay away from seven mortal sins. … Idolatry with Allah, occult magic, killing a soul that Allah has sanctified except for a just cause, consuming usury, usurping the property of an orphan, fleeing the battlefield, and accusing chaste but unwary believing women
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Weather: Do not curse wind directed by Allah
t: Ibn Abbas reported: A man cursed the wind in front of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet said, “Do not curse the wind, for it only acts as it was commanded. Verily, whoever curses anything that does not deserve it, the curse will backfire against him.”
q: Do not curse the wind, for it only acts as it was commanded. Verily, whoever curses anything that does not deserve it, the curse will backfire against him.

title: Hadith on Cursing: Do not curse roosters, they wake you for prayer
t: Zayd ibn Khalid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not disparage the rooster, as it wakes you up for prayer.”
q: Do not disparage the rooster, as it wakes you up for prayer.

title: Hadith on Cursing: Be careful what you curse for
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was riding on a journey and a man cursed his she-camel. The Prophet said, “Where is the owner of the she-camel?” The man said, “It is me.” The Prophet said, “Leave her behind, for your curse has been answered.”
q: Where is the owner of the she-camel? … Leave her behind, for your curse has been answered
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Animals: Do not curse your riding animals
t: Anas reported: A man was riding with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he cursed his camel. The Prophet said, “O servant of Allah, do not ride with us upon a cursed camel!”
q: O servant of Allah, do not ride with us upon a cursed camel

title: Hadith on Cursing: Unjust curses backfire on accuser
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a curse is uttered, it is directed to the one for whom it was uttered. If it finds a path and a way, it is allowed to proceed. Otherwise, it returns to its Lord, saying: O Lord, such a person directed me to another, but I did not find a way and a path, so what do you command? Allah will say: Return against the one from whom you came.”
q: When a curse is uttered, it is directed to the one for whom it was uttered. If it finds a path and a way, it is allowed to proceed. Otherwise, it returns to its Lord, saying: O Lord, such a person directed me to another, but I did not find a way and a path, so what do you command? Allah will say: Return against the one from whom you came
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Curses: We viewed cursing brothers as major sin
t: Yazid ibn Abi ‘Ubayd reported: Salamah ibn al-Akwa’, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “If we saw a man curse his brother, we considered it as if he had come to a door of mortal sin.”

title: Hadith on Cursing: Not befitting believers to curse others
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believer is not in the habit of cursing others.”
q: The believer is not in the habit of cursing others.

title: Hadith on Cursing: Insulting believers on brink of destruction
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Cursing a believer is like being on the brink of destruction.”
q: Cursing a believer is like being on the brink of destruction.

title: Hadith on Takfir: He commits unbelief by wrongly accusing believers
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man never accuses another man of unbelief but that it backfires on one of them. Either he is an unbeliever, or he has committed unbelief by his accusation.”
q: A man never accuses another man of unbelief but that it backfires on one of them. Either he is an unbeliever, or he has committed unbelief by his accusation.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Jannah: Special rooms for kind words, praying at night
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, in Paradise, are rooms whose outside can be seen from inside and whose inside can be seen from outside.” Abu Musa said, “Who are they for, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “For those who speak mildly, feed the hungry, and spend the night standing for the sake of Allah while people sleep.”
q: Verily, in Paradise, are rooms whose outside can be seen from inside and whose inside can be seen from outside … For those who speak mildly, feed the hungry, and spend the night standing for the sake of Allah while people sleep

title: Hadith on Jannah: Feeding hungry, kind words in Paradise
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Feed the hungry, spread peace, speak kind words, and pray at night when people are sleeping. You will enter Paradise in peace.”
q: Feed the hungry, spread peace, speak kind words, and pray at night when people are sleeping. You will enter Paradise in peace
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Do not belittle any charity, do not return insults
t: Abu Jurayy reported: I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and I said, “O Messenger of Allah, we are people of the desert. Teach us something with which Allah will benefit us.” The Prophet said, “Do not belittle any good deed, even pouring your leftovers into another’s cistern, even speaking to your brother while smiling at him. Beware of trailing your garment; it is a form of vanity that Allah does not approve. If a man insults you with what he knows about you, do not insult him with what you know about him. Verily, you will have a reward, and the penalty is upon the one who spoke it.”
q: Do not belittle any good deed, even pouring your leftovers into another’s cistern, even speaking to your brother while smiling at him. Beware of trailing your garment; it is a form of vanity that Allah does not approve. If a man insults you with what he knows about you, do not insult him with what you know about him. Verily, you will have a reward, and the penalty is upon the one who spoke it.

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Removing harm, enjoining good are charity
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, your smile in the face of your brother is charity. Lifting harmful things from the road is recorded for you as charity. Pouring your leftovers into your brother’s vessel is charity. Enjoining good and forbidding evil is your charity. Guiding a lost person is charity.”
q: Verily, your smile in the face of your brother is charity. Lifting harmful things from the road is recorded for you as charity. Pouring your leftovers into your brother’s vessel is charity. Enjoining good and forbidding evil is your charity. Guiding a lost person is charity.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Cheerful face, guiding travelers are charity
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Smiling in the face of your brother is your charity. Enjoining good and forbidding evil is charity. Guiding a lost man through the land is your charity. Lending your eyesight to a man who cannot see well is your charity. Removing rocks, thorns, and bones from the road is your charity. Pouring your leftovers into your brother’s vessel is your charity.”
q: Smiling in the face of your brother is your charity. Enjoining good and forbidding evil is charity. Guiding a lost man through the land is your charity. Lending your eyesight to a man who cannot see well is your charity. Removing rocks, thorns, and bones from the road is your charity. Pouring your leftovers into your brother’s vessel is your charity.

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Worst Muslims talk too much
t: Abu Tha’labah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most beloved of you and closest to me in the Hereafter are those with the best character. The most hateful of you to me and furthest from me in the Hereafter are those with the worst character: the braggarts, the verbose, the loquacious.”
q: Verily, the most beloved of you and closest to me in the Hereafter are those with the best character. The most hateful of you to me and furthest from me in the Hereafter are those with the worst character: the braggarts, the verbose, the loquacious.

title: Hadith on Gossip: Worst Muslims spread rumors, divide people
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most beloved to me are those of you with the best character, soft in nature, friendly and befriended. The most hateful of you to Allah are those who spread gossip, causing discord between loved ones and seeking misery for the innocent.”
q: Verily, the most beloved to me are those of you with the best character, soft in nature, friendly and befriended. The most hateful of you to Allah are those who spread gossip, causing discord between loved ones and seeking misery for the innocent.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Best Muslims have longest lives, good character
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of you are those with the longest lives and the most excellent character.”
q: The best of you are those with the longest lives and the most excellent character.

title: Hadith on Life: Best Muslims have long lives full of good deeds
t: Abdullah ibn Busr reported: A bedouin said, “O Messenger of Allah, who are the best people?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One with a long life of good deeds.”
q: One with a long life of good deeds

title: Hadith on Khuluq: Allah lets him achieve greatness by good character
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah lets a servant achieve by his good character the rank of one who regularly fasts and prays.”
q: Verily, Allah lets a servant achieve by his good character the rank of one who regularly fasts and prays.

title: Hadith on Khuluq: By good character he reaches incredible heights
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, a man may reach by his good character the rank of one who stands for prayer at night, thirsty from fasting in the heat of day.”
q: Verily, a man may reach by his good character the rank of one who stands for prayer at night, thirsty from fasting in the heat of day.

title: Hadith on Rifq: Allah loves kindness, making things easy
t: Abdullah ibn Mughaffal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is gentle and he loves gentleness. He gives for it what is not given for harshness.”
q: Verily, Allah is gentle and he loves gentleness. He gives for it what is not given for harshness

title: Hadith on Rifq: Allah supports kindness, gentleness and loves it
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty loves gentleness and is pleased with it. He lends support for in a way he does not support harshness.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty loves gentleness and is pleased with it. He lends support for in a way he does not support harshness.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Haya: Islam is characterized by modesty
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, every religion has a character and the character of Islam is modesty.”
q: Verily, every religion has a character and the character of Islam is modesty.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Haya: If modesty and obscenity took human form
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If modesty were to take the form of a man, he would be a righteous man. If shamelessness were to take the form of a man, he would be a wicked man.”
q: If modesty were to take the form of a man, he would be a righteous man. If shamelessness were to take the form of a man, he would be a wicked man.

title: Hadith on Haya: All of Islam revolves around modesty
t: Qurrah ibn Iyas reported: We were with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when modesty was mentioned to him. They said, “O Messenger of Allah, is modesty part of the religion?” The Prophet said, “Rather, it is the entire religion.” Then, the Prophet said, “Verily, modesty, abstinence, reticence of the tongue but not the heart, and deeds are all part of faith. They bring gain in the Hereafter and loss in the world: what is gained in the Hereafter is much greater than what is missed in the world.”
q: Rather, it is the entire religion … Verily, modesty, abstinence, reticence of the tongue but not the heart, and deeds are all part of faith. They bring gain in the Hereafter and loss in the world: what is gained in the Hereafter is much greater than what is missed in the world.

title: Hadith on Words: Enormous consequences for speaking
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, a servant may speak a word pleasing to Allah, thinking nothing of it, yet by it Allah raises his status by a degree. Verily, a servant may speak a word displeasing to Allah, thinking nothing of it, yet by it he plummets into Hell.”
q: Verily, a servant may speak a word pleasing to Allah, thinking nothing of it, yet by it Allah raises his status by a degree. Verily, a servant may speak a word displeasing to Allah, thinking nothing of it, yet by it he plummets into Hell.

title: Hadith on Speech: Every limb complains of a sharp tongue
t: Abu Bakr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no limb on the body but that it complains of the sharpness of the tongue.”
q: There is no limb on the body but that it complains of the sharpness of the tongue.

title: Hadith on Ihsan: Worship Allah as you see Him, control your words
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: He said, “O Messenger of Allah, instruct me.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Worship Allah as if you can see Him and prepare yourself for death. If you wish, I will tell you what should be reigned in more than all of that. It is this,” and the Prophet pointed to his tongue.
q: Worship Allah as if you can see Him and prepare yourself for death. If you wish, I will tell you what should be reigned in more than all of that. It is this,

title: Hadith on Discipline: Use words and deeds only for good
t: Aswad ibn Asram reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, instruct me.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Can you control your tongue?” I said, “But what do I control if I cannot control my tongue?” The Prophet said, “Can you control your hands?” I said, “But what do I control if I cannot control my hands?” The Prophet said, “Do not say anything on your tongue except what is right, and do not stretch out your hand except to do good.”
q: Can you control your tongue? … Can you control your hands? … Do not say anything on your tongue except what is right, and do not stretch out your hand except to do good

title: Hadith on Speech: Hold firmly in control of your words
t: Al-Harith ibn Hisham reported: He said, “Tell me of a matter I can hold firmly.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Control this,” and he pointed to his tongue.
q: Control this

title: Hadith on Chastity: Guarding speech, controlling lust in Paradise
t: Abu Rafi’ reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever protects what is between his jaws and his thighs, he will enter Paradise.”
q: Whoever protects what is between his jaws and his thighs, he will enter Paradise

title: Hadith on Chastity: Whoever guards tongue, passions in Paradise
t: Abu Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever guards what is between his jaws and guards his chastity, he will enter Paradise.”
q: Whoever guards what is between his jaws and guards his chastity, he will enter Paradise.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Virtue: Blessed one controls speech, weeps for sins
t: Thawban reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Blessed is one who controls his tongue, whose house is spacious enough, and who weeps for his sins.”
q: Blessed is one who controls his tongue, whose house is spacious enough, and who weeps for his sins.

title: Hadith on Speech: Restrain your tongue except good words
t: Al-Bara’ reported: A bedouin came, saying, “O Prophet of Allah, teach me a deed that will admit me into Paradise.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Although you have expressed it in few words, the matter is broad. Emancipate an individual, and free a slave.” The man said, “Are they not the same?” The Prophet said, “No, emancipating an individual is that you emancipate him yourself, and freeing a slave is that you help someone else free him. Lend a healthy animal to be milked, and treat your relatives well. If you cannot do that, enjoin good and forbid evil. If you cannot do that, hold back your tongue except to say good words.”
q: Although you have expressed it in few words, the matter is broad. Emancipate an individual, and free a slave. … No, emancipating an individual is that you emancipate him yourself, and freeing a slave is that you help someone else free him. Lend a healthy animal to be milked, and treat your relatives well. If you cannot do that, enjoin good and forbid evil. If you cannot do that, hold back your tongue except to say good words

title: Hadith on Salah: Best deed to pray on time
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, which deeds are best?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Prayer on time.” I said, “Then what, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Good treatment of your parents.” I said, “Then what, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “That people are safe from your tongue.”
q: Prayer on time … Good treatment of your parents … That people are safe from your tongue

title: Hadith on Islam: Best Muslims do no harm with words, deeds
t: Abu Musa reported: They said, “O Messenger, of Allah, whose Islam is best?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One from whose tongue and hand Muslims are safe.”
q: One from whose tongue and hand Muslims are safe
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Speech: The Prophet fears sins of the tongue
t: Sufyan ibn ‘Abdillah reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell me of a matter I can depend upon?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Say: My Lord is Allah. Then, remain upright.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you fear most for me?” The Prophet pointed to his tongue, saying, “This.”
q: Say: My Lord is Allah. Then, remain upright … This

title: Hadith on Nafs: Only the strong can defeat their lower-self
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The strong are not those who defeat people. Rather, the strong are those who defeat their own ego.”
q: The strong are not those who defeat people. Rather, the strong are those who defeat their own ego

title: Hadith on Anger: Teach me a saying to benefit me in the Hereafter
t: Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, give me a word that will benefit me, but keep it short so I can understand it.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not be angry.” The man repeated the question, and the Prophet said every time, “Do not be angry.”
q: Do not be angry … Do not be angry

title: Hadith on Anger: Distance yourself from wrath of Allah
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: He asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “What will distance me from the anger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Do not be angry.”
q: Do not be angry
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Rage: Anger gives rise to every evil
t: Humayd reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, instruct me.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not be angry.” The man said, “I reflected upon what the Prophet said, and it occurred to me that anger gives rise to every evil.”
q: Do not be angry

title: Hadith on Wealth: Little but enough better than abundant but heedless
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “What is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and negligent.”
q: What is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and negligent.

title: Hadith on Hamd: Paradise for praising Allah in every circumstance
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The first to be called to Paradise are those who always praised Allah in times of prosperity and adversity.”
q: The first to be called to Paradise are those who always praised Allah in times of prosperity and adversity.

title: Hadith on Dreams: Truest dreams seen in last hours of night
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most truthful of dreams are seen shortly before dawn.”
q: The most truthful of dreams are seen shortly before dawn.

title: Hadith on Angels: Two come every day and night
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The sun never rises but that two angels are sent at its sides, calling out. All the earth’s inhabitants hear them, except humans and jinn: O people, come quickly to your Lord! What is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and negligent! The sun never sets but two angels are sent at its sides, calling out. All the earth’s inhabitants hear them, except humans and jinn: O Allah, repay the one who spends in charity! O Allah, destroy the one who withholds charity!”
q: The sun never rises but that two angels are sent at its sides, calling out. All the earth’s inhabitants hear them, except humans and jinn: O people, come quickly to your Lord! What is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and negligent! The sun never sets but two angels are sent at its sides, calling out. All the earth’s inhabitants hear them, except humans and jinn: O Allah, repay the one who spends in charity! O Allah, destroy the one who withholds charity!

title: Amir on Certainty: If the Veil lifted, our conviction not increased
t: Al-Qushayri reported: ‘Amr ibn Abdi Qays, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Were the veil over the Unseen to be lifted, that would not increase our conviction.”

title: Hadith on Justice: He is in Paradise if his justice overcomes his injustice
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever seeks to be a judge over the Muslims such that he acquires it and his justice outweighs his tyranny, he will have Paradise. If his tyranny outweighs his justice, he will have Hellfire.”
q: Whoever seeks to be a judge over the Muslims such that he acquires it and his justice outweighs his tyranny, he will have Paradise. If his tyranny outweighs his justice, he will have Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Authority: Allah sends angels to guide an unwilling judge
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever seeks to be a judge and asks others to intercede so he can have it, he will be left to himself. Whoever is forced into it, Allah will send down an angel to direct him.”
q: Whoever seeks to be a judge and asks others to intercede so he can have it, he will be left to himself. Whoever is forced into it, Allah will send down an angel to direct him

title: Hadith on Imams: Allah treats rulers as they treated their subjects
t: Mu’adh reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is appointed over the affairs of people in any way and he conceals benefit from the weak and the needy, Allah will conceal benefit from him on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever is appointed over the affairs of people in any way and he conceals benefit from the weak and the needy, Allah will conceal benefit from him on the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Imams: Leaders chained on Judgment Day until justice is served
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No man is appointed as leader for more than ten days but that he will be brought on the Day of Resurrection with his hands shackled to his neck, until judgment is issued between him and them.”
q: No man is appointed as leader for more than ten days but that he will be brought on the Day of Resurrection with his hands shackled to his neck, until judgment is issued between him and them.

title: Hadith on Imams: A single night of dishonest leadership leads to Hellfire
t: Abdullah ibn Maghaffal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No Imam or authority spends the dark of night being deceptive in his jurisdiction but that Allah will forbid him from entering Paradise.”
q: No Imam or authority spends the dark of night being deceptive in his jurisdiction but that Allah will forbid him from entering Paradise.

title: Hadith on Ghish: Malevolent and dishonest leaders are in Hellfire
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is appointed over the Muslims in any way and he is deceitful to them, he is in the Hellfire.”
q: Whoever is appointed over the Muslims in any way and he is deceitful to them, he is in the Hellfire

title: Hadith on Leadership: Rulers not treating subjects as themselves
t: Ma’qil ibn Yasar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No man is appointed over others and then he does not protect them as he would protect himself and his own family except that Allah will cast him into the fire of Hell.”
q: No man is appointed over others and then h … e does not protect them as he would protect himself and his own family except that Allah will cast him into the fire of Hell.

title: Hadith on Authority: Dishonest leaders never smell Paradise
t: Ma’qil ibn Yasar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No servant is given authority by Allah, but he does not fulfill its duties sincerely, except that he will never smell the fragrance of Paradise.”
q: No servant is given authority by Allah, but he does not fulfill its duties sincerely, except that he will never smell the fragrance of Paradise
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sins: Prayer of three people will not be accepted
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are three whose prayer will not rise even a hand span over their heads: an Imam who leads people in prayer who hate him, a wife who spends the night while her husband is displeased, and two brothers who sever their relationship.”
q: There are three whose prayer will not rise even a hand span over their heads: an Imam who leads people in prayer who hate him, a wife who spends the night while her husband is displeased, and two brothers who sever their relationship.

title: Rabiah on Tawbah: You can only repent if Allah turns to you first
t: Al-Qushayri reported: A man said to Al-Rabiah al-‘Adwiyyah, may Allah have mercy on her, “I have committed many sins and acts of disobedience. If I turn to Allah in repentance, will he turn to me?” Al-Rabiah said, “No, rather only if he turned to you first could you turn to him. Know that Allah Almighty said: Verily, Allah loves those who repent and purify themselves.” (2:222)
q: Verily, Allah loves those who repent and purify themselves.

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet seeks refuge from travel
t: Abdullah ibn Sarjis reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say when he traveled, “O Allah, You are the companion on the journey and the caretaker of the family. O Allah, accompany us on our journey and take care of our families. I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, returning in sorrow, loss after gain, the supplication of the oppressed, and the evil glance at our families and property.”
q: O Allah, You are the companion on the journey and the caretaker of the family. O Allah, accompany us on our journey and take care of our families. I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, returning in sorrow, loss after gain, the supplication of the oppressed, and the evil glance at our families and property.

title: Hadith on ‘Ilm: Angels lower wings for seekers of knowledge
t: Safwan ibn ‘Assal reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one leaves their house in search of knowledge but that the angels will lower their wings in approval of what he does.”
q: No one leaves their house in search of knowledge but that the angels will lower their wings in approval of what he does

title: Hadith on Shuhada: None wishes to return to earth, except martyrs
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one who enters Paradise would like to return to the world, even if he could have everything on earth, except for the martyr. He will wish to return to the world and be killed ten more times due to the generous reward he sees.”
q: No one who enters Paradise would like to return to the world, even if he could have everything on earth, except for the martyr. He will wish to return to the world and be killed ten more times due to the generous reward he sees.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ignorance: Learning from young a sign of the Hour
t: Abu Umayyah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among the signs of the Hour is that knowledge will be sought from the youth.”
q: Verily, among the signs of the Hour is that knowledge will be sought from the youth.

title: Hadith on Shuyukh: Blessings are with your elders
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Blessings are with your eldest.”
q: Blessings are with your eldest

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Knowledge: Learn from the Prophet’s companions, elders
t: Sa’id ibn Wahb reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “People will continue to be virtuous as long as they take knowledge from the companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and their elders. If they take their knowledge from the young, that is when they will be ruined.”

title: Hadith on Gheerah: Protective jealousy that Allah loves and hates
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among protective jealousy is what Allah loves and hates. As for what Allah loves, it is jealousy when there is probable cause. As for what Allah hates, it is jealousy without probable cause.”
q: Among protective jealousy is what Allah loves and hates. As for what Allah loves, it is jealousy when there is probable cause. As for what Allah hates, it is jealousy without probable cause.

title: Warraq on Whims: Lowly desires begin downward spiral into evil
t: Ibn al-Jawzi reported: Abu Bakr al-Warraq, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The source of overpowering whims is approaching what is lusted. When whims overpower the heart, it will commit wrong. When the heart commits wrong, the chest will be tightened. When the chest is tightened, character will be bad. When character is bad, the creation will hate him. When the creation hates him, he will hate them. When he hates them, he will be harsh with them. When he is harsh with them, he becomes an accursed devil.”

title: Hadith on Ramadan: A portion of food due for Zakat al-Fitr
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: We would bring for Zakat al-Fitr a portion of food, or a portion of barley, or a portion of dates, or a portion of cheese, or a portion of raisins.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Zakat al-Fitr as purification for misbehavior
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, obligated Zakat al-Fitr as purification of the fasting person from vain talk and misbehavior, as food for the poor. Whoever pays it before the Eid prayer, it is accepted as Zakat. Whoever pays it after the Eid prayer, it is part of voluntary charity.

title: Hadith on Salat: Imam may not be elevated above his followers
t: Abu Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited the Imam from leading the prayer at any height above the people behind him.

title: Ibrahim on Whims: People of whims never brought any good
t: Abu Hamzah reported: Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “By Allah, I have not seen in what they produce as much good as the weight of a seed,” meaning the people of whims, opinions, and speculation.

title: Abu ‘Aliyah on Whims: Beware lowly desires inciting to hatred, enmity
t: ‘Asim al-Ahwal reported: Abu al-‘Aliyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Learn the Quran and once you learn it, never place your desires elsewhere. Beware of these whims of yours, for they incite hostility and hatred between you.”

title: Hadith on Women: Best of your women, worst of your women
t: Abu Udhaynah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of your women are loving, fertile, suitable, and comforting, if they fear Allah. The worst of your women unveil their beauty, take pride in their appearance, and they are hypocrites. None of them will enter Paradise except as rarely as you see a red-beaked crow.”
q: The best of your women are loving, fertile, suitable, and comforting, if they fear Allah. The worst of your women unveil their beauty, take pride in their appearance, and they are hypocrites. None of them will enter Paradise except as rarely as you see a red-beaked crow.

title: ‘Ata on Whims: Rationality defeated by lusts, whims, lowly desires
t: Miskin Abi Fatimah reported: ‘Ata al-Salimi, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “We have heard that lusts and whims can even overpower knowledge, reason, and eloquence.”

title: Ma’la on Ramadan: Companions supplicate for Ramadan all year round
t: Ibn Rajab reported: Ma’la ibn al-Fadl, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The companions would supplicate to Allah for six months prior that they would reach Ramadan. Then, they would supplicate to him for six months afterward to accept their deeds.”

title: Yahya on Ramadan: Keep me safe in Ramadan, accept my deeds
t: Al-Awza’i reported: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, would supplicate when the month of Ramdan arrived, “O Allah, secure me for Ramadan, secure Ramadan for me, and receive my deeds with acceptance.”

title: Hadith on Hijab: Women veiling even from blind men
t: Umm Salamah reported: While we were with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, Ibn Maktum was given permission to enter and that was after the command to veil, so the Prophet said, “Veil yourselves from him.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, is he not blind? He cannot see or recognize us.” The Prophet said, “Are you blind such that you cannot see him?”
q: Veil yourselves from him … Are you blind such that you cannot see him

title: Hadith on Umar: The Prophet’s dream about Umar ibn al-Khattab
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “While I was sleeping, I saw people displayed before me. They were wearing shirts, some of which covered their chests and some of which covered below that. Umar ibn al-Khattab passed by me and he was wearing a shirt dragging behind him.” They said, “What is its interpretation, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “The religion.”
q: While I was sleeping, I saw people displayed before me. They were wearing shirts, some of which covered their chests and some of which covered below that. Umar ibn al-Khattab passed by me and he was wearing a shirt dragging behind him. … The religion
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ali on Zuhd: Renouncing worldliness makes calamities easier to endure
t:
Qabisah ibn Jabir reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever renounces the worldly life, afflictions will be made easy for him. Whoever expects to die, he will hasten to good deeds.”

In another narration, Ali said, “Whoever yearns for Paradise, he will forget his lusts. Whoever is afraid of the Hellfire, he will turn away from unlawful deeds.”

title: Ibn Sirin on Whims: Do not listen to people of lowly desires
t: Hisham reported: Muhammad ibn Sirin, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Do not sit with the people of whims, do not debate them, and do not listen to them.”

title: Abu Qilabah on Whims: Beware of sitting with people of lowly desires
t:
Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani reported: Abu Qilabah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Be on guard from three traits: beware of the gates of rulers, beware of sitting with the people of whims, and keep working for yourself, as independence is part of wellness.”

In another narration, Abu Qilabah said, “Do not sit with the people of whims and do not debate them. Indeed, there is no safety from them immersing you in their misguidance or confusing you with that they know.”

title: Hadith on Ahruf: Seven readings of Quran to ease teaching, learning
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was met by Gabriel and he said, “O Gabriel, I have been sent to an unlettered nation, among them are the disabled, the elderly, young boys and girls, and men who have never read a book.” Gabriel said, “O Muhammad, the Quran has been revealed in seven readings.”
q: O Gabriel, I have been sent to an unlettered nation, among them are the disabled, the elderly, young boys and girls, and men who have never read a book.

title: Hadith on Ahruf: Quran revealed in seven canonical readings
t:
Abdullah ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Gabriel, upon him be peace, taught me to recite the Quran in one reading and I requested another. I continued to ask for more until he stopped at seven readings.”

Ibn Shihab said, “It reached me that these seven readings are united in the matter. There is no difference in what they allow and forbid.”
q: Gabriel, upon him be peace, taught me to recite the Quran in one reading and I requested another. I continued to ask for more until he stopped at seven readings.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hajj: The Prophet calmly stones the Jamarat at Hajj
t: Qudamah ibn Abdullah reported: I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, stoning the Jamarat at Hajj while he was on his camel. There was no hitting, nor crowding, nor anyone shouting for people to move.

title: Ahmad on Sahaba: Speaking badly of the Companions is against Islam
t: Abdul Malik ibn Maymun reported: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, said to me, “If you see a man speaking badly about any of the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, be wary of his practice of Islam.”

title: Abu Huraira on Akhlaq: Speech part of deeds, character part of religion
t: Al-Dahhak reported: Abu Huraira, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever does not view his speech as part of his deeds and his character as part of his religion, he will be ruined without realizing it.”

title: Hadith on Whims: The Prophet disavows people of whims, heresies
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Aisha, “O Aisha! Verily, those who divided their religion and became sects (6:159), they are the people of innovations and whims. They will not repent. I disavow them and they disavow me.”
q: O Aisha! Verily, those who divided their religion and became sects … , they are the people of innovations and whims. They will not repent. I disavow them and they disavow me.

title: Hasan on Salvation: Four traits to protect from Hellfire, Satan
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whoever has four traits, Allah will forbid him from entering Hellfire and grant him refuge from Satan: one who controls himself at a time of hope and a time of fear, at a time of passion and a time of anger.”

title: Wahb on Kufr: Four pillars of unbelief are anger, lust, greed, fear
t: Aban reported: Wahb, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I read in the wisdom that unbelief has four pillars: a pillar of anger, a pillar of lust, a pillar of greed, and a pillar of fear.”

title: Hatim on Shahwah: Three types of lust in eating, speaking, staring
t: Al-Bayhaqi reported: Hatim al-Asamm, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Lusts are three types: lust in eating, lust in speaking, and lust in gazing. Guard your eating with confidence, your tongue with truthfulness, and your gaze with tears.”

title: Mujahid on Whims: Guidance to Islam, protection from lowly desires
t: Al-A’mash reported: Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I do not know which of my two blessings are greater: that I was guided to Islam or that I was protected from whims.”

title: Sarri on Shukr: Thankfulness for a blessing is itself a blessing
t: Al-Junayd reported: Al-Sarri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Gratitude for a blessing is itself a blessing.”

title: Hadith on Jannah: Believers enter Paradise as young, beautiful
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people of Paradise will enter Paradise with smooth and hairless skin, kohl upon their eyes, at thirty or thirty-three years of age.”
q: The people of Paradise will enter Paradise with smooth and hairless skin, kohl upon their eyes, at thirty or thirty-three years of age.

title: Hadith on Retaliation: Sin against instigator, unless he transgresses
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If two people exchange harsh words, it is against the instigator as long as the one wronged does not transgress.”
q: If two people exchange harsh words, it is against the instigator as long as the one wronged does not transgress.

title: Hadith on Akhirah: Paradise surrounded by hardship, Hellfire by desires
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Hellfire is veiled by lusts, and Paradise is veiled by hardships.”
q: Hellfire is veiled by lusts, and Paradise is veiled by hardships.

title: Hadith on Riya: The Prophet fears hidden lusts, showing off in worship
t: Abdullah ibn Zayd reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, what I fear most for you after me is ostentation and hidden lusts,” meaning adultery.
q: Verily, what I fear most for you after me is ostentation and hidden lusts,

title: Abu Qilabah on Whims: People of desires agree upon violence
t: Ayyub reported: Abu Qilabah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The example of the people of whims is that of the hypocrites. Allah Almighty mentioned the hypocrites with different words and deeds, the summary of which is misguidance. The people of whims disagree over their whims, but they agree upon the sword.”

title: Hasan on Whims: Lowly desires worst spiritual disease of hearts
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whims are the worst disease to interfere with a heart.”

title: Waki’ on Ramadan: Zakat al-Fitr like prostration of forgetfulness
t: Al-Nawawi reported: Waki’ ibn al-Jarrah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Zakat al-Fitr is to the month of Ramadan like the prostration of forgetfulness is to prayer. It makes up for deficiencies in fasting just as the prostration makes up for deficiencies in prayer.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Friends: Choose companions who remind you of Allah
t: Abu al-Ahwas reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Remember Allah Almighty often. You must not accompany anyone unless they help you remember Allah Almighty.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Ask Allah for pardon and wellness
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Ask your Lord for forgiveness and wellness in the world and the Hereafter. If you are given forgiveness and wellness in the world and the Hereafter, you have succeeded.”
q: Ask your Lord for forgiveness and wellness in the world and the Hereafter. If you are given forgiveness and wellness in the world and the Hereafter, you have succeeded.

title: Awza’i on Caprice: Satan spreads lowly desires among children of Adam
t: Ibn al-Mubarak reported: Al-Awza’i, may Allah have mercy on him said, “Iblis said to his allies: With what have you come to the son of Adam? They said: With everything. Iblis said: Have you come to them before they seek forgiveness? They said: It is impossible, for it is connected to monotheism! Iblis said: I will spread something among them for which they will not seek forgiveness from Allah. Thus, Iblis spread whims among them.”

title: Kalbi on Whims: Arabs worshiped idols representing lowly desires
t: Al-Qurtubi reported: Al-Kalbi, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It was the habit of the Arabs that if a man among them desired anything, he would worship it besides Allah. If he saw something better, he would leave what he first worshipped and worship what is better. This is the meaning of the verse: Have you seen one who takes his desires as his god?” (25:43)
q: Have you seen one who takes his desires as his god?

title: Sha’bi on Whims: Lowly desires whisk their companions to Hellfire
t: Ibn Shubrumah reported: Al-Sha’bi, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, whims are only named as such because they whisk their companions away to the Hellfire.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Whims: The Quran casts blame upon lowly desires
