t: Ibn al-Jawzi reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Allah Almighty did not mention whims in any place in his book but that he cast blame on it.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Sins: Prevalence of sins, prevalence of divine afflictions
t: Yahya ibn Sa’id reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Adultery does not become prevalent among people but that there will be much death among them. People do not defraud in weights and measures but that their provision will be cut off. People do not judge by other than the truth but that bloodshed will be prevalent among them. People do not betray their covenants but that Allah will give their enemies power over them.”

title: Hadith on Consequences: Five collevtive punishments for deadly sins
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Five sins come with five afflictions: People do not violate their covenant except that their enemies are given power over them. They do not judge with anything other than Allah’s revelation except that poverty will be spread among them. Obscenity does not prevail among them except that death will be spread among them. They do not cheat in measurements except that crops are prevented from growing, so they suffer years of drought. They do not withhold the obligatory charity except that the sky will hold back its rain.”
q: Five sins come with five afflictions: People do not violate their covenant except that their enemies are given power over them. They do not judge with anything other than Allah’s revelation except that poverty will be spread among them. Obscenity does not prevail among them except that death will be spread among them. They do not cheat in measurements except that crops are prevented from growing, so they suffer years of drought. They do not withhold the obligatory charity except that the sky will hold back its rain.

title: Umar on Meat: Beware of being addicted to eating meat
t: Yahya ibn Sa’id reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Beware of eating too much meat, for it can be as addictive as wine.”
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-San’ani

title: Hadith on Kids: The Prophet plays with Zaynab bint Umm Salamah
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would play with Zaynab, the daughter of Umm Salamah. The Prophet would keep saying, “O Zaynab! O Zaynab!”

title: Hadith on Vices: Greed, caprice, and vanity are destructive vices
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Three deeds are destructive vices: greed that is obeyed, whims that are followed, and everyone impressed by their own opinion.”
q: Three deeds are destructive vices: greed that is obeyed, whims that are followed, and everyone impressed by their own opinion.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Your shield from Hellfire is remembrance of Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Take up your shields.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, is the enemy present?” The Prophet said, “No, rather your shields from the Hellfire are to declare the glory of Allah, the praise of Allah, there is no God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest. Verily, they will come on the Day of Resurrection as saviors and guardian angels, and they are ‘righteous deeds everlasting.’” (18:46)
q: Take up your shields … No, rather your shields from the Hellfire are to declare the glory of Allah, the praise of Allah, there is no God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest. Verily, they will come on the Day of Resurrection as saviors and guardian angels, and they are ‘righteous deeds everlasting.’

title: Hadith on Virtues: Three salvific virtues, three destructive vices
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Three deeds are salvific virtues and three are destructive vices. As for salvific virtues, they are fear of Allah in public and private, a word of truth in pleasure or displeasure, and moderation in wealth or poverty. As for destructive vices, they are whims that are followed, greed that is obeyed, and a man being impressed with himself, which is the worst of them.”
q: Three deeds are salvific virtues and three are destructive vices. As for salvific virtues, they are fear of Allah in public and private, a word of truth in pleasure or displeasure, and moderation in wealth or poverty. As for destructive vices, they are whims that are followed, greed that is obeyed, and a man being impressed with himself, which is the worst of them
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Salat: Complete rows as angels stand before their Lord
t: Jabir ibn Samurah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us and he said, “Be calm in prayer.” Then, the Prophet came out to us another time and he said, “Will you not form your prayer rows as the angels do before their Lord?” We said, “O Messenger of Allah, how do the angels form rows before their Lord?” The Prophet said, “They complete the first rows and fill in the gaps between rows.”
q: Be calm in prayer … Will you not form your prayer rows as the angels do before their Lord? … They complete the first rows and fill in the gaps between rows.

title: Hadith on Deeds: Three expiations, salvific virtues, and destructive vices
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Three deeds are destructive vices, three are salvific virtues, three are expiations, and three are a rise in ranks. As for destructive vices, they are greed that is obeyed, whims that are followed, and man being impressed with himself. As for salvific virtues, they are justice in a time of anger or pleasure, moderation in wealth or poverty, and fear of Allah in public and private. As for expiations, they are waiting for prayer in between prayers, thorough ablution on cold mornings, and walking to the congregations. As for rises in ranks, they are feeding the poor, spreading peace, and prayer at night while people sleep.”
q: Three deeds are destructive vices, three are salvific virtues, three are expiations, and three are a rise in ranks. As for destructive vices, they are greed that is obeyed, whims that are followed, and man being impressed with himself. As for salvific virtues, they are justice in a time of anger or pleasure, moderation in wealth or poverty, and fear of Allah in public and private. As for expiations, they are waiting for prayer in between prayers, thorough ablution on cold mornings, and walking to the congregations. As for rises in ranks, they are feeding the poor, spreading peace, and prayer at night while people sleep.

title: Ibn Abbas on Rizq: Allah decreases his provision if he takes Haram
t: Sa’id ibn Jubayr reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “There is no believer or sinner but that Allah Almighty has decreed his provision from the lawful. If he is patient until it comes to him, Allah will give it to him. If he becomes anxious and consumes something from the unlawful, Allah will decrease his provision from the lawful.”

title: Malik on Hearts: Worst punishment from Allah is having a hard heart
t: Al-Qurtubi reported: Malik ibn Dinar, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A servant is not struck by a greater punishment than having a hard heart. Allah is not angry with people but that he removes mercy from their hearts.”

title: Malik on Salvation: The Sunnah is like the Ark of Noah
t: Ibn ‘Asakir reported: Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The Sunnah is like the Ark of Noah. Whoever boards it will be saved, and whoever does not board it will drown.”

title: Hadith on Dunya: Allah protects beloved servants from worldly life
t: Qatadah ibn al-Nu’man reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Allah loves a servant, He protects them from the worldly life, just as one of you protects the sick from drinking too much water.”
q: When Allah loves a servant, He protects them from the worldly life, just as one of you protects the sick from drinking too much water

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet’s supplication for a newly-wed couple
t: Abu Huraira reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, congratulated a couple for getting married, he would say, “May Allah grant you blessings, send blessings upon you, and bring you together in goodness.”
q: May Allah grant you blessings, send blessings upon you, and bring you together in goodness

title: Hadith on Sins: Oppression, injustice punished in this world
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Every consequence of sin is delayed by Allah until the Day of Resurrection, as He wills, except for injustice, disrespect to parents, or severing family ties. He will hasten the punishment of one who commits them in this world before he dies.”
q: Every consequence of sin is delayed by Allah until the Day of Resurrection, as He wills, except for injustice, disrespect to parents, or severing family ties. He will hasten the punishment of one who commits them in this world before he dies.

title: Hadith on Parents: Return to your parents, make them laugh
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “I have come to pledge allegiance to you upon emigration, and I left my parents weeping.” The Prophet said, “Return to them and make them laugh, just as you made them cry.”
q: Return to them and make them laugh, just as you made them cry

title: Hadith on Tilawah: The Prophet recited Quran clearly, word by word
t: Ya’la ibn Mamlak reported: He asked Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, about his recitation and his prayer. Umm Salamah said, “Not as you can pray. The Prophet would pray, then sleep for the amount he prayed. Then he would pray the amount he slept, then he would sleep the amount he prayed until morning.” She further described his recitation, saying, “It was a distinct recitation, word for word.”

title: Hadith on Salat: No voluntary prayer after ‘Asr and Fajr, with exceptions
t:
Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, only prayed two cycles after the afternoon prayer because some property came to him, which occupied him from performing two cycles after the noon prayer. The Prophet prayed them after the afternoon prayer and he did not repeat it.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “Most of the people of knowledge agreed upon the disapproval of praying after the afternoon prayer until the sun sets and after the dawn prayer until the sun rises. They made exceptions to that, such as praying in Mecca after the afternoon prayer until the sun rises, after the dawn prayer until the sin rises, and after performing Tawaf; it was said by Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq.”

title: Hadith on Travel: Praying two cycles upon return from a journey
t: Ka’b reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, returned home in the forenoon after a journey, he would enter the mosque and pray two cycles before sitting down.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Sufyan on Fiqh: Hadith cause misguidance, except for scholars of Fiqh
t: Al-Qayrawani reported: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The prophetic Hadith cause misguidance, except for the scholars of Fiqh.”

title: Hadith on Sahaba: Companions had fun, yet showed courage
t: Bakr ibn Abdullah reported: The companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would throw melons at each other for fun, but when it came to the truth, they would be real men.

title: Hadith on Salat: You are in prayer if you are waiting for prayer
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: We prayed with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, at nightfall and he did not come out until half of the night had passed. The Prophet said, “Take your places.” We took our places and the Prophet said, “Verily, people have prayed and laid down in their beds, but you continue to be in prayer as long as you wait for prayer. Were it not for the weakness of the weak and the sickness of the sick, I would delay this prayer until half of the night had passed.”
q: Take your places … Verily, people have prayed and laid down in their beds, but you continue to be in prayer as long as you wait for prayer. Were it not for the weakness of the weak and the sickness of the sick, I would delay this prayer until half of the night had passed

title: Hadith on Oaths: Do not swear many oaths for your business
t: Abu Qatadah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of swearing many oaths while trading. Verily, it helps trade but erases the blessing.”
q: Beware of swearing many oaths while trading. Verily, it helps trade but erases the blessing.

title: Hadith on Salat: Imam should lighten prayer for sick, elderly with him
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you leads people in prayer, let him lighten it as among them are the weak, sick, and elderly. If one of you prays by himself, let him pray for as long as he wishes.”
q: If one of you leads people in prayer, let him lighten it as among them are the weak, sick, and elderly. If one of you prays by himself, let him pray for as long as he wishes.

title: Hadith on Trade: Honest merchants with prophets, truthful, martyrs
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The honest and trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful, and the martyrs.”
q: The honest and trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful, and the martyrs.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Salat: Voluntary prayer better in private
t: Suhayb ibn Sinan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Prayer in congregation is like performing twenty-five prayers alone. Voluntary prayer where no one can see him is like performing twenty-five prayers under the eyes of people.”
q: Prayer in congregation is like performing twenty-five prayers alone. Voluntary prayer where no one can see him is like performing twenty-five prayers under the eyes of people.
s: al-Targhīb fī Faḍā’il al-A’māl li-Ibn Shāhīn 67

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Signs: Disappearance of righteous a sign of the Hour
t:
Abdur Rahman ibn Yazid reported: Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The righteous will disappear and the people of doubts will remain.” They said, “O Abu Abdur Rahman, who are the people of doubts?” Ibn Mas’ud said, “People who do not enjoin good and do not forbid evil.”

In another narration, Ibn Mas’ud said, “They do not acknowledge good, nor reject evil.”
gf: Rijal al-Sahih (narrators are reliable) according to Al-Haythami

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Is there any hope for our repentance?
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Some people among the idolaters had committed many acts of murder and adultery. They came to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and they said, “What you call to is good, but tell us what we can do as an expiation?” Then, the verse was revealed, “Those who do not call upon another god besides Allah, who do not kill a soul Allah has sanctified except for a just cause, and who do not commit adultery; whoever does so will meet a penalty. Punishment will be multiplied for him on the Day of Resurrection and he will be humiliated therein, except for those who repent, have faith, and do good deeds. For those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds.” (25:68-70). And the verse was revealed, “Say to My servants who have transgressed against themselves: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah.” (39:53)
q: Those who do not call upon another god besides Allah, who do not kill a soul Allah has sanctified except for a just cause, and who do not commit adultery; whoever does so will meet a penalty. Punishment will be multiplied for him on the Day of Resurrection and he will be humiliated therein, except for those who repent, have faith, and do good deeds. For those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds … Say to My servants who have transgressed against themselves: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah.

title: Hadith on Salat: Imam should turn around after finishing prayer
t: Yazid ibn al-Aswad reported: I prayed behind the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and when he finished, he would turn around to face us.

title: Hadith on Children: Why do you not treat sons and daughters equally?
t: Anas reported: A man was with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when his son came. He kissed him and sat him down on his thigh. Then, his daughter came and she sat to his side. The Prophet said, “Why do you not treat them equally?”
q: Why do you not treat them equally?

title: Hadith on Talbiyah: Responding to the call of Hajj pilgrimage
t:
Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would answer the call of the pilgrimage, saying, “I am here at Your service, O Allah, at Your service! I am here at Your service, You have no partner! I am here at Your service! Verily, all praise and blessings are Yours, sovereignty belongs to You, and You have no partner!”

Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, would add to it, “I am here at Your service, at Your service, ready to obey You! All good is in Your hands! I am here at Your service! All hope and good deeds are for you!”
q: I am here at Your service, O Allah, at Your service! I am here at Your service, You have no partner! I am here at Your service! Verily, all praise and blessings are Yours, sovereignty belongs to You, and You have no partner!
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ali on Insults: No better punishment for fools than to be silent
t: Al-Qurtubi reported: A man insulted Qanbar, who was under the patronage of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him. Ali called out to him, “O Qanbar! Leave one who insults you and ignore him. It will please the Merciful, displease Satan, and punish your insulter. No punishment for the fool is like refusing to answer him.”

title: Hadith on Istighfar: Praying for repentance after committing a sin
t: Abu Bakr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No man commits a sin, then purifies himself in ablution, then prays, and then asks Allah for forgiveness, but that Allah will forgive him.” Then, the Prophet recited this verse, “Those who, if they behave immorally or wrong themselves, they remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins. Who forgives sins besides Allah? And they do not insist on what they have done, while they know better.” (3:135)
q: No man commits a sin, then purifies himself in ablution, then prays, and then asks Allah for forgiveness, but that Allah will forgive him … Those who, if they behave immorally or wrong themselves, they remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins. Who forgives sins besides Allah? And they do not insist on what they have done, while they know better

title: Hadith on Dua: Praise to Allah, abundant, good, blessed therein
t: Anas reported: A man came and entered the row of prayer, breathing heavily. The man said, “All praise is due to Allah, abundant praise, goodness, and blessings therein.” When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, finished the prayer, he said, “Which one of you spoke these words?” The people were silent, and the Prophet said, “Which one of you spoke them? He said nothing wrong.” The man said, “I came and I was having trouble breathing, so I said them.” The Prophet said, “I saw twelve angels competing for which of them would take it up.”
q: Which one of you spoke these words? … Which one of you spoke them? He said nothing wrong … I saw twelve angels competing for which of them would take it up.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Believers will see the Face of Allah in Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do you overlook a crowd to see the full moon? Do you overlook a crowd to see the sun?” They said no. The Prophet said, “Verily, you will see your Lord just as you see the full moon and you will not need to overlook a crowd to see him.”
q: Do you overlook a crowd to see the full moon? Do you overlook a crowd to see the sun? … Verily, you will see your Lord just as you see the full moon and you will not need to overlook a crowd to see him

title: Umar on Zina: No right to punish the unborn child of adultery
t: Abu Sufyan reported: A man was absent from his wife for two years and he returned to find her pregnant. Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, came and he considered stoning her. Mu’adh said to him, “Even if you have a legal case against her, you have no case against what is in her belly.” Umar left her and she gave birth to a boy who clearly resembled his father. His front teeth came out and the man said, “This is my son.” Umar said, “If only women could give birth to the likes of Mu’adh! Were it not for Mu’adh, Umar would be ruined.”

title: Hadith on Justice: Day of just leadership better than years of worship
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A day of just leadership is better than sixty years of worship, and a legal limit properly established in the land is more pure for it than forty days of rain.”
q: A day of just leadership is better than sixty years of worship, and a legal limit properly established in the land is more pure for it than forty days of rain.

title: Hadith on Humility: Everything raised up in world will be humbled
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had a camel named Al-‘Adba and she could not be outraced. A bedouin came riding his camel and outraced her. That was difficult for the Muslims and they said, “Al-‘Adba has been beaten!” The Prophet said, “Verily, it is a duty upon Allah that nothing is raised up in this world but that it will eventually be humbled.”
q: Verily, it is a duty upon Allah that nothing is raised up in this world but that it will eventually be humbled

title: Ali on Dua: Distance between heaven and earth an answered prayer
t: Maslamah ibn Muharib reported: It was said to Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, “What is the distance between heaven and earth?” Ali said, “An answered prayer.”

title: Hadith on Shuhada: Souls of martyrs alive in green birds of Paradise
t: Ka’b ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the souls of martyrs are in green birds, hanging from the fruits of Paradise, or the trees of Paradise.”
q: Verily, the souls of martyrs are in green birds, hanging from the fruits of Paradise, or the trees of Paradise

title: Sa’id on Ramadan: Reward for attending prayer on Laylat al-Qadr
t: Malik reported: Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever attends evening prayer on the Night of Decree has taken his share of reward from it.”

title: Hadith on Hereafter: The Prophet first to intercede on Judgment Day
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I am the master of the children of Adam, and it is no boast. I will be the first to intercede and whose intercession will be accepted, and it is no boast.”
q: I am the master of the children of Adam, and it is no boast. I will be the first to intercede and whose intercession will be accepted, and it is no boast.

title: Hadith on Fiqh: People like mines of silver and gold
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “People are like minerals of silver and gold. The best of them in the time of ignorance are the best of them in Islam, if they have religious understanding.”
q: People are like minerals of silver and gold. The best of them in the time of ignorance are the best of them in Islam, if they have religious understanding.

title: Yazid on Listening: Speaker awaits trial, listener awaits mercy
t: Ibn Abdul Barr reported: Yazid ibn Abi Habib, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, the speaker only awaits a trial, and the listener only awaits mercy.”

title: Hadith on Mosques: The Masjid was only built to remember Allah
t: Buraydah reported: A man announced loudly in the mosque, saying, “Has anyone seen my red camel?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “May you not find it! Verily, the mosques were only built for the purpose they were built.”
q: May you not find it! Verily, the mosques were only built for the purpose they were built.

title: Ibn Abi Ghassan on Learning: You have knowledge if you remain a student
t: Ibn Abdul Barr reported: Ibn Abi Ghassan, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “You will have knowledge as long as you are a student. If you consider yourself sufficient, you will become ignorant.”

title: Ka’b on Pilgrims: Soldiers and pilgrims are guest of Allah
t: Abdullah ibn Damrah reported: Ka’b, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The pilgrims of Hajj and Umrah and soldiers in the way of Allah are the guests of Allah. If they ask, give them. If they call you, answer them.”

title: Abu Darda on Curses: Do not curse anyone, not befitting believers
t: Hakim ibn Jabir reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, was lying down between his companions and he had a cloth over his face. A priest passed by him and they were amazed at how fat he was. They said, “O Allah, curse him! How big is he! How fat is he!” Abu Darda lifted the cloth from his face and he said, “Who have you cursed so disdainfully?” They said, “A priest passed by us.” Abu Darda said, “Do not curse anyone. It is not befitting for one in the habit of cursing to be among the truthful to Allah on the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Hasan on ‘Aql: Loving kindness is half of sound reason
t: Ibn Abi Dunya reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Loving kindness towards people is half of reason.”

title: Fudayl on Company: Spend time with those having good character
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you mix with people, mix with those who have good character; it only invites to good. Do not mix with those who have bad character, for it only invites to evil.”

title: Abu Huraira on Fasting: Easy spoils by fasting short winter days
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Abu Huraira, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Shall I tell you about easy spoils?” They said, “O Abu Huraira, what are they?” Abu Huraira said, “Fasting in the winter.”

title: Ali on Rulers: Beware of the gates of the ruler
t: Al-Bayhaqi reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Beware of the gates of the ruler.”

title: Abu Darda on Doubts: Leave what is doubtful for certainty
t: Al-Tabari reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Goodness is in peace of mind and evil is in doubt. Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.”

title: Sa’id on Knowledge: Muslim has knowledge only if he keeps learning
t: Al-Nawawi reported: Sa’id ibn Jubayr, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A man will continue to have knowledge as long as he is learning. If he forsakes knowledge and assumes that he is sufficient and already has enough, he will become ignorant.”

title: Malik on Adab: Duty of students to have good manners
t: Ibn ‘Abdul Barr reported: Imam Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Surely, it is the duty of a student of knowledge to behave with dignity, calm, and reverence, and to follow the narrations of those who came before him.”

title: Ikramah on Yusuf: Allah raised up Joseph by his forgiveness
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: ‘Ikramah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Allah Almighty said to Joseph: O Joseph, by your forgiveness of your brothers I have raised your status among those who are mentioned.”

title: Hadith on Flags: The Prophet’s flag black, standard white
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The flag of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was black and his standard was white.

title: Hadith on Salat: Supplication for starting the prayer
t: Aisha reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, began his prayer, he would say, “Glory to You, O Allah, with Your praises. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.”
q: Glory to You, O Allah, with Your praises. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You

title: Hadith on Manners: Allah likes sneezing, dislikes yawning
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah likes sneezing and dislikes yawning. When one of you sneezes and praises Allah, it is a duty on every Muslim to say to him: May Allah have mercy on you. As for yawning, it is from Satan. When one of you yawns, let him hold it back as much as he can. When one of you yawns, Satan laughs at him.”
q: Verily, Allah likes sneezing and dislikes yawning. When one of you sneezes and praises Allah, it is a duty on every Muslim to say to him: May Allah have mercy on you. As for yawning, it is from Satan. When one of you yawns, let him hold it back as much as he can. When one of you yawns, Satan laughs at him

title: Yunus on Love: I encourage my soul to love others as myself
t: Ja’far ibn Burqan reported: I heard that Yunus ibn Ubaid, may Allah have mercy on him, was virtuous and righteous, so I wrote to him saying, “O brother, write to me about what you do.” Yunus wrote back, “I received your letter asking me to write to you about what I do, and I will tell you. Verily, I encouraged my soul to love for people what it loves for itself, and to hate for them what it hates for itself, yet it is far from that. Then I encouraged it another time to not mention people except with what is good, but I found that fasting on an intensely hot day at its peak in Basra is easier for it than to abandon this matter. O brother, peace be with you.”

title: Hadith on Bribery: Accepting a bribe is a great door of usury
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever intercedes for his brother and he is given a gift for it and he accepts it, he has come to a great door among the doors of usury.”
q: Whoever intercedes for his brother and he is given a gift for it and he accepts it, he has come to a great door among the doors of usury.

title: Hadith on Bribery: Allah curses one who gives, accepts bribes
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him said, “Allah has cursed the one who offers a bribe and the one who accepts a bribe to receive a favorable judgment.”
q: Allah has cursed the one who offers a bribe and the one who accepts a bribe to receive a favorable judgment.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Theft: A man steals a cloak from the Prophet
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man named Kirkirah was entrusted to look after the possessions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The man died and the Prophet said, “He is in the Hellfire.” They went to look at him and they found that he had stolen a cloak.
q: He is in the Hellfire

title: Hadith on Kufran: Beware ingratitude to husbands, wives, spouses
t: Asma’ reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by a group of women in the mosque one day. The Prophet waved with his hand to greet them with peace and he said, “Beware of ingratitude to those who bless you. Beware of ingratitude to those who bless you.” One of the women said, “O Messenger of Allah, I seek refuge in Allah, O Prophet of Allah, from being ungrateful to Allah.” The Prophet said, “Rather, one of you will be widowed for a long time throughout her middle years, then Allah provides her with a husband and he benefits her with a child, the joy of her life. Then, she gets very angry and she swears by Allah, saying: I never had one good moment with you! That is ingratitude to the blessings of Allah. That is ingratitude to those who bless her.”
q: Beware of ingratitude to those who bless you. Beware of ingratitude to those who bless you … Rather, one of you will be widowed for a long time throughout her middle years, then Allah provides her with a husband and he benefits her with a child, the joy of her life. Then, she gets very angry and she swears by Allah, saying: I never had one good moment with you! That is ingratitude to the blessings of Allah. That is ingratitude to those who bless her

title: Hadith on Debts: Delayed payment by a rich person is injustice
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Delayed payment by a rich person is an act of injustice.”
q: Delayed payment by a rich person is an act of injustice.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Shafi’i on Silence: Seek help in your words with silence, reflection
t: Al-Rabia’ ibn Sulayman reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Seek help in speaking with silence, and in reasoning with reflection.”

title: Hadith on Quran: Necessity of reciting in a pleasant voice
t: Abu Lubabah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He is not one of us who does not try to recite the Quran in a pleasant voice.”
q: He is not one of us who does not try to recite the Quran in a pleasant voice.

title: Hadith on Tilawah: Reciting the Quran aloud in a pleasant voice
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah does not listen to anything as he does to the beautiful voice of a prophet, reciting the Quran aloud pleasantly.”
q: Allah does not listen to anything as he does to the beautiful voice of a prophet, reciting the Quran aloud pleasantly
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Prayer: Delay prayer until after eating, using bathroom
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no praying when a meal is presented, nor when one needs to relieve himself.”
q: There is no praying when a meal is presented, nor when one needs to relieve himself.

title: Hadith on Cleanliness: Right hand for eating, left for cleaning
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used his right hand for eating and used his left hand for cleaning himself and whatever was harmful.

title: Hadith on Wisdom: No wisdom unless one has experience of age
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no forbearance unless one has blundered, and there is no wisdom unless one has experience.”
q: There is no forbearance unless one has blundered, and there is no wisdom unless one has experience.

title: Hadith on Luxury: More furniture than needed is blameworthy
t: Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is a bedding for a man and a bedding for his wife. The third bedding is for his guest, and the fourth is for Satan.”
q: There is a bedding for a man and a bedding for his wife. The third bedding is for his guest, and the fourth is for Satan

title: Hadith on Wealth: Let Allah see the traces of His blessings on you
t: Malik ibn Nadlah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If Allah has given you wealth, let the traces of his blessings and generosity be seen upon you.”
q: If Allah has given you wealth, let the traces of his blessings and generosity be seen upon you

title: Hadith on Humility: What the companions said when praised
t: ‘Adi ibn Artah reported: When a man among the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was praised for his righteousness, he would say, “O Allah, do not blame me for what they say and forgive me for what they do not know!”

title: Hadith on Cleanliness: Concession to urinate while standing if needed
t:
Hudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to a waste area used by people and he urinated over it while standing. I brought him water for ablution and then left him to his privacy. The Prophet called me until I was behind him and he performed ablution, wiping over his leather socks.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “A concession was granted from some of the people of knowledge to urinate while standing.”

title: Hadith on Cleanliness: The Prophet does not urinate standing up
t:
Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would not urinate unless he was sitting.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “The prohibition of urinating while standing means it is a matter of etiquette and not absolute forbiddance.”

title: Sufyan on Men: Who is weaker than a man unable to lower his gaze?
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A woman will pass by a man and he cannot restrain himself from looking at her lustfully although there is no benefit in it. What could be weaker than this?”

title: Abu Hazim on Allah: Set right with people if set right with Allah
t: Al-Dhahabi reported: Abu Hazim, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A servant does not set things right between himself and Allah but that Allah will set things right between him and people. A servant does not damage things between himself and Allah but that Allah will damage things between himself and people.”

title: Hadith on Quran: Parents of children who recite Quran given a crown
t: Mu’adh al-Juhani reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever recites the Quran and acts according to what is in it, his parents will be crowned on the Day of Resurrection with a light brighter than the light of the sun in your worldly houses, were it among you. What do you think of one who acts upon this?”
q: Whoever recites the Quran and acts according to what is in it, his parents will be crowned on the Day of Resurrection with a light brighter than the light of the sun in your worldly houses, were it among you. What do you think of one who acts upon this?

title: Qays on Rifq: Whoever is gentle in the world benefits in Hereafter
t: Waki’ reported: Qays, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It is said that whoever has the quality of gentleness, it will benefit him in the Hereafter.”

title: Mughirah on Prophets: Jesus appears before and after Muhammad
t: ‘Amir reported: A man said in front of Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah, may Allah be pleased with him, “Allah send blessings upon Muhammad, the seal of the prophets. There is no prophet after him.” Al-Mughirah said, “It is enough for you to say he is the seal of the prophets. We have been told that Jesus, upon him be peace, will come out; he came before him and he will come after him.”

title: Salman on Humility: Humble yourself for Allah, Allah raises you up
t: Jarir reported: Salman al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, said “O Jarir, be humble for the sake of Allah. Whoever humbles himself for Allah, Allah will raise him up on the Day of Resurrection. O Jarir, do you know what will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection?” I said, “I do not know.” Salman said, “Acts of injustice between people in the world.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Rizq: Be graceful in seeking Halal provision
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O people, fear Allah and be decent in seeking provision, for a soul will never die until it finishes its apportioned provision. If it is slow in coming, fear Allah and seek provision gracefully. Take what is lawful and leave what is unlawful.”
q: O people, fear Allah and be decent in seeking provision, for a soul will never die until it finishes its apportioned provision. If it is slow in coming, fear Allah and seek provision gracefully. Take what is lawful and leave what is unlawful.

title: Hadith on Rizq: Let him not seek provision by sinful means
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the Holy Spirit inspired in my mind that a soul will never die until it finishes its term and consumes its provision. Thus, be graceful in seeking provision, and let not one of you allow the delay of provision to compel him to seek it by disobedience. Verily, Allah does not grant what is with Him but by obedience to Him.”
q: Verily, the Holy Spirit inspired in my mind that a soul will never die until it finishes its term and consumes its provision. Thus, be graceful in seeking provision, and let not one of you allow the delay of provision to compel him to seek it by disobedience. Verily, Allah does not grant what is with Him but by obedience to Him.

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for entering and exiting home
t: Abu Malik al-Asha’ri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a man enters his house, let him say: O Allah, I asked you for the good of this entrance and exit, in the name of Allah I enter and in the name of Allah I leave, and upon Allah our Lord we rely. Then let him greet his family with peace.”
q: When a man enters his house, let him say: O Allah, I asked you for the good of this entrance and exit, in the name of Allah I enter and in the name of Allah I leave, and upon Allah our Lord we rely. Then let him greet his family with peace.

title: Hadith on Taqwa: Be mindful of Allah as it is sum of all good
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, instruct me.” The Prophet said, “You must fear Allah, for it is the sum of all good. You must wage jihad in the way of Allah, for it is the monasticism of the Muslims. You must remember Allah and recite His Book, for it will be your light upon the earth and your mention in the heavens. You must hold your tongue unless it is good, for by it you will defeat Satan.”
q: You must fear Allah, for it is the sum of all good. You must wage jihad in the way of Allah, for it is the monasticism of the Muslims. You must remember Allah and recite His Book, for it will be your light upon the earth and your mention in the heavens. You must hold your tongue unless it is good, for by it you will defeat Satan
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Fasting: Spouses kissing each other while fasting
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, leaned forward to kiss me. I said, “I am fasting.” The Prophet said, “And I am fasting,” then he kissed me.
q: And I am fasting

title: Hadith on Humility: Allah raises those who humble themselves
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever humbles himself by a degree for Allah, glory be to Him, Allah will raise him by a degree. Whoever is arrogant to Allah by a degree, Allah will lower him by a degree until he is made ‘the lowest of the low.’” (95:5)
q: Whoever humbles himself by a degree for Allah, glory be to Him, Allah will raise him by a degree. Whoever is arrogant to Allah by a degree, Allah will lower him by a degree until he is made ‘the lowest of the low.’

title: Hadith on Guests: Host him even if he did not host you
t: Malik ibn Nadlah reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, I stayed with a man and he did not host me or show me hospitality. Now he is staying with me. Shall I recompense him with the same?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No, host him.”
q: No, host him

title: Hadith on Marriage: Spouses helping each other pray at night
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “May Allah have mercy on a man who stands at night to pray and wakes his wife to pray. If she refuses, he sprinkles water on her face. May Allah have mercy on a wife who stands at night to pray and wakes her husband to pray. If he refuses, she sprinkles water on his face.”
q: May Allah have mercy on a man who stands at night to pray and wakes his wife to pray. If she refuses, he sprinkles water on her face. May Allah have mercy on a wife who stands at night to pray and wakes her husband to pray. If he refuses, she sprinkles water on his face

title: Hadith on Charity: Parable of the spender and miser of charity
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the miser and the spender is that of two men clad in armor from their chests to their collars. As for the spender, he does not spend but that it extends or broadens over his skin until it covers the tips of his hands and feet. As for the miser, he does not want to spend anything but that every ring contracts in its place; he tries to loosen it, but it will not.”
q: The parable of the miser and the spender is that of two men clad in armor from their chests to their collars. As for the spender, he does not spend but that it extends or broadens over his skin until it covers the tips of his hands and feet. As for the miser, he does not want to spend anything but that every ring contracts in its place; he tries to loosen it, but it will not.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Hereafter: One is either relieved or relieved from
t: Abu Wa’il reported: Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever acts to show off, Allah will show him off. Whoever acts to be heard, Allah will make him heard. Whoever lengthens himself to aggrandize himself, Allah will debase him. Whoever humbles himself reverently, Allah will raise him. Whoever was extravagant in the world, he will be deprived in the Hereafter. Whoever was deprived in the world, he will be extravagant in the Hereafter. One is either relieved or relieved from.” They said, “Who is relieved?” Ibn Mas’ud said, “The believer is relieved when he dies. As for one relieved from, it is one who wrongs people and cheats them in the world. When he dies, he is relieved from.”
gf: Jayyid (very good) according to Ibn al-Mulaqqin

title: Hadith on Hypocrisy: Allah will expose hypocrites on Judgment Day
t: Jundub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever acts to be heard, Allah will make him heard. Whoever acts to show off, Allah will show him off.
q: Whoever acts to be heard, Allah will make him heard. Whoever acts to show off, Allah will show him off
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Umar on Sermons: Do not burden people with long prayers, lectures
t: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Adi reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O people, do not make Allah hateful to his servants.” They said, “How is that? Allah correct you!” Umar said, “One of you is an Imam and he prolongs the prayer for people until what is in it becomes hateful to them. And one of you sits to lecture and he prolongs it for people until what is in it becomes hateful to them.”

title: Umar on Humility: Allah raises his wisdom if he humbles himself
t: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Adi reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said upon the pulpit, “Verily, if a servant humbles himself for Allah Almighty, he will increase his wisdom.”

title: Hadith on Humility: Whoever does his own chores is not arrogant
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He is not arrogant who eats with his servants, rides a donkey in the market, tends to his sheep and milks them.”
q: He is not arrogant who eats with his servants, rides a donkey in the market, tends to his sheep and milks them

title: Hadith on Virtues: Which prayer, charity, and faith is best?
t: ‘Umayr ibn Qatadah reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, which prayer is best?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One finished with a long supplication.” The man said, “Which charity is best?” The Prophet said, “Great effort with little means.” The man said, “Which believers are most complete?” The Prophet said, “Those with the best character.”
q: One finished with a long supplication … Great effort with little means … Those with the best character
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Sermons: Prolong the prayer, make sermon concise
t: ‘Ammar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the length of a man’s prayer and the brevity of his sermon is a sign of his understanding. Lengthen the prayer and shorten the sermon. Verily, some eloquence is charming.”
q: Verily, the length of a man’s prayer and the brevity of his sermon is a sign of his understanding. Lengthen the prayer and shorten the sermon. Verily, some eloquence is charming

title: Aisha on Muhammad: None had better character than the Prophet
t: ‘Urwah reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “No one had better character than the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. No one from his companions or his family called upon him but that he would say: I am at your service. For this reason, Allah Almighty revealed the verse: Verily, you are upon great moral character.” (68:4)
q: I am at your service … Verily, you are upon great moral character.

title: Hadith on Tarawih: Reward for praying with the Imam until he finishes
t:
Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, whoever stands for prayer in Ramadan with the Imam until he is finished, it will be recorded as if he prayed the entire night.”

Imam al-Tirmidhi commented, “The scholars differed over the night prayer in Ramadan. Some of them are of the view that it is prayed with forty-one cycles including witr prayer, which is the opinion of the people of Medina as practiced in Medina. Most of the scholars are of the opinion that it is prayed with twenty cycles, as narrated from Umar, Ali, and others among the companions of the Prophet; it is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, and Al-Shafi’i. Al-Shafi’i said: Such was done in our land of Mecca, praying twenty cycles. Ahmad said it has been narrated in various ways, and he did not fix any number for it.”
q: Verily, whoever stands for prayer in Ramadan with the Imam until he is finished, it will be recorded as if he prayed the entire night.

title: Hadith on Dua: Umar ibn al-Khattab’s supplication in prayer
t: ‘Abdah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, would say these words aloud in prayer, “Glory be to You, O Allah, with Your praises. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty. There is no God other than You.”

title: Hadith on Tarawih: The Prophet’s night prayer in Ramadan
t: Abu Salamah reported: He asked Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, “How was the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, during Ramadan?” Aisha said, “He would not pray more than eleven cycles in Ramadan or other times. He would pray four cycles, but do not ask about their beauty or length. Then, he would pray four cycles, but do not ask about their beauty or length. Then, he would pray three cycles. I asked him: O Messenger of Allah, do you sleep before Witr prayer? The Prophet said: O Aisha, my eyes sleep, but my heart does not sleep.”
q: O Aisha, my eyes sleep, but my heart does not sleep
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fasting: Prophets ordered to delay morning meal, hasten to break fast
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, we company of prophets have been commanded to delay our pre-fasting meal, to hasten to break our fast, and to place our rights hands over our left hands in prayer.”
q: Verily, we company of prophets have been commanded to delay our pre-fasting meal, to hasten to break our fast, and to place our rights hands over our left hands in prayer.

title: Hadith on Akhirah: If the Hereafter is his only worry, Allah is enough
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever focuses on only one concern, the afterlife, Allah will be enough for his concerns in the world. Whoever scatters his concerns among the matters of the world, it does not matter to Allah in which valley he meets his demise.”
q: Whoever focuses on only one concern, the afterlife, Allah will be enough for his concerns in the world. Whoever scatters his concerns among the matters of the world, it does not matter to Allah in which valley he meets his demise

title: Ibn Salam on ‘Ilm: Masters of knowledge act upon what they know
t: ‘Ubaydullah ibn Umar reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said to Abdullah ibn Salam, “Who are the masters of knowledge?” Abdullah said, “Those who act upon what they know.” Umar said, “What nullifies knowledge in the hearts of men?” Abdullah said, “Greed.”

title: Hadith on Husayn: Hasan and Husayn are my two sweet-basils
t: Ibn Abi Nu’m reported: I watched Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, as he was asked about a man killing mosquitoes. Ibn Umar said, “Where are you from?” The man said, “The people of Iraq.” Ibn Umar said, “Look at this man! He asks me about killing mosquitoes when they killed the grandsons of the Prophet? I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: They are my two sweet-basils in the world.”
q: They are my two sweet-basils in the world.

title: Hadith on Tafsir: Warning not to interpret Quran without knowledge
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever speaks on the Quran without knowledge, let him take his seat in Hellfire.”
q: Whoever speaks on the Quran without knowledge, let him take his seat in Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Sermons: Avoid preaching to people too often, stubbornly
t: ‘Ikramah reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Preach to people once a week every Friday. If you refuse, then two times. If you desire more, then three times. Do not make people averse to this Quran. Do not come to people while they are talking and begin to lecture them, cutting into their conversation and upsetting them. Rather, keep quiet and if they request it, speak to them when they are eager to hear it. Avoid using rhyming prose in supplication, for I lived in the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and his companions; they would only avoid doing so.”

title: Abu Huraira on Hadith: I spend a third of the night remembering Hadith
t: Al-Darimi reported: Abu Huraira, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “I have divided the night into three parts. I sleep in a third of it, I stand in prayer for a third of it, and for a third of it I recall the traditions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.”

title: Hadith on Faith: Parable of the believer is a horse in a stable
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon, him, said, “The parable of the believer and faith is that of a horse in its stable. It roams about and then returns to its stable. Verily, the believer becomes negligent and then returns back to faith.”
q: The parable of the believer and faith is that of a horse in its stable. It roams about and then returns to its stable. Verily, the believer becomes negligent and then returns back to faith.

title: Hadith on Inheritance: Better to leave family wealthy than begging
t: Sa’d reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, visited me while I was ill in Mecca. I said, “I have some wealth. May I donate all of it?” The Prophet said, “No.” I said, “Half of it?” The Prophet said, “No.” I said, “A third of it?” The Prophet said, “Yes a third, but this is still too much. That you leave your inheritors wealthy is better than leaving them dependent, begging for what people have. Whatever you spend on them is charity for you, even the morsel you feed to your wife.”
q: No … No … Yes a third, but this is still too much. That you leave your inheritors wealthy is better than leaving them dependent, begging for what people have. Whatever you spend on them is charity for you, even the morsel you feed to your wife

title: Hadith on Vows: Allah does not need you to punish yourself
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saw an old man walking with the support of his two sons. The Prophet said, “What is the matter with this man?” They said, “He has vowed to walk to the Ka’bah.” The Prophet said, “Allah does not need this man to torture himself,” and he ordered him to ride on a mount.
q: What is the matter with this man? … Allah does not need this man to torture himself
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Food: Allah reveals Halal and Haram food
t: Abu al-Sha’tha reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The people of the time of ignorance would eat some things and leave other things believing they were unclean. Allah sent his Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and revealed his book allowing what is lawful and forbidding what is unlawful. What is allowed in it is lawful, and what is forbidden in it is unlawful. Whatever it is silent upon is an act of clemency.” Then he recited the verse, “Say: I do not find in what was revealed to me anything forbidden to eat except dead animals, blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine,” (6:145) until the end of the verse.
q: Say: I do not find in what was revealed to me anything forbidden to eat except dead animals, blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine,

title: Hadith on Quran: Female companions learn Quran from the Prophet
t:
Umm Hisham bint Harithah reported: I took the chapter, “Qaf, by the Glorious Quran,” (50:1) from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on Friday. The Prophet would recite it on the pulpit every Friday.

In another narration, she said: The Prophet would pray with it in the dawn prayer.
q: Qaf, by the Glorious Quran

title: Hadith on Fasting: Using water to cool off while fasting
t: Abu Bakr reported: I have seen the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in al-‘Araj pouring water over his head while he was fasting, either due to thirst or heat.

title: Hadith on Responsibility: The pen is lifted from three people
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The pen is lifted from three people: a sleeping person until he awakens, a child until he becomes an adult, and an insane person until he regains his sanity.”
q: The pen is lifted from three people: a sleeping person until he awakens, a child until he becomes an adult, and an insane person until he regains his sanity

title: Hadith on Mosques: Masjid is the home of every righteous believer
t: Salman al-Farisi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The mosque is the home of every righteous believer. Allah Almighty has guaranteed comfort and gratification to those who take the mosques as their homes, and safe passage over the bridge of Hell unto the pleasure of Allah Almighty.”
q: The mosque is the home of every righteous believer. Allah Almighty has guaranteed comfort and gratification to those who take the mosques as their homes, and safe passage over the bridge of Hell unto the pleasure of Allah Almighty.

title: Qatadah on Istighfar: Quran shows us spiritual diseases, their cures
t: Salam ibn Miskin reported: Qatadah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, this Quran tells you about your diseases and your cures. As for your diseases, they are your sins. As for your cures, it is seeking the forgiveness of Allah.”

title: Hadith on Food: The Prophet eats a balanced diet
t: Abdullah ibn Ja’far reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, eating fresh dates with cucumbers.

title: Shafi’i on Personality: Balance yourself between introversion, extroversion
t: Yunus al-Sadafi reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Being withdrawn from people will earn hostility and being pompous with them will result in bad companions. Thus, be between an introvert and an extrovert.”

title: Hadith on Insults: Major sin to over-retaliate to provocation
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among the worst of major sins, is to attack the reputation of a Muslim man without a just cause, and among the major sins is to revile twice in response to one insult.”
q: Verily, among the worst of major sins, is to attack the reputation of a Muslim man without a just cause, and among the major sins is to revile twice in response to one insult.

title: Hadith on Oaths: Only swear an oath by Allah when truthful
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not swear an oath by your father, nor your mothers, nor by rivals to Allah. Do not swear an oath unless it is by Allah and you are honest.”
q: Do not swear an oath by your father, nor your mothers, nor by rivals to Allah. Do not swear an oath unless it is by Allah and you are honest.

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Children fasting Ramadan if they are able
t: Al-Rabia’ bint Mu’awwidh reported: We would order our children to fast and we would make toys for them out of wool. If one of them cried for food, we would give them those toys until it was time to break fast.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hasan on Musa: Moses asks his Lord about all goodness
t: Hasan al-Basri reported: Moses, peace and blessings be upon him, asked his Lord about what encompasses all goodness. Allah said: Be a companion to people in the way you would love to be accompanied yourself.”

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Perform voluntary prayers at home
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you finishes the prayer in his mosque, let him perform a portion of his prayer in his house. Verily, Allah will bring about good from his prayer in his house.”
q: When one of you finishes the prayer in his mosque, let him perform a portion of his prayer in his house. Verily, Allah will bring about good from his prayer in his house.

title: Abu Darda on Knowledge: Be a scholar, student, devotee, or follower
t: Al-Hasan reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Be a scholar, a student, a devotee, or a follower; do not be the fifth type lest you be ruined.” It was said to Al-Hasan, “Who is the fifth type?” Al-Hasan said, “A heretic.”

title: Hadith on Ummah: Allah guides people of Fiqh, Hadith
t:
Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah will not let my nation agree upon misguidance. The hand of Allah is over the united community.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “The interpretation of the united community, according to the scholars, are the people of Fiqh, knowledge, and Hadith.”
q: Verily, Allah will not let my nation agree upon misguidance. The hand of Allah is over the united community

title: Hadith on Mosques: Best prayer for women at home, except sacred mosques
t: Abu Amr al-Shaybani reported: Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “No woman performs prayer in a better place than her house, except if it is at the Sacred Mosque or the Mosque of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.”
gf: Rijal al-Sahih (narrators are reliable) according to Al-Haythami

title: Hadith on Mosques: Umar does not stop his wife from visiting the Masjid
t: Ibn Umar reported: One of the wives of Umar attended dawn and evening prayers in congregation in the mosque. It was said to her, “Why do you go out while you know Umar dislikes it and he is jealous?” She said, “What stops him from prohibiting me?” It was said, “The statement of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: Do not prevent the maidservants of Allah from the mosques of Allah.”
q: Do not prevent the maidservants of Allah from the mosques of Allah

title: Hadith on Ramadan: The Prophet secludes himself in the last ten nights
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would retreat to the mosque in the last ten nights of Ramadan.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hijrah: No obligatory emigration if Islam practiced freely
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said on the day Mecca was liberated, “There is no longer emigration, but rather only jihad and good intentions. When you are called to duty, go forth.”
q: There is no longer emigration, but rather only jihad and good intentions. When you are called to duty, go forth.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibrahim on Healing: Medicine for the soul is in five things
t: Al-Azdi reported: Ibrahim al-Khawwas, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The cure of the heart is in five things: reading the Quran with contemplation, emptying the stomach, standing for prayer at night, humbly supplicating at dawn, and sitting with the righteous.”

title: Hadith on Friday: Reward for coming early, listening to sermon
t: Aws ibn Aws reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever performs a thorough ritual bath on Friday, proceeds at the earliest to the mosque, sits below the Imam and listens carefully without talking, he will have a reward for each step he took a year’s worth of fasting and praying.”
q: Whoever performs a thorough ritual bath on Friday, proceeds at the earliest to the mosque, sits below the Imam and listens carefully without talking, he will have a reward for each step he took a year’s worth of fasting and praying

title: Hadith on Signs: The Hour is preceded by major social upheaval
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Just before the Hour, the greeting of peace will only be given to specific people, trade will proliferate to the point that a woman will help her husband in his business, family ties will be severed, the pen will spread, false testimony will prevail and truthful testimony will be concealed.”
q: Just before the Hour, the greeting of peace will only be given to specific people, trade will proliferate to the point that a woman will help her husband in his business, family ties will be severed, the pen will spread, false testimony will prevail and truthful testimony will be concealed.

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: Number of raka’at in Witr prayer
t:
Umm Salamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, performed the night prayer with Witr by thirteen cycles, but when he became older and weaker, he performed it with seven cycles.

Imam al-Tirmidhi commented, “It has been narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that Witr prayer is by thirteen, eleven, nine, seven, five, three, or even one cycle.”

title: Hadith on Duha: The Prophet prays eight cycles in forenoon
t: Umm Hani’ reported: I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace blessings be upon him, in the year of the liberation, and I found him taking a bath. When the Prophet finished his bath, he performed eight cycles of prayer, and that was in the forenoon.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Duha: The Prophet prays in forenoon four cycles
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would perform forenoon prayer with four cycles and he would add more as Allah willed.

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Every morning your joints owe charity
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Upon every one of your joints in the morning is charity due. Every glorification of Allah is charity. Every praise of Allah is charity. Every declaration of the oneness of Allah is charity. Every exaltation of Allah is charity. Enjoining good and forbidding evil is charity. It is enough of that to perform two cycles of prayer in the forenoon.”
q: Upon every one of your joints in the morning is charity due. Every glorification of Allah is charity. Every praise of Allah is charity. Every declaration of the oneness of Allah is charity. Every exaltation of Allah is charity. Enjoining good and forbidding evil is charity. It is enough of that to perform two cycles of prayer in the forenoon.

title: Hadith on Witr: End of night is best for Witr prayer
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever fears he cannot stand for prayer at the end of the night, let him perform Witr prayer in its beginning. Whoever hopes to stand for prayer at the end of the night, let him perform Witr prayer at its ending. Verily, prayer at the end of the night is witnessed, and that is better.”
q: Whoever fears he cannot stand for prayer at the end of the night, let him perform Witr prayer in its beginning. Whoever hopes to stand for prayer at the end of the night, let him perform Witr prayer at its ending. Verily, prayer at the end of the night is witnessed, and that is better.

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Pray Witr before morning comes
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Perform Witr prayer before the morning.”
q: Perform Witr prayer before the morning

title: Hadith on Witr: Make last prayer at night Witr
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Make the last of your prayers at night the Witr prayer.”
q: Make the last of your prayers at night the Witr prayer.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Witr: The Prophet prays Witr before dawn
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would perform Witr prayer every night, either at the beginning, middle, or end of the night, finishing his Witr prayer before the break of dawn.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Witr prayer recommended, not obligation
t:
Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is numerically odd and He loves what is odd, so perform the Witr prayer, O people of the Quran!”

Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The Witr prayer is not required like your prescribed prayers, but rather it is the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.”
q: Verily, Allah is numerically odd and He loves what is odd, so perform the Witr prayer, O people of the Quran!

title: Hadith on Friday: The Prophet prays after Friday in his house
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would not pray after Friday prayer until he had departed and thus would pray in his house.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Praying Witr prayer, Sunan of dawn prayer
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would pray at night, two by two, and make it odd with one cycle. The Prophet would pray two cycles before the morning prayer, so lightly as if the call to prayer were in his ears.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Voluntary Sunan prayers throughout day
t: Ibn Umar reported: I prayed with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, two prostrations before and after noon prayer, two prostrations after sunset prayer, two prostrations after evening prayer, and two prostrations after Friday prayer. As for sunset and evening prayer, they were in his house.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on ‘Ashura: Fasting 9th of Muharram with ‘Ashura
t: Abdullah ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If I live until next year, I will certainly fast the ninth day of al-Muharram.”
q: If I live until next year, I will certainly fast the ninth day of al-Muharram.

title: Hadith on Sawm: Fasting each month purifies the heart
t: Amr ibn Shurahbil reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I tell you what will rid the chest of disturbances? Fasting for three days each month.”
q: Shall I tell you what will rid the chest of disturbances?

title: Hadith on Travel: Allah has waived fasting, half of prayer
t: Amr ibn Umayyah reported: I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, from a journey and he said, “Stay to eat, O Abu Umayyah.” I said, “Indeed, I am fasting.” The Prophet said, “Come close to me and I will tell you about the traveler. Verily, Allah Almighty has waived for him fasting and half of the prayer.”
q: Stay to eat, O Abu Umayyah. … Come close to me and I will tell you about the traveler. Verily, Allah Almighty has waived for him fasting and half of the prayer.

title: Hadith on Fasting: Allah distances him from Hell by 100 years
t: ‘Uqbah ibn Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever fasts a day in the way of Allah Almighty, Allah will distance him from Hell by a measure of one hundred years of travel.”
q: Whoever fasts a day in the way of Allah Almighty, Allah will distance him from Hell by a measure of one hundred years of travel.

title: Hadith on Fasting: Allah delivers him from Hell by seventy autumns
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever fasts a day in the way of Allah Almighty, by that day Allah will deliver his face from the Hellfire a distance of seventy autumns of travel.”
q: Whoever fasts a day in the way of Allah Almighty, by that day Allah will deliver his face from the Hellfire a distance of seventy autumns of travel.

title: Hadith on Siyam: Sins of tongue damage fasting
t: Abu ‘Ubaydah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Fasting is a shield, as long as you do not damage it.”
q: Fasting is a shield, as long as you do not damage it.

title: Hadith on Akhirah: People are tested and questioned in the grave
t: Asma’ bint Abi Bakr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It has been revealed to me that you will be put to trial in the grave, similar to the trial of the False Messiah. As for the believer or Muslim, he will say: Muhammad came to us with clear evidence and we answered him and believed in him. It will be said: Sleep in peace, for we knew you had conviction. As for the hypocrite or the doubter, he will say: I do not know, for I heard people saying something and I repeated it.”
q: It has been revealed to me that you will be put to trial in the grave, similar to the trial of the False Messiah. As for the believer or Muslim, he will say: Muhammad came to us with clear evidence and we answered him and believed in him. It will be said: Sleep in peace, for we knew you had conviction. As for the hypocrite or the doubter, he will say: I do not know, for I heard people saying something and I repeated it.

title: Abu Sulayman on Dhikr: Thinking about Hereafter is life for the heart
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Abu Sulayman, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Thinking about the world is a veil over the Hereafter and a punishment for people. Thinking about the Hereafter produces wisdom and life in the heart. Whoever looks to the world as his protector will come to accept its delusions.”

title: Malik on Arguments: Should he argue to defend the Sunnah?
t: Al-Haytam ibn Jamil reported: I said to Malik, “O servant of Allah, if a man has knowledge of the Sunnah, should he argue to defend it?” Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “No, rather he should convey the Sunnah if they might accept it from him, otherwise he should remain silent.”

title: Ma’ruf on Arguing: If Allah guides him, he acts and does not argue
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Ma’ruf al-Karkhi, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If Allah wills goodness for a servant, He opens the door of action and closes the door of disputation. If Allah wills harm for a servant, He closes the door of action and opens the door of disputation.”

title: Hadith on Gratitude: A thankful eater is like a patient faster
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The one who eats gratefully has the status of one who fasts patiently.”
q: The one who eats gratefully has the status of one who fasts patiently.

title: Hadith on Fasting: Angels bless those who break their fast together
t: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, broke his fast with Sa’d ibn Mu’adh and he said, “The fasting have broken their fast with you, the righteous have eaten your food, and the angels send blessings upon you.”
q: The fasting have broken their fast with you, the righteous have eaten your food, and the angels send blessings upon you
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Siyam: The Prophet fasts on Mondays and Thursdays
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was eager to fast on Monday and Thursday.

title: Ibrahim on Islam: If kings knew our inner-peace, they would fight us for it
t: Ibrahim ibn Bashar reported: Ibrahim ibn Adham, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If the kings and their sons knew what we experience of pleasure and happiness in Islam, they would fight us for it with their swords.”

title: Hadith on Martyrdom: Cannot claim a specific person is a martyr
t: Abu al-‘Ajfa reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “You say about those who are killed or died in your campaigns that ‘this person was killed as a martyr’ or ‘this person died as a martyr.’ Perhaps he only intended to load his animal with spoils, or cover his mount in gold, or pursue his business. Do not say that, but rather say as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever is killed or died in the way of Allah is in Paradise.”
q: Whoever is killed or died in the way of Allah is in Paradise

title: Khawlani on Zuhd: Asceticism is to trust Allah over yourself
t: Ahmad ibn Hanbal reported: Abu Muslim al-Khawlani, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “To renounce the world does not mean to forbid what is allowed, nor to squander wealth. Verily, to renounce the world means to be more reliant on what is in the hand of Allah than your own hand. If you are afflicted with a calamity, you have stronger hope for the reward in store for you, if you continue to endure it.”

title: Hadith on Paradise: Women in Heaven better than whole world
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Were a woman among the women of Paradise to gaze upon the earth, she would illuminate whatever is between them and fill it all with the scent of perfume. Her veil alone is better than the world and everything in it.”
