q: Were a woman among the women of Paradise to gaze upon the earth, she would illuminate whatever is between them and fill it all with the scent of perfume. Her veil alone is better than the world and everything in it

title: Ibn Mubarak on Adab: Seek manners before other Islamic sciences
t: Ibn al-Jazari reported: Ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I sought manners for thirty years and I sought sacred knowledge for twenty years. The righteous predecessors would seek manners first, then seek knowledge.”

title: Ibn Wahb on Character: Learning manners best type of knowledge
t: Ibn Abdul Barr reported: Ibn Wahb, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “What I learned from the manners of Malik was better than his knowledge.”

title: Malik on Adab: I learned manners before sacred knowledge
t: Al-Qadi ‘Iyad reported: Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “My mother would dress me up and say to me: Go to Shaykh Rabi’ah and learn from his manners before his knowledge.”

title: Hadith on I’tikaf: Permission to leave spiritual retreat for a valid need
t: Aisha reported: If the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was in spiritual retreat in the mosque (al-I’tikaf), he would tilt his head towards me and I would comb his hair. He would not enter the house except for the need to relieve himself.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Suhoor: Best pre-fasting morning meal is dates
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most excellent pre-fasting meal of the believer is dates.”
q: The most excellent pre-fasting meal … of the believer is dates

title: Hadith on Quran: Teach me to recite a comprehensive Surah
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessing be upon him, and he said, “Teach me to recite, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “Recite three chapters which begin with Alif Lam Ra.” The man said, “I am very old. It will be difficult on my heart and rough on my tongue.” The Prophet said, “Recite three chapters which begin with Ha Mim.” The man said as he did before. The Prophet said, “Recite three chapters which begin with the glory of Allah.” The man said as he did before and he added, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me a comprehensive chapter.” The Prophet recited the verses, “When the earth is shaken…” (99:1) until he reached the end of the chapter. The man said, “By Him who sent you with the truth, I will never add anything to it.” Then the man departed and the Prophet said, “The little man has succeeded.”
q: Recite three chapters which begin with Alif Lam Ra … Recite three chapters which begin with Ha Mim … Recite three chapters which begin with the glory of Allah … When the earth is shaken… … The little man has succeeded

title: Hadith on Fasting: The Prophet fasts Sha’ban and Ramadan together
t: Umm Salamah reported: I did not see the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, fast for two consecutive months in a row except for Sha’ban and Ramadan.

title: Hadith on Guidance: The Prophet frowns, turns away from blind man
t: Aisha reported: The blind man Ibn Umm Maktum came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, guide me.” At the time, high-ranking men among the idolaters were in the presence of the Prophet, so he turned away from him and faced them. The blind man said, “Have I said something wrong to you?” The Prophet said “No,” and upon this the verse was revealed, “He frowned and turned away,” (80:1).
q: No … He frowned and turned away

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication upon seeing the crescent moon
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when he sighted the crescent of a new moon, he used to say, “O Allah, bring it over us with safety and faith, security and Islam, guidance to what You love and is pleasing to You. Our Lord and your Lord is Allah.”
q: O Allah, bring it over us with safety and faith, security and Islam, guidance to what You love and is pleasing to You. Our Lord and your Lord is Allah.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Travel: Permission to break fast before intending to travel
t:
Muhammad ibn Ka’b reported: I came to Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, during Ramadan and he intended to travel. His mount was prepared for him and he put on his traveling clothes. He called for some food and he ate it. I said to him, “Is it the Sunnah?” Anas said, “Yes, it is the Sunnah.” Then he departed.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “Some of the people of knowledge adhered to this tradition. They said a traveler may break his fast in his house before leaving. He may not shorten his prayers until he leaves the borders of the city or town.”

title: Hadith on Fasting: Making up missed fasts on behalf of deceased
t: Ibn Abbas reported: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and she said, “My mother has died and she owed a month of fasting.” The Prophet said, “Do you think if she had a debt you would repay it on her behalf?” She said yes. The Prophet said, “The debts of Allah are more worthy to be repaid.”
q: Do you think if she had a debt you would repay it on her behalf? … The debts of Allah are more worthy to be repaid.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on ‘Ashura: The Prophet eager to fast ‘Ashura
t: Ibn Abbas reported: I did not see the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as eager to fast a day and preferring it over others except for this day of ‘Ashura and this month of Ramadan.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Huquq: Rights of family over voluntary worship
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him, “I am told you fast and never break your fast and you never stop praying at night? Fast and break your fast, pray at night, and sleep. Verily, your eyes deserve a share of your time, and your own self and your family deserve a share of your time.”
q: I am told you fast and never break your fast and you never stop praying at night? Fast and break your fast, pray at night, and sleep. Verily, your eyes deserve a share of your time, and your own self and your family deserve a share of your time.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Friday: Do not single out Friday for night prayer, fasting
t:
Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not single out the night of Friday for voluntary prayer to the exclusion of other nights. Do not single out the day of Friday for fasting to the exclusion of other days, unless it is the routine of one of you.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “Let not one of you fast on Friday unless he also fasts a day before or after it.”
q: Do not single out the night of Friday for voluntary prayer to the exclusion of other nights. Do not single out the day of Friday for fasting to the exclusion of other days, unless it is the routine of one of you … Let not one of you fast on Friday unless he also fasts a day before or after it.

title: Hadith on Siyam: Fasting on Monday, three days a month
t: Abu Qatadah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about fasting on Monday. The Prophet said, “That is the day I was born and the day I was sent with revelation. Fasting three days of every month and Ramadan after Ramadan is like fasting for a lifetime.”
q: That is the day I was born and the day I was sent with revelation. Fasting three days of every month and Ramadan after Ramadan is like fasting for a lifetime

title: Hadith on Menses: Women make up missed fasts, not prayers
t: Mu’adhah reported: I asked Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, “Why do menstruating women make up missed fasts but not missed prayers?” Aisha said, “When we were afflicted with menstruation, we were ordered to make up missed fasts but not missed prayers.”

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Fasting this month expiates sins before it
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever fasts the month of Ramadan, acknowledging its limits and guarding it as it should be, then it will expiate the sins which came before it.”
q: Whoever fasts the month of Ramadan, acknowledging its limits and guarding it as it should be, then it will expiate the sins which came before it.

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Every locale follows their own moon sighting
t: Kurayb repoted: I came to Syria and tended to my needs. The crescent of Ramadan appeared over me while I was in Syria and I saw it on Friday, then I came to Medina at the end of the month. Abdullah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, asked me about it and I mentioned the crescent. Ibn Abbas said, “When did you see it?” I said, “We saw it on Friday night.” Ibn Abbas said, “You saw it?” I said, “Yes, people saw it and they fasted, as did Mu’awiyah.” Ibn Abbas said, “But we saw it on Saturday night, so we will continue fasting until we complete thirty days or we see it.” I said, “Is it not enough that Mu’awiyah saw it and he fasted?” Ibn Abbas said, “No, such was the command of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.”

title: Hadith on Travel: Permission to fast or not on journey, whatever is easiest
t: Aisha reported: Hamzah ibn Amr asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about fasting while traveling. The Prophet said, “If you wish, you may fast. And if you wish, you may break your fast.”
q: If you wish, you may fast. And if you wish, you may break your fast.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Abbas on Fasting: Permission to taste food while fasting if needed
t:
Ibn Qudamah reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “There is nothing wrong for a fasting person to taste food, vinegar, or something he wants to purchase.”

Ahmad ibn Hanbal said, “I prefer to avoid tasting food, but there is no harm and nothing wrong if it is done.”

title: Shafi’i on Debate: Best answer to a fool is silence
t: Imam al-Shafi’i, may Allah be pleased with him, said in his poetry, “If a fool speaks to you, do not answer him, for the best answer is silence. If you speak to him, you have delighted him. If you leave him, he nearly dies in anguish.”

title: Hadith on Ramadan: The Prophet reviews the Quran in Ramadan
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would review the Quran once every year in Ramadan, and he reviewed it twice in the year he passed away. The Prophet would retreat in the mosque for ten days every year, and he secluded himself for twenty days in the year he passed away.

title: Hadith on Sha’ban: The Prophet fasts in Sha’ban before Ramadan
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would fast until we said he will never break his fast, and he would not fast until we said he would never fast. I did not see the Prophet complete an entire month of fasting except for Ramadan, and I did not see him complete more voluntary fasts than in the month of Sha’ban.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Umar on Injustice: Supplication of oppressed always answered
t: Aslam reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, appointed a client of his named Hunayy to tend the pasture, saying, “O Hunayy, lower your wing for the Muslims and beware the supplication of the oppressed, for the supplication of the oppressed is answered.”

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Gabriel comes to review the Quran twice
t: Fatimah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Gabriel would come to me to revise the Quran once every year. This year he revised with me twice. I do not think it means anything but that my term will come to an end. Verily, you will be the first of the people of my house to meet me.” So I wept and the Prophet said, “Are you not pleased to be the master of the women of Paradise or of the believing women?” So I laughed at that.
q: Gabriel would come to me to revise the Quran once every year. This year he revised with me twice. I do not think it means anything but that my term will come to an end. Verily, you will be the first of the people of my house to meet me. … Are you not pleased to be the master of the women of Paradise or of the believing women?
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Abu Bakr on Muhammad: Whoever worships the Prophet, he has died
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, went to the door of the mosque when he heard the news of the passing of the Prophet. Abu Bakr said, “To proceed: Whoever among you worships Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, then Muhammad has died. Whoever worships Allah, then Allah is alive and cannot die. Allah Almighty said: Muhammad is not but a Messenger. Messengers have passed before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?” (3:144) Ibn Abbas said, “By Allah, it was as if the people had not known that Allah revealed this verse until Abu Bakr recited it.”
q: Muhammad is not but a Messenger. Messengers have passed before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?

title: Ali on Hadith: Narrate to people only what they can understand
t: Al-Bukhari reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Speak to people only according to their level of knowledge. Would you like for Allah and His Messenger to be denied?”

title: Hadith on Masjid: Allah is joyful at Muslims attending mosque
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No Muslim man settles into the mosque for prayer and remembrance but that Allah is delighted for him, just as a family is delighted when their absentees return to them.”
q: No Muslim man settles into the mosque for prayer and remembrance but that Allah is delighted for him, just as a family is delighted when their absentees return to them.

title: Hadith on Rulers: Whoever goes to the ruler will experience trials
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever goes to the gates of the ruler will be afflicted with trials.”
q: Whoever goes to the gates of the ruler will be afflicted with trials.

title: Hadith on Clothing: No harm in garments falling to ankles
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The garment of a Muslim should be lowered to the middle of the shin, but there is no harm or blame in what is between it and the ankles. Whatever is lower than the ankles is in the Hellfire. Whoever trails his garment in pride, Allah will never look at him.”
q: The garment of a Muslim should be lowered to the middle of the shin, but there is no harm or blame in what is between it and the ankles. Whatever is lower than the ankles is in the Hellfire. Whoever trails his garment in pride, Allah will never look at him.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Conscience: Sin agitates the heart and mind
t: Hannad ibn al-Sari reported: Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Sin is disturbing to the heart. There is never a glimpse of it but that Satan has ambition for it.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Greeting: I would respond to Pharaoh if he greeted me
t: Sa’id ibn Jubayr reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “If Pharaoh had said to me, ‘May Allah bless you,’ I would have said, ‘And you too,’ but Pharaoh has already died.”

title: Wuhayb on Hereafter: Woe to one who hopes in the world
t: Muhammad ibn Yahya reported: Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Woe to one who places his hopes in the world and sinful are his deeds, great is his violence and little is his intelligence, knowledgeable of the affairs of the world yet ignorant of the affairs of the Hereafter.”

title: Hadith on Injustice: Exploitation of women, workers, animals
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among the greatest of sins to Allah is that a man marries a woman and, when he fulfills his needs with her, he divorces her and leaves with her dowry. And that a man employs another man and leaves without paying him, and finally one who kills an animal for fun.”
q: Among the greatest of sins to Allah is that a man marries a woman and, when he fulfills his needs with her, he divorces her and leaves with her dowry. And that a man employs another man and leaves without paying him, and finally one who kills an animal for fun.

title: Hadith on Trials: Believer purified by illness like iron in a fire
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Azhar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the parable of the believer, when he is afflicted by illness or fever, is that of a piece of iron placed in the fire; its defects vanish while its purities remains.”
q: Verily, the parable of the believer, when he is afflicted by illness or fever, is that of a piece of iron placed in the fire; its defects vanish while its purities remains

title: Ibm Umar on Mothers: Do you think I have fully repaid my mother?
t: Abu Burdah reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, watched a Yemeni man circling the House while carrying his mother on his back, saying, “I am her humble camel. If her mount is scared, I am not scared.” Then he said, “O Ibn Umar, do you think I have repaid her?” Ibn Umar said, “No, not even for a single pang of pregnancy.”

title: Hadith on Medicine: Unqualified doctors responsible for malpractice
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever practices medicine without any prior knowledge of medicine will be held liable.”
q: Whoever practices medicine without any prior knowledge of medicine will be held liable.

title: Hadith on Leadership: Disapproval of seeking power, authority
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Samurah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “O Abdur Rahman, do not ask for authority! If it is given to you at your request, you will be held fully responsible for it. If it is given to you without your request, you will be helped by Allah in it.”
q: O Abdur Rahman, do not ask for authority! If it is given to you at your request, you will be held fully responsible for it. If it is given to you without your request, you will be helped by Allah in it
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Caution: Not exposing confusing matters to common people
t: ‘Ubaydullah reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “You do not narrate to people what their minds cannot grasp but that it will be a trial for some of them.”

title: Hadith on Commands: The Prophet forbids nine things
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, enjoined upon me nine deeds, “Do not associate anything with Allah, even if you are cut or burned. Do not deliberately leave off the prescribed prayer, for those who leave it have forfeited protection from Allah. Do not drink wine, for it is the key opening to every evil. Obey your parents, even if they order you to take from your worldly possession, take it out for them. Do not contend with those in authority, even if you think you are right. Do not run away when the army advances, even if you meet your demise and your companions flee. Send from your means upon your family and do not raise the rod against them. And enjoin them to fear Allah Almighty.”
q: Do not associate anything with Allah, even if you are cut or burned. Do not deliberately leave off the prescribed prayer, for those who leave it have forfeited protection from Allah. Do not drink wine, for it is the key opening to every evil. Obey your parents, even if they order you to take from your worldly possession, take it out for them. Do not contend with those in authority, even if you think you are right. Do not run away when the army advances, even if you meet your demise and your companions flee. Send from your means upon your family and do not raise the rod against them. And enjoin them to fear Allah Almighty.

title: Mutarrif on Moderation: Middle path between two extremes is best
t: Abu ‘Ubaydah reported: Mutarrif ibn Abdullah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The best of matters is the middle course, for a good deed is between two evil deeds.”

title: Sa’id on Backbiting: All their good deeds are spoiled by backbiting
t: Ibn al-Jawzi reported: Sa’id ibn al-Jubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and presented with his record. He will not see his prayers, nor his fasting, nor his good deeds. He will say: O Lord, this is the record of someone else, for I had good deeds not in this record. It will be said to him: Verily, your Lord does not overlook or forget. Your deeds have vanished because you were backbiting people.”

title: Abu Dujanah on Deeds: Pure heart to Muslims, mind own business
t: Zayd ibn Aslam reported: He as admitted into the home of Abu Dujanah, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was ill, but his face was joyful. It was said to him, “Why is your face joyful?” Abu Dujanah said, “There is no work more reliable to me than two things: that I do not speak of what does not concern me, and that my heart is pure towards the Muslims.”

title: Umar on Wealth: The Caliph laments when he finds treasure
t: Ibn Rajab reported: When the treasures of Khosrau were opened for Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, he wept and he said, “Verily, the likes of this were never opened for people but that Allah made it a source of enmity between them.”

title: Hadith on Debt: Erasing debt is shaded under the Throne
t: Abu Qatadah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever grants relief to a debtor or absolves his debt, he will be in the shade of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever grants relief to a debtor or absolves his debt, he will be in the shade of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Salaam: Offering peace, kind words leads to Paradise
t: Hani’ ibn Yazid reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among the deeds that must result in forgiveness are offering peace and good words.”
q: Verily, among the deeds that must result in forgiveness are offering peace and good words

title: Hadith on Huquq: Rights of husbands and mothers are greatest
t: Aisha reported: She said, “O Messenger of Allah, who among people has the greatest right over the wife?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Her husband.” Aisha said, “Who among people has the greatest right of the man?” The Prophet said, “His mother.”
q: Her husband … His mother

title: Hasan on Shura: Blessing in consulting your companions
t: Ibn Muflih reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Indeed, Allah Almighty did not command his Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to consult his companions because he needed their opinions. Rather, he intended for them to recognize the blessing in consultation.”

title: Umar II on Sabr: Reward of patience better than material blessings
t: Muhammad ibn Amr reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said upon the pulpit, “Allah does not grant a servant a blessing and then removes the blessing, then compensates him with patience in place of what was removed, but that what he was granted is better than what was taken away.” Then, Umar recited the verse, “Verily, the reward of the patient will be fulfilled without account,” (39:10).
q: Verily, the reward of the patient will be fulfilled without account

title: Fudayl on Tazkiyyah: Prophets and righteous have pure hearts
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It has been said that among the character of the prophets and chosen elect is the purity of their hearts. They are three characteristics: forbearance, penitence, and a portion of prayer in the night.”

title: Hadith on Trials: Believers do not seek unnecessary hardship
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is not befitting for a believer to humiliate himself.” They said, “How does he humiliate himself?” The Prophet said, “He confronts a trial he cannot endure.”
q: It is not befitting for a believer to humiliate himself. … He confronts a trial he cannot endure.

title: Ibrahim on Hilm: Toughest on Satan is a gentle, patient scholar
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Ibrahim ibn Adham, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It is said that nothing is harder upon Iblis (Satan) than a forbearing scholar. If he speaks, he speaks with knowledge. If he is silent, he is silent with forbearance.”

title: Sufyan on Zuhd: He gains wisdom once he forsakes worldly life
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “When a servant renounces the world, Allah will cause wisdom to grow in his heart and to come forth from his tongue. He will grant him insight into the faults of the world, its diseases, and its cures.”

title: Hadith on Debt: Paying debts on behalf of deceased
t: Salamah ibn al-Akwa’ reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was presented with a funeral for him to pray over it. The Prophet said, “Does he have debt?” They said no, so the Prophet prayed over him. Then he was presented with another funeral and the Prophet said, “Does he have debt?” They said yes. The Prophet said, “Pray over your companion.” Abu Qatadah said, “I take responsibility for his debt, O Messenger of Allah,” so the Prophet prayed over him.
q: Does he have debt … Does he have debt … Pray over your companion

title: Hadith on Uthman: Most modest of the Ummah is Uthman
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Modesty is part of faith, and the most modest of my nation is Uthman.”
q: Modesty is part of faith, and the most modest of my nation is Uthman

title: Hadith on Dua: I am pleased with Allah, Muhammad, Islam
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever says when he enters the evening, ‘I am pleased with Allah as a Lord, with Islam as a religion, and with Muhammad as a prophet,’ it will be a duty upon Allah to please him.”
q: Whoever says when he enters the evening, ‘I am pleased with Allah as a Lord, with Islam as a religion, and with Muhammad as a prophet,’ it will be a duty upon Allah to please him.

title: Hadith on Debt: Reward for one who eases someone’s debt
t: Buraydah ibn al-Aslami reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever grants respite to one in a difficult debt, he will have a reward of charity for each day. Whoever grants him respite after payment is due, he will have the like of it in charity for each day.”
q: Whoever grants respite to one in a difficult debt, he will have a reward of charity for each day. Whoever grants him respite after payment is due, he will have the like of it in charity for each day.

title: Ibn Abbas on Deeds: Three deeds not accepted without three others
t: Al-Saffarini reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Three verses were revealed in connection with three others. One will not be accepted without its counterpart. First, the verse, ‘Establish prayer and give charity,’ (2:43). Whoever prays and does not give charity, his prayer is not accepted. Second, the saying of the Almighty, ‘Be grateful to me and your parents,’ (31:14). Whoever is grateful to Allah and is not grateful to his parents, it will not be accepted from him. Third, the saying of the Almighty, “Obey Allah and obey the messenger,’ (3:32). Whoever obeys Allah and does not obey the messenger, it will not be accepted from him.”
q: Establish prayer and give charity … Be grateful to me and your parents … Obey Allah and obey the messenger

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Hasad: Envier is an enemy to the decree of Allah
t:
Al-Qurtubi reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Do not be an enemy to the blessings of Allah.” It was said, “Who is an enemy to the blessings of Allah?” Ibn Mas’ud said, “Those who envy people for what Allah has given them by His grace.”

Imam al-Qurtubi commented, “Allah Almighty said in some of His scriptures: The envier is an enemy of My blessings, resentful of My decree, and not pleased with My distribution.”

title: Hadith on Tawbah: True repentance wipes away all sins
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The one who truly repented of sin is like one without sin.”
q: The one who truly repented of sin is like one without sin.

title: Hadith on Shahid: Martyr is forgiven except sins against people
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The martyr is forgiven for every sin except debt.”
q: The martyr is forgiven for every sin except debt.

title: Umar II on Knowledge: Action without knowledge more harmful than good
t: Sa’id ibn Abdul Aziz reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote to the people of Medina, “Whoever worships without knowledge will cause more harm than good. Whoever considers his words part of his deeds will speak little unless it concerns him. Whoever makes the purpose of his religion to indulge in arguments, he will frequently change his position.”

title: Hadith on Injustice: Three types of wrongdoing to Allah
t:
Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are three kinds of wrongdoing: wrong that Allah does not ignore, wrong that He forgives, and wrong that He does not forgive. As for wrong which is not forgiven, it is idolatry that Allah does not forgive. As for wrong that is forgiven, it is the wrong of a servant between himself and his Lord. As for that which He does not ignore, it is retaliation against some people on behalf of others.”

Souurce: Musnad Abī Dāwud al-Ṭayyālisī 2209
q: There are three kinds of wrongdoing: wrong that Allah does not ignore, wrong that He forgives, and wrong that He does not forgive. As for wrong which is not forgiven, it is idolatry that Allah does not forgive. As for wrong that is forgiven, it is the wrong of a servant between himself and his Lord. As for that which He does not ignore, it is retaliation against some people on behalf of others.

title: Abu Darda on Backbiting: Loan them your reputation until Judgment Day
t: Yahya ibn Sa’id reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “I realized that people were like leaves with no thorns among them, but then they became thorns with no leaves among them. If you criticize them, they will criticize you. If you leave them alone, they will not leave you alone.” They said, “What shall we do?” Abu Darda said, “Loan them some of your reputation, until the Day on which you are impoverished.”

title: Sayfi on Adab: Worst of manners to constantly blame others
t: Sharqi ibn al-Quttami reported: Sayfi ibn Rabah, may Allah have mercy on him, said to his son, “O my son, know that quickest crime to be punished is oppression and that the worst supporter is transgression. The foundation of good character is to restrict speech, and the most evil of manners is excessively fault others.”

title: Ibn Sirin on Honor: Evil to only mention bad about your brother
t: Al-Rabia’ reported: Ibn Sirin, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It is an act of wrong against your brother that you mention what you know is evil about him, while you are silent upon his good.”

title: Hadith on Jesus: Blessed is he who lives after the Second Coming
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Blessed is the one who lives after the coming of the Messiah! Blessed is the one who lives after the coming of the Messiah! The heavens will be called upon for the land, and the earth will be called upon for the crops. If you were to sow your seed upon the rock, it would surely grow. Thus, you will not have greed for each other, nor envy each other, nor hate each other, until even a man passes by a lion unharmed, and he steps over a snake unharmed. You will not have greed for each other, nor envy each other, nor hate each other.”
q: Blessed is the one who lives after the coming of the Messiah! Blessed is the one who lives after the coming of the Messiah! The heavens will be called upon for the land, and the earth will be called upon for the crops. If you were to sow your seed upon the rock, it would surely grow. Thus, you will not have greed for each other, nor envy each other, nor hate each other, until even a man passes by a lion unharmed, and he steps over a snake unharmed. You will not have greed for each other, nor envy each other, nor hate each other.

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: Do the right thing, do not hate each other
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be servants of Allah as brothers. Do not be hostile to each other and do not hate each other. Follow the right course, seek nearness to Allah in worship, and give glad tidings.”
q: Be servants of Allah as brothers. Do not be hostile to each other and do not hate each other. Follow the right course, seek nearness to Allah in worship, and give glad tidings

title: Hadith on Honesty: You must be truthful, not hate each other
t: Abu Bakr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must be truthful, for it is alongside righteousness and they are both in Paradise. Beware of falsehood, for it is alongside wickedness and they are both in the Hellfire. Ask Allah for wellness, for no one is given anything better after conviction than wellness. Do not envy each other, do not hate each other, do not cut each other off, and do not turn away from each other. Be servants of Allah as brothers.”
q: You must be truthful, for it is alongside righteousness and they are both in Paradise. Beware of falsehood, for it is alongside wickedness and they are both in the Hellfire. Ask Allah for wellness, for no one is given anything better after conviction than wellness. Do not envy each other, do not hate each other, do not cut each other off, and do not turn away from each other. Be servants of Allah as brothers

title: Hadith on Ummah: The Prophet warns against diseases of nations
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the diseases of nations will afflict my nation.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what are the diseases of nations?” The Prophet said, “Insolence, hubris, turning their backs to one another, competing for worldly possessions, hating each other, and miserliness, until there will be oppression and then there will be bloodshed.”
q: Verily, the diseases of nations will afflict my nation. … Insolence, hubris, turning their backs to one another, competing for worldly possessions, hating each other, and miserliness, until there will be oppression and then there will be bloodshed.

title: Amr on Hilm: True forbearance is patience with insults, abuse
t: Abu Salil reported: Amr ibn al-‘As, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The truly forbearing one is not one who is forbearing to those who tolerate him but insults whoever insults him. Rather, the truly forbearing one is forbearing to both those who tolerate him and to those who insult him.”

title: Abu Darda on Ego: One who follows his ego harms himself
t: Hasan reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever follows his ego in everything he sees in people, his sadness will be lengthened and his rage will not be healed.”

title: Hasan on Repentance: Believers continue to repent again and again
t: Sufyan al-Thawri reported: It was said to Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, regarding a man who sins and then repents, then sins and repents three more times. Hasan said, “These are the manners of the believer.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Humility: Remember your own faults before other people
t: Mujahid reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “If you intend to mention the faults of your companions, then remember your own faults.”

title: Umar II on Akhirah: Set right your Hereafter, Allah will care for your world
t: Ibn Abi Dunya reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Take care of your Hereafter and Allah will take care of your worldly life. Take care of your private life and Allah will take care of your public life.”

title: Ibrahim on Contentment: Spiritual freedom is satisfaction with decree of Allah
t: Ibn al-Qayyim reported: Ibrahim ibn Shayban, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Dignity is in humility, honor is in righteousness, and freedom is in contentment.”

title: Hadith on Sin: One who is pleased with sin is like a witness to it
t: Al-‘Urs ibn ‘Amirah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When sin is committed on the earth, whoever witnessed it and hated it and rejected it will be like one who was absent from it. Whoever was absent from it and was pleased with it will be like one who witnessed it.”
q: When sin is committed on the earth, whoever witnessed it and hated it and rejected it will be like one who was absent from it. Whoever was absent from it and was pleased with it will be like one who witnessed it

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Quran: Keep busy filling your hearts with Quran
t: Ibn al-Aswad reported: Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, these hearts are vessels, so occupy them with the Quran; do not let them be occupied with anything else.”

title: Ali on Forgiveness: If he lied about me, may Allah forgive him
t: Sufyan reported: A man came to Ali ibn al-Husyan, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said to him, “Indeed, a man has harmed and disparaged you!” Ali said, “Come to him with us.” They departed with him and he saw that he would stand up for himself, so when they came to the man, Ali said, “O you! If what you said is true, may Allah forgive me. If what you said is false, may Allah forgive you.”

title: Hasan on Shirk: Idol of the Muslim nation is wealth
t: Ibn Muflih reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Every nation has an idol that they worship, and the idol of this nation is the gold and silver coin.”

title: Hadith on Jihad: No harm to people in religious buildings
t:
Thabit ibn al-Hajjaj reported: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, stood up among the people and praised and thanked Allah, then he said, “No doubt, do not kill the monk in the monastery.”

Ibn Taymiyyah said, “The majority of scholars say monks are not killed (during war) unless they are among those who assist in fighting in its entirety; otherwise they are (immune) like women and children.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Enjoining: He would not be mad at them, he was gentle
t: Ahmad ibn Hanbal reported: The companions of Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, if they passed by people from whom they saw something they disapproved, they would say, “Take it easy, may Allah have mercy on you.”

title: Sufyan on Enjoining: Forbid evil with gentleness, justice, knowledge
t: Al-Khallal reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “There is no enjoining good or forbidding evil except for one who has three qualities: gentleness in what he enjoins and forbids, justice in what he enjoins and forbids, and knowledge of what he enjoins and forbids.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Evil: You will see evil you cannot change
t: Al-Rabi’ ibn ‘Umaylah reported: Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Soon one of you will see evil he cannot change, yet Allah knows that he hates it in his heart.”

title: Ibn Mubarak on Backbiting: Why sit with backbiters instead of companions?
t: Shaqiq al-Balkhi reported: It was said to Ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him, “When you pray, why do you not sit with us afterwards?” Ibn al-Mubarak said, “I sit with the companions and the successors. I look into their books and what they left behind. What would I do with you? You backbite people.”

title: Malik on Speech: Sins of the tongue become weakness in the body
t: Al-Munawi reported: Malik ibn Dinar, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you see hardness in your heart, weakness in your body, and deprivation in your provision, then know that you have spoken about what is not your concern.”

title: Umar on Provision: Reliance upon Allah means to work for provision
t: Al-Ghazali reported: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Let not one of you refrain from working for his provision, supplicating to Allah to provide while he knows that the sky does not rain gold and silver.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Four powerful supplications for morning
t: Juwayriah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to her one morning for the dawn prayer and she was in the mosque. Then, he returned later in the morning while she was sitting. The Prophet said, “You have not left this position you are in.” She said yes. The Prophet said, “I said four words after you, three times each. If these words were weighed against whatever you said since this morning, it would surely outweigh them: Glory be to Allah and His praise by the number of His creation, by His pleasure, by the weight of His Throne, and by the vastness of His words.”
q: You have not left this position you are in … I said four words after you, three times each. If these words were weighed against whatever you said since this morning, it would surely outweigh them: Glory be to Allah and His praise by the number of His creation, by His pleasure, by the weight of His Throne, and by the vastness of His words.

title: Hadith on Pain: Supplication to say when experiencing pain
t: Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As reported: He complained to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, of pain he felt in his body since he had embraced Islam. The Prophet said to him, “Place your hand over the part of your body where you feel pain and say three times: In the name of Allah. And say seven times: I seek refuge in Allah and his power from the evil of what I feel and worry.”
q: Place your hand over the part of your body where you feel pain and say three times: In the name of Allah. And say seven times: I seek refuge in Allah and his power from the evil of what I feel and worry

title: Hadith on Tawhid: I asked of you less than that in the world
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty will say to the one least punished in the Hellfire: If you had anything on the earth, would you ransom yourself with it? He will say yes. Allah will say: I asked from you less than that while you were in the backbone of Adam, that you not associate anything with Me, but you refused only for the sake of your idolatry.”
q: Allah Almighty will say to the one least punished in the Hellfire: If you had anything on the earth, would you ransom yourself with it? He will say yes. Allah will say: I asked from you less than that while you were in the backbone of Adam, that you not associate anything with Me, but you refused only for the sake of your idolatry
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Shafi’i on Knowledge: I desire no praise or credit for teaching
t: Ibn Abi Hatim reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I never debated anyone and loved for him to be wrong. There is no knowledge in my heart but that I wish everyone could have it and attribute none of it to me.”

title: Shafi’i on Debate: Only debate those who might accept truth
t:
Al-Bayhaqi reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I never debated anyone I knew to be founded upon innovation.”

Al-Bayhaqi said, “This is because the one founded upon innovation rarely turns away from his innovation through debate. Indeed, he would only debate whomever it was hoped would turn to the truth if it were clarified to him.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for performing ablution
t: Abu Musa reported: I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace an blessings be upon him, while he was performing ablution and I heard him supplicating, saying, “O Allah, forgive my sins, expand my abode, and bless me in my provision.” I said, “O Prophet of Allah, I heard you supplicating with these words.” The Prophet said, “Do they leave anything out?”
q: O Allah, forgive my sins, expand my abode, and bless me in my provision … Do they leave anything out

title: Hadith on Hajj: The Hour will not come until Hajj is abandoned
t:
Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hajj and the Umrah pilgrimages will continue even after the emergence of Gog and Magog.”

Al-Shu’bah said, “The Hour will not be established until no one performs the Hajj.”
q: The Hajj and the Umrah pilgrimages will continue even after the emergence of Gog and Magog

title: Hadith on Ruqyah: Gabriel supplicates over the Prophet for healing
t: Aisha reported: If the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was afflicted by something, the Angel Gabriel would supplicate over him, saying, “In the name of Allah, may he cure you, may he heal you from every ailment, from the evil of the envier when he envies, and from the evil of every eye.”
q: In the name of Allah, may he cure you, may he heal you from every ailment, from the evil of the envier when he envies, and from the evil of every eye.

title: Umar on Salat: Most important matter to me is prayer
t: Nafi’ reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to his deputies, saying, “Verily, the most important of your affairs to me is the prayer. Whoever maintains it and watches over it will maintain his religion. Whoever wastes it will be even more wasteful of other things.”

title: Shafi’i on Debates: Arguing in religion breeds hate, bad will
t:
Al-Rabia’ ibn Sulayman reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Arguing about the religion hardens the heart and produces resentment.”

And Al-Shafi’i said, “I never debated anyone but with sincere good will.”

title: Hadith on Sakinah: Make things easy, calm for people
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Make things easy and do not make things difficult. Make people calm and do not frighten them away.”
q: Make things easy and do not make things difficult. … Make people calm and do not frighten them away
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Medicine: Hot, sweet, healthy drinks bring comfort
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, talbina rests the heart of a sick person and takes away some grief.”
q: Verily, talbina rests the heart of a sick person and takes away some grief.

title: Hadith on Shyness: Let not shyness stop you from seeking knowledge
t:
Safiyyah bint Shaybah reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “How excellent are the women of the Ansar! They do not allow shyness to prevent them from understanding the religion.”

In another narration, Aisha said, “They do not allow shyness to prevent them from asking questions about the religion and seeking to understand it.”

title: Hadith on Suicide: Muslim who kills himself not an unbeliever
t: Jabir reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, emigrated to Medina, Al-Tufayl ibn ‘Amr also emigrated along with a man from his people. They strongly disliked the climate of Medina and the man became sick and suffered from anxiety. He took some of his arrowheads, cut the joints of his fingers, and his hands bled out until he died. Al-Tufayl saw him in a dream looking as if he were well but his hands were covered. Al-Tufayl said, “How has your Lord treated you?” The man said, “He has forgiven me due to my emigration to His Prophet.” Al-Tufayl said, “Why do I see your hands covered?” The man said, “I was told that ‘we would not repair what you yourself have ruined.’” Al-Tufayl told the story to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Allah, forgive his hands as well.”
q: O Allah, forgive his hands as well.

title: Hadith on Dunya: The Prophet in the world, not of the world
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I am not of the world and it is not of me. Verily, I have been sent and the Hour is not far behind.”
q: I am not of the world and it is not of me. Verily, I have been sent and the Hour is not far behind.

title: Hadith on Revelation: Weighty calm of the Prophet’s divine inspiration
t: Zayd ibn Thabit reported: I was sitting to the side of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, one day as the revelation came to him. The Prophet was overcome with calm, and his thigh fell upon my thigh as the calm overtook him. By Allah, I have never found anything heavier than the thigh of the Messenger of Allah, and then he was released from it. The Prophet said, “Write, O Zayd.” I took a shoulder bone and the Prophet said, “Write: Not equal are those who stay back and those who wage jihad among the believers,” until the end of the verse, “… a great reward,” (4:95). So I wrote that on a shoulder bone.
q: Write, O Zayd … Write: Not equal are those who stay back and those who wage jihad among the believers … … a great reward

title: Hasan on Funerals: How to console non-Muslims at their funerals
t:
Ibn al-Qayyim reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you console a non-Muslim citizen, say: May nothing beset you but goodness.”

Huraym reported: I heard Al-Ajlah, may Allah have mercy on him, console a Christian and he said, “You must be mindful of Allah and be patient.”

Mansur reported: Ibrahim, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you intend to console a man from the people of the Book, say: May Allah increase your wealth and children and lengthen your life.”

Harb reported: I said to Ishaq, may Allah have mercy on him, “How is an idolater consoled?” Ishaq said, “It is said: May Allah increase your wealth and children.”

title: Hadith on Funerals: If a non-Muslim relative passes away
t: Ali reported: I said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “Your uncle, the misguided old man, has died.” The Prophet said, “Go bury your father and do nothing until you come back to me.” I buried him and I came back to him. The Prophet ordered me to bathe myself and he supplicated for me.
q: Go bury your father and do nothing until you come back to me

title: Sufyan on Nafs: Hardest struggle was against my own self
t: Waki’ reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I never dealt with anything more difficult on me than my own self. Sometimes it would be against me, and sometimes it would be for me.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for blessings after eating, drinking
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is provided food from Allah, let him say: O Allah, bless us in it and feed us with what is even better. Whoever is provided a drink of milk from Allah, let him say: O Allah, bless us in it and provide us with more.”
q: Whoever is provided food from Allah, let him say: O Allah, bless us in it and feed us with what is even better. Whoever is provided a drink of milk from Allah, let him say: O Allah, bless us in it and provide us with more.

title: Hadith on Hair: Discouragement to partially shave head, leave rest
t:
Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited partial shaving. It was said to Nafi’, “What is partial shaving?” Nafi’ said, “It is to shave part of a boy’s head and leave the rest.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “Shave it all or leave it all.”
q: Shave it all or leave it all
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hajj: Those offering sacrifices not cut hair or nails
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If the ten days of Dhul Hijjah begin and one of you intends to sacrifice, let him not remove anything from his hair or skin.”
q: If the ten days of Dhul Hijjah begin and one of you intends to sacrifice, let him not remove anything from his hair or skin.

title: Hadith on Charity: Spend in charity, do not be miserly
t: Asma’ reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Spend in charity and do not count it, lest Allah count it against you. Do not hoard it, lest Allah withhold from you.”
q: Spend in charity and do not count it, lest Allah count it against you. Do not hoard it, lest Allah withhold from you
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sujud: Allah expiates sins by prostration in prayer
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No servant prostrates for the sake of Allah but that Allah will record for him one good deed, erase one bad deed, and raise his status by a degree. Thus, perform many prostrations.”
q: No servant prostrates for the sake of Allah but that Allah will record for him one good deed, erase one bad deed, and raise his status by a degree. Thus, perform many prostrations.

title: Hadith on Salat: Beware of ruin by distraction in prayer
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “O my son, beware of being distracted in prayer, for distraction in prayer is a cause of ruin.”
q: O my son, beware of being distracted in prayer, for distraction in prayer is a cause of ruin.

title: Hasan on Jihad: Your greatest enemy is your own ego
t:
Al-Tabari reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Your enemy is not the one you are relieved from if you killed him. Rather, your true enemy is your own soul, between your two sides.”

Al-Tabari said, “It is the jihad against the greatest of enemies to a man. There is no doubt that it is greater in reward to Allah than the jihad against the people of idolatry.”

title: Sha’bi on Khutbah: Every preacher is accountable on Judgment Day
t: Ibn al-Mubarak reported: Al-Sha’bi, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “No preacher delivers a sermon but that he will be confronted with his sermon on the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Hadith on Janazah: Better to stand for funerals, permissible to sit
t: Ali reported: We saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, stand for funerals and so we stood up. The Prophet would sit and so we sat.

title: Hadith on Funerals: Speak well of deceased or say nothing
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Mention what is good about your dead, and refrain from speaking about their flaws.”
q: Mention what is good about your dead, and refrain from speaking about their flaws.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Death: Do not curse the dead, hurt the living
t: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not abuse the dead and thus harm the living.”
q: Do not abuse the dead and thus harm the living.

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet’s delight in his prayers
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beloved to me in the world are women and perfume, yet the delight of my eyes was made in prayer.”
q: Beloved to me in the world are women and perfume, yet the delight of my eyes was made in prayer.

title: Hadith on Fatimah: The Prophet’s love and respect for his daughter
t: Aisha reported: I have not seen anyone more closely resemble the disposition, mannerism, and characteristics of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, than his daughter Fatimah, may Allah honor her countenance. If she entered his home, the Prophet would stand for her, take her by the hand, kiss her, and seat her in his place. If the Prophet entered her home, she would stand for him, take him by the hand, kiss him, and seat him in her place.

title: Hadith on Shaytan: Do not curse Satan, rather turn to Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not curse Satan, but rather seek refuge in Allah from his evil.”
q: Do not curse Satan, but rather seek refuge in Allah from his evil.

title: Malik on Personality: Everyone do good deeds easiest for them
t: Ibn Abdul Barr reported: Abdullah ibn Abdul Aziz wrote to Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, encouraging him to isolate himself for worship and discouraging him from gatherings of knowledge. Malik wrote back to him, “Allah Almighty has distributed good deeds just as he has distributed provision. A man may have the way of prayer opened for him but the way of fasting is unopened for him. Another may have the way of charity opened for him but the way of fasting is unopened for him. Another may have the way of jihad opened for him but the way of prayer is unopened for him. The spreading of knowledge and teaching it is among the best of righteous deeds. I am pleased with what Allah has opened for me of it. I do not suspect that what I have in it is lesser than what you have of it. I hope that each of us are upon good. It is necessary for each person among us to be pleased with what Allah has distributed for us. Peace.”

title: Hadith on Islam: This religion will reach everywhere in the world
t: Al-Miqdam ibn al-Aswad reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No house of brick, nor fur, will remain upon the face of the earth but that Allah will cause the message of Islam to enter it, by which the honorable will be honored and the disgraceful will be disgraced.”
q: No house of brick, nor fur, will remain upon the face of the earth but that Allah will cause the message of Islam to enter it, by which the honorable will be honored and the disgraceful will be disgraced

title: Dahhak on Character: Head of the matter is good character
t: Abu Rawq reported: Al-Dahhak, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The head of the matter is good character.”

title: Abu Bakr on Custody: A divorced mother has more right to her children
t: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab had married a woman of the Ansar and she gave birth to ‘Asim ibn Umar, then he divorced her. Umar came to Quba’ and he found his son ‘Asim playing in the courtyard of the mosque. He took him by the arm and placed him in front of him on his mount. The grandmother of the boy noticed him and argued with him until they were brought before Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. Umar said, “He is my son.” The mother said, “He is my son.” Abu Bakr said, “Leave him and her together.” Umar did not repeat what he had said.

title: Hadith on Adam: Allah created Adam in His image
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you fights his brother, let him avoid the face. Verily, Allah created Adam in His image.”
q: If one of you fights his brother, let him avoid the face. Verily, Allah created Adam in His image.

title: Rabia’ on Dua: No, rather I will pray for the thief
t: Al-‘Ala ibn al-Musayyib reported: A horse was stolen from Al-Rabia’, may Allah have mercy on him, so the people with him said, “Pray to Allah Almighty against him!” Al-Rabia’ said, “No, rather I will pray for him. O Allah, if he was rich, turn his heart! If he was poor, enrich him!”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Quran: Let the amazing verses move your heart
t: ‘Alqamah reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Do not scatter the Quran as if it were dates falling from a tree, nor recite quickly as if it were poetry. Stop at its verses that amaze you and let it move your hearts. Let not your concern be reaching the end of the surah.”

title: Umar on Hudud: Strict requirement of four witnesses to adultery
t: Ibn al-Musayyib reported: Three men testified against Al-Mughirah that he had committed adultery, while an additional witness abstained. Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, punished the three men and he said to them, “Repent and I will accept your testimony.” Two men repented and Abu Bakrah did not repent, so Umar did not accept his testimony.

title: Umar II on Jihad: Best jihad is against one’s lowly desires
t: Ibn Muflih reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The best jihad is the jihad against whims.”

title: Ibrahim on Jihad: Most difficult jihad is against desires
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Ibrahim ibn Adham, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The most difficult jihad is the jihad against desire. Whoever can restrain his soul from its desires will be relieved from the world and its trials, and he will be protected and safe from its harms.”

title: Hadith on Farewell: I leave you to the protection of Allah
t: Salim reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, would say to a man if he intended to travel, “I bid you farewell as the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would bid farewell. The Prophet would say: I leave you under the protection of Allah in your religion, your trusts, and your final deeds.”
q: I leave you under the protection of Allah in your religion, your trusts, and your final deeds.

title: Hadith on Quran: Faith is given to a Muslim before Quran
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, I recite the Quran but I do not find that my heart understands it.” The Prophet said, “Verily, your heart is filled with faith, and faith is given to a servant before the Quran.”
q: Verily, your heart is filled with faith, and faith is given to a servant before the Quran.

title: Hadith on Faith: Companions learn faith before the Quran
t: Jundub ibn Abdullah reported: We were with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while we were strong young boys. We learned faith before we learned the Quran, then we learned the Quran and it strengthened our faith.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Poor enter Paradise long before the wealthy
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The poor Muslims will enter Paradise before the rich by half of a day, the length of which is like five hundred years.”
q: The poor Muslims will enter Paradise before the rich by half of a day, the length of which is like five hundred years

title: Layth on Dunya: Whoever cares for the world does not belong to Allah
t: Al-Ma’afi reported: Layth ibn Sulaim, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A servant does not draw closer to the ruler but that he moves further away from Allah. A servant does not gather more wealth but that his reckoning will be more severe. He does not gather a following but that he will gather more devils to himself. Whoever awakens with his greatest concern something besides Allah does not belong to Allah. Whoever is not concerned with the affairs of the Muslims does not belong to them.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Salat: You are in prayer as long as you remember Allah
t: Ibn Taymiyyah reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “As long as you remember Allah you are in prayer, even if you are in the market.”

title: Hadith on Quran: People of Allah’s Book are His chosen
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has His own people among humanity.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, who are they?” The Prophet said, “They are the people of the Quran, the people of Allah and His chosen ones.”
q: Verily, Allah has His own people among humanity. … They are the people of the Quran, the people of Allah and His chosen ones

title: Hadith on Ramadan: No make up fasts if broken accidentally
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever breaks his fast forgetfully in the month of Ramadan, there is no compensation or expiation for it.”
q: Whoever breaks his fast forgetfully in the month of Ramadan, there is no compensation or expiation for it.

title: Hadith on Loneliness: The Prophet forbids total social isolation
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited isolation, that a man spend the night alone or travel alone.

title: Hadith on Dua: Abu Bakr’s supplication for morning, evening, sleep
t: Abu Huraira reported: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O Messenger of Allah, instruct me with something to say in the mornings and evenings.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Say: O Allah, the Knower of the seen and the unseen, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, the Lord and Sovereign of everything, I testify there is no God but you. I seek refuge in You from the evil in myself, and the evil of Satan and his idolatry. Say it in the morning, the evening, and when you lie down for sleep.”
q: Say: O Allah, the Knower of the seen and the unseen, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, the Lord and Sovereign of everything, I testify there is no God but you. I seek refuge in You from the evil in myself, and the evil of Satan and his idolatry. Say it in the morning, the evening, and when you lie down for sleep.

title: Hadith on Fasting: Warning to those who break fast without excuse
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “While I was sleeping, two men came to me and took me by the arm to a rough mountain. They said: Climb up. I said: I am unable to do so. They said: We will make it easy for you. I climbed until I was halfway up the mountain and I heard loud voices. I said: What are these loud voices? They said: This is the howling of the people of Hellfire. Then, they departed with me until I saw some people hanging by their heels, the corners of their mouth split open and running with blood. I said: Who are these? They said: They are those who would break their fasting before it was complete.”
q: While I was sleeping, two men came to me and took me by the arm to a rough mountain. They said: Climb up. I said: I am unable to do so. They said: We will make it easy for you. I climbed until I was halfway up the mountain and I heard loud voices. I said: What are these loud voices? They said: This is the howling of the people of Hellfire. Then, they departed with me until I saw some people hanging by their heels, the corners of their mouth split open and running with blood. I said: Who are these? They said: They are those who would break their fasting before it was complete

title: Hadith on Quran: Hold fast to the rope of Allah
t: Abu Shurayh reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to them one day, saying, “Rejoice! Do you not witness that there is no God but Allah, and I am the Messenger of Allah?” They said yes. The Prophet said, “Verily, this Quran is a rope. One end is in the hand of Allah, and the other end is in your hands. Hold fast to it, for you will never be led astray or ruined ever again.”
q: Rejoice! Do you not witness that there is no God but Allah, and I am the Messenger of Allah? … Verily, this Quran is a rope. One end is in the hand of Allah, and the other end is in your hands. Hold fast to it, for you will never be led astray or ruined ever again.

title: Hadith on Haya: Modesty, speaking less are branches of faith
t:
Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Modesty and reticence are two branches of faith. Profanity and temerity are two branches of hypocrisy.”

Imam al-Tirmidhi commented, “Reticence is to speak little. Profanity is to speak obscenely. Temerity is to speak too often, such as those preachers who preach at great length and with eloquence, to be praised by people in what is not pleasing to Allah.”
q: Modesty and reticence are two branches of faith. Profanity and temerity are two branches of hypocrisy

title: Hadith on Islam: New Muslims forgiven for all previous sins
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a servant embraces Islam and practices his Islam well, Allah will record every good deed and erase every bad deed that he did prior to it. Thereafter he will be held accountable. A good deed will be counted as ten like it, up to seven hundred times. An evil deed will be counted as one like it, unless Allah Almighty overlooks it.”
q: When a servant embraces Islam and practices his Islam well, Allah will record every good deed and erase every bad deed that he did prior to it. Thereafter he will be held accountable. A good deed will be counted as ten like it, up to seven hundred times. An evil deed will be counted as one like it, unless Allah Almighty overlooks it

title: Hadith on Sales: Allah forgives those who cancel regretful sales
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever cancels the sale of a regretful Muslim, Allah will cancel his mistakes on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever cancels the sale of a … regretful Muslim, Allah will cancel his mistakes on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Abu Darda on Friends: Loneliness is better than an evil companion
t: Ibn Hibban reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “A righteous companion is better than loneliness, and loneliness is better than an evil companion. A good writer is better than one silent, and one silent is better than an evil writer.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Mercy: Allah’s forgiveness will surpass all expectations
t: ‘Awn ibn Abdullah reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Allah Almighty will certainly forgive on the Day of Resurrection, with such forgiveness as has never been conceived by the heart of any person.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Whoever complains to Allah, relief will come
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is afflicted by a pressing need and complains to people, his need will never be satisfied. Whoever is afflicted by a pressing need and complains to Allah, eventually Allah will provide for him, sooner or later.”
q: Whoever is afflicted by a pressing need and complains to people, his need will never be satisfied. Whoever is afflicted by a pressing need and complains to Allah, eventually Allah will provide for him, sooner or later

title: Hadith on Intercession: Allah has mercy on people who never did good
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah will certainly be praised on the Day of Resurrection by some people who never did any good. He will take them out of the Hellfire after they are burned and admit them into Paradise by His mercy, after the intercession of those who intercede.”
q: Allah will certainly be praised on the Day of Resurrection by some people who never did any good. He will take them out of the Hellfire after they are burned and admit them into Paradise by His mercy, after the intercession of those who intercede.
gf: Hasan li gharyihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Khayr: Allah sweetens him with good deeds
t: Surayj reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If Allah Almighty wills goodness for a servant, He sweetens him.” It was said, “What is his sweetness?” The Prophet said, “Allah Almighty opens the door of righteous deeds for him before his death and then receives his soul in that state.”
q: If Allah Almighty wills goodness for a servant, He sweetens him … Allah Almighty opens the door of righteous deeds for him before his death and then receives his soul in that state

title: Hassan on Salat: Difference between mindful and neglectful prayer
t: Al-Awza’i reported: Hassan ibn ‘Atiyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, people will be in prayer as one, yet the difference between them is like that between the heavens and earth. A man may be reverent and facing forward in his prayer, yet another is unmindful and neglectful.”

title: Umar on Desires: Muslim destroyed if prefers desires over religion
t: Mujahid reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O people, beware of gluttony in eating. Verily, it causes laziness in prayer, it harms the body, it contracts disease, and Allah Almighty detests the fatness of a cleric. Rather, you must be moderate in your provisions, for it is closer to righteousness, further from extravagance, and stronger for the worship of Allah. Verily, a servant is not destroyed unless he prefers his desires over his religion.”

title: Shafi’i on Masculinity: Four pillars of a true man
t: Al-Rabia’ reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Manhood is based upon four pillars: good character, generosity, humility, and cautious piety.”

title: Hadith on Marriage: Encouragement to stay married in old age
t: Al-Miqdam ibn Ma’di reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stood up for the people and praised Allah as is due to Him, saying, “Verily, Allah instructs you to treat women well, and again, Allah instructs you to treat women well, for they are your mothers, your daughters, and your aunts. A man from the People of the Book would stay married to a woman who owned not as much as a thread, neither of them finding the other attractive.”
q: Verily, Allah instructs you to treat women well, and again, Allah instructs you to treat women well, for they are your mothers, your daughters, and your aunts. A man from the People of the Book would stay married to a woman who owned not as much as a thread, neither of them finding the other attractive.

title: Hadith on Marriage: Husband should beautify himself for his wife
t: ‘Ikramah reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, I love to beautify myself for my wife, just as I love for her to beautify herself for me, due to the saying of Allah Almighty: They have rights similar to those over them.” (2:228)
q: They have rights similar to those over them

title: Hadith on Punishment: No corporal punishment if results in unjust death
t: Ali reported: A servant girl belonging to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, committed adultery and he ordered me to whip her. She was enduring post-natal bleeding and I feared that if I whipped her I would kill her. I mentioned that to the Prophet and he said, “You have done well.”
q: You have done well

title: Hadith on Rape: Compelled sex a type of criminal abuse
t: Salamah ibn al-Muhabbiq reported: A man had intercourse with the servant girl of his wife, so the matter was referred to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet said, “If she had done so willingly, then she belongs to him and he must pay the likes of her price. If he had forced her, then she is free and he must pay the likes of her price.”
q: If she had done so willingly, then she belongs to him and he must pay the likes of her price. If he had forced her, then she is free and he must pay the likes of her price.

title: Umar on Slaves: Slave injured by their master must be set free
t: Malik reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was presented with a servant woman who had been struck by her master with a piece of fire or had been injured by it, so he ordered him to emancipate her.

title: Umar on Slaves: Umm walad is emancipated when her master dies
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “When a servant woman gives birth from her master, then he may not sell her, or bestow her, or bequeath her. He may enjoy her and she becomes free when he dies.”

title: Hadith on Warning: The Prophet’s final warning to the Muslim nation
t: Ali reported: The final words of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, were, “The prayer, the prayer! Fear Allah regarding those under custodianship of your right hands!”
q: The prayer, the prayer! Fear Allah regarding those under custodianship of your right hands!

title: Hadith on Slaves: Do not torture slaves, whom Allah created
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is suitable for you among your slaves,  feed them from the same food you eat and clothe them from the same clothes you wear. Whoever is not suitable for you, sell them and do not torture the creation of Allah.”
q: Whoever is suitable for you among your slaves,  feed them from the same food you eat and clothe them from the same clothes you wear. Whoever is not suitable for you, sell them and do not torture the creation of Allah.

title: Umar on Servants: How can you prefer yourselves over your servants?
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by some people one day who were eating while their servants were standing. Umar said, “Why do I not see your servants eating with you? Do you not desire them?” A man said, “No, by Allah, O leader of the faithful. Rather, we have preference over them.” Umar became very angry, then he said, “What is the matter with people who prefer themselves over their servants? Allah Almighty will deal with them and it is done!” Then Umar said to the servants, “Sit down and eat.” The servants sat to eat and the leader of the faithful did not eat.

title: Salman on Servants: Salman helps his servant with the house chores
t: Abu Qilabah reported: A man entered the home of Salman, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was kneading dough. The man said, “What is this?” Salman said, “We sent out the servant on an errand and we dislike for him to have two tasks at once.”

title: Hadith on Maiming: The Prophet prohibits cruelty to slaves
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: Zinba’ Abi Rawh found his servant boy with a servant girl, so he maimed his nose and castrated him. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came afterward, and he said, “Who did this to you?” The boy said, “Zinba’.” The Prophet summoned Zinba’, and he said, “What made you do this?” Zinba’ said, “He was misbehaving in such a way.” The Prophet told the slave, “Go, for you are free.” Zinba’ said, “Am I not his guardian?” The Prophet said, “His guardian is Allah and His Messenger.”
q: Who did this to you … What made you do this … Go, for you are free … His guardian is Allah and His Messenger

title: Hadith on Sutrah: Protect prayer from disruption with barrier
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you stands for prayer, he is screened by a barrier if there is an object before him like the back of saddle. If there is nothing like the back of a saddle before him, his prayer is disrupted by the passing of a donkey, a woman, or a black dog.”
q: If one of you stands for prayer, he is screened by a barrier … if there is an object before him like the back of saddle. If there is nothing like the back of a saddle before him, his prayer is disrupted by the passing of a donkey, a woman, or a black dog.

title: Hadith on Dua: Allah shy to turn away a sincere prayer
