t: Salman al-Farsi reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is conscientious and generous. He would be shy, when a man raises his hands to Him, to turn them away empty and disappointed.”
q: Verily, Allah is conscientious and generous. He would be shy, when a man raises his hands to Him, to turn them away empty and disappointed

title: Hadith on Sun: The sun is under the control of Allah Almighty
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him when the sun had set, “Do you know where it has gone?” Abu Dharr said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Prophet said, “Verily, it has gone until it prostrates under the Throne. It seeks permission to rise and it is given permission. A time will come when it is about to prostrate and it will not be accepted from it. It will seek permission to rise and it will not be given permission. It will be said to it: Return from where you came. Thus, it will rise from the west. That is the saying of the Almighty: The sun runs upon its appointed term. That is the determination of the Mighty, the Knowing.” (36:38)
q: Do you know where it has gone … Verily, it has gone until it prostrates under the Throne. It seeks permission to rise and it is given permission. A time will come when it is about to prostrate and it will not be accepted from it. It will seek permission to rise and it will not be given permission. It will be said to it: Return from where you came. Thus, it will rise from the west. That is the saying of the Almighty: The sun runs upon its appointed term. That is the determination of the Mighty, the Knowing
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Sireen on Tyrants: Your sins worse for you than Ruler’s crimes
t: Al-Haytham ibn ‘Ubayd reported: Ibn Sirin, may Allah be pleased with him, heard a man cursing Al-Hajjaj, so he said, “Calm down, sir! When you arrive in the Hereafter, the smallest sins you committed will be worse for you than the greatest sins committed by Al-Hajjaj. Know that Allah judges with justice! If He takes something away from Al-Hajjaj because of his wrongdoing, He also gives back to Al-Hajjaj because he was wronged, so do not busy yourself with cursing him.”

title: Hadith on Women: Best men are best in character to women
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of you are those who are best to women.”
q: The best of you are those who are best to women

title: Sufyan on Ihsan: If public and private are equal, it is justice
t: Al-Mada’ini reported: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If one’s inner self is equal to one’s public self, that is justice. If one’s inner self is better than one’s public self, that is excellence. If one’s public self is better than one’s inner self, that is transgression.”

title: Hadith on Greed: If meat did not decay, the rich would hoard it
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Were is not for the children of Israel, meat would not spoil. Were it not for Eve, a wife would not betray her husband.”
q: Were is not for the children of Israel, meat would not spoil. Were it not for Eve, a wife would not betray her husband
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ibn Mas’ud: His shins weigh more than Uhud
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: He was harvesting toothsticks from an Arak tree and he had tiny shins. The wind blew and made him fall over, so people laughed at him. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “What are you laughing at?” They said, “O Prophet of Allah, he has tiny shins!” The Prophet said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, they will both be heavier on the Scale than the mountain of Uhud.”
q: What are you laughing at … By the One in whose hand is my soul, they will both be heavier on the Scale than the mountain of Uhud
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Dawud on Talaq: Worst men divorce their wives for trivial reasons
t: Raja’ reported: Dawud ibn Abi Hind, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I sat with the learned jurists and I found my religion with them. I sat with the preachers and I found softness in my heart. I sat with the elders of people and I found manhood among them. I sat with the worst of people and I found that one of them would divorce his wife for an offense that does not even amount to a hair.”

title: Ayyub on Manhood: Real men forgive others, overlook their faults
t: Abdullah ibn Shumayt reported: Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A man will not hit the mark, nor fulfill his manhood, until he has two characteristics: Forgiving people and overlooking their faults.”

title: Ahnaf on Manhood: True men are forbearing, forgiving
t: Al-Mada’ini reported: It was said to Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, may Allah have mercy on him, “What is manhood?” Al-Ahnaf said, “Forbearance at a time of anger, and forgiveness at a time of power.”

title: Hadith on Wine: Let him not sit at a table where wine is drank
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever has faith in Allah and the Last Day, let him not sit at a table over which wine is being served.”
q: Whoever has faith in Allah and the Last Day, let him not sit at a table over which wine is being served.

title: Hadith on Mosques: The Prophet lets women leave before himself
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would end prayer with salutations of peace and remain in his place for a while. The Prophet would end prayer and the women would depart to enter their homes before he would depart.

title: Hadith on Fajr: Women attend dawn prayer with the Prophet
t: Aisha reported: The believing women would pray the dawn prayer with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Then, they would return home wrapped in their mantles; they would not be recognized by anyone.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Prayer: Women leading their household in prayer
t: Umm Waraqah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would visit her in her house, he appointed a caller to prayer for her, and he ordered her to lead the people of her household in prayer. Abdur Rahman ibn Khallad said, “I saw her caller to prayer. He was an old man.”

title: Hadith on Mosques: The Prophet makes women’s door in Masjid
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It would be better if you had left this door to the mosque for women.” Nafi’ said, “Ibn Umar never again entered through it until the day he died.”
q: It would be better if you had left this door to the mosque for women.

title: Hadith on Mosques: Women having proper etiquette in the mosque
t: ‘Amrah bint Abdur Rahman reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “Were the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, to see what women are now doing, he would have prevented them from attending the mosque, just as the women of the children of Israel were prevented from attending.”

title: Abdullah on Jihad: Start with the jihad against your soul
t: Hannan ibn Kharija reported: I said to Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, may Allah be pleased with him, “What do you say about jihad and military campaigns?” Abdullah said, “Begin with your soul and wage jihad against it. Begin with your soul and wage a military campaign against it.”

title: Hadith on Women: Four best women in Paradise
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of women among the people of Paradise are Khadija bint Khuwaylid, Fatimah bint Muhammad, Maryam bint ‘Imran, and ‘Asiyah bint Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh.”
q: The best of women among the people of Paradise are Khadija bint Khuwaylid, Fatimah bint Muhammad, Maryam bint ‘Imran, and ‘Asiyah bint Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh

title: Hadith on Women: Allah reveals verses to include women
t: Umm ‘Umarah reported: She came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and she said, “I do not see anything but for men, and I do not see anything mentioned for women.” Thus, the verse was revealed, “Verily, the Muslim men and women, the believing men and women, the obedient men and women, the truthful men and women, the patient men and women, the humble men and women, the charitable men and women, the fasting men and women, the chaste men and women, the men and women who remember Allah often, Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.” (33:35)
q: Verily, the Muslim men and women, the believing men and women, the obedient men and women, the truthful men and women, the patient men and women, the humble men and women, the charitable men and women, the fasting men and women, the chaste men and women, the men and women who remember Allah often, Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.

title: Ibn Nadr on Men: Real manliness is smiling, kindness, caring
t: Ahmad ibn Jamil reported: Muhammad ibn al-Nadr, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The first part of manhood is a cheerful face. The second part is loving kindness to people. The third part is fulfilling the needs of others.”

title: Hadith on Dunya: Do not place your hopes in worldly life
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not be preoccupied with accumulating much wealth, such that you place your hope in the world.”
q: Do not be preoccupied with accumulating much wealth, such that you place your hope in the world

title: Hadith on Faith: Modest, simple living is part of faith
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, humble living is part of faith, humble living is part of faith,” meaning asceticism.
q: Verily, humble living is part of faith, humble living is part of faith,

title: Hadith on Contentment: Blessed is one satisfied with Islam
t: Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Blessed is one who is guided to Islam, whose livelihood is sufficient, and who is content with what he has.”
q: Blessed is one who is guided to Islam, whose livelihood is sufficient, and who is content with what he has.

title: Hadith on Signs: Lies, gluttony prevail before end of time
t: ‘Imran ibn Husayn reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of you belong to my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them. Verily, after you will come deceitful people who cannot be trusted. They will swear oaths without being asked to swear oaths, they will make vows they do not fulfill, and gluttony will prevail among them.”
q: The best of you belong to my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them. Verily, after you will come deceitful people who cannot be trusted. They will swear oaths without being asked to swear oaths, they will make vows they do not fulfill, and gluttony will prevail among them
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hajj: Proceed calmly during the pilgrimage
t: Ibn Abbas reported: He was riding with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, on the day of Arafat. The Prophet heard people behind him making a loud disturbance, striking and shouting at their camels. The Prophet pointed to them with his whip, and he said, “O people, you must be calm, for there is no righteousness in urgency.”
q: O people, you must be calm, for there is no righteousness in urgency

title: Hadith on Laughter: The Prophet was moderate, dignified in laughter
t: Aisha reported: I never saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, laughing so hard that one could see the back of his throat. Rather, he would only smile.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Food: The Prophet never filled his stomach with bread
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, left this world while he had never ate to his fill of barley bread.

title: Sufyan on Sabr: Believers need patience like food and water
t: Al-Humaydi reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The believer is in need of patience just as he is in need of food and drink.”

title: Hadith on Leadership: Regretful to desire leadership, authority
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, you may earnestly desire a position of leadership but you will regret it on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Verily, you may earnestly desire a position of leadership but you will regret it on the Day of Resurrection

title: Abu Ja’far on Gluttony: If stomach is full, body will sin
t: Ibn Abi Dunya reported: Abu Ja’far, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “When the belly is full, the body will transgress.”

title: Hadith on Hunger: The Prophet suffers from hunger all day
t: Umar reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, spend the entire day suffering from hunger. The Prophet could not find even the worst dates with which to fill his stomach.

title: Hadith on Gluttony: Charity better for you than eating too much
t: Ja’dah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saw a man with a large belly. The Prophet pointed to his belly and he said, “If this had been placed elsewhere, it would have been better for you.”
q: If this had been placed elsewhere, it would have been better for you

title: Umar on Gluttony: A large belly is a punishment, not a blessing
t: Al-Hasan reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, saw a man with a large belly and he said, “What is this?” The man said, “It is a blessing from Allah.” Umar said, “No, rather it is a punishment.”

title: Shafi’i on Knowledge: It is only knowledge if it benefits you
t: Al-Rabia’ reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Knowledge is not merely what is memorized. Knowledge is what benefits.”

title: Aisha on Gluttony: First trial among Muslims was eating too much
t: ‘Urwah reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “Verily, the first trial to occur in this nation after the passing of its Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was people eating to their fill. For when people fill their stomachs, their bodies are fattened, their hearts are hardened, and their desires are uncontrollable.”

title: Sahl on Spirituality: Four qualities which make a saint
t: Abu Talib al-Makki reported: Sahl al-Tustari, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “All good is combined in these four traits, and by them the righteous replacements became saints: having slender bellies, silence, sleeplessness, and withdrawing from people.”

title: Hadith on Hunger: The Prophet spent many nights hungry
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would spend several nights in a row with an empty stomach, and his family would not find anything for dinner. Most of their bread was made from barley.

title: Hadith on Bread: Caution against refined, processed white flour
t: Abu Hazm reported: He asked Sahl, “Did you see refined flour in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him?” Sahl said no. He said, “Would you sift the barley flour?” Sahl said, “No, but we would blow the husks from it.”

title: Hadith on Satiety: The Prophet never ate his fill unless with people
t: Malik ibn Dinar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, never ate to his fill of bread or meat unless he was eating with people.

title: Hadith on Food: The Prophet only ate his fill with guests
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, never combined a dish of his with meat and bread for lunch, nor for dinner, unless he was eating with a gathering of people.

title: Hadith on Gluttony: Those who overate will be hungry in Hereafter
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the people who ate to their fill in the world today will be the people of hunger in the Hereafter tomorrow.”
q: Verily, the people who ate to their fill in the world today will be the people of hunger in the Hereafter tomorrow

title: Hadith on Dua: An hour supplications are answered every night
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, there is an hour of the night in which a Muslim man does not ask for good in the affairs of the world and the Hereafter but that he is given it, and that is for every night.”
q: Verily, there is an hour of the night in which a Muslim man does not ask for good in the affairs of the world and the Hereafter but that he is given it, and that is for every night.

title: Hadith on Questions: Asking unnecessary questions arrogantly
t: Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among the most criminal of Muslims towards other Muslims are those who ask about a matter that is not forbidden, then it becomes forbidden for people due to his questioning.”
q: Among the most criminal of Muslims towards other Muslims are those who ask about a matter that is not forbidden, then it becomes forbidden for people due to his questioning.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Mubarak on Akhlaq: Good character is to abandon anger
t:
Ibn Rajab reported: It was said to Ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him, “Summarize good character for us in a single sentence.” Ibn al-Mubarak said, “Leave aside anger.”

Ibn Rajab said, “The same explanation was offered by Imam Ahmad and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, that good character is to leave aside anger.”

title: Hadith on Haya: Be modest before Allah as you would people
t: Sa’id ibn Yazid reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I enjoin you to be modest in front of Allah Almighty as you would be modest in front of a righteous man among your people.”
q: I enjoin you to be modest in front of Allah Almighty as you would be modest in front of a righteous man among your people

title: Umar on Humility: The woman is right, the man is wrong
t:
Abdur Rahman al-Salami reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Do not be excessive in the dowry of women.” A woman said, “It is not so, O Umar! For Allah said: You gave one of them a great amount” (4:20). Umar said, “Indeed, a woman has disputed Umar and she has defeated him.”

In another narration, Umar said, “The woman is right and the man is wrong.”

title: Hadith on Marriage: Lawful marriage must be announced publicly
t: Muhammad ibn Hatib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The difference between an unlawful and lawful marriage is the beating of drums and raising of voices.”
q: The difference between an unlawful and lawful marriage is the beating of drums and raising of voices

title: Umar on Zina: Secret marriage is a type of adultery
t: Abu al-Zubayr reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was presented with a marriage which no one had witnessed but one man and one woman. Umar said, “This is a secret marriage and I do not permit it. If I had known of it beforehand, I would have stoned them.”

title: Hadith on Marriage: Recommendation to have one wife only
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a man has two wives and he is not just between them, he will come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides collapsed.”
q: If a man has two wives and he is not just between them, he will come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides collapsed

title: Hadith on Miracles: Question the Prophet wished he had not asked
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I asked my Lord a question I wish I had not asked. I said: O Lord, there were messengers before me, among them those for whom you subordinated the wind and among them those who resurrected the dead. Allah said: Did I not find you as an orphan and give you refuge? Did I not find you lost and guided you? Have I not opened your heart and lifted your burdens? I said: Of course, O Lord.”
q: I asked my Lord a question I wish I had not asked. I said: O Lord, there were messengers before me, among them those for whom you subordinated the wind and among them those who resurrected the dead. Allah said: Did I not find you as an orphan and give you refuge? Did I not find you lost and guided you? Have I not opened your heart and lifted your burdens? I said: Of course, O Lord.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Allah praises one who cures his soul with ablution
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man from my nation arises in the night to treat himself with purification. There are knots over him. If he washes his hands, a knot is unraveled. If he washes his face, a knot is unraveled. If he wipes his head, a knot is unraveled. If he washes his feet, a knot is unraveled. Allah Almighty will say to those in the Unseen: Behold this servant of mine, treating his soul and asking from me. Whatever this servant of mine asks me, he will have it.”
q: A man from my nation arises in the night to treat himself with purification. There are knots over him. If he washes his hands, a knot is unraveled. If he washes his face, a knot is unraveled. If he wipes his head, a knot is unraveled. If he washes his feet, a knot is unraveled. Allah Almighty will say to those in the Unseen: Behold this servant of mine, treating his soul and asking from me. Whatever this servant of mine asks me, he will have it.”

title: Hadith on Parents: Not until our parents enter with us!
t: Shurjil ibn Shuf’ah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It will be said to children on the Day of Resurrection: Enter Paradise! They will say: Our Lord, not unless our fathers and mothers enter! Allah Almighty will say: Why do I see them hesitant? Enter Paradise! They will say: O Lord, our fathers and mothers! Allah will say: Enter Paradise, all of you with your parents!”
q: It will be said to children on the Day of Resurrection: Enter Paradise! They will say: Our Lord, not unless our fathers and mothers enter! Allah Almighty will say: Why do I see them hesitant? Enter Paradise! They will say: O Lord, our fathers and mothers! Allah will say: Enter Paradise, all of you with your parents!

title: Hadith on Rahmah: Rather, the gate of repentance and mercy
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Quraysh said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “Call upon your Lord to turn mount Safa into gold for us and we will have faith in you.” The Prophet said, “And you will do so?” They said yes. The Prophet supplicated to Allah and Gabriel came to him and he said, “Verily, your Lord Almighty greets you with peace. He says that if you wish, I will turn the mount of Safa into gold for them, but whoever among them disbelieves after that will be punished with a great punishment like no one else in the worlds. And if you wish, the door of repentance and mercy will be opened for them.” The Prophet said, “Rather, the door of repentance and mercy.”
q: And you will do so … Rather, the door of repentance and mercy

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for good at night is answered
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No Muslim retires for the night in a state of remembrance and purification, then wakes up in the night and asks Allah for goodness in the world and the Hereafter, except that he will be given it.”
q: No Muslim retires for the night in a state of remembrance and purification, then wakes up in the night and asks Allah for goodness in the world and the Hereafter, except that he will be given it

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication to say when waking up in night
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever wakes up in the night and says, ‘There is no God but Allah, alone without any partner. To Him belong the dominion and all praise, and He has power over all things. All praise is due to Allah, glory be to Allah, there is no God but Allah, Allah is the greatest, and there is no movement or might but by Allah,’ then he says, ‘O Allah, forgive me,’ or he supplicates to be answered, then if he performs ablution and prays, his prayer will be accepted.”
q: Whoever wakes up in the night and says, ‘There is no God but Allah, alone without any partner. To Him belong the dominion and all praise, and He has power over all things. All praise is due to Allah, glory be to Allah, there is no God but Allah, Allah is the greatest, and there is no movement or might but by Allah,’ then he says, ‘O Allah, forgive me,’ or he supplicates to be answered, then if he performs ablution and prays, his prayer will be accepted

title: Hadith on Imams: Most knowledgeable of Quran should lead prayer
t: Abu Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best versed in the recitation of the Quran should lead the prayer. If they are equal in their recitation, then the one most knowledgeable of them in the Sunnah. If are equal in knowledge of the Sunnah, then the one who first performed emigration. If they emigrated at the same time, then the one who first embraced Islam. No man should lead another man in prayer, nor sit in the honored place in his home, unless he has his permission.”
q: The best versed in the recitation of the Quran should lead the prayer. If they are equal in their recitation, then the one most knowledgeable of them in the Sunnah. If are equal in knowledge of the Sunnah, then the one who first performed emigration. If they emigrated at the same time, then the one who first embraced Islam. No man should lead another man in prayer, nor sit in the honored place in his home, unless he has his permission

title: Hadith on Faith: Allah is with you wherever you are
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among the best of faith is that you know Allah is with you wherever you are.”
q: Verily, among the best of faith is that you know Allah is with you wherever you are

title: Hadith on Sleep: Let him lie on his right side and say this
t: Abu Salih reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded us, when one intends to sleep, to lie on his right side and then say, “O Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the Great Throne, our Lord and the Lord of all things, the Splitter of the grain and seed, the Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Criterion (the Quran), I seek refuge in you from the evil of everything whose forelock you hold. O Allah, you are the First, there is nothing before you. You are the Last, there is nothing after you. You are the Manifest, there is nothing above you. You are the Hidden, there is nothing beyond you. Relinquish my debts and enrich me from poverty.”
q: O Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the Great Throne, our Lord and the Lord of all things, the Splitter of the grain and seed, the Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Criterion … I seek refuge in you from the evil of everything whose forelock you hold. O Allah, you are the First, there is nothing before you. You are the Last, there is nothing after you. You are the Manifest, there is nothing above you. You are the Hidden, there is nothing beyond you. Relinquish my debts and enrich me from poverty

title: Hadith on Salat: Allah in front of you when praying
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you is in prayer, let him not spit in front of himself, for Allah is in front of him as he prays.”
q: If one of you is in prayer, let him not spit in front of himself, for Allah is in front of him as he prays
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salat: Believer in private conversation with Allah in prayer
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the believer in prayer is in a private conversation with his Lord. Let him not spit in front of him, nor to his right side, but rather to his left side or beneath his feet.”
q: Verily, the believer in prayer is in a private conversation with his Lord. Let him not spit in front of him, nor to his right side, but rather to his left side or beneath his feet
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Akhirah: Allah will speak to you without translator
t: ‘Adi ibn Hatim reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are none among you but that his Lord will speak to him in the Hereafter without a translator between them, nor a veil to separate them.”
q: There are none among you but that his Lord will speak to him … in the Hereafter … without a translator between them, nor a veil to separate them
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Repentance: Allah laughs at two men in Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah laughs at two men, one of them killed the other, yet they both entered Paradise. This one fought in the way of Allah and was killed, then his killer repented and was also martyred.”
q: Allah laughs at two men, one of them killed the other, yet they both entered Paradise. This one fought in the way of Allah and was killed, then his killer repented and was also martyred
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Send mercy upon this pain, that it might pass
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever among you is afflicted with something, or his brother is afflicted, then let him say: Our Lord is Allah, who is in the heavens. Holy is Your name, Your command is in the heavens and on the earth. As Your mercy is in the heavens, place Your mercy upon the earth. Forgive our mistakes and our sins. You are the Lord of all who are good. Send down mercy from your mercy, healing from Your healing, upon this pain that it might pass.”
q: Whoever among you is afflicted with something, or his brother is afflicted, then let him say: Our Lord is Allah, who is in the heavens. Holy is Your name, Your command is in the heavens and on the earth. As Your mercy is in the heavens, place Your mercy upon the earth. Forgive our mistakes and our sins. You are the Lord of all who are good. Send down mercy from your mercy, healing from Your healing, upon this pain that it might pass.

title: Malik on Divinity: Attributes of Allah affirmed, modality unknown
t: Abdullah ibn Nafi’ reported: Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about the saying of Allah Almighty, “The Most Merciful rose above the Throne,” (20:5). The man said, “How is His rising?” Malik said, “The rising is acknowledged, its modality is unknown, and asking about it is an innovation. I see you are a man who intended evil with this question.”
q: The Most Merciful rose above the Throne

title: Hadith on Rajm: Verse of stoning not meant to be in Quran
t: Kathir ibn al-Salt reported: Amr ibn al-‘As and Zayd ibn Thabit would write down the Quran. They passed over this verse, and Zayd said, “I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: The married old man and old woman, if they commit adultery, then stone them irrevocably.” Umar said, “When this was revealed, I went to the Prophet and I said: Let me write it.” Shu’bah said, “It was as if the Prophet disliked that.” Umar said, “No doubt, you see that if an old man is unmarried, he is merely flogged, while if a youth commits adultery while married is stoned.”
q: The married old man and old woman, if they commit adultery, then stone them irrevocably.

title: Abu Darda on Marriage: Husband and wife should try to please each other
t: Ibrahim ibn Adham reported: Abu Darda said to his wife Umm Darda, may Allah be pleased with both of them, “If I become angry, then try to please me. If you become angry, then I will try to please you. Were we not to act this way, how quickly would we be separated!”

title: Ayyub on Fatwa: Most ignorant people quickest to issue verdicts
t: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah reported: Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The most daring of people to issue religious verdicts are those with the least knowledge of the disagreements of scholars. The most restrained of people from issuing religious verdicts are those with the most knowledge of the disagreements of scholars.”

title: Shafi’i on Nasihah: Sincere advice is given in private, not public
t: Al-Muzanni reported: Imam al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whoever admonishes his brother in private has been sincere to him and protected his reputation. Whoever admonishes him in public has humiliated him and betrayed him.”

title: Hadith on Milk: Blessing in pure organic grassfed cow’s milk
t: Tariq ibn Shihab reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty did not place an ailment but that He also placed its cure. You should drink the milk of cows, for they are invigorated by all kinds of plants.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty did not place an ailment but that He also placed its cure. You should drink the milk of cows, for they are invigorated by all kinds of plants
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Aqiqah: Sacrificing one sheep for each boy, girl
t:
Nafi’ reported: Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, was not asked by anyone from his family to provide a newborn celebration but that he would perform it. He would perform a newborn celebration for his child by sacrificing a sheep for each boy and girl.

Malik said, “The matter in which there is no disagreement among us regarding the newborn celebration, is that whoever performs it does so for his child by offering a sheep for each male and female. The newborn celebration is not an obligation, but rather it is recommended to act upon it.”

title: Hadith on Jama’ah: Pray with congregation, even if already prayed
t:
Yazid ibn Al-Aswad reported: I witness the Hajj pilgrimage with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and I prayed the dawn prayer with him in the mosque of Al-Khaif. When the Prophet finished his prayer and turned around, he saw two men in the back of the people who had not prayed with him. The Prophet said, “I must see them both.” I brought them while they were trembling with fear. The Prophet said, “What stopped you both from praying with us?” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, we had already prayed at our camp.” The Prophet said, “Do not do so. If you pray in your camp and then come to a congregation in the mosque, pray with them for it will be awarded to you as a voluntary deed.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “It is the opinion of more than one of the scholars and it was said by Sufyan al-Thawri, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq. They said if a man prays alone and then reached the congregation, he should repeat all of the prayers with the congregation.”
q: I must see them both … What stopped you both from praying with us? … Do not do so. If you pray in your camp and then come to a congregation in the mosque, pray with them for it will be awarded to you as a voluntary deed.

title: Umayr on Sahaba: I have not seen anyone easier than the Companions
t: Ibn ‘Awn reported: ‘Umayr ibn Ishaq, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I have met more companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, than anyone before me. I have not seen anyone more lenient in living, nor less harsh than them.”

title: Hadith on Salat: Pray in Masjid after Adhan is announced
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you are in the mosque and you are called to prayer, one of you should not leave until he has prayed.”
q: If you are in the mosque and you are called to prayer, one of you should not leave until he has prayed

title: Hadith on Dua: Two supplications rarely turned away
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two supplications are not rejected, or seldom rejected: the supplication at the call to prayer and at the time of the rain.”
q: Two supplications are not rejected, or seldom rejected: the supplication at the call to prayer and at the time of the rain

title: Hadith on Adhan: Repeat the call to prayer, then supplicate
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, the callers to prayer have been favored over us.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Say as they have said. When you have finished, ask Allah and you will receive.”
q: Say as they have said. When you have finished, ask Allah and you will receive.

title: Hadith on Prayer: Supplications during and after call to prayer
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you hear the caller to prayer, repeat what he says and then send blessings upon me. Verily, whoever sends blessings upon me, Allah will send blessings upon him ten times. Then, ask Allah to grant me the means of approach, for it is a station in Paradise not befitting but for one servant among the servants of Allah. I hope I am that one servant. Whoever asks Allah to grant me the means of approach, the intercession is permitted for him.”
q: When you hear the caller to prayer, repeat what he says and then send blessings upon me. Verily, whoever sends blessings upon me, Allah will send blessings upon him ten times. Then, ask Allah to grant me the means of approach … for it is a station in Paradise not befitting but for one servant among the servants of Allah. I hope I am that one servant. Whoever asks Allah to grant me the means of approach, the intercession is permitted for him

title: Hadith on Adhan: Raise your voice in call to prayer, even if alone
t: Abdullah ibn Abdur Rahman reported: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him, “I see you love sheep and the desert. When you are among your sheep or in your desert and announce the call to prayer, raise your voice with the call. Verily, the sound of the caller’s voice is not heard by any jinn, nor human, nor anything but that it will testify for him on the Day of Resurrection. I heard it from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.”

title: Hadith on Adhan: Caller to prayer taking wages for his call
t:
Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As reported: Among my last commitments to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, is that I would employ a caller to prayer who would not take wages for his call.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “This is acted upon by the people of knowledge. They discouraged the caller to prayer from taking wages for his call; they preferred the caller to seek reward from Allah for his call.”

title: Hadith on Salat: Angels pray with one who prays alone
t: Salman al-Farsi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a man is in a deserted land and the time of prayer arrives, let him perform ablution. If he does not find water, let him perform dry ablution. If he performs the prayer, two angels pray with him. If he announces the call to prayer and performs the prayer, behind him will be angels among the armies of Allah whose great numbers cannot be seen.”
q: If a man is in a deserted land and the time of prayer arrives, let him perform ablution. If he does not find water, let him perform dry ablution. If he performs the prayer, two angels pray with him. If he announces the call to prayer and performs the prayer, behind him will be angels among the armies of Allah whose great numbers cannot be seen

title: Hadith on Prayer: O Allah, guide the Imams and forgive the callers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Imam is responsible for the prayer and the caller to prayer is a trustee. O Allah, guide the Imams and forgive the callers.”
q: The Imam is responsible for the prayer and the caller to prayer is a trustee. O Allah, guide the Imams and forgive the callers.

title: Hadith on Adhan: Callers to prayer rewarded for all who hear
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the angels send blessings upon those in the first row of prayer. The caller to prayer is forgiven for as far as his voice reaches, and his truthfulness is affirmed by whichever creatures hear him, wet or dry. He will have a reward similar to those who pray with him.”
q: Verily, the angels send blessings upon those in the first row of prayer. The caller to prayer is forgiven for as far as his voice reaches, and his truthfulness is affirmed by whichever creatures hear him, wet or dry. He will have a reward similar to those who pray with him
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Marriage: Duty of husband to fulfill wife’s rights
t:
‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most worthy of conditions to fulfill in marriage are those that permit intimacy.”

Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, rights are at the intersection of conditions. You will have what you accepted as conditions.”
q: The most worthy of conditions to fulfill … in marriage … are those that permit intimacy
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Umar on Nikah: Muslims uphold conditions in marriage contracts
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Ghanm reported: I was sitting closely with Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. A man said, “O commander of the faithful, I married this woman and I accepted her condition that she would keep her house. I have settled my affairs such that I am moving residence to a new land.” Umar said, “She has her condition.” The man said, “She has ruined men! No woman wishes to divorce her husband, but she may do so?” Umar said, “The Muslims adhere to their conditions at the intersection of their rights.”

title: Hadith on Rahmah: The Prophet more merciful to us than ourselves
t:
Umaymah bint Ruqayqah reported: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, with a group of women. The Prophet said to us, “In so far as you are able and capable.” I said, “Allah and his messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves.” And I said, “O Messenger of Allah, accept our pledge,” meaning shake our hands. The Prophet said, “Verily, my statement to one hundred women is like my statement to one woman.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “Verily, I do not shake hands with women.”
q: In so far as you are able and capable … Verily, my statement to one hundred women is like my statement to one woman. … Verily, I do not shake hands with women

title: Hadith on Wudu: Wiping over socks and headgear in ablution
t: Bilal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, wiped over leather socks and head coverings in ablution.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Wiping socks invalidated by major impurity
t: Safwan ibn ‘Assal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered us when we were travelers to wipe over our leather socks and to not remove them for three days due to defecating, urinating, or sleeping, except to remove them in case of major impurity.

title: Ali on Deen: Religion is based on revelation, not opinion
t: ‘Abd Khayr reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “If the religion were based upon one’s opinion, one might expect the bottom of the leather sock to be wiped instead of the top. I have seen the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, wiping over the upper part of his leather socks.”

title: Hadith on Salat: Praying in clean shoes, sandals
t: Sa’id ibn Yazid reported: I asked Anas ibn Malik, “Did the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, pray in his sandals?” Anas said, “Yes.”

title: Hadith on Wudu: Wiping over non-leather socks, sandals
t:
Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, performed ablution by wiping over non-leather socks and sandals.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “It is the view of more than one of the scholars, as is said by Sufyan al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq. They said one may wipe over non-leather socks, even though they are not sandals, if they are thick.”

title: Hadith on Wudu: Wiping socks three days in travel, one day residency
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, permitted wiping over leather socks for three day and nights for the traveler, and one day and night for the resident.

title: Hadith on Gabriel: Angel avoid visiting the unkempt
t: Ibn Abbas reported: It was said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “O Messenger of Allah, Gabriel, upon him be peace, has been slow to come to you.” The Prophet said, “And why should he not be slow to come to me while you are around me without brushing your teeth, clipping your nails, shortening your mustaches, or cleaning your knuckles?”
q: And why should he not be slow to come to me while you are around me without brushing your teeth, clipping your nails, shortening your mustaches, or cleaning your knuckles

title: Hadith on Cleanliness: Display a dignified, pleasant appearance
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to us and he saw an unkempt man with disheveled hair. The Prophet said, “Could this man find nothing to groom his hair?” The Prophet saw another man with a dirty garment and he said, “Could this man find nothing to wash his garment?”
q: Could this man find nothing to groom his hair … Could this man find nothing to wash his garment

title: Hadith on Fitrah: Ten acts part of natural cleanliness
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Ten acts are part of natural instinct: trimming the moustache, letting the beard grow, using the toothstick, sniffing water into the nose, clipping the nails, washing the knuckles, removing hair from the underarms, shaving the pubic hair, and cleaning the private parts with water.” Mus’ab said, “I forgot the tenth, except that it might be rinsing the mouth.”
q: Ten acts are part of natural instinct: trimming the moustache, letting the beard grow, using the toothstick, sniffing water into the nose, clipping the nails, washing the knuckles, removing hair from the underarms, shaving the pubic hair, and cleaning the private parts with water.

title: Hadith on Ghusl: Take a bath at least once a week
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is a duty for Allah upon every Muslim to perform a ritual bath at least once every seven days, washing his head and his body.”
q: It is a duty for Allah upon every Muslim to perform a ritual bath at least once every seven days, washing his head and his body
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Adhan: Callers to prayer are masters on Judgment Day
t: Mu’awiyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The callers to prayer will have the longest necks of the people on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: The callers to prayer will have the longest necks of the people on the Day of Resurrection

title: Hadith on Perfume: The perfume of men and women
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The perfume of men is that which scent is apparent and color is hidden. The perfume of women is that which scent is hidden and color is apparent.”
q: The perfume of men is that which scent is apparent and color is hidden. The perfume of women is that which scent is hidden and color is apparent

title: Hadith on Sunan: The Prophets have four traditions
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are four traditions of the Messengers: Modesty, wearing fragrance, using the toothstick, and marriage.”
q: There are four traditions of the Messengers: Modesty, wearing fragrance, using the toothstick, and marriage

title: Hadith on Blessings: Allah blesses them as long as they give
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has people for whom He has assigned blessings to benefit His servants. He consolidates their blessings as long as they offer them to others. If they refuse to give them, He takes them away and directs them to others.”
q: Verily, Allah has people for whom He has assigned blessings to benefit His servants. He consolidates their blessings as long as they offer them to others. If they refuse to give them, He takes them away and directs them to others
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Yahya on Dunya: Worldly life is nothing to Allah, nothing to you
t: Abdullah ibn Sahl reported: Yahya ibn Mu’adh, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The world has no worth to its Lord, although he owns it. It should not be worthwhile to you, while you do not own it.”

title: Hadith on Tawaf: Circling the Ka’bah is like performing prayer
t:
Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Circling around the House is similar to prayer, except that you speak during it. Whoever speaks during it, let him speak nothing but goodness.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “This is practiced by the majority of scholars, that it is recommended for a man not to speak during circumambulation except for a need, to mention Allah, or to spread knowledge.”
q: Circling around the House … is similar to prayer, except that you speak during it. Whoever speaks during it, let him speak nothing but goodness

title: Hadith on Ease: The Prophet makes things easy for his nation
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Were it not hardship upon my nation, I would have commanded them to perform ablution with every prayer or to use the toothstick with every ablution. And I would have delayed the evening prayer until a third of the night.”
q: Were it not hardship upon my nation, I would have commanded them to perform ablution with every prayer or to use the toothstick with every ablution. And I would have delayed the evening prayer … until a third of the night.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: The Prophet remembers Allah all the time
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would remember Allah at all times.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Perform ablution if sleeping with major impurity
t: Aisha reported: If the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, intended to sleep while in a state of major ritual impurity, he would perform ablution before he slept.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Wudu: Ablution required before prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Prayer is not accepted from one in a state of minor impurity until he renews ablution.” A man from Hadhramaut said, “Abu Huraira, what is minor impurity?” Abu Huraira said, “It is passing wind or gas.”
q: Prayer is not accepted from one in a state of minor impurity … until he renews ablution
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sabr: Patient woman rewarded with Paradise
t: Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah reported: Ibn Abbas said to me, “Shall I not show you a woman of Paradise?” I said, “Of course.” Ibn Abbas said, “There was a dark-skinned woman who came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and she said: Indeed, I suffer seizures and I become uncovered, so supplicate to Allah for me. The Prophet said: If you wish you can be patient and have Paradise, or if you wish I will supplicate for Allah to heal you. She said: I will be patient, but supplicate to Allah that I will not become uncovered. Thus, the Prophet supplicated for her.”
q: If you wish you can be patient and have Paradise, or if you wish I will supplicate for Allah to heal you
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Wudu: Ablution invalidated by loss of consciousness
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, fainted and then regained consciousness, so he performed a ritual bath for prayer. Then, the Prophet fainted again and regained consciousness, so he performed a ritual bath for prayer.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Light sleep does not invalidate ablution
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would sleep lightly and then perform prayer without renewing ablution.

title: Hadith on Oppression: Injustice will be darkness on Judgment Day
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, oppression will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Verily, oppression will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: The Muslim is a brother to another Muslim
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Muslim is the brother of another Muslim. He does not wrong him, nor surrender him. Whoever fulfills the needs of his brother, Allah will fulfill his needs. Whoever relieves a Muslim from distress, Allah will relieve him from distress on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever covers the faults of a Muslim, Allah will cover his faults on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: The Muslim is the brother of another Muslim. He does not wrong him, nor surrender him. Whoever fulfills the needs of his brother, Allah will fulfill his needs. Whoever relieves a Muslim from distress, Allah will relieve him from distress on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever covers the faults of a Muslim, Allah will cover his faults on the Day of Resurrection
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Adab: The Prophet is polite to a vulgar, rude man
t: Aisha reported: A man sought permission to enter the home of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and when he saw him, the Prophet said, “A wretched brother of a hostile clan, a wretched son of a hostile clan.” When the man entered, the Prophet greeted him cheerfully and smiled at him. Aisha said, “O Messenger of Allah, you said what you said about him, but then you greeted him cheerfully and smiled at him.” The Prophet said, “O Aisha, have you ever known me to use foul language? Verily, the worst of people to Allah on the Day of Resurrection are those whom people avoid for fear of their evil.”
q: A wretched brother of a hostile clan, a wretched son of a hostile clan. … O Aisha, have you ever known me to use foul language? Verily, the worst of people to Allah on the Day of Resurrection are those whom people avoid for fear of their evil
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Curses: O Allah, have mercy on believers I cursed
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, I am only a human being. Whenever I scold, curse, or punish a Muslim man, then turn it into purification and mercy for him.”
q: O Allah, I am only a human being. Whenever I … scold, curse, or punish a Muslim man, then turn it into purification and mercy for him.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet’s night prayer routine
t: Shariq al-Hawzani reported: I entered the home of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and I asked her, “How did the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, begin his prayer when he awakened at night?” Aisha said, “When the Prophet awakened at night, he would exalt Allah ten times, praise Allah ten times, and glorify Allah with praises ten times. The Prophet would say ten times: Glory be to the King, the Holy. The Prophet would seek the forgiveness of Allah ten times and declare the oneness of Allah ten times. Then, the Prophet would say ten times: O Allah, I seek refuge in you from the confinement of the world and the confinement of the Day of Resurrection. Then, he would begin his prayer.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in you from the confinement of the world and the confinement of the Day of Resurrection

title: Ibn Samak on Death: I loved the believer, even if I fell short
t: Al-Ghazali reported: Ibn al-Samak, may Allah have mercy on him, said on his death bed, “O Allah, you know that if I disobeyed you, I still loved those who obeyed you. Make that a means of nearness to you.”

title: Hadith on Salaam: Better of them initiates greeting of peace
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is not lawful for a Muslim to boycott his brother for more than three nights, such that they meet each other and turn away. The better of the two is the one who initiates the greeting of peace.”
q: It is not lawful for a Muslim to boycott his brother for more than three nights, such that they meet each other and turn away. The better of the two is the one who initiates the greeting of peace
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Love: He will be in the Hereafter with those he loves
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man who loves a people but his deeds do not compare to theirs?” The Prophet said, “A person will be with those whom he loves.”
q: A person will be with those whom he loves
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Wudu: Performing multiple prayers with single ablution
t: Buraydah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed multiple prayers on the day of liberation with a single ablution and he wiped over his leather socks. Umar said to him, “You have done something today you have not used to do.” The Prophet said, “I have done it on purpose, O Umar.”
q: I have done it on purpose, O Umar

title: Hadith on Wudu: Performing ablution for every prayer
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would perform ablution at the time of every prayer. ‘Amr said, “How would you do so?” Anas said, “It is permissible for one of us to maintain ablution for multiple prayers, as long as he does not become ritually impure.”

title: Hadith on Cleanliness: Your Prophet taught you everything!
t: Salman reported: The idolaters said, “Indeed, your companion teaches you everything, even he teaches you how to defecate!” Salman said, “It is so. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited us from removing excrement using the right hand, or while facing the direction of prayer. The Prophet prohibited us from using dung or bones to do so, and he said not to use less than three stones.”

title: Hadith on Wudu: Amount of water used for ablution, ritual bathing
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would perform ablution with one mudd, or half of a kilogram, and would perform a ritual bath with one sa’, or two kilograms, up to five mudd.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hajj: We begin as Allah began in the Quran
t:
Jabir reported: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when he arrived in Mecca, circling the House seven times, and reciting the verse, “Take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer,” (2:125). The Prophet prayed behind the station, then he came to the black stone and greeted it. Then, the Prophet said, “We begin as Allah has began,” and he recited the verse, “Verily, Al-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.” (2:158).

Al-Tirmidhi said, “This is acted upon by the people of knowledge, that they would begin with Al-Safa before Al-Marwah.”
q: Take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer … We begin as Allah has began … Verily, Al-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah

title: Hadith on Wudu: Evidence continuity in ablution is obligatory
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: A man performed ablution and he left out a spot on his foot the size of a fingernail. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Go back and perform ablution well.” The man went back and then prayed.
q: Go back and perform ablution well

title: Hadith on Wudu: Wiping head and ears in ablution
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would wipe his head and his ears in ablution, both inner and outer parts.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Run fingers between fingers and toes in ablution
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you perform ablution, run your fingers between the fingers on your hands and your toes.”
q: When you perform ablution, run your fingers between the fingers on your hands and your toes.

title: Hadith on Wudu: Wiping ears with new water in ablution
t: Abdullah ibn Zaid reported: He saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, performing ablution and using water for his ears that was different from what he used for his head.

title: Hadith on Taharah: Wash hands on waking up, before ablution
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you awakens from sleep, do not let him dip his hands into the vessel until he washes them three times. Verily, he does not know where his hand spent the night.”
q: When one of you awakens from sleep, do not let him dip his hands into the vessel until he washes them three times. Verily, he does not know where his hand spent the night.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Wudu: Running fingers through thick beard in ablution
t:
Uthman ibn Affan reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would run his fingers through his beard during ablution.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “According to this, the majority of the people of knowledge among the companions of the Prophet, and those after them, hold the opinion that fingers should be run through the beard. It was said by Al-Shafi’i. Ahmad said if one overlooks running his fingers through the beard, it is still permitted.”

title: Hadith on Wudu: Perform acts of ablution three times each
t:
Ali reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would perform acts of ablution three times.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “This is acted upon by the majority of scholars, that it permissible to perform ablution with one act each, it is better to perform it with two acts each, and it is best to perform it with three acts each; there is nothing better after this.”

title: Hadith on Mindfulness: Beginning actions with the right side
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, liked to begin on his right side when putting on his shoes, combing his hair, performing his ablution, and in all of his affairs.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Bismillah: Reciting name of Allah to begin prayer
t:
Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as well as Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, would open the prayer by reciting, “All praise is due to Allah.” (1:1)

In the narration of Muslim, Anas said: I did not hear any of them recite aloud, “In the name of Allah, the Gracious, the Merciful.”
q: All praise is due to Allah … In the name of Allah, the Gracious, the Merciful
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tashahhud: Pointing the finger while sitting in prayer
t: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would point his finger when sitting in prayer and he would not move it.

title: Hadith on Dua: O Allah, make it blessed rain for us
t: Aisha reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saw rain, he would say, “O Allah, a beneficial downpour.”
q: O Allah, a beneficial downpour

title: Hadith on Salat: Description of position of hands in prayer
t: Wa’il ibn Hujr reported: He saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, raise his hands upon entering into prayer, exalting Allah, and Hammam described his hands as parallel to his ears. Then, the Prophet wrapped his hands in his cloak and placed his right hand over his left hand. When he intended to bow, he would take his hands out from his cloak, raise them, exalt Allah, and then bow. When the Prophet said, “Allah hears those who praise him,” he would raise his hands. When the Prophet prostrated, he prostrated between his two palms.
q: Allah hears those who praise him

title: Hadith on Masajid: Where are the neighbors of Allah?
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah will announce on the Day of Resurrection: Where are my neighbors? Where are my neighbors? The angels will say: Our Lord, who is befitting to be your neighbor? Allah will say: Where are those who filled the mosques?”
q: Allah will announce on the Day of Resurrection: Where are my neighbors? Where are my neighbors? The angels will say: Our Lord, who is befitting to be your neighbor? Allah will say: Where are those who filled the mosques?

title: Hadith on Nations: A nation that exploits the weak is never holy
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A nation will not be sanctified if the weak cannot take their rights without surmounting obstacles.”
q: A nation will not be sanctified if the weak cannot take their rights without surmounting obstacles.

title: Hadith on Salat: Sitting properly in prayer unless unable
t: Abdullah ibn Abdullah reported: I saw Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, sitting cross-legged in the prayer, so I did so too, as in that day I was young. Ibn Umar forbade me from doing it and he said, “Indeed, the Sunnah of prayer is to prop up the right foot and tuck the left foot.” I said, “But I saw you sitting cross-legged.” Ibn Umar said, “My feet cannot support me.”

title: Hadith on Utensils: Wash vessels of unbelievers if they eat pork, drink wine
t: Abu Tha’labah reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, we live in a land of the people of the Book. Can we eat from their utensils?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not eat from them unless you cannot find anything else, then wash them and eat from them.”
q: Do not eat from them unless you cannot find anything else, then wash them and eat from them
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Utensils: Using the dishware of idolaters if necessary
t: Imran ibn Hussein reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his companions performed ablution from the waterskin of an idolatrous woman.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salat: Description of raising the hands in prayer
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would raise his hands parallel to his shoulders when he entered into prayer, and when he exalted Allah for bowing. When he raised his head from bowing, he would likewise raise his hands and say, “Allah hears those who praise him. Our Lord, for you is praise.” The Prophet would not do so in the prostration.
q: Allah hears those who praise him. Our Lord, for you is praise.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Halal: No need to investigate food of Muslim host
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you enters the home of his brother Muslim, and he serves him food, let him eat his food and not ask him about it. If he serves him one of his drinks, let him drink from it and not ask about it.”
q: When one of you enters the home of his brother Muslim, and he serves him food, let him eat his food and not ask him about it. If he serves him one of his drinks, let him drink from it and not ask about it

title: Hadith on Mushaf: Ablution required before touching the Quran
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one should touch the Quran unless they are pure.”
q: No one should touch the Quran unless they are pure

title: Hadith on Taharah: Water is pure unless change in smell, taste, color
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Water is pure for ablution and nothing makes it impure.”
q: Water is pure for ablution and nothing makes it impure

title: Hadith on Marriage: Is my wife Aisha invited to dinner, too?
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had a Persian neighbour who would make good soup. He made some for the Prophet and then came to invite him. The Prophet said, “And this is my wife, Aisha.” The man said no, so the Prophet said no. The man returned another time and invited him. The Prophet said, “And this is my wife.” The man said no, so the Prophet said no. Then, the man returned another time and invited him. The Prophet said, “And this is my wife.” The man said yes on the third time. The two left together until they arrived at the man’s house.
q: And this is my wife, Aisha … And this is my wife … And this is my wife

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet corrects his companion gently
t: Abu Bakrah reported: He reached the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was bowing in prayer, so he bowed before joining the rows of prayer. It was mentioned to the Prophet, and he said, “May Allah increase your eagerness, but do not do so again.”
q: May Allah increase your eagerness, but do not do so again

title: Hadith on Wudu: No renewal of ablution after touching private parts
t:
Talq ibn ‘Ali reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about touching the private area and he said, “Is it not but a piece of flesh, or a part of you?”

Imam al-Tirmidhi commented, “It has been narrated from more than one of the companions and some of the successors that they did not see an obligation to perform ablution after touching the private area; it is the position of the scholars of Al-Kufah and Ibn al-Mubarak.”

title: Hadith on Travel: Prayer shortened to two cycles during travel
t: Ibn Umar reported: I accompanied the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and during travel he would not add more to his prayer than two cycles. Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman did likewise, may Allah be pleased with them.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Travel: Permission to shorten prayers during travel
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: We went out with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, from Medina to Mecca and he would pray two cycles at a time until he returned. Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq said, “How long did he remain in Mecca?” Anas said, “Ten days.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Worship: The Prophet advises three practices
t: Abu Huraira reported: My dear friend the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, advised me to do three deeds and I will never abandon them until I die: to fast three days of every month, to perform forenoon prayer, and to sleep after performing the Witr prayer.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Travel: The Prophet combined prayers during travel
t:
Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, combined sunset and evening prayers if he was undertaking a journey.

And Ibn Abbas said, “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, combined the noon prayers and afternoon prayers if he was on a journey, as well as combining the sunset and evening prayers.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salah: What if you forget how much you prayed?
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you doubts his prayer and does not know how much he has prayed, whether three or four cycles, then let him put aside his doubt and act upon what he is certain of. Then, perform two prostrations before he offers salutations of peace. If he had mistakenly prayed five cycles, the prostrations would make his prayer even. If he had prayed precisely four cycles, it would be humiliation for Satan.”
q: If one of you doubts his prayer and does not know how much he has prayed, whether three or four cycles … then let him put aside his doubt and act upon what he is certain of. Then, perform two prostrations before he offers salutations of peace. If he had … mistakenly … prayed five cycles, the prostrations would make his prayer even. If he had prayed precisely four cycles, it would be humiliation for Satan

title: Hadith on Salat: Pray on time if congregation is delayed
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “O Abu Dharr, how will you be if your leaders delay the prayer from its proper time, or let it die altogether?” I said, “What do you command me to do?” The Prophet said, “Perform the prayer in its proper time. Then, if you pray with them later, you will be rewarded for a voluntary deed.”
q: O Abu Dharr, how will you be if your leaders delay the prayer from its proper time, or let it die altogether … Perform the prayer in its proper time. Then, if you pray with them later, you will be rewarded for a voluntary deed.

title: Hasan on Good Will: The Prophet’s companions spread good will on Earth
t: Ibn Abi Dunya reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A man among the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you wish I will swear to you by Allah that the most beloved servants to Allah are those who cause Allah to be loved by his servants and who strive in the earth with good will.”

title: Ali on ‘Ilm: No good in silence on beneficial knowledge
t: Al-Razi reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “There is no good in silence when it comes to knowledge, just as there is no good in speaking when it comes to ignorance.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication of the distressed
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The supplication of the distressed is this: O Allah, I hope in Your mercy. Do not abandon me to myself, not even for a moment, and take care of all my affairs. There is no God but You.”
q: The supplication of the distressed is this: O Allah, I hope in Your mercy. Do not abandon me to myself, not even for a moment, and take care of all my affairs. There is no God but You

title: Mujahid on Service: I wanted to serve Ibn Umar, but he served me instead
t: Ibn Asakir reported: Mujahid said, “I accompanied Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, on a journey that I might serve him, yet it was he who served me.”

title: Abu Hanifa on Fear: Humble response when told to fear Allah
t: Al-Dhahabi reported: A man said to Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, “Fear Allah!” Abu Hanifa began to tremble, become pale, and lower his head, then he said, “May Allah reward you with good.”

title: Hadith on Iman: O Allah, adorn us with the beauty of faith
t: ‘Ammar ibn Yasar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, by Your knowledge of the Unseen and Your power over the creation, give me life as long as You know life is good for me and take me away if You know passing is better for me. O Allah, I ask You for fear of You in the Unseen and the seen. I ask You for truthful words in times of pleasure and anger. I ask You for moderation in times of poverty and wealth. I ask You for a blessing that will never expire. I ask You for comfort that will never end. I ask You for satisfaction after the decree of providence. I ask You for a soothing existence after death. I ask You for the sweetness of looking upon Your face and longing to meet You without enduring a harmful calamity nor a misguiding trial. O Allah, adorn us with the beauty of faith and make us guides to guide others.”
q: O Allah, by Your knowledge of the Unseen and Your power over the creation, give me life as long as You know life is good for me and take me away if You know passing is better for me. O Allah, I ask You for fear of You in the Unseen and the seen. I ask You for truthful words in times of pleasure and anger. I ask You for moderation in times of poverty and wealth. I ask You for a blessing that will never expire. I ask You for comfort that will never end. I ask You for satisfaction after the decree of providence. I ask You for a soothing existence after death. I ask You for the sweetness of looking upon Your face and longing to meet You without enduring a harmful calamity nor a misguiding trial. O Allah, adorn us with the beauty of faith and make us guides to guide others

title: Hadith on Hereafter: You do not know status of deceased
t: Anas reported: A man among the companions of the Prophet passed away, so another man said, “Receive glad tidings of Paradise!” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Certainly, you do not know for sure! Perhaps he spoke of what does not concern him, or he was miserly with what would not disadvantage him.”
q: Certainly, you do not know for sure! Perhaps he spoke of what does not concern him, or he was miserly with what would not disadvantage him
gf: Sahih li ghayri (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hasan on Malice: Sufficient evil to raise prices unjustly
t: Al-Bayhaqi reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It is enough malevolence against the Muslims that one desires to raise their prices.”

title: Hadith on Hoarding: Allah punishes those who hoard food
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever hoards food away from the Muslims, Allah will afflict him with leprosy and poverty.”
q: Whoever hoards food away from the Muslims, Allah will afflict him with leprosy and poverty

title: Hadith on Boycotts: Not enter Paradise together if divided
t: Hisham ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is not lawful for a Muslim to boycott another Muslim for longer than three nights.
