Verily, they are both diverting from the truth as long as they are divided. The first of them to return will have his sin expiated by his initiative in returning. If he greets him with peace and he does not accept it, and he rejects his offer of peace, the angels will respond to his greeting of peace and Satan will respond to the other. If they both die while they are divided, they will never enter Paradise together.”
q: It is not lawful for a Muslim to boycott another Muslim for longer than three nights. Verily, they are both diverting from the truth as long as they are divided. The first of them to return will have his sin expiated by his initiative in returning. If he greets him with peace and he does not accept it, and he rejects his offer of peace, the angels will respond to his greeting of peace and Satan will respond to the other. If they both die while they are divided, they will never enter Paradise together.

title: Hadith on Charity: Whoever awarded a good deed enters Paradise
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever removes a stone from the road, a good deed will be recorded for him. Whoever has done a good deed, he will enter Paradise.”
q: Whoever removes a stone from the road, a good deed will be recorded for him. Whoever has done a good deed, he will enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Speech: Speak as you like to be spoken to
t: Harmalah ibn Abdullah reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you command me to do?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Harmalah, do what is good and avoid what is evil. Consider what you are pleased to hear people say to you; when you stand to leave them, behave this way. Consider what you dislike to hear people say to you; when you stand to leave them, avoid doing it.” When I went back, I reflected on it and found that these two sayings did not leave anything out.
q: O Harmalah, do what is good and avoid what is evil. Consider what you are pleased to hear people say to you; when you stand to leave them, behave this way. Consider what you dislike to hear people say to you; when you stand to leave them, avoid doing it.

title: Hadith on Dua: I seek refuge in Allah from bad character
t: Qutbah ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, I seek refuge in you from evil character traits, evil deeds, and evil desires.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in you from evil character traits, evil deeds, and evil desires

title: Hadith on Death: One is relieved, and one is relieved from
t: Abu Qatadah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by a funeral and he said, “One is relieved and one is relieved from.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is one relieved and one relieved from?” The Prophet said, “The believing servant is relieved from the hardships and harms of the world to the mercy of Allah. The wicked are those from whom are relieved the servants, lands, trees, and creatures.”
q: One is relieved and one is relieved from … The believing servant is relieved from the hardships and harms of the world to the mercy of Allah. The wicked are those from whom are relieved the servants, lands, trees, and creatures.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Qayyim on Reason: Islam conforms to reason and nature
t:
Ibn al-Qayyim reported: It was said to one of the Bedouins who embraced Islam, when he recognized the call of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “What made you become a Muslim? What did you see in him that told you he is the Messenger of Allah?” The Bedouin said, “The Prophet did not command anything that my reason said should be prohibited. He did not prohibit anything that my reason said should be commanded. He did not allow anything that my reason said should be forbidden. And he did not forbid anything that my reason said should be allowed.”

Ibn al-Qayyim said, “Look at this Bedouin, his sound mind and his instincts, the strength of his faith, and his conclusion that the authenticity of the Prophet’s call is due to its correspondence with everything the mind knows is good.”

title: Abu Darda on Nifaq: Beware of hypocrisy of reverence, humility
t: Muhammad ibn Sa’d reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Seek refuge in Allah from the reverence of hypocrisy.” It was said, “What is the reverence of hypocrisy?” Abu Darda said, “It is that you see the body in reverence, but the heart is not reverent.”

title: Hadith on Community: Not a true Muslim who incites discord
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He is not one of us who instigates a wife against her husband, or a servant against his master.”
q: He is not one of us who instigates a wife against her husband, or a servant against his master.

title: Shafi’i on Brotherhood: Be brothers, even if you disagree on issues
t: Yunus al-Sadafi reported: I have not seen anyone wiser than Imam al-Shafi’i, may Allah be pleased with him. I argued with him one day over an issue and then we departed. He later met me and took my hand, then he said, “O Abu Musa, can we not continue to be brothers even if we disagree on an issue?”

title: Hadith on Polygamy: Do not marry second wife if first wife harmed
t: Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah reported: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say upon the pulpit, “Verily, the sons of Hisham ibn al-Mughirah have sought my permission to marry their daughters to Ali ibn Abi Talib. I do not give permission, again, I do not give permission, and again, I do not give permission unless Ali ibn Abi Talib intends to divorce my daughter and marry their daughters. Verily, she is only a part of me. I am upset by what upsets her, and I am harmed by what harms her.”
q: Verily, the sons of Hisham ibn al-Mughirah have sought my permission to marry their daughters to Ali ibn Abi Talib. I do not give permission, again, I do not give permission, and again, I do not give permission unless Ali ibn Abi Talib intends to divorce my daughter and marry their daughters. Verily, she is only a part of me. I am upset by what upsets her, and I am harmed by what harms her
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Wudu: Recommendation to mention Allah before ablution
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no prayer for one without ablution, and there is no ablution for one without mentioning the name of Allah before it.”
q: There is no prayer for one without ablution, and there is no ablution for one without mentioning the name of Allah before it.

title: Hadith on Women: Among greatest trials for men is women
t: Usamah ibn Zayd reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have not left a trial after me more harmful to men than women.”
q: I have not left a trial after me more harmful to men than women
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Mahram: Men and women should not mix in private
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever has faith in Allah and the Last Day, let him not be secluded with an unrelated woman without her guardian, lest Satan be the third of them.”

title: Ahmad on Sunnah: Do not blindly follow me, follow Hadith
t:
Ibn Abdul Barr reported: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Al-Awza’i had opinions, Malik had opinions, Sufyan al-Thawri had opinions. Each of them had opinions, and it is all the same to me. Indeed, the proof is only in the narrations.”

In another narration, Imam Ahmad said, “Do not uncritically follow me, nor Malik, nor Al-Thawri, nor Al-Awza’i. Rather, take from where they took.”

title: Abu Hanifa on Sunnah: Follow the Sunnah first, jurists second
t: Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi reported: Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said to his student Abu Yusuf one day, “Woe to you, O Ya’qub! Do not write down everything you hear from me. Indeed, I may have an opinion today and abandon it tomorrow, or I may have an opinion tomorrow and abandon it the day after tomorrow.”

title: Shafi’i on Sunnah: Leave my opinion if it contradicts Sunnah
t: Al-Nawawi reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If a prophetic narration is authenticated and it contradicts my opinion, act according to the narration and abandon my opinion.”

title: Hadith on Wudu: No ablution after kissing your spouse
t:
Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, kissed some of his wives and then left for prayer without renewing ablution. ‘Urwah said, “Who was she if not you?” And Aisha laughed.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “It is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri and the people of Kufa that there is no obligatory ablution after kissing.”

title: Hadith on Qiblah: Prayer direction between two cardinal directions
t:
Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whatever is between east and west is the direction of prayer.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “It has been narrated from more than one of the companions of the Prophet, that what is between east and west is the direction of prayer. Among them, Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Ibn Abbas. Ibn Umar said: If the west is on your right side and the east is on your left side, the direction of prayer is between them if you set it up.”
q: Whatever is between east and west is the direction of prayer

title: Hadith on Prayer: When the Prophet forgot ablution for prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The prayer had been prepared and the rows straightened, then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us. When he stood in his place of prayer, he remembered that he was in a state of ritual impurity (junub). The Prophet said to us, “Stay in your place.” Then, he went back inside to perform a ritual bath (ghusl) and then he came out to us with his hair dripping wet. The Prophet exalted Allah and we prayed with him.
q: Stay in your place.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jumu’ah: Supplications for the Prophet on Friday
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Increase your supplications for me on the day and night of Friday. Whoever blesses me once, Allah will bless him ten times.”
q: Increase your supplications for me on the day and night of Friday. Whoever blesses me once, Allah will bless him ten times.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Sincerity: Ask Allah to guide sinners, not curse them
t: Abu ‘Ubaydah reported: Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “If you see a man among you seduced into a sin, then neither supplicate to Allah against him nor curse him. Rather, supplicate for Allah to save him and to accept his repentance. When we saw a man do good at the end of his life, we would hope for him. When we saw a man do evil at the end of his life, we would fear for him.”

title: Mutarrif on Worship: Humble regret better than arrogant worship
t: Ahmad reported: Mutarrif, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “That I spend the night sleeping and awaken regretful is more beloved to me than to spend the night standing in prayer and awaken impressed with myself.”

title: Yahya on Dhikr: Poor are happier than rich if they remember Allah
t: Abu Nuaym reported: Yahya ibn Mu’adh, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, the poor only become happier than the rich due to remembrance, for they are in the custody of Allah. Were the siege of poverty to be lifted, you would find few of them stand firm in remembrance.”

title: Hadith on Tolerance: Be tolerant, Allah will be tolerant with you
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be tolerant and you will receive tolerance.”
q: Be tolerant and you will receive tolerance.

title: Hadith on Dua: O Allah, bring our hearts together
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, bring our hearts together, reconcile between us, guide us to ways of peace, and deliver us from darkness into light. Keep us away from immorality, outwardly and inwardly, and bless us in our hearing, our seeing, our hearts, our spouses, and our children. Accept our repentance, for You alone are the Relenting, the Merciful. Make us grateful for Your blessings, praising and accepting them, and give them to us in full.”
q: O Allah, bring our hearts together, reconcile between us, guide us to ways of peace, and deliver us from darkness into light. Keep us away from immorality, outwardly and inwardly, and bless us in our hearing, our seeing, our hearts, our spouses, and our children. Accept our repentance, for You alone are the Relenting, the Merciful. Make us grateful for Your blessings, praising and accepting them, and give them to us in full.

title: Hadith on Hudud: Pardon good people their faults, not crimes
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Overlook the faults of good people, except for legal punishments.”
q: Overlook the faults of good people, except for legal punishments

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: Only sins can ruin fellowship in Islam
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No two people loved one another for the sake of Allah Almighty, or for Islam, then separated from one another but that it was due to a sin one of them committed.”
q: No two people loved one another for the sake of Allah Almighty, or for Islam, then separated from one another but that it was due to a sin one of them committed

title: Hadith on Emancipation: Freeing slaves protects one from Hellfire
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever emancipates a believing slave, Allah will free every organ of his from Hellfire in equal measure.”
q: Whoever emancipates a believing slave, Allah will free every organ of his from Hellfire in equal measure

title: Hadith on Emancipation: Freeing slaves rewarded with protection from Hellfire
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whenever a Muslim man emancipates a Muslim man, he will be his freedom from Hellfire; he will be rewarded for every limb of his in equal measure. Whenever a Muslim man emancipates two Muslim women, they will be his freedom from Hellfire; he will be rewarded for every limb of theirs in equal measure. Whenever a Muslim woman emancipates a Muslim woman, she will be her freedom from Hellfire; she will be rewarded for every limb of hers in equal measure.”
q: Whenever a Muslim man emancipates a Muslim man, he will be his freedom from Hellfire; he will be rewarded for every limb of his in equal measure. Whenever a Muslim man emancipates two Muslim women, they will be his freedom from Hellfire; he will be rewarded for every limb of theirs in equal measure. Whenever a Muslim woman emancipates a Muslim woman, she will be her freedom from Hellfire; she will be rewarded for every limb of hers in equal measure

title: Hadith on Orphans: Care for the orphans, free the slaves
t: Malik ibn Al-Harith reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever embraces an orphan of two Muslim parents by feeding him and giving him drink until he is independent of him, Paradise will certainly be necessary for him. Whoever emancipates a Muslim man, he will be his freedom from the Hellfire; he will be rewarded for every limb of his in equal measure.”
q: Whoever embraces an orphan of two Muslim parents by feeding him and giving him drink until he is independent of him, Paradise will certainly be necessary for him. Whoever emancipates a Muslim man, he will be his freedom from the Hellfire; he will be rewarded for every limb of his in equal measure.
gf: Sahih li ghayri (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Sufyan on Sins: Hope for repentance, fear for sins
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whoever commits a sin due to desire, hope for his repentance. Verily, Adam, upon him be peace, disobeyed due to desire and he was forgiven. If a sin is committed due to pride, fear that the perpetrator may be cursed. Verily, Iblis disobeyed due to pride and he was cursed.”

title: Hadith on Nikah: Declare marriage in public, not in secret
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Announce this marriage publicly, conduct it in the mosque, and strike the drums for it.”
q: Announce this marriage publicly, conduct it in the mosque, and strike the drums for it.

title: Ibn Umar on Taqwa: Peak righteousness is a clear conscience
t: Al-Bukhari reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The servant will not reach the level of true righteousness until he leaves what wavers in his heart.”

title: Hadith on Taxes: Cheating tax collector will enter Hellfire
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The unjust tax collector will not enter Paradise.”
q: The unjust tax collector will not enter Paradise

title: Fudayl on Virtue: What is humility? What is patience?
t: Ibrahim ibn al-Ash’at reported: I asked Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, “What is humility?” Al-Fudayl said, “It is to humble yourself for the truth, to act in accordance with it, and to accept it even if you hear it from a child.” I asked, “What is patience with calamity?” Al-Fudayl said, “It is to not publicize your complaint.”

title: Hadith on Prayer: Four cycles of Salat al-Duha
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: Son of Adam, bow to Me in four cycles of prayer at the beginning of the day and I will suffice you for the rest of it.”
q: Allah Almighty said: Son of Adam, bow to Me in four cycles of prayer … at the beginning of the day and I will suffice you for the rest of it

title: Hadith on Mala’ikah: Angels worshiping and glorifying Allah
t: ‘Adi ibn Artah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty has angels whose limbs shudder from fear of him. No angel among them sheds a tear from his eye but that it falls upon another angel glorifying Allah.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty has angels whose limbs shudder from fear of him. … No angel among them sheds a tear from his eye but that it falls upon another angel glorifying Allah

title: Hadith on Charity: Allah helps him as long as he helps others
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah continues to fulfill the needs of the servant as long as he fulfills the needs of his brother.”
q: Allah continues to fulfill the needs of the servant as long as he fulfills the needs of his brother.
gf: Sahih li ghayri (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Yahya on Akhirah: Seek Hereafter only, you will get the world
t: Ibn al-Jawzi reported: Yahya ibn Mu’adh, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “O son of Adam, you seek the world as one seeks what he must have, and you seek the Hereafter as one who has no need of it. The world will suffice you as long as you do not seek it, yet by seeking the Hereafter you will acquire it. Thus, understand your affair.”

title: Sufyan on Sin: Backbiting is worse than fornication, drinking wine
t: Al-Bayhaqi reported: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Backbiting is worse to Allah than fornication and drinking wine, as fornication and drinking wine is a sin between you and your Lord. If you repent from them, Allah will accept your repentance. Yet backbiting is not forgiven unless the victim forgives you.”

title: Hadith on Teaching: Allah sent me to be a gentle teacher
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah did not send me to be harsh or obstinate, rather He sent me to teach and to put at ease.”
q: Verily, Allah did not send me to be harsh or obstinate, rather He sent me to teach and to put at ease

title: Hadith on Dreams: Prophets dream lucidly, their hearts are awake
t: ‘Ata’ reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, we among the prophets, our eyes will sleep yet our hearts do not sleep.”
q: Verily, we among the prophets, our eyes will sleep yet our hearts do not sleep.

title: Hadith on Flattery: Beware of exaggerating praise of others
t: Al-Miqdad reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you see those who flatter others, throw sand in their faces.”
q: When you see those who flatter others, throw sand in their faces

title: Hadith on Qiblah: Those who pray towards Mecca are Muslims
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever performs our prayer, faces our direction of prayer, and eats our slaughtered animals, they are Muslims under the protection of Allah and His Messenger. Thus, do not betray Allah in the matter of His protection.”
q: Whoever performs our prayer, faces our direction of prayer … and eats our slaughtered animals, they are Muslims under the protection of Allah and His Messenger. Thus, do not betray Allah in the matter of His protection

title: Hadith on Waswas: Angels suggest good, devils suggest evil
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Satan influences the son of Adam and so does the angel. As for the influence of Satan, he threatens evil and denies the truth. As for the influence of the angel, he promises goodness and affirms the truth. Whoever finds this goodness, let him know it is from Allah, and let him praise Allah. Whoever finds something else, let him seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “Satan threatens you with poverty and commands evil, but Allah promises you forgiveness and grace from Him.” (2:268)
q: Verily, Satan influences the son of Adam and so does the angel. As for the influence of Satan, he threatens evil and denies the truth. As for the influence of the angel, he promises goodness and affirms the truth. Whoever finds this goodness, let him know it is from Allah, and let him praise Allah. Whoever finds something else, let him seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. … Satan threatens you with poverty and commands evil, but Allah promises you forgiveness and grace from Him

title: Abu Umamah on Backbiting: Good deeds given to believers backbitten
t: Al-Samarqandi reported: Abu Umamah al-Bahili, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, the servant will be given his record on the Day of Resurrection and he will see good deeds that he had not done. He will say: O Lord, from where does these come? Allah will say: These are from people who had backbitten against you while you were unaware.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Prayer: Modest prayers with mindfulness are better
t: Ibn al-Mubarak reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Two moderate cycles of prayer in contemplation are better than praying the whole night with a neglectful heart.”

title: Qushayri on Mindfulness: Hope leads to good deeds, away from sins
t: Al-Qushayri reported: Al-Nasrabadhi, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Hope motivates you to acts of obedience, and fear leads you away from acts of disobedience. Mindfulness leads to pathways of truth.”

title: Sa’d on Wealth: Never enriched by wealth if not content with Allah
t: Ibn Qutaybah reported: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, said to his son Umar, “O my son, when you seek richness, seek it in contentment. For if you are not content, wealth will never enrich you.”

title: Hadith on Dress: The Prophet agrees with People of the Book
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would let his hair hang down, while the idolaters would part their hair. The People of the Book would let their hair hang down, and the Prophet liked to agree with the People of the Book in matters for which he received no divine commandments. Then, later on he would part his hair.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet’s supplication for sleep, waking up
t: Hudhayfah reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, laid down at night, he would place his hand under his cheek and then say, “O Allah, in Your name I die and I live.” When the Prophet would awaken, he would say, “All praise is due to Allah, who has given us life after our death, and unto Him is the Resurrection.”
q: O Allah, in Your name I die and I live … All praise is due to Allah, who has given us life after our death, and unto Him is the Resurrection.

title: Salman on Silence: Speak truth or be silent, do not be angry
t: Maymun ibn Mihran reported: A man came to Salman al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said, “O Abu Abdullah, advise me.” Salman said, “Do not speak.” The man said, “How can one live among people and not speak?” Salman said, “If you speak, speak the truth or be silent.” The man said, “Tell me more.” Salman said, “Do not be angry.” The man said, “You have commanded me not to be angry, yet it overcomes me in a way I cannot control.” Salman said, “If you are angry, restrain your tongue and your hand.” The man said, “Tell me more.” Salman said, “Do not mix with people.” The man said, “How can one live among people and not mix with them?” Salman said, “If you mix with people, speak truthfully and fulfill the trust.”

title: Wahb on Health: Foundation of health is diet, wisdom is silence
t: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad reported: Wahb ibn Munabbih, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The doctors agreed that the head of medicine is diet. The wise men agreed that the head of wisdom is silence.”

title: Abu Sa’id on Silence: By silence you will overcome the Devil
t: ‘Aqil ibn Mudrik reported: A man said to Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, “Advise me.” Abu Sa’id said, “You must be silent except in the truth, for by it you will defeat Satan.”

title: Hadith on Dignity: Calm manners are a part of Prophethood
t: Abdullah ibn Sarjis reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Good composure, consideration, and moderation are among the twenty-four parts of prophecy.”
q: Good composure, consideration, and moderation are among the twenty-four parts of prophecy

title: Hadith on Silence: The Prophet was often silent, sometimes laughed
t: Simak reported: I said to Jabir ibn Samrah, “Have you sat with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him?” Jabir said, “Yes, and he would observe silence for long periods of time and seldom laugh. His companions would mention poetry in his presence and some of their affairs. They would laugh and smile at times.”

title: Qushayri on Mindfulness: Being present in the moment
t: Al-Qushayri reported: Abu Bakr al-Farisi, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about the practice of inward silence and he said, “It is to abandon preoccupation with the past and the future.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Allah responds directly to supplications
t: Anas reported: A bedouin came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me what is good.” The Prophet took him by the hand and he said, “Say: Glory be to Allah, all praise is due to Allah, there is no God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest.” The bedouin committed to what was in his hand and he went on his way. He reflected upon it and then returned. The Prophet smiled and said, “One in need has reflected and came back.” The bedouin said, “O Messenger of Allah, glory be to Allah, all praise is due to Allah, there is no God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest, these words are for Allah. What is for me?” The Prophet said, “O bedouin, when you say glory be to Allah, Allah says: He is truthful. When you say all praise is due to Allah, Allah says: He is truthful. When you say there is no God but Allah, Allah says: He is truthful. When you say Allah is the greatest, Allah says: He is truthful. When you ask Allah to forgive you, Allah says: I have done so. When you ask Allah to have mercy upon you, Allah says: I have done so. When you ask Allah to provide for you, Allah says: I have done so.” The bedouin committed himself to the seven sayings in his hand, then he returned on his way.
q: Say: Glory be to Allah, all praise is due to Allah, there is no God but Allah, and Allah is the greatest … One in need has reflected and came back … O bedouin, when you say glory be to Allah, Allah says: He is truthful. When you say all praise is due to Allah, Allah says: He is truthful. When you say there is no God but Allah, Allah says: He is truthful. When you say Allah is the greatest, Allah says: He is truthful. When you ask Allah to forgive you, Allah says: I have done so. When you ask Allah to have mercy upon you, Allah says: I have done so. When you ask Allah to provide for you, Allah says: I have done so.

title: Urwah on Trust: No faith for one who cannot be trusted
t: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah reported: ‘Urwah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Be not deceived by the prayer of a man, nor by his fasting. Whoever wills can fast and whoever wills can pray, yet there is no religion for one who cannot be trusted.”

title: Hadith on Wudu: Angels bless those who sleep with ablution
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Purify these bodies of yours, that Allah may purify you. No servant retires for the night in a state of purity but that an angel resides with him in his bed. Every time he turns about for an hour, the angel says: O Allah, forgive your servant, as he has retired in a state of purity.”
q: Purify these bodies of yours, that Allah may purify you. No servant retires for the night in a state of purity but that an angel resides with him in his bed. Every time he turns about for an hour, the angel says: O Allah, forgive your servant, as he has retired in a state of purity

title: Ibn Sirin on Sin: Biggest sinners mention other people’s sins
t: Hisham ibn Hassan reported: Muhammad ibn Sirin, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “We used to say that people with the most faults are the quickest of them to mention the faults of others.”

title: Hadith on Water: Best charity is giving water to thirsty people
t: Sa’d ibn ‘Ubadah reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, my mother has died. Shall I give charity on her behalf?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Yes.” I said, “Which charity is best?” The Prophet said, “A drink of water.”
q: Yes … A drink of water

title: Sufyan on Sins: To sin against people is more severe to Allah
t: Al-Samarqandi reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “For you to meet Allah Almighty with seventy sins between you and Allah would be easier on you than to meet Him with a single sin between you and His servants.”

title: Umar on Dua: I am harsh, so make me gentle
t: Shaddad ibn Aws reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O Allah, I am weak, so make me strong. I am harsh, so make me gentle. I am miserly, so make me generous.”

title: Amr on Hypocrisy: He sees a speck in his eye, not a log in his own
t: Ali ibn Rabah reported: Amr ibn al-‘As, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “I am bewildered by a man who flees from the divine decree and is in battle with it. He sees the mote in the eye of his brother, yet he places a beam in his own eye. He brings out resentment in the soul of his brother, yet places resentment within his own self.”

title: Abu Darda on Reciprocity: As you judge others, so you are judged
t: Abu Qilabah reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Be as you will, for as you judge you shall be judged.”

title: Hadith on Fitnah: If no Muslim leader, withdraw from all sects
t: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman reported: The people used to ask the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about good, but I would ask him about evil for fear it would overtake me. I said, “O Messenger of Allah, we were in ignorance and evil, but then Allah sent us this good. Will there be evil after this good?” The Prophet said, “Yes.” I said, “Will there be good after that evil?” The Prophet said, “Yes, but within it is smog.” I said, “What is its smog?” The Prophet said, “Some people will not be guided by my guidance. You will recognize them and reject them.” I said, “Will there be evil after that good?” The Prophet said, “Yes, callers to the gates of Hellfire. Whoever answers them will taste it therein.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, describe them to us.” The Prophet said, “They are from our ethnicity and speak our language.” I said, “What do you order me to do should that overtake me?” The Prophet said, “Hold fast to the community of Muslims and their leader.” I said, “What if there is no community and no leader?” The Prophet said, “Then withdraw from all of these sects, even if you must gnaw at tree roots until death overtakes you while doing so.”
q: Yes … Yes, but within it is smog … Some people will not be guided by my guidance. You will recognize them and reject them … Yes, callers to the gates of Hellfire. Whoever answers them will taste it therein … They are from our ethnicity and speak our language. … Hold fast to the community of Muslims and their leader … Then withdraw from all of these sects, even if you must gnaw at tree roots until death overtakes you while doing so
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: ‘Urwah on Torah: Gentleness, mercy are head of wisdom
t: Ibn Abi Shaybah reported: ‘Urwah, may Allah have mercy on him said, “It has reached me that it is written in the Torah: As you give mercy you will receive mercy. And it has reached me that it is written in the Torah: Gentleness is the head of wisdom.”

title: Kattani on Nafs: True strength is to properly manage one’s self
t: Mansur ibn Abdullah reported: Al-Kattani, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The truly weak man is he who is too weak to manage himself.”

title: Abu Darda on Wisdom: Silence is wisdom, but few practice it
t: Ibn Abdul Barr reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Silence is a form of wisdom, yet few people practice it.”

title: Hadith on Gratitude: Best wealth is thankfulness, a righteous spouse
t: Thawban reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best wealth is a tongue that remembers Allah, a grateful heart, and a believing wife to help one in his faith.”
q: The best wealth is a tongue that remembers Allah, a grateful heart, and a believing wife to help one in his faith

title: Hadith on Hijab: Men must respect women, not stare at them
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Al-Fadl was riding with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and a woman from Khash’am came. Al-Fadl began to stare at her and she stared at him. The Prophet made Al-Fadl turn his face in the other direction.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Sa’id on Hilm: A real man does not disparage others
t: Ibn Abi Dunya reported: Sa’id ibn al-‘As, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I have not insulted a man ever since I became a man.”

title: Hadith on Clothes: Wearing the clothing of unbelievers
t: Al-Mughirah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, wore a Roman coat with tight sleeves.

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Muslims flee to the mountains, escaping persecution
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Soon the best property of a Muslim will be a flock of sheep he takes to the top of a mountain, or in the valleys of rainfall, fleeing with his religion from tribulations.”
q: Soon the best property of a Muslim will be a flock of sheep he takes to the top of a mountain, or in the valleys of rainfall, fleeing with his religion from tribulations

title: Hadith on Sham: If Syrians are corrupt, Ummah is corrupt
t: Qurrah ibn Iyas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If the people of Syria are corrupted, there will be no good in you. A group among my nation will continue to be supported, unharmed by those who fail them until the establishment of the Hour.”
q: If the people of Syria … are corrupted, there will be no good in you. A group among my nation will continue to be supported, unharmed by those who fail them until the establishment of the Hour

title: Hadith on Recitation: Surat al-Fatihah is enough, more is better
t: Ata’ reported: Abu Huraira, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “In every prayer is a recitation. Prayers that were recited aloud by the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, we have recited aloud to you, and what he recited silently, we have kept silent with you. Whoever recites the foundation of the Book, Surat al-Fatihah, has done enough, but to recite more is better.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Quran: Ask only from Allah with the Quran
t: ‘Imran ibn Husayn reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever reads the Quran, let him ask Allah by it. Verily, people will come who recite the Quran and ask people by it.”
q: Whoever reads the Quran, let him ask Allah by it. Verily, people will come who recite the Quran and ask people by it.
gf: Sahih li ghayri (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Salat: Pray two raka’at when entering, leaving home
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you leave your home, pray two cycles to prevent you from an evil exit. When you enter your home, pray two cycles to prevent you from an evil entrance.”
q: When you leave your home, pray two cycles … to prevent you from an evil exit. When you enter your home, pray two cycles to prevent you from an evil entrance.

title: Hadith on Shakk: Even Prophets must overcome their doubts
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “We are more likely to doubt than Abraham, when he said: Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. Allah said: Do you not have faith? Abraham said: Of course, but rather to put my heart at rest.” (2:260)
q: We are more likely to doubt than Abraham, when he said: Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. Allah said: Do you not have faith? Abraham said: Of course, but rather to put my heart at rest.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Eid: Wear your best clothes on Eid
t: Nafi’ reported: Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, would wear his best clothes on the days of the two Eids.

title: Ja’far on Akhirah: Worry about the Hereafter is light in the heart
t: Ibn al-Mubarak reported: Ja’far ibn Sulaiman, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Concern about the world is a darkness in the heart, and concern about the Hereafter is a light in the heart.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Ramadan: Pregnant women have permission to break fast
t: Sa’id ibn Jubayr reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “If a pregnant woman fears for herself and the nursing of her child during Ramadan, she should break her fast and in place of each day feed a poor person. She does not need to make up the fasts.”

title: Umar on Truth: Guide me to the truth, to follow it
t: Al-Buhuti reported: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O Allah, show me the truth as truth and guide me to follow it. Show me the false as false and guide me to avoid it.”

title: Hadith on Mushaf: Let him read the written Quran
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever would be pleased to love Allah and his messenger, let him read from the written Quran.”
q: Whoever would be pleased to love Allah and his messenger, let him read from the written Quran

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Remove from Hell all who remembered Allah
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah will say: Take out from the Hellfire whoever remembered Me for a day, or who feared to stand before Me.”
q: Allah will say: Take out from the Hellfire whoever remembered Me for a day, or who feared to stand before Me

title: Ka’b on Mercy: Blessed are those who are merciful to creation
t: Ka’b reported: Allah Almighty said to Moses, upon him be peace, “O Moses, be soft in nature, for the most abhorred creation to me is one within whom is arrogance, in whose tongue is sharpness, and in whose heart is hardness. The most beloved character traits to me are mercy, compassion, kindness, and gentleness. O Moses, be merciful to my creation and I will have mercy on you. O Moses, I am merciful and I love those who are merciful. Blessed are those who are merciful. Again, blessed are those who are merciful. And again, blessed are those who are merciful.”

title: Khalid on Haste: Hurry to good before you lose an opportunity
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Khalid ibn Ma’dan, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If a door of good is open for one of you, let him rush to it. He does not know when it will be closed to him.”

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Time of few scholars, many preachers
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, you are in a time of many scholars and few preachers. Whoever leaves a tenth of what he knows will be ruined. There will come a time for people of few scholars and many preachers. Whoever adheres to a tenth of what he knows will be saved.”
q: Verily, you are in a time of many scholars and few preachers. Whoever leaves a tenth of what he knows will be ruined. There will come a time for people of few scholars and many preachers. … Whoever adheres to a tenth of what he knows will be saved

title: Hadith on Guidance: O Allah, keep our hearts upon Islam
t: Umm Salamah reported:  I said, “O Messenger of Allah, how often you supplicate saying: O Turner of the hearts, keep my heart firm upon Your religion!” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Umm Salamah, there is no human but that his heart is between the fingers of Allah. Whoever He wills is kept steadfast, and whoever He wills is deviated.” Mu’adh recited the verse, “Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after you have guided us!” (3:8)
q: O Turner of the hearts, keep my heart firm upon Your religion … O Umm Salamah, there is no human but that his heart is between the fingers of Allah. Whoever He wills is kept steadfast, and whoever He wills is deviated … Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after you have guided us

title: Hadith on Hearts: O Allah, keep my heart steadfast upon Islam
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would often say, “O Turner of the hearts, keep my heart firm upon Your religion!”
q: O Turner of the hearts, keep my heart firm upon Your religion!

title: Hadith on Oaths: I swear by the turner of the hearts
t: Ibn Umar reported: The oath of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was, “No, by the turner of the hearts!”
q: No, by the turner of the hearts!

title: Hasan on Nifaq: Only believers fear committing acts of hypocrisy
t: Ibn al-Qayyim reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “No one fears hypocrisy but a believer. No one feels safe from hypocrisy but a hypocrite.”

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Whoever fasts Ramadan will have his sins forgiven
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Awf reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Ramadan is a month in which Allah Almighty has obligated its fasting. I have instituted for Muslims the practice of prayer at night. Thus, whoever fasts it with faith and expecting reward will be rid of sins like the day he was born from his mother.”
q: Verily, Ramadan is a month in which Allah Almighty has obligated its fasting. I have instituted for Muslims the … practice of prayer at night. Thus, whoever fasts it with faith and expecting reward will be rid of sins like the day he was born from his mother.

title: Hadith on Hygiene: Clean your nose three times in morning
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you awakens from his sleep, then let him perform ablution and sniff water into his nose three times. Verily, Satan spends the night in the upper part of his nose.”
q: When one of you awakens from his sleep, then let him perform ablution and sniff water into his nose three times. Verily, Satan spends the night in the upper part of his nose
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Qiyamah: Judgment for believers will be shorter and easier
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Day of Resurrection for the believers will be like the length of time between noon and afternoon prayers.”
q: The Day of Resurrection for the believers will be like the length of time between noon and afternoon prayers

title: Hadith on Khawarij: Violent rebels are worst killed under heaven
t: Abu Ghalib reported: Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The khawarij are the worst of those slain under the heavens, and the best of those slain are those who were killed by them. They are the dogs of Hellfire. They were Muslims and then became unbelievers.” I said, “O Abu Umamah, is this something you say?” Abu Umamah said, “No, rather I heard it from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.”

title: Malik on Knowledge: Muslims should never stop learning
t: Ibn Abdul Barr reported: Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It is not befitting for anyone with knowledge to give up learning.”

title: Hadith on Worship: If he comes to Me walking, I come running
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty says: Whoever comes with a good deed will have the reward of ten like it and even more. Whoever comes with an evil deed will be recompensed for one evil deed like it or he will be forgiven. Whoever draws close to Me by the length of a hand, I will draw close to him by the length of an arm. Whoever draws close to Me the by length of an arm, I will draw close to him by the length of a fathom. Whoever comes to Me walking, I will come to him running. Whoever meets Me with enough sins to fill the earth, not associating any partners with Me, I will meet him with as much forgiveness.”
q: Allah Almighty says: Whoever comes with a good deed will have the reward of ten like it and even more. Whoever comes with an evil deed will be recompensed for one evil deed like it or he will be forgiven. Whoever draws close to Me by the length of a hand, I will draw close to him by the length of an arm. Whoever draws close to Me the by length of an arm, I will draw close to him by the length of a fathom. Whoever comes to Me walking, I will come to him running. Whoever meets Me with enough sins to fill the earth, not associating any partners with Me, I will meet him with as much forgiveness.

title: Hasan on Mosques: Only discuss Islam in the Masjid
t: Abu Hazim reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A time will come to people when their discussions in the mosques will be about the affairs of their world. Allah has no need of it, so do not sit with them.”

title: Hadith on Alcohol: Stubborn wine drinkers become idol worshipers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The one addicted to wine becomes like a worshiper of idols.”
q: The one addicted to wine becomes like a worshiper of idols.

title: Uthman on Khamr: Alcohol is the mother of all evil deeds
t: Al-Harith reported: Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Stay away from wine, for it is the mother of wickedness. By Allah, faith and addiction to wine cannot be combined but that one of them will eventually expel the other.”

title: Hadith on Dua: He asked Allah by His greatest name
t: Buraydah al-Aslami reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, heard a man supplicating, saying, “O Allah, I ask you by my testimony that you are Allah, there is no God but you, the One, the Eternal Refuge, who does not give birth and was not born, and to whom no one is equal,” (112:1-4). The Prophet said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, he has asked Allah by His greatest name, for which He answers when called upon and He gives when asked.”
q: By the One in whose hand is my soul, he has asked Allah by His greatest name, for which He answers when called upon and He gives when asked

title: Hadith on Jerusalem: Sins forgiven by praying at Masjid al-Aqsa
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Solomon, son of David, peace and blessings be upon him, built the Sacred House, he asked Allah Almighty for the three things throughout. Solomon asked Allah Almighty for judgment coinciding with His judgment, and he was given it. Solomon asked Allah Almighty for a kingdom none would have after him, and he was given it. And Solomon asked Allah Almighty when he finished the foundations of the Mosque that none would come to it, intending only to pray, but that his sins would be expunged like the day he was born from his mother.”
q: When Solomon, son of David, peace and blessings be upon him, built the Sacred House, he asked Allah Almighty for the three things throughout. Solomon asked Allah Almighty for judgment coinciding with His judgment, and he was given it. Solomon asked Allah Almighty for a kingdom none would have after him, and he was given it. And Solomon asked Allah Almighty when he finished the foundations of the Mosque that none would come to it, intending only to pray, but that his sins would be expunged like the day he was born from his mother

title: Nakha’i on Fasting: Telling lies will break the fast
t: Al-A’mash reported: Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The righteous predecessors used to say that telling lies will break the fast.”

title: Mujahid on Fasting: Backbiting and lies harm fasting
t:
Layth reported: Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whoever is safe from two characteristics will secure his fasting: backbiting and falsehood.”

Al-Bayhaqi said, “Just as one guards his fasting from what is not befitting, one must guard himself in the month of Ramadan to obey Allah as much as possible.”

title: Maymun on Siyam: Easiest part of fasting is not eating or drinking
t: Ja’far reported: Maymun ibn Mihran, may Allah have mercy on him, would say, “Verily, the easiest part of fasting is leaving food and drink.”

title: Abu Aliyah on Fasting: Backbiting ruins fasting as worship
t: Ibn al-Sari reported: Abu al-‘Alyiah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The fasting person is in an act of worship as long as he does not backbite anyone, even if he is sleeping on his bed.”

title: Umar on Fasting: True fasting is to avoid sins, vain talk
t: Al-Sha’bi reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Fasting is not merely from food and drink alone. Rather, it is from lies, falsehood, vain talk, and swearing.”

title: Hadith on Mala’ikah: Angels bless those who give in charity
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, there is an angel at a gate among the gates of Paradise, saying: Whoever offers a good loan today will be rewarded tomorrow! And there is an angel at another door, saying: O Allah, give repayment to one who spends in charity, and give destruction to one who withholds charity!”
q: Verily, there is an angel at a gate among the gates of Paradise, saying: Whoever offers a good loan today will be rewarded tomorrow! And there is an angel at another door, saying: O Allah, give repayment to one who spends in charity, and give destruction to one who withholds charity!

title: Hadith on Charity: On door of Paradise is inscribed virtue of charity
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man entered Paradise and he saw written upon its door: Charity is multiplied by ten times, and a good loan is multiplied by eighteen times.”
q: A man entered Paradise and he saw written upon its door: Charity is multiplied by ten times, and a good loan is multiplied by eighteen times

title: Jabir on Fasting: You must fast from sins with dignity, tranquility
t: Sulayman ibn Musa reported: Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “When you fast, then let your hearing, seeing, and tongue fast as well from falsehood and sins, and avoid harming your servants. Rather, you must have dignity and calmness on the day of your fasting. Do not make days you do not fast and days you fast as if they were the same.”

title: Ali on Justice: Treat others as you want to be treated
t: Ibn Asakir reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever desires to be fair to people, let him love for them as he loves for himself.”

title: Abdullah on Justice: If you want to be fair, treat others as yourself
t: Al-Bayhaqi reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever wishes for himself to be fair with people, let him treat people as he would love to be treated.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Repentance: Monk forgiven for adultery by his charity
t: Abu al-Za’ra’ reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “A monk worshiped Allah in his hermitage for sixty years. Then, a woman came and lay down at his side, so he lay down with her and was intimate with her for six nights. He became regretful and fled. He arrived at a mosque and sought refuge in it, while he remained inside for three days without eating anything. He was given a loaf of bread, so he broke it into two halves, giving half to the man on his right and half to the man on his left. Allah sent to him the angel of death to take hold of his soul. The angel placed his good deeds of sixty years upon one side of the Scale and placed the six nights of adultery on the other side, yet the six nights outweighed it. Then, he placed the loaf of bread on the Scale, outweighing the six nights.”

title: Salaf on Fasting: Remember the poor, starving while fasting
t: Hassan ibn Ahmad reported: He asked the commander of the faithful Al-Ma’mun ‘Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, may Allah have mercy on him, “Is there any benefit to fasting in the wisdom?” Al-Ma’mun said, “Allah Almighty knows what the impoverished endure of severe hunger, so He made the rich perform fasting that by necessity they might taste the flavor of hunger, such that they do not forget the severe hunger of the impoverished.”

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Continue your good habits from before Islam
t: Al-Sa’ib ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him, “O Sa’ib, look at the good character of your deeds in the time of ignorance and continue them in Islam: honor the guest, be generous to the orphan, and be good to your neighbor.”
q: O Sa’ib, look at the good character of your deeds in the time of ignorance and continue them in Islam: honor the guest, be generous to the orphan, and be good to your neighbor.
gf: Rijal al-Sahih (narrators are reliable) according to Al-Haythami

title: Hadith on Beauty: Allah is beautiful, loves beautiful character
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is beautiful and He loves beauty. He loves the loftiest of affairs and disapproves of pettiness.”
q: Verily, Allah is beautiful and He loves beauty. He loves the loftiest of affairs and disapproves of pettiness

title: Ibn Umar on Family: Goodness to family rewarded in this life
t: Al-Bukhari reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever fears his Lord and maintains family ties, his life will be prolonged, his wealth will be enriched, and his family will love him.”

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Spread peace, offer food, be modest before Allah
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent him to a people and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, instruct me.” The Prophet said, “Spread peace, offer food, and be modest before Allah as you would for a man of dignity from your family. If you do a bad deed, follow it with a good deed. Make your character as excellent as you can.”
q: Spread peace, offer food, and be modest before Allah as you would for a man of dignity from your family. If you do a bad deed, follow it with a good deed. Make your character as excellent as you can

title: Hadith on Rifq: Kind and gentle behavior always benefits family
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people of a household are not granted kindness but that it will benefit them.”
q: The people of a household are not granted kindness but that it will benefit them

title: Hadith on Kindness: Allah supports kind and gentle people
t: Ma’dan ibn Abi Talhah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty is kind. He loves kindness and is pleased by it. He offers support for it, that which is not offered for harshness.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty is kind. He loves kindness and is pleased by it. He offers support for it, that which is not offered for harshness.

title: Hadith on Satan: Devil always tempts people with their wealth
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Awf reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Satan, whom Allah has cursed, said: The owner of wealth will never be safe from me by one of three ways. I come to him with them and leave with them: His taking of wealth without permission, his spending it without right, and my making it so beloved to him that he obstructs its rightful use.”
q: Satan, whom Allah has cursed, said: The owner of wealth will never be safe from me by one of three ways. I come to him with them and leave with them: His taking of wealth without permission, his spending it without right, and my making it so beloved to him that he obstructs its rightful use

title: Hadith on Greed: Human beings covet for more until death
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If the son of Adam had a valley of date palms, he would wish for another like it, then another and another, until he wished to have many valleys. Nothing will satisfy his belly but the dust of the grave.”
q: If the son of Adam had a valley of date palms, he would wish for another like it, then another and another, until he wished to have many valleys. Nothing will satisfy his belly but the dust … of the grave

title: Hadith on Gatherings: Best assembly is for remembrance, virtue, learning
t: Ibn Abbas reported: It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, which gathering is best?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A gathering of those who inspire you to remember Allah when you see them, whose discourse increases your knowledge, and whose good deeds inspire you to remember the Hereafter.”
q: A gathering of those who inspire you to remember Allah when you see them, whose discourse increases your knowledge, and whose good deeds inspire you to remember the Hereafter.

title: Wahb on Arrogance: Beware of lowly desires, evil friends, selfish pride
t: Ahmad reported: Wahb ibn Munnabih, may Allah have mercy on him, delivered a sermon to the people upon the pulpit, and he said, “Guard for me three things. Beware of whims that are followed, an evil companion, and the vanity of a man impressed by his own opinion.”

title: Hadith on Tyranny: Valley in Hellfire named Habhab for tyrants
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, there is a valley in Hell named Habhab, in which will reside every tyrant. Beware lest you be among them!”
q: Verily, there is a valley in Hell named Habhab, in which will reside every tyrant. Beware lest you be among them!

title: Hadith on Pride: Beware of arrogance from wealth, clothing
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of arrogance, for arrogance may be in a man by the cloak upon him.”
q: Beware of arrogance, for arrogance may be in a man by the cloak upon him.

title: Hadith on Humility: I eat as a servant eats, as a servant sits
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Aisha, if I had wished, a mountain of gold would have been sent with me. An angel came to me whose belt was like the Ka’bah. He said: Verily, your Lord sends you greetings of peace and He says, if you wish, you may be a prophet-servant or a prophet-king. I looked to Gabriel and he indicated that I should humble myself, so I said I will be a prophet-servant.” After that, the Prophet never ate while reclining and he would say, “I eat as the servant eats, and I sit as the servant sits.”
q: O Aisha, if I had wished, a mountain of gold would have been sent with me. An angel came to me whose belt was like the Ka’bah. He said: Verily, your Lord sends you greetings of peace and He says, if you wish, you may be a prophet-servant or a prophet-king. I looked to Gabriel and he indicated that I should humble myself, so I said I will be a prophet-servant … I eat as the servant eats, and I sit as the servant sits.

title: Hadith on Humility: The Prophet is a humble servant
t: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I eat as the servant eats, and I sit as the servant sits. Verily, I am only a servant.”
q: I eat as the servant eats, and I sit as the servant sits. Verily, I am only a servant.

title: Hadith on Family: Fear Allah and be good to your family
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Fear Allah and maintain relations with your family members.”
q: Fear Allah and maintain relations with your family members

title: Hadith on Sects: The Prophet warns of violent sectarianism ahead
t: Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do you imagine that I will be the last of you to die? No doubt, I will be among the first of you to die and coming after me will be sects that destroy each other.”
q: Do you imagine that I will be the last of you to die? No doubt, I will be among the first of you to die and coming after me will be sects that destroy each other

title: Hadith on Calamity: Hasten to good deeds before disaster strikes
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Hurry to perform good deeds before seven events: Are you waiting for poverty that makes you forgetful or wealth that burdens you? A debilitating disease or senility? A sudden death or the False Messiah? Are you waiting for evil in the Unseen or the Hour itself? The Hour will be most bitter and terrible!”
q: Hurry to perform good deeds before seven events: Are you waiting for poverty that makes you forgetful or wealth that burdens you? A debilitating disease or senility? A sudden death or the False Messiah? Are you waiting for evil in the Unseen or the Hour itself? The Hour will be most bitter and terrible!

title: Hadith on Akhirah: No true life but the Hereafter
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, there is no life worth living but the life of the Hereafter, so be generous to the Ansar and the Muhajirun.”
q: O Allah, there is no life worth living but the life of the Hereafter, so be generous to the Ansar and the Muhajirun.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hereafter: They will be resurrected with ones they loved
t: Ali reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No man loves a people but that he will be resurrected with them.”
q: No man loves a people but that he will be resurrected with them.

title: Hadith on Rage: Strong man controls anger, defeats Satan
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by people wrestling, and he said, “What is this?” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, this is a wrestler, and no one can wrestle like him!” The Prophet said, “Shall I not tell you who is even stronger than him? It is a man wronged by another man, yet he suppresses his rage, and thus he defeats it. He defeats his devil, and he defeats the devil of his companion.”
q: What is this? … Shall I not tell you who is even stronger than him? It is a man wronged by another man, yet he suppresses his rage, and thus he defeats it. He defeats his devil, and he defeats the devil of his companion.

title: Umar on Dhimmi: The Caliph enjoins good treatment of non-Muslims
t: ‘Amr ibn Maymun reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Enjoin the Caliph after me to be good to the people under the protection of Allah and His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, that he honors their covenant, he fights on their behalf, and he only holds them responsible for what they can do.”

title: Fudayl on Sincerity: Good will to love others more than yourself
t: Ibn ‘Asakir reported: Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you love for people to be equal to you, you have not fulfilled sincerity for the sake of your Lord. How so while you love for people to be less than you?”

title: Fudayl on Altruism: Let him not love for his sandal to be better
t: Ibn Rajab reported: Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said regarding the verse, “This is the home of the Hereafter that We make for those who desire not exaltation in the earth,” (28:83) that it means, “It is one who does not love for even his sandal to be better than the sandal of another, nor for his shoelace to be better than the shoelace of another.”
q: This is the home of the Hereafter that We make for those who desire not exaltation in the earth

title: Hasan on Faith: How can you be Muslim and harm people?
t: Al-Bayhaqi reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “O son of Adam, how can you be a believer while your neighbor is not secure from you? O son of Adam, how can you be a Muslim while people are not safe from you? O son of Adam, you will never achieve the reality of faith in your heart until you do not fault people for the same fault that is in yourself. Begin by correcting your own faults. If you do so, you will correct a fault only to find another.”

title: Umar on Qadr: Run from decree of Allah to decree of Allah
t: Abdullah ibn Abbas reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, went out to Syria until he arrived at Sargh. The commanders of the army, Abu ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah and his companions, met him and told him that an epidemic had befallen the land of Syria. Umar announced to the people, “I will turn back in the morning, so you must as well.” Abu ‘Ubaydah said, “Are you fleeing from the decree of Allah?” Umar said, “Would that another had said so, O Abu ‘Ubaydah! Yes, we are fleeing from the decree of Allah to the decree of Allah. Do you not see that if you had camels descending in a valley with two fields, one of them fertile and the other barren, you would graze in the fertile field by the decree of Allah or you would graze in the barren field by the decree of Allah?”

title: Sufyan on Silence: Being silent for long periods is the key to worship
t: Al-Humaydi reported: Sufyan Ath-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It is said that observing long periods of silence is the key to worship.”

title: Hadith on Care: The Prophet cares for a mentally ill woman
t: Anas reported: A woman with some illness in her mind said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have a problem!” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O mother of a child, come to whichever side of the road you wish that I may take care of your need.” The Prophet spoke privately with her in part of the road until she was free from her need.
q: O mother of a child, come to whichever side of the road you wish that I may take care of your need

title: Hadith on Love: Joined in Paradise with the one he loves
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever loves a man for the sake of Allah, then he should say: I love you for the sake of Allah. They will both enter Paradise together. He whose love is greater will be raised in status over the other; he will be joined with the one he loved for the sake of Allah.”
q: Whoever loves a man for the sake of Allah, then he should say: I love you for the sake of Allah. They will both enter Paradise together. He whose love is greater will be raised in status over the other; he will be joined with the one he loved for the sake of Allah

title: Ali on Justice: Make a scale between you and others
t: Al-Muttaqi al-Hindi reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Make yourself a scale between you and others. Love for those besides you what you love for yourself, and hate for them what you hate for yourself. Do not wrong others, as you would love not to be wronged. Be good to others, as you would love to be treated well.”

title: Ahnaf on Knowledge: Learn by treating others as yourself
t: Ibn al-Mulaqqin reported: Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked, “From whom did you learn sacred knowledge?” Al-Ahnaf said, “From myself.” It was said, “And how is that?” Al-Ahnaf said, “If I hated something did by another, I would never do the same to anyone else.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Quickest answer a supplication for one absent
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No supplication is quicker to be answered than a supplication on behalf of one absent.”
q: No supplication is quicker to be answered than a supplication on behalf of one absent.

title: Urwah on Aisha: The Prophet’s wife was very generous, ascetic
t: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, would give seventy thousand coins in charity while her clothes were covered in patches.

title: Hadith on Thoughts: Rejection of bad thoughts a sign of faith
t: Abu Huraira reported: Some of the companions came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and they asked him, “We find within ourselves that which is too grievous to speak of.” The Prophet said, “You have indeed found it so?” They said yes. The Prophet said, “That is pure faith.”
q: You have indeed found it so? … That is pure faith

title: Hadith on Silence: Be restrained about Companions, Qadr, and stars
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If my companions are mentioned, be restrained. If the stars are mentioned, be restrained. If the divine decree is mentioned, be restrained.”
q: If my companions are mentioned, be restrained. If the stars are mentioned, be restrained. If the divine decree is mentioned, be restrained.

title: Fudayl on Moderation: Too much food and sleep hardens the heart
t: Ibn Asakir reported: Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Two characteristics harden the heart: too much sleeping and too much eating.”

title: Hadith on Qadr: Pens have dried upon Allah’s decree
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty created His creation in darkness and He cast over them His light. Whoever is touched by that light is guided, and whoever misses it is led astray. Thus, I say the pens have been dried upon the knowledge of Allah.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty created His creation in darkness and He cast over them His light. Whoever is touched by that light is guided, and whoever misses it is led astray. Thus, I say the pens have been dried upon the knowledge of Allah.

title: Hadith on Qadr: All must act to fulfill their destinies
t: ‘Imran ibn Husayn reported: It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, are the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire known?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said yes. It was said, “Then what is the use of deeds?” The Prophet said, “Everyone will be facilitated to that for which he was created.”
q: Everyone will be facilitated to that for which he was created.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Providence: Act right to earn favor of Allah’s decree
t: Ali reported: We were sitting with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “There are none among you but that his place in Paradise or his place in Hellfire are decreed.” We said, “O Messenger of Allah, shall we not depend on this alone?” The Prophet said, “No, you must work, for all will be facilitated.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “As for one who gave in charity and was righteous and affirmed the best, We facilitate for him the easy path.” (92:5-7)
q: There are none among you but that his place in Paradise or his place in Hellfire are decreed … No, you must work, for all will be facilitated. … As for one who gave in charity and was righteous and affirmed the best, We facilitate for him the easy path
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Qadr: Every day Allah attends to some matters
t: Abu Darda reported: Regarding the saying of the Almighty, “Every day he brings forth a matter,” (55:29), the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among his affairs are forgiving sins, relieving hardship, raising people and debasing others.”
q: Every day he brings forth a matter … Among his affairs are forgiving sins, relieving hardship, raising people and debasing others.

title: Umar on Qadr: O Allah, if my fate is evil then change it
t: Abu Uthman al-Hindi reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was circling the House and he was weeping, saying, “O Allah, if you have written me among the blessed, affirm it therein. And if you have written me among the sinful and the damned, wipe it away and affirm me among the blessed. Verily, you wipe away and affirm whatever you will, and with you is the mother of the Book.” (13:39)

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Providence: O Allah, affirm me among the blessed
t: Abu Qilabah reported: Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, would say, “O Allah, if you have written me among the damned, then wipe it away from me and affirm me among the blessed.”

title: Shaqiq on Destiny: O Allah, erase our evil destiny and record us among the blessed
t: Al-A’mash reported: Shaqiq ibn Salamah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “O Allah, if you have written us among the damned, then wipe it away and record us among the blessed. And if you have written us among the blessed, then affirm it for us. Verily, you wipe away or affirm whatever you will, and with you is the mother of the Book.” (13:39)

title: Hadith on Dua: Write for him an abundance of love, mercy
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If the servant glorifies Allah, Allah Almighty says: Record for my servant an abundance of my mercy. If the servant praises Allah, Allah Almighty says: Record for my servant an abundance of my mercy. If the servant declares there is no God but Allah, Allah Almighty says: Record for my servant an abundance of my love.”
q: If the servant glorifies Allah, Allah Almighty says: Record for my servant an abundance of my mercy. If the servant praises Allah, Allah Almighty says: Record for my servant an abundance of my mercy. If the servant declares there is no God but Allah, Allah Almighty says: Record for my servant an abundance of my love
gf: Hasan li ghayri (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Nothing saves you like remembrance of Allah
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The son of Adam never acts with a deed better to save him from the punishment of Allah than with the remembrance of Allah.” It was said, “Not even jihad in the way of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Not even jihad, except if one of you continues to strike with his sword until it breaks.”
q: The son of Adam never acts with a deed better to save him from the punishment of Allah than with the remembrance of Allah … Not even jihad, except if one of you continues to strike with his sword until it breaks
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Best deed for salvation is to remember Allah
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The son of Adam does not act with a deed better to save him from the punishment of Allah than with the remembrance of Allah.”
q: The son of Adam does not act with a deed better to save him from the punishment of Allah than with the remembrance of Allah

title: Ibn Abbas on Deeds: Good deeds bring light, evil deeds darkness
t: Ibn al-Qayyim reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, good deeds bring brightness upon the face, a light in the heart, an expanse of provision, strength in the body, and love in the hearts of the creation. And evil deeds bring blackness upon the face, darkness in the grave and in the heart, weakness in the body, a restriction of provision, and hatred in the hearts of the creation.”

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Giving charity to people of all religions
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to order charity only for the people of Islam, until this verse was revealed, “It is not upon you to guide them, for Allah guides whom He wills. Whatever you spend of good is for yourselves, not spending it but to seek the countenance of Allah. Whatever you spend of good, you will be fully repaid and will not be wronged,” (2:272). Then, the Prophet ordered charity for anyone who asked from every religion.
q: It is not upon you to guide them, for Allah guides whom He wills. Whatever you spend of good is for yourselves, not spending it but to seek the countenance of Allah. Whatever you spend of good, you will be fully repaid and will not be wronged,

title: Hadith on Quran: Readers of Quran never enter Hellfire
t:
‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If the Quran were placed in a leatherskin and then thrown into the fire, it would not burn.”

Al-Bayhaqi said, “It means whoever carries the Quran and recites it will never be touched by Hellfire.”
q: If the Quran were placed in a leatherskin and then thrown into the fire, it would not burn

title: Sufyan on Taqwa: Righteousness is to love people as yourself
t:
Al-Tha’labi reported: Sufyan al-Thawri and Al-Fudayl, may Allah have mercy on them both, said, “The righteous man is he who loves for people what he loves for himself.”

And Al-Junayd ibn Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The righteous man is not he who loves for people what he loves for himself. Rather, the righteous man is only he who loves for people greater than he loves for himself.”

title: Hadith on Haram: Protect yourself with a barrier of the lawful
