t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Make between yourself and the unlawful a buffer of what is lawful. Whoever does so will clear himself in regard to his honor and his religion. A shepherd who grazes near the side of a sanctum will nearly fall into it. Verily, every king has a sanctum and the sanctum of Allah is His prohibitions.”
q: Make between yourself and the unlawful a buffer of what is lawful. Whoever does so will clear himself in regard to his honor and his religion. A shepherd who grazes near the side of a sanctum will nearly fall into it. Verily, every king has a sanctum and the sanctum of Allah is His prohibitions

title: Hadith on Adab: House in paradise for those with good character
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever abandons lies in support of falsehood, a house will be built for him in the surroundings of Paradise. Whoever abandons arguments even though he is right, a house will be built for him in its middle. Whoever makes his character excellent, a house will be built for him in its highest part.”
q: Whoever abandons lies in support of falsehood, a house will be built for him in the surroundings of Paradise. Whoever abandons arguments even though he is right, a house will be built for him in its middle. Whoever makes his character excellent, a house will be built for him in its highest part

title: Hadith on Hikmah: The Prophet’s wise advice for Abu Dharr
t: Abu Dharr reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, instruct me.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I advise you to fear Allah Almighty, for it will beautify all of your affairs.” I said, “Tell me more.” The Prophet said, “You must recite the Quran and remember Allah Almighty, for you will be mentioned in heaven and you will have light upon the earth.” I said, “Tell me more.” The Prophet said, “You must observe long periods of silence, for it will drive away Satan and help you in the matter of your religion.” I said, “Tell me more.” The Prophet said, “Beware of too much laughter, for it will deaden the heart and take away the light on your face.” I said, “Tell me more.” The Prophet said, “Speak the truth, even if it is bitter.” I said, “Tell me more.” The Prophet said, “Do not fear the blame of any critic in the matter of Allah.”
q: I advise you to fear Allah Almighty, for it will beautify all of your affairs … You must recite the Quran and remember Allah Almighty, for you will be mentioned in heaven and you will have light upon the earth … You must observe long periods of silence, for it will drive away Satan and help you in the matter of your religion … Beware of too much laughter, for it will deaden the heart and take away the light on your face. … Speak the truth, even if it is bitter. … Do not fear the blame of any critic in the matter of Allah.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Ahmad on Akhlaq: Good character is patience, restraining anger
t: Ibn Rajab reported: Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Good character is to not get angry or enraged. Good character is to patiently endure what comes from people.”

title: Hadith on Virtue: Justice engraved on the Prophet’s sword
t: Ali reported: When the weapon of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had been assembled, I found three sayings on the handle or blade of his sword, “Maintain relations with those who cut you off, speak the truth even if it is against yourself, and be good to one who is evil to you.”
q: Maintain relations with those who cut you off, speak the truth even if it is against yourself, and be good to one who is evil to you

title: Hadith on Aggression: The Prophet’s sword condemns unjust killing
t: Aisha reported: I found an engraving on the sword of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that wrote, “Verily, the worst of people in insolence are those who strike those who never struck anyone, a man who kills those who never killed anyone, and a man who claims allegiance to those other than his rightful benefactors. Whoever does so has disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger. Allah will not accept his obligatory or voluntary deeds.”
q: Verily, the worst of people in insolence are those who strike those who never struck anyone, a man who kills those who never killed anyone, and a man who claims allegiance to those other than his rightful benefactors. Whoever does so has disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger. Allah will not accept his obligatory or voluntary deeds
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Busiri

title: Hadith on Dua: Exalt, glorify, praise Allah before asking
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: Umm Sulaym came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and she said, “Teach me some words to say in my prayer.” The Prophet said, “Exalt Allah ten times, glorify Allah ten times, praise Allah ten times, then ask for whatever you wish. Allah will say: Yes, yes.”
q: Exalt Allah ten times, glorify Allah ten times, praise Allah ten times, then ask for whatever you wish. Allah will say: Yes, yes

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for leaving the lavatory
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say upon leaving the washroom, “All praise is due to Allah, who has removed harm from me and granted me wellness.”
q: All praise is due to Allah, who has removed harm from me and granted me wellness

title: Hadith on Salat: Praying the five prayers saves from Hellfire
t: Hanzala al-Asaydi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever guards the five prayers, their ablution, their timing, their bowing, and their prostration, and knowing they are the right of Allah over him, then Allah will forbid him from entering Hellfire.”
q: Whoever guards the five prayers, their ablution, their timing, their bowing, and their prostration, and knowing they are the right of Allah over him, then Allah will forbid him from entering Hellfire

title: Hadith on Charity: Man who gave charity to thief, prostitute
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man intended to give charity, so he went out with his charity and placed it in the hands of a thief. In the morning, people were saying: Charity was given to a thief! The man said: O Allah, praise be to you! The man again intended to give charity, so he went out with his charity and placed it in the hands of an adulteress. In the morning, people were saying: Charity was given to an adulteress in the night! The man said: O Allah, praise be to you for the adulteress! The man again intended to give charity, so he went out with his charity and placed it in the hands of a wealthy person. In the morning, people were saying: Charity was given to a wealthy person! The man said: O Allah, praise be to you for the thief, the adulteress, and the wealthy person! Then, it came to him in a dream and it was said: As for your charity to the thief, perhaps it will cause him to give up stealing. As for the adulteress, perhaps it will cause her to give up adultery. As for the wealthy person, perhaps he will learn a lesson and spend in charity from what Allah has given him.”
q: A man intended to give charity, so he went out with his charity and placed it in the hands of a thief. In the morning, people were saying: Charity was given to a thief! The man said: O Allah, praise be to you! The man again intended to give charity, so he went out with his charity and placed it in the hands of an adulteress. In the morning, people were saying: Charity was given to an adulteress in the night! The man said: O Allah, praise be to you for the adulteress! The man again intended to give charity, so he went out with his charity and placed it in the hands of a wealthy person. In the morning, people were saying: Charity was given to a wealthy person! The man said: O Allah, praise be to you for the thief, the adulteress, and the wealthy person! Then, it came to him in a dream and it was said: As for your charity to the thief, perhaps it will cause him to give up stealing. As for the adulteress, perhaps it will cause her to give up adultery. As for the wealthy person, perhaps he will learn a lesson and spend in charity from what Allah has given him
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tafakkur: Reflect deeply on the blessings of Allah
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Reflect deeply upon the blessings of Allah, but do not reflect upon the essence of Allah.”
q: Reflect deeply upon the blessings of Allah, but do not reflect upon the essence of Allah

title: Hadith on Reflection: Think about wonders of creation, not Allah’s essence
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by some people who were thinking about the essence of Allah. The Prophet said, “Reflect upon acts of creation, but do not reflect upon the essence of the Creator. Verily, you cannot possibly comprehend His magnitude.”
q: Reflect upon acts of creation, but do not reflect upon the essence of the Creator. Verily, you cannot possibly comprehend His magnitude.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Fitnah: In darkest trials, stay inside and hide
t: Jundub ibn Sufyan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will come after me a tribulation like the dark of night, in which a man will awaken as a believer but enter evening as an unbeliever, or awaken as an unbeliever but enter evening as a believer.” A man among the Muslims said, “What shall we do in that case, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Stay in your homes and hide yourselves.” A man said, “What shall we do if someone invades our home?” The Prophet said, “Restrain your hands and be the servant of Allah who is killed, and do not be the servant of Allah who kills. Verily, a man will be among a party in Islam, yet he consumes the wealth of his brother, he sheds his blood, he disobeys his Lord, and he disbelieves in his Creator. Thus, he must enter the Hellfire.”
q: There will come after me a tribulation like the dark of night, in which a man will awaken as a believer but enter evening as an unbeliever, or awaken as an unbeliever but enter evening as a believer. … Stay in your homes and hide yourselves. … Restrain your hands and be the servant of Allah who is killed, and do not be the servant of Allah who kills. Verily, a man will be among a party in Islam, yet he consumes the wealth of his brother, he sheds his blood, he disobeys his Lord, and he disbelieves in his Creator. Thus, he must enter the Hellfire

title: Hadith on Sincerity: Good will protects from hatred, malice
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are three traits by which a believer will have no malice: sincerity in deeds for Allah, goodwill to the Muslims, and uniting with their community.”
q: There are three traits by which a believer will have no malice: sincerity in deeds for Allah, goodwill to the Muslims, and uniting with their community.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Tha’labi on Taqwa: True piety to not feel shame for anything
t: Al-Tha’labi reported: Some of the wise men said, “A man does not reach the peak of righteousness until it is such that, were he to place what is in his heart on a plate and go around the market with it, he would not be ashamed of anything on it.”

title: Sufyan on Honesty: You must be truthful in everything you do
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “You must be honest in all things. Beware of lying and treachery and sitting with those who commit them; it will all be a burden of sin. Beware, my brother, of ostentation in words and deeds, as it is a form of idolatry. Beware of vanity, for good deeds within which is vanity will not be exalted.”

title: Kattani on Islam: Religion of Allah is truth, justice, and honesty
t: Al-Ghazali reported: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kattani, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “We have found that the religion of Allah Almighty is built upon three pillars: truth, honesty, and justice. Truth is in the body, justice is in the heart, and honesty is in the mind.”

title: Hadith on Shirk: Beware lesser idolatry, ostentation in worship
t: Ma’qil ibn Yasar reported: I departed with Abu Bakr to meet the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Prophet said, “O Abu Bakr, there is idolatry among you more hidden than the crawling of an ant.” Abu Bakr said, “Is there idolatry other than to make a god alongside Allah?” The Prophet said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, there is idolatry more hidden than the crawling of an ant. Shall I not tell you something to say to rid you of it, both minor and major? Say: O Allah, I seek refuge in You that I associate partners with You while I know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know.”
q: O Abu Bakr, there is idolatry among you more hidden than the crawling of an ant. … By the One in whose hand is my soul, there is idolatry more hidden than the crawling of an ant. Shall I not tell you something to say to rid you of it, both minor and major? Say: O Allah, I seek refuge in You that I associate partners with You while I know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know.

title: Abu Aliyah on Ikhlas: Only do good deeds for Allah, no one else
t: Abu al-Aliyah reported: The companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “Do not do a good deed for anyone besides Allah, for Allah will leave you in the charge of the one for whom you did it.”

title: Mutarrif on Sincerity: True servants of Allah are pure inwardly, outwardly
t: Ibn al-Sari reported: Mutarrif, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, when the inward state of the servant matches his public behavior, Allah says: This is my true servant.”

title: Umar on Niyyah: Best action to have sincere intention for Allah
t: Ibn Rajab reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The best deeds are to fulfill the obligations of Allah, to be cautious of the prohibitions of Allah, and to have an honest intention before Allah Almighty.”

title: Hadith on Idolatry: Showing off is lesser idolatry
t: Shaddad ibn Aws reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever prays to be seen has associated partners with Allah. Whoever fasts to be seen has associated partners with Allah.”
q: Whoever prays to be seen has associated partners with Allah. Whoever fasts to be seen has associated partners with Allah

title: Hadith on Sincerity: Make your deeds pure for Allah alone
t: Al-Dahhak ibn Qays reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty says: I am the best partner. Whoever associates another partner with Me, then I leave him to My partner.” Then, the Prophet said, “O people, make your deeds sincere for Allah Almighty. Verily, Allah does not accept any deed unless it is sincerely for Him. Do not say: This is for the sake of Allah and this is for the sake of my relatives. Verily, it was done for your relatives and none of it was for Allah. Do not say: This is for the sake of Allah and for your sake. Verily, it was done for their sake and none of it was for Allah.”
q: Allah Almighty says: I am the best partner. Whoever associates another partner with Me, then I leave him to My partner. … O people, make your deeds sincere for Allah Almighty. Verily, Allah does not accept any deed unless it is sincerely for Him. Do not say: This is for the sake of Allah and this is for the sake of my relatives. Verily, it was done for your relatives and none of it was for Allah. Do not say: This is for the sake of Allah and for your sake. Verily, it was done for their sake and none of it was for Allah.

title: Hadith on Military: Only jihad for the right reason is rewarded
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Military expeditions are two kinds. As for one who seeks the countenance of Allah, obeys the leader, spends in charity from his precious possessions, shows leniency to his colleagues, and avoids corruption, then the entirety of his sleep and vigilance is rewarded. As for one who fights out of pride, showing off, and seeking a reputation, who disobeys the leader and commits corruption in the land, then he will return with nothing of importance.”
q: Military expeditions are two kinds. As for one who seeks the countenance of Allah, obeys the leader, spends in charity from his precious possessions, shows leniency to his colleagues, and avoids corruption, then the entirety of his sleep and vigilance is rewarded. As for one who fights out of pride, showing off, and seeking a reputation, who disobeys the leader and commits corruption in the land, then he will return with nothing of importance.

title: Hadith on Resurrection: People are only judged by their intentions
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the people will only be resurrected for judgment based upon their intentions.”
q: Verily, the people will only be resurrected for judgment based upon their intentions.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Shirk: Allah does not accept deeds shared with idols
t: Abu Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Allah gathers the people on the Day of Resurrection, a day of which there is no doubt, an announcement will be made: To those who shared with anyone in deeds to be done for Allah, let him seek his reward from those besides Allah! Verily, Allah is free of any partners!”
q: When Allah gathers the people on the Day of Resurrection, a day of which there is no doubt, an announcement will be made: To those who shared with anyone in deeds to be done for Allah, let him seek his reward from those besides Allah! Verily, Allah is free of any partners!
gf: Jayyid (very good) according to Ibn Hajar

title: Bilal on Hypocrisy: Do not show people two faces with an evil heart
t: Ibn Abi Dunya reported: Bilal ibn Sa’d, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Do not be one with two faces and two tongues, making a show for people to praise you while your heart is wicked.”

title: Ibn Mu’adh on Niyyah: Sincerity distinguishes good and bad deeds
t:
Abu Hayyan reported: Ibn Mu’adh, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Sincerity distinguishes good deeds from sins, just as milk is distinguished from filth and blood.”

And Sa’id ibn Jubayr, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Sincerity is to not associate partners with Allah in one’s religion, and to not display ostentation in good deeds to anyone.”

title: Umar on Sincerity: Allah takes care of those who are sincere
t: ‘Amir al-Sha’bi reported: Umar ibn Al-Khattab wrote to Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with them both, saying, “Whoever purifies his intention, Allah will take care of his affairs between people. Whoever embellishes for people what Allah knows is not in his heart, Allah Almighty will disgrace him.”

title: Abu Sulayman on Ikhlaas: Blessed are those who walk sincerely to Allah
t:
Ibn Qudamah reported: Abu Sulayman, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Blessed is he who takes a single step, desiring nothing but Allah Almighty.”

Ma’ruf al-Karkhi would strike himself and say, “O my soul! Be sincere and purify yourself!”

title: Junayd on Ikhlaas: Sincerity leads to every door of righteousness
t:
Al-Ghazali reported: Al-Junayd, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, Allah has servants who use their minds. When they reason, they act. When they act, they are sincere. Sincerity calls them to all of the gates of righteousness.”

Al-Susi, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Allah only desires sincerity in the deeds of his creatures.”

title: Ibn Mubarak on Ikhlaas: Best deed is to be sincere to Allah
t: Ibn Abi Dunya reported: Ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked, “Which deed is best?” Ibn al-Mubarak said, “Sincerity to Allah.”
s: al-Amr bil-Ma’rūf li Ibn Abī Dunyā 71

title: Fudayl on Sincerity: Righteous became so by generosity, purity, sincerity
t: Abu Nuaim reported: Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Those who achieved did not do so, in our view, with an abundance of fasts, nor prayers. Indeed, they only achieved, in our view, with the spirit of generosity, purity of heart, and sincerity to the community.”

title: Hadith on Nush: Best act of worship is sincerity for Allah
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: The most beloved act with which My servant worships Me is goodwill for My sake.”
q: Allah Almighty said: The most beloved act with which My servant worships Me is goodwill for My sake.

title: Hadith on Ikhlaas: Sincere Muslims do not stay in Hellfire forever
t: ‘Itban ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to me one morning and a man said, “Where is Malik ibn al-Dukhshun?” Another man among us said, “That one is a hypocrite! He does not love Allah and His Messenger!” The Prophet said to him, “Do you not agree that he says there is no God but Allah, seeking thereby of the countenance of Allah?” The man said, “Of course.” The Prophet said, “Verily, a servant is not brought on the Day of Resurrection saying so but that Allah will forbid him from entering the Hellfire.”
q: Do you not agree that he says there is no God but Allah, seeking thereby of the countenance of Allah … Verily, a servant is not brought on the Day of Resurrection saying so but that Allah will forbid him from entering the Hellfire
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sincerity: Whoever has honest faith not in Hell forever
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and Mu’adh ibn Jabal were riding together on a journey. The Prophet said, “O Mu’adh ibn Jabal!” Mu’adh said, “I am here, O Messenger of Allah, at your service.” The Prophet said, “No one testifies that there is no God but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, honestly from the heart, but that Allah will forbid him from entering Hellfire.” Mu’adh said, “O Messenger of Allah, shall I not share the good news with people?” The Prophet said, “If so, they would take it for granted.”
q: O Mu’adh ibn Jabal … No one testifies that there is no God but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, honestly from the heart, but that Allah will forbid him from entering Hellfire. … If so, they would take it for granted
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ikhlaas: Allah only accepts sincere good deeds
t: Abu Umamah reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “If a man battles for the sake of reward and fame, what do you think he has?” The Prophet said, “He has nothing.” The man repeated his question three times, and the Prophet said, “He has nothing.” Then, the Prophet said, “Verily, Allah does not accept any good deeds unless they are done sincerely and in pursuit of His countenance.”
q: He has nothing … He has nothing … Verily, Allah does not accept any good deeds unless they are done sincerely and in pursuit of His countenance.

title: Ayyub on Pardon: Nobility is in detachment from the world and in forgiveness
t: Ibn Hibban reported: Ayyub As-Sakhtiyani, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “A man will not achieve nobility until he has two qualities: to be indifferent to what people possess, and to pardon them.”

title: Hadith on ‘Adn: Their sins forgiven in the Garden of Eden
t: Samrah ibn Jundab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two angels came to me in the night and took me until we arrived at a city built with gold and silver bricks. We met some men whose first half was the most beautiful you had ever seen, but their second half was the ugliest you had ever seen. The two angels said to them: Go and dip yourselves in this river. They dipped themselves in it and then returned to us with their ugly half removed, such that they were in the most beautiful of appearances. The two angels said to me: This is the Garden of Eden and that is your residence. As for those who were half beautiful and half ugly, they are those who mixed righteous deeds with evil deeds, and Allah pardoned them.”
q: Two angels came to me in the night and took me until we arrived at a city built with gold and silver bricks. We met some men whose first half was the most beautiful you had ever seen, but their second half was the ugliest you had ever seen. The two angels said to them: Go and dip yourselves in this river. They dipped themselves in it and then returned to us with their ugly half removed, such that they were in the most beautiful of appearances. The two angels said to me: This is the Garden of Eden and that is your residence. As for those who were half beautiful and half ugly, they are those who mixed righteous deeds with evil deeds, and Allah pardoned them

title: Ali on Sabr: Patience to faith like a head to a body
t: Masruq reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, patience is to faith as the head is to the body. If the head is cut, the body will perish.” Then, Ali raised his voice and he said, “No doubt, there is no faith for one without patience!”

title: Hadith on Sabr: Reward for patience at first strike is Paradise
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty says: O son of Adam, if you are patient and restrained at the first shock of calamity, I would not be pleased with any reward for you less than Paradise.”
q: Allah Almighty says: O son of Adam, if you are patient and restrained at the first shock of calamity, I would not be pleased with any reward for you less than Paradise

title: Hadith on Funerals: Muslims whose good is witnessed enter Paradise
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whenever four persons testify to the goodness of a Muslim, he will enter Paradise.” We said, “And three?” The Prophet said, “Even three.” We said, “And two?” The Prophet said, “Even two.” Thereafter, we did not ask about only one person.
q: Whenever four persons testify to the goodness of a Muslim, he will enter Paradise … Even three … Even two

title: Hadith on Society: How can Allah sanctify a cruel nation?
t: Jabir reported: When the emigrants returned to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, from across the sea, the Prophet said, “Will you not tell me about the most amazing things you saw in the land of Abyssinia?” They said, “Of course, O Messenger of Allah. While we were sitting, an elderly woman among the senior nuns passed by us carrying a jug of water on top of her head. As she passed by some young men among them, one of them pushed her back, she fell to her knees, and her jug was broken. When she got back up, she turned to him and said: Soon you will know, traitor! When Allah takes up the Throne and gathers the former and latter generations, and hands and feet are made to speak about what they have earned, you will come to know mine and your affair shortly!” The Prophet said, “She spoke the truth! She spoke the truth! How can Allah sanctify a nation if their strong do not support their weak?”
q: Will you not tell me about the most amazing things you saw in the land of Abyssinia … She spoke the truth! She spoke the truth! How can Allah sanctify a nation if their strong do not support their weak?

title: Hasan on Akhlaq: Good character is generosity, charity, love
t: Al-Washa’ reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about good character and he said, “It is generosity, charitable giving, and loving kindness towards people.”

title: Baqir on Character: Kindness and good character all that is good
t: Ibn al-Mubarak reported: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Whoever has qualities of character and kindness has been given all that is good and comforting. His situation will be pleasant in his life and in his Hereafter. Whoever is deprived of qualities of kindness and character, it will be a means of every evil and adversity for him, except for those who are protected by Allah Almighty.”

title: Raja’ on Islam: How excellent is Islam when adorned by faith
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Raja’ ibn Haywah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “How excellent is Islam when it is adorned with faith! And how excellent is faith when it is adorned with mindfulness! And how excellent is mindfulness when it is adorned with knowledge! And how excellent is knowledge when it is adorned with forbearance! And how excellent is forbearance when it is adorned with gentleness!”

title: Umar II on Kindness: None is kind but that Allah will be kind to him
t: Ibn Hibban reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The most beloved matters to Allah are three: forgiveness in a position of power, moderation in a position of affluence, and gentleness in worship. No one is kind to another in this world but that Allah will be gentle with him on the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Fitnah: Seek refuge in Allah from misguiding trials
t: Al-Qurtubi reported: Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Do not say: O Allah, fortify me from trials. Indeed, not one of you returns to his family and children but that it is included among the trials. Rather, say: O Allah, I seek refuge in you from trials of misguidance.”

title: Umar on Patience: Best response to sin is obeying Allah
t: Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “There is no better response to those who disobey Allah with respect to you than to obey Allah with respect to them. You must adhere to the truth, even if the truth kills you.”

title: Hadith on Adab: Good character rewarded with Paradise, increased life
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, whoever has been given the quality of kindness has been given his share of good in this life and in the Hereafter. Maintaining family ties, good character, and good treatment of neighbors will build their heavenly abodes and increase their life spans.”
q: Verily, whoever has been given the quality of kindness has been given his share of good in this life and in the Hereafter. Maintaining family ties, good character, and good treatment of neighbors will build their heavenly abodes and increase their life spans

title: Hadith on Quran: Learn Allah’s Book, but not to gain wealth
t: Mu’awiyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Learn the Quran. When you have learned it, do not exaggerate with it, do not abandon it, do not earn your livelihood from it, and do not accumulate wealth from it.”
q: Learn the Quran. When you have learned it, do not exaggerate with it, do not abandon it, do not earn your livelihood from it, and do not accumulate wealth from it

title: Umar II on Humility: Caliph orders son to sell his valuable jewelry
t: Al-Qurtubi reported: It reached Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, that his son had purchased a ring for a thousand coins, so he wrote to him saying, “Indeed, I have heard that you purchased a ring for a thousand coins, so sell it and feed a thousand starving people and buy a ring of iron for one coin. Write over it, ‘May Allah have mercy on a man who knows his place.’”

title: Hadith on Knowledge: Scholars are successors of prophets
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The scholars are the successors of the prophets. Verily, the prophets do not pass on gold and silver coins, but rather they only impart knowledge.”
q: The scholars are the successors of the prophets. Verily, the prophets do not pass on gold and silver coins, but rather they only impart knowledge.

title: Hadith on Tyranny: Years of deceit and injustice to come
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Years of treachery will come to people in which the liars are believed and the truthful are denied, the deceitful are trusted and the trustworthy are considered traitors, and the disgraceful will deliver speeches.” It was said, “Who are the disgraceful?” The Prophet said, “Petty men with authority over the common people.”
q: Years of treachery will come to people in which the liars are believed and the truthful are denied, the deceitful are trusted and the trustworthy are considered traitors, and the disgraceful will deliver speeches … Petty men with authority over the common people

title: Hadith on Virtues: Good deeds protect from evil fates in Hereafter
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Good works protect from evil fates. Charity in secret extinguishes the wrath of the Lord, maintaining family ties increases life span, and every good deed is charity. The people of good in the world are the people of good in the Hereafter, and the people of evil in the world are the people of evil in the Hereafter. And the first to enter Paradise are the people of good.”
q: Good works protect from evil fates. Charity in secret extinguishes the wrath of the Lord, maintaining family ties increases life span, and every good deed is charity. The people of good in the world are the people of good in the Hereafter, and the people of evil in the world are the people of evil in the Hereafter. And the first to enter Paradise are the people of good.

title: Hadith on Neighbors: Two neighbors first to dispute on Judgment Day
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among the first disputants on the Day of Resurrection will be two neighbors.”
q: Among the first disputants on the Day of Resurrection will be two neighbors

title: Hadith on Daughters: Your daughters are precious companions
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not hate your daughters, for they are your precious companions.”
q: Do not hate your daughters, for they are your precious companions.

title: Hadith on Kindness: Whoever is gentle is blessed with good
t: Abu Darda reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever has the quality of kindness has been given his share of goodness. Whoever is deprived of the quality of kindness has been deprived of his share of goodness.”
q: Whoever has the quality of kindness has been given his share of goodness. Whoever is deprived of the quality of kindness has been deprived of his share of goodness

title: Hadith on Eating: All praise to Allah who provided for us
t: Abu Sa’id reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, ate or drank, he would say, “All praise is due to Allah who has fed us, given us drink, and has made us Muslims.”
q: All praise is due to Allah who has fed us, given us drink, and has made us Muslims

title: Qasim on Religion: Piety, night worship, pure heart are best
t: Al-Khatib reported: Qasim al-Ju’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The religion is based upon cautious piety. The best worship is undertaken at night, and the best of paths to Paradise is to have a pure heart.”

title: Mu’awiyah on Hilm: Man has little insight until he is forbearing
t: Ibn ‘Asakir reported: Mu’awiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “A man will not achieve the range of insight until his forbearance overcomes his ignorance, and his patience overcomes his desires. He will not achieve that unless his forbearance is strong.”

title: Ibn Dinar on Akhirah: You reap in Hereafter what you sow in life
t: Abi Hatim reported: Malik ibn Dinar, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It is written in the Torah: As you judge others, so are you judged. As you reap, so shall you sow.”

title: Hadith on Truth: Verify information before you rely upon it
t: Abu Qilabah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is an evil mount for a man to rely upon what others merely assert.”
q: It is an evil mount for a man to rely upon what others merely assert

title: Hadith on Charity: Giving in charity like freeing slaves
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever donates a gift of milk, or a piece of silver, or who guides others through a strait, he will be rewarded as if he has freed a slave.”
q: Whoever donates a gift of milk, or a piece of silver, or who guides others through a strait, he will be rewarded as if he has freed a slave.

title: Hadith on Bid’ah: Every religious innovation erases a Sunnah
t: Ghudayf ibn al-Harith reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “People do not contrive an innovation in religion but that it removes a Sunnah like it.”
q: People do not contrive an innovation in religion but that it removes a Sunnah like it.
gf: Jayyid (very good) according to Ibn Hajar

title: Hadith on Whims: The Prophet fears Muslims follow desires
t: Abu Barzah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among what I fear most for you are seductive temptations in your appetites and your lusts, and the misguidance of whims.”
q: Verily, among what I fear most for you are seductive temptations in your appetites and your lusts, and the misguidance of whims

title: Hadith on Quran: Hold fast to the Quran, you will never go astray
t: Jubayr ibn Mut’am reported: We were with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Do you not bear witness that there is no God but Allah without any partner, that I am the messenger of Allah, and that the Quran has come from Allah?” We said, “Of course.” The Prophet said, “Then rejoice, for one end of this Quran is in the hand of Allah and the other is in your hands, so hold fast to it. Verily, you will never be ruined or led astray ever again.”
q: Do you not bear witness that there is no God but Allah without any partner, that I am the messenger of Allah, and that the Quran has come from Allah … Then rejoice, for one end of this Quran is in the hand of Allah and the other is in your hands, so hold fast to it. Verily, you will never be ruined or led astray ever again.

title: Hadith on Qadr: True faith is to believe Allah controls destiny
t: Abu Darda reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Everything has a reality, and the servant will not reach the reality of faith until he knows that what afflicted him could never have missed him, and that what missed him could never have reached him.”
q: Everything has a reality, and the servant will not reach the reality of faith until he knows that what afflicted him could never have missed him, and that what missed him could never have reached him.

title: Hadith on Qadr: Believers must accept the Divine Decree
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A servant does not have faith until he believes in divine providence, both its good and its harm, and until he knows that what afflicts him could never have missed him and what missed him could have never afflicted him.”
q: A servant does not have faith until he believes in divine providence, both its good and its harm, and until he knows that what afflicts him could never have missed him and what missed him could have never afflicted him

title: Hadith on Virtues: Spread peace, be brothers as Allah commanded
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Spread peace, feed the hungry, and be brothers as Allah Almighty has commanded you.”
q: Spread peace, feed the hungry, and be brothers as Allah Almighty has commanded you.

title: Hadith on Rifq: Allah guides His beloved to kindness
t: Jarir ibn ‘Abdillah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty rewards for gentleness what He does not give for rudeness. If Allah loves a servant, then He grants him the quality of gentleness. No household is deprived of kindness but that they have been truly deprived.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty rewards for gentleness what He does not give for rudeness. If Allah loves a servant, then He grants him the quality of gentleness. No household is deprived of kindness but that they have been truly deprived
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Humility: The Prophet is not a king, so do not fear
t: Abu Mas’ud reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his voice trembled as he spoke to him. The Prophet said to him, “Be calm, for I am not a king. Verily, I am only the son of a woman who ate jerky.”
q: Be calm, for I am not a king. Verily, I am only the son of a woman who ate jerky.

title: Hadith on Salaam: Spread peace, you will receive peace
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Spread peace and you will receive peace.”
q: Spread peace and you will receive peace

title: Hadith on Greed: Love of money destroys nations
t: Abu Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Surely, there is no doubt that gold and silver coins destroyed those before you, for they are both causes of your ruin.”
q: Surely, there is no doubt that gold and silver coins destroyed those before you, for they are both causes of your ruin

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: It is enough evil to belittle a Muslim
t: Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Muslim is sacred to another Muslim: his life, his honor, and his wealth. The Muslim is the brother of another Muslim. He does not wrong him or betray him. Righteousness is here,” and he pointed to his heart. The Prophet said, “It is enough evil for a man to look down upon his Muslim brother.”
q: The Muslim is sacred to another Muslim: his life, his honor, and his wealth. The Muslim is the brother of another Muslim. He does not wrong him or betray him. Righteousness is here … It is enough evil for a man to look down upon his Muslim brother
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Rahmah: Whoever is not merciful will not receive mercy
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is not merciful to people will not be shown mercy from Allah.”
q: Whoever is not merciful to people will not be shown mercy from Allah

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Best charity is reconciliation, good relations
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best act of charity is to reconcile between people.”
q: The best act of charity is to reconcile between people.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Tyranny: When wicked rulers rule, look for the Hour
t: Abu Hurairah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings upon him, said, “When trust is lost, then wait for the Hour.” He said, “How is the trust lost, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “When authority is given to those who do not deserve it, then wait for the Hour.”
q: When trust is lost, then wait for the Hour … When authority is given to those who do not deserve it, then wait for the Hour

title: Hadith on Virtues: Prayer, reconciliation, good character best deeds
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The son of Adam does not act with anything better than prayer, reconciliation between people, and good character.”
q: The son of Adam does not act with anything better than prayer, reconciliation between people, and good character

title: Hadith on Words: People stumble with words more than their feet
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, a servant may say a word for no reason but to make people laugh, yet by it he plunges farther than the distance between heaven and earth. A man stumbles more with his tongue than with his two feet.”
q: Verily, a servant may say a word for no reason but to make people laugh, yet by it he plunges farther than the distance between heaven and earth. A man stumbles more with his tongue than with his two feet.

title: Hadith on Words: Single word earns Allah’s wrath or pleasure
t: Bilal ibn al-Harith reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, one of you may speak a word pleasing to Allah, thinking it does not amount to much, yet by it Allah decrees His pleasure with him until the day he meets Him. Verily, one of you may speak a word displeasing to Allah, thinking it does not amount to much, yet by it Allah decrees His displeasure with him until the day he meets Him.”
q: Verily, one of you may speak a word pleasing to Allah, thinking it does not amount to much, yet by it Allah decrees His pleasure with him until the day he meets Him. Verily, one of you may speak a word displeasing to Allah, thinking it does not amount to much, yet by it Allah decrees His displeasure with him until the day he meets Him

title: Hadith on Women: Best men treat women in best manner
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of you are the best to their women.”
q: The best of you are the best to their women.

title: Hadith on Trials: Every discomfort an expiation for sins
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Nothing afflicts a Muslim of hardship, nor illness, nor anxiety, nor sorrow, nor harm, nor distress, nor even the pricking of a thorn, but that Allah will expiate his sins by it.”
q: Nothing afflicts a Muslim of hardship, nor illness, nor anxiety, nor sorrow, nor harm, nor distress, nor even the pricking of a thorn, but that Allah will expiate his sins by it.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Awn on Improvement: Be a better person day after day
t: Ibn al-Mubarak reported: Awn ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “A man advised his son, saying: O my son, you must be mindful of Allah. If you are able to be better today than you were yesterday, and to be better tomorrow than you are today, then do so.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Salat: No prayer unless it prohibits from evil
t: Ibn Kathir reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “There is no prayer for one who does not obey the prayer, and obedience to prayer is to stop committing debauchery and evil.”

title: Abdullah on Humility: Is my heart too arrogant for this work?
t: Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj reported: Abdullah ibn Salaam, may Allah be pleased with him, came out from behind a building while carrying a bundle of firewood. When people saw him, they said, “O Abu Yusuf, your son and your servant are enough to help you with this!” Abdullah said, “I want to compel my heart. Is it too proud to reject this?”

title: Abu Darda on Virtue: No deeds better than prayer, good character
t: Abu Idris reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “No deeds of the children of Adam are better than walking to prayer, having exceptional character, and reconciling people.”

title: Hadith on Takfir: Excommunicating a Muslim like killing him
t: ‘Imran ibn Husayn reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a man declares his brother to be an unbeliever, it is as if he has killed him. Cursing a believer is like killing him.”
q: If a man declares his brother to be an unbeliever, it is as if he has killed him. Cursing a believer is like killing him.

title: Umar on Men: Real men are trustworthy, honorable to others
t: Ibn al-Mubarak reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Do not let yourselves be impressed by the roar of a man. Rather, if he fulfills the trust and restrains himself from harming the honor of people, he will truly be a man.”

title: Umar II on Curses: He curses his oppressor until he is even worse
t: Ribah ibn ‘Ubaydah reported: I was sitting with Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, when the ruler Al-Hajjaj was mentioned, so I reviled and denounced him. Umar said, “Calm down, O Ribah! Verily, I have heard that a man might be oppressed with a great wrong, and he continues to revile and belittle his oppressor until he forfeits his right and he owes his oppressor even more.”

title: Ibn Umar on Curses: Most hated people to Allah curse often
t: Qatadah reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, the most hateful of servants to Allah is every transgressor, cursing others.”

title: Makhul on Youth: Allah forgive the young and inexperienced
t: Ibn al-Mubarak reported: A man said to Al-Makhul, may Allah have mercy on him, “Indeed, someone has slandered you!” Al-Makhul said, “May Allah have mercy on him, for he is merely inexperienced.”

title: Hasan on Moderation: Be balanced in your love, hatred for others
t: Yahya ibn al-Mukhtar reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Love others moderately and hate others moderately. Some people were extreme in their love of others and were destroyed by it, and some people were extreme in their hatred of others and were destroyed by it. Do not be extreme in your love and do not be extreme in your hatred. Whoever finds his brother sinning beneath a veil should not expose him. Do not spy on your brother, for you have been prohibited from spying. Do not abandon him and do not alienate him.”

title: Hasan on Islam: Religion is to worship Allah, at peace with others
t: Isra’il Abi Musa reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “What is Islam? It is that you surrender your heart to Allah Almighty, and that every Muslim and protected person is safe from you.”

title: Hadith on Poverty: Less wealth means easier Judgment Day
t: Mahmud ibn Labid reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two things are hated by the son of Adam. He hates death, although it is better for the believer than tribulation, and he hates to have little wealth, although it means his reckoning will be easier.”
q: Two things are hated by the son of Adam. … He hates death, although it is better for the believer than tribulation, and he hates to have little wealth, although it means his reckoning will be easier.

title: Salaf on Satan: Devil celebrates bloodshed, unbelief, fear
t: Ibn al-Qayyim reported: Some of the righteous predecessors said, “When Iblis and his soldiers gather, they do not rejoice for anything as much as three things: a believer who kills a believer, a man who dies upon unbelief, and a heart in which is fear of poverty.”

title: Fudayl on Mercy: Whoever forgives others has defeated Satan
t: Abu Razin reported: A man came to Al-Fudayl ibn Bazwan, may Allah have mercy on him, and he said, “Indeed, a man has slandered you!” Al-Fudayl said, “Verily, I will infuriate the one who commanded him! May Allah forgive me and forgive him.” It was said, “Who has commanded him?” Al-Fudayl said, “Satan.” Ibn Farafisah said, “Whoever seeks forgiveness for his oppressor has defeated Satan.”

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Noble morals and manners leads to Paradise
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Noble character is among the deeds of Paradise.”
q: Noble character is among the deeds of Paradise

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Tawbah: Allah accepts repentance for adultery, fornication
t: ‘Alqamah reported: Abdullah Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about a man who has illicit intercourse with a woman and then marries her. Abdullah recited the verse, “Those who do evil deeds and thereafter repent and have faith, your Lord after that is forgiving and merciful.” (7:153) Abdullah recited the verse ten times, but he did not command them or prohibit them from doing so.
q: Those who do evil deeds and thereafter repent and have faith, your Lord after that is forgiving and merciful

title: Hadith on Pardon: Conceal legal offenses from punishment if possible
t:
Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Keep away from these ugly deeds that Allah has prohibited. Whoever falls into them should cover himself with the covering of Allah Almighty.”

Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It is narrated from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, that in the lifetime of the Prophet (ṣ) he commanded a man who committed a legal offense to conceal his deed. Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, commanded the same.”
q: Keep away from these ugly deeds that Allah has prohibited. Whoever falls into them should cover himself with the covering of Allah Almighty

title: Hadith on Integrity: Pleasure of Allah better than displeasure of people
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever seeks the pleasure of Allah by the displeasure of people, Allah will suffice him against the people. Whoever seeks the pleasure of people by the displeasure of Allah, Allah will leave him to the patronage of the people.”
q: Whoever seeks the pleasure of Allah by the displeasure of people, Allah will suffice him against the people. Whoever seeks the pleasure of people by the displeasure of Allah, Allah will leave him to the patronage of the people.

title: Abu Qilabah on Excuses: My brother has an excuse I do not know
t: Humayd al-Tawil reported: Abu Qilabah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you hear something about your brother that you hate, then make an effort to obtain an excuse for him. If you do not find an excuse, then say to yourself: Perhaps my brother has an excuse I do not know.”

title: Ibn Abbas on ‘Ilm: Learn from many sources, blindly follow no one
t: Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Take knowledge wherever you find it and do not uncritically accept the opinion jurists have of one another. Indeed, they differ with each other like goats in a pen.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Set right my religion, my life, my Hereafter
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, set right my religion which is a guardian of my affairs, set right my worldly life in which is my livelihood, and set right my Hereafter which is my place of return. Make life an abundance of every good and make death a relief from every evil.”
q: O Allah, set right my religion which is a guardian of my affairs, set right my worldly life in which is my livelihood, and set right my Hereafter which is my place of return. Make life an abundance of every good and make death a relief from every evil.

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet prays for his enemies to be guided
t: Jabir reported: It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, the arrows of the tribe of Thaqif have pierced us, so pray against them!” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, guide the tribe of Thaqif!”
q: O Allah, guide the tribe of Thaqif!

title: Hadith on Love: I ask you for love of good deeds and the poor
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, I ask You for good deeds, avoidance of evil deeds, and love for the poor. Forgive me, and have mercy on me. If You intend to put people to trial, take me away unscathed. I ask You for Your love, the love of those who love You, and the love of good deeds that bring me closer to Your love.”
q: O Allah, I ask You for good deeds, avoidance of evil deeds, and love for the poor. Forgive me, and have mercy on me. If You intend to put people to trial, take me away unscathed. I ask You for Your love, the love of those who love You, and the love of good deeds that bring me closer to Your love.

title: Hadith on Tawaf: Every step around the Ka’bah is rewarded
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever circles the Ka’bah seven times and prays two cycles will be rewarded as if he had freed a slave. A man does not raise his foot, nor bring it back down, but that ten good deeds will be written for him, ten bad deeds will be erased, and he will be raised by ten degrees.”
q: Whoever circles the Ka’bah seven times … and prays two cycles … will be rewarded as if he had freed a slave. A man does not raise his foot, nor bring it back down, but that ten good deeds will be written for him, ten bad deeds will be erased, and he will be raised by ten degrees

title: Hadith on Hajj: Pilgrims are special guests of Allah
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The pilgrims of Hajj and Umrah are the guests of Allah. He called them, and they answered him. They ask from Him, and He gives them.”
q: The pilgrims of Hajj and Umrah are the guests of Allah. He called them, and they answered him. They ask from Him, and He gives them

title: Hadith on Calm: Composure from Allah, haste from Satan
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Equanimity is from Allah, and rushing is from Satan.”
q: Equanimity is from Allah, and rushing is from Satan

title: Hadith on Salat: Sins fall away as they bow, prostrate
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when a servant stands to pray, his sins are placed on top of his head and shoulders. Every time he bows or prostrates, they fall away from him.”
q: Verily, when a servant stands to pray, his sins are placed on top of his head and shoulders. Every time he bows or prostrates, they fall away from him

title: Hadith on Hajj: Forgive pilgrims, those they supplicate for
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, forgive the pilgrims and those for whom the pilgrims seek forgiveness.”
q: O Allah, forgive the pilgrims and those for whom the pilgrims seek forgiveness.

title: Hadith on Arafat: Hajj culminates in day of ‘Arafah
t: ‘Abdu Rahman ibn Ya’mar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hajj is Arafat. Whoever reaches the night of Arafat before the rising of the sun at dawn the next day, he has completed his pilgrimage.”
q: The Hajj is Arafat. Whoever reaches the night of Arafat before the rising of the sun at dawn the next day, he has completed his pilgrimage.

title: Hadith on Salat: You are in prayer even as you wait for it
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One of you continues to be in prayer as long as the prayer occupies him, and nothing stops him from returning to his family but prayer.”
q: One of you continues to be in prayer as long as the prayer occupies him, and nothing stops him from returning to his family but prayer

title: Hadith on Munafiq: Hypocrites do not have manners, understand Islam
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two virtues are not combined in the hypocrite: good behavior and understanding of religion.”
q: Two virtues are not combined in the hypocrite: good behavior and understanding of religion
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Wealth: True richness is contentment in the heart
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Abu Dharr, do you say an abundance of possessions is wealth?” I said yes. The Prophet said, “Do you say a lack of possessions is poverty?” I said yes. The Prophet repeated this three times, then he said, “Wealth is in the heart and poverty is in the heart. Whoever is wealthy in his heart will not be harmed no matter what happens in the world. Whoever is impoverished in his heart will not be satisfied no matter how much he has in the world. Verily, he will only be harmed by the greed of his own soul.”
q: O Abu Dharr, do you say an abundance of possessions is wealth? … Do you say a lack of possessions is poverty? … Wealth is in the heart and poverty is in the heart. Whoever is wealthy in his heart will not be harmed no matter what happens in the world. Whoever is impoverished in his heart will not be satisfied no matter how much he has in the world. Verily, he will only be harmed by the greed of his own soul.

title: Hadith on Harm: There is no harm, reciprocating harm
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not cause harm or return harm. Whoever harms others, Allah will harm him. Whoever is harsh with others, Allah will be harsh with him.”
q: Do not cause … harm or return harm. Whoever harms others, Allah will harm him. Whoever is harsh with others, Allah will be harsh with him.

title: Hadith on Anxiety: Supplication to relieve worry and debt
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered the mosque one day while a man from the Ansar named Abu Umamah was there. The Prophet said, “O Abu Umamah, what is the matter that I see you sitting in the mosque while it is not time for prayer?” He said, “O Messenger of Allah, I am compelled by anxiety and debts.” The Prophet said, “Shall I not teach you a word to say by which Allah Almighty will relive your worry and complete your debt?” He said, “Of course, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “Say in the morning and evening: O Allah, I seek refuge in you from worry and sadness. I seek refuge in you from weakness and laziness. I seek refuge in you from cowardice and miserliness. And I seek refuge in you from being overwhelmed by debt and the tyranny of men.”
q: O Abu Umamah, what is the matter that I see you sitting in the mosque while it is not time for prayer? … Shall I not teach you a word to say by which Allah Almighty will relive your worry and complete your debt? … Say in the morning and evening: O Allah, I seek refuge in you from worry and sadness. I seek refuge in you from weakness and laziness. I seek refuge in you from cowardice and miserliness. And I seek refuge in you from being overwhelmed by debt and the tyranny of men

title: Hadith on Blessings: Health is better than wealth for believers
t: Yasar al-Juhani reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is nothing wrong with being wealthy for one who fears Allah, yet good health is better than wealth for one who fears Allah, and cheerfulness is itself among the blessings.”
q: There is nothing wrong with being wealthy for one who fears Allah, yet good health is better than wealth for one who fears Allah, and cheerfulness is itself among the blessings.

title: Hadith on Medicine: Every disease has a cure by which Allah heals
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Every disease has a cure. If a cure is applied to the disease, it is relieved by the permission of Allah Almighty.”
q: Every disease has a cure. If a cure is applied to the disease, it is relieved by the permission of Allah Almighty

title: Hadith on Medicine: Seek cure for disease from what is lawful
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah sent down the disease and the cure, and for every disease He made a cure. Seek treatment, but do not seek treatment by the unlawful.”
q: Verily, Allah sent down the disease and the cure, and for every disease He made a cure. Seek treatment, but do not seek treatment by the unlawful.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Charity: Best Muslims give food in charity to others
t: Suhayb ibn Sinan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of you are those who feed others.”
q: The best of you are those who feed others.

title: Hadith on Manners: Supplication for good character after prayer
t: Abu Umamah reported: I never prayed behind the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while I was near to him but that I would hear him say at the end of every prayer, “O Allah, forgive all of my sins and mistakes. O Allah, refresh me and protect me and guide me to righteous deeds and character, for none can guide to its righteousness and divert its evil but You.”
q: O Allah, forgive all of my sins and mistakes. O Allah, refresh me and protect me and guide me to righteous deeds and character, for none can guide to its righteousness and divert its evil but You.

title: Hadith on Enthusiasm: Energy for good deeds has a time limit
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, every deed has enthusiasm, and every enthusiasm has a time-limit. Whoever is enthusiastic for my Sunnah has succeeded, but whoever is enthusiastic for something else has been ruined.”
q: Verily, every deed has enthusiasm, and every enthusiasm has a time-limit. Whoever is enthusiastic for my Sunnah … has succeeded, but whoever is enthusiastic for something else has been ruined

title: Hadith on Imams: Obeying Muslim rulers unless they order sin
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah. Whoever obeys my deputy has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys my deputy has disobeyed me.”
q: Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah. Whoever obeys my deputy has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys my deputy has disobeyed me.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Abdullah on Hypocrisy: Time will come when mosques have no believers
t: Khaythama reported: Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “A time will come to people when they gather and pray in the mosques, yet there will not be a believer among them.”

title: Hadith on Rahmah: Mercy of Allah more beloved than the entire world
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I would not love to have the world or anything within it in exchange for this verse: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Verily, Allah forgives all sins, for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.” (39:53)
q: I would not love to have the world or anything within it in exchange for this verse: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Verily, Allah forgives all sins, for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

title: Hadith on Character: He is not one of us who is rude, cruel
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most complete of believers in faith are those with the best character, careful around others, friendly and befriended. He is not one of us who is neither friendly, nor befriended.”
q: The most complete of believers in faith are those with the best character, careful around others, friendly and befriended. He is not one of us who is neither friendly, nor befriended.

title: Hadith on Greed: The Prophet fears Muslims compete for wealth
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I do not fear poverty for you, rather I fear that you will compete for riches. I do not fear for your mistakes, rather I fear for what you do on purpose.”
q: I do not fear poverty for you, rather I fear that you will compete for riches. I do not fear for your mistakes, rather I fear for what you do on purpose.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: World is nothing but a needle in the sea
t: Al-Mustawrid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “What is the world compared to the Hereafter but like a needle dipped into ocean compared to its vast waters?”
q: What is the world compared to the Hereafter but like a needle dipped into ocean compared to its vast waters?

title: Hadith on Trials: Sickness cause by sins, but Allah holds back
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The veins and the eyes do not tremble with illness but due to sins, yet Allah repels even more.”
q: The veins and the eyes do not tremble with illness but due to sins, yet Allah repels even more

title: Hadith on Love: Allah honors those who love each other
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A servant does not love another servant for the sake of Allah Almighty but that Allah will honor him.”
q: A servant does not love another servant for the sake of Allah Almighty but that Allah will honor him

title: Hadith on Madinah: Whoever terrorizes Medina is cursed by Allah
t: Al-Sa’ib ibn Khallad reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever terrorizes the people of Medina with oppression, Allah will terrorize him. The curse of Allah, the angels, and the people altogether will be upon him. Allah will not accept his obligatory or voluntary good deeds on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever terrorizes the people of Medina with oppression, Allah will terrorize him. The curse of Allah, the angels, and the people altogether will be upon him. Allah will not accept his obligatory or voluntary good deeds on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Madinah: Whoever wrongs Medina is punished by Allah
t: Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, whoever oppresses the people of Medina and terrorizes them, terrorize him. The curse of Allah, the angels, and the people altogether will be upon him. Allah will not accept his obligatory or voluntary good deeds.”
q: O Allah, whoever oppresses the people of Medina and terrorizes them, terrorize him. The curse of Allah, the angels, and the people altogether will be upon him. Allah will not accept his obligatory or voluntary good deeds.

title: Hadith on Medina: O Allah, bless Medina in their business and trade
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, bless them in their measurements and bless them in their portions and allotments,” meaning the people of Medina.
q: O Allah, bless them in their measurements and bless them in their portions and allotments
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Madinah: Those who plot against Medina defeated by Allah
t: Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None plot against the people of Medina but that they will melt away, just as salt is melted by water.”
q: None plot against the people of Medina but that they will melt away, just as salt is melted by water
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Shaytan: Devils try to block people giving charity
t: Buraydah ibn al-Hasib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Charity does not part with a man until it is freed from the jaws of seventy devils.”
q: Charity does not part with a man until it is freed from the jaws of seventy devils.

title: Hadith on Refuge: The Prophet seeks refuge from evil moments
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would say, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from an evil day, from an evil night, from an evil moment, from an evil companion, and from an evil neighbor in the final abode.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from an evil day, from an evil night, from an evil moment, from an evil companion, and from an evil neighbor in the final abode

title: Hadith on Prayer: People would race to prayer if they knew
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If people knew the virtues in the call to prayer and the first row of prayer and that they could not get it but by drawing lots, they would surely draw lots. If they knew the virtue in joining prayer at the beginning of its time, they would race to it. If they knew the virtue in prayer at evening and at dawn, they would surely come even if they had to crawl.”
q: If people knew the virtues in the call to prayer and the first row of prayer and that they could not get it but by drawing lots, they would surely draw lots. If they knew the virtue in joining prayer at the beginning of its time, they would race to it. If they knew the virtue in prayer at evening and at dawn, they would surely come even if they had to crawl.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Siyam: Fasting is a fortress, shield for believers
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Fasting is a shield and a fortress among the fortresses of the believer. Every deed is for its companion, but Allah says: Except fasting, as it is for Me, and I will reward it.”
q: Fasting is a shield and a fortress among the fortresses of the believer. Every deed is for its companion, but Allah says: Except fasting, as it is for Me, and I will reward it.

title: Hadith on Grudges: Let go of hatred, malice, and enmity
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Forgive each other and drop the grudges between yourselves.”
q: Forgive each other and drop the grudges between yourselves.

title: Hadith on Siyam: True fasting is from falsehood and sin
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, fasting is not only from eating and drinking. Rather, fasting is from vanity and obscenity. If someone abuses you or acts foolish against you, then say: Indeed, I am fasting.”
q: Verily, fasting is not only from eating and drinking. Rather, fasting is from vanity and obscenity. If someone abuses you or acts foolish against you, then say: Indeed, I am fasting.

title: Hadith on Fasting: Nothing is similar to fasting in reward
t: Abu Umamah reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell me a deed to do.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must fast, for there is nothing equal to it.”
q: You must fast, for there is nothing equal to it

title: Hadith on Dua: O Allah, take malice out of my heart
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to supplicate, saying, “O Lord, help me and do not help anyone against me, support me and do not support anyone against me, plan for me and do not plan against me. Guide me and make guidance easy for me. Support me against those who transgress against me. O Lord, make me grateful to You, remembering of You, fearful of You, obedient to You, humble to You, penitent and repenting. O Lord, accept my repentance, wash away my sin, answer my supplication, establish my proof, direct my tongue, guide my heart, and remove resentment from my chest.”
q: O Lord, help me and do not help anyone against me, support me and do not support anyone against me, plan for me and do not plan against me. Guide me and make guidance easy for me. Support me against those who transgress against me. O Lord, make me grateful to You, remembering of You, fearful of You, obedient to You, humble to You, penitent and repenting. O Lord, accept my repentance, wash away my sin, answer my supplication, establish my proof, direct my tongue, guide my heart, and remove resentment from my chest

title: Hadith on Gratitude: People asked about their blessings first
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the first thing a servant will be asked about on the Day of Resurrection will be his blessings. It will be said to him: Have We not given you health in your body and nourished you with cool water to drink?”
q: Verily, the first thing a servant will be asked about on the Day of Resurrection will be his blessings. It will be said to him: Have We not given you health in your body and nourished you with cool water to drink?

title: Hadith on Dua: O Allah, I ask you for love and good deeds
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “David would supplicate, saying: O Allah, I ask you for your love and the love of those who love you and the deeds that will bring me your love. O Allah, make your love more beloved to me than myself and my family and even cold water.”
q: David would supplicate, saying: O Allah, I ask you for your love and the love of those who love you and the deeds that will bring me your love. O Allah, make your love more beloved to me than myself and my family and even cold water.

title: Hadith on Optimism: The Prophet was optimistic, had good expectations
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was optimistic, he did not see evil omens, and he liked good names.

title: Hadith on Love: Allah never throws His beloved into Hellfire
t: Anas reported: There was a child on the road as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed through with his companions. When the mother saw the people coming, she was afraid they would trample her son. She quickly gathered him up, saying, “My son! My son!” The companions said, “O Messenger of Allah, this woman would never cast her child into the fire.” The Prophet said, “No, and neither would Allah cast His beloved into the Hellfire.”
q: No, and neither would Allah cast His beloved into the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Salat: Blessing on the right side of prayer rows
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah and His angels send blessings upon those on the right side of the prayer rows.”
q: Verily, Allah and His angels send blessings upon those on the right side of the prayer rows.

title: Hadith on Dua: Do not supplicate against yourself, your community
t:
Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not supplicate against yourselves, do not supplicate against your children, and do not supplicate against your wealth, lest it coincide with a time in which Allah is asked and he gives and your supplication is answered.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “Do not supplicate against your servants.”
q: Do not supplicate against yourselves, do not supplicate against your children, and do not supplicate against your wealth, lest it coincide with a time in which Allah is asked and he gives and your supplication is answered. … Do not supplicate against your servants

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplications of oppressed answered, even if wicked
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The supplication of the oppressed is answered, even if he is wicked, for his wickedness is only against himself.”
q: The supplication of the oppressed is answered, even if he is wicked, for his wickedness is only against himself

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication of oppressed ascends to heaven
