q: Verily, you are in a time when one who leaves a tenth of what he has been commanded is ruined. Then, there will be a time when one who practices a tenth of what he has been commanded is saved.”

title: Aisha on Humility: Among the best acts of worship is humility
t: Ibn al-Mubarak reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “Verily, you are neglecting the best act of worship: humility.”

title: Abu Darda on Nifaq: Muslim might lose their religion after one trial
t: Jubayr ibn Nufayr reported: I entered the residence of Abu Darda while he was standing and praying in his place of prayer. When he sat down, he began fervently to recite the testimony of faith and to seek refuge in Allah from hypocrisy. After he finished, I said, “May Allah forgive you, O Abu Darda! What is it about you and hypocrisy?” Abu Darda said, “O Allah, your forgiveness! Who is safe from trial? Who is safe from trial? Who is safe from trial? By Allah, a man might be tested for only an hour and he turns away from his religion.”

title: Hadith on Graves: Plastering, writing, and sitting on graves
t:
Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited plastering over graves, writing upon them, building over them, and treading upon them.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “Some of the scholars granted a concession, among them Al-Hasan al-Basri, to put clay over the graves. Al-Shafi’i said: There is nothing wrong with putting clay over a grave.”

title: Hadith on Graves: Strong warning not to sit on graves
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “For one of you to sit upon a hot coal and burn himself and his clothes would be better than sitting upon a grave.”
q: For one of you to sit upon a hot coal and burn himself and his clothes would be better than sitting upon a grave

title: Hadith on Graves: Desecrating the dead like harming the living
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Breaking the bones of a dead person is like breaking them when he is alive.”
q: Breaking the bones of a dead person is like breaking them when he is alive.

title: Sufyan on Knowledge: Purpose of learning is to be God-fearing
t: Ibn ‘Abdul Barr reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Surely, sacred knowledge is only studied to become mindful of Allah. Knowledge is only favored over other virtues because it makes one fearful of Allah.”

title: Hadith on Rizq: You are given provision for helping the weak
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: There were two brothers in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, one of whom would attend the lessons of the Prophet and the other would engage in business. The businessman complained to the Prophet about his brother, and the Prophet said, “Perhaps you are granted provision because of him.”
q: Perhaps you are granted provision because of him.

title: Hadith on Marriage: Husband has right to wife, but may not hurt her
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a man calls his wife to bed and she refuses and he spends the night angry with her, the angels will curse her until the morning.”
q: If a man calls his wife to bed and she refuses … and he spends the night angry with her, the angels will curse her until the morning
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Duties: Enough sin for man to neglect his dependents
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is enough sin for a man to withhold from those dependent upon him.”
q: It is enough sin for a man to withhold from those dependent upon him.

title: Hadith on Death: Fear and hope at the time of death
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered the home of a young man in the throes of death. The Prophet said, “How do you feel?” The man said, “By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I hope in Allah and I fear for my sins.” The Prophet said, “These two feelings are not combined in the heart of a servant in this situation but that Allah will give him what he hopes and save him from what he fears.”
q: How do you feel? … These two feelings are not combined in the heart of a servant in this situation but that Allah will give him what he hopes and save him from what he fears

title: Umar on Dhimmi: Non-Muslims given share of public welfare
t: Abu Bakrah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by the door of some people, over which was an old blind man begging for charity. Umar tapped him on the shoulder from behind, saying, “From which People of the Book are you?” The man said, “I am a Jew.” Umar said, “What has forced you into what I see here?” The Jew said, “I am begging so I can pay tribute, for my needs and my old age.” Umar took him by the hand, went with him to his house, and offered him something from inside. Then, Umar sent him to the public treasury, saying, “Look at this man and his taxes! By Allah, we have not been fair to him, for we have eaten ourselves but left him in his old age! Allah Almighty said, ‘Verily, charity is for the poor and the needy,‘ (9:60) and ‘the poor’ are the Muslims and this man is ‘the needy’ among the People of the Book.” Thus, Umar exempted him from paying tribute and from his taxes.
q: Verily, charity is for the poor and the needy,

title: Hadith on Children: The Prophet condemns killing of children
t: Aswad ibn Sari’ reported: I came with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and participated in the battle with him. I engaged in the skirmish that day, until some people killed children. The Prophet was told about it and he said, “What is wrong with these people transgressing the limits of killing, even having killed children?” A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, they are only the children of idolaters.” The Prophet said, “No doubt, the best of you are the children of idolaters.” Then, the Prophet said, “No doubt, do not kill children! Do not kill children! Every soul is born upon its natural instinct until he expresses it with his tongue, then his father turns him into a Jew or a Christian.”
q: What is wrong with these people transgressing the limits of killing, even having killed children? … No doubt, the best of you are the children of idolaters … No doubt, do not kill children! Do not kill children! Every soul is born upon its natural instinct until he expresses it with his tongue, then his father turns him into a Jew or a Christian

title: Umar on Jizyah: Non-Muslims given from public treasury as charity
t: Abu Ja’far reported: The commander of the faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by an old man among the non-Muslim citizens who was going from house to house begging for charity. Umar said, “We have not been fair to you, that we take tribute from you in your youth and now you are helpless in your old age.” Then, Umar ordered for him to be given money from the public treasury to meet his needs.

title: Hadith on Rukhsa: Allah loves to make things easy for you
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah loves for you to take His concessions, just as He dislikes for you to be disobedient to Him.”
q: Verily, Allah loves for you to take His concessions, just as He dislikes for you to be disobedient to Him.

title: Fudayl on Faith: Believer is happy for others, has good will
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Admiration is part of faith and envy is part of hypocrisy. The believer admires others and does not envy others. The hypocrite envies others and does not admire others. The believer overlooks the faults of others, admonishes others, and gives good advice. The hypocrite disgraces others, insults others, and betrays others.”

title: Fudayl on Justice: No harming animals, how can you harm believers?
t: Al-Dhahabi reported: Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “By Allah, it is not lawful for you to harm a dog or a pig without a just cause, so how can you harm a Muslim?”

title: Hadith on Islam: Best practice of Islam is to make people safe
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man asked, “O Messenger of Allah, whose Islam is best?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Those from whose tongue and hand people are safe.”
q: Those from whose tongue and hand people are safe

title: Qatadah on Justice: Fulfill the measure as you would for yourself
t: Al-Tabari reported: Qatadah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “O son of Adam, be just as you would love justice for yourself, and fulfill the measure as you would love for it to be fulfilled for yourself. Verily, in justice is the well-being of people.”

title: Umar at Jerusalem: Covenant between Umar and the Christians
t: At-Tabari reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, made peace with the people of Jerusalem at Al-Jabiya and therein he wrote a single covenant for every village besides Jerusalem: In the name of Allah, the Gracious, the Merciful. This is what is granted of security by the servant of Allah, Umar, the commander of the faithful, to the people of Jerusalem. He grants them safety for their lives, their property, their churches, and their crucifixes, for their ill, their healthy, and their entire community. Their churches will not be occupied, demolished, or decreased in number. Their churches and crucifixes will not be desecrated and neither anything else of their property. They will not be coerced to abandon their religion and none of them will be harmed.

title: Ibn Abbas on Fatwa: Wisdom in issuing legal verdicts
t: Sa’d ibn ‘Ubaydah reported: A man came to Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said, “Is there repentance for one who kills a believer?” Ibn Abbas said, “No, there is nothing but Hellfire.” After the man left, those sitting nearby said to him, “What is this? You have given us two different judgments, for earlier you judged that whoever killed a believer may have his repentance accepted. What is the matter today?” Ibn Abbas said, “Indeed, I suspect he was an angry man intending to kill a believer.” Later they followed the man and found that it was true.

title: Hamdun on Excuses: Make seventy excuses for your brother
t: Al-Bayhaqi reported: Hamdun al-Qassar, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If one of your brothers commits an error, seek seventy excuses for him. If your hearts do not accept it, know that the fault is with yourselves.”

title: Hadith on Masajid: Mosques of Allah are gardens of Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you pass by the meadows of Paradise, graze as you like.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what are the meadows of Paradise?” The Prophet said, “The mosques.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is its grazing?” The Prophet said, “To declare the glory of Allah, the praise of Allah, the greatness of Allah, and that there is no God but Allah.”
q: When you pass by the meadows of Paradise, graze as you like … The mosques … To declare the glory of Allah, the praise of Allah, the greatness of Allah, and that there is no God but Allah.

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Circles of remembrance are gardens of Paradise
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you pass by the meadows of Paradise, graze as you like.” They said, “What are the meadows of Paradise?” The Prophet said, “Circles of remembrance.”
q: When you pass by the meadows of Paradise, graze as you like … Circles of remembrance

title: Ali on Sincerity: Believers have good will, love for each other
t: Ibn ‘Asakir reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, the believers are people with good will and love for each other, even if their lands and countries are far apart. The hypocrites are people with malevolence for each other.”

title: Hadith on Justice: When oppressed become oppressors
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, some people were weak and poor, and they were being fought by tyrants who outnumbered them. Then, Allah allowed the oppressed to prevail over them, so they seized their enemies, exploited them, and imposed rule over them. Thus, Allah is displeased with them until the Day they meet Him.”
q: “Verily, some people were weak and poor, and they were being fought by tyrants who outnumbered them. Then, Allah allowed the oppressed to prevail over them, so they seized their enemies, exploited them, and imposed rule over them. Thus, Allah is displeased with them until the Day they meet Him

title: Hadith on ‘Arafah: Best supplication on day of Arafat
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best supplication is that which is made on the day of Arafat. The best of it is what was said by myself and the Prophets before me, ‘There is no God but Allah alone, without any partners, unto Him belongs the dominion and all praise, and He has power over all things.’”
q: The best supplication is that which is made on the day of Arafat. The best of it is what was said by myself and the Prophets before me, ‘There is no God but Allah alone, without any partners, unto Him belongs the dominion and all praise, and He has power over all things.’

title: Shafi’i on Knowledge: Learn sciences of the religion and world
t: Ibn Abi Hatim reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, knowledge is only two types: knowledge of the religion and knowledge of the world. The knowledge of religion is to achieve juristic understanding (fiqh) and the knowledge of the world is medicine. Do not settle in a land in which there is no scholar to inform you about your religion, nor a doctor to inform you about your body.”

title: Hadith on Habits: Best deeds are consistent, even if small
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Take up good deeds only as much as you are able, for the best deeds are those done regularly even if they are few.”
q: Take up good deeds only as much as you are able, for the best deeds are those done regularly even if they are few

title: Hadith on Hajj: Reward for those who die during pilgrimage
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever goes out for the Hajj pilgrimage and dies, the reward of Hajj will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever goes out for the Umrah pilgrimage and dies, the reward of Umrah will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever goes out for military service and dies, the reward of military service will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever goes out for the Hajj pilgrimage and dies, the reward of Hajj will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever goes out for the Umrah pilgrimage and dies, the reward of Umrah will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever goes out for military service and dies, the reward of military service will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection
gf: Sahih li ghayri (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Charity: Speak kind words, offer peace, feed poor
t: Abu Shurayh reported: He said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell me something that will guarantee Paradise for me.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Speak kind words, offer peace, and feed the hungry.”
q: Speak kind words, offer peace, and feed the hungry

title: Hasan on Eid: Every day Muslims obey Allah a celebration
t: Ibn Rajab reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Every day in which Allah is not disobeyed is a celebration. Every day the believer spends in obedience, servitude, remembrance, and gratitude is a celebration.”

title: Hadith on Parents: Father is middle gate of Paradise
t: Abu Darda reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The father is the middle of the gates of Paradise. If you wish, you can squander this gate or keep to it.”
q: The father is the middle of the gates of Paradise. If you wish, you can squander this gate or keep to it.

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplicate in prosperity if you want answer in adversity
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever would like for Allah to answer him during times of hardship and difficulty, let him supplicate often during times of ease.”
q: Whoever would like for Allah to answer him during times of hardship and difficulty, let him supplicate often during times of ease

title: Umar on Judgment: The Caliph judges in favor of a Jew
t: Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was presented with a dispute between a Muslim and a Jew. Umar believed that the truth was on the side of the Jew, so he judged in his favor. The Jew said to him, “By Allah, you have judged with the truth!” Umar rapped him with his whip, saying, “How do you know?” The Jew said, “Indeed, we find written in the Torah that no one judges with the truth but that an angel is on his right and his left, keeping him steady and guided in truth. If he abandons the truth, they will ascend and leave him.”

title: Hadith on Akhirah: Sinful monotheists in Hellfire, then Paradise
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Some people among those who worshiped Allah alone will be punished in Hellfire until they are coals. Then, the mercy of Allah will reach them. They will be taken out and presented at the gates of Paradise. The people of Paradise will pour water over them, and they will grow just as the stubble carried by the stream grows. Then, they will enter Paradise.”
q: Some people among those who worshiped Allah alone … will be punished in Hellfire until they are coals. Then, the mercy of Allah will reach them. They will be taken out and presented at the gates of Paradise. The people of Paradise will pour water over them, and they will grow just as the stubble carried by the stream grows. Then, they will enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Zeal: Success whose energy for Islam is sincere, moderate
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, everything has a zeal, and every zeal has a timelimit. Whoever does so properly and moderately, then hope for his success. Whoever does so for people to point at him, do not count him among the righteous.”
q: Verily, everything has a zeal, and every zeal has a timelimit. Whoever does so properly and moderately, then hope for his success. Whoever does so for people to point at him, do not count him among the righteous

title: Shafi’i on Debate: I love for my opponent to be guided
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I never debated anyone but that I would love for him to be guided, directed, helped, and for him to be under the care of Allah and His protection. And I never debated with anyone but that I did not mind whether Allah clarified the truth on my tongue or his tongue.”

title: Hadith on Islam: Religion of Islam to reach everywhere in the world
t: Tamim al-Dari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “This matter will certainly reach every place touched by the night and day. Allah will not leave a house or residence but that Allah will cause this religion to enter it, by which the honorable will be honored, and the disgraceful will be disgraced. Allah will honor the honorable with Islam, and he will disgrace the disgraceful with unbelief.”
q: This matter will certainly reach every place touched by the night and day. Allah will not leave a house or residence but that Allah will cause this religion to enter it, by which the honorable will be honored, and the disgraceful will be disgraced. Allah will honor the honorable with Islam, and he will disgrace the disgraceful with unbelief

title: Hadith on Istighfar: Blessed is one who seeks forgiveness often
t: Abdullah ibn Busr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Blessed is he who finds many prayers for forgiveness in his record.”
q: Blessed is he who finds many prayers for forgiveness in his record

title: Umar II on Humility: Allah have mercy on one who shows me my flaws
t: Al-Kalabadhi reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “May Allah have mercy on a man who shows me my faults.”

title: Abu Darda on Learning: Knowledge, forbearance must be nurtured
t: Raja’ ibn Haywah reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, knowledge only comes by learning and forbearance only comes by cultivating forbearance. Whoever aims for good will receive goodness and whoever seeks to evade evil will be protected from it.”

title: Sufyan on Confidence: If you know your self, you will not be harmed
t: Ibn al-Mubarak reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you know yourself, you will not be harmed by whatever is said about you.”

title: Hadith on Patience: When practicing Islam is like holding a hot coal
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A time of patience will come to people in which adhering to one’s religion is like grasping a hot coal.”
q: A time of patience will come to people in which adhering to one’s religion is like grasping a hot coal

title: Hadith on Laylat al-Qadr: Dua on Night of Decree in Ramadan
t: Aisha reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, if I know which night is the Night of Decree, what should I say during it?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Say: O Allah, You are pardoning. You love to forgive, so forgive me.”
q: Say: O Allah, You are pardoning. You love to forgive, so forgive me

title: Hadith on Rights: Your family and own body has rights over you
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent for Uthman ibn Mazh’un and he came. The Prophet said, “O Uthman, do you not desire my practice?” Uthman said, “O Messenger of Allah, no by Allah. I seek your practice.” The Prophet said, “Verily, I sleep and I pray, I fast and I break my fast, and I marry women. Fear Allah, O Uthman, for your family has rights over you and your guest has rights over you. Verily, your own self has rights over you, so fast and break your fast, pray and sleep.”
q: O Uthman, do you not desire my practice … Verily, I sleep and I pray, I fast and I break my fast, and I marry women. Fear Allah, O Uthman, for your family has rights over you and your guest has rights over you. Verily, your own self has rights over you, so fast and break your fast, pray and sleep

title: Hadith on Fitnah: The Prophet fought to end persecution
t:
Sa’id ibn Jubayr reported: Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, came out to us, and we hoped that he would narrate to us a good tradition. A man approached him, and he said, “O Abu ‘Abdur Rahman, tell us about fighting during times of persecution, as Allah said: Fight them until there is no more persecution.” (8:39) Ibn Umar said, “Do you know what ‘persecution’ is? May your mother be bereaved of you! Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, only fought the idolaters as there was persecution to make them enter their religion. It was not like your fighting for the sake of ruling.”

In another narration, Ibn Umar said, “A man used to be persecuted for his religion, whether they killed him or tortured him, until the followers of Islam became plentiful and there was no longer persecution.”
q: Fight them until there is no more persecution

title: Umar on Nikah: Nothing benefits like a righteous spouse
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Nothing benefits a man, after faith in Allah, as much as a wife with good character, loving and fertile. Nothing harms a man, after unbelief in Allah, as much as a wife with evil character and a sharp tongue.”

title: Hadith on Funerals: The Prophet’s beautiful supplication for the deceased
t:
Awf ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, performed the funeral prayer and I memorized his supplication, “O Allah, forgive him, have mercy on him, make him well, and pardon him. Dignify his residence and make his resting place spacious. Cleanse him with water, snow, and ice. Purify him from sins just as a white garment is purified from dirt. Offer him a home better than his home, people better than his people, and a wife better than his wife. Admit him into Paradise and save him from the punishment of the grave and the Hellfire.”

Awf said, “The Prophet continued supplicating until I wished that I had been that dead person.”
q: O Allah, forgive him, have mercy on him, make him well, and pardon him. Dignify his residence and make his resting place spacious. Cleanse him with water, snow, and ice. Purify him from sins just as a white garment is purified from dirt. Offer him a home better than his home, people better than his people, and a wife better than his wife. Admit him into Paradise and save him from the punishment of the grave and the Hellfire

title: Umar on Shukr: O Allah, make us among the few grateful
t: Ibrahim al-Taymi reported: A man in front of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was saying, “O Allah, make me among the few.” Umar said, “What is this supplication?” The man said, “I heard Allah say: And few of My servants are grateful, (34:13). So I call upon Allah to make me among these few.” Umar said, “All of the people know better than Umar!”
q: And few of My servants are grateful,

title: Hadith on Dua: I seek refuge in You from evil I have done
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say in his supplications, “O Allah, I seek refuge in you from the evil I have done and the evil I have not done.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in you from the evil I have done and the evil I have not done

title: Hadith on Dua: Praising Allah remove sins like falling leaves
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by a tree with dry leaves and he struck it with his staff, making the leaves fall. The Prophet said, “Verily, the praise of Allah, the glorification of Allah, the declaration there is no God but Allah, and the exaltation of Allah remove sins from the servant just as the falling leaves of this tree.”
q: Verily, the praise of Allah … the glorification of Allah … the declaration there is no God but Allah … and the exaltation of Allah … remove sins from the servant just as the falling leaves of this tree.

title: Hasan on Muhasabah: Believers hold themselves accountable in the world
t: Ibn al-Mubarak reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, the believer is a guardian over himself and he holds himself accountable to Allah Almighty. The reckoning will only be lightened on the Day of Resurrection for people who held themselves accountable in this world. Verily, the reckoning will only be grueling on the Day of Resurrection for people who did not hold themselves accountable.”

title: Ibrahim on Mercy: A man has wronged me, I will show mercy
t: Al-Dhahabi reported: Ibrahim al-Taymi, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Indeed, a man has wronged me, so I will have mercy on him.”

title: Hadith on Benefit: Whoever can benefit his brother should do it
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever among you is able to benefit his brother, let him do so.”
q: Whoever among you is able to benefit his brother, let him do so

title: Hadith on Hasad: People will be good unless they envy
t: Damurah ibn Tha’labah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “People will continue to prosper as long as they do not envy each other.”
q: People will continue to prosper as long as they do not envy each other

title: Hadith on Muhammad: They love to see the Prophet, even at great cost
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among the strongest in love for me in my nation are some people who will come after me. One of them would wish to see me, even in place of his family and his wealth.”
q: Among the strongest in love for me in my nation are some people who will come after me. One of them would wish to see me, even in place of his family and his wealth

title: Hadith on Muhammad: I will be a Prophet-Servant, not a King
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Allah sent an angel to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, along with the Angel Gabriel, upon him be peace. The angel said, “O Muhammad, Allah Almighty has given you the choice to be a prophet-servant or a prophet-king.” The Prophet turned to Gabriel for advice, and Gabriel indicated that he should be humble. The Prophet said, “Rather, I will be a prophet-servant.” Thereafter, the Prophet never ate leisurely until he met his Lord.
q: Rather, I will be a prophet-servant

title: Hadith on Hawd: I will admire your great numbers at the Fountain
t: Al-Sunabih al-Ahmasi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No doubt, I will reach the Fountain ahead of you. I will admire your great numbers before the nations, so do not kill each after I am gone.”
q: No doubt, I will reach the Fountain … ahead of you. I will admire your great numbers before the nations, so do not kill each after I am gone.

title: Iyas on Faults: Foolish man cannot recognize his faults
t: Ibn ‘Asakir reported: Iyas ibn Mu’awiyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “No man cannot recognize the defects in his own soul but that he is the greatest of fools.” It was said, “O Abu Wathilah, what is your defect?” Iyas said, “Speaking too much.”

title: Hadith on ‘Ilm: Ask Allah for beneficial knowledge
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Ask Allah for beneficial knowledge and seek refuge in Allah from knowledge without benefit.”
q: Ask Allah for beneficial knowledge and seek refuge in Allah from knowledge without benefit.

title: Hadith on Wealth: I do not fear poverty for you, rather riches
t: Amr ibn Awf reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By Allah, it is not poverty that I fear for you, but rather I fear you will be given the wealth of the world, just as it was given to those before you. You will compete for it just as they competed for it, and it will ruin you just as it ruined them.”
q: By Allah, it is not poverty that I fear for you, but rather I fear you will be given the wealth of the world, just as it was given to those before you. You will compete for it just as they competed for it, and it will ruin you just as it ruined them
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fitnah: What if the world is given to you?
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If the treasures of Persia and Rome were opened for you, what kind of people will you be?” Abdur Rahman ibn Awf said, “We will be as Allah has ordered us.” The Prophet said, “Perhaps you will be something else. You will compete with each other, then envy each other, then turn away from each other, then hate each other, and so on. Then, you will go to the poor emigrants and make some of them slavedrivers over others.”
q: If the treasures of Persia and Rome were opened for you, what kind of people will you be … Perhaps you will be something else. You will compete with each other, then envy each other, then turn away from each other, then hate each other, and so on. Then, you will go to the poor emigrants and make some of them slavedrivers over others.

title: Hadith on ‘Ilm: Virtue of knowledge over worship
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The virtue of knowledge is more beloved to me than the virtue of worship, and the best of your religion is conscientious piety.”
q: The virtue of knowledge is more beloved to me than the virtue of worship, and the best of your religion is conscientious piety

title: Hadith on Prayer: O Allah, guide me to righteous character
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, my prayer, my rites, my life, and my death are for Allah the Lord of the worlds. He has no partner and with this I have been commanded and I am among the Muslims. O Allah, guide me to the best deeds and the best character, for no one guides to the best of them but you. Protect me from evil deeds and evil character, for no one protects from the evil of them but you.”
q: Verily, my prayer, my rites, my life, and my death are for Allah the Lord of the worlds. He has no partner and with this I have been commanded and I am among the Muslims. O Allah, guide me to the best deeds and the best character, for no one guides to the best of them but you. Protect me from evil deeds and evil character, for no one protects from the evil of them but you

title: Hadith on Charms: Whoever wears an amulet is entrusted to it
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever ties a knot and blows on it has performed magic, and whoever performs magic has committed idolatry. Whoever hangs something as a charm will be entrusted to it.”
q: Whoever ties a knot and blows on it has performed magic, and whoever performs magic has committed idolatry. Whoever hangs something as a charm will be entrusted to it

title: Hadith on Spells: Amulets and charms are forbidden medicine
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, magic spells, amulets, and charms are acts of idolatry.” Abdullah’s wife, Zaynab, said, “Why do you say this? By Allah, I would go to a Jewish man when my eye was discharging. He would invoke a spell over me, and then it would calm.” Abdullah said, “This is the work of Satan who was picking at it with his hand, and when the man uttered the spell, he stopped. Verily, it is enough for you to say as the Prophet said: Take away the pain, O Lord of the people, and heal it for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no trace of illness.”
q: Verily, magic spells, amulets, and charms are acts of idolatry. … Take away the pain, O Lord of the people, and heal it for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no trace of illness.

title: Hadith on Nikah: Marrying couples of similar age
t: Buraydah reported: Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, offered a marriage proposal to the Prophet’s daughter Fatimah. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “She is too young.” Then, Ali proposed to Fatimah and the Prophet married her to him.
q: She is too young

title: Hadith on Dua: Bring us new moon with faith, peace, Islam
t: Talhah ibn ‘Ubayd reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saw the crescent moon, he would say, “O Allah, bring it over us with blessings and faith, safety and Islam. My Lord and your Lord is Allah.”
q: O Allah, bring it over us with blessings and faith, safety and Islam. My Lord and your Lord is Allah

title: Hadith on Silence: The silent saved from speaking evil
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is silent has been saved.”
q: Whoever is silent has been saved

title: Hadith on Jannah: Last deeds are righteous, enter Paradise
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever declares there is no God but Allah, seeking the countenance of Allah as his last deed, he will enter Paradise. Whoever fasts a day, seeking the countenance of Allah as his last deed, he will enter Paradise. Whoever gives in charity, seeking the countenance of Allah as his last deed, he will enter Paradise.”
q: Whoever declares there is no God but Allah, seeking the countenance of Allah as his last deed, he will enter Paradise. Whoever fasts a day, seeking the countenance of Allah as his last deed, he will enter Paradise. Whoever gives in charity, seeking the countenance of Allah as his last deed, he will enter Paradise
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Silence: Nothing deserves jail like the tongue
t: ‘Anbas ibn ‘Uqbah reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “By Allah, besides whom there is no God, nothing on earth is in greater need of a lengthy prison sentence than the tongue.”

title: Umayr on Belief: Faith increases if we remember our Lord
t: Abu Ja’far reported: ‘Umayr ibn Habib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Faith increases and decreases.” It was said, “How does it increase and decrease?” ‘Umayr said, “If we remember our Lord and fear him, it will increase. If we are heedless and we forget and we waste our time,  it will decrease.”

title: Ahnaf on Envy: No rest for the envious, hateful
t: Al-Bayhaqi reported: Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Five are as I say: There is no rest for the envious, there is no manhood for the liar, there is no loyalty for kings, there is no escape for the miser, and there is no respect for bad character.”

title: Hadith on Masjid: Believers in mosques are guest of Allah
t: Salman reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever performs ablution well in his home and then comes to the mosque, he is the guest of Allah, and it is a duty upon the Host to honor his guest.”
q: Whoever performs ablution well in his home and then comes to the mosque, he is the guest of Allah, and it is a duty upon the Host to honor his guest.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Conviction: Patience half of faith, certainty all of faith
t: ‘Alqamah reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Patience is half of faith and conviction is faith in its entirety.”

title: Hadith on Sins: We have hope for people of major sins
t: Ibn Umar reported: We withheld ourselves from seeking forgiveness for people of major sins until we heard our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say, “Verily, I have delayed my intercession for the people of major sins among my nation for the Day of Resurrection.” Ibn Umar said, “Thus, we restrained much of what was in ourselves and we had hope for them.”
q: Verily, I have delayed my intercession for the people of major sins among my nation for the Day of Resurrection

title: Hadith on Hijrah: Best emigration is to leave what Allah dislikes
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man asked, “O Messenger of Allah, which emigration is best?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “To emigrate away from that which Allah disapproves. Emigration is of two kinds: the emigration of the resident and the bedouin. As for the emigration of the bedouin, he responds when he is called and he obeys when he is commanded. As for the emigration of the resident, its trial is more severe and its reward is greater.”
q: To emigrate away from that which Allah disapproves. Emigration is of two kinds: the emigration of the resident and the bedouin. As for the emigration of the bedouin, he responds when he is called and he obeys when he is commanded. As for the emigration of the resident, its trial is more severe and its reward is greater

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Allah loves good character, silent reflection
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, met Abu Dharr and he said, “O Abu Dharr, shall I not tell you of two qualities that are easy on your back and heavier on the scale of good than others?” Abu Dharr said, “Of course, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “You must have good character and observe long periods of silence. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one can behave with deeds more beloved to Allah than these two.”
q: O Abu Dharr, shall I not tell you of two qualities that are easy on your back and heavier on the scale of good than others? … You must have good character and observe long periods of silence. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one can behave with deeds more beloved to Allah than these two

title: Wahb on Akhirah: Parable of world and Hereafter is two wives
t: Ibn al-Mubarak reported: Wahb ibn Munabbih, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The parable of this world and the Hereafter is that of a man with two wives. If he pleases one of them, he will displease the other.”

title: Hasan on Ali: Hasan descreibes virtues of Ali ibn Abi Talib
t:
‘Amr ibn Hubshi reported: Hasan ibn Ali addressed the people after the killing of Ali ibn Abi Talib and he said, “A man has departed you yesterday whom none from the early generation could surpass in knowledge and none from the later generation will match him. If the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would send him with the banner, he would not give up until victory had been granted to him. He did not leave behind any gold or silver except for seven hundred coins of his stipend that he kept to buy a servant for his family.”

In another narration, Hasan said, “A man has departed you yesterday who was surpassed in knowledge by none from the early generation and none from the later generation will match him. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent him with the banner, with Gabriel on his right side and Michael on his left. He did not give up until he was granted victory.”

title: Hasan on Khawarij: Rebels fight for sake of the world, not Islam
t: Abu Hayyan al-Tawhidi reported: A man from the Khawarij came to Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, and he said, “What do you say about the rebels?” Hasan said, “They are seekers of the world.” The man said, “Why do you say that when one of them goes out with his spear until it breaks and he leaves his family and children?” Hasan said, “Tell me about the ruler. Does he prevent you from establishing prayer, giving charity, and performing the pilgrimage?” The man said no. Hasan said, “As I see it, he has only prevented you from seeking the world and you have fought him for it.”

title: Sufyan on Akhirah: Take care of your Hereafter, Allah takes care of you
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Behave well in your private life and Allah will make your public life excellent. Take care of what is between you and Allah, and he will take care of what is between you and the people. Work for your Hereafter and Allah will suffice your affairs in this world. Sell your worldly life for your Hereafter and you will profit in them both together, and do not sell your Hereafter for your worldly life or you will lose them both together.”

title: Sufyan on Mercy: Be merciful to common people, even if they wrong you
t: Abu Nu’aim reported: Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Do not hate anyone who obeys Allah. Be merciful to the common people and their leaders. Do not sever family ties, and keep good relations with those who cut you off. Keep good relations with them, even if they cut you off. Overlook those who wrong you, for you will be a companion to the prophets and the martyrs.”

title: Hasan on Jihad: Best jihad is against your soul, desires
t: Ibn al-Qayyim reported: It was said to Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, “O Abu Sa’id, which jihad is best?” Hasan said, “Your jihad against your desires.”

title: Sa’id on Rulers: Beware of scholars who frequently visit rulers
t: Ibn Muflih reported: Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you see a scholar become too close the rulers, beware of him for he is a thief.”

title: Hadith on Rulers: Beware of closeness to political leadership
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever goes to the gates of the ruler will be put to trial. A servant does not move closer to the ruler but that he moves further away from Allah.”
q: Whoever goes to the gates of the ruler will be put to trial. A servant does not move closer to the ruler but that he moves further away from Allah

title: Hadith on Paradise: Story of the last man to enter Paradise
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I know who will be the last to come out of the Hellfire and the last to enter Paradise. He is a man who will come out of the Hellfire crawling. Allah will say to him: Go and enter Paradise. The man will go out but imagine it is full, so he will return and say: O Lord, I have found it full. Allah will say: Go and enter Paradise and you will have as much as the world and ten times more. The man will say: Do You mock me or laugh at me while you are the King?”
q: Verily, I know who will be the last to come out of the Hellfire and the last to enter Paradise. He is a man who will come out of the Hellfire crawling. Allah will say to him: Go and enter Paradise. The man will go out but imagine it is full, so he will return and say: O Lord, I have found it full. Allah will say: Go and enter Paradise and you will have as much as the world and ten times more. The man will say: Do You mock me or laugh at me while you are the King?
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Trees planted in Paradise when praising Allah
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever declares the glory of Allah and his praise will have a palm tree planted for him in Paradise.”
q: Whoever declares the glory of Allah and his praise will have a palm tree planted for him in Paradise.

title: Hadith on Debts: Allah merciful to lenitent creditor
t: Hudhayfa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The angels received the soul of a man who lived before you. They said: Have you done anything good? The man said no. They said: Try to remember. The man said: I used to give loans and I would order my servants to give respite to those in difficulty, and to overlook the faults of those in ease. Allah Almighty said: Overlook his faults.”
q: The angels received the soul of a man who lived before you. They said: Have you done anything good? The man said no. They said: Try to remember. The man said: I used to give loans and I would order my servants to give respite to those in difficulty, and to overlook the faults of those in ease. Allah Almighty said: Overlook his faults.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Leniency: Allah rewards gentleness in business
t: Uthman ibn Affan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty will admit a man into Paradise who was lenient in his buying and his selling, in his paying debts and his seeking repayments.”
q: Allah Almighty will admit a man into Paradise who was lenient in his buying and his selling, in his paying debts and his seeking repayments

title: Zuhri on Character: Our lessons in manners were better for us
t: Al-Awza’i reported: Al-Zuhri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “We would come to a scholar and what we learned from his manners was more beloved to us than his knowledge.”

title: Hadith on Virtues: Best deeds are faith, jihad, patience, tolerance
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Prophet of Allah, which deed is best?” The Prophet said, “Faith in Allah, belief in Him, and jihad in His way.” The man said, “O Messenger of Allah, I want something easier than this.” The Prophet said, “Behave with tolerance and patience.” The man said, “O Messenger of Allah, I want something easier than this.” The Prophet said, “Do not blame Allah Almighty in anything He has decreed for you.”
q: Faith in Allah, belief in Him, and jihad in His way. … Behave with tolerance and patience … Do not blame Allah Almighty in anything He has decreed for you
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (authentic) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Allah boasts to Angels of His remembrance
t: Mu’awiyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to a gathering of his Companions, saying, “Why are you sitting?” They said, “We are sitting to remember Allah, to praise him for guiding us to Islam and for blessing us with it.” The Prophet said, “Are you only sitting like this for the sake of Allah?” They said, “By Allah, we are only sitting for this reason.” The Prophet said, “Surely, I would not ask for your oath because I doubt you, but rather Gabriel has told me that Allah Almighty is boasting of you before the angels.”
q: Why are you sitting … Are you only sitting like this for the sake of Allah … Surely, I would not ask for your oath because I doubt you, but rather Gabriel has told me that Allah Almighty is boasting of you before the angels.

title: Malik on ‘Ilm: Knowledge is a light, not just information
t:
Ibn Wahb reported: Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Knowledge is a light that Allah places wherever he wills. It does not consist of memorizing many narrations.”

In another narration, Malik said, “Knowledge is not knowing many narrations. Verily, knowledge is only a light that Allah places in the hearts.”

title: Hadith on Bloodshed: Worst tyrants kill innocents for revenge
t: Abu Shurayh reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most tyrannical of people to Allah Almighty is one who kills those who never killed anyone, or he demands the blood feuds of ignorance be settled by the people of Islam, or he claims his eyes have seen in a dream what they did not see.”
q: Verily, the most tyrannical of people to Allah Almighty is one who kills those who never killed anyone, or he demands the blood feuds of ignorance be settled by the people of Islam, or he claims his eyes have seen in a dream what they did not see.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Umar on Compassion: You are believers as Muslims hunger?
t: Murih ibn Masruq reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “You consider yourselves to be believers while among you a believer is starving?”

title: Hadith on Roads: Remove harmful things from pathways
t: Abu Barzah reported: I said, “O Prophet of Allah, teach me something that will benefit me.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Remove harmful things from the roads of the Muslims.”
q: Remove harmful things from the roads of the Muslims

title: Abu Bakr on Hudud: I prefer Allah to cover their sins
t:
Zubayd ibn al-Salt reported: Abu Bakr al-Sidiq, may Allah be pleased with him, say, “Were I to take hold of a drinker of wine, I would prefer for Allah to cover his sin. Were I to take hold of a thief, I would prefer for Allah to cover his sin.”

In another narration, Abu Bakr said, “If I found nothing with the thief, the adulterer, and the drinker of wine but my robe, I would prefer to cover them with it.”

title: Hadith on Alcohol: Gradual prohibition of wine, intoxicants
t: ‘Amr ibn Shurahbil reported: When the prohibition of wine was yet to be declared, Umar ibn al-Khattab said, “O Allah, give us a clear explanation of wine.” Allah revealed the verse, “They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin,” (2:219). Umar was called and it was recited to him, then he said, “O Allah, give us a clear explanation of wine.” Allah revealed the verse, “O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated,” (4:43). Umar was called and it was recited him, then he said, “O Allah, give us a clear explanation of wine.” Allah revealed the verse, “Satan only wants to cause animosity and hatred between you through intoxicants and gambling and to divert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not abstain?” (5:91). Umar was called and it was recited to him, then he said, “We have abstained.”
q: They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin … O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated … Satan only wants to cause animosity and hatred between you through intoxicants and gambling and to divert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not abstain?

title: Hadith on Khamr: Muslims abandon alcohol when the verse comes
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was addressing people in Medina, saying, “O people, Allah Almighty is alluding to wine. Perhaps Allah will soon reveal an order regarding it. Whoever has some of it, let him sell it and benefit from it.” We did not wait but a little while until the Prophet said, “Verily, Allah Almighty has forbidden wine. Whoever knows this verse and has some of it, let him neither drink it nor sell it.” The people came out into the street with what they had and poured it out.
q: O people, Allah Almighty is alluding to wine. Perhaps Allah will soon reveal an order regarding it. Whoever has some of it, let him sell it and benefit from it … Verily, Allah Almighty has forbidden wine. Whoever knows this verse and has some of it, let him neither drink it nor sell it

title: Hadith on Fasting: Easy reward for fasting short winter days
t: ‘Amir ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Fasting in the winter is the easy reward.”
q: Fasting in the winter is the easy reward.

title: Shafi’i on Fatwa: Scholars disliked to say Halal or Haram
t:
Al-Shafi’i reported: Abu Yusuf, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I know our elders among the scholars would dislike to say in their verdicts that this is lawful and this is unlawful, unless it was clearly found in the Book of Allah Almighty, without needing to be explained.”

Ibrahim al-Nakha’i narrated from his companions, “When they intended to issue a verdict on something, or prohibit something, they would say ‘this is disliked’ or ‘there is no harm in it.’ As for when we say this is lawful and this is unlawful, there is nothing greater than this.”

title: Hadith on Signs: People wear the Mark of the Beast
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Beast will emerge and place a mark on the faces of the people. There will be so many among you such that a man will purchase a camel, and it will be said: From whom did you buy it? He will say: I bought it from one of those with the mark.”
q: The Beast will emerge and place a mark on the faces of the people. There will be so many among you such that a man will purchase a camel, and it will be said: From whom did you buy it? He will say: I bought it from one of those with the mark

title: Al-Warraq on Nearness: Seek nearness to Allah by asking from Him and not people
t: Muhammad ibn Hamid reported: I asked Abu Bakr Al-Warraq, “Teach me something that will bring me closer to people.” Abu Bakr said, “As for what brings you closer to Allah, then continue to ask him. As for what brings you closer to people, then stop asking from them.”

title: Hadith on Muhammad: A man who loves the Prophet more than anything
t: Aisha reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I love you more than myself, more than my family and wealth. You are more beloved to me than my children. I would be in my house and remember you until I cannot wait to see you. When I remember my death and your death, I know you will enter Paradise with the status of the prophets, but if I enter Paradise I am afraid I will not see you.” The Prophet did not answer him with anything until Gabriel, upon him be peace, was sent with this verse, “Whoever obeys Allah and the messenger, they will be with those whom Allah has blessed among the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous.” (4:69)
q: Whoever obeys Allah and the messenger, they will be with those whom Allah has blessed among the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Ahmad Shakir

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet’s supplication for leaving home
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say when leaving the house, “In the name of Allah, I trust in Allah. O Allah, we seek refuge in You from misstepping or being led astray, from wronging or being wronged, from abusing or being abused.”
q: In the name of Allah, I trust in Allah. O Allah, we seek refuge in You from misstepping or being led astray, from wronging or being wronged, … from abusing or being abused

title: Ibrahim on Dua: Why are our supplications not answered?
t: Al-Qurtubi reported: It was said to Ibrahim ibn Adham, “What is wrong with us that we supplicate and receive no answer?” Ibrahim said, “It is because you know Allah and you do not obey him. You know the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and you do not follow him or his Sunnah. You know the Quran and you do not act according to it. You eat from the blessings of Allah and you are not thankful for it. You know Paradise and you do not seek it. You know Hellfire and you do not flee from it. You know Satan and you do not fight him, rather you agree with him. You know death and you do not prepare for it. You bury the dead and you do not learn from it. You ignore your own faults and you are busy with the faults of other people.”

title: Hadith on Leadership: Woe to rulers who will regret everything
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessing be upon him, said, “Woe to the rulers! Woe to the chiefs! Woe to the trustees! On the Day of Resurrection, some people will wish that their hair was hanging from the sky and swinging between heaven and earth, rather than had done anything they did.”
q: Woe to the rulers! Woe to the chiefs! Woe to the trustees! On the Day of Resurrection, some people will wish that their hair was hanging from the sky and swinging between heaven and earth, rather than had done anything they did

title: Hadith on ‘Afiyah: I ask for wellness in this life, the Hereafter
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, never forgot to say these supplications whenever he entered morning and evening, “O Allah, I ask You for wellness in this world and in the Hereafter. O Allah, I ask You for forgiveness and wellness in my religion and in my worldly affairs, in my family and in my property. O Allah, cover my faults and protect me from what I fear. O Allah, guard me from the front and the back, from the right and the left, and from above. I seek refuge in Your greatness from a catastrophe underneath me.”
q: O Allah, I ask You for wellness in this world and in the Hereafter. O Allah, I ask You for forgiveness and wellness in my religion and in my worldly affairs, in my family and in my property. O Allah, cover my faults and protect me from what I fear. O Allah, guard me from the front and the back, from the right and the left, and from above. I seek refuge in Your greatness from a catastrophe underneath me.

title: Sufyan on Reason: Intelligent person follows good, avoids evil
t: Bishr ibn al-Harith reported: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The reasonable person is not one who merely recognizes good and evil. Rather, the reasonable person is only one who follows good when he sees it and avoids evil when he sees it.”

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Beware of the little black tribulation
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he mentioned many trials until he mentioned a trial in which people should remain in their houses. It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is this trial in which people should remain in their houses?” The Prophet said, “It is evacuation and war. Then there will come a trial which appears pleasant. Its murkiness is due to the coming of a man from my household who imagines that he is part of me but he is not, for my allies are only the righteous who fear Allah. Then the people will gather under a man unstable like a hip bone over a rib. Then there will be the little black tribulation which not leave anyone from this nation unaffected, and just when people say it is finished it will be extended further. During this trial a man will be a believer in the morning and an unbeliever by evening, such that people will be in two camps: the camp of faith without hypocrisy and the camp of hypocrisy without faith. When that happens, then expect the False Messiah to emerge that day or the next.”
q: It is evacuation and war. Then there will come a trial which appears pleasant. Its murkiness is due to the coming of a man from my household who imagines that he is part of me but he is not, for my allies are only the righteous who fear Allah. Then the people will gather under a man unstable like a hip bone over a rib. Then there will be the little black tribulation which not leave anyone from this nation unaffected, and just when people say it is finished it will be extended further. During this trial a man will be a believer in the morning and an unbeliever by evening, such that people will be in two camps: the camp of faith without hypocrisy and the camp of hypocrisy without faith. When that happens, then expect the False Messiah to emerge that day or the next

title: Hadith on Fitnah: A trial coming in which to flee, not fight
t: Abu Musa al-Ash’ari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, before the Hour there will be a tribulation like pieces of the dark night in which a man may be a believer in the morning but an unbeliever by evening, or a believer in the evening but an unbeliever by morning. He who sits down during it will be better than one who rises up, and he who walks during it will be better than one running.”
q: Verily, before the Hour there will be a tribulation like pieces of the dark night in which a man may be a believer in the morning but an unbeliever by evening, or a believer in the evening but an unbeliever by morning. He who sits down during it will be better than one who rises up, and he who walks during it will be better than one running.

title: Hadith on Hasan: O Allah, love whoever loves Hasan ibn Ali
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Hasan ibn Ali, “O Allah, I love him, so love him and whoever loves him.”
q: O Allah, I love him, so love him and whoever loves him
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Peace: Obligation to accept peace offerings from enemy
t: Ibn Abbas reported: A man from the tribe of Sulaym passed by a group of companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he had some sheep with him. The man greeted them with peace and they said, “He only offered peace to protect himself.” They attacked him, killed him, and took his sheep. They went to the Prophet with them and Allah Almighty revealed the verse, “O you who have faith, when you go forth in the cause of Allah, do not say to whoever greets you with peace that you are not a believer.” (4:94)
q: O you who have faith, when you go forth in the cause of Allah, do not say to whoever greets you with peace that you are not a believer

title: Hadith on ‘Ashura: The day Moses fasted to thank Allah
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to Medina and he found the Jews fasting on the day of ‘Ashura. The Prophet said, “What is this day you are fasting?” They said, “This is a great day in which Allah saved Moses and his people, and he drowned Pharaoh and his people. Moses fasted on it due to gratitude, so we also fast on it.” The Prophet said, “We are more worthy and closer to Moses than you.” The Prophet fasted the day of ‘Ashura and he commanded fasting on it.
q: What is this day you are fasting … We are more worthy and closer to Moses than you
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sahaba: Do not speak badly of the Prophet’s companions
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Leave my companions alone. By the One in whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend as much gold as the mountain of Uhud in charity, you would still not reach their level of good deeds.”
q: Leave my companions alone. By the One in whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend as much gold as the mountain of Uhud in charity, you would still not reach their level of good deeds

title: Hadith on Madinah: The Prophet loves his city Medina
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, returned from a journey and saw the walls of Medina from afar, he would quicken his pace and, if he was on an animal, he would make it gallop out of his love for Medina.

title: Umar on Rights: I fear Allah will ask me about my animals
t: Dawud ibn Ali reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “If a lost sheep under my care were to die on the banks of the Euphrates, I would expect Allah the Exalted to question me about it on the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Sufyan on Sabr: Three traits are part of patience
t: Yusuf ibn Absat reported: Sufyan a-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Three qualities are part of patience: not speaking about your sins, nor your pain, nor the purity of your heart.”

title: Hadith on Takfir: Accuser closer to unbelief than accused
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I fear for you that a man will recite the Quran, until his resplendence is seen and he is a supporter of Islam. Then, he changes into whatever Allah wills for him, such that it is stripped from him and he throws it behind his back, assaulting his neighbor with the sword and accusing him of idolatry.” I said, “O Prophet of Allah, which one is closer to idolatry? The accused or the accuser?” The Prophet said, “Rather, it is the accuser.”
q: Verily, I fear for you that a man will recite the Quran, until his resplendence is seen and he is a supporter of Islam. Then, he changes into whatever Allah wills for him, such that it is stripped from him and he throws it behind his back, assaulting his neighbor with the sword and accusing him of idolatry … Rather, it is the accuser

title: Hadith on Khawarij: Violent rebels are dogs of Hellfire
t: Ibn Abi Awfa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The khawarij are the dogs of Hellfire.”
q: The khawarij … are the dogs of Hellfire

title: Hadith on Graves: O Anas, do not pray towards the graves
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, saw me while I was praying near a grave and he raised his voice, saying, “The grave!” I thought he said something else, so I looked toward the sky. Umar came and he said, “Indeed, I said the grave. Do not pray towards it.”

title: Hadith on Sahaba: I enjoin you to follow my companions
t: Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I enjoin you to follow my companions, then those after them and those after them. Thereafter, falsehood will spread until a man offers his oath without being asked and a witness gives testimony without being asked. No doubt, a man is not in seclusion with a woman but that Satan is the third of them. Hold fast to the community and beware of division, for Satan is with one alone and he is further from two together. Whoever wants the best place in Paradise, let him hold fast to the community. Whoever rejoices with his good deeds and is saddened by his evil deeds is the believer among you.”
q: I enjoin you to follow my companions, then those after them and those after them. Thereafter, falsehood will spread until a man offers his oath without being asked and a witness gives testimony without being asked. No doubt, a man is not in seclusion with a woman but that Satan is the third of them. Hold fast to the community and beware of division, for Satan is with one alone and he is further from two together. Whoever wants the best place in Paradise, let him hold fast to the community. Whoever rejoices with his good deeds and is saddened by his evil deeds is the believer among you

title: Hasan on Backbiting: Hasan sends gifts to those who backbite him
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khadimi reported: A man said to Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, “Indeed, someone has backbitten you!” Hasan sent a dish of sweet dates to the backbiter and he said, “I heard that you have given me your good deeds as a gift, so I want to repay you for it, but please excuse me for I am unable to completely repay you.”

title: Ibn Qayyim on Fatwa: Rulings may change by time, place, condition
t: Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, writes, “As for knowing the condition of people, this is a tremendous principle required of the scholar and judge. For if he does not have a proper understanding of commanding and forbidding and then he applies one judgment over another, it will cause more harm than benefit. Indeed, if he does not understand the condition of people in the matter, he will make the oppressor appear like the oppressed and vice versa, he will make the truth appear like falsehood and vice versa and he will spread its deceit, treachery, and fraud. He will make heresy appear as righteousness and falsehood appear as truth, and he will dress every lie in a false garment beneath which is sin and wickedness. It is ignorance of the people, their circumstances, their customs, and their traditions for which he cannot distinguish this from that. Rather, the scholar must understand the tendency of people to plot, deceive, and defraud, as well as their customs and traditions. Indeed, the judgment (fatwa) changes with the change of time, place, custom, and circumstance. All of this is from the religion of Allah as has been explained, and success comes from Allah.”

title: Umar on II Secrecy: Beware secret religious cults of misguidance
t: Al-Awza’i reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you see people meeting in secret for their religion to the exclusion of the public, then know that they are establishing misguidance.”

title: Hadith on Medina: The Prophet intercedes for those patient in Madinah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one is patient with the rigors and hardship of Medina but that I will be an intercessor for him or a witness on his behalf.”
q: No one is patient with the rigors and hardship of Medina but that I will be an intercessor for him or a witness on his behalf

title: Hadith on Khawarij: Rebels with beautiful preaching, evil deeds
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will be division and sectarianism in my nation, and a people will come with beautiful words and evil deeds. They will recite the Quran, but it will not pass beyond their throats. They will leave the religion as an arrow leaves its target, and they will not return to it as the arrow does not return to its bow. They are the worst of the creation. Blessed are those who fight them and are killed by them. They call to the Book of Allah, but they have nothing to do with it. Whoever fights them is better to Allah than them.”
q: There will be division and sectarianism in my nation, and a people … will come with beautiful words and evil deeds. They will recite the Quran, but it will not pass beyond their throats. They will leave the religion as an arrow leaves its target, and they will not return to it as the arrow does not return to its bow. They are the worst of the creation. Blessed are those who fight them and are killed by them. They call to the Book of Allah, but they have nothing to do with it. Whoever fights them is better to Allah than them

title: Hadith on Kufr: Unbelievers rewarded in this life only
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when the unbeliever performs a good deed, he is given a taste of its reward in the world. As for the believer, Allah will store his good deeds for him in the Hereafter and provide his sustenance in the world due to his obedience.”
q: Verily, when the unbeliever performs a good deed, he is given a taste of its reward in the world. As for the believer, Allah will store his good deeds for him in the Hereafter and provide his sustenance in the world due to his obedience

title: Hadith on Captives: The Prophet’s good treatment of prisoners
t: Abu ‘Aziz ibn ‘Umayr reported: I was among the prisoners of war on the day of the battle of Badr. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I enjoin you to treat the captives well.” I was among a group of the Ansar. When the time of their lunch or dinner arrived, they would eat dates and I was fed bread due to the Messenger of Allah’s command for them.
q: I enjoin you to treat the captives well.

title: Hadith on Munkar: Allah punishes people who do not condemn evil
t: Adi’ al-Kindi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty will not punish a community for the sins of a few unless they see evil appear among themselves and, while they are able to reject it, they do not. If they do not, then Allah will punish the sinners and the entire community.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty will not punish a community for the sins of a few unless they see evil appear among themselves and, while they are able to reject it, they do not. If they do not, then Allah will punish the sinners and the entire community

title: Hadith on Satan: Devil sits with those who curse each other
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man insulted Abu Bakr while the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was sitting down. The Prophet was initially impressed by Abu Bakr and he smiled, but then Abu Bakr insulted the man with some of the same words as him. The Prophet became angry and he stood to leave. Abu Bakr went to the Prophet, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, the man insulted me, and you were sitting, but when I responded in kind, you became angry and stood up.” The Prophet said, “Verily, there was an angel with you responding on your behalf, but Satan appeared when you responded with some of the same words as him. I will not sit in the presence of Satan.”
q: Verily, there was an angel with you responding on your behalf, but Satan appeared when you responded with some of the same words as him. I will not sit in the presence of Satan

title: Ibn Qayyim on Hearts: A void that can only be filled by love of Allah
t: Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “In the heart are disorders that cannot be remedied except by responding to Allah. In it is a desolate feeling that cannot be removed except by intimacy with Him solitude. In it is sadness which will not leave except by happiness with knowing Him and truthfulness in his dealings. In it is anxiety that is not made tranquil except by gathering for His sake and fleeing to Him from His punishment. In it is a fire of regret which cannot be extinguished except by satisfaction with His commands, prohibitions, and decrees, and embracing patience with that until the time he meets Him. In it is a strong desire that will not cease until He is the only one who is sought. In it is a void that cannot be filled except by His love, turning to Him, always remembering Him, and being sincere to Him. Were a person to be given the entire world and everything in it, that would never fill the void.”

title: Hadith on Greetings: Shaking hands erases sins
t: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when the believer meets another believer, greets him with peace, and shakes his hand, the sins of them both will shed like leaves falling from a tree.”
q: Verily, when the believer meets another believer, greets him with peace, and shakes his hand, the sins of them both will shed like leaves falling from a tree.

title: Ibn Mubarak on Respect: Do not belittle three types of people
t: Al-Dhahabi reported: Ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It is a duty upon the wise man not to belittle three persons: the scholars, the authorities, and his brothers. Indeed, whoever belittles the scholars will lose his place in the Hereafter. Whoever belittles the authorities will lose his place in the world. Whoever belittles his brothers will lose his manhood.”

title: Ibn Qayyim on Jama’ah: Even if you are alone, you are the Jama’ah
t:
Ibn al-Qayyim reported: Abdullah Ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The united community is that which adheres to the truth, even if you are alone.”

Nuaym ibn Hammad said, “If the community becomes corrupted, you must adhere to its practice before it became corrupt. Even if you are alone, you by yourself would be the united community.”

title: Umar II on Jihad: Our sins more harmful than plots of enemies
t: Maslamah ibn Abi Bakr reported: Umar ibn ‘Abdul ‘Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, took a pledge from some of his military deputies, saying, “You must fear Allah in every situation you find yourselves. Verily, the fear of Allah is greater for preparation, a better plan, and a stronger force. There is nothing of the hostility of your enemies that deserves more caution than your own selves and those with you who are sinfully disobedient to Allah. For I fear the sins of our people more than the plots of their enemies. Verily, we were only transgressed by our enemy and given divine support over them due to their sinful disobedience. Were it not for that, we would have no power over them.”

title: Hadith on Trials: The Prophet fears six trials for the Ummah
t: ‘Awf ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I fear for you six trials: foolish leaders, shedding of blood, bribery in judgments, severing family ties, those who take the Quran as music, and an excessive amount of police.”
q: I fear for you six trials: foolish leaders, shedding of blood, bribery in judgments, severing family ties, those who take the Quran as music, and an excessive amount of police.

title: Hadith on Marriage: Marry the loving, fruitful to increase believers
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered us to get married and he strongly prohibited celibacy for us. The Prophet said, “Marry the loving and fertile. Verily, I will have most followers among the prophets on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Marry the loving and fertile. Verily, I will have most followers … among the prophets on the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Abu Bakr on Decapitation: Prohibition of severed heads as trophies
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: He came to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, with a severed head, and Abu Bakr condemned it. ‘Uqbah said, “O Caliph of the Messenger of Allah, they do that to us!” Abu Bakr said, “You follow the way of the Persians and the Romans? Rather, do not come to me with a severed head! It is enough for you to write and inform me.”

title: Qurtubi on Jihad: Best jihad to build a mosque, teach good
