t: Yusayrah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must glorify Allah and declare the oneness and the sanctity of Allah. Count them on your fingers. Verily, the fingers will be questioned and made to testify. Do not be unmindful such that you forget the mercy of Allah.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication between Adhan and Iqamah not rejected
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Supplication is not rejected between the call to prayer and its commencement.” They said, “What should we say, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Ask Allah for wellness in the world and in the Hereafter.”
q: Ask Allah for wellness in the world and in the Hereafter

title: Hadith on Zamzam: Believers drink from the well of Zamzam
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, a sign between us and the hypocrites is that they do not drink Zamzam water.”

title: Hadith on Hagar: The Zamzam well would be a flowing spring
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “May Allah have mercy upon the mother of Ishmael. If she had not hastened to take water, the Zamzam well would have become a flowing spring.”

title: Hadith on Janazah: When forty Muslims pray the funeral prayer
t: Abdullah ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A Muslim man does not die while forty men pray over him, who do not associate any partners with Allah, but that Allah will accept their intercession for him.”

title: Hadith on Funerals: Great rewards for attending a funeral
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever follows the funeral of Muslim, in faith and seeking reward, and he remains with it until the prayer is offered and the burial ceremony is finished, then he will return with two great rewards. Each reward is like the size of mount Uhud. Whoever offers the funeral prayer and returns before the burial, then he will return with one great reward.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Siwak: Toothstick cleans mouth, pleases Lord
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The toothstick is cleansing for the mouth and pleasing to the Lord.”

title: Sa’id on Sunnah: Punished for praying differently from Sunnah
t: Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib reported: He saw a man praying after sunrise at dawn with more than two cycles, and he was excessive in his bowing and prostration, so Sa’id prohibited him. The man said, “O Abu Muhammad, will Allah punish us for praying?” Sa’id said, “No, but he will punish you for opposing the Sunnah.”

title: Hadith on Zakat: If he gives food, clothing, or prayer in charity
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a man earns wealth from what is lawful and he feeds himself, or clothes another among the creation of Allah, it will be regarded as charity for him. When a Muslim man is without means to give in charity, he should say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger, and send blessings upon the believing men and women and the Muslim men and women. If he says this, it will be regarded as charity for him.”

title: Hadith on Conviction: Call upon Allah with certainty, without distraction
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Call upon Allah with certainty that He will answer you. Know that Allah will not answer the supplication of an unmindful and distracted heart.”
q: Call upon Allah with certainty that He will answer you. Know that Allah will not answer the supplication of an unmindful and distracted heart.

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplications answered at night, end of prayer
t: Abu Umamah reported: It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, which supplication will be heard best?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One in the last part of the night and at the end of the prescribed prayers.”
q: One in the last part of the night and at the end of the prescribed prayers
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Visiting: Angels bless one who visits the sick
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No Muslim visits another sick Muslim in the morning but that seventy thousand angels will bless him until the evening. He does not visit him in the evening but that seventy thousand angels will bless him until the morning, and he will reap the fruits of Paradise.”

title: Hadith on Visiting: Angels bless those who visit the ill
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you visit a sick or dying person, supplicate for goodness. Verily, the angels will affirm whatever you said.”

title: Hadith on Mercy: Failed and lost if he shows no mercy to people
t: ‘Amr ibn Abi Habib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A servant has failed and lost if Allah has not placed mercy in his heart towards humanity.”

title: Hadith on Hajj: Recommendation to shave head, permission to cut only
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: At the end of the Hajj pilgrimage, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, have mercy upon those who shaved their heads.” They said, “And those who cut their hair short, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “O Allah, have mercy upon those who shaved their heads.” They said, “And those who cut their hair short, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “And those who cut their hair short.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Abu Bakr: My life and wealth only for the Prophet
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The wealth of no one has benefited me as much as the wealth of Abu Bakr.” Abu Bakr wept, saying, “Are my life and my wealth for anyone but you, O Messenger of Allah?”

title: Hadith on Fitrah: Five acts part of natural human instinct
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Five acts are a part of natural instinct: circumcision, shaving pubic hair, plucking hair from the armpits, shortening the moustache, and clipping the nails.”
q: Five acts are a part of natural instinct: circumcision, shaving pubic hair, plucking hair from the armpits, shortening the moustache, and clipping the nails.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Kuhl: Best kind of kohl to use is antimony
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the best of the kohl that you use is antimony, for it brightens the eyes and grows the hair.”

title: Hadith on Miswak: The Prophet cleans his teeth after waking
t: Hudhayfah reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, arose at night, he would clean his mouth with the toothstick.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hajj: Stone turned black from sins of humankind
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The black stone descended from Paradise and it was whiter than milk, but it became black due to the sins of the children of Adam.”

title: Hadith on Shade: Helping others in the shade of Allah
t: Abu al-Yasar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever would love to be shaded in the shade of Allah, let him help someone in hardship or waive a loan.”

title: Umar on Treachery: Execution for Muslim betraying unbeliever
t: Malik reported: A man from the people of Kufa said that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to a commander in an army he had dispatched, saying, “I have heard that it is the habit of some of your men to chase an unbeliever until he takes refuge in a high place. Then a man tells him in Persian to not be afraid, and when he comes down, they kill him. By the One in whose hand is my soul, if I knew a man had done that once, I would strike his neck.”

title: Umar on Treachery: Execution for unlawfully killing unbeliever
t: Abu Salamah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “By Allah, if one of you were to give a gesture of safety to an idolater and he came trusting you and you killed him, then I would execute him for it.”
gf: Qawi li ghayrihi (strengthened by external evidence) according to al-Mushayqih

title: Hadith on Hajj: When someone dies while on the pilgrimage
t: Ibn Abbas reported: A man performing the pilgrimage was thrown from his camel and died while we were with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet said, “Wash him with water mixed with the leaves of a lote tree and shroud him in his two garments. Do not cover his head, for Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection performing the call of the pilgrimage.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Aisha on Ihram: Wearing underwear during the pilgrimage
t: Al-Bukhari reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, did not see any harm in wearing an undergarment for those in her caravan traveling the pilgrimage.

title: Hadith on Ihram: Clothing for men and women at pilgrimage
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: A man stood up and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, what should I wear to prepare for the pilgrimage?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not wear a shirt, or pants, or turban, or a hooded cloak. If someone has no shoes, he may wear leather socks if they are cut lower than his ankles. Do not wear any perfume or fragrance. The woman prepared for pilgrimage should not cover her face or wear gloves.”

title: Hadith on Lineage: The Prophet does not let him disown his child
t: Abu Huraira reported: A bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Indeed, my wife has given birth to a black boy and I have disowned him.” The Prophet said, “Do you have camels?” He said yes. The Prophet said, “What color are they?” He said, “They are red.” The Prophet said, “Are any of them gray?” He said, “There are gray camels among them.” The Prophet said, “Where do you think this color came from?” He said, “O Messenger of Allah, it is hereditary.” The Prophet said, “Perhaps this boy’s color is hereditary.” The Prophet did not allow him to disown his child.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Declaring Allah is One, morning and evening
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One says in the morning: O Allah, we have reached morning, calling You to witness, calling the carriers of Your Throne to witness, Your angels, and all of creation that You are Allah and none has the right to be worshiped but You alone, without any partners, and that Muhammad is Your servant and messenger. None says this but that Allah will forgive him for what he did during the day. If he says it in the evening, Allah will forgive his sins during the night.”

title: Hadith on Quba: Reward for praying in Masjid Quba
t: Sahl ibn Hunayf reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever purifies himself in his house, then comes to the mosque of Quba and prays in it, he will have a reward like the Umrah pilgrimage.”

title: Hadith on Injustice: Muslims abandoned if fail to stop oppression
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you see my nation afraid to tell the oppressor that he is an oppressor, they have been forsaken.”

title: Hadith on Muhammad: Allah has made me generous and humble, not a tyrant
t: Abdullah ibn Busr reported: I gave a sheep as a gift to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Prophet sat on his knees to eat. A bedouin said, “What is this sitting?” The Prophet said, “Verily, Allah has made me a noble servant and he has not made me a stubborn tyrant.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Marriage: Husband not demanding all his rights
t:
‘Ikramah reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “I do not like to invoke all of my rights over my wife due to the saying of Allah Almighty: And for men is a degree over them.” (2:228)

Imam al-Tabari commented, “What Ibn Abbas said is the ‘degree,’ which Allah mentioned in this verse, is that a man should excuse his wife from some of her obligations, he should be lenient regarding his rights over her, but he must still fulfill all of his obligations toward her.”

title: Hadith on David: Most beloved fasting and prayer to Allah
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most beloved fasting to Allah is the fasting of David, and the most beloved prayer to Allah is the prayer of David, upon him be peace. He would sleep half of the night, stand in prayer for a third of it, and then sleep for a sixth of it. He would fast every other day.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Istighfar: Parents rewarded for their good children
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty will raise the status of His righteous servants in Paradise, and they will say: O Lord, what is this? Allah will say: This is your child seeking forgiveness for you.”

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet’s supplication for entering a city
t: Suhayb reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, intended to enter a town, he would say, “O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and what they overshadow, Lord of the seven earths and what they cover, Lord of the devils and who they lead astray, Lord of the winds and what they scatter. Verily, we ask you for the goodness in this town and the goodness of its people, and we seek refuge in you from the evil within it and the evil of its people.”

title: Hadith on Jerusalem: Pray in Masjid al-Aqsa, or send gifts
t: Maymunah reported: She said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell us about the Sacred House in Jerusalem.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is the land of the gathering and the Resurrection. Go there and pray, for one prayer in it is like a thousand prayers elsewhere.” She said, “What if I cannot endure travel to there?” The Prophet said, “Let one send a gift of oil to light its lamps, for whoever does so is as if he has gone there.”

title: Hadith on Rulers: Advise misguided leaders in private if possible
t: ‘Iyad ibn Ghanam reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever has advice for the ruler, let him take his hand and give it privately. If he accepts it, then he accepts it. If he rejects it, the duty upon him has been fulfilled.”

title: Hadith on Rifq: Gentleness is beautiful, cruelty is disgraceful
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, gentleness is not found in anything but that it beautifies it, and it is not removed from anything but that it disgraces it.”

title: Hadith on Dua: All praise is due to Allah, morning and evening
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say during the evening, “We have entered the evening and so has the dominion of Allah. All praise is due to Allah, there is no God but Allah alone without any partners.” I think the Prophet said in it, “To him belong the dominion and praise and he has power over all things. My Lord, I ask you for goodness in this night and goodness after it. I seek refuge in you from the evil in this night and the evil after it. My Lord, I seek refuge in you from laziness and the evil of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in you from the punishment of the Hellfire and punishment in the grave.” When the Prophet awakened, he would say likewise, “We have entered the morning and so has the dominion of Allah.”

title: Ibn al-Qayyim on Mercy: Forgiveness more beloved to Allah than revenge
t: Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Forgiveness is more beloved to Allah than vengeance, mercy is more beloved to Him than punishment, grace is more beloved to Him than justice, and giving is more beloved to Him than withholding.”

title: Hadith on Faith: Blessed are those who never saw him but believed
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Blessed are those who had faith in me and saw me, and blessed seven times are those who had faith in me and never saw me.”

title: Hadith on Qadr: People may change their fate in the end
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must not be impressed with anyone until you see their end. Verily, a servant may perform righteous deeds throughout his life, or for a long time. If he were to die in that state, he would enter Paradise, but then he changes himself and commits evil deeds. Verily, a servant may commit evil deeds for a long time. If he were to die in that state, he would enter Hellfire, but then he changes himself and forms righteous deeds. If Allah intends goodness for a servant, He puts him into action before his death.” They said, O Messenger of Allah, how is he put into action?” The Prophet said, “He is guided to righteous deeds and he holds firmly to it.”

title: Ibn Taymiyyah on Sakinah: What can my enemies do to me?
t: Ibn al-Qayyim reported: Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said to me once, “What can my enemies do to me? My paradise and my garden are in my heart wherever I go. They are with me and never leave me. If I am imprisoned, it is seclusion for worship. If I am killed, it is martyrdom. If they expel me from my land, it is tourism.”

title: Ibn Taymiyyah on Paradise: Spiritual bliss is experienced now before Paradise
t: Ibn al-Qayyim reported: I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah sanctify his spirit, say, “Verily, there is a Paradise in this world and whoever does not enter it now will not enter the Paradise of the Hereafter.”

title: Hadith on Faith: Parable of the believer as a piece of gold
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the parable of the believer is that of a piece of gold. Its owner blows upon it, yet it never changes or diminishes. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the parable of the believer is that of a bee. It consumes and produces what is wholesome. It falls down, yet it never breaks or spoils.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Ibn Abbas on Sin: No sin too major, no sin too minor
t:
Sa’id ibn Jubayr reported: A man said to Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, “How many major sins are there? Are they seven?” Ibn Abbas said, “They are closer to seven hundred than only seven, yet no sin is too enormous if forgiveness is sought, and no sin is too minor if committed stubbornly.”

Source Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī 9207

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Believers rise to great rank by good character
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the Muslim is directed in the right manner to achieve the level of one who regularly fasts and stands for prayer with the verses of Allah, due to his good character and his generous nature.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Islam: What does the Prophet call to?
t: Abu Tamimah reported: A man from Balhujaym said, “O Messenger of Allah, to what are you calling?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I call to Allah alone. If He lets you be harmed, you will call upon Him, and He will remove it. If you are lost in the wilderness, you will call upon Him, and He will bring you back. If you are afflicted by famine, you will call upon Him, and He will make your crops grow.” The man said, “Advise me.” The Prophet said, “Do not insult anyone, and do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face, or sharing your vessel with a thirsty person. Raise your garment to the middle of your shin or, if you must, to the ankles. Beware of trailing your garments out of pride, for Allah does not love the boastful.”

title: Maymun on Sin: Whoever sins in secret, let him repent in secret
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Maymun ibn Mihran said, “Whoever commits evil in secret, let him repent in secret. Whoever commits evil in public, let him repent in public. Verily, Allah will forgive him and he will not condemn him, but people will condemn him and they will not forgive him.”

title: Hadith on Hudud: Private repentance accepted to avoid legal punishment
t: Zayd ibn Aslam reported: A man confessed of adultery in the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet called for a whip and he was given a broken whip. The Prophet said, “Greater than this.” He was brought another whip whose knots had not been cut. The Prophet said, “Lesser than this.” He was brought a whip that had been used and was more flexible. The Prophet gave the order and the man was flogged, then the Prophet said, “O people, the time has now come for you to observe the limits of Allah. Whoever has had any of these ugly matters befall him should cover them up with the veil of Allah. Whoever reveals to us his sins, we will act against him according to the Book of Allah.”
gf: Hasan li ghayri (fair due to external evidence) according to Ibn Hajar

title: Hadith on Jihad: Seeking knowledge is jihad in way of Allah
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever goes out seeking knowledge is in the way of Allah until he returns.”

title: Hadith on Calamity: Allah honors those who console believers
t: ‘Amr ibn Hazm reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No believer consoles his brother at the time of calamity but that Allah, glory be to him, will dress him with noble garments on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: No believer consoles his brother at the time of calamity but that Allah, glory be to him, will dress him with noble garments on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Siwak: Cleanse your mouth for recitation of Quran
t: Samurah ibn Jundub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Freshen your mouths with the toothstick. Verily, they are the pathways of the Quran.”

title: Hadith on Ruin: Withdraw from those leading Ummah astray
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people will be ruined by a branch of the Quraysh tribe.” They said, “What do you command us to do?” The Prophet said, “If only the people would withdraw from them.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Protect me from my enemies with Islam
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would supplicate, saying, “O Allah, protect me with Islam standing, protect me with Islam sitting, protect me with Islam lying down. Let not my enemies gloat over me in envy. O Allah, I ask you for every good that is stored in your hand, and I seek refuge in you from every evil that is stored in your hand.”

title: Hadith on Justice: Closest to Allah in Hereafter are just leaders
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most beloved of people to Allah on the Day of Resurrection and the nearest to Him will be the just leader. The most hated of people to Allah and the furthest from Him will be the tyrannical leader.”

title: Hadith on Sincerity: The Prophet’s intercession for sincere believers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most blessed of people to have my intercession on the Day of Resurrection are those who say ‘there is no God but Allah,’ sincerely from the heart.”

title: Hadith on Bid’ah: Every innovation is misguidance in Hellfire
t: Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would praise Allah in his sermon, as He deserves to be praised, and then say, “Whomever Allah guides, no one can lead him astray. Whomever Allah sends astray, no one can guide him. The truest word is the Book of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad. The most evil matters in religion are those that are newly invented, for every newly invented matter is an innovation, every innovation is misguidance, and every misguidance is in the Hellfire.”

title: Hadith on Friendliness: Best people are kind, benefit others
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believer is friendly and befriended, for there is no goodness in one who is neither friendly nor befriended. The best of people are those who are most beneficial to people.”

title: Hadith on Paradise: The Prophet called to his praiseworthy station
t: Hudhayfah reported: The people will be gathered upon the leveled earth and no soul will speak. The first to be called will be Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet will say, “I am here at Your service. All good is in Your hand and evil cannot be ascribed to You. One will only be guided if You guide him. I am the servant, son of your servant, by You and for You. There is no escape or refuge from You but with You. Blessed and exalted are You.” This is the saying of Allah, “Perhaps He will raise you to a praiseworthy station.” (17:79)

title: Hadith on Sins: You are not responsible for three persons
t: Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are three persons you will not be asked about: a man who separates from the community and disobeys his leader and dies in a state of disobedience, a servant who abandons his master and then dies, and a woman with sufficient provision who displays her beauty when her husband is absent. There are three others you will not be asked about: a man who competes with Allah regarding His cloak for His cloak is pride and His garment is might, a man who doubts the command of Allah, and those who despair of the mercy of Allah.”

title: Hadith on Adultery: Shameless promiscuity sign of the Hour
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hour will not be established until people mate with each other in the road as if they were donkeys.” I said, “Will it really happen?” The Prophet said, “Yes, it will truly happen.”
q: Yes, it will truly happen

title: Hadith on Jihad: Nothing in the path of Allah but fighting?
t: Abu Huraira reported: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when a young man approached us. When we saw him, we said, “If only this young man had given his youth and effort and strength in the path of Allah!” The Prophet heard our conversation, and he said, “Is there nothing in the path of Allah but fighting? Whoever strives for his parents is in the way of Allah. Whoever strives for his family is in the way of Allah. Whoever strives for himself to be independent is in the way of Allah. Whoever strives to gain many possessions for himself is in the way of Satan.”

title: Hadith on Sins: Three people will not enter Paradise
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Three persons will not be looked upon by Allah Almighty on the Day of Resurrection: one who disobeys his parents, a woman who imitates men, and a man who allows his women to fornicate. Three persons will not enter Paradise: one who disobeys his parents, a drunkard, and one who reminds others of his charity.”

title: Hadith on Paradise: Three people among first to enter Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I was shown three people who will be among the first to enter Paradise: a martyr, one who refrains from begging, and a servant who worships Allah in the best manner and is sincere to his master.”

title: Hadith on Taqwa: Peak piety to leave permissible things, fearing sin
t: ‘Atiyyah al-Sa’di reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The servant will not reach the level of the truly righteous until he leaves harmless things due to caution they might be harmful.”

title: Hadith on Worldly Hopes: Man cannot escape trials of life
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, drew a square, and in the middle he drew a line which poked out the end. Across the middle line, he drew some smaller lines. The Prophet said, “This is man and the square surrounding him is death. The middle line is his worldly hopes, and the smaller lines are his troubles. If this one misses him, another will distress him. If that one misses him, another will distress him.”

title: Hadith on Death: Man continues to hope until death catches up
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, drew some lines in the sand and he said, “This one is the worldly hopes of man and the other is his lifespan. A man will continue like this until the other line overtakes him.”

title: Hadith on Trade: Merchants with the wicked, unless they fear Allah
t: Rifa’ah ibn Rafi’ reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, merchants will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with the wicked, except for those who fear Allah, behave righteously, and are truthful.”

title: Hadith on Hereafter: The Prophet is raised to praiseworthy station
t: Adam ibn Ali reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said, “Verily, the people will fall to their knees on the Day of Resurrection, and every nation will follow its prophet. They will say: O prophet, intercede for us! Then, the intercession will be given to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and on that day he will be raised to the praiseworthy station.”

title: Hadith on Zakat: Rain held back if people withhold charity
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Never do people withhold alms from their wealth but that a portion from the sky will be held back; were it not for the animals, it would never rain.”

title: Hadith on Yunus: Allah answers supplication of Prophet Jonah
t: Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The supplication of Jonah, Dhul Nun, when he called upon Allah inside the belly of the whale was this, ‘There is no God but You, glory be to You for I have certainly been among the wrongdoers,’ (21:87). Verily, a Muslim never supplicates for anything with it but that Allah will answer him.”

title: Hadith on Purity: Believers can never be filthy, impure
t: Abu Huraira reported: He met the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in the road of Medina while he was in a state of impurity. He slipped away and left to take a bath, then he returned. The Prophet said, “O Abu Huraira, where were you?” He said, “I was in a state of impurity and I disliked to sit with you while I am not pure.” The Prophet said, “Glory be to Allah. Verily, the Muslim is not impure.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Angels: Whatever offends people also offends angels
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever eats onions, garlic, or leeks should not approach our mosque, for the angels are offended by whatever offends the children of Adam.”

title: Hadith on Ihsan: Allah is excellent, loves excellence in everything
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you make a judgment, be just. If you have to kill, kill in the best manner. Verily, Allah Almighty is excellent and he loves excellence.”

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Trials will immerse hearts of people in desires
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Tribulation will be exposed to the hearts of people like a reed mat woven, stick by stick. Any heart afflicted by them will have a black mark put into it, but any heart that rejects them will have a white mark put into it. Thus, there will be two kinds of hearts: one is pure like a white gemstone; it will not be harmed by any trial as long as the heavens and earth endure. The other is black and dusty like a worn-out vessel, neither acknowledging good nor rejecting evil, rather absorbed in its desires.”

title: Hadith on Fitnah: When the pen is mightier than the sword
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will be a tribulation that will wipe out the Arabs, in which those killed on both sides are in the Hellfire. In that time, the spoken word will be stronger than the sword.”

title: Hadith on Soothsayers: They contact the jinn, mix truth with lies
t: Aisha reported: Some people asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about soothsayers. The Prophet said, “They are upon nothing.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, sometimes they speak about things that come true.” The Prophet said, “Those are the words snatched by the jinn, who whisper it into the ears of their friends, and it is mixed with more than one hundred lies.”
q: They are upon nothing
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fever: The Prophet afflicted with twice as much fever
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: I entered the home of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was suffering from fever. I said, “O Messenger of Allah, you are suffering from a strong fever.” The Prophet said, “Yes, for I am afflicted with fever like two men among you.” I said, “Is it that you have a double reward?” The Prophet said, “Yes, it is so. Likewise, there is no Muslim who is afflicted with pain as much as the prick of a thorn, or more, but that Allah will expiate his sins, just as leaves fall from a tree.”
q: Yes, for I am afflicted with fever like two men among you … Yes, it is so. Likewise, … t
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fever: Do not curse fever, it expiates sins
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered the home of Umm Sa’ib, and he said, “What ails you, O Umm Sa’ib? You are shivering.” She said, “It is a fever. Allah has not blessed it.” The Prophet said, “Do not curse fever. Verily, it removes the sins of the children of Adam, just as a furnace removes dirt from iron.”

title: Hadith on Sultan: Be patient with tyranny from your rulers
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever sees something from his ruler that he hates, let him be patient. Whoever secedes from the community by as much as a handspan and dies will have died a death of ignorance.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hypocrisy: Three signs of a hypocrite, even if he is Muslim
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among the signs of a hypocrite are three, even if he fasts and prays and claims to be a Muslim: when he speaks he lies, when he gives a promise he breaks it, and when he is trusted he betrays.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Faith: Only practicing the pillars of Islam?
t: Jabir reported: A man asked the Prophet, “Do you think if I pray the five prescribed prayers, I fast the month of Ramadan, and I uphold what is lawful and unlawful without adding anything to it, will I enter Paradise?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Yes.” The man said, “By Allah, I will not add anything to it.”

title: Hadith on Signs: The Hour is preceded by rise of the foolish
t: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hour will not be established until the happiest of people in the world is the depraved fool, son of the depraved fool.”

title: Hadith of Gabriel: Angel Jibril came to teach you Islam
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, one day, a man appeared with very white clothes and very black hair. There were no signs of travel on him and we did not recognize him. He sat in front of the Prophet, rested his knees by his knees, and placed his hands on his thighs. The man said, “O Muhammad, tell me about Islam.” The Prophet said, “Islam is to testify there is no God but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish prayer, to give charity, to fast the month of Ramadan, and to perform pilgrimage to the House if a way is possible.” The man said, “You have spoken truthfully.” We were surprised that he asked him and said he was truthful. He said, “Tell me about faith.” The Prophet said, “Faith is to believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and to believe in providence, its good and its harm.” The man said, “You have spoken truthfully. Tell me about excellence.” The Prophet said, “Excellence is to worship Allah as if you see Him, for if you do not see Him, He surely sees you.” The man said, “Tell me about the final hour.” The Prophet said, “The one asked does not know more than the one asking.” The man said, “Tell me about its signs.” The Prophet said, “The slave-girl will give birth to her mistress and you will see barefoot, naked, and dependent shepherds compete in the construction of tall buildings.” Then, the man returned and I remained. The Prophet said to me, “O Umar, do you know who he was?” I said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Prophet said, “Verily, he was Gabriel who came to teach you your religion.”
q: Islam is to testify there is no God but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish prayer, to give charity, to fast the month of Ramadan, and to perform pilgrimage to the House if a way is possible. … Faith is to believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and to believe in providence, its good and its harm. … Excellence is to worship Allah as if you see Him, for if you do not see Him, He surely sees you. … The one asked does not know more than the one asking. … The slave-girl will give birth to her mistress and you will see barefoot, naked, and dependent shepherds compete in the construction of tall buildings. … O Umar, do you know who he was? … Verily, he was Gabriel who came to teach you your religion.

title: Hadith on Leniency: Who swore by Allah not to do good?
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, heard the loud voices of two men arguing at the door. One of them was asking the other to lessen his debt and show leniency. The man said, “By Allah, I will not do so!” The Prophet came out, saying, “Where is the one who swore by Allah that he would not do good?” The man said, “It was me, O Messenger of Allah. He may now have what he likes.”
q: Where is the one who swore by Allah that he would not do good
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Abu Bakr on Truth: How Abu Bakr got the name al-Siddiq
t: Aisha reported: After the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was miraculously taken by night to the furthest mosque in Jerusalem, the people began to talk about it. Some of them renounced their faith and belief in him. They sought Abu Bakr and they said, “Have you heard that your friend imagined he was taken by night to the sacred house?” Abu Bakr said, “Did he say that?” They said yes. Abu Bakr said, “If he said it, he has spoken the truth.” They said, “Do you believe he went by night to the sacred house and returned before morning?” Abu Bakr said, “Yes. Verily, I believe what is even more astonishing than that. I believe he has received messages from heaven for everything he does.” For this reason, Abu Bakr was named the Truthful, al-Siddiq.

title: Umar on Apostasy: I did not command it, I was not pleased
t: Muhammad ibn al-Qari reported: A man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, from Abu Musa al-Ashari. Umar asked him about the people and he informed him. Then, Umar said, “Do you have any recent news?” Abu Musa said, “Yes, a man turned back to unbelief after his Islam.” Umar said, “What have you done with him?” Abu Musa said, “We let him approach and we struck his neck.” Umar said, “Did you not imprison him for three days and feed him each day with bread and call him to repent and return to the command of Allah?” Then, Umar said, “O Allah, I was not present and I did not command it and I was not pleased when I heard it!”

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Best sinners are those who repent
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “All of the children of Adam are sinners, and the best sinners are those who repent.”

title: Hadith on Extravagance: Believers do not live a life of luxury
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent him to Yemen and he said, “Beware of luxury, for the servants of Allah do not live luxuriously.”

title: Umar on Islam: Muslims ruined by faulty scholars, leaders, hypocrites
t: Ziyad ibn Hudayr reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said to me, “Do you know what will dismantle Islam?” I said no. Umar said, “Islam will be dismantled by the faults of scholars, the bickering of hypocrites over the Book, and the judgments of misguided leaders.”

title: Hadith on Brothers: Allah helps those who help in private
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever supports his brother in his absence, Allah will support him in this world and in the Hereafter.”

title: Hadith on Children: Sin of separating parents from their children
t: Abu Ayyub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever separates a mother from her child, Allah will separate him from his loved ones on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever separates a mother from her child, Allah will separate him from his loved ones on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Forgiveness: O Allah, forgive Aisha for all her sins
t: Aisha reported: When I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, with a cheerful face, I said, “O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah for me.” The Prophet said, “O Allah, forgive Aisha for her past and future sins, in secret and in public.” Aisha laughed so much that her head fell from his lap. The Prophet said to her, “Does my supplication make you happy?” Aisha said, “Why would your supplication not make me happy?” The Prophet said, “By Allah, it is my supplication for my nation in every prayer.”

title: Umar on Testimony: How do you know a man is righteous, truthful?
t: Kharashah ibn al-Hurr reported: A man gave his testimony to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. Umar said to him, “I do not know you and it will not harm you that I do not know. Bring someone who knows you.” A man from his people said, “I know him.” Umar said, “What do you know about him?” The man said, “His justice and virtue.” Umar said, “Is he your closest neighbor, such that you know him by his coming and going by day and night?” The man said no. Umar said, “Then, have you had business dealings with him, by which you are shown his piety?” The man said no. Umar said, “Then, have you traveled with him on a journey, by which you are shown his good character?” The man said no. Umar said, “You do not know him.” Umar turned to the witness and said, “Bring me someone who knows you.”

title: Hadith on Abstinence: Allah replaces it with something better
t: Abu Qatadah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, you will never leave anything for the sake of Allah Almighty but that Allah will replace it with something better for you.”

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Enrich people with good character, smiling
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, you cannot enrich all of the people with your wealth, but rather you enrich them with your cheerful faces and good character.”

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Good character best thing given by Allah
t: Usamah ibn Sharik reported: I witnessed bedouins ask the Prophet, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, what is the best thing a servant may be given?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Good character.”

title: Ahmad on Creation: Life from an egg evidence for the Creator
t: Ibn Kathir reported: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about the existence of the Creator. Ahmad said, “Consider an impenetrable fortress without any doors or exits. The outside is like white silver and the inside is like shimmering gold. It is built like this until its walls crack and out comes an animal hearing and seeing with a beautiful shape and a pleasant voice.” Ahmad meant by that an egg when the chick comes out of it.

title: Shafi’i on Creation: Unity of creation proves existence of Creator
t: Ibn Kathir reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about the existence of the Creator, so he said, “The leaves of a berry bush all have one taste. Worms eat it and produce silk, bees eat it and produce honey. Goats, camels, and cows eat it and produce droppings and dung. Deer eat it and produce musk. Yet, all of these come from one thing.”

title: Malik on Creation: Languages, voice evidence of the Creator
t: Ibn Kathir reported: Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked by Caliph Harun Rashid about evidence for the Creator. Malik said, “You will find evidence in the different languages, different voices, and different melodies.”

title: Hadith on Sujud: You are nearest to Allah in prostration
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The servant is closest to his Lord during prostration, so increase your supplications therein.”

title: Hadith on Salat: Glorify Allah 33 times after every prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The poor emigrants came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “The wealthy have taken the highest degrees and blessed ranks!” The Prophet said, “How is that?” They said, “They pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, they give in charity but we do not have charity to give, they free slaves but we have none to free.” The Prophet said, “Shall I teach you something by which you will catch up to those ahead of you, surpass those who had outraced you, and no one will be better than you but one who acts like you?” They said, “Of course, O Messenger of Allah!” The Prophet said, “Glorify Allah, exalt Allah, and praise Allah thirty-three times after every prayer.”
q: How is that
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Teach me words to say for my Lord
t: Sa’d reported: A bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Teach me some words to say.” The Prophet said, “Say: There is no god but Allah without any partner, Allah is the greatest of the great, all praise is due to Allah in abundance, glory be to Allah the Lord of the worlds, there is no movement or might but in Allah, the Almighty, the Wise.” The man said, “These words are for my Lord, but what is for me?” The Prophet said, “Say: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy upon me, guide me, and provide for me.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Beloved prayer of the Angels
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked, “Which statement is best?” The Prophet said, “It is what Allah has chosen for His angels and His servants: Glory be to Allah and with His praise.”

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Great virtue of glorifying Allah daily
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever declares one hundred times a day, ‘There is no God but Allah without any partner, to Him belongs sovereignty and all praise and He is powerful over everything,’ he will have the reward of emancipating ten slaves, a hundred good deeds will be recorded for him, a hundred sins will be erased from his record, and he will have a guard against Satan during the day until evening. No one will exceed him but one who recited these words more often.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dhikr: The Prophet loves remembering Allah most
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “To declare the glory of Allah, the praise of Allah, the oneness of Allah, and the greatness of Allah is more beloved to me than anything over which the sun rises.”

title: Hadith on Slavery: Double reward for freeing, marrying slaves
t: Abu Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a man teaches his slave-girl good manners, educates her in the best way, then emancipates her and marries her, he will have a double reward. If he believes in Jesus and then believes in me, he will have a double reward. If a servant fears his Lord and obeys his master, he will have a double reward.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Masruq on Aisha: Companions seek Islamic knowledge from Aisha
t: Masruq reported: It was said, “Did Aisha have knowledge of the obligations?” Masruq said, “By the one in whose hand is my soul, I saw the learned elders among the companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, ask her about the obligations.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Majesty of your countenance, greatness of authority
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A servant of Allah said: O Lord, all praise is due to you as befits the majesty of your countenance and the greatness of your authority. The angels were unsure and did not know how to record it, so they ascended to heaven and said: O Lord, your servant has said a word we are not sure how to record. Allah, although he is most knowing of what his servant said, replied to them: What did my servant say? The angels said: O Lord, all praise is due to you as befits the majesty of your countenance and the greatness of your authority. Allah said: Write it down as my servant has said it until he meets me and I will reward him.”
q: A
gf: Jayyid (very good) according to Ahmad Shakir

title: Hadith on Prayer: Do you love to strive in supplication?
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do you wish to strive in supplication? Say: O Allah, help me to be grateful to You, to remember You, and to worship You in the best manner.”

title: Hadith on Friday: Allah seals hearts of those who neglect Friday prayer
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever hears the announcement of Friday prayer and he does not come, then he hears it again and does not come, then he hears it again and does not come, Allah will place a seal over his heart and turn his heart into the heart of a hypocrite.”

title: Umar on Judgment: We judge outward deeds, not inner-states
t: Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, people were judged by revelation in the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and the revelation has ceased. We only judge now what is manifested outwardly of your deeds. Whoever shows us good, we will trust him and bring him close. It is not for us to judge anything of his inner secrets. Allah will hold him accountable for his inner secrets. Whoever shows us evil, we will never trust him or believe him even if it is said his intentions are good.”

title: Ibn ‘Asakir on Sin: Public sins harm the entire community
t: Ibn ‘Asakir reported: Bilal ibn Sa’d, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, if sinful disobedience is committed in private, it only harms the one who did it. If it is committed in public and is not rectified, it will harm everyone.”

title: Hasan on Speech: Wise people think before they speak
t: Al-Bayhaqi reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The intelligent man has his tongue behind his heart. If he intends to say something, he consults his heart whether he should say it or be silent. The foolish man has his tongue in front of his heart. If he intends to say something, he lets his tongue speak first.”

title: Hasan on Fear: Believer are righteous by fear of Allah
t: Al-Dhahabi reported: Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The believer is the best of people in good deeds, but has the strongest apprehension. If he were to spend a mountain of his wealth in charity, he would not be sure of the reward until he sees it. He does not increase in piety and righteousness unless he increases in fear. The hypocrite says: There are many people, so I will be forgiven and I will not be harmed. Thus, he commits evil deeds yet still has hope in Allah.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Sins: Believers fears their sins, wicked do not
t: Al-Harith ibn Suwaid reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, the believer views his sins as if he were sitting under a mountain, fearing it will fall upon him. The wicked views his sins as if they were a fly passing over his nose.”

title: Hadith on Shukr: Believer is rewarded for patience or gratitude
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I am amazed by the believer. If he is granted goodness, he praises Allah and is grateful. If he is afflicted with a calamity, he praises Allah and is patient. The believer is rewarded for every matter, even feeding a morsel of food to his wife.”

title: Hadith on Qadr: Allah only decrees goodness for believers
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I am amazed by the believer. Verily, Allah does not decree anything for the believers except what is good for them.”

title: Hadith on Quran: Reciting Surat al-Falaq and al-Nas before sleep
t: Aisha reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would lie down for sleep, he would blow into his hands, recite the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and al-Nas, and he would wipe his hands over his body.

title: Hadith on Sleep: Clean your bed, lie on your right side, supplicate
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you goes to his bed, let him clean his bed with his garment, for he does not know what was left upon it. Then, let him say: By Your name, O Lord, I place my side and by You I rise. If You take my soul, have mercy on me. If You send it back, protect it with the protection of your righteous servants.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Quran: The Prophet recites al-Sajdah, al-Mulk before sleep
t:
Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would not go to sleep until he had recited the chapters, “The revelation of the Book, in which there is no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds,” (32:1) and, “Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and has power over all things,” (67:1).

Tawus said, “They both have seventy more virtues than every other chapter of the Quran.”
q: The revelation of the Book, in which there is no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds,

title: Hadith on Quran: The Prophet recites Quran before sleep
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would not sleep in his bed until he has recited Surat Bani Isra’il and Al-Zumar.

title: Hadith on Isha: The Prophet sleeps after evening prayer
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would not sleep before evening prayer and he would not stay up after it.

title: Hadith on Isha: Discouraged to sleep before evening prayer, talk after it
t:
Abu Barzah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, disliked sleeping before evening prayer or talking after it.

In another narration, he said: The Prophet delayed the evening prayer until a third of the night had passed. He would recite in the dawn prayer sixty to a hundred verses. We would depart when it was light enough to see each other’s faces.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Shirk: All sins are forgiven besides idolatry
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: Whoever knows that I have power to forgive sins, I will forgive him and I will not mind, as long as he does not associate any partners with me.”

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Believers will be shaded by their charity
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, charity will extinguish the heat of the graves for their people. Only the believer can seek shade on the Day of Resurrection in the shade of his charity.”

title: Hadith on Deeds: Fastest deeds to be rewarded or punished
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The quickest good deeds to be rewarded are righteousness and upholding family ties. The quickest evil deeds to be punished are transgression and severing family ties.”

title: Hadith on Children: Enter Paradise by being just with daughters
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever has a daughter and he does not bury her alive, nor humiliate her, nor prefer his sons over her, he will enter Paradise due to her.”
q: Whoever

title: Hasan on Tawbah: Satan wants you to tire of repentance
t: Ja’far ibn Burqan reported: I said to a man from Basra, “How can one of us continue to kneel before his Lord, seeking his forgiveness for a sin, then he returns to sin, then again he seeks forgiveness, then again he returns to sin?” It was mentioned to Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, and he said, “Satan wishes for you to think like this, so do not be discouraged from seeking forgiveness.”

title: Hadith on Mawt: Do not wish for death, you might repent
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Let none of you wish for death. If he is a good-doer, he might increase his good deeds. If he is an evil-doer, he might make amends.”

title: Hadith on Living: Four things part of happiness, misery
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Four things are part of happiness: a righteous spouse, a spacious dwelling, a righteous neighbor, and a comfortable mount. Four things are part of misery: a bad neighbor, a bad spouse, a restrictive dwelling, and a bad mount.”

title: Hadith on Comfort: Happiness in good neighbors, ride, and home
t: Nafi’ ibn ‘Abdul Harith reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is part of a man’s happiness to have a righteous neighbor, a comfortable mount, and a spacious dwelling.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Prayer: When one forgets number of raka’at in prayer
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed with us five cycles (raka’at). We said, “O Messenger of Allah, you added something to the prayer.” The Prophet said, “What is that?” They said, “You have prayed five cycles.” The Prophet said, “Verily, I am only a human being like you. I remember as you remember and I forget as you forget.” Then, the Prophet performed two prostrations for forgetfulness.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sunnah: Time will come when Muslims abandon Sunnah
t: Al-Miqdam ibn Ma’dikarib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have surely been given the Quran and something similar along with it. Soon, the time will come when a man will recline on his couch, saying: Only follow the Quran, make lawful what you find in it as lawful and outlaw what you find in it as unlawful.”

title: Hadith on ‘Ibadah: Busy yourself with worship, problem solved
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: O son of Adam, use your free time to worship Me and I will fill your heart with riches and alleviate your poverty, otherwise I will fill your life with troubles and never relieve your poverty.”

title: Hadith on Graves: Worst people turn graves into places of worship
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the worst of people are those upon whom the Hour is established while they are alive, and those who take graves as places of worship.”

title: Hadith on Qadr: Victory comes with patience, hardship with ease
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Know that there is much good in being patient with what you detest, victory will come with patience, relief will come with affliction, and ‘with the hardship will come an ease.’” (94:5)
q: Know that there is much good in being patient with what you detest, victory will come with patience, relief will come with affliction, and ‘with the hardship will come an ease

title: Hadith on Sin: Signs of the Hour are ignorance, adultery
t:
Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among the signs of the Hour are the reduction of knowledge, the prevalence of ignorance, the prevalence of adultery, and the abundance of women and scarcity of men such that fifty women will be maintained by a single man.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “And drinking of wine.”
q: And drinking of wine
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Eating: Hold back your burping, do not overeat
t: Abu Juhayfah reported: I ate a stew of bread and fattened meat. Then, I came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and I belched loudly. The Prophet said, “Restrain your belching. Verily, those who ate to their fill the most in this world will be the hungriest in the Hereafter.”

title: Hadith on Islam: Whoever neglects these has abandoned part of Islam
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Islam is to worship Allah without associating any partner with Him, to establish prayer, to give charity, to fast the month of Ramadan, to perform pilgrimage to the House, to enjoin good and forbid evil, and to greet your people with peace. Whoever neglects anything from them has abandoned a part of Islam, and whoever neglects all of them has thrown Islam behind his back.”
gf: Sahih li ghayri (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: The Prophet’s supplications in night prayer
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stood for prayer at night, he would say, “I turn my face to the One who originated the heavens and the earth, to worship Him for I am not among the idolaters. Verily, my prayer, my rites, my living, and my dying are for Allah, the Lord of the worlds, who has no partner, as I have been commanded, and I am among the Muslims. O Allah, You are the King, there is no God but You. Guide me to the best of character, for none can guide to the best of it but You. Divert me from the worst of it, for none can divert it but You. I am here at Your service. All goodness is in Your hand, and evil is not befitting for You. I am from You and returning to You. Blessed and exalted are You. I seek Your forgiveness, and I repent to You.” When the Prophet bowed, he would say, “O Allah, I have bowed for You, I have faith in You, and I humbly surrender to You, my hearing, my seeing, my essence, my bones, and my limbs.” When the Prophet raised up, he would say, “O Allah, our Lord, Your praise fills the heavens, the earth, whatever is between them, and everything after that as You will.” When the Prophet prostrated, he would say, “O Allah, I have prostrated for You, I have faith in You, and I surrender to You, prostrating to the One who created it, shaped it, and formed its seeing and hearing. Blessed is Allah, the best of Creators.” Then, the Prophet would say at the end of sitting between the testimony of faith and invocation of peace, “Forgive me for what I have done and will do, in secret and in public, exceeding the limits. No one knows me better than You. You are the First and the Last, there is no God but You.”
q: I turn my face to the One who originated the heavens and the earth, to worship Him for I am not among the idolaters. Verily, my prayer, my rites, my living, and my dying are for Allah, the Lord of the worlds, who has no partner, as I have been commanded, and I am among the Muslims. O Allah, You are the King, there is no God but You. Guide me to the best of character, for none can guide to the best of it but You. Divert me from the worst of it, for none can divert it but You. I am here at Your service. All goodness is in Your hand, and evil is not befitting for You. I am from You and returning to You. Blessed and exalted are You. I seek Your forgiveness, and I repent to You. … O Allah, I have bowed for You, I have faith in You, and I humbly surrender to You, my hearing, my seeing, my essence, my bones, and my limbs … O Allah, our Lord, Your praise fills the heavens, the earth, whatever is between them, and everything after that as You will. … O Allah, I have prostrated for You, I have faith in You, and I surrender to You, prostrating to the One who created it, shaped it, and formed its seeing and hearing. Blessed is Allah, the best of Creators … Forgive me for what I have done and will do, in secret and in public, exceeding the limits. No one knows me better than You. You are the First and the Last, there is no God but You

title: Hadith on Zuhd: The Prophet was a traveler in the world
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, laid down upon a reed mat and it left marks on his side. When he woke up, I started wiping his side, and I said, “O Messenger of Allah, why do you not let us spread something on top of this mat for you?” The Prophet said, “What is the world to me? What am I to the world? Verily, the parable of myself and this world is that of a rider who seeks shade under a tree, then he moves on and leaves it behind.”

title: Hadith on Hudud: The Prophet reluctantly punishes a thief
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: I will tell you about the first man to have his hand cut. He was brought for stealing, and the order was given to cut his hand. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was so upset his face changed color as if it were covered with dust. They said, “O Messenger of Allah, do you dislike cutting his hand?” The Prophet said, “What could prevent me? Do not help Satan against one of your brothers! The leader must carry out a case of legal punishment brought to him. Verily, Allah Almighty is forgiving and He loves forgiveness.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “Let them pardon and overlook. Would you not love for Allah to forgive you? Allah is surely forgiving and merciful.” (24:22)

title: Hadith on Ibrahim: The Prophet meets Abraham in Heaven
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I met Abraham on the night of my Ascension and he said: O Muhammad, greet your nation with peace from me. Tell them Paradise has pure soil and delicious water, that it is a level plain and its plants grow with declarations of the glory of Allah, the praise of Allah, the oneness of Allah, and the greatness of Allah.”

title: Hadith on Gifts: The Prophet accepts gifts from non-Muslim leaders
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was given gifts by Khosrau and he accepted them. Kings would give him gifts and he would accept them.

title: Hadith on Gifts: Permission to accept gifts from idolaters
t: Abu Qabus reported: A woman asked Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, “We have a nurse among the Magians and they give us gifts on their festivals.” Aisha said, “As for the meat they have slaughtered, do not eat it. Rather, you may eat from the fruit of their trees.”

title: Hadith on Eid: Festivals of ignorance replaced by two Eids
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, arrived in Medina during two days which they were celebrating. The Prophet said, “What are these two days?” They said, “We would celebrate these two days in the time of ignorance.” The Prophet said, “Verily, Allah has replaced these two days with two better days: Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Fitr.”

title: Hadith on Sins: Beware of accumulating many minor sins
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of minor sins. Verily, they pile upon a man until he is ruined.”

title: Hadith on Sins: Beware minor sins piling up like firewood
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of minor offenses, like people who descend into the bottom of a valley. One comes with log after log until they bake their bread. Verily, when the one who persistently committed minor sins is taken to account for them, they will ruin him.”

title: Hadith on Courage: Let not fear stop you from speaking truth
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Let not fear of the people stop one of you from speaking the truth, if he knows it.”

title: Hadith on Fitnah: People will leave Islam in crowds
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, people have entered the religion of Allah in crowds, and they will leave it in crowds.”

title: Hadith on Rahmah: Be merciful, forgive so Allah forgives you
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be merciful to others, and you will receive mercy. Forgive others, and Allah will forgive you.”

title: Hadith on Elders: Whoever honors elders will be honored in old age
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No youth honors his elders but that Allah will appoint someone to honor him in his old age.”

title: Hadith on Patience: Allah afflicts him to compensate for his deeds
t: Al-Jallaj ibn Hakim reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, if a servant is destined for a rank he has not achieved by his good deeds, Allah puts him to trial in his body, or his wealth, or his children. Then, Allah makes him endure it until he reaches the rank decreed for him.”
q: Verily, if a servant is destined for a rank he has not achieved by his good deeds, Allah puts him to trial in his body, or his wealth, or his children. … Then, Allah makes him endure it until he reaches the rank decreed for him.

title: Malik on ‘Ilm: Do not extinguish light of knowledge with sins
t: Ibn al-Qayyim reported: When Imam al-Shafi’i, may Allah have mercy on him, sat in front of Malik and read to him, Malik was impressed by his intelligence, wisdom, and complete understanding. Malik said, “Verily, I see Allah has placed light in your heart, so do not extinguish it with the darkness of disobedience.”

title: Shurayh on Calamity: I praise Allah four times if I am afflicted
t: Al-Sha’bi reported: Shurayh, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, if I am afflicted by a calamity, then I praise Allah four times. I praise Him that it was not worse than it was. I praise Him as He provides me with the patience to bear it. I praise Him as He guides me to recall my hope for reward, and I praise Him as He did not make it a calamity in my religion.”

title: Hadith on Wudu: Remembering Allah in a state of purity
t: Al-Muhajir ibn Qunfudh reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I dislike to mention the name of Allah unless I am in a state of purity.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Door of mercy for those who supplicate
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever among you has the door of supplication opened for him, the door of mercy is opened for him as well. Allah is not asked for anything more beloved to Him than to be asked for wellness. Supplication benefits by what is sent down and what is not sent down. O servants of Allah, you must supplicate.”

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet weeps during his prayers
t: Abu Mutarrif reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was praying. His chest made a sound like a boiling water pot from his crying.

title: Hadith on Jumu’ah: Friday is an Eid, dress nice, wear perfume
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has made this day of Friday a celebration for the Muslims. Whoever comes to Friday prayer, let him bathe himself, apply perfume if he has it, and use the toothstick.”

title: Hadith on Trials: Believers put to trial until all sins expiated
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believing men and women continue to be under trial in their lives, their children, and their wealth, until they meet Allah without any sin.”

title: Hadith on Sabr: Patience with losing eyesight leads to Paradise
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah said: If I afflict My servant in his two dear eyes and he remains patient, he will be compensated for them with Paradise.”

title: Hadith on Pestilence: Believers who die by plague are martyrs
t: Aisha reported: She asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about plagues, and he said, “It is a punishment that Allah sends upon whomever He wills, but Allah has made it mercy for the believers. Any servant who resides in a land afflicted by plague, remaining patient and hoping in reward from Allah, knowing that nothing will befall him but what Allah has decreed, then he will be given the reward of a martyr.”

title: Abu Sa’id on Wudu: Supplication to raise a good deed to the Throne
t: Qays ibn ‘Ubad reported: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever performs ablution and completes his ablution by saying, ‘Glory to you, O Allah, I bear witness there is no god but you, I seek your forgiveness and I repent to you,’ then Allah will leave an imprint upon the deed, it will be raised to the Throne, and nothing will break it until the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Hadith on Haya: Modesty in Paradise, shamelessness in Hellfire
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Modesty is part of faith and faith is in Paradise. Shamelessness is part of insolence and insolence is in Hellfire.”

title: Hadith on Haya’: Modesty is beauty, obscenity is ugly
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Vulgarity is not found in anything but that it disgraces it, and modesty is not found in anything but that it beautifies it.”

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Best charity is to spend on your family
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best coin for a man to spend is the coin spent on his dependents, and the coin spent by a man on his mount in the way of Allah, and the coin spent by a man on his companions in the way of Allah.”

title: Hadith on Charity: Do not withhold, lest Allah hold it against you
t: Asma’ bint Abi Bakr reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have nothing in my house but what was given to me by my husband Al-Zubayr. Shall I give it in charity?” The Prophet said, “Yes, do not withhold it, lest Allah hold it against you.”

title: Hadith on Pardon: Forgive your servant seventy times a day
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, how many times should I pardon my servant?” The Prophet said, “Seventy times in each day.”

title: Hadith on Wudu: Angels supplicate for those who sleep with ablution
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever retired for the night in a state of purity, an angel will reside with him in his bed. He will not awaken for an hour in the night but that the angel says: O Allah, forgive this servant of yours, for he retired in a state of purity.”

title: Hadith on Graves: The Prophet allows women to visit graveyards
t: Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, returned one day from the graveyard. I said, “O mother of the believers, from where have you returned?” Aisha said, “From the grave of my brother, Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Bakr.” I said, “Did not the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibit you women from visiting graves?” Aisha said, “Yes, he prohibited us at first, but then he commanded us to visit them.”

title: Hadith on Da’wah: Give glad tidings, make it easy, remain united
t: Abu Burdah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent him and Mu’adh to Yemen, saying, “Make things easy and do not make things difficult. Give glad tidings and do not repel people. Cooperate with each other and do not become divided.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tajwid: Make the Quran beautiful with your recitations
t: Al-Bara ibn ‘Azib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beautify the Quran with your voices.”
q: Beautify the Quran with your voices

title: Hadith on Quran: O Lord, let him be clothed with nobility
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Quran will be brought on the Day of resurrection and it will say for its reciter: O Lord, decorate him. So he will be clothed with a crown of nobility. Then it will say: O Lord, give him more. So he will be clothed with a suit of nobility. Then it will say: O Lord, be pleased with him. So Allah will be pleased with him and He will say: Recite and rise up, be increased in goodness for every verse.”

title: Hadith on Protection: Three people have a guarantee from Allah
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Three people have a guarantee from Allah.
