If he lives he will have provision to suffice him, and if he dies he will enter Paradise: one who enters and greets with peace has a guarantee from Allah, one who goes out to the mosque has a guarantee from Allah, and one who goes out in the way of Allah has a guarantee from Allah.”

title: Hadith on Istidraj: Gradually increasing punishment of sinners
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you see Allah giving a servant what he loves from the worldly life, despite his sinful disobedience, then surely it is luring him to destruction.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “Thus, when they forgot what they were reminded of, We opened the doors of every good thing for them until, as they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly with utter despair.” (6:44)
q: If you see Allah giving a servant what he loves from the worldly life, despite his sinful disobedience, then surely it is luring him to destruction. … Thus, when they forgot what they were reminded of, We opened the doors of every good thing for them until, as they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly with utter despair.

title: Hadith on Adultery: Warning not to sexually touch unrelated women
t: Ma’qil ibn Yasar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “For an iron nail to pierce the head of one of you would be better for him than to touch a woman who is not lawful for him.”

title: Hadith on Dunya: Allah protects His beloved from the world
t: Mahmud ibn Labid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty will put his faithful servant on a diet from the world when He loves him, just as you put your sick on a diet from food and drink, fearing for him.”

title: Hadith on Signs: Muslim civil wars are signs of the Hour
t: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the one in whose hand is my soul, the Hour will not be established until you kill your leader, you confront each other with swords, and your property will be inherited by the worst of you.”
gf: Jayyid (very good) according to Ibn Hajar

title: Umar on Pleasure: Rather, I wanted to keep my good deeds
t: Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “I surely know best the easy life. If I wished, I would have eaten fine liver and roasted meat, but rather I want to keep my good deeds. Allah Almighty described some people, saying: You exhausted your pleasures during your life in the world and you enjoyed them.” (46:20)

title: Hadith on Gazing: No second glance at a woman
t: Buraydah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not follow one glance at a woman with another. Verily, you are excused for the first one but not for the second.”

title: Hadith on Women: Accidentally glancing at a woman
t: Jarir reported: I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about accidentally glancing at a woman. The Prophet ordered me to look the other way.

title: Hadith on Muhammad: Sunlight shining from his face
t: Abu Huraira reported: I have not seen anyone more graceful than the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, as if the sunlight emanated from his face. I have not seen anyone quicker in his walking than the Prophet, as if the earth was folded for him. We would exert ourselves while he would not endure any difficulty.

title: Awza’i on Sunnah: Be careful not to contradict the Prophet
t: ‘Amir ibn Yasaf reported: Al-Awza’i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “O ‘Amir, if a tradition reaches you from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon, beware not to say differently. Verily, the Prophet conveyed from Allah Almighty.”

title: Hadith on Sujud: Each prostration rewarded by a degree
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No servant prostrates for the sake of Allah but that Allah will raise his status by a degree and expiate one of his sins.”
q: No servant prostrates for the sake of Allah but that Allah will raise his status by a degree and expiate one of his sins

title: Hadith on Salat: Allah blesses those who fill prayer rows
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah and His angels send blessings upon those who connect the rows of prayer, and those who fill the gaps will be raised a degree by Allah.”

title: Hadith on Greetings: Best to shake hands, not bow or kiss
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, when a man among us meets his brother or friend, should he bow for him?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No.” The man said, “Should he embrace him and kiss him?” The Prophet said, “No.” The man said, “Should he shake his hand?” The Prophet said, “Yes.”

title: Hadith of Dhikr: Best of you inspire the remembrance of Allah
t: Asma’ bint Yazid reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you about the best of you?” They said, “Of course.” The Prophet said, “Those who, if they are seen, they remind you of Allah. Shall I not tell you about the worst of you?” They said, “Of course.” The Prophet said, “Those who carry gossip and ruin relations between loved ones, seeking misery for the innocent.”
q: Shall I not tell you about the best of you? … Those who, if they are seen, they remind you of Allah. Shall I not tell you about the worst of you? … Those who carry gossip and ruin relations between loved ones, seeking misery for the innocent

title: Hadith on Salat: Guarding prayer is light, proof, and salvation
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, mentioned the prayer one day and he said, “Whoever preserves the prayers, they will be his light, proof, and salvation on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever does not preserve them will not have proof, nor light, nor salvation, and on the Day of Resurrection, he will be alongside Qarun, Haman, Pharaoh, and Ubayy ibn Khalaf.”
q: Whoever preserves the prayers, they will be his light, proof, and salvation on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever does not preserve them will not have proof, nor light, nor salvation, and on the Day of Resurrection, he will be alongside Qarun, Haman, Pharaoh, and Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

title: Hadith on Islam: Bonds of Islam undone until people do not pray
t: Abu Umamah al-Bahili reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The bonds of Islam will be undone one by one, and every time a bond is undone, the people will cling to what follows it. The first to be undone will be loss of judgment, and the last will be the prayer.”

title: Hadith on Quran: Companions learn ten verses at a time
t: Abu Abdur Rahman reported: The companions would learn to recite ten verses from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. They would not take another ten verses until they understood the knowledge and deeds they contained. They would say, “We learned sacred knowledge and action together.”

title: Hadith on Sujud: Keep forearms raised in prostration
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be straight in prostration and let none of you put his forearms on the ground like a dog.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Quran: Allah have mercy on one who reminded me
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was listening to a man recite the Quran in the mosque and he said, “May Allah have mercy upon him. He reminded me of a verse I was made to forget.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Quran: Do not say I deliberately forgot the Quran
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Wretched is one who says: I have forgotten such a verse. Rather, he was made to forget it. Strive to remember the Quran, for it is quicker to escape the hearts of men than camels.“
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Quran: Recite the Quran regularly, or you will forget
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the parable of the companion of the Quran is that of a tied camel. If he is committed to it, he will keep it. If he releases it, he will lose it.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Memorization: Review the Quran, it can be forgotten quickly
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be committed to the Quran. By the One in whose hand is my soul, it can leave you faster than a camel from its reins.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Forgiveness: Pardon the murderer, or be like him
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, with the killer of his relative. The Prophet said, “Pardon him,” but the man refused. The Prophet said, “Take the blood money,” but the man refused. The Prophet said, “Go and kill him, for you are like him.” Someone met with the man and told him that the Messenger of Allah said, “Kill him, for you are like him.” Thus, the man let him go.

title: Hadith on Honor: When a Muslim defends his brother’s reputation
t: Abu Darda reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever defends the reputation of his brother, Allah will defend his face from the Hellfire on the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Hadith on Malice: Do not gloat over your brother’s hardship
t: Wathilah ibn Al-Asqa’ reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not rejoice over the misfortune of your brother, lest Allah have mercy upon him and afflict you with trials.”

title: Hadith on Ayat al-Kursi: Throne Verse is greatest in Quran
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Abu Mundhir, do you know which verse in the Book of Allah with you is greatest?” I recited, “Allah! There is no God worthy of worship except Him, the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining,” (2:255). The Prophet struck me on the chest, saying, “By Allah, O Abu Mundhir, rejoice in this knowledge!”
q: Allah! There is no God worthy of worship except Him, the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining,

title: Hadith on Community: Devil attacks the isolated sheep
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If three people in a town or in the desert do not establish prayer among them, then Satan has overcome them. You must establish the congregation, for the wolf eats the isolated sheep.”

title: Hadith on Jama’ah: Prayer in mosque is twenty seven times better
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Prayer in congregation is better than prayer alone by twenty-seven degrees.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Masjid: Angels bless those who wait for prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The prayer of a man in congregation is twenty-five times better than prayer in his home or shop. When he performs ablution in a good manner and leaves to the mosque only to perform the prayer, then his every step will raise him a degree and expiate a sin until he enters the mosque. When he is performing prayer, the angels send blessings upon him for as long as he remains in his place of prayer. They say: O Allah, bless him and have mercy upon him. One of you continues to be in prayer as long as he is waiting for prayer.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Istighfar: Seek forgiveness for yourself and believers
t: Abdullah ibn Sarjis reported: I met the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and I ate a meal of stew with him. I said, “I ask Allah to forgive you, O Prophet.” The Prophet said, “Yes, and for you as well.” Then the Prophet recited the verse, “Seek forgiveness for your sins and for the believing men and women as well.” (47:19)

title: Hadith on Dishonesty: Allah punishes miserliness, false oaths
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are three to whom Allah will not speak on the Day of Resurrection, nor will he look at them, nor will he purify them, and they will have a painful punishment: A man who has extra water in his vessel but prevents a traveler from drinking it. And a man who trades goods after midday prayer, swearing by Allah that he had taken it for a certain price but it is not so. And a man who pledges allegiance to a Muslim leader only for something in the world. If he is given, he fulfills his pledge, and if he is not given, he does not fulfill it.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Mosques: More reward for walking to the Masjid
t: Jabir reported: A plot of land around the mosque was vacant, so the tribe of Salimah intended to move there to be closer to the mosque. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was told about that and he said to them, “I have heard that you intend to move closer to the mosque.” They said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we intend to do so.” The Prophet said, “O tribe of Salimah, keep to your houses and your steps will be recorded, keep to your houses and your steps will be recorded.”
q: I have heard that you intend to move closer to the mosque. … O tribe of Salimah, keep to your houses and your steps will be recorded, keep to your houses and your steps will be recorded.

title: Hadith on Masajid: Walkers to the Mosque given light
t: Burdah al-Aslami reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Give glad tidings to those who walk to the mosque in darkness of perfect light on the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Hadith on Curses: Prohibition of cursing people by name
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, raised his head from the last bowing in dawn prayer, saying, “O Allah, curse this person, and this person, and this person,” Then, Allah revealed the verse, “You have no say in the matter. It is up to Allah to turn to them in mercy or punish them, for they are surely wrongdoers.” (3:128)
q: You have no say in the matter. It is up to Allah to turn to them in mercy or punish them, for they are surely wrongdoers.

title: Hadith on Jumuah: Special moment for Friday supplications
t: Abu Burdah reported: Abdullah ibn Umar said to me, “Have you heard anything narrated by your father from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about the special moment on Friday?” I said, “Yes. I heard him narrate that the Messenger of Allah said, ‘It is the moment between the beginning of the sermon and the completion of the prayer.’”

title: Hadith on Jumuah: Special hour for Friday supplications
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, mentioned the day of Friday and he said, “In it is a moment in which no Muslim stands to pray and ask Allah for something but that he will be given it,” and he indicated with his hand that the time is very short.
q: In it is a moment in which no Muslim stands to pray and ask Allah for something but that he will be given it
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ghusl: Recommendation to bathe on Friday
t:
Samurah ibn Jundab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever performs ablution on Friday has done well, but whoever performs a ritual bath has done better.”

Al-Shafi’i said, “The command of the Prophet to perform a ritual bath on Friday indicates a preference for it, not an obligation.”

title: Hadith on Jumuah: Neglecting Friday prayer leads to hard heart
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said while upon his wooden pulpit, “People need to stop neglecting the Friday prayers, lest Allah place a seal over their hearts and then they become heedless.”

title: Hadith on Jumuah: Minor sins forgiven until next Friday
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever performs ablution in the best manner, comes to Friday prayer, and listens while remaining quiet, his sins will be forgiven until the next Friday and an additional three days, but whoever plays with pebbles has behaved frivolously.”

title: Hadith on Jumu’ah: Angels record attendance at Friday prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Friday arrives, angels are over the door of every mosque to record those who arrive one by one. When the Imam sits to begin, they close their scrolls and come to listen to the reminder. The parable of one who comes early is that of one who offers a fine camel, the next like one who offers a cow, the next like one who offers a ram, the next like one who offers a chicken, the next like one who offers an egg.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Prayer: Men pray in front, women in back
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best rows for men are the front rows and the worst are the back rows. The best rows for women are the back rows and the worst are the front rows.”

title: Hadith on Trade: Honest business is blessed, lying is not
t: Hakim ibn Hizam reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Both parties in a business transaction have the right to annul it, as long as they have not separated. If they are truthful and clear with one another, their transaction is blessed. If they lie and conceal something, the blessing of their transaction will be eliminated.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Greed: The Prophet fears Muslims will fight for wealth
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I am not afraid that you will commit idolatry, rather I am afraid you will compete with each other for the world.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Mahdi: Prosperity appears before end of time
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will be a Caliph near the end of time who will distribute wealth without counting it.”

title: Hadith on Dajjal: False Messiah promises fake paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you about the False Messiah which no prophet has told his people before? Verily, he is blind in one eye. He will come with the likeness of paradise and fire. That which he calls ‘paradise’ is the Hellfire. I have surely warned you just as Noah had warned his people.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dajjal: No Fitnah greater than False Messiah
t: ‘Imran ibn Husayn reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Nothing between the creation of Adam until the establishment of the Hour is a greater tribulation than the False Messiah.”

title: Hadith on Dajjal: False Messiah enters every country except Mecca and Medina
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No land will be safe from the False Messiah except for Mecca and Medina. No passage leads to them but that it will be guarded by angels arranged in ranks. The False Messiah will appear in a barren place next to Medina, and the city will be shaken three times. Allah will expel from it every unbeliever and hypocrite.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Imams: Followers not responsible for Imam’s mistakes
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You will be led in prayer. If they are correct, it will be a reward for them and for you. If they make mistakes, it will be for you and against them.”

title: Hadith on Water: Conserve water even by a running stream
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by Sa’d while he was performing ablution. The Prophet said, “What is this extravagance?” Sa’d said, “Is there extravagance with water in ablution?” The Prophet said, “Yes, even if you were on the banks of a flowing river.”

title: Hadith on Murder: Allah throws them all in Hell together
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Were the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth to conspire in the killing of a believer, Allah would cast them all into Hellfire.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Dua: Reward for each believer he seeks forgiveness for
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever seeks forgiveness for the believing men and women, Allah will record a good deed for him by each man and woman.”

title: Hadith on Siyam: Recommendation to fast three days a month
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Abu Dharr, if you are going to fast three days of the month, then fast on the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days.”

title: Hadith on Salat: Shorter surahs in day, longer at dawn
t: Jabir ibn Samurah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would recite in the noon prayer, “By the night as it envelopes,” (92:1) and similar chapters to those in the afternoon prayer, and in the morning prayer he would recite longer than those

title: Hadith on Juz: Reciting a part of the Quran nightly
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever falls asleep and forgets to recite his portion of the Quran, or a part of it, if he recites it between the dawn and noon prayers it will be recorded as if he recited it during the night.”

title: Hadith on Salat: Recitation of shorter surahs in mid-day prayers
t: Jabir ibn Samurah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would recite in the noon and afternoon prayers the chapters, “By the heaven and the morning star,” (86:1) and, “By the heaven with great stars,” (85:1) and other chapters of similar length.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Eids: Days of Eid are celebrations, not for fasting
t:
‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The day of Arafat, the day of sacrifice, and the three following days of al-Tashriq are celebrations for the people of Islam. They are days of eating and drinking.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “The people of knowledge acted upon this. They disapproved of fasting the three days of al-Tashriq.”

title: Hadith on Hajj: Fasting or not on the day of Arafat
t:
Ibn Umar reported: I have performed the Hajj pilgrimage with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he did not fast during Arafat. I performed it with Abu Bakr and he did not fast, with Umar and he did not fast, and with Uthman and he did not fast. I do not fast it, nor do I command it or prohibit it.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “The practice among the majority of scholars is that it is recommended to break fasting on the day of Arafat for a man to have strength to supplicate. Some scholars would fast on the day of Arafat while at Arafat.”

title: Hadith on Ihram: Pilgrims may kill harmful animals if needed
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Five animals are harmful and are lawful to kill while in a state of pilgrimage or otherwise: a snake, a speckled crow, a rat, a biting dog, and a kite.”

title: Hadith on Hajj: Trading during pilgrimage season
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Dhul al-Majaz, ‘Ukazha, and Matjar were markets people attended in the time of ignorance. When Islam came, the companions disliked that during the Hajj season until the verse was revealed, “There is no blame on you for seeking the bounty of your Lord during this journey.” (2:198)
q: There is no blame on you for seeking the bounty of your Lord during this journey.

title: Hadith on Hajj: Taking children to the pilgrimage
t: Ibn Abbas reported: A woman lifted up her child and said, “O Messenger of Allah, is the Hajj pilgrimage for this child?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Yes, you will have a reward.”

title: Hadith on Hajj: Perform Hajj and ‘Umrah for parents
t: Al-Fadl reported: A woman from the tribe of Khath’am said, “O Messenger of Allah, my father is an old man and Allah has obligated him to perform the Hajj pilgrimage, but he cannot ride on the back of a camel.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Perform the Hajj pilgrimage on his behalf.”
q: P

title: Hadith on Pilgrimage: ‘Umrah in Ramadan equal to Hajj
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the ‘Umrah pilgrimage during Ramadan is equal to Hajj.”
q: Verily, the ‘Umrah pilgrimage during Ramadan is equal to Hajj
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Beggars: No blessing in persistent begging
t: Mu’awiyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not be persistent in begging. By Allah, if one of you asks me for something and I bring out what he asked for and give it to him unwillingly, there is no blessing in it.”

title: Hadith on Islam: Successful are those content with Islam
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He has succeeded who embraced Islam, whose provision is sufficient, and whom Allah has made content with what He has given him.”

title: Hadith on Begging: Permission to beg for charity in three cases
t: Qabisah ibn Mukhariq reported: I was under debt so I came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and I asked him about it. The Prophet said, “Wait until we receive charity, then we will order it to be given to you.” Then the Prophet said, “O Qabisah, begging is not lawful except for one of three cases: a man who is in heavy debt, so asking others is permissible for him until he pays it, after which he must stop; a man whose property is destroyed by a calamity, so asking is permissible for him until he can support himself; and a man who is afflicted by poverty attested to by three astute members of his people, so asking is permissible for him until he can support himself. O Qabisah, besides these three begging is forbidden and the beggar consumes what is forbidden.”

title: Hadith on Beggars: Whoever begs without need in Hellfire
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever begs people for wealth in order to accumulate more riches, he is only asking for a hot coal from Hellfire. Let him ask for a little or a lot.”

title: Hadith on Charity: A pure soul who receives charity is blessed in it
t: Hakim ibn Hizam reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, this wealth is green and sweet. Whoever receives it with a pure soul will be blessed in it. Whoever receives it with a selfish soul will not be blessed in it, for he is like one who eats and is not satiated. The upper hand is better than the lower hand.”
q: Verily, this
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Begging: Permission to beg in dire circumstances
t: Samurah ibn Jundub reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Acts of begging are lacerations with which a man disfigures his face. Whoever wishes may preserve his dignity and whoever wishes may abandon it, unless a man asks those in authority or he has no other way in the matter.”

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Allah multiplies reward for spending charity
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None gives charity from what is good, for Allah only accepts what is good, except that the Merciful takes it with His right hand. Even if it is a date, it is nurtured in the hand of the Merciful until it becomes greater than a mountain, just as one of you nurtures his young horse or camel.”

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Giving charity is better than receiving it
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The upper hand is better than the lower hand. The upper hand is one that gives and the lower hand is one that takes.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Beggars: Truly poor people refrain from begging
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The poor person is not the one who is satisfied with a date or two, or a morsel or two, but rather the poor person is only one who abstains from begging. Recite the verse if you wish: They do not beg people persistently.” (2:273)
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Beggars: Punishment for too much begging
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man continues to beg people until he will come on the Day of Resurrection without any flesh on his face.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Zakat: No charity is due on minimum amounts
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No charity is due on less than five bundles of dates, nor less than five camels, nor less than five ounces of silver.”
q: No charity is due on less than five bundles of dates, nor less than five camels, nor less than five ounces of silver

title: Hadith on Salah: Satan makes him remember the world in prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, if one of you stands for prayer, Satan comes to distract him until he does not know how many cycles he has performed. When that happens to one of you, let him perform two prostrations while he is sitting.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Knowledge of Laylat al-Qadr removed by insults
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to inform people about the Night of Decree in Ramadan, but two Muslim men were insulting each other. The Prophet said, “Verily, I have come out to tell you about the Night of Decree, but two men were insulting each other. Thus, its knowledge was taken away and perhaps it is better for you. Look for it during the seventh, ninth, or fifth night of the last ten nights.”

title: Hadith on Travel: Supplication for returning home
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, whenever he returned from the armies, campaigns, Hajj, or ‘Umrah, he would exalt Allah three times at the top of every hill or plateau. Then, the Prophet would say, “There is no God but Allah alone, without any partner, who controls the dominion, deserves all praise, and has power over all things. We are returning, repenting, worshiping, prostrating to our Lord, and praising Him. Allah alone fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, and routed the Confederates.”
q: There is no God but Allah alone, without any partner, who controls the dominion, deserves all praise, and has power over all things. We are returning, repenting, worshiping, prostrating to our Lord, and praising Him. Allah alone fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, and routed the Confederates.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hajj: Go perform pilgrimage with your wife
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man should not be alone with a woman, nor should a woman travel unless a guardian is with her.” A man stood up and said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have been assigned to a military expedition, but my wife has already left for the Hajj pilgrimage.” The Prophet said, “Go and perform the pilgrimage with your wife.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Mahram: Women travel with guardians for protection
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is not lawful for a woman who has faith in Allah and the Last Day to travel for a day and a night without her guardian.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet’s supplication for coming home
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: Abu Talha and I returned from a journey along with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and Safiyya rode behind him on his camel. When we reached the outskirts of Medina, the Prophet said, “We are returning and repenting, worshiping our Lord and praising Him.” The Prophet continued to say this until we reached Medina.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Travel: Do not surprise family in the night
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you is absent for a long time while traveling, let him not startle his family in the night upon his return.”
q: If one of you is absent for a long time while traveling, let him not startle his family in the night upon his return
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Travel: Return to family as fast as you can
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Travel is a piece of torment. It prevents one of you from eating, drinking, and sleeping. When he has finished his purpose, let him quickly return to his family.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for traveling at night
t: Ibn Umar reported: Whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, set out on a journey, he would say by nightfall, “O earth, my Lord and your Lord is Allah. I seek refuge in Him from your evil, from the evil you contain, from the evil created in you, and from the evil of what walks upon you. I seek refuge in Allah from lions, from serpents, from scorpions, from the inhabitants of the land, and from an evil parent and his offspring.”

title: Hadith on Dua: I seek refuge in perfect words of Quran
t: Khawlah bint Hakim reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever enters a residence and then says, ‘I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created,’ nothing will harm him until he departs from that residence.”

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet supplicates for travelers
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, I intend to travel, so instruct me.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must be mindful of Allah and exalt Him every time you ascend a height.” As the man turned to leave, the Prophet said, “O Allah, shorten the distance for him and make travel easy upon him.”

title: Hadith on Istighfar: Allah pleased by asking His forgiveness
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, your Lord is delighted when His servant says: O Lord, forgive my sins, for none forgives sins besides You.”

title: Hadith on Travel: The Prophet’s supplication for journey
t: Ibn Umar reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would mount his camel for travel, he would exalt Allah three times and then say, “Glory be to Him who has made this subservient to us, for we have no power over it ourselves, and to our Lord we shall return. O Allah, we ask You during this journey for righteousness, fear of You, and such deeds that are pleasing to You. O Allah, make this journey easy for us and make the distance short for us. O Allah, You are our companion during the journey and the guardian of the family. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, ugly scenes, and an evil return to our property and family.” When the Prophet returned, he would say these words and add to them, “We are those who return, those who repent, those who worship and who praise our Lord.”

title: Hadith on Animals: Fear Allah in creatures you own
t: Abdullah ibn Ja’far reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered a garden among the Ansar. When a camel saw the Prophet, it started weeping and making sounds as its tears flowed. The Prophet came to it and patted it on the head, so it became silent. The Prophet said, “Who is the master of this camel? To whom does it belong?” A young man from the Ansar came and said, “This is mine, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “Do you not fear Allah in this animal whom Allah has placed in your possession? She has complained to me that you keep her hungry and tired.”
q: Who is the master of this camel? To whom does it belong?

title: Hadith on Safety: Dangerous to travel alone at night
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If people knew what I knew about traveling alone, no one would set out alone at night.”

title: Hadith on Morning: Bless my Ummah in early mornings
t:
Sakhr ibn al-Ghamidi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, bless my nation in their early morning.”

Sakhr said, “When the Prophet prepared a company or army, he would dispatch them at the start of the day. When he prepared a trading convoy, he would dispatch them at the start of the day and they would acquire much wealth.”

title: Hadith on Intimacy: The Prophet’s supplication before marital intimacy
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you goes to his wife, he should say: In the name of Allah, keep Satan away and keep Satan away from what you have provided us. If Allah has decreed a child for them, he will not be harmed.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Khusu’: Reverence for Allah to become rare
t: Abu Darda reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The first thing to be taken from this nation will be humble reverence, until you will not see anyone in it with reverence.”

title: Hadith on Salaam: Greet with peace when asking permission
t: Rib’i ibn Hirash reported: A man from the tribe of ‘Amir sought permission to enter the home of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The man said, “May I enter?” The Prophet said to his servant, “Go out to this man and teach him how to ask permission to enter. Tell him to say: Peace be upon you, may I enter?” The man heard this and said, “Peace be upon you, may I enter?” Then, the Prophet permitted him to enter.

title: Hadith on Salaam: Greet with peace when coming and going
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you arrives in a gathering, let him greet them with peace. When he intends to leave, let him leave them with peace. The first greeting is not more worthy than the last.”

title: Hadith on Salaam: Greet your family with peace
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “O my son, when you enter upon your family, greet them with peace. It will be a blessing for you and the people of your household.”
q: O my son, w

title: Hadith on Salaam: Greet with peace again and again
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you meets his brother, let him greet him with peace. If they are separated by a tree, a wall, or a stone, and he meets him again, let him greet him with peace again.”
q: When one of you meets his brother, let him greet him with peace. If they are separated by a tree, a wall, or a stone, and he meets him again, let him greet him with peace again.

title: Hadith on Salaam: Best people initiate greetings of peace
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the closest to Allah are those who are first to greet with peace.”

title: Hadith on Salaam: Greeting groups with peace
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The rider should greet with peace those who are walking, those who are walking should greet those who are sitting, and a small group should greet a larger group.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salaam: Greeting with peace during night
t: Al-Miqdam ibn al-Aswad reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would come during the night and he would greet with peace, such that those who were sleeping would not be awakened but those who were awake would hear it.

title: Hadith on Speaking: Talk clearly for understanding
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would speak, he repeated himself three times until he was understood. Whenever he came to people and greeted them with peace, he would greet them three times.

title: Hadith on Jibreel: Angel Gabriel greets you with peace
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to her, “O Aisha, here is the Angel Gabriel to greet you with peace.” Aisha said, “And upon him be peace, the mercy of Allah, and His blessings. You see what I do not see.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Umar on Salaam: Ibn Umar greets everyone in market
t: Al-Tufayl reported: I would come with Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, to the market and when we did so, Ibn Umar would not pass anyone but that he would greet them with peace, whether they were selling merchandise or were poor. I came to Ibn Umar one day and asked him to follow me to the market. I said, “What will you do in the market, if you will not sell or buy or barter or sit in the gatherings?” Ibn Umar said, “O big bellied one! We only go out in the morning to greet them with peace. We greet with peace whomever we meet.”

title: Hadith on Ahkam: Seven prohibitions and commands
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited us from seven things: using gold rings, silk, flax, brocade, red saddle clothes, taffeta, and silver vessels. And the Prophet commanded us to do seven things: to visit the sick, to follow the funeral procession, to bless those who sneeze, to return the greeting of peace, to accept invitations, to help others fulfill their oaths, and to support the oppressed.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jannah: Description of believers in Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The first group to enter Paradise will be shining like a full moon on a clear night, and those who follow them will be glittering like the most brilliant stars in the heaven. They will not need to spt, sneeze, or relieve themselves. Their utensils will be gold, and their combs will be gold and silver. Their centers will be fragranced with aloe wood, and their perspiration will emit the pleasant fragrance of musk. Each man may have two wives, the marrow of their bones visible due to their beauty. There will be no disagreement between them. They will not hate each other. Their hearts will be like one heart, glorifying Allah morning and evening.”
q: There will be no disagreement between them. They will not hate each other. Their hearts will be like one heart, glorifying Allah morning and evening
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salaam: Allah teaches Adam greeting of peace
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah created Adam in His image, sixty cubits tall. When He created him, Allah said: Go and greet these groups of assembled angels with peace and listen to how they greet you, for this will be the greeting among your progeny. Adam said: Peace be upon you. The angels said: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. Thus, they added the mercy of Allah. Everyone who enters Paradise will be in the image of Adam, for the creation has continued to diminish in stature until now.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ameen: Saying ameen with the Imam and the angels
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the Imam says ameen, then say ameen as the angels say ameen. Whoever says ameen when the angels do, his previous sins will be forgiven.”
q: When the Imam says ameen, then say ameen as the angels say ameen. Whoever says ameen when the angels do, his previous sins will be forgiven.”

title: Hadith on Salat: Saying ameen aloud after Surat al-Fatihah
t:
Wa’il ibn Hujr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would recite the verse, “Not those who have earned anger, nor who go astray,” (1:7) and he would say with a raised voice, “Ameen.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “More than one of the people of knowledge among the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, their successors, and those after them narrated that a man should raise his voice to say ameen and he should not make it silent. Such was said by Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq.”

title: Hadith on Hamd: Praise for Allah even after children die
t: Abu Musa al-Ashari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the child of a servant dies, Allah says to the angels: Have you taken the life of My servant’s child? They say yes. Allah says: Have you taken the fruit of his heart? They say yes. Allah says: What has My servant said? They say: He has praised You and said to Allah we belong and to Allah we return. Allah says: Build a house for My servant in Paradise and name it the House of Praise.”

title: Hadith on Hamd: Every matter begins with praising Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Every matter of importance that is not begun with the praise of Allah will be left deficient.”

title: Hadith on Fitrah: The Prophet chooses natural milk, not wine
t: Abu Huraira reported: On the night of the Ascension, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was presented with two vessels, one full of wine and the other full of milk. The Prophet looked at them both, and he chose the vessel full of milk. The Angel Gabriel, upon him be peace, said, “All praise is due to Allah, who has guided you to that which is natural, for had you chosen the wine your nation would have been led astray.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Lies: The worst of false claims
t: Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the worst of lies are for a man to claim lineage from someone other than his father, or that he saw a dream he did not see, or to say the Messenger of Allah said what he did not say.”

title: Hadith on Nightmares: Refuge in Allah from bad dreams
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you sees a dream he dislikes, let him blow on his left side three times and seek refuge in Allah from Satan three times. Let him turn to the other side from which he was sleeping.”
q: If one of you sees a dream he dislikes, let him blow on his left side three times and seek refuge in Allah from Satan three times. Let him turn to the other side from which he was sleeping.

title: Hadith on Dreams: Refuge in Allah from nightmares
t: Abu Qatadah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The good dream is from Allah and the bad dream is from Satan. Whoever sees something he dislikes, let him blow to his left side three times and seek refuge from Satan. Verily, it will not harm him and Satan cannot appear as me.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Visions: Seeing the Prophet in your dreams
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever sees me in a dream has truly seen me, for Satan cannot imitate me.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for leaving gathering
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would not stand to leave an assembly until saying these supplications for his companions, “O Allah, apportion us fear of You that will stop us from disobeying You, apportion us obedience to You that will allow us to reach Paradise, and apportion us conviction that will make calamities in the world easier for us to endure. Let us enjoy our hearing, our sight, and our power, as long as You let us live. Make heirs among us and let retaliation be upon those who oppress us. Support us against our enemies and let no calamity afflict our religion. Let not the world be our greatest worry, nor the extent of our knowledge, and let not the unmerciful rule over us.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication to expiate sins in gathering
t: Abu Barzah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would say some final words when intending to leave an assembly, “O Allah, glory and praise be to You. I testify there is no God but You, I ask Your forgiveness, and I repent to You.” A man once said to him, “O Messenger of Allah, you spoke words you have not in the past.” The Prophet said, “It is an expiation for what is done in the assembly.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication after idle talk in gathering
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever sits in a gathering and indulges in idle talk, then let him say before leaving that gathering, ‘Glory be to You, O Allah, and Your praises. I bear witness there is no God but You, I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You,’ as he will be forgiven for what happened in that gathering of his.”

title: Hadith on Assembly: Best gatherings make room for everyone
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best gatherings make room for the most people.”

title: Hadith on Gathering: Let him keep his seat when he returns
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a man stands from his seat and later returns to it, he is more entitled to it.”

title: Hadith on Gathering: Make room for everyone to sit down
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man should not be made to stand so another can sit in his place. Rather, be accommodating and make room.”
q: A man should not be made to stand so another can sit in his place.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Rest: Not sitting in undignified manner
t: Al-Sharid ibn Suwayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by me while I was sitting with my left hand behind my back and leaning upon it. The Prophet said, “Do you sit like one with whom Allah is angry?”

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Allah displeased with unmindful gatherings
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No people sit in a gathering without remembering Allah, or sending blessings upon their Prophet, but that they will earn the displeasure of Allah. If Allah wills, He will punish them. If He wills, He will forgive them.”

title: Hadith on Sitting: Companions in awe of the Prophet
t: Qaylah bint Makhramah reported: I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sitting with his arms around his legs. When I saw the Messenger of Allah sitting so humbly, I trembled in awe of him.

title: Hadith on Sitting: Thighs on stomach, arms around legs
t: Ibn Umar reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sitting by the Ka’bah with his thighs on his stomach and arms around his legs.

title: Hadith on Fajr: The Prophet sits after prayer until sunrise
t: Jabir ibn Samurah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would pray the dawn prayer and sit crossed legged in his place until the sun had risen brightly.

title: Hadith on Rest: Laying on one’s back, one foot over other
t: Abdullah ibn Zayd reported: He saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, lying on his back in the mosque, placing one leg over the other.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Consequences for forgetting Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever sits in a place and does not remember Allah, he will face a consequence from Allah. Whoever lies down to sleep and does not remember Allah, he will face a consequence from Allah.”

title: Hadith on Resting: Discouraged to lie on stomach
t: Takhfah ibn Qays reported: While I was lying on my belly in the mosque, a man shook me with his foot, saying, “Verily, Allah hates this posture.” I looked up and it was the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.

title: Hadith on Extravagance: Silver and gold dishes, cutlery forbidden
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever drinks from a vessel of gold or silver, surely he has only filled his belly with the fire of Hell.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Luxury: Prohibition of silk clothes, gold dishes
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not drink from gold or silver vessels, and do not wear silk or brocade. Verily, these are for unbelievers in the world and for us in the Hereafter.”
q: Do not drink from gold or silver vessels, and do not wear silk or brocade. Verily, these are for unbelievers in the world and for us in the Hereafter.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hosting: Serves guests before yourself
t: Abu Qatadah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One who serves drinks to his guests should be the last to drink.”

title: Hadith on Manners: Concession to eat walking, drink standing
t: Ibn Umar reported: In the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, we would eat while walking and drink while standing.

title: Hadith on Meals: Blessings in sharing food with others
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The food of one person is enough for two, the food of two is enough for four, and the food of four is enough for eight.”

title: Hadith on Humility: The Prophet never walks ahead of anyone
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: I never saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, eating while reclining, nor walking with two men behind him.

title: Hadith on Community: Eat food together, remember Allah
t: Washi ibn Harb reported: They said, “O Messenger of Allah, we eat but we are not satiated.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Perhaps you eat separately?” They said yes. The Prophet said, “Eat your meals together and mention the name of Allah over it, for you will be blessed in it.”
q: Perhaps you eat separately?
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Invitations: Accept invites, supplicate for host
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you is invited for a meal, let him respond. If he is fasting, let him pray for the host. If he is not fasting, let him eat.”

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet’s supplication for finishing meal
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say when he cleared the table of his meal, “All praise is due to Allah, abundantly, purely, and blessed in it, yet such praise is neither enough, nor abandoned, nor is it without need, Our Lord.”

title: Hadith on Eating: Remembering Allah is enough
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was eating with six of his companions when a bedouin came and ate all of the food in two bites. The Prophet said, “If he had mentioned the name of Allah, it would have been enough for all of you.”

title: Hadith on Meals: Satan eats with him until Allah remembered
t: Umayyah ibn Makshi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was sitting and a man was eating food, but he did not mention the name of Allah until nothing remained but a morsel. When the man raised it to his mouth, he said, “In the name of Allah, beginning and ending.” The Prophet laughed, and then he said, “Satan continued to eat with him, but when he mentioned the name of Allah Almighty, he vomited what was in his stomach.”
q: Satan continued to eat with him, but when he mentioned the name of Allah Almighty, he vomited what was in his stomach

title: Hadith on Food: Satan eats when Allah is not remembered
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Satan permits himself to eat the food over which the name of Allah is not mentioned.”

title: Hadith on Food: Remember Allah, eat with right hand
t: ‘Umar ibn Abi Salamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “Young man, mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat what is in front of you.”
q: Young man, mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat what is in front of you.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Silk: Men wearing silk for medical reasons
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, granted a concession to Al-Zubayr and Abdur Rahman to wear silk when they were suffering from a rash.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Vanity: Using expensive vessels and silk furniture
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited us from eating and drinking out of golden or silver vessels. He prohibited us from wearing silk or brocade, or sitting upon anything made from them.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Vanity: Prayer not accepted in trailing garments
t: Abu Huraira reported: While a man was praying with his garment draped below himself, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Go and perform ablution.” The man went and performed ablution, then he came to the Prophet. The Prophet said, “Go and perform ablution.” The man went and performed ablution, then he came back to the Prophet. Another man said to him, “O Messenger of Allah, why did you order him to perform ablution again?” The Prophet said, “Verily, he was praying with his garment draped below himself. Allah Almighty does not accept the prayer of a man who drapes his garment.”
q: Go and perform ablution … Go and perform ablution … Verily, he was praying with his garment draped below himself. Allah Almighty does not accept the prayer of a man who drapes his garment

title: Hadith on Insults: Do not reciprocate harsh words
t: Jabir ibn Sulaym reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a man insults you and disparages you for what he knows about you, do not disparage him for what you know about him. Verily, the penalty will only be against him.”

title: Hadith on Janazah: The Prophet shrouded for his funeral
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was shrouded for his funeral in three white cotton garments, among which was neither a shirt, nor a turban.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Turbans: The Prophet wears a black turban
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered Mecca on the day of its liberation while wearing a black turban, without preparing to perform the pilgrimage.

title: Hadith on Clothes: Permission to wear green clothing
t: Abu Rimthah reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, wearing two green cloaks.

title: Hadith on Clothing: The Prophet was handsome, wore red clothing
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was of moderate height, with broad shoulders and hair that reached to his ears. I once saw him wearing a red mantle and I have not seen anyone more handsome than him.

title: Hadith on Iftar: Angels bless those give food to break fast
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to the home of Sa’d ibn ‘Ubadah, who presented him with bread and olive oil. The Prophet ate them and he said, “The fasting have broken their fast with you, the righteous have eaten your food, and the angels send blessings upon you.”
q: The fasting have broken their fast with you, the righteous have eaten your food, and the angels send blessings upon you.

title: Hadith on Fasting: Angels bless a fasting person who feeds others
t: Umm ‘Umarah bint Ka’b reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered her home and she served him food. The Prophet said, “Will you eat?” She said, “Indeed, I am fasting.” The Prophet said, “Verily, angels send blessings upon a fasting person when others eat in their presence until they finish.”
q: Will you eat

title: Hadith on Clothing: The Prophet’s supplication for wearing new clothes
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, wore a new garment he would name it, such as a turban, a shirt, or a cloak, and then he would say, “O Allah, praise be to you that you have dressed me with it. I ask you for its goodness and the goodness for which it was made. I seek refuge in you from its evil and the evil for which it was made.”

title: Hadith on Humility: Let him choose any garment of faith to wear
t: Mu’adh ibn Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever gives up fine clothes due to humility for the sake of Allah, even though he is able to wear them, then Allah will call him on the Day of Resurrection in front of all creation that he may choose any garment of faith he desires to wear.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Vanity: Humiliation for clothing in ostentation
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever wears a garment in vanity, Allah will make him wear a garment of humiliation on the Day of Resurrection, then He will set it ablaze with fire.”

title: Hadith on Imitation: Whoever imitates people is one of them
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever imitates a people is one of them.”

title: Hadith on Clothing: The Prophet wore long sleeves
t: Asma’ bint Yazid reported: The sleeves of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would extend to his wrists.

title: Hadith on Qamis: The Prophet’s favorite clothing
t: Umm Salamah reported: The most beloved garment to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was the long shirt.

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for meals and getting dressed
t: Mu’adh ibn Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever eats a meal and then says, ‘All praise is due to Allah, who has fed me this food and provided for me, without any power or strength from myself,’ he will be forgiven for his past and future sins. Whoever wears a new garment and then says, ‘All praise is due to Allah, who has clothed me with this garment and provided for me, without any power for strength from myself,’  he will be forgiven for his past and future sins.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Seek refuge before using the lavatory
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered the washroom, he would say, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from foul and noxious things.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for bedtime, waking up
t: Abu Dharr reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would go to sleep at night, he would say, “In Your name we die and we live.” When the Prophet woke up, he would say, “All praise is due to Allah, who has given us life after our death, and unto Him is the Resurrection.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for leaving home, protection from Satan
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever says when he leaves his house, ‘In the name of Allah, I trust in Allah, for there is no movement or might but in Allah,’ then it will be said to him that you have been sufficed and protected, and the devils will be far from him.”

title: Hadith on Salah: When walking to prayer, you are in prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the prayer is established, do not come to it running, but rather come to it walking. You must be calm, for you may pray it if you reach it in time. If you miss anything from it, you may complete it.” And the Prophet said, “Verily, when you are deliberately walking to prayer, you are in a state of prayer.”
q: Verily, when you are deliberately walking to prayer, you are in a state of prayer
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fasting: Making intention before days of obligatory fasting
t:
Hafsa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever does not have the intention to fast before dawn, there is no fasting for him.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “The meaning according to the people of knowledge is that the fast is invalid if intention is not made before sunrise in Ramadan, or for making up a Ramadan fast, or fasting for a vow. If one does not intend to do so in the night, it is not allowed. As for voluntary fasting, it is permissible to make an intention after morning; it is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq.”

title: Hadith on Fasting: Late intention when voluntarily fasting
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me one day, “O Aisha, do you have anything to eat?” She said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have nothing.” The Prophet said, “Then I am fasting.”

title: Hadith on Fasting: Waking up in major impurity before fasting
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would wake up at dawn in a state of major impurity, then he would perform a ritual bath and observe fasting.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Siyam: Sniff water deep in nose unless fasting
t:
Laqit ibn Sabrah reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell me about ablution.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Perform ablution well, clean the base of your fingers, and sniff water deep into your nose, unless you are fasting.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “The people of knowledge disapproved for a fasting person to sniff water deeply into the nose and they considered it as breaking his fast.”

title: Hadith on Siyam: The Prophet loved to fast Monday, Thursday
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The deeds are presented on Monday and Thursday. Thus, I love for my deeds to be presented while I am fasting.”

title: Hadith on Iftar: The Prophet breaks his fast with dates, water
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would break his fast before praying with fresh dates. If there were no fresh dates, then with dry dates. If there were no dry dates, then with some sips of water.

title: Hadith on Fasting: Time to break fast at sunset, Maghrib
t: Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you see the sun set and night has come from the east, it is time to break the fast.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fasting: When sun sets, time for Iftar
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the night approaches from the east and day retreats from the west and the sun has set, it is time to break the fast.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Iftar: Allah loves hastening to break fasting
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: The most beloved among My servants are those who are quickest to break their fast.”

title: Hadith on Siyam: The Prophet hastens to break his fast
t: Abu ‘Atiyyah reported: Masruq and I visited Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and he said, “O mother of the believers, there are two companions of Muhammad and neither of them hold back from doing good. One of them hastens to break his fast and to perform the evening prayer, while the other delays breaking his fast and performing the prayer.” Aisha asked, “Who is the one who breaks his fast and performs prayer?” He said, “It is Abdullah ibn Mas’ud.” Aisha said, “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to do so.”

title: Hadith on Fasting: Hastening to break the fast
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “People will continue in goodness as long as they hasten to break their fast.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Imams: Obey Muslim leaders unless they order sin
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is a duty upon a Muslim man to listen and obey authorities, whether he likes it or not, unless they command sinful disobedience. If they command sinful disobedience, then there is no listening or obedience to them.”
q: It is a duty upon a Muslim man to listen and obey authorities, whether he likes it or not, unless they command sinful disobedience. If they command sinful disobedience, then there is no listening or obedience to them.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Suhur: Angels bless those who eat pre-fasting meal
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The pre-fasting meal is a blessed meal, so do not abandon it even if you only take a sip of water. Verily, Allah and His angels send blessings upon those who take the pre-fasting meal.”

title: Hadith on Jihad: Believers wage Jihad against their souls
t: Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said during the final pilgrimage, “Have I not informed you? The believer is the one who is trusted with the lives and wealth of people. The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand people are safe. The one striving in jihad in the way of Allah is the one who strives against himself in obedience to Allah. The emigrant is one who emigrates away from sins and evil deeds.”
q: jihad …

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Laylat al-Qadr in last ten nights of Ramadan
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Search for the Night of Decree in the odd nights among the last ten nights of Ramadan.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Children: His daughters are a shield from Hellfire
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever has three daughters and he is patient with them, he provides food and drink for them, and he clothes them, they will be his shield from the Hellfire on the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Hadith on Women: Treat daughters, sisters well to enter Paradise
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is not one of you with three daughters or three sisters, or two daughters or two sisters, fearing Allah regarding them and treating them in the best manner, but that he will enter Paradise.”
q: There is not one
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Finish meal when you hear Fajr call to prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you hears the call to prayer while eating the pre-fasting meal and his vessel is in his hand, let him not put it down until he fulfills his needs from it.”
q: while eating the pre-fasting meal and

title: Hadith on Suhur: Prolonging pre-fasting meal before Fajr
t: Zayd ibn Thabit reported: We ate the pre-fasting meal with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and then we stood for prayer. It was asked, “How long was it between the two calls to prayer?” Zayd said, “It was time enough to recite fifty verses from the Quran.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fasting: Eat suhur until you see redness on the horizon
t:
Abu Talaq reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Eat and drink in the pre-fasting meal and let not the ascending light stop you. Eat and drink until you see redness on the horizon.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “The people of knowledge acted upon this tradition, that they would not forbid a fasting person from eating or drinking until the red dawn was present.”
q: the pre-fasting meal

title: Hadith on Gluttony: Those who overate will be hungriest in Hereafter
t: Salman reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the people who ate to their fill the most in this world will be the hungriest on the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Hadith on Food: Believers are moderate in eating, drinking
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The unbeliever eats with seven intestines, and the believer eats with one intestine.”
gf: Mutaffaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Suhoor: Do not neglect blessed pre-fasting meal
t: Abdullah ibn al-Harith reported: A man among the companions entered upon the Prophet while he was eating the pre-fasting meal. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, it is a blessing that Allah has given you, so do not abandon it.”

title: Hadith on Suhur: Eat the blessed pre-fasting meal
t: Al-Miqdam ibn Ma’dikarib reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must take the pre-fasting meal, for it is a blessed meal.”

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Come to the blessed pre-fasting meal
t: Al-‘Irbad ibn Sariyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, invited me to the pre-fasting meal during Ramadan and he said, “Onward to the blessed meal!”

title: Hadith on Suhur: Blessings in pre-fasting morning meal
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Take the pre-fasting meal, for surely there are blessings in the pre-fasting meal.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Vanity: Three sinners punished on Judgment Day
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are three to whom Allah will not speak on the Day of Resurrection: one who does not give anything in charity unless his generosity is praised, a hypocrite who sells goods upon a false oath, and one who trails his garment in pride.”

title: Hadith on Arrogance: Man exalts himself until he becomes a tyrant
t: Salamah ibn al-Akwa’ reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man continues to exalt himself until he is recorded among the tyrants. He will be punished as they are punished.”

title: Hadith on Vanity: Earth swallows a man impressed by himself
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “While a man was walking in a fine garment, with his hair groomed and impressed with himself, Allah caused the earth to swallow him up. He will be buried until the Day of Resurrection.”
q: While a man was walking in a fine garment, with his hair groomed and impressed with himself, Allah caused the earth to swallow him up. He will be buried until the Day of Resurrection.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sins: Allah will not purify three people
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are three people to whom Allah will not speak on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, nor will He look at them, and they will have an agonizing punishment: an old man who commits adultery, a king who lies, and an arrogant dependent.”

title: Hadith on Akhirah: People of Paradise are humble, Hellfire arrogant
t: Harithah ibn Wahb reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you about the inhabitants of Paradise? Every meek and humble person, but if they swore an oath by Allah, He would surely fulfill it. Shall I not tell you about the inhabitants of Hellfire? Everyone cruel, rude, and arrogant.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Sahaba on Janazah: Companions attend funeral of Christian woman
t:
Al-Sha’bi reported: Umm al-Harith bint Abi Rabi’ah died and she was a Christian woman. Her funeral was accompanied by the companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.

Sufyan al-Thawri said in some narrations, “It was commanded that they should walk in front of her.”

title: Umar on Jahiliyyah: Islam is undone if people do not know ignorance
t: Ibn Taymiyyah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, the bonds of Islam will undone, one by one, only if there arise people in Islam who never knew the time of ignorance.”

title: Hadith on Siyam: Every night people saved by fasting
