t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: My love is assured for those who love each other for My sake, who sit together for My sake, who visit each other for My sake, and who spend on each other for My sake.”
q: Allah Almighty said: My love is assured for those who love each other for My sake, who sit together for My sake, who visit each other for My sake, and who spend on each other for My sake.

title: Hadith on Love: Great reward for those who loved each other
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, those who loved each other will have chambers in Paradise that are seen as if they were rising stars in the east or west. It will be said: Who are these people? Thus it will be said: They are those who loved each other for the sake of Allah Almighty.”
gf: Rijal al-Sahih (narrators reliable) according to Al-Haythami

title: Hadith on Love: Allah’s love a right upon them
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: My love is a right upon those who love each other for My sake. My love is a right upon those who maintain relations for My sake. My love is a right upon those who visit each other for My sake. My love is a right upon those who spend on each other for My sake.”
q: Allah Almighty said:

title: Umar on Deen: We are only honored by Islam, nothing else
t: Tariq ibn Shihab reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, we were a disgraceful people and Allah honored us with Islam. If we seek honor from anything besides that with which Allah honored us, Allah will disgrace us.”

title: Umar on Relations: Believer is good to those who are evil to him
t: ‘Ikramah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The one who reconciles is not the one who maintains relations with those who are good to him, for that is merely reciprocation. Rather, the one who reconciles is one who maintains relations with those who cut him off.”

title: Hadith on Mercy: Never be deprived by a Lord who laughs
t: Abu Razin reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah laughs for the despair of His servant, for He will soon relieve him.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, does the Lord laugh?” The Prophet said, “Yes.” I said, “We will never be deprived of goodness by a Lord who laughs!”
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Suicide: Praying over a Muslim who kills himself
t:
Jabir ibn Samurah reported: A man killed himself and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not pray over him.

Al-Tirmidhi said, “The people of knowledge disagreed on this issue. Some of them said that the Muslims should perform funeral prayers over every person who prayed towards Mecca, including the one who killed himself. This is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri and Ishaq. Ahmad said that the Muslim leader does not perform funeral prayers the one who killed himself, but he is prayed over by others besides him.”

title: Hadith on Graves: Do not sit on graves, do not pray to them
t: Abu Marthad reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not sit upon the graves and do not pray towards them.”

title: Ibn Wahb on Fiqh: I would be led astray, if not for Imam Malik
t: Al-Dhahabi reported: Ibn Wahb, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Were it not for Malik and Al-Layth, I would have been ruined. I used to believe that everything narrated about the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, should be acted upon.”

title: Ibn Abi Layla on Arabs: Most of jurists were non-Arabs
t: Ibn Abi Layla reported: Eisa ibn Musa said to me, and he was a religious man who was severe in his tribalism on behalf of the Arabs, “Who is the jurist of Basra?” I said, “Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Sireen.” He said, “What are these two?” I said, “They are both freed slaves.” He said, “And who is the jurist of Mecca?” I said, “’Ata’ ibn Rabah, Mujahid, Sa’eed ibn Jubair, and Sulaiman ibn Yassar.” He said, “What are they?” I said, “Freed slaves.” He said, “And who are the jurists of Medina?” I said, “Zaid ibn Aslam, Muhammad ibn Al-Munkadar, and Nafi’ ibn Abi Junaih.” He said, “What are they?” I said, “Freed slaves.” The color of his face began to change and he said, “And who is the jurist of Quba?” I said, “Rabia Ar-Ra’i and Ibn Abi Az-Zinad.” He said, “What are they?” I said, “Among the freed slaves.” Then his face darkened and he said, “And who is the jurist of Yemen?” I said, “Tawus, his sons, and Ibn Munabbih.” He said, “What are they?” I said, “Among the freed slaves.” His veins began to bulge, he stood up from his seat, and he said, “And who is the jurist of Khorasan?” I said, “‘Ata’ ibn Abdullah Al-Khurasani.” He said, “What is this ‘Ata’?” I said, “A freed slave.” His face became more inflamed and darker until he calmed down, and he said, “And who is the jurist of Syria?” I said, “Makhul.” He said, “What is Makhul?” I said, “A freed slave.” He sighed heavily and he said, “And who is the jurist of Kufa?” By Allah, I would have said Al-Hakim ibn ‘Utbah and ‘Ammar ibn Abi Salman, but I feared evil from him. I said, “He is Ibrahim ibn An-Nakha’i and Ash-Sha’bi.” He said, “What are they?” I said, “They are both Arabs.” He said, “Allah is the greatest!” Then he finally settled down.

title: Hadith on Sodomy: The Prophet fears Muslims will follow people of Lot
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, what I fear most for my nation is the deed of the people of Lot.”

title: Hadith on Sodomy: Allah has cursed anal intercourse
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He has been cursed, who goes into his wife from her back side.”

title: Hadith on Hajj: Touch black stone, but it has no powers
t: ‘Abis ibn Rabi’ah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, came to the black stone and he kissed it. Umar said, “Verily, I know you are only a stone with no power to harm or benefit me. Were it not that I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, kiss you, I would not have kissed you.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salawat: Send blessings upon all the Prophets
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Send blessings upon the Prophets and Messengers of Allah. Verily, Allah has sent them just as he has sent me.”

title: Hadith on Resurrection: People raised barefoot, naked, uncircumcised
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people will be assembled barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, will the men and women look at each other?” The Prophet said, “The matter will be too serious for them to notice.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Gheerah: Allah prohibits obscenity, loves to be praised
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one has a greater sense of honor than Allah, so He has made obscenities unlawful in public and in private. And no one loves to be praised more than Allah.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hudud: Modified punishment if criminal is too weak
t: Sa’d ibn Ubadah reported: There was a man living among us who had a physical defect and, to our surprise, we saw him having intercourse with one of the servant girls. Sa’d referred his case to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Strike him with the whip one hundred times.” They said, “O Prophet of Allah, he is too weak for that. If you strike him one hundred times, he might die.” The Prophet said, “Then take a branch with one hundred twigs and strike him once.”

title: Umar on Zina: Man sentenced for illegal intercourse with captive
t: Harun ibn al-Asim reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, dispatched Khalid ibn al-Walid with the army. Khalid sent Dirar ibn al-Azwar along with a company of horsemen and they raided a district belonging to the tribe of Asad. They captured a woman who was a beautiful bride-to-be and she amazed Dirar. He asked his companions for her and they gave her to him, then he had intercourse with her. When he returned from the expedition, he regretted what he had done and he collapsed in dismay. It was referred to Khalid and told him what he had done. Khalid said, “Indeed, I have made her permissible and wholesome for you.” Dirar said, “No, not until you write to Umar.” Umar replied that he should be stoned to death, but he had passed away from natural causes by the time Umar’s letter arrived. Khalid said, “Allah did not want to disgrace Dirar ibn al-Azwar.”

title: Malik on Rape: Rapist must be punished, victim not punished
t:
Ibn Shihab reported: The Caliph Abdul Malik ibn Marwan judged that a woman who was raped must be paid her dowry by the one who raped her.

Malik said, “The issue among us concerning the man who rapes a woman, whether she is a virgin or not, is that he must pay her dowry if she is free. If she is a servant, he must pay what has been taken from her value. The legal punishment is applied to the rapist and there is no punishment for the woman who was raped in any case.”

title: Hadith on Prayer: Eating dinner before Maghrib prayer
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If dinner is presented close to the time of prayer, begin eating before you perform sunset prayer and do not need to rush away from your dinner.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Prayer: Perform your prayer as if it is your last
t: Abu Ayyub reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me and make it concise.” The Prophet said, “When you stand for your prayer, pray as if you are saying farewell. Do not say anything for which you must apologize, and give up any desire to acquire what people have.”

title: Hadith on Prayer: Repeat what is said by the caller to prayer
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you hear the call to prayer, say something similar to what the caller has said.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Best remembrance, best supplication
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best remembrance is to declare there is no God but Allah. The best supplication is to declare all praise is due to Allah.”

title: Hadith on Salvation: Guard your speech, weep for your sins
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what will save us?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Restrain your tongue, let your house be enough for you, and weep for your sins.”

title: Hadith on Warning: Adultery and usury widespread, punishment follows
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Adultery and usury do not become prevalent among people but that the punishment of Allah Almighty is justified against them.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Riba: Allah curses all involved in usury
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah has cursed the one who consumes usury, its client, its witness, and its recorder. Usury and adultery do not become widespread among people but that they will become vulnerable to the punishment of Allah Almighty.”
q: Allah has cursed the one who consumes usury, its client, its witness, and its recorder … Usury and adultery do not become widespread among people but that they will become vulnerable to the punishment of Allah Almighty

title: Hadith on Speech: Most sins committed by the tongue
t:
Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Most of the sins of the children of Adam are on their tongues.”

Ibn Mas’ud said, “O tongue! Speak goodness and be rewarded, or remain silent and be safe, lest you become regretful.”

title: Hadith on Jannah: Six good deeds to enter Paradise
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Guarantee for me six deeds and I will guarantee for you Paradise: Be truthful when you speak, keep your promises when you make them, fulfill the trust when you are trusted, guard your chastity, lower your gaze, and restrain your hands from harming others.”
q: from harming others.
gf: Sahih li ghayri (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Work: Best earnings are honest business, personal labor
t: Hani’ ibn Niyar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked, “What are the best earnings?” The Prophet said, “It is an honest sale or a man’s work with his hands.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Dua: Do not supplicate so loudly, Allah is Hearing
t: Abu Musa reported: We were with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, on a journey when the people began to exalt Allah loudly. The Prophet said, “O people, be gentle with yourselves! You are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent, rather you are calling upon the Hearing, the Seeing.” I was behind the Prophet and I said to myself, “There is no movement or might but with Allah.” The Prophet said, “O Abdullah ibn Qays, say, ‘There is no movement or might but with Allah,’ for it is one of the treasures of Paradise.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Quran: Read entire Quran once every month
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Read the Quran once in every month.” I said, “I have strength to do more.” The Prophet said, “Then read it in twenty nights.” I said, “I have strength to do more.” The Prophet said, “Then read it in seven nights, and do not do more than that.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Rahmah: Allah divided mercy into one hundred parts
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has one hundred mercies and He sent down a single part of them between the jinn, the humans, the animals, and the insects, by which they are compassionate and merciful to each other, such as the compassion of a beast for its offspring. Allah kept ninety-nine mercies by which He will show mercy to His servants on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Verily, Allah has one hundred mercies and He sent down a single part of them between the jinn, the humans, the animals, and the insects, by which they are compassionate and merciful to each other, such as the compassion of a beast for its offspring. Allah kept ninety-nine mercies by which He will show mercy to His servants on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Fasting: Wives need permission from husband to voluntarily fast
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A woman should not fast in the presence of her husband except with his permission.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Marriage: Wives encouraged to treat husbands well
t: Al-Husayn ibn Mihsan reported: His aunt came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, with a need and when she finished explaining her need, the Prophet said to her, “Do you have a husband?” She said yes. The Prophet said, “How are you with him?” She said, “I do not neglect him unless I am unable.” The Prophet said, “Look to yourself regarding him. Verily, he is your Paradise or your Hellfire.”
q: Look to

title: Hadith on Manners: Closest to the Prophet have best character
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most beloved and nearest to my gathering on the Day of Resurrection are those of you with the best character. Verily, the most reprehensible of you to me and the furthest from my gathering on the Day of Resurrection will be the pompous, the braggarts, and the pretentious.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, we know the pompous and the braggarts, but who are the pretentious?” The Prophet said, “The arrogant.”

title: Hadith on Kindness: The Prophet did not want to hurt his feelings
t: Al-Sa’b ibn Jathamah reported: He presented the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, with a wild donkey as a gift when he was at Al-Abwa, or Waddan, and the Prophet returned it to him. When the Prophet saw the look of disappointment on his face, he said, “Indeed, we have only returned it because we are performing the pilgrimage right now.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Shukr: Most thankful to Allah are grateful to people
t: Usamah ibn Zayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most grateful of people to Allah are those who are most grateful to people.”

title: Hadith on Jihad: Best jihad to speak truth to oppressors
t: Tariq ibn Shihab reported: A man asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while he had his leg in the stirrup, “Which jihad is best?” The Prophet said, “A word of truth before a tyrannical ruler.”
q: A word of truth before a tyrannical ruler.

title: Hadith on Jihad: Most beloved jihad speaking justice to oppressors
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked, “Which jihad is most beloved to Allah?” The Prophet said, “A word of truth before a tyrannical leader.”

title: Hadith on Salat: How people steal from their own prayers
t: Abdullah ibn Mughafal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the worst thieves among people are those who steal from their prayers.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, how do they steal from their prayers?” The Prophet said, “They do not complete its bowing or prostration properly. The most miserly of people are those who are miserly with the greeting of peace.”
q: Verily, … t

title: Umar on Spying: Umar catches drinking party, lets them go
t: Abdur Rahman ibn Awf reported: He would patrol the city at night with Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and on one occasion they were walking when the lamp of a household caught their attention. They approached it until they heard loud voices inside the door. Umar grabbed the hand of Abdur Rahman and he said, “Do you know whose house this is?” He said no. Umar said, “This is the house of Rabi’ah ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and they are inside drinking wine right now! What do you think?” Abdur Rahman said, “Indeed, I think we have done what Allah has prohibited for us. Allah Almighty said, ‘Do not spy,’ (49:12) and we have spied on them.” Umar turned away and he left them alone.

title: Tusi on Jihad: True jihad is against one’s lowly desires
t: Al-Dhahabi reported: Abu Hamid al-Tusi, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Know that the religion has two conditions. The first is to abandon what has been forbidden. The other is to perform righteous acts of obedience. Abandoning what is forbidden is more difficult than being obedient. Everyone is capable of being obedient, but none are capable of abandoning lowly desires except the truthful. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The true emigrant is one who emigrates away from evil, and the one striving in jihad for the sake of Allah is he who strives against his desires.”

title: Hadith on Wages: Pay your workers in a timely manner
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Pay the worker his wages before his sweat has dried.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Khamr: Alcohol is the key to every evil
t: Abu Darda reported: My dear friend the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, instructed me, “Do not associate anything with Allah, even if you are slashed and burned. Do not leave the obligatory prayers on purpose, for whoever leaves them on purpose has forfeited the protection of Allah. Do not drink wine, for it is the key to every evil.”
q: Do not associate anything with Allah, even if you are slashed and burned. Do not leave the obligatory prayers on purpose, for whoever leaves them on purpose has forfeited the protection of Allah. Do not drink wine, for it is the key to every evil.

title: Hadith on Silence: Speak truth, or be silent and safe
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “May Allah have mercy on a man who spoke rightly and was rewarded, or who was silent and remained safe.”

title: Hadith on Wudu: None maintains ablution but a believer
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Remain upright, though you cannot encompass it entirely. Know that the best of your good deeds is prayer and that none can preserve his ablution but a believer.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Most helpless are those who cannot pray
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most helpless of people are those unable to supplicate. The most miserly of people are those who are miserly with the greeting of peace.”

title: Hadith on Mercy: None has faith until merciful to creation
t: Abu Musa al-Ashari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You will never have faith until you love each other. Shall I tell you what will make you love each other?” They said, “Of course, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “Spread peace between yourselves. By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you are merciful to others.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, all of us are merciful.” The Prophet said, “Verily, it is not only mercy between yourselves, but rather it is mercy for everyone.”

title: Hadith on Anger: Do not get angry, you will enter Paradise
t: Abu Darda reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell me about a deed that will admit me into Paradise.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not be angry and you will enter Paradise.”

title: Hadith on Signs: Wondrous signs to occur before the Hour
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, the Hour will not be established until predators speak to humans, until the tip of a man’s whip and the strap of his sandal speak, and his thigh informs him of what his family has done in his absence.”

title: Hadith on Trials: Reason will disappear before the Hour
t: Abu Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, before the Hour will be an upheaval.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is the upheaval?” The Prophet said, “Killing.” Some of the Muslims said, “O Messenger of Allah, right now we fight many idolaters every year.” The Prophet said, “It is not that you will fight the idolaters, but rather you will fight each other, until a man kills his neighbor, the son of his aunt, and his close relatives.” Some people said, “O Messenger of Allah, will we be reasonable on that day?” The Prophet said, “No, reason will be taken away from most people in that era, and insignificant people will remain who do not use their reason.”

title: Hadith on Gifts: Take gifts to keep or give away in charity
t: Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gave me a gift and I said, “Give it to someone poorer than me.” The Prophet said, “Take it and keep it or give it in charity. Whatever comes to you of this property, take it without extravagance or begging for it. Whatever does not come, let not your soul pursue it.” Salim said, “For this reason, Ibn Umar would not ask anyone for anything, nor would he reject anything given as a gift.”
q: Take it and keep it or give it in charity. Whatever comes to you of this property, take it without extravagance or begging for it. Whatever does not come, let not your soul pursue it.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on al-Firdaws: Ask Allah for the highest level of Paradise
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Paradise has one hundred levels, and between every two levels is a distance like that between the heavens and earth. Al-Firdaws is its highest level, from which four rivers of Paradise flow, and above is the Throne. When you ask from Allah, ask for Al-Firdaws.”

title: Hadith on Conscience: Leave sins that shake your soul
t: Abu Umamah reported: A man asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “What is faith?” The Prophet said, “If you are happy with your good deeds and saddened by your bad deeds, you are a believer.” The man said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is sin?” The Prophet said, “If something waivers in your soul, you should leave it.”

title: Hadith on Marriage: Marry the righteous or else there is corruption
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If someone proposes marriage to you whose religion and character satisfies you, then you should accept it. If you do not do so, there will be trials on the earth and the spread of corruption.”

title: Hadith on Praise: Thanking Allah for blessings better than receiving
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah does not bestow His bounties upon a servant and he says, ‘All praise is due to Allah,’ but that what he has given for praise is better than what he has taken of bounties.”

title: Hadith on Bounties: Allah loves to see traces of His blessings
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when Allah Almighty bestows bounties upon a servant, He loves to see the traces of His bounties upon him. He dislikes one who wallows in misery and pessimism. Allah hates the obstinate questioner, and He loves those who are modest, chaste, and sober.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Bounties: Allah loves to see His blessings on His servants
t: Zuhayr ibn Abi ‘Alqamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty loves to see the traces of blessings on his servant. He does not love one who wallows in misery and pessimism.”

title: Hadith on Charity: Best food to Allah is shared by most people
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most beloved food to Allah is that which is received by many hands.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Praising Allah gratefully before going to sleep
t: Ibn Umar reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would lie down on his side for sleep, he would say, “All praise is due to Allah, who has sufficed me, protected me, fed me, and given me drink, who has been favorable to me and who has given to me lavishly. All praise is due to Allah in every circumstance. O Allah, Lord of all things, their Sovereign, and God of all things, I seek refuge in You from the Hellfire.”

title: Hadith on Tahmid: The Prophet praises Allah in every situation
t: Aisha reported: If the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saw something he liked, he would say, “All praise is due to Allah, by whose favor good deeds are accomplished.” If the Prophet saw something he disliked, he would say, “All praise is due to Allah in every circumstance.”

title: Hadith on Dua: O Allah, teach me what will benefit me
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, benefit me with what you have taught me, teach me what will benefit me, and increase my knowledge. All praise is due to Allah in every circumstance, and I seek refuge in Allah from the condition of the people of the Hellfire.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplications for sneezing, responding to sneeze
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you sneezes, let him say: All praise is due to Allah in every circumstance. Those with him should say: May Allah have mercy upon you. He should respond to them by saying: May Allah guide you and amend your affairs.”

title: Hadith on Vows: The Prophet tells a woman to carry out her vows
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A woman came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and she said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have made a vow I will play the drum for you.” The Prophet said, “Fulfill your vow.” She said, “I have made a vow to sacrifice at a certain place where they slaughtered in the time of ignorance.” The Prophet said, “For an idol?” She said no. The Prophet said, “For an image?” She said no. The Prophet said, “Fulfill your vow.”

title: Hadith on Iman: Best of faith is to hate evil for others
t: Mu’adh ibn Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of faith is to love for the sake of Allah, to hate for the sake of Allah, and to work your tongue in the remembrance of Allah.” Mu’adh said, “How is it, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “That you love for people what you love for yourself, hate for them what you hate for yourself, and speak goodness or remain silent.”
gf: Sahih li ghayri (authentic due to external evidence) according to al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Gabriel fears Hellfire, hopes in Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Allah created Paradise and Hellfire, He sent Gabriel to Paradise saying: Behold it and what I have prepared therein for its people. Gabriel came and looked at it and what Allah had prepared therein for its people, then he returned to Allah and he said: By Your might, no one will hear of it but that he will enter it. Allah ordered that it be surrounded by adversity and He said: Return to it and behold what I have prepared therein for its people. Gabriel returned and found that it was surrounded by hardship, then he returned to Allah and he said: By Your might, I fear that no one will enter it. Allah said: Go to the Hellfire and behold it and what I have prepared therein for its people. Gabriel found that it was in layers, one above another, then he returned to Allah and he said: By Your might, no one who hears of it will enter it. Allah ordered that it be surrounded by desires and He said: Return to it. Gabriel returned and he said: By Your might, I fear that no one will escape it.”

title: Hadith on Haya: Be modest with Allah in mind, body, soul
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be modest before Allah, as is His right.” We said, “O Messenger of Allah, surely we have modesty, all praise is due to Allah!” The Prophet said, “It is not so. Rather, modesty before Allah, as is His right, is to guard the mind and what runs through it, to guard the stomach and what fills it, and to reflect upon death and trials. Whoever desires the Hereafter, let him abandon the embellishments of worldly life. Whoever does so has been modest before Allah, as is His right.”
q: It is not so

title: Hadith on Hudud: Better to mistake in forgiveness than punishment
t:
Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Avoid applying legal punishments against the Muslims if you are able. If the criminal has a way out, then leave him to his way. Verily, for the leader to err in pardoning is better than to err in punishing.”

Imam al-Tirmidhi commented, “It has likewise been narrated from more than one of the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that they said the same as this.”

title: Hadith on Kindness: No goodness without friendliness
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believer is friendly, for there is no goodness in one who is neither friendly nor befriended.”

title: Hadith on Hearts: If you want to soften your heart, be kind
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he complained about the hardness of his heart. The Prophet said, “If you want to soften your heart, feed the poor and pat the head of the orphan.”

title: Hadith on Kindness: Allah lets gentleness enter their home
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If Allah Almighty intends goodness for a household, He lets gentleness enter their home.”
q: If

title: Hadith on Trusts: Fulfill trusts, do not reciprocate betrayal
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Fulfill the trust of those to whom they are due, and do not be treacherous to the one who betrays you.”

title: Hadith on Virtues: Most beloved to Allah benefit people
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most beloved people to Allah are those who are most beneficial to people. The most beloved deed to Allah is to make a Muslim happy, or remove one of his troubles, or forgive his debt, or feed his hunger. That I walk with a brother regarding a need is more beloved to me than that I seclude myself in this mosque in Medina for a month. Whoever swallows his anger, then Allah will conceal his faults. Whoever suppresses his rage, even though he could fulfill his anger if he wished, then Allah will secure his heart on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever walks with his brother regarding a need until he secures it for him, then Allah Almighty will make his footing firm across the bridge on the day when the footings are shaken.”

title: Hadith on Dua: Fear supplications of oppressed, even unbelievers
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of the supplication of the oppressed, even if he is an unbeliever, for there is nothing to block it.”

title: Hadith on Character: Calm from Allah, haste from Satan
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Composure is from Allah, and rushing is from Satan.”
q: Composure

title: Ibn Kathir on God: Creation itself evidence for the Creator
t: Ibn Kathir reported: Some of the Arabs were asked, “What is the evidence for the existence of the Lord Almighty?” They said, “O, glory be to Allah! The camel’s dung testifies to the existence of the camel, and the track testifies to the fact that someone was walking. A sky that holds the stars, a land that has fairways and a sea that has waves? Does not all of this testify to the existence of the Subtle, Knowledgeable?”

title: Salman on Khilafah: Unjust leaders are kings, not Caliphs
t: Salman al-Farisi reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him, “Am I a king or a Caliph?” Salman said, “If you acquire as much as two coins from the lands of the Muslims, more or less, then you place it where it does not belong, you are a king and not a Caliph.” Umar wept when he heard this.

title: Hadith on Ramadan: May his face be dusted in humility
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “May he be humbled in whose presence I am mentioned, but he does not send blessings upon me. May he be humbled who enters the month of Ramadan, but it passes before he is forgiven. May he be humbled who lives to see his parents in their old age, but he does not enter Paradise.”

title: Hadith on Salawat: Blessing the Prophet on Friday
t: Aws ibn Aws reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the best of your days is Friday. Adam was created on it, he died on it, the Trumpet will be blown on it, and the Shout will be made on it. Thus, send blessings upon me often, for your blessings are presented to me.”

title: Hadith on Salawat: Nearest to Prophet blessed him most
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The closest of people to me on the Day of Resurrection are those who sent the most blessings upon me.”

title: Hadith on Salawat: Misers refuse to bless the Prophet
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The miser is one in whose presence I am mentioned, but he does not send blessings upon me.”

title: Hadith on Ziyarah: Greeting the Prophet at his grave
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None of you greets me with peace (at his grave) except Allah returns my spirit, that I may return his greeting of peace.”
q: N

title: Hadith on Mosques: Paradise for regular Masjid attendance
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever comes and goes between the mosque, Allah will prepare his place in Paradise every time he comes and goes.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Masjid: Reward for walking to prayer, waiting for Imam
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people with the greatest reward are those who walk the furthest, then the next furthest. Those who wait to pray with the Imam have a greater reward than those who pray alone and then sleep.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Songs: People of Medina sing, play drums for the Prophet
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by some of the girls of Medina and they were playing their drums and singing the words, “Muhammad is an excellent neighbor! We are neighbors from the tribe of Najjar!” The Prophet said, “Verily, Allah knows that you are dear to me.”

title: Hadith on Sahaba: Do not curse companions of the Prophet
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not insult my companions. If one of you were to spend the likes of mount Uhud in gold, it would not reach a small portion of theirs or even half of that.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Quran: How the Companions divided the Mushaf
t: Aws ibn Hudhayfah reported: I asked the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, how they divided the Quran. They said, “Three chapters, then five, then seven, then nine, then eleven, then thirteen, and then al-Mufassal as a single part.”

title: Ali on Khawarij: A word of truth by which they intend falsehood
t: ‘Ubaydullah ibn Abi Rafi’ reported: The Haruriyya (Khawarij) came out against Ali ibn Abi Talib and they said, “There is no rule but for Allah,” (12:40). Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “A word of truth by which is intended falsehood. Verily, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, described some people and I recognized their description in these people. They speak the truth with their words but it does not go beyond this,” and he pointed to this throat.

title: Hadith on Satire: Using poetry to defend Islam and the Prophet
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would set up a pulpit in the mosque for Hassan and he would stand on it and satirize in poetry whoever spoke against the Messenger of Allah. The Prophet said, “Verily, the holy spirit is with Hassan as long as he defends the Messenger of Allah.”

title: Hadith on Divorce: The Prophet protects wife from abusive husband
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The wife of Al-Walid ibn ‘Uqbah came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and she complained to him saying, “O Messenger of Allah! Al-Walid has beaten me!” The Prophet said, “Say to him: He has protected me.” She did not stay but for a while until she returned and she said, “He did not give me anything but more beatings!” The Prophet tore a piece of cloth from his shirt and he said, “Say to him: Verily, the Messenger of Allah has given me his protection.” She did not stay but for a while until she returned and she said, “He did not give me anything but more beatings!” The Prophet raised his hands and he said, “O Allah, you must deal with Al-Walid, for he has sinned against me twice.”

title: Hadith on Hearts: Four types of hearts in faith, unbelief, hypocrisy
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are four kinds of hearts: a polished heart as shiny as a radiant lamp, a sealed heart with a knot tied around it, a heart that is turned upside down, and a heart that is wrapped. As for the polished heart, it is the heart of the believer and its lamp is the light of faith. The sealed heart is the heart of the unbeliever. The heart that is turned upside down is the heart of a pure hypocrite, for he had knowledge but he denied it. As for the heart that is wrapped, it is the heart that contains both faith and hypocrisy. The parable of faith in this heart is the parable of the herb that is sustained by pure water, and the parable of the hypocrisy in it is the parable of an ulcer that thrives upon puss and blood; whichever of the two is greater will dominate.”

title: Hadith on Women: The Prophet enjoins good treatment of wives
t: ‘Amr ibn al-Ahwas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said during his farewell sermon, “Verily, I enjoin you to treat women well, for surely they are your dependents. You do not have any right to treat them otherwise, unless they commit clear obscenity. If they do so, you may forsake their beds and then ‘strike’ them without hurting them, but if they obey you, then you may not do so. You have rights over your wives, and they have rights over you. Among your rights over them is that they do not give their beds to anyone but you, and they do not let anyone you dislike enter your homes. Among their rights over you is that you treat them well, clothe them, and feed them.”
q: Verily, I

title: Hadith on Women: Fear Allah with women, marriage is a trust
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Fear Allah regarding women. Verily, you have taken them as a trust from Allah, and intercourse has been made lawful by the word of Allah. Your rights over them are that they do not let anyone in the house you dislike. If they do so,  you may strike them without violence. Their rights over you are that you provide for them and clothe them in a reasonable manner.”

title: Hadith on Talaq: The Prophet divorces husband who beat his wife
t: Yahya ibn Sa’id reported: Habibah bint Sahl was married to Thabit ibn Qays, and Thabit had struck her. When she woke up, she went to the door of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while it was not yet daylight. She said, “Thabit and I cannot be together.” Thabit came to the Prophet and the Prophet said to him, “Take what she owes you and let her go her way.” She said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have everything he has given me.” Thabit took it from her and she returned to settle with her family.
q: Take what she owes you and let her go her way

title: Hadith on Covenants: Civil protection of the Muslims is one
t:
Ali Ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The protection of the Muslims is one; they strive to fulfill it among the least of them. Whoever betrays a Muslim, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and the people altogether. His obligatory and voluntary good deeds will not be accepted.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “The lives of the believers are equal. They strive to fulfill the covenant of the least of them, and they give support against whoever opposes them.”

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Some people tested on Judgment Day
t: Al-Aswad ibn Sari’ reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are four kinds of people on the Day of Resurrection: a deaf man who cannot hear anything, a mad man, a senile man, and a man who died in the period before Islam. The deaf man will say: O Lord, Islam came and I could not hear anything. The mad man will say: O Lord, Islam came and the children threw filth at me. The senile man will say: O Lord, Islam came and I could not understand anything. The man who died before Islam will say: O Lord, there was no messenger from You who came to me. Allah will make them promise to obey Him. Then, He will command them to enter the fire. By the one in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if they enter the fire, it will become cool and peaceful.”

title: Hadith on Faith: Relations with the Prophet do not guarantee Paradise
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, where is my father?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He is in Hellfire.” When he turned away, the Prophet called to him and he said, “Verily, my father and your father are in Hellfire.”
q: He is in Hellfire

title: Ibn Umar on Sahaba: Faith of companions greater than mountains
t: Qatadah reported: It was asked of Ibm Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, “Did the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, laugh?” Ibn Umar said, “Yes, and the faith in their hearts was greater than the mountains.”

title: Ja’far on Excuses: Give your brother up to seventy excuses
t: Al-Bayhaqi reported: Ja’far ibn Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If you hear something from your brother that you reject, make an excuse for him up to seventy excuses. If you cannot do it, then say: Perhaps he has an excuse I do not know.”

title: Ibrahim on Jihad: Greater Jihad is struggle to purify the heart
t:
Ibn Rajab reported: Ibrahim ibn Abi ‘Alqamah, may Allah have mercy on him, said to his people when they returned from a military expedition, “You have come from the lesser jihad, but you have not performed the greater jihad.” They said, “What is the greater jihad?” Ibrahim said, “It is the jihad of the heart.”

Imam Ibn Rajab commented, “Courage is to be patient for a time. This is the jihad against outward enemies, which is jihad against unbelievers. Likewise is the jihad against inward enemies, which is the jihad against the ego and lowly desires. Indeed, this is the greater of the two jihads.”

title: Hadith on Mourning: Grieve for deceased three days, except husbands
t: Muhammad ibn Sirin reported: The son of Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah be pleased with her, passed away. On the third day, she called for yellow perfume and wiped it over he body, saying, “We have been prohibited from mourning for more than three days, except for our husbands.”

title: Hadith on Khawarij: Violent rebels recite Quran, but do not understand
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will come a people from the east, who recite the Quran but it does not go beyond their throats. They will go out of the religion, just as an arrow pierces through its target, and they will not return to it, just as the arrow does not return to the bow.” It was said, “What will be their sign?” The Prophet said, “Their sign is shaving.” Or he said, “It is shearing.”
q: Their sign … It is shearing

title: Hadith on Graves: Permission to visit graves as a reminder
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, visited the grave of his mother and he wept and made others around him start weeping. The Prophet said, “I asked my Lord for permission to seek forgiveness for her and He did not give me permission, then I asked my Lord for permission to visit her grave and He gave me permission, so visit the graveyards. Verily, it is a reminder of death.”

title: Hadith on Dunya: Worldly life is nearly worthless to Allah
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If the world were as worthy to Allah as the wing of a mosquito, an unbeliever would not even be given a sip of water.”
q: If the world were as worthy to Allah as the wing of a mosquito, an unbeliever would not even be given a sip of water.

title: Hadith on Wahy: Wisdom in gradual revelation of Quran
t: Yusuf ibn Mahak reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “Verily, the first verses to be revealed were from the shorter chapters at the end of the Quran. In them is mentioned Paradise and Hellfire, until people were firmly established upon Islam and verses of lawful and unlawful were revealed. If the first verse to be revealed was ‘do not drink wine,’ they would have said, ‘we will never stop drinking wine.’ And if the first verse to be revealed was ‘do not commit adultery,’ they would have said, ‘we will never stop committing adultery.'”

title: Hadith on Punishment: Allah punishes entire nation, resurrects them as individuals
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Allah intends to punish a people, the punishment afflicts everyone among them. Then, they are resurrected according to their deeds.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Trials: Disappearance of righteous a sign of the Hour
t: Mirdas al-Aslami reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Righteous people will be taken away, one after another, until only the dregs of society will remain like the sediment of barley or dates. Allah will have no esteem for them.”

title: Hadith on Violence: Sign of the Hour is fighting for wealth
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hour will not be established until the Euphrates river uncovers a mountain of gold and people will fight over it. Every ninety-nine people out of a hundred will be killed, and each man among them will say: Perhaps I will be the one who is saved!”

title: Hadith on Dajjal: False Messiah will not harm true believers
t: Al-Mughira ibn Shu’bah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about the False Messiah more than anything else. The Prophet said to me, “O my son, why are you worrying about him? He will not harm you.” I said, “The people will imagine he has flowing rivers and mountains of bread with him.” The Prophet said, “He is too insignificant to Allah to harm you with that.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dajjal: People flee False Messiah to the mountains
t: Umm Sharik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people will flee from the False Messiah into the mountains.” She said, “O Messenger of Allah, where will the Arabs be on that day?” The Prophet said, “They will be few.”

title: Hadith on Paradise: Best reward to look at the Face of Allah
t: Suhayb reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the people of Paradise enter it, Allah Almighty will say: Would you like anything more? They will say: Have You not brightened our faces? Have You not admitted us into Paradise and saved us from Hellfire? Then, Allah will lift the veil and nothing they are given will be more beloved to them than looking at their Lord Almighty.” The Prophet recited the verse, “For those who do good is the best and even more.” (10:26)
q: Then,

title: Hadith on Jannah: You will see your Lord like the full moon
t: Jarir ibn Abdullah reported: We were with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he looked at the full moon one night. The Prophet said, “Verily, you will see your Lord just as you see this moon. There will be no crowd to block your sight. Thus, if you can avoid missing prayer before the rising of the sun and its setting, then do so.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “Glorify your Lord with praises before the rising of the sun and its setting.” (50:39)
q: Verily, you will see your Lord just as you see this moon. There will be no crowd to block your sight. Thus, if you can avoid missing prayer before the rising of the sun and its setting, then do so … Glorify your Lord with praises before the rising of the sun and its setting
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jannah: Ultimate reward of gaining Allah’s pleasure
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah will say to the people of Paradise: O people of Paradise! They will say: We are at Your service, our Lord, all goodness is in Your hand! Allah will say: Are you satisfied? They will say: Why would we not be satisfied when You have given us what You have not given to any other creation? Allah will say: Shall I not give you something better than all of that? They will say: O Lord, what could be better than that? Allah will say: I will grant you My pleasure, such that I will never be displeased with you ever again.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authentic) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Paradise: Lowest in Paradise has all desires fulfilled
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the lowest in position among you in Paradise will have it said to him: Have whatever you desire. He will express his desires again and again. It will be said: Have your desires been satisfied? He will say yes. It will be said: For you is whatever you desire and more along with it.”

title: Hadith on Jannah: People of Paradise increase in beauty
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, there is a market in Paradise to which the people will come every Friday. The wind will scatter fragrance on their faces and clothes and will increase their excellence and beauty. They will return to their families after having been increased in excellence and beauty and they will say: By Allah, we have seen you increased in excellence and beauty! They will say them: By Allah, you as well have increased in excellence and beauty!”

title: Hadith on Paradise: Believers in Paradise admire those above them
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the people of Paradise will look upon the inhabitants of mansions above them, just as they look at a brilliant star on the horizon in the East or West, due to their favor over them.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, are these the dwellings of the prophets whom no one else can reach?” The Prophet said, “No. By the One in whose hand is my soul, they are men who had faith in Allah and believed in the messengers.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jannah: Wonders of the people of Paradise
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people of Paradise will eat and drink, but they will neither defecate, nor sneeze, nor urinate. Rather, their food will be digested, emitting a scent like musk. They will glorify and praise Allah as easily as you breathe.”

title: Hadith on Istighfar: The Prophet seeks forgiveness 100 times
t: Ibn Umar reported: We counted the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saying one hundred times in a single sitting before he stood up, “My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance. Verily, You alone are the Relenting, the Forgiving.”

title: Hadith on Istighfar: The Prophet anchors his mindfulness of Allah
t: Al-Aghar al-Muzani reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, there is fog over my heart at times, so I seek the forgiveness of Allah one hundred times in a day.”

title: Hadith on Guidance: Whoever institutes a good practice in Islam
t: Jarir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever institutes a good practice in Islam will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it without diminishing their rewards at all. Whoever institutes an evil practice in Islam will have its sin and the sin of those who act upon it without diminishing their sins at all.”

title: Ibn Umar on Rebels: Khawarij apply verses about unbelievers on Muslims
t: Al-Bukhari reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, considered the Khawarij rebels to be the worst of Allah’s creation and he said, “Indeed, they take verses that were revealed about unbelievers and use them against believers.”

title: Hadith on Sickness: Your illness is purification, if Allah wills
t: Ibn Abbas reported: If the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered the home of sick person to visit him, he would say, “It will not harm you. It is purification, if Allah wills.”
q: It will not harm you. It is purification, if Allah wills

title: Hadith on Sahaba: Ten companions promised Paradise
t: Abdur Rahman ibn ‘Awf reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Abu Bakr is in Paradise. Umar is in Paradise. Uthman is in Paradise. Ali is in Paradise. Talhah is in Paradise. Al-Zubayr is in Paradise. Abdur Rahman ibn ‘Awf is in Paradise. Sa’d is in Paradise. Sa’id is in Paradise. Abu ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah is in Paradise.”

title: Ali on Caliphs: Best companions are Abu Bakr and Umar
t: Abu Juhayfah reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Shall I not tell you about the best of this nation after its Prophet? It is Abu Bakr and Umar.”

title: Hadith on Caliphs: After the Prophet, follow Abu Bakr and Umar
t: Hudhayfah reported: We were sitting with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “I surely do not know how much longer I will remain with you. After me, follow these two,” and the Prophet pointed to Abu Bakr and Umar.

title: Hadith on Iman: No true faith until he believes in four things
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one has faith until he believes in four things: He testifies there is no God but Allah, and I am the Messenger of Allah sent with the truth, he believes in the resurrection after death, and he believes in divine providence.”

title: Hadith on Arguments: People led astray by bickering
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No people are led astray after being guided but that they indulged in arguments.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “They strike an example for you only to argue. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.” (43:58)

title: Hadith on Arguing: Previous nations were destroyed by arguments
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: He heard the shouting of two men disputing over a verse. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us and we could see the anger on his face, and he said, “Verily, those before you were ruined by their differences over the Book.”

title: Hadith on Tafsir: Beware deviants misusing unclear verses
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, recited the verse, “It is He who revealed the Book to you in which are decisive verses that are the foundation of the Book, while others are ambiguous. As for those in whose hearts is deviance, they follow what is ambiguous from it, seeking discord and its interpretation, but none knows its interpretation but Allah, and those grounded in knowledge say: We have faith in them, all of it is from our Lord. Yet none will take heed but those of understanding.” (3:7) Then, the Prophet said, “If you see those who seek the ambiguous verses in it, they are those whom Allah has named. Beware of them!”
q: It is He who revealed the Book to you in which are decisive verses that are the foundation of the Book, while others are ambiguous. As for those in whose hearts is deviance, they follow what is ambiguous from it, seeking discord and its interpretation, but none knows its interpretation but Allah, and those grounded in knowledge say: We have faith in them, all of it is from our Lord. Yet none will take heed but those of understanding.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Faith: There will always be righteous believers
t: Abu ‘Inabah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah will continue to cultivate in this religion those He uses to act in obedience to Him.”

title: Hadith on Sunnah: I have left you upon a clear path
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us while we were discussing our fear of poverty.  The Prophet said, “Is it poverty that you fear? By the One in whose hand is my soul, the world will come to you in such abundance that nothing else will deviate your hearts. By Allah, I have left you upon a clear path, the clarity of which is the same by night or day.”

title: Hadith on Shirk: Punishment of idolatrous image-makers
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the makers of these graven images will be tormented on the Day of Resurrection. It will be said to them: Bring to life what you have created!”

title: Hadith on Shirk: Folly of trying to rival Allah’s creation
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: Who is more unjust than one who considers his creation as My creation? Let him create the smallest ant, or let him create a grain of wheat or barely.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Faith: The Prophet calls Romans to a common word
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb told me that the Byzantine Roman king, Heraclius, called for his interpreter and then asked for the letter of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Heraclius read in it, “In the name of Allah, the Gracious, the Merciful. From Muhammad the servant of Allah and His Messenger to Heraclius: O people of the Book, let us come to a common word between us and you.” (3:64)
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Persecution: The Quraysh persecute the Prophet for preaching
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would present himself to people and he said, “Is there a man who can take me to his people? Verily, the Quraysh have prevented me from preaching the word of my Lord.”

title: Hadith on Ummah: The Prophet will be pleased with his nation
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, recited the saying of Allah Almighty about Abraham, upon him be peace, “My Lord, the idols have misled many people, so whoever follows me is part of me,” (14:36). And the words of Jesus, upon him be peace, “If You punish them,  they are Your servants, but if You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the Wise.” (5:117). Then the Prophet raised his hands and he said, “O Allah, my nation, my nation!” And the Prophet wept. Allah Almighty said, “O Gabriel, go to Muhammad – and your Lord is most knowing – and ask him why he is crying.” Gabriel came to him and he asked him and the Prophet told him about it, though Allah knows best. Allah said, “O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say: Verily, We will please you regarding your nation and We will not disappoint you.”

title: Hadith on Intercession: The Prophet delays his supplication for the Hereafter
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Every prophet has a supplication that is answered and has hastened his supplication. I will delay my supplication as intercession for my nation on the Day of Resurrection. It is granted, if Allah wills, to whoever dies in my nation not associating anything with Allah.”
q: Every prophet has a supplication that is answered and has hastened his supplication. I will delay my supplication as intercession for my nation on the Day of Resurrection … It is granted, if Allah wills, to whoever dies in my nation not associating anything with Allah

title: Hadith on Tawhid: The Prophet cannot protect his relatives from Allah
t: Aisha reported: When the verse was revealed, “Warn your tribe and nearest kindred,” (26:214), the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stood upon mount Safa and he said, “O Fatima, daughter of Muhammad! O Safiya, daughter of Abdul Muttalib! O sons of Abdul Muttalib! I have no power at all to protect you from Allah, but you may ask me for some of my property as you wish.”

title: Hadith on Hidayah: The Prophet’s beloved uncle dies an unbeliever
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to his uncle Abu Talib as he was dying, “Say there is no God but Allah, and I will testify for you on the Day of Resurrection.” Abu Talib said, “Were the Quraysh not to blame me and say only anxiety made him do that, I would delight your eyes.” Then, Allah revealed the verse, “Verily, you do not guide those you love, rather only Allah guides whom he wills.” (28:56)
q: Verily, you do not guide those you love, rather only Allah guides whom he wills

title: Hadith on Quran: Verses of the sealed testament of Muhammad
t: ‘Alqamah reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever would like to look at the testament upon which is the seal of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, let him recite these verses: Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden, that you not associate any partners with him, that you be good to your parents, that you not kill your children fearing poverty. We will provide for you and them, and that you not come near to debauchery outwardly or inwardly, that you not kill a soul Allah has made sacred except for a just cause; this he has instructed you that you will reason. That you not come near to the property of an orphan unless to improve it until he reaches maturity, that you give full measure and weight in fairness. We do not hold a soul responsible except for what is within its capacity, that you be just when you testify, even against a relative, that you fulfill the covenant of Allah; this he has instructed you that you may be reminded. This is my straight path; follow it and do not follow other ways, lest you be diverted from his way; this he has instructed you that you may be righteous.” (6:151-153)
q: Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden, that you not associate any partners with him, that you be good to your parents, that you not kill your children fearing poverty. We will provide for you and them, and that you not come near to debauchery outwardly or inwardly, that you not kill a soul Allah has made sacred except for a just cause; this he has instructed you that you will reason. That you not come near to the property of an orphan unless to improve it until he reaches maturity, that you give full measure and weight in fairness. We do not hold a soul responsible except for what is within its capacity, that you be just when you testify, even against a relative, that you fulfill the covenant of Allah; this he has instructed you that you may be reminded. This is my straight path; follow it and do not follow other ways, lest you be diverted from his way; this he has instructed you that you may be righteous.

title: Hadith on Virtue: Allah commands justice, excellence, charity
t: ‘Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Gabriel, upon him be peace, has come and commanded me to put this verse in this place, in this chapter: Verily, Allah has commanded justice and excellence and giving to relatives, and He has prohibited debauchery, sin, and aggression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will remember.” (16:90)

title: Hadith on Religion: Fate of Jews, Christians, non-Muslims before Islam
t: Salman al-Farisi reported: I asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, about the people of religion who had been with me, mentioning their prayers and acts of worship. Then, Allah revealed the verse, “Verily, those who have faith, those who are Jewish, Christian, or Sabians, whoever believed in Allah and the Last Day and worked righteousness will have their reward with their Lord and they will not fear nor grieve.” (2:62)

title: Hadith on Mercy: Turn my curses into their blessings
t: Salman al-Farisi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If I scold a man among my nation, or I curse him in my anger, then know that I am only a son of Adam. I get angry as they do. Verily, I was only sent as a mercy to the worlds, so I ask Allah to turn them into blessings on the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Hadith on Aisha: Companions go to Aisha for answers
t: Abu Musa reported: We never had a problem occur to us, the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, but that we would ask Aisha and find that she knew something about it.

title: Hadith on Women: Greatness of Maryam, Asiyah, and Aisha
t: Abu Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There were many men who achieved perfection, but none were perfect among women except Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh, and Mary, the daughter of ‘Imran. Verily, the virtue of Aisha over other women is like the virtue of a fine stew over all other foods.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Talha on Aisha: None were more eloquent than Aisha
t: Abdul Malik ibn ‘Umayr reported: Musa ibn Talha said, “I have not seen anyone more eloquent than Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her.”

title: Hadith on Greetings: Responding to peace greetings or insults
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when the Jews greet you, they say death be upon you, so say: And upon you.”

title: Hadith on Ahruf: Nations were destroyed by differing over the Book
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: A man was reciting a verse which I had heard differently from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. I took his hand and brought him to the Prophet and he said, “Both of your recitations are good. Do not differ, for the nations before you were destroyed by their differences.”

title: Hadith on Prophets: Do not say a prophet is better than another
t:
Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not make the prophets better than one another.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “Do not say that anyone is better than Jonah son of Mata, upon him be peace.”
q: Do not say that anyone is better than Jonah son of Mata, upon him be peace
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ahruf: Quran has been revealed in seven dialects
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: I heard Hisham ibn Hakim reciting the Surat al-Furqan in a way different from how I recited it and how it was taught to me by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. I was about to argue with him, but then I waited until he finished and I tied his shirt around his neck and took him to the Prophet. I said, “Indeed, I heard this man recite in a way different from what you taught me!” The Prophet said to me, “Bring him to me.” Then, Prophet said to him, “Recite.” He recited and the Prophet said, “As it has been revealed.” Then, the Prophet said to me, “Recite.” I recited and the Prophet said, “As it has been revealed. Verily, the Quran has been revealed in seven dialects. Recite whichever of them you find easy.”
q: Recite
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Aisha: The Prophet is told Aisha is his wife in Hereafter
t: Aisha reported: Gabriel came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, with her image on a green, silken cloth and he said, “Verily, this is your wife in this world and in the Hereafter.”

title: Hadith on Trials: Be like Habil who refused to kill his brother
t: Khalid ibn ‘Urfutah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “O Khalid, after me there will be affairs, civil wars, and conflicts. If you can be like the servant of Allah, Abel, who was killed but did not kill, then do so.”

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: Servants nearest to Allah pray at night
t: ‘Amr ibn ‘Abasah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The closest the servant is to the Lord is during the last depth of the night. If you can be among those who remember Allah in this moment, then do so.”

title: Hadith on Sins: Believers punished with afflictions in this life
t: Abu Zuhair reported: He said, “O Messenger of Allah, will we be recompensed for every evil thing we did?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “May Allah have mercy on you, O Abu Bakr. Are you not afflicted by harm? Are you not struck by grief? Do you not endure illness? This is how you are recompensed.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Ahl Kitab: Righteous among People of the Book
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, delayed the evening prayer, then he later came out to the mosque to find people waiting for prayer. The Prophet said, “Are there none among the people of these religions remembering Allah at this hour besides you?” Then, Allah revealed the verse, “Yet they are not all alike: there are some among the People of the Book who are upright, who recite Allah’s revelations throughout the night, prostrating in prayer. They believe in Allah and the Last Day, encourage good and forbid evil, and race with one another in doing good. They are truly among the righteous. They will never be denied the reward for any good they have done. And Allah has knowledge of those mindful of Him.” (3:113-115)
q: Yet they are not all alike: there are some among the People of the Book who are upright, who recite Allah’s revelations throughout the night, prostrating in prayer. They believe in Allah and the Last Day, encourage good and forbid evil, and race with one another in doing good. They are truly among the righteous. They will never be denied the reward for any good they have done. And Allah has knowledge of those mindful of Him.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Gifts: Giving gifts to non-Muslim family
t: Ibn Umar reported: Umar saw a silken cloak for sale and he requested that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, buy it to wear on Fridays and days he receives delegations. The Prophet said, “Verily, this is a garment worn by those with no share in the Hereafter.” Later, the Prophet received some silken cloaks similar to those and he sent one to Umar. Umar said to the Prophet, “How can I wear it considering what you said?” The Prophet said, “I have surely not given it to you to wear, but rather to sell or give to someone else.” Umar sent it to his brother among the people of Mecca before he had accepted Islam.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on War: Deceiving enemy troops during war
t: Ka’b ibn Malik reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, intended to set out on a military expedition, he would pretend to go somewhere else. The Prophet would say, “War is deception.”

title: Hadith on Jihad: The Prophet fights to protect Islam
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say there is no God but Allah. If they say there is no God but Allah, then they will be granted protection from me for their lives and property, except by right of justice, and their reckoning is with Allah.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “Verily, you are only a reminder. You are not over them as a dictator.” (88:22)
q: I have been commanded to fight the people until they say there is no God but Allah. If they say there is no God but Allah, then they will be granted protection from me for their lives and property, except by right of justice, and their reckoning is with Allah

title: Hadith on Madinah: The Prophet’s city of Medina is sacred ground
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Medina is sacred from the mountain unto the end. Whoever innovates a heresy in it or aids a heretic, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and the people altogether. His obligatory and surplus good deeds will not be accepted. The protection of the Muslims is one. Whoever betrays a Muslim, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and the people altogether. His obligatory and surplus good deeds will not be accepted.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Bathing: Husband and wife bathing together
t:
Maymunah, wife of the Prophet, reported: I would take a bath with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, cleaning ourselves of impurities from the same vessel.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “It is the opinion of the majority of jurists, that there is no harm for a husband and wife to bathe from the same vessel.”

title: Suyuti on Fiqh: Five principles of the school of Al-Shafi’i
t: Al-Suyuti reported: The judge Abu Sa’id responded comprehensively in regard to a question about the school of Al-Shafi’i with four rules (qawa’id); first, certainty does not remove doubt. The basis of this is the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “Verily, Satan comes to one of you while he is in prayer and he says to him: you have lost your ablution; so do let him not leave unless he hears a sound or finds an odor.” Second, hardship leads to ease, and the basis of this is the saying of the Almighty, “We have not placed upon you hardship in religion,” (22:78) and the saying of the Prophet, “I was sent with the upright, lenient religion.” Third, harm should be removed, and the basis of this is the saying of the Prophet, “There is no harming, nor harming others.” Fourth, customs are a basis of judgment, because of the saying of the Prophet, “What the Muslims view as good is regarded by Allah as good.” Thus, he ended his letter. Other scholars said that these four rules are the pillars of juristic understanding (al-fiqh) and the entirety of doctrine, and some of them added to it a fifth rule, which is that matters are according to their objectives (al-maqasid), because of the saying of the Prophet, “Deeds are according to intentions,” and he said, “Islam is built upon five pillars,” and likewise jurisprudence is based upon five rules.
