q: Verily, Satan comes to one of you while he is in prayer and he says to him: you have lost your ablution; so do let him not leave unless he hears a sound or finds an odor. … We have not placed upon you hardship in religion … I was sent with the upright, lenient religion … There is no harming, nor harming others … Deeds are according to intentions

title: Hadith on Sunnah: I have left you with the Book, the Sunnah
t: Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have left you with two matters which will never lead you astray, as long as you hold to them: the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of his Prophet.”
gf: Sahih (authentic) according to Ibn Abdul Barr

title: Hadith on Muhammad: Whoever says this about the Prophet is a liar
t: Masruq reported: I asked Aisha, “O mother, did Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, see his Lord?” Aisha said, “What you said makes my hair stand on end! Know that if someone tells you one of three things, he is a liar. Whoever tells you that Muhammad saw his Lord is a liar.” Then, she recited the verse, “No vision can grasp Him, but His grasp is over all vision, for He is the Subtle, the Aware,” (6:103) and, “It is not for a man that Allah speak to him but by inspiration, or from behind a veil,” (42:51). Aisha said, “Whoever tells you that the Prophet knows what will happen tomorrow is a liar.” Then, she recited the verse, “No soul can know what it will earn tomorrow,” (31:34). Aisha said, “Whoever tells you that the Prophet concealed the revelation is a liar.” Then, she recited the verse, “O Messenger, proclaim the message which has been sent to you from your Lord,” (5:67). Aisha said, “But the Prophet did see Gabriel twice in his natural form.”

title: Hadith on Hasad: Jealousy destroys deeds, charity expiates sins
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Envy consumes good deeds just as fire burns wood. Charity extinguishes sinful deeds just as water extinguishes fire. Prayer is the light of the believer and fasting is his shield from the Hellfire.”

title: Hadith on Riba: Time coming when everyone affected by usury
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A time will surely come upon people in which none will remain but that he consumes usury. If he does not consume it, he will be afflicted by its dust.”
q: A time will surely come upon people in which none will remain but that he consumes usury. If he does not consume it, he will be afflicted by its dust.

title: Hadith on Sects: Only followers of Sunnah and Sahaba enter Paradise
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “What comes over my nation will surely be what came over the children of Israel, step by step, such that if one of them fornicated with his mother, someone from my nation would do the same. Verily, the children of Israel split into seventy-two sects, and my nation will split into seventy-three sects. All of them are in the Hellfire except for one denomination.” They said, “Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Those upon my way and the way of my companions.”
q: What comes over my nation will surely be what came over the children of Israel, step by step, such that if one of them fornicated with his mother, someone from my nation would do the same. Verily, the children of Israel split into seventy-two sects, and my nation will split into seventy-three sects. All of them are in the Hellfire except for one denomination.

title: Hadith on Ummah: Only the Jama’ah will go to Paradise
t: ‘Afw ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Jews split into seventy-one sects, one of them is in Paradise and seventy are in the Hellfire. The Christians split into seventy-two sects, seventy-one are in the Hellfire and one of them is in Paradise. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, my nation will split into seventy-three sects, one of them is in Paradise and seventy-two are in the Hellfire.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, who are the ones in Paradise?” The Prophet said, “The united community.”
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Islam: This religion is vast, so embrace it with gentleness
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, this religion is firmly solid, so come into it gently.”

title: Ibn Mas’ud on ‘Urf: Good customs to Muslims are good to Allah
t: Zirr ibn Hubaysh reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, Allah looked at the hearts of the servants, and He found that the heart of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, was the best among them, so He chose him for Himself and He sent him with His message. Then, He looked at the hearts of His servants after Muhammad, and He found that the hearts of his companions were the best among them. Thus, He made them into the ministers of His Prophet, fighting for the sake of His religion. Whatever the Muslims view as good is good to Allah, and whatever they view as evil is evil to Allah.”

title: Hadith on Ramadan: The Prophet prays eleven raka’at at night, plus two
t: Abu Salama reported: I came to Aisha and I said, “O mother, tell me about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.” Aisha said, “His night prayer during the month of Ramadan and at other times consisted of thirteen cycles, including two before the dawn prayer.”

title: Malik on Fiqh: Imam Malik does not force his school on Muslims
t: Ibn ‘Abdul Barr reported: Imam Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy upon him, said: When the Caliph Abu Ja’far al-Mansur performed the pilgrimage, he called for me, so I entered upon him and he spoke to me, asking me questions, and I replied. Then, he said, “I am determined to have several copies made of these books of yours. I will send a copy to every region in the lands of the Muslims. I will command them to adhere to its contents without referring to any other, and they will set aside everything but this new knowledge. Indeed, I see the foundation of knowledge in the narrations of the people of Medina and their teachings.” I said, “O Commander of the Faithful, do not do so, for the people have received sayings, heard reports, and transmitted various accounts. Each one holds to what it has received and acts according to it. They practice as such due to people’s differences, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah and others. Turning them away from their beliefs would surely be difficult, so leave the people with what they are upon and what every country has chosen for themselves.” Al-Mansur said, “I swear on my life, if you had obeyed me in this matter, I would have commanded it.”

title: Hadith on Marriage: The Prophet has fun with his wives
t: Aisha reported: She was with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while on a journey. Aisha said, “I raced him on foot and I outran him, but when I gained some weight, I raced him again and he outran me. The Prophet said: This is for that race.”
q: This is for that race

title: Hadith on Humility: The Prophet disliked his companions to stand for him
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: There was no person more beloved to the companions than the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. When they saw him coming, they would not stand up because they knew he disliked that.

title: Hadith on Haram: Unlawful earnings a sign of the Hour
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “An era will surely come to people in which a man will not care from where he acquires his wealth, either lawfully or unlawfully.”
q: An era will surely come to people in which a man will not care from where he acquires his wealth, either lawfully or unlawfully.

title: Hadith on Women: Never hate the believing sisters in Islam
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A believing man does not despise a believing woman. If he finds something in her character he dislikes, he will be pleased by something else.”
q: A believing man does not despise a believing woman. If he finds something in her character he dislikes, he will be pleased by something else.

title: Hadith on Qira’at: Abu Musa given beautiful voice for recitation
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him, “O Abu Musa, you have been given a voice for recitation from the instruments of the house of David.”
q: O Abu Musa, you have been given a voice for recitation from the instruments of the house of David.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Charity: The Prophet gives everything he has each night
t:
Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The house of Muhammad has not reached evening with a share of dates or grain.”

In another narration, Anas said, “The Prophet would not store anything for tomorrow.”
q: The house of Muhammad has not reached evening with a share of dates or grain

title: Hadith on Beatings: The Prophet never hit women, servants, animals
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, never struck anything with his hand, neither a woman nor a servant, unless he was fighting in the way of Allah.

title: Hadith on Patience: The Prophet will not repay evil with evil
t: Abu ‘Abdillah al-Khadali reported: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. Aisha said, “The Prophet was not indecent, nor obscene, nor would he shout in the markets. He would not respond to an evil deed with an evil deed, but rather he would forgive and overlook.”

title: Umar on Women: Samra bint Nahik takes charge of market
t: Yahya ibn Abi Sulaym reported: I saw Samra’ bint Nahik, who had met the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. She was wearing a thick corset and veil, and she had a whip in her hand with which she disciplined people, enjoining good and forbidding evil.

title: Hadith on Animals: Forbidden to use living animals as targets
t:
Sa’id ibn Jubayr reported: I was with Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, when we passed by a group who had tied down a chicken and they were using it as a target. When they saw Ibn Umar, they fled and left it behind. Ibn Umar said, “Who has done this? The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, has cursed whoever has done this.”

In another narration, Ibn Umar said, “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, has cursed whoever takes something with a soul as his target.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on War: The Prophet forbids plundering, mutilation
t: Abdullah ibn Yazid Reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited plundering and mutilation.

title: Hadith on Mutilation: The Prophet forbids mutilation, encourages charity
t: Al-Hayyaj ibn ‘Imran reported: A servant boy of ‘Imran had ran away and he vowed to Allah that if he caught him, he would cut off his hand. Then, he sent me to ask about that, so I came to Samurah ibn Jundab and I asked him. Samurah said, “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, encouraged us to give in charity and he forbade us from mutilation.” Then, I went to ‘Imran ibn Husayn and I asked him. ‘Imran said, “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, encouraged us to give in charity and he forbade us from mutilation.”

title: Hadith on Anfal: No reward for one who fights only for spoils
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, a man intends to fight for the sake of Allah, and he is seeking worldly gains.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no reward for him.” The people found that very difficult, so they said, “Return to the Messenger of Allah, for perhaps he did not understand you.” The man returned, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, a man intends to fight for the sake of Allah, and he is seeking worldly gain.” The Messenger of Allah said, “There is no reward for him.” Then he returned a third time and the Messenger of Allah said, “There is no reward for him.”
q: There is no reward for him … There is no reward for him … There is no reward for him.

title: Hadith on Bloodshed: Believers are most hesitant to kill
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most hesitant of people in killing are the people of faith.”
q: The most hesitant of people in killing are the people of faith

title: Hadith on Slaves: The Prophet orders good treatment of slaves
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, enjoined good treatment of slaves and he would say, “Feed them from the same food you eat, clothe them from the same clothes you wear, and do not torture the creation of Allah Almighty.”
q: Feed them from the same food you eat, clothe them from the same clothes you wear, and do not torture the creation of Allah Almighty

title: Ammar on Slaves: Allah retaliates for slaves unjustly abused
t: Maymun ibn Abi Shabib reported: ‘Ammar ibn Yasir, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “None of you strikes his slave unjustly but that the slave will be granted retaliation on the Day of Resurrection.”

title: Hadith on Freedom: Expiation for beating slaves is emancipation
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever strikes his young slave sharply without right, or punches him, the expiation for the sin is to emancipate him.”
q: Whoever strikes his young slave sharply without right, or punches him, the expiation for the sin is to emancipate him

title: Hadith on Animals: Forbidden to mutilate, torture animals
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited beating or cauterizing animals on the face.

title: Hadith on Freedom: Slave boy who was beaten is set free
t: Abu Mas’ud reported: I was beating a servant-boy of mine when I heard a voice from behind me, “Know, O Abu Mas’ud, that Allah has more power over you than you have over him.” I turned around and it was the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. I said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have freed him for the sake of Allah.” The Prophet said, “If you had not done so, you would have been burnt in the Hellfire.”
q: Know, O Abu Mas’ud, that Allah has more power over you than you have over him … If you had not done so, you would have been burnt in the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Freedom: Treat your slaves well, and free them
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came from Khaybar with two young boys. The Prophet gave one of them to Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he said, “Do not beat him. I have prohibited hitting the people of prayer, and I saw him praying.” The Prophet gave the other boy to Abu Dharr, and he said, “I enjoin you to treat him well.” Later, the Prophet said, “O Abu Dharr, what have you done with the boy I gave to you?” Abu Dharr said, “You enjoined me to treat him well, so I have freed him.”
q: Do not beat him. I have prohibited hitting the people of prayer, and I saw him praying … I enjoin you to treat him well. … O Abu Dharr, what have you done with the boy I gave to you

title: Hadith on Children: Parents led by their deceased children into Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no Muslim couple whose three children die before reaching maturity but that Allah will admit them into Paradise by His mercy. It will be said to them: Enter Paradise! They will say: Let our parents come along!” The Prophet said three times, “They will say likewise until it is said to them: Enter Paradise, you and your parents!”
q: There is no Muslim couple whose three children die before reaching maturity but that Allah will admit them into Paradise by His mercy. It will be said to them: Enter Paradise! They will say: Let our parents come along … They will say likewise until it is said to them: Enter Paradise, you and your parents!

title: Hadith on Children: Their children are playing in Paradise
t: Abu Hassan reported: I said to Abu Huraira, “I have two sons who died. Can you tell us something from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, to cheer up our souls after their death?” Abu Huraira said, “Yes, the Prophet said: Their young are roaming about in Paradise.”
q: Their young are roaming about in Paradise

title: Hadith on Rukhsa: Why not take the Prophet’s concession?
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, performed an action in which was a concession. News of that reached some of the companions, as if they did not like it or approve it. The Prophet was told about this, so he stood to address the people. The Prophet said, “What is wrong with men who heard from me about a matter in which I made a concession, yet they disliked it and disapproved of it? By Allah, I surely know more about Allah than them and I fear Allah more than them.”
q: What is wrong with men who heard from me about a matter in which I made a concession, yet they disliked it and disapproved of it? By Allah, I surely know more about Allah than them and I fear Allah more than them.

title: Hadith on Scandal: Calumny to corrupt people’s relationships
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do you know what calumny is?” They said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Prophet said, “It is spreading news between people to ruin their relationships.”
q: Do you know what calumny is? … It is spreading news between people to ruin their relationships.

title: Hadith on Hajj: Speak kind words, feed poor in pilgrimage
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The righteous Hajj pilgrimage has no reward but Paradise.” Jabir said, “What is its righteousness?” The Prophet said, “To feed the poor and speak kind words.”
q: The righteous Hajj pilgrimage has no reward but Paradise. … To feed the poor and speak kind words
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Qadr: Every Muslim can divert evil by supplication
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no Muslim on earth who calls upon Allah in supplication but that Allah will grant it to him or divert some evil away from him, so long as he does not ask for something sinful or to cut off family ties.” A man said, “In that case we will ask for more.” The Prophet said, “Allah has even more.”
q: There is no Muslim on earth who calls upon Allah in supplication but that Allah will grant it to him or divert some evil away from him, so long as he does not ask for something sinful or to cut off family ties … Allah has even more

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication repels the divine decree
t: Salman reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Nothing repels the divine decree but supplication, and nothing increases life span but righteousness.”
q: Nothing repels the divine decree but supplication, and nothing increases life span but righteousness

title: Hadith on Qadr: The Prophet forbids arguing about providence
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to us while we were arguing about the divine decree. Then, the Prophet became angry until his face was red, as if a pomegranate were bursting from his cheeks. The Prophet said, “With this I have commanded you? With this I was sent to you? Verily, the people before you were destroyed when they argued over this matter. I am determined for you not to argue over it.”
q: With this I have commanded you? With this I was sent to you? … Verily, the people before you were destroyed when they argued over this matter. I am determined for you not to argue over it

title: Hadith on Whims: Hearts are like feathers blown in the wind
t: Abu Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the heart is that of a feather blown about by the wind of the desert.”
q: The parable of the heart is that of a feather blown about by the wind of the desert.

title: Hadith on Qadr: Righteousness increases life span, repels evil fate
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The span of life is not increased but by righteousness, and the divine decree is not repelled but by supplication. Verily, a man is deprived of provision due to the sins he commits.”
q: The span of life is not increased but by righteousness, and the divine decree is not repelled but by supplication. Verily, a man is deprived of provision due to the sins he commits.

title: Hadith on Yusuf: The nobleman, son of the noblemen
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The nobleman, son of the nobleman, son of the nobleman, son of the nobleman. That was Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, upon them be peace.”
q: The nobleman, son of the nobleman, son of the nobleman, son of the nobleman. That was Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, upon them be peace

title: Hadith on Sins: Allah curses theft, idolatry, cruelty, obscenity
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah has cursed the one who falsely changes the boundaries of the land. Allah has cursed the one who offers a sacrifice for another besides Allah. Allah has cursed the one who curses his parents. Allah has cursed the servant who attributes himself to another master. Allah has cursed the one who pushes a blind person from the path. Allah has cursed the one who commits bestiality, and Allah has cursed one who behaves like the people of Lot,” and he said it three times.
q: Allah has cursed the one who falsely changes the boundaries of the land. Allah has cursed the one who offers a sacrifice for another besides Allah. Allah has cursed the one who curses his parents. Allah has cursed the servant who attributes himself to another master. Allah has cursed the one who pushes a blind person from the path. Allah has cursed the one who commits bestiality, and Allah has cursed one who behaves like the people of Lot,

title: Hadith on Patience: The Prophet does not harm those who insult him
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A Jewish man passed by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Death be upon you!” The Prophet replied, “And upon you.” The Prophet then said to his companions, “Do you know what he said? He said: Death be upon you.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, shall we kill him? The Prophet said, “No, but when the people of the Book greet you, then say: And upon you.”
q: And upon you … Do you know what he said? He said: Death be upon you … No, but when the people of the Book greet you, then say: And upon you

title: Hadith on Trials: The Hour preceded by great slaughter
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hour will not be established until two groups fight each other. There will be a massive slaughter between them, although their claim is one and the same. The Hour will not be established until close to thirty lying impostors appear, each one imagining that he is the messenger of Allah.”
q: The Hour will not be established until two groups fight each other. There will be a massive slaughter between them, although their claim is one and the same. The Hour will not be established until close to thirty lying impostors appear, each one imagining that he is the messenger of Allah.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Muhammad: Martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah
t: Abu al-Ahwas reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “For me to swear by Allah nine times that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had been killed is more beloved to me than swearing once that he was not, for Allah Almighty appointed him as Prophet and took him as a martyr.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Honor: Best in honor are best in character
t: Yazid ibn al-‘Asim reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “What do you consider nobility? Allah has made clear the most noble to Allah is the most righteous. What do you consider honor? The best in honor are those among you with the best character.”

title: Hadith on Gifts: Spread the love by giving to others
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Give each other gifts and you will love each other.”
q: Give each other gifts and you will love each other.

title: Abu Huraira on Hypocrisy: You ignore the plank in your own eye?
t: Yazid ibn al-Asim reported: Abu Huraira, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “One of you looks at the speck in his brother’s eye while he ignores the plank or log in his own eye.”

title: Hadith on Yemen: Faith is Yemeni, peace among sheep
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Faith is from Yemen and unbelief is from the east. Tranquility is found among people who tend to sheep. Pride and showing off are found among the uncivil owners of horses and camels.”
q: Faith is from Yemen and unbelief is from the east. Tranquility is found among people who tend to sheep. Pride and showing off are found among the uncivil owners of horses and camels.

title: Hadith on Alliances: Just pacts before Islam are affirmed
t: Amr ibn Shuaib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is party to a just pact during the time of ignorance, then Islam does not increase it but in strength.”
q: Whoever is party to a just pact during the time of ignorance, then Islam does not increase it but in strength … .

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Paradise is Allah’s mercy, Hellfire is His punishment
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hellfire and Paradise disputed each other. Hellfire said: The arrogant and the tyrants will dwell in me. Paradise said: What is the matter with me that only the meek and humble of the people will enter me? Allah said to Paradise: You are My mercy with which I show mercy to those of My servants whom I will. Allah said to Hellfire: You are My punishment with which I punish those of My servants whom I will, and both of you will be full. As for Hellfire, it will not be filled until Allah puts His foot over it and Hellfire will say: Enough! Enough! All of its parts will be filled together and Allah will not wrong any of His creatures. As for Paradise, Allah will create a new creation with which to fill it.”
q: The Hellfire and Paradise disputed each other. Hellfire said: The arrogant and the tyrants will dwell in me. Paradise said: What is the matter with me that only the meek and humble of the people will enter me? Allah said to Paradise: You are My mercy with which I show mercy to those of My servants whom I will. Allah said to Hellfire: You are My punishment with which I punish those of My servants whom I will, and both of you will be full. As for Hellfire, it will not be filled until Allah puts His foot over it and Hellfire will say: Enough! Enough! All of its parts will be filled together and Allah will not wrong any of His creatures. As for Paradise, Allah will create a new creation with which to fill it
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Takabbur: Arrogant meet Allah while He is displeased
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever exalts himself or carries himself with arrogance, he will meet Allah while He is angry.”
q: Whoever exalts himself or carries himself with arrogance, he will meet Allah while He is angry

title: Hadith on Love: Better person has stronger love for others
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No two persons love each other for the sake of Allah but that the better of the two is the one with the strongest love for his companion.”
q: No two persons love each other for the sake of Allah but that the better of the two is the one with the strongest love for his companion

title: Hadith on Chores: The Prophet humblys serve himself
t: Aisha reported: I was asked, “What did the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, do in his home?” I said, “The Prophet was a man among men. He would remove fleas from his clothes, milk his sheep, and serve himself.”

title: Hadith on Trees: Finish planting trees, even if Last Day established
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Even if the Resurrection were established upon one of you while he has in his hand a sapling, let him plant it.”
q: Even if the Resurrection were established upon one of you while he has in his hand a sapling, let him plant it

title: Hadith on Gentleness: You must be kind, even to animals
t: Aisha reported: I was on a camel that was misbehaving, so I started to beat it. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “You must be gentle. Verily, gentleness is not in anything but that it beautifies it, and it is not removed from anything but that it disgraces it.”
q: You must be gentle. Verily, gentleness is not in anything but that it beautifies it, and it is not removed from anything but that it disgraces it

title: Hadith on Ruh: Souls of people are like troops collected
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The souls are troops collected together. They come close upon what they recognize, and they differ upon what they reject.”
q: The souls are troops collected together. They come close upon what they recognize, and they differ upon what they reject.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Prophets: Ali is to Muhammad as Aaron to Moses
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, set out to Tabuk and he left Ali behind. Ali said, “You leave me behind with the women and children?” The Prophet said, “Are you not pleased in the same position for me as Aaron was to Moses? But there is no prophet after me.”
q: Are you not pleased in the same position for me as Aaron was to Moses? But there is no prophet after me.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fath: Liberation of Mecca is a day of mercy
t: Ibn Asakir reported: When Sa’d passed by Abu Sufyan with the banner of the Prophet on the day Mecca was liberated, he announced, “O Abu Sufyan! Today is a day of slaughter! Today the unlawful will be lawful! Today Allah will disgrace the Quraish!” So the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Abu Sufyan, today is a day of mercy. Today Allah will honor the Quraish.”
q: O Abu Sufyan, today is a day of mercy. Today Allah will honor the Quraish

title: Hadith on Tazkiyyah: Purify your heart from malice and deceit
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “Young man, if you are able every morning and evening to remove any malevolence in your heart towards anyone, then do so.” Then, the Prophet said to me, “Young man, that is my Sunnah. Whoever revives my Sunnah has loved me, and whoever loves me will be with me in Paradise.”
q: Young man, if you are able every morning and evening to remove any malevolence in your heart towards anyone, then do so … Young man, that is my Sunnah … Whoever revives my Sunnah has loved me, and whoever loves me will be with me in Paradise

title: Hadith on Jihad: Charity work is jihad in the way of Allah
t: Rafi’ ibn Khadij reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One who works for charity in a just cause is like one who campaigns in the way of Allah until he returns home.”
q: One who works for charity in a just cause is like one who campaigns in the way of Allah until he returns home

title: Hadith on Tawakkul: Trust in Allah, but tie your camel
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, should I tie my camel and trust in Allah, or should I leave her untied and trust in Allah?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Tie her and trust in Allah.”
q: Tie her and trust in Allah.

title: Hadith on Arafat: The Prophet’s farewell sermon at Arafat
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said during his farewell sermon, “Which month do you know has the greatest sanctity?” They said, “No doubt, this month of ours, Dhul Hijjah.” The Prophet said, “Which city do you know has the greatest sanctity?” They said, “No doubt, this city of ours, Mecca.” The Prophet said, “Which day do you know has the greatest sanctity?” They said, “No doubt, this day of ours, Arafat.” The Prophet said, “Verily, Allah Almighty has sanctified your lives, your wealth, and your honor, except by right of justice, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this city of yours, in this month of yours. Have I not delivered the message?” The Prophet said all of that three times and they said, “No doubt, yes.” The Prophet said, “Be warned! Do not turn back to unbelief after me by striking the necks of each other.”
q: Which month do you know has the greatest sanctity … Which city do you know has the greatest sanctity … Which day do you know has the greatest sanctity … Verily, Allah Almighty has sanctified your lives, your wealth, and your honor, except by right of justice, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this city of yours, in this month of yours. Have I not delivered the message? … Be warned! D … o not turn back to unbelief after me by striking the necks of each other

title: Hadith on Evil: Most hated are criminals, heretics, killers
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most hated of people to Allah are three persons: a person who deviates into the unlawful, a person who seeks for the traditions of ignorance to remain in Islam, and a person who seeks to shed the blood of another without a just cause.”
q: The most hated of people to Allah are three persons: a person who deviates into the unlawful, a person who seeks for the traditions of ignorance to remain in Islam, and a person who seeks to shed the blood of another without a just cause

title: Hadith on Hudud: Do not curse him, do not help Satan
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man was brought to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, for drinking wine. The Prophet said, “Strike him.” Some of us struck him with our hands, others with their shoes, and others with their shirts twisted into a lash. When we finished, someone said to him, “May Allah disgrace you!” The Prophet said, “Do not speak like this. Do not help Satan against him.”
q: Strike him … Do not speak like this. Do not help Satan against him

title: Hadith on Drunkards: Do not curse him, he loves Allah
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: In the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, there was a man named Abdullah who was nicknamed ‘Donkey,’ and he would make the Prophet laugh. The Prophet lashed him for drinking wine, and one day the man was brought again and the Prophet ordered him to be lashed. Another man among the people said, “O Allah, curse him! How many times has he been brought?” The Prophet said, “Do not curse him. By Allah, I know that he loves Allah and His Messenger.”
q: Do not curse him. By Allah, I know that he loves Allah and His Messenger.

title: Hadith on Apostasy: Allah accepts an apostate’s repentance
t: Ibn Abbas reported: A man among the Ansar embraced Islam and then he became an apostate and joined the idolaters, but he regretted it later. He sent word to his people, saying, “Ask the Messenger of Allah if there is any repentance for me.” His people came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and they said, “He has regretted what he has done, and he wants us to ask you if there is any repentance for him.” Thus, Allah revealed, “How shall Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their faith,” up to His words, “Except for those who repent after that and correct themselves. Verily, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.” (3:86-89) They sent for him and he embraced Islam.
q: How shall Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their faith, … Except for those who repent after that and correct themselves. Verily, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

title: Hadith on Riddah: The Prophet pardons an apostate traitor
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Abdullah ibn Sa’d ibn Abi Sarh would write for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, but the devil deceived him and he joined the unbelievers. The Prophet ordered that he should be killed on the day of liberation, but Uthman ibn Affan sought protection for him. Thus, the Prophet granted him protection.

title: Hadith on Signs: Many women, few men a sign of the Hour
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A time will come to people when a man will go around with gold to give in charity, but he will find no one to accept it, and a single man will be seen followed by forty women seeking refuge with him, due to the scarcity of men and abundance of women.”
q: A time will come to people when a man will go around with gold to give in charity, but he will find no one to accept it, and a single man will be seen followed by forty women seeking refuge with him, due to the scarcity of men and abundance of women.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Every joint has charity due, even a good word
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Charity is due upon every joint of the people for every day upon which the sun rises. Justly reconciling two people is charity. Helping a man with his animal and lifting his luggage upon it is charity. A kind word is charity. Every step that you take towards the mosque is charity, and removing harmful things from the road is charity.”
q: Charity is due upon every joint of the people for every day upon which the sun rises. Justly reconciling two people is charity. Helping a man with his animal and lifting his luggage upon it is charity. A kind word is charity. Every step that you take towards the mosque is charity, and removing harmful things from the road is charity.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Animals: Allah rebukes a prophet for killing ants
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “An ant bit one of the Prophets, so he ordered that the colony of ants be burned. Allah revealed to him: One ant has bitten you, so you destroy one of the nations that praise Allah?”
q: An ant bit one of the Prophets, so he ordered that the colony of ants be burned. Allah revealed to him: One ant has bitten you, so you destroy one of the nations that praise Allah?
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Rulers: Allah treats leaders as they treat their subjects
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, whoever is given charge over my nation and he is harsh with them, be harsh with him. Whoever is given charge over my nation and he is gentle with them, be gentle with him.”
q: O Allah, whoever is given charge over my nation and he is harsh with them, be harsh with him. Whoever is given charge over my nation and he is gentle with them, be gentle with him.

title: Hadith on Muhammad: The Prophet was forbearing, forgiving
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was not presented with two matters but that he would choose the easier of them, as long as it was not sinful. If it was sinful, he would be the furthest of people from it. The Prophet did not take revenge for wrongs against himself, unless the sacred limits of Allah were violated, for then he would retaliate for the sake of Allah.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Kindness: Every polite, easy-going believer in Paradise
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you of one forbidden for Hellfire or Hellfire is forbidden for him? It is everyone accessible, polite, and easy-going.”
q: Shall I not tell you of one forbidden for Hellfire or Hellfire is forbidden for him? It is everyone accessible, polite, and easy-going
gf: Sahih li gharyihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Allah loves forbearance, clemency
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Al-Ashajj ‘Abdul Qays, “Verily, you have two qualities beloved to Allah: forbearance and clemency.”
q: Verily, you have two qualities beloved to Allah: forbearance and clemency.

title: Hadith on Muhammad: The Prophet’s enemies in fear and awe
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have been supported against the enemy by dread, and I have been given concise, meaningful words. While I was sleeping, the keys of the treasures of the earth were brought to me and placed in my hand.”
q: I have been supported against the enemy by dread, and I have been given concise, meaningful words. … While I was sleeping, the keys of the treasures of the earth were brought to me and placed in my hand
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Marriage: Men who hit their wives not the best
t: Iyas ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not strike the maidens of Allah,” but Umar came to the Prophet and he said, “Women have become emboldened toward their husbands.” The Prophet gave them a concession to strike them lightly. Then, many women came to the family of the Prophet and complained about their husbands. The Prophet said, “Many women have come to the family of Muhammad complaining about their husbands. These men are not the best among you.”
q: Do not strike the maidens of Allah … Many women have come to the family of Muhammad complaining about their husbands. T … hese men are not the best among you

title: Hadith on Salah: Avoiding distractions in prayer
t: Aisha reported: Things that disrupt the prayer were mentioned in her presence, saying, “A dog, a donkey, and a woman disrupt the prayer.” Aisha said, “You have turned us into dogs! I have seen the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, praying while I was between him and the direction of prayer, lying on the bed. If I needed something, I disliked to face him directly, then I would slip away quietly.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Superstition: No omens in women, houses, or animals
t: Abu Hassan al-A’raj reported: Two men entered the home of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and they said, “Abu Huraira narrates that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Verily, omens are in women, animals, and houses.” Aisha became upset and she said, “By the one who revealed the Quran to Abu al-Qasim, it is not like that. The Prophet was saying: The people of ignorance used to say omens are in women, houses, and animals.” Then, she recited the verse, “No affliction occurs in the earth or within yourselves except that it is written in a book.” (57:22)
q: The people of ignorance used to say omens are in women, houses, and animals … No affliction occurs in the earth or within yourselves except that it is written in a book.

title: Hadith on Gender: Men and women complementary to each other
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, women are the counterparts of men.”
q: Verily, women are the counterparts of men.

title: Hadith on Prayer: Straighten rows, lest it cause discord
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Straighten the rows of prayer or else Allah will surely disfigure your faces.”
q: Straighten the rows of prayer or else Allah will surely disfigure your faces.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Women: A dutiful wife enters Paradise by any gate
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a woman prays her five prayers, fasts her month of Ramadan, guards her chastity, and obeys her husband, she will enter Paradise from any gate she wishes.”
q: If a woman prays her five prayers, fasts her month of Ramadan, guards her chastity, and obeys her husband, she will enter Paradise from any gate she wishes.

title: Hadith on Pride: The Prophet rebukes Hafsa for insulting Safiyyah
t: Anas reported: Safiyyah heard that Hafsa called her “the daughter of a Jew,” so Safiyyah started crying. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered while she was crying and he said, “What makes you cry?” Safiyyah said, “Hafsa called me the daughter of a Jew.” The Prophet said, “Verily, you are the daughter of a prophet, your uncle is a prophet, and you are married to a prophet, so how can she boast over you?” Then, the Prophet said, “Fear Allah, O Hafsa!”
q: What makes you cry? … Verily, you are the daughter of a prophet, your uncle is a prophet, and you are married to a prophet, so how can she boast over you? … Fear Allah, O Hafsa

title: Hadith on Names: Use names of prophets, not war or bitterness
t: Abu Wahb al-Jushami reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Name yourselves with the names of the prophets. The most beloved names to Allah are Abdullah, the servant of Allah, and Abdur Rahman, the servant of the Merciful. The most truthful of them is Harith, the harvester of good, and Hamam, the brave one. The worst names are names of war and bitterness.”
q: Name yourselves with the names of the prophets. The most beloved names to Allah are Abdullah, the servant of Allah, and Abdur Rahman, the servant of the Merciful. The most truthful of them is Harith, the harvester of good, and Hamam, the brave one. The worst names are names of war and bitterness.
gf: Hasan (fair) according to Ibn Abdul Barr

title: Hadith on Shaytan: Do not respond to insults like the Devil
t: ‘Iyad ibn Himar reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who insults me in a gathering beneath me, so I reciprocate him. Is there any blame on me?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two people who insult each other are like two devils accusing and denouncing each other.”
q: Two people who insult each other are like two devils accusing and denouncing each other.

title: Hadith on Life: Whoever is healthy, safe, faithful has everything
t: ‘Ubaydullah ibn Mihsan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever among you wakes up secure in his property, healthy in his body, and he has his food for the day, it is as if he were given the entire world.”
q: Whoever among you wakes up secure in his property, healthy in his body, and he has his food for the day, it is as if he were given the entire world.

title: Hadith on Character: Four qualities to transcend worldly life
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you have these four qualities, you will not worry about what you missed in the world: fulfilling the trust, truthful speech, good character, and restraint with food.”
q: If you have these four qualities, you will not worry about what you missed in the world: fulfilling the trust, truthful speech, good character, and restraint with food.

title: Hadith on Faith: Most beloved religion is natural monotheism
t: Ibn Abbas reported:  It was said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “Which religion is the most beloved to Allah?” The Prophet said, “Pure, magnanimous theism.”
q: Pure, magnanimous theism
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: True believer cannot be miserly, have bad character
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two qualities are never combined in a believer: miserliness and bad character.”
q: Two qualities are never combined in a believer: miserliness and bad character.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Hasad: Faith and envy never coexist in heart
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Faith and envy are not combined within a believing servant.”
q: Faith and envy are not combined within a believing servant.

title: Hadith on Generosity: None more generous than Aisha and Asma
t: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr reported: I have not seen anyone more generous than Aisha and Asma’, though their generosity was different. Aisha would gather things and after they had been collected, she would share them. As for Asma’, should would not leave anything for tomorrow.

title: Hadith on Muhammad: The Prophet is gentle to a demanding bedouin
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was merciful. No one came to him in need but that he would promise him and follow through if he could. The prayer was commenced and a bedouin came, taking hold of the Prophet’s shirt and saying, “I still have needs!” The man had frightened the Prophet’s wives but the Prophet went with him until his need was met, then he returned and prayed.

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: The Prophet’s beloved have best character
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I tell you about the most beloved to me and the closest to my assembly on the Day of Resurrection? Those with the best character.”
q: Shall I tell you about the most beloved to me and the closest to my assembly on the Day of Resurrection? … Those with the best character

title: Hadith on Hidayah: Guiding to good rewarded like one who acted
t: Abu Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever guides someone to goodness will have a reward like one who did it.”
q: Whoever guides someone to goodness will have a reward like one who did it.

title: Ibn Mas’ud on Takfir: Dangerous to call someone an enemy of Allah
t: Qays reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “If a man declares his companion to be his enemy, then he has rebelled against Islam or his companion is innocent.”

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: The Prophet is sent to teach good character
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I have only been sent to perfect righteous character.”
q: Verily, I have only been sent to perfect righteous character.

title: Hadith on Salawat: Dedicating supplications to bless the Prophet
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, I send blessings upon you often. How many of my prayers should be for blessings upon you?” The Prophet said, “As you wish.” I said, “A fourth?” The Prophet said, “As you wish, but more is better for you.” I said, “A half?” The Prophet said, “As you wish, but more is better for you.” I said, “Two-thirds?” The Prophet said, “As you wish, but more is better for you.” I said, “Should I say all of my prayers for blessings upon you?” The Prophet said, “If so, your worries will be resolved, and your sins will be forgiven.”

title: Hadith on Independence: Companions pledge not to ask from anyone
t: ‘Awf ibn Malik reported: We were with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while there were seven, or eight, or nine of us. The Prophet said, “Will you not give your pledge to the Messenger of Allah?” We had recently given our pledge, so we said, “We have given you our pledge of allegiance,” but the Prophet said it again three times. We offered our hands and pledged allegiance to him again. Someone said, “O Messenger of Allah, we have already given you our pledge, so what are we pledging to now?” The Prophet said, “That you worship Allah and do not associate any partners with him, that you pray for five prayers, that you listen and obey,” and then the Prophet said something very softly, “And that you do not ask people for anything.” Indeed, some of those people obeyed this to the extent that if his whip were to fall from his mount, he would not ask anyone to hand it to him.
q: Will you not give your pledge to the Messenger of Allah? … That you worship Allah and do not associate any partners with him, that you pray for five prayers, that you listen and obey … And that you do not ask people for anything

title: Hadith on Fitrah: Humans born to worship, but Satan leads astray
t: ‘Iyad ibn Himar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, my Lord has commanded me to teach you what you do not know, from what he has taught me this day, ‘All wealth I bestowed upon them is lawful. I have created all of My servants inclined to worship, but devils come to them who turn them away from their religion. They outlaw what has been made lawful for them, and they command them to associate partners with Me for which no authority has been revealed.’ Verily, Allah looked at the people of the earth and He detested all of them, Arabs and foreigners alike, except for remnants of the people of the Book.”
q: Verily, my Lord has commanded me to teach you what you do not know, from what he has taught me this day, ‘All wealth I bestowed upon them is lawful. I have created all of My servants inclined to worship, but devils come to them who turn them away from their religion. They outlaw what has been made lawful for them, and they command them to associate partners with Me for which no authority has been revealed.’ Verily, Allah looked at the people of the earth and He detested all of them, Arabs and foreigners alike, except for remnants of the people of the Book

title: Hadith on Iman: No true faith until he loves others as himself
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The servant does not attain the reality of faith until he loves for people what he loves for himself of goodness.”
q: The servant does not attain the reality of faith until he loves for people what he loves for himself of goodness

title: Hadith on Faith: Treat people how you love to be treated
t: Abu al-Muntafiq reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me what will save me from the punishment of Allah and admit me into Paradise.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, establish the prescribed prayers, give the obligatory charity, perform the Hajj and Umrah pilgrimages, and fast the month of Ramadan. Look at the way you would love people to treat you and do so to them, and whatever you would hate for them to do to you, spare them of it.”
q: Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, establish the prescribed prayers, give the obligatory charity, perform the Hajj and Umrah pilgrimages … and f … ast the month of Ramadan. Look at the way you would love people to treat you and do so to them, and whatever you would hate for them to do to you, spare them of it.

title: Hadith on Hatred: Beware spiritual diseases of hate, envy
t: Al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Lurking towards you are the diseases of the nations before you. Envy and hatred are the razor. I do not say they shave hair, but rather they shave the religion. By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you have faith, and you will not have faith until you love each other. Shall I tell you what can establish that for you? Spread peace between yourselves.”
q: Lurking … towards you are … the diseases of the nations before you. Envy and hatred are the razor. I do not say they shave hair, but rather they shave the religion. … By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you have faith, and you will not have faith until you love each other. … Shall I tell you what can establish that for you? Spread peace between yourselves.

title: Hadith on Fasting: Sins erased by fasting ‘Arafat, ‘Ashura
t: Abu Qatadah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about fasting the day of ‘Arafat, and he said, “It will expiate the sins of the previous and upcoming years.” Then, the Prophet was asked about fasting the day of ‘Ashura, and he said, “It will expiate the sins of the past year.”
q: It will expiate the sins of the previous and upcoming years. … It will expiate the sins of the past year

title: Hadith on Arafat: Allah saves them from Hell at ‘Arafah
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no day upon which Allah frees more of His servants from the Hellfire than the day of Arafat. He draws near and then He boasts of them to the angels, saying: What do these servants want?”
q: There is no day upon which Allah frees more of His servants from the Hellfire than the day of Arafat. He draws near and then He boasts of them to the angels, saying: What do these servants want?

title: Abu Darda on Relaxing: Enjoy entertainment to renew strength for worship
t: Al-Ghazali reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Indeed, I will relax myself with something entertaining, to help me continue upon the truth.”

title: Ibn Sirin on Fun: Companions would have fun, sing poetry
t: Qurrah ibn Khalid reported: I asked Muhammad ibn Sirin, may Allah have mercy on him, “Did the companions have fun?” Ibn Sirin said, “They were not but people. Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, would have fun and compose songs of poetry.”

title: Hadith on Songs: The Prophet allows singers at weddings
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Aisha gave away one of her relatives in marriage to a man among the Ansar. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came and he said, “Did you send them a girl?” They said yes. The Prophet said, “Did you send someone to sing with her?” She said no. The Prophet said, “Verily, the Ansar are a people who love poetry, so you should send someone along with her to say: Here we come, to you we come, greet us as we greet you.”
q: Did you send them a girl … Did you send someone to sing with her … Verily, the Ansar are a people who love poetry, so you should send someone along with her to say: Here we come, to you we come, greet us as we greet you.

title: Hadith on Entertainment: The Prophet entertains Ansar for a wedding
t: Aisha reported: She prepared a lady for marriage to a man among the Ansar. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Aisha, do you have any entertainment? Verily, the Ansar are fond of entertainment.”
q: O Aisha, do you have any entertainment? Verily, the Ansar are fond of entertainment

title: Hadith on Unseen: The Prophet does not know the future
t: Al-Rubayyi’ bint Mu’awwidh reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to me after performing our marriage and he sat on my bed. Some young girls were playing the drums and singing in lamentation of my father, who had been killed at the battle of Badr. Then, one of the girls said, “There is a prophet among us who knows what will happen tomorrow.” The Prophet said, “Do not say this, but continue saying what you had said before.”
q: Do not say this, but continue saying what you had said before

title: Hadith on Forbearance: Be good to those who are evil to you
t: Mu’adh ibn Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of virtues is that you maintain relations with one who cuts you off, that you give to one who deprives you, and that you forgive one who insults you.”
q: The best of virtues is that you maintain relations with one who cuts you off, that you give to one who deprives you, and that you forgive one who insults you.

title: Hadith on Leniency: Let the Jews know Islam is tolerant
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, placed my chin on his shoulder so I could watch the Abyssinians dancing until I felt tired and turned away. The Prophet said on that day, “Let the Jews know there is room in our religion. Verily, I have been sent with a pure, tolerant way.”
q: Let the Jews know … there is room in our religion. Verily, I have been sent with a pure, tolerant way

title: Hadith on Khamr: Muslims drink alcohol, calling it other names
t: Abu Malik al-Ashari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Some people from my nation will drink wine, calling it by different names, and musical instruments will be played for them, and girls will sing to them. Allah will cause the earth to swallow them up, and He will turn some of them into apes and pigs.”
q: Some people from my nation will drink wine, calling it by different names, and musical instruments will be played for them, and girls will sing to them. Allah will cause the earth to swallow them up, and He will turn some of them into apes and pigs

title: Hadith on Shi’r: Poetry is used for good or evil
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Poetry is in the same position as speech. The beautiful among it is like beautiful words, and the ugly among it is like ugly words.”
q: Poetry is in the same position as speech. The beautiful among it is like beautiful words, and the ugly among it is like ugly words.

title: Hadith on Satire: Worst liar attacks entire tribe in poetry
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the greatest liar among people is a man who insults another man by satirizing the entire tribe, and a man who disowns his father and accuses his mother of adultery.”
q: Verily, the greatest liar among people is a man who insults another man by satirizing the entire tribe, and a man who disowns his father and accuses his mother of adultery

title: Hadith on Independence: Paradise for not asking people for anything
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Who will guarantee for me that he will not ask people for anything, and I will guarantee for him Paradise?” Thawban said, “I will,” and after that he would not ask anyone for anything
q: Who will guarantee for me that he will not ask people for anything, and I will guarantee for him Paradise?

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Keep your tongue always remembering Allah
t: Abdullah ibn Busr reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, the laws of Islam are too many for me, so tell me something I can hold onto.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Keep your tongue moist with the remembrance of Allah.”
q: Keep your tongue moist with the remembrance of Allah

title: Hadith on Death: Allah reveals to the Prophet his end is near
t: Abu Razin reported: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, asked Ibn Abbas about the verse, “When the help of Allah comes and the victory,” (110:1). Ibn Abbas said, “When this verse was revealed, it was an announcement to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, about his passing.”
q: When the help of Allah comes and the victory,

title: Hadith on Freedom: The Prophet frees the slaves of al-Ta’if
t: Ibn Abbas reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, besieged the people of Al-Ta’if, he freed their slaves who came out to him.

title: Hadith on Pacts: Every treaty of justice before Islam affirmed
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Islam does not increase any just pact from the time of ignorance but in firmness or magnitude.”
q: Islam does not increase any just pact from the time of ignorance but in firmness or magnitude.

title: Hadith on Muhammad: I have never seen anyone like him
t: Abu Huraira reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, turned to face someone, he turned to them completely. When he turned away from someone, he turned away completely. I have never seen anyone like him, nor will I ever see anyone else like him.

title: Hadith on Patience: Believer who mixes with people rewarded more
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believer who mixes with people and is patient with their harm has a greater reward than the believer who does not mix with people, nor is patient with their harm.”
q: The believer who mixes with people and is patient with their harm has a greater reward than the believer who does not mix with people, nor is patient with their harm.

title: Ali on Sin: Doing and spreading vulgarity equal in sin
t: Hassan ibn Kurayb reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “One who says something vulgar and one who publicizes it are equal in sin.”

title: Hadith on Emancipation: Abu Bakr frees slaves he cursed
t: Aisha reported: Abu Bakr once cursed some of his slaves. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Abu Bakr! Those who curse, or those who are true? No, by the Lord of the Ka’bah!” The Prophet said it two or three times. On that day, Abu Bakr freed some of his slaves. Then, the Prophet came to him, saying, “Do not do it again.”
q: O Abu Bakr! Those who curse, or those who are true? No, by the Lord of the Ka’bah! … Do not do it again

title: Ali on Curses: Those who curse others are themselves cursed
t: ‘Ubayd al-Kindi reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Those who curse others are themselves cursed.”

title: Hadith on Joking: Do not take something from another person as a joke or otherwise
t: Abdullah ibn Sa’ib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Let none of you take the goods of his companion as a joke or otherwise. If one of you has taken his companion’s staff, then return it to him.”
q: Let none of you take the goods of his companion as a joke or otherwise. If one of you has taken his companion’s staff, then return it to him.

title: Hadith on Tawrat: The Prophet’s description in the Torah
t: ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar reported: I met Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with him, and I said, “Tell me about the description of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in the Torah.” Abdullah said, “By Allah, he is described in the Torah with some of what is mentioned in the Quran: O Prophet, We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of glad tidings, and to give warning, (33:45) and to guard over the illiterate, for you are My servant and My messenger. I have called you a trustworthy man, who is neither rude nor loud in the markets, nor does he return evil with evil, rather he pardons and forgives. Allah Almighty will not take him back until he has made straight the religion which was crooked, that they will say there is no God but Allah, through which eyes are made to see, ears are made to hear, and neglectful hearts are awakened.”
q: : O Prophet, We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of glad tidings, and to give warning

title: Hadith on Laughter: Why make My servants despair?
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to a group of his companions while they were laughing and talking. The Prophet said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you knew what I knew, you would laugh little and weep often.” The Prophet departed and people started weeping, so Allah Almighty revealed to him, “O Muhammad, why have you made My servants despair?” The Prophet returned and he said, “Give glad tidings, follow the right course, and seek nearness to Allah.”
q: By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you knew what I knew, you would laugh little and weep often … O Muhammad, why have you made My servants despair? … Give glad tidings, follow the right course, and seek nearness to Allah

title: Hadith on Pardon: The Prophet forgives woman who poisoned him
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A Jewish woman came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, with a poisoned sheep, and he ate from it. She was brought to him and he asked her about it. She said, “I want to kill you.” The Prophet said, “Allah has given you no authority over me.” It was said, “Should we kill her?” The Prophet said, “No.” I continued to notice the effects of the poison upon the Messenger of Allah.
q: Allah has given you no authority … over me … No
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Friends: The Prophet keeps relations with Khadijah’s friends
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was given something, he would say, “Go to such person, for they were a friend of Khadijah. Go to the house of such person, for they were loved by Khadijah.”
q: Go to such person, for they were a friend of Khadijah. Go to the house of such person, for they were loved by Khadijah.

title: Hadith on Akhirah: They are in the Hereafter as they were in life
t: Qabisah ibn Burmah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The people of virtue in the world are the people of virtue in the Hereafter. The people of vice in the world are the people of vice in the Hereafter.”
q: The people of virtue in the world are the people of virtue in the Hereafter. The people of vice in the world are the people of vice in the Hereafter
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Ibn Umar on Daughters: You want your daughters to die?
t: Al-Bukhari reported: A man in the presence of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said he wished that his daughters would die. Ibn Umar became angry and he said, “While you are providing for them?”

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Feeding your household is charity
t: Al-Miqdam ibn Ma’di reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “What you feed yourself is your charity, what you feed your children is your charity, what you feed your wife is your charity, and what you feed your servant is your charity.”
q: What you feed yourself is your charity, what you feed your children is your charity, what you feed your wife is your charity, and what you feed your servant is your charity.

title: Hadith on Shura: One who is consulted in a position of trust
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One is who is consulted is in a position of trust.”
q: One is who is consulted is in a position of trust

title: Hadith on Daughters: He will enter Paradise if he cares for even one
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever has three daughters and he cares for them, he is merciful to them, and he clothes them, then Paradise is certainly required for him.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, what if he has only two?” The Prophet said, “Even two.” Some people thought that if they had said to him one, the Prophet would have said even one.
q: Whoever has three daughters and he cares for them, he is merciful to them, and he clothes them, then Paradise is certainly required for him … Even two

title: Hadith on Freedom: The Prophet encourages freeing slaves, prisoners
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Abu al-Haytham, “Do you have a servant?” He said no. The Prophet said, “If we receive prisoners of war, come to us.” Then, the Prophet had with him two prisoners. He came and the Prophet said, “Choose between them.” He said, “O Messenger of Allah, choose for me.” The Prophet said, “Verily, one who is consulted is in a position of trust. Take this one as a servant, for I have seen him praying. I enjoin you to treat him well.” His wife said to him, “You will not fulfill what the Prophet said about him unless you free him.” He said, “Then he is emancipated.”
q: Do you have a servant? … If we receive prisoners of war, come to us … Choose between them … Verily, one who is consulted is in a position of trust. Take this one as a servant, for I have seen him praying. I enjoin you to treat him well

title: Hadith on Medicine: Healing properties of blackseed
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “This blackseed is healing for all diseases but poison.” She said, “What is poison?” The Prophet said, “Death.”
q: This blackseed is healing for all diseases but poison … Death

title: Hadith on Wudu: Rinsing the nose and mouth in ablution
t: Abu Ghatafan reported: I entered the home of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and I found him performing ablution. Then, I saw him rinsing his nose and mouth, and he said, “The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would do so two or three times.”

title: Hadith on Salat: Fifty prayers reduces to five prayers a day
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Allah commanded your Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to perform fifty prayers in a day. Then, the Prophet asked his Lord Almighty about it, so Allah made them five prayers in a day.

title: Hadith on Girls: The Prophet is gentle with little girls in prayer
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would be praying and two young girls would come and stand in front of him near his head. The Prophet would direct them to the side, or he would gesture with his hand right or left.

title: Hadith on Tashahhud: Variants of Prayer’s ending supplication
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would teach us the testimony of faith in prayer, just as he would teach us a chapter from the Quran. The Prophet would say, “Greetings, blessings, prayers, and good words are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I testify that there is no God but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.”
q: Greetings, blessings, prayers, and good words are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I testify that there is no God but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

title: Hadith on Sahaba: Best nation raised up for people
t: Sa’id ibn Jubary reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Allah Almighty said: You are the best nation brought forth for people (3:110). They are those who emigrated with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, from Mecca to Medina.”
q: You are the best nation brought forth for people

title: Hadith on Prayers: The Prophet combined prayers to ease his nation
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed noon prayers and afternoon prayers in combination for reasons other than danger or travel. Sai’d ibn Jubayr said, “Why did he do that?” Ibn Abbas said, “The Prophet intended to not cause hardship for anyone in his nation.”

title: Hadith on Mahr: The Prophet marries couple with modest dowry
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: I was among people with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, as a woman stood up and she said, “O Messenger of Allah, she has given herself in marriage to you, so what is your answer?” The Prophet did not reply. She stood up again and she said, “O Messenger of Allah, she has given herself to you, so what is your answer.” The Prophet again did not reply. She stood up a third time and she said, “She has given herself in marriage to you, so what is your answer?” A man stood up and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, marry her to me.” The Prophet said, “Do you have anything as a dowry?” He said no. The Prophet said, “Go find something, even an iron ring.” The man went and searched, then he came back and he said, “I could not find anything, not even an iron ring.” The Prophet said, “Have you learned anything from the Quran?” He said, “Yes, I know some chapters.” The Prophet said, “Go, for I have married you both with what you have learned from the Quran.”
q: Do you have anything as a dowry? … Go find something, even an iron ring … Have you learned anything from the Quran … Go, for I have married you both with what you have learned from the Quran.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jihad: True Mujahid fights jihad against his own soul
t: Fadalah ibn ‘Ubayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The one who strives in jihad is the one who strives against himself.”
q: The one who strives in jihad is the one who strives against himself

title: Hadith on Humility: The Prophet is humble with young servants
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: Any of the young servant-girls among the people of Medina would take the hand of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and lead him wherever she wished.

title: Hadith on Kids: The Prophet plays with children, tell jokes
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was the best of people in character. I had a brother who was called Abu ‘Umayr. When the Prophet would come and see him, he said, “What has the little sparrow done?” And he would play with him.
q: What has the little sparrow done?
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Women: The Prophet orders gentleness with women
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to some of his wives while they were being driven by a camel-driver named Anjasha. The Prophet said, “O driver, be gentle when you carry the precious glass.”
q: O driver, be gentle when you carry the precious glass.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ikhwah: Believer is a mirror to his brother
t:
Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believer is a mirror to his faithful brother. He protects him against loss and defends him behind his back.”

Abu Huraira said, “The believer is a mirror to his brother. If he sees something wrong in him, he should correct it.”
q: The believer is a mirror to his faithful brother. He protects him against loss and defends him behind his back

title: Hadith on Nafs: Human ego reluctant to obey Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said to the soul: Go forth! It replied: I will not go but reluctantly.”
q: Allah Almighty said to the soul: Go forth! It replied: I will not go but reluctantly.

title: Hadith on Charity: Whoever asks by Allah, give him
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever seeks refuge in the name of Allah, grant him refuge. Whoever asks you in the name of Allah, give him.
