Whoever invites you, answer him. Whoever does something good for you, reciprocate him. If you have nothing to reciprocate, supplicate for him until he sees that you have repaid him.”
q: Whoever seeks refuge in the name of Allah, grant him refuge. Whoever asks you in the name of Allah, give him. Whoever invites you, answer him. Whoever does something good for you, reciprocate him. If you have nothing to reciprocate, supplicate for him until he sees that you have repaid him

title: Hadith on Gratitude: Thank those who do you favors
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is treated well, let him repay them. If he cannot find repayment, let him praise them for that is thanking them. If he conceals it, he was been ungrateful to them. Whoever adorns himself with what he has not been given, it is as if he wears a garment of lies.”
q: Whoever is treated well, let him repay them. If he cannot find repayment, let him praise them for that is thanking them. If he conceals it, he was been ungrateful to them. Whoever adorns himself with what he has not been given, it is as if he wears a garment of lies

title: Hadith of Dua: I seek refuge in Allah from an evil neighbor
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say, “O Allah, I seek refuge in you from an evil neighbor in the final abode. Verily, a neighbor in this world can be changed.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in you from an evil neighbor in the final abode. Verily, a neighbor in this world can be changed
gf: Sahih li ghayri (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Trials: Sign of the Hour is killing neighbors, family members
t: Abu Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hour will not be established until a man kills his neighbor, his brother, and his father.”
q: The Hour will not be established until a man kills his neighbor, his brother, and his father.

title: Hadith on Neighbors: Sharing food with your neighbors
t:
Abu Dharr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Abu Dharr, when you cook a stew, put more water in the broth and take care of your neighbors.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “Pour some of it for them courteously.”
q: O Abu Dharr, when you cook a stew, put more water in the broth and take care of your neighbors. … Pour some of it for them courteously

title: Hadith on Neighbors: How many bad neighbors on Judgment Day?
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “How many neighbors will be brought with their neighbors on the Day of Resurrection? One will say: O Lord, this man closed his door to me and refused to show courtesy!”
q: How many neighbors will be brought with their neighbors on the Day of Resurrection? One will say: O Lord, this man closed his door to me and refused to show courtesy
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Jihad: Mujahid like one who constantly worships
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of one who strives in jihad in the way of Allah, and Allah knows best who strives in His way, is that of one who is always fasting and praying. Allah guarantees that one who strives in His way will enter Paradise if he passes away, or he will return home safely with a reward or spoils.”
q: The parable of one who strives in jihad in the way of Allah, and Allah knows best who strives in His way, is that of one who is always fasting and praying. Allah guarantees that one who strives in His way will enter Paradise if he passes away, or he will return home safely with a reward or spoils
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Malik on Knowledge: Teaching, learning in mosque is jihad
t: Malik reported: Abu Bakr ibn Abdur Rahman, may Allah have mercy on him, used to say, “Whoever departs to the mosque in the morning, intending to go nowhere else and to teach goodness or to learn it himself, then he returns to his house, he is like one who wages jihad in the way of Allah and returns with spoils.”

title: Hadith on Jihad: Entering mosque to learn is jihad in the way of Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever enters our mosque to teach goodness, or to learn it himself, is like one waging jihad in the way of Allah. Whoever enters it for another reason, he is an observer of what does not belong to him.”
q: Whoever enters our mosque to teach goodness, or to learn it himself, is like one waging jihad in the way of Allah. Whoever enters it for another reason, he is an observer of what does not belong to him

title: Hasan on Shura: Muslims consulted are given best options
t: Al-Sari reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “By Allah, people are never consulted but that the best option is made available to them.” Then, he recited the verse, “Those who conduct their affairs by consulting between themselves.” (42:39)
q: Those who conduct their affairs by consulting between themselves

title: Hadith on Help: The Prophet encourages companions to help the needy
t: Abu Musa reported: If a beggar or a needy person came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, he would say to his companions, “Intercede and you will be rewarded; let Allah decree upon the tongue of his messenger what he wills.”
q: Intercede and you will be rewarded; let Allah decree upon the tongue of his messenger what he wills
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salat: Pray as you see the Prophet praying
t: Malik ibn al-Huwayrith reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Pray as you have seen me praying. When the time for prayer arrives, let one of you announce the call to prayer for everyone and then let the older of you lead the prayer.”
q: “Pray as you have seen me praying. When the time for prayer arrives, let one of you announce the call to prayer for everyone and then let the older of you lead the prayer.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith of Dua: The Prophet’s supplication for night prayer
t: Ibn Abbas reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would pray at night, he would say, “O Allah, our Lord, praise be to You, for You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth. Praise be to You, for You are the Lord of the heavens and the earth and everyone in them. Praise be to You, the Light of the heavens and the earth and everyone in them. You are the truth and Your word is the truth. Your promise is the truth and Your meeting is the truth. Paradise is the truth, Hellfire is the truth, and the Hour is the truth. O Allah, I surrender to You, I have faith in You, and I rely upon You. I have argued for Your sake and judged for Your sake. Forgive me for what I have done and will do, what I keep secret and what I do in public. No one knows me better than You, for there is no God but You.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fajr: Satan tries to stop Muslims praying at night
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Satan ties three knots on the back of your head while you are asleep. On every knot he puts the saying: The night is long, stay asleep. When you wake up and remember Allah, one knot is undone. When you perform ablution, the second knot is undone. When you pray, the third knot is undone and you will wake up energetic with a good heart; otherwise, you will wake up lazy with a mischievous heart.”
q: Satan ties three knots on the back of your head while you are asleep. On every knot he puts the saying: The night is long, stay asleep. When you wake up and remember Allah, one knot is undone. When you perform ablution, the second knot is undone. When you pray, the third knot is undone and you will wake up energetic with a good heart; otherwise, you will wake up lazy with a mischievous heart

title: Hadith on Trials: Signs of the Hour will come on rapidly
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among the first signs to appear are the rising of the sun from the west and the emergence of the beast before people at noon. Whichever of them occurs first, the other will soon follow.”
q: Verily, among the first signs to appear are the rising of the sun from the west and the emergence of the beast before people at noon. Whichever of them occurs first, the other will soon follow.

title: Hadith on Disciples: The Prophet’s disciple is Zubayr ibn ‘Awwam
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, every prophet has a disciple, and my disciple is Al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam.”
q: Verily, every prophet has a disciple, and my disciple is Al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam.

title: Hadith on Trials: Be prompt with good deeds before the Hour
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Hasten to perform good deeds before a tribulation which will be like the dark part of the night, in which a man will be a believer in the morning and an unbeliever in the evening, or he will be a believer in the evening and an unbeliever in the morning. He would sell his faith for some goods in the world.”
q: Hasten to perform good deeds before a tribulation which will be like the dark part of the night, in which a man will be a believer in the morning and an unbeliever in the evening, or he will be a believer in the evening and an unbeliever in the morning. He would sell his faith for some goods in the world.

title: Sufyan on Manners: The predecessors studied manners first
t: Abu Nu’aym reported: Sufyān al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, would say, “If a man intended to write the prophetic traditions (hadith), he would study good manners and worship for twenty years before doing so.”

title: Hadith on Ummah: The Prophet sees multitudes of Muslims in Paradise
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I was shown the nations before me and one or two prophets would pass by with only a few followers, another would pass by with none at all. Then, a large crowd of people passed in front of me and I said: Is this my nation? It was said: No, this is Moses and his people. Then it was said: Look at the horizon! Behold, there was a multitude of people filling the horizon. It was said to me: This is your nation from which seventy thousand will enter Paradise without reckoning.” Then, the Prophet entered his home and did not clarify who they were. The people started discussing the matter and they said, “We are those with faith in Allah and we followed His Messenger, so we are them! Or they are our children born into Islam, but we were born in the time of ignorance.” The Prophet heard them and he came out, saying, “They are those who do not seek treatment by Ruqyah, nor do they believe in omens, nor do they brand themselves. Rather, they rely upon their Lord.” ‘Ukkashah ibn Mihsan said, “Am I one of them, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said yes. Another man said, “Am I one of them?” The Prophet said, “’Ukkashah has surpassed you.”
q: I was shown the nations before me and one or two prophets would pass by with only a few followers, another would pass by with none at all. Then, a large crowd of people passed in front of me and I said: Is this my nation? It was said: No, this is Moses and his people. Then it was said: Look at the horizon! Behold, there was a multitude of people filling the horizon. It was said to me: This is your nation from which seventy thousand will enter Paradise without reckoning … They are those who do not seek treatment by Ruqyah, nor do they believe in omens, nor do they brand themselves. Rather, they rely upon their Lord. … Ukkashah has surpassed you.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Prophets: Every Prophet has followers defending his Sunnah
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah did not send any Prophet to the nations before me but that he was given disciples and companions who held to his tradition and followed his command. Then, after them came their successors, who said what they did not practice and who practiced what they were not commanded. He who strove against them with his hand was a believer, and he who strove against them with his tongue was a believer, and he who strove against them with his heart was a believer; after that there is not even a mustard seed of faith.”
q: Allah did not send any Prophet to the nations before me but that he was given disciples and companions who held to his tradition and followed his command. Then, after them came their successors, who said what they did not practice and who practiced what they were not commanded. He who strove against them with his hand was a believer, and he who strove against them with his tongue was a believer, and he who strove against them with his heart was a believer; after that there is not even a mustard seed of faith

title: Hadith on Graves: Two punished for easily avoidable sins
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by two graves and he said, “Both of them are being punished, but not for a sin difficult to avoid. As for this man, he did not stop his urine from soiling himself. And as for this man, he would spread gossip.” The Prophet then asked for a green leaf from a date-palm. The Prophet split it into two pieces and planted one on each grave, and he said, “Perhaps it will be lightened for them as long as these two leaves are not dried.”
q: Both of them are being punished, but not for a sin difficult to avoid. As for this man, he did not stop his urine from soiling himself. And as for this man, he would spread gossip … Perhaps it will be lightened for them as long as these two leaves are not dried.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Musa: Moses hurt by people, but was patient
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was distributing charity when a man from the Ansar said, “By Allah, Muhammad did not intend to please Allah with this!” I came to the Prophet and told him about it, then anger could be seen on his face. Then, the Prophet said, “Who would be just if Allah and His Messenger are not just?” Then, the Prophet said, “May Allah have mercy on Moses! He was hurt by more than this, yet he was patient.”
q: Who would be just if Allah and His Messenger are not just? … May Allah have mercy on … Moses! He was hurt by more than this, yet he was patient
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Admiration: No envy except for charity, knowledge
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no envy but in two cases: a man whom Allah has given wealth and he spends it rightly, and a man whom Allah has given wisdom and he judges and teaches with it.”
q: There is no envy but in two cases: a man whom Allah has given wealth and he spends it rightly, and a man whom Allah has given wisdom and he judges and teaches with it.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fitrah: Every child born to believe in Allah
t:
Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No child is born but that he is upon natural instinct. His parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or Magian. As an animal delivers a child with limbs intact, do you detect any flaws?” Then, Abu Huraira recited the verse, “The nature of Allah upon which he has set people,” (30:30).

Ibn Shihab said, “The funeral prayer should be offered for every child, even if he were the son of a prostitute, as he was born with a natural inclination towards Islam. If his parents are Muslims, or only his father and even if his mother practiced other than Islam, and if he cries after the delivery before his death, his funeral prayer must be offered. If the child does not cry after the delivery, his funeral prayer should not be offered and he will be considered a miscarriage.”
q: No child is born but that he is upon natural instinct. His parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or Magian. As an animal delivers a child with limbs intact, do you detect any flaws … The nature of Allah upon which he has set people,
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jumu’ah: Allah guides us to congregate on Friday
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “We are the last nation but the foremost on the Day of Resurrection. They were given the book before us and we were given it after them. They disagreed about this day of Friday and Allah guided. Tomorrow is for the Jews and the day after tomorrow is for the Christians.”
q: We are the last nation but the foremost on the Day of Resurrection. They were given the book before us and we were given it after them. They disagreed about this day of Friday and Allah guided. Tomorrow is for the Jews and the day after tomorrow is for the Christians
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Religions: Parable of Jews, Christians, and Muslims
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of Muslims, Jews, and Christians is that of a man who employed laborers to work for him from morning until night. They worked until the middle of the day and they said: We are not in need of your reward. The man employed another group and he said to them: Complete the rest of the day and you will have the wages I allocated for the first group. They worked until the time of evening prayer and they said: Whatever we have done is for you. The man employed another group and they worked for the rest of the day until the sun had set, and they received the wages of the two other groups.”
q: The parable of Muslims, Jews, and Christians is that of a man who employed laborers to work for him from morning until night. They worked until the middle of the day and they said: We are not in need of your reward. The man employed another group and he said to them: Complete the rest of the day and you will have the wages I allocated for the first group. They worked until the time of evening prayer and they said: Whatever we have done is for you. The man employed another group and they worked for the rest of the day until the sun had set, and they received the wages of the two other groups

title: Hadith on Suicide: Man kills himself and loses Paradise
t: Jundub reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man among those before you was wounded. He was in such anguish that he took a knife, slit his wrist, and let the blood flow until he died. Allah Almighty said: My servant has preceded me with his soul, so I have forbidden Paradise for him.”
q: A man among those before you was wounded. He was in such anguish that he took a knife, slit his wrist, and let the blood flow until he died. Allah Almighty said: My servant has preceded me with his soul, so I have forbidden Paradise for him.

title: Hadith on Maryam: Why Mary is called sister of Aaron
t: Mughira ibn Shu’ba reported: When I came to Najran, the Christian monks asked me, “You recite the verse, ‘O sister of Aaron,’ (19:28) but Moses was born long before Jesus by many years.” When I came back to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, I asked him about it and he said, “Verily, they used to name people with the names of prophets and righteous people who had passed before them.”
q: O sister of Aaron … Verily, they used to name people with the names of prophets and righteous people who had passed before them

title: Hadith on Believers: Demise of world less than killing a Muslim
t:
Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The passing of the world is less significant to Allah than the killing of a Muslim.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “The killing of a believer is a greater tragedy to Allah than the passing of the world.”
q: The passing of the world is less significant to Allah than the killing of a Muslim. … The killing of a believer is a greater tragedy to Allah than the passing of the world.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Charity is a duty upon every Muslim
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Charity is a duty upon every Muslim.” They said, “What if he has nothing?” The Prophet said, “Then he should work with his hands to benefit himself and give in charity.” They said, “What if he cannot do so?” The Prophet said, “Then he should help a depressed, needy person.” They said, “What if he cannot do so?” The Prophet said, “Then he should enjoin goodness and virtue.” They said, “What if he cannot do so?” The Prophet said, “Then he should refrain from evil, for that will be his charity.”
q: Charity is a duty upon every Muslim … Then he should work with his hands to benefit himself and give in charity. … Then he should help a depressed, needy person. … Then he should enjoin goodness and virtue … Then he should refrain from evil, for that will be his charity
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Neighbors: Charity to near neighbors before far neighbors
t: Aisha reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have two neighbors; to whom should I send my gifts?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “To the neighbor who is closest to your door.”
q: To the neighbor who is closest to your door

title: Hadith on Khadijah: Good news of Paradise for the Prophet’s wife
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Angel Gabriel came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, here is Khadijah coming to you with a dish of stew, food, and drink. When she arrives before you, greet her with peace on behalf of her Lord and myself. Give her glad tidings of a palace in Paradise made of reeds, wherein there will be no turbulence, nor fatigue.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Aisha on Khadijah: I was never jealous of any woman like Khadijah
t: ‘Urwah reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “I never felt so jealous about any woman as I did for Khadijah. She had died three years before I married the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. I heard him mentioning her so often, and his Lord ordered him to give her glad tidings of her palace in Paradise made of reeds. The Prophet would slaughter a sheep and distribute its meat among her friends.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Orphans: The Prophet and caretakers together in Paradise
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Myself and the caretaker of an orphan will be in Paradise like this,” and he held his two fingers together.
q: Myself and the caretaker of an orphan will be in Paradise like this

title: Hadith on Charity: The Prophet never refused to give in charity
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was never asked anything for which he said no.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Marriage: The Prophet can recognize his wife’s mood
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Indeed, I can tell when you are angry or pleased with me.” I said, “How do you know that, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Verily, when you are pleased, you say: Yes, by the Lord of Muhammad! But when we you are upset, you say: No, by the Lord of Abraham!” I said, “Yes, I do not leave out anything but your name.”
q: Indeed, I can tell when you are angry or pleased with me. … Verily, when you are pleased, you say: Yes, by the Lord of Muhammad! But when we you are upset, you say: No, by the Lord of Abraham!

title: Hadith on Guests: The Prophet is a well-mannered guest
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, visited a house among the Ansar and he ate a meal with them. When the Prophet intended to leave, he asked for a place in the house to pray. A mat was placed, water was sprinkled over it, and he prayed on it. Then, the Prophet would supplicate to Allah on behalf of them.

title: Hadith on Hilm: The Prophet responds with kindness, charity
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: I was walking with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was wearing a Najrani cloak with a thick border. A bedouin Arab overtook the Prophet and forcibly pulled his clothes. I looked at the shoulder of the Prophet and I saw that the edge of his shirt had left a mark because of the strength of his pull. The man said, “O Muhammad! Order them to give me something from Allah’s wealth which you have!” The Prophet turned and he smiled, then he ordered that the man be given charity.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Miracles: The Prophet prays for rain, it rains
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, on Friday while he was delivering a sermon in Medina. The man said, “There is no rain, so please call upon your Lord to bless us with rain.” The Prophet looked at the sky when there were no clouds, and he called upon Allah for rain. Clouds started gathering together, and it rained until the valleys of Medina were flowing with water. It continued raining until the following Friday. Then, another man stood up while the Prophet delivered a sermon and said, “We are drowning, so please call upon your Lord to withhold it from us.” The Prophet smiled, and he said three times, “O Allah, let it rain around us and not upon us.” The clouds started dispersing over Medina to the right and left, and it rained around Medina and not upon Medina. Allah showed them the miracle of His Prophet and His answer to his supplication.
q: O Allah, let it rain around us and not upon us

title: Hadith on Hidayah: Best speech is Quran, best guide is Muhammad
t: Tariq reported: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, the best speech is the book of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.”

title: Hadith on Shirk: None more patient with falsehood than Allah
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one, or nothing, is more patient with harmful words he hears than Allah. Verily, they ascribe children to him, yet he gives them wellness and provision.”
q: No one, or nothing, is more patient with harmful words he hears than Allah. Verily, they ascribe children to him, yet he gives them wellness and provision

title: Hadith on Lies: Awful punishment of a terrible liar
t: Samurah ibn Jundub reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I saw a dream at night in which two men came to me. They said: The one whose face you saw being torn away was great liar, who would tell a lie that would be carried away until it reached the horizons. This will be done to him until the Day of Resurrection.”
q: I saw a dream at night in which two men came to me. They said: The one whose face you saw being torn away was great liar, who would tell a lie that would be carried away until it reached the horizons. This will be done to him until the Day of Resurrection

title: Hadith on Muslims: Cursing him is wicked, killing is unbelief
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Disparaging a Muslim is an act of wickedness, and fighting him is an act of unbelief.”
q: Disparaging a Muslim is an act of wickedness, and fighting him is an act of unbelief.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Takfir: False accusations will backfire against accusers
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man does not accuse another man of wickedness or unbelief but that it will be turned against him, if his companion is innocent.”
q: A man does not accuse another man of wickedness or unbelief but that it will be turned against him, if his companion is innocent

title: Hadith on Shirk: The Prophet removes graven images from home
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered the house while there was a curtain with pictures on it. The color of his face changed, then he grabbed the curtain and tore it into pieces. The Prophet said, “Verily, among the most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are those who make such graven images.”
q: Verily, among the most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are those who make such graven images.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Nawafil: Best voluntary prayer offered at home
t: Zayd ibn Thabit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O people, perform prayer in your houses, for the best prayer of a man is in his house, except for the prescribed prayers.”
q: O people, perform prayer in your houses, for the best prayer of a man is in his house, except for the prescribed prayers.

title: Hadith on Takfir: Accusations of unbelief can backfire
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a man accuses his brother of being an unbeliever, then it will be turned against at least one of them.”
q: When a man accuses his brother of being an unbeliever, then it will be turned against at least one of them.

title: Hadith on Salat: Lighten prayer for weak, elderly, needy
t: Abu Mas’ud reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, I am late to prayer today because such a person makes it too long for us.” I never saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, as angry in his preaching as he was on that day. The Prophet said, “Verily, some of you cause people to flee. Whenever you lead people in prayer, then lighten it as among them are the weak, the elderly, and the needy.”
q: Verily, some of you cause people to flee. Whenever you lead people in prayer, then lighten it as among them are the weak, the elderly, and the needy.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Rights: If a husband fails to fulfill his family’s rights
t: Aisha reported: Hind bint ‘Utba came and she said, “O Messenger of Allah, Abu Sufyan is a stingy man. Is there any blame on me for using his wealth to feed our dependents?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no blame if you feed them with a reasonable amount.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Court: The Prophet judges cases like any human being
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, heard some people disputing near the door of his house. The Prophet came out and said, “Verily, I am only a human being. Two opponents come to me for judgment and perhaps some of you are more articulate than others, so I consider him truthful and by that I judge in his favor. For whomever I mistakenly forfeit the right of a Muslim, it is only a piece of Hellfire; let him take it or leave it.”
q: Verily, I am only a human being. Two opponents come to me for judgment and perhaps some of you are more articulate than others, so I consider him truthful and by that I judge in his favor. For whomever I mistakenly forfeit the right of a Muslim, it is only a piece of Hellfire; let him take it or leave it.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Abu Hanifa on God: Abu Hanifa stumps the atheist
t: Ibn Abi al-‘Izz reported: It is said that Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, was approached by some philosphers who intended to discuss with him the oneness of Allah’s Lordship. Abu Hanifa said, “Before we discuss this question, tell me what you think about a boat in the Euphrates, which goes to shore, loads itself with food and other things, then returns, anchors and unloads all by itself, without anyone sailing or controlling it?” They said, “This is impossible.” Abu Hanifa said, “If it is impossible with a boat, then how is it possible for the world, in all its vastness, to move by itself?”

title: Hadith on Da’wah: Guiding a person to Islam better than all wealth
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By Allah, that Allah guides a man through you is better for you than a herd of expensive red camels.”
q: By Allah, that Allah guides a man through you is better for you than a herd of expensive red camels
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hadith: Allah blesses one who narrates from the Prophet
t: Zayd ibn Thabit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “May Allah brighten the face of a person who hears a tradition from us and he memorizes it until he can convey it to others. Perhaps he will convey it to one who understands better than him, and perhaps one who conveys knowledge does not understand it himself.”
q: May Allah brighten the face of a person who hears a tradition from us and he memorizes it until he can convey it to others. Perhaps he will convey it to one who understands better than him, and perhaps one who conveys knowledge does not understand it himself.

title: Hadith on Isra’iliyat: The Prophet narrates Israelite stories
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would narrate stories about the children of Israel until the morning came. The Prophet would not stand up but for the greatness of prayer.

title: Hadith on Ayat: Narrate traditions from me, even a single verse
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Convey from me, even a single verse. Narrate from the children of Israel, for there is no blame in it. Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in Hellfire.”
q: Convey from me, even a single verse. Narrate from the children of Israel, for there is no blame in it. Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in Hellfire

title: Hadith on Family: Keep good relations, even if they do not
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The one who keeps good relations with family is not the one who is reciprocated. Rather, the one who keeps good relations with family is one who does so, despite being cut off by them.”
q: The one who keeps good relations with family is not the one who is reciprocated. Rather, the one who keeps good relations with family is one who does so, despite being cut off by them

title: Hadith on Rahim: Good relations with family increase wealth, extend life
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is pleased to have his provision expanded and his life span extended, let him keep good relations with his family.”
q: Whoever is pleased to have his provision expanded and his life span extended, let him keep good relations with his family.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Children: O Allah, be merciful to them as I am merciful
t: Usamah ibn Zayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would put me on one of his thighs and he would put Hasan ibn Ali on his other thigh. Then, the Prophet would hug us and he would say, “O Allah, be merciful to them as I am merciful to them.”
q: O Allah, be merciful to them as I am merciful to them.

title: Hadith on Sins: Major sins are idolatry, infanticide, adultery
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is the greatest sin?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “To set up a partner alongside Allah, even though He alone created you.” I said, “What is next?” The Prophet said, “To kill your child, fearing he will eat with you.” I said, “What is next?” The Prophet said, “To commit adultery with the wife of your neighbor.” Then, Allah confirmed the saying of the Prophet with the verse, “Those who do not call upon another god besides Allah, nor kill a soul Allah has made sacred, except by right of justice, and do not commit adultery.” (25:68)
q: To set up a partner alongside Allah, even though He alone created you … To kill your child, fearing he will eat with you … To commit adultery with the wife of your neighbor … Those who do not call upon another god besides Allah, nor kill a soul Allah has made sacred, except by right of justice, and do not commit adultery.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Mercy: The Prophet is merciful to children
t: Aisha reported: A bedouin came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “You kiss the children? We do not kiss them.” The Prophet said, “I cannot put mercy into your heart if Allah has removed it from you.”
q: I cannot put mercy into your heart if Allah has removed it from you.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet prays holding a small child
t: Abu Qatadah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us with Umamah, the daughter of Abul al-‘As, on his shoulder. The Prophet prayed and when he bowed, he would put her down. When he arose, he would lift her up.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Islam: New Muslims keep all previous good deeds
t: Hakim ibn Hazim reported: He said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of my good deeds which I did in the time of ignorance, such as upholding family ties, freeing my slaves, and giving charity. Will I receive their reward?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You have embraced Islam along with the good you have done.”
q: You have embraced Islam along with the good you have done

title: Hadith on Parents: Allah forbids disobedience to mothers
t: Al-Mughirah ibn Sha’bah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has forbidden you from disobeying your mothers, withholding charity, demanding from others, and burying your daughters alive. Allah disapproves that you spread talebearing and gossip, ask many unnecessary questions, and waste your wealth.”
q: Verily, Allah has forbidden you from disobeying your mothers, withholding charity, demanding from others, and burying your daughters alive. Allah disapproves that you spread talebearing and gossip, ask many unnecessary questions, and waste your wealth
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Curses: Prohibition of cursing another’s parents
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among the major sins is that a man curses his own parents.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, how can a man curse his own parents?” The Prophet said, “He insults the father of another man, and then that man insults his father and his mother.”
q: Verily, among the major sins is that a man curses his own parents … He insults the father of another man, and then that man insults his father and his mother.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Cats: Cats not impure, do not nullify ablution
t:
Abu Qatadah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, cats are not impure, as they meander around you.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “It is the majority opinion of the scholars among the companions of the Prophet (ṣ), the successors, and those after them such as Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq; they did not see harm in the remnants of cats, and this is the best of what is narrated on this topic.”
q: “Verily, cats are not impure, as they meander around you.

title: Hadith on Immunity: Diplomatic immunity granted to enemy forces
t: Nu’aym ibn Mas’ud reported: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, speaking to those who were reading the letter of the false prophet Musaylimah the Liar, saying, “What do you both say?” They said, “We say what he said.” The Prophet said, “By Allah, were it not that diplomats are not killed, I would strike both of your necks.”
q: What do you both say

title: Hadith on Firasah: Believers see with light from Allah
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said, “Beware of the intuition of the believer. Verily, he sees with the light of Allah.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “Verily, in that are signs for those of discernment.” (15:75)
q: Beware of the intuition of the believer. Verily, he sees with the light of Allah. … Verily, in that are signs for those of discernment.

title: Hadith on Mercy: General amnesty the day Mecca is liberated
t: Ibn Abbas reported: In the year of Mecca’s liberation, Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, with Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and he embraced Islam. Al-Abbas said, “O Messenger of Allah, Abu Sufyan is a proud man, so give him something.” The Prophet said, “Yes. Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan will be safe. Whoever shuts his door will be safe.”
q: Yes. Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan will be safe. Whoever shuts his door will be safe

title: Scholars on Animals: Rights of creatures over humankind
t: ‘Izz al-Din ibn ‘Abd al-Salaam, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Among the rights of animals and beasts over human beings is that they be provided for in a manner appropriate to them, even if they become old, disabled, or ill such that no benefit can be derived from them; that they not be burdened beyond what they can bear; that they not be brought together with others—of their own kind or of another—that would harm them through biting, goring, or wounding; that they be slaughtered properly if they are slaughtered; that their skin not be torn nor their bones broken until they have cooled and life has fully departed; that their young not be slaughtered in their sight; that they be kept separate when necessary; that their resting places and shelters be well maintained; that their males and females be brought together at the time of mating; and that their game not be struck or thrown down, nor shot with anything that breaks its bones or kills it in a manner that does not render its meat lawful.”

title: Mu’adh on Faith: Sit with us and increase our faith
t: Al-Bukhari reported: Mu’adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Come and sit with us. We will have faith for a while to remember Allah.”

title: Hadith on Muhammad: Umar learns to love the Prophet more
t: Abdullah ibn Hisham reported: We were with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he was holding the hand of Umar ibn al-Khattab. Umar said to him, “O Messenger of Allah, you are more beloved to me than everything but myself.” The Prophet said, “No, by the One in whose hand is my soul, until I am more beloved to you than yourself.” Umar said, “Indeed, I swear by Allah that you are more beloved to me now than myself.” The Prophet said, “Now you are right, O Umar.”
q: No, by the One in whose hand is my soul, until I am more beloved to you than yourself … Now you are right, O Umar

title: Hadith on Anbiya: All of the prophets were good shepherds
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah did not send any prophet but that he cared for sheep.” The companions asked, “And you as well?” The Prophet said, “Yes. I was a shepherd with a modest wage on behalf of the people of Mecca.”
q: Allah did not send any prophet but that he cared for sheep … Yes. I was a shepherd with a modest wage on behalf of the people of Mecca

title: Hadith on Animals: Allah forgives prostitute for kindness to dog
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A prostitute had once been forgiven. She passed by a dog panting near a well. Thirst had nearly killed him, so she took off her sock, tied it to her veil, and drew up some water. Allah forgave her for that.”
q: A prostitute had once been forgiven. She passed by a dog panting near a well. Thirst had nearly killed him, so she took off her sock, tied it to her veil, and drew up some water. Allah forgave her for that.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Animals: Man forgiven for mercy to thirsty dog
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man suffered from thirst while he was walking on a journey. When he found a well, he climbed down into it and drank from it. Then he came out and saw a dog lolling its tongue from thirst and licking the ground. The man said: This dog has suffered thirst just as I have suffered from it. He climbed down into the well, filled his shoe with water, and caught it in his mouth as he climbed up. Then he gave the dog a drink. Allah appreciated his deed, so He forgave him.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, is there a reward for charity even for the animals?” The Prophet said, “Yes, in every creature with a moist liver is a reward for charity.”
q: A … man suffered from thirst while he was walking on a journey. When he found a well, he climbed down into it and drank from it. Then he came out and saw a dog lolling its tongue from thirst and licking the ground. The man said: This dog has suffered thirst just as I have suffered from it. He climbed down into the well, filled his shoe with water, and caught it in his mouth as he climbed up. Then he gave the dog a drink. Allah appreciated his deed, so He forgave him. … Yes, in every creature with a moist liver is a reward for charity
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Trials: Punishment in this world as mercy
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If Allah wills goodness for His servant, He hastens his punishment in this world. If Allah wills to harm His servant, He withholds punishment for his sins until he arrives on the Day of Resurrection. Verily, with greater rewards come greater trials. If Allah loves a people, He afflicts them with trials. Whoever is content will be given contentment, and whoever is displeased will be given displeasure.”
q: If Allah wills goodness for His servant, He hastens his punishment in this world. If Allah wills to harm His servant, He withholds punishment for his sins until he arrives on the Day of Resurrection. … Verily, with greater rewards come greater trials. If Allah loves a people, He afflicts them with trials. Whoever is content will be given contentment, and whoever is displeased will be given displeasure

title: Hadith on Madinah: People of Medina rejoice at arrival of the Prophet
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, arrived in Medina, the Abyssinians began playing, rejoicing at his arrival, and they played with their spears.

title: Hadith on Trials: The Prophets, righteous most severely tested
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, which people are tested most severely?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “They are the prophets, then the next best, then the next best. A man is put to trial according to his religion. If he is firm in his religion, his trials will be more severe. If he is weak in his religion, he is put to trial according to his strength in religion. The servant will continue to be put to trial until he is left walking upon the earth without any sin.”
q: They are the prophets, then the next best, then the next best. A man is put to trial according to his religion. If he is firm in his religion, his trials will be more severe. If he is weak in his religion, he is put to trial according to his strength in religion. The servant will continue to be put to trial until he is left walking upon the earth without any sin

title: Hadith on Umar: If anyone in Ummah is divinely-inspired, it is Umar
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Before you were nations with divinely inspired people. If such a person were in my nation, it would surely be Umar.”
q: Before you were nations with divinely inspired people. If such a person were in my nation, it would surely be Umar.

title: Hadith on Jazak: Ask Allah to reward good-doers
t: Usamah ibn Zayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever receives a good deed and says to its doer, ‘May Allah reward you with goodness,’ he has praised him to the greatest extent.”
q: Whoever receives a good deed and says to its doer, ‘May Allah reward you with goodness,’ he has praised him to the greatest extent

title: Hadith on Masajid: Best places are mosques, worst are markets
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most beloved of places to Allah are the mosques, and the most hated of places to Allah are the markets.”

title: Hadith on Hellfire: Parable of the fire, moths, and insects
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the parable of myself and the people is that of a man who kindled a fire. When it lighted all that was around it, moths and insects started falling into the fire. The man tried to pull them out, but they overcame him and rushed into it. Thus, I take hold of your belts to keep you from falling in, yet you rush into it anyway.”
q: Verily, the parable of myself and the people is that of a man who kindled a fire. When it lighted all that was around it, moths and insects started falling into the fire. The man tried to pull them out, but they overcame him and rushed into it. Thus, I take hold of your belts to keep you from falling in, yet you rush into it anyway.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Akhirah: Paradise, Hellfire nearer than your shoestring
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Paradise is closer to one of you than the strap of his sandal, and so is the Hellfire.”
q: Paradise is closer to one of you than the strap of his sandal, and so is the Hellfire

title: Hadith on Goodwill: Islam is sincerity to Allah and the people
t: Tamim al-Dari reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The religion is sincere good will.” We said, “To whom?” The Prophet said, “To Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims, and their common people.”
q: The religion is sincere good will … To Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims, and their common people.

title: Anas on Muhlikat: You think your sins are minor, but we did not
t:
Ghaylan reported: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, you indulge in bad deeds that are as insignificant as a hair in your eyes, yet in the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, we considered them mortal sins.”

Abu Abdullah said, “By that he means they are destructive vices.”

title: Hadith on Gheerah: Allah’s honor violated by Haram
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has a sense of honor. The honor of Allah is offended when believers approach what Allah has made unlawful.”
q: Verily, Allah has a sense of honor. The honor of Allah is offended when believers approach what Allah has made unlawful
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Virtues: Prayer, goodness to parents, jihad
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: I asked, “O Messenger of Allah, which deed is best?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Prayer in its proper time.” I asked, “What is next?” The Prophet said, “Good treatment of your parents.” I said, “What is next?” The Prophet said, “Jihad in the way of Allah.” I became silent and if I had asked him more, he would have told me.
q: Prayer in its proper time … Good treatment of your parents … Jihad in the way of Allah
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Niyyah: They are resurrected upon their intentions
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “An army will raid the Ka’bah, but when they reach a desert land, all of them will be swallowed by the earth.” I asked, “O Messenger of Allah, how will all of them be swallowed by the earth while among them are their markets and unrelated people?” The Prophet said, “They will all be swallowed up, then they will be resurrected for judgment upon their intentions.”
q: An army will raid the Ka’bah, but when they reach a desert land, all of them will be swallowed by the earth … They will all be swallowed up, then they will be resurrected for judgment upon their intentions.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Eating: Filling stomach a third for food, drink, air
t: Al-Miqdam ibn Ma’dikarib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The son of Adam cannot fill a vessel worse than his stomach, as it is enough for him to take a few bites to straighten his back. If he cannot do it, then he may fill it with a third of his food, a third of his drink, and a third of his breath.”
q: The son of Adam cannot fill a vessel worse than his stomach, as it is enough for him to take a few bites to straighten his back. If he cannot do it, then he may fill it with a third of his food, a third of his drink, and a third of his breath.

title: Hadith on Altruism: Believers prefer others over their own selves
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man from the Ansar was hosting a guest and he had nothing with him but just enough food for himself and his children. The man said to his wife, “Put the children to sleep, put out the lamp, and serve our guest with what we have.” Then, Allah revealed the verse, “They prefer others over their own selves, despite themselves being in need.” (59:9)
q: They prefer others over their own selves, despite themselves being in need.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Competition: Umar tries to compete with Abu Bakr
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered us to give charity and at the time I had some wealth. I said to myself, “Today I will outdo Abu Bakr, if ever there were a day to outdo him.” I went with half of my wealth to the Prophet and he said, “What have you left for your family?” I said, “The same amount.” Then, Abu Bakr came with everything he had. The Prophet said, “O Abu Bakr, what have you left for your family?” Abu Bakr said, “Allah and His Messenger.” I said, “By Allah, I will never do better than Abu Bakr.”
q: What have you left for your family … O Abu Bakr, what have you left for your family

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Children are a trial, even for the Prophet
t: Abu Buraydah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was delivering a sermon when Hasan and Husayn came wearing red shirts, walking and tripping. The Prophet descended from the pulpit, picked them both up, and placed them in his lap. The Prophet said, “Allah spoke the truth when He said: Verily, your wealth and your children are only a trial for you (64:15). I looked at these two boys walking and tripping and I could not be patient, even I cut short my speech to pick them up.”
q: Allah spoke the truth when He said: Verily, your wealth and your children are only a trial for you … I looked at these two boys walking and tripping and I could not be patient, even I cut short my speech to pick them up

title: Hadith on Shuhada: Those killed in the way of Allah alive in Paradise
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The souls of martyrs are alive in the bodies of green birds who have their nests in chandeliers hanging from the Throne of the Almighty. They eat the fruits of Paradise from wherever they wish and they nestle among these chandeliers. Once their Lord cast a glance at them and He said: Do you want anything? They said: What more could we desire? We eat the fruit of Paradise from wherever we wish. Their Lord asked them the same question three times. When they saw that they will continue to be asked, they said: O Lord, we wish that You could return our souls to our bodies so that we could be martyred in Your way once again. When Allah saw that they had no needs, He left them to enjoy.”
q: The souls of martyrs are alive in the bodies of green birds who have their nests in chandeliers hanging from the Throne of the Almighty. They eat the fruits of Paradise from wherever they wish and they nestle among these chandeliers. Once their Lord cast a glance at them and He said: Do you want anything? They said: What more could we desire? We eat the fruit of Paradise from wherever we wish. Their Lord asked them the same question three times. When they saw that they will continue to be asked, they said: O Lord, we wish that You could return our souls to our bodies so that we could be martyred in Your way once again. When Allah saw that they had no needs, He left them to enjoy

title: Hadith on Wahy: The Prophet describes his revelations
t:
Aisha reported: Al-Harith ibn Hisham asked, “O Messenger of Allah, how do you receive revelation?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Sometimes it is revealed like the ringing of a bell. This form of revelation is the hardest of all, but this hardship subsides once I have grasped what is revealed. Sometimes the angel comes in the form of a man and talks to me, and I understand whatever he says.”

Aisha said, “Verily, I saw the Prophet receiving revelation on a very cold day and I noticed sweat dropping from his forehead.”
q: Sometimes it is revealed like the ringing of a bell. This form of revelation is the hardest of all, but this hardship subsides once I have grasped what is revealed. Sometimes the angel comes in the form of a man and talks to me, and I understand whatever he says.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Umar on Hadith: Following Sunnah exactly as he heard it
t: Abu Ja’far reported: When Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, heard a tradition from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, he never added to it and he never fell short of it.

title: Hadith on Khilafah: The Prophet orders Abu Bakr to lead prayer
t:
Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, became ill, and when his condition was critical, he said, “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Aisha said, “He is a soft-hearted man. He will not be able to lead in your place.” The Prophet said again, “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Aisha repeated her concern again, but the Prophet said, “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. Verily, you are like the companions of Joseph.” A messenger was sent to Abu Bakr, and he led the people in prayer during the Prophet’s lifetime.

Aisha said, “I argued back on that with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. Nothing made me continue talking back, except that it occurred to me, the people would never love a man who took his place. I thought that no one could take his place but that people would see it as a bad omen. Thus, I wanted the Prophet to give up the idea of Abu Bakr succeeding him.”
q: Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer … Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer … Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. Verily, you are like the companions of Joseph
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Persecution: Abu Bakr comes to save the Prophet
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: I saw ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt coming to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was praying. ‘Uqbah put his sheet around the Prophet’s neck and squeezed it tightly. Abu Bakr came and pulled ‘Uqbah away from the Prophet and he said, “Do you kill a man only because he says, ‘My Lord is Allah,’ and he brought you clear evidence from your Lord?”

title: Hadith on Lust: Paradise for controlling passions
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whomever Allah protects from the evil between his jaws and the evil between his legs, he will enter Paradise.”
q: Whomever Allah protects from the evil between his jaws and the evil between his legs, he will enter Paradise

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Mention Allah often, or heart will harden
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not speak too much without mentioning Allah. Verily, talking too much without remembering Allah hardens the heart. The furthest of people from Allah is one with a hard heart.”
q: Do not speak too much without mentioning Allah. Verily, talking too much without remembering Allah hardens the heart. The furthest of people from Allah is one with a hard heart.

title: Hadith on Caliphs: The Prophet’s vision of Abu Bakr and Umar
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “While I was sleeping, I saw myself standing at a well and upon it was a bucket. I drew water from the well as much as Allah willed. Then, Ibn Abi Quhafah, Abu Bakr, took the bucket from me and brought out one or two buckets, but there was some weakness in his drawing the water. May Allah forgive his weakness! Then, the bucket became large, and Umar Ibn al-Khattab took it over. I have never seen such a mighty leader of people as Umar, drawing so much water until they even brought their camels to drink.”
q: While I was sleeping, I saw myself standing at a well and upon it was a bucket. I drew water from the well as much as Allah willed. Then, Ibn Abi Quhafah, Abu Bakr, took the bucket from me and brought out one or two buckets, but there was some weakness in his drawing the water. May Allah forgive his weakness! Then, the bucket became large, and Umar Ibn al-Khattab took it over. I have never seen such a mighty leader of people as Umar, drawing so much water until they even brought their camels to drink.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Doubts: Jesus gives believers benefit of the doubt
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Jesus, son of Mary, saw a person he thought was stealing. Jesus said to him: Have you committed theft? The man said: No, by Him besides whom there is no God! Jesus said: I believe in Allah and disbelieve my own eyes.”
q: Jesus, son of Mary, saw a person he thought was stealing. Jesus said to him: Have you committed theft? The man said: No, by Him besides whom there is no God! Jesus said: I believe in Allah and disbelieve my own eyes
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Restraint: Guarding tongue, chastity in Paradise
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever guarantees for me what is between his jaws and his legs, I can guarantee for him Paradise.”
q: Whoever guarantees for me what is between his jaws and his legs, I can guarantee for him Paradise.

title: Hadith on Freedom: Bilal, from our slave to our master
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say, “Abu Bakr is our master and he emancipated our master,” meaning Bilal.

title: Hadith on Servants: Provide food, clothing, shelter for servants
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Those in your custody are to be fed and clothed. Do not assign them a task unless they are able to do it.”
q: Those in your custody are to be fed and clothed. Do not assign them a task unless they are able to do it

title: Hadith on Equality: Slaves are equals in food, clothing, dignity
t: Al-Ma’rur ibn Suwayd reported: I met Abu Dharr while he was wearing the same clothes as his servant boy. I asked him about it, and he said, “I once abused a man and insulted his mother, so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, ‘O Abu Dharr, you insulted him by his mother? You are a man with ignorance in you. They are your brothers and your assistants. Allah has placed them in your hands. Whoever has his brother in his custody, let him feed him with the same food he eats and clothe him with the same clothes he wears. Do not assign them a task they cannot do; if you do so, then help them.”
q: O Abu Dharr, you insulted him by his mother? You are a man with ignorance in you. They are your brothers and your assistants. Allah has placed them in your hands. Whoever has his brother in his custody, let him feed him with the same food he eats and clothe him with the same clothes he wears. Do not assign them a task they cannot do; if you do so, then help them
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Thieves: Cutting the hand applied to grand theft, not petty theft
t: Aisha reported: The hand of the thief was never cut in the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, for what is less than the price of a shield or piece of armor, and both of them were expensive.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dajjal: False Messiah is one-eyed, clear unbeliever
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No prophet was sent but that he warned his nation of the one-eyed liar. Verily, he is blind in one eye while your Lord is not, and between his two eyes is written the word of unbelief.”
q: No prophet was sent but that he warned his nation of the one-eyed liar. Verily, he is blind in one eye while your Lord is not, and between his two eyes is written the word of unbelief.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Justice: Legal punishments apply equally in society
t: Aisha reported: The Quraysh had been anxious about a woman who had committed theft and they said, “Who will speak to the Messenger of Allah about her?” Some said, “Who would dare to but Usama, one beloved by the Messenger of Allah?” Thus, Usama spoke to him and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do you intercede regarding a punishment prescribed by Allah?” The Prophet then stood up and addressed the people, saying, “O people, those who came before you were destroyed because if a person of high status committed theft among them, they would spare him, but if a person of lower status committed theft, they would apply the punishment upon him. By Allah, if Fatima the daughter of Muhammad were to steal, I would have cut off her hand.”
q: Do you intercede regarding a punishment prescribed by Allah … O people, those who came before you were destroyed because if a person of high status committed theft among them, they would spare him, but if a person of lower status committed theft, they would apply the punishment upon him. By Allah, if Fatima the daughter of Muhammad were to steal, I would have cut off her hand

title: Hadith on Discipline: The Prophet threatens spanking, but fears Allah
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was in her house when he called for her servant girl. When the servant was delayed, the displeasure of the Prophet could be seen on his face. Umm Salamah arose and looked through the curtain to see the girl playing. The Prophet had a toothstick in his hand and he said, “If I did not fear retribution on the Day of Resurrection, I would have made you sore with this.”
q: If I did not fear retribution on the Day of Resurrection, I would have made you sore with this.

title: Hadith on Beatings: Allah retaliates for those beaten
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever strikes someone unjustly will receive retribution for it on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever strikes someone unjustly will receive retribution for it on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Umar on Hudud: Punishment of theft suspended during famine
t: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The hand of the thief is not cut who steals a bundle of dates or in a year of famine.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Jihad: Do not fight women, children, peaceful people
t: Al-Tabari reported: Ibn Abbas explained the saying of Allah Almighty, “Fight in the way of Allah those who fight you but do not transgress, for Allah does not love transgressors,” (2:190) saying, “Do not kill women, children, old men, or whoever comes to you with peace and he restrains his hand from fighting, for if you did so you would have certainly transgressed.”
q: Fight in the way of Allah those who fight you but do not transgress, for Allah does not love transgressors

title: Hadith on Hospitality: Let him honor his guests, speak goodness
t: Abu Shurayh reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest and recompense him.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is his recompense?” The Prophet said, “It is for a day and a night, as good hospitality is for three days and after that it is charity.” And the Prophet said, “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak goodness or remain silent.”
q: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest and recompense him … It is for a day and a night, as good hospitality is for three days and after that it is charity. … Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak goodness or remain silent
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Afterlife: No death in the Hereafter, only eternity
t: Abu Sa’id reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a white ram, and it will be made to stand between Paradise and Hellfire. It will be said to the people of Paradise: Do you recognize this? They will raise their heads, looking towards it, and they will say: Yes, it is death. Then, it will be said to the people of Hellfire: Do you recognize this? They will raise their heads, looking towards it, and they will say: Yes, it is death. Then, the command will be given to slaughter the ram and it will be said: O people of Paradise, there is everlasting life for you and no death! And it will be said: O people of Hellfire, there is everlasting life for you and no death!” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “Warn them of this day of dismay, when their affairs will be decided, yet they are heedless and they do not have faith,” (19:39) and he pointed with his hand to the world.
q: Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a white ram, and it will be made to stand between Paradise and Hellfire. It will be said to the people of Paradise: Do you recognize this? They will raise their heads, looking towards it, and they will say: Yes, it is death. Then, it will be said to the people of Hellfire: Do you recognize this? They will raise their heads, looking towards it, and they will say: Yes, it is death. Then, the command will be given to slaughter the ram and it will be said: O people of Paradise, there is everlasting life for you and no death! And it will be said: O people of Hellfire, there is everlasting life for you and no death! … Warn them of this day of dismay, when their affairs will be decided, yet they are heedless and they do not have faith,
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authentic) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hajj: Obligation of Hajj once in lifetime
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was delivering a sermon to us, saying, “O people, the Hajj pilgrimage has been made an obligation, so undertake it.” A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, is it every year?” The Prophet remained silent until the man repeated his question three times. Then, the Prophet said, “If I had said yes, it would have been required and you would not be able to do it.”
q: O people, the Hajj pilgrimage has been made an obligation, so undertake it … If I had said yes, it would have been required and you would not be able to do it.

title: Hadith on Backbiting: Horrific punishment in Hellfire
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When I was taken up during the Night Journey, I passed by people who had nails of copper, scratching their faces and chests. I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? Gabriel said: These are the ones who ‘eat the flesh of people’ (49:12) and defame their reputations.”
q: When I was taken up during the Night Journey, I passed by people who had nails of copper, scratching their faces and chests. I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? Gabriel said: These are the ones who ‘eat the flesh of people’ … and defame their reputations

title: Hadith on Gheebah: Companions smell evil wind of backbiting
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: We were with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when we detected a foul odor carried by the wind. The Prophet said, “Do you know what this wind is? It is the smell of those who backbite the believers.”
q: Do you know what this wind is? It is the smell of those who backbite the believers

title: Hadith on Signs: Hurry to good before signs of Hour
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Hasten to perform good deeds before six events: the False Messiah, the smoke, the beast from the earth, the rising of the sun from the west, the general turmoil, and your demise.”
q: Hasten to perform good deeds before six events: the False Messiah, the smoke, the beast from the earth, the rising of the sun from the west, the general turmoil, and your demise.

title: Hadith on Gratitude: Shall I not be a grateful servant?
t: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would pray until his feet were swollen. It was said to him, “Why do you do this when Allah has forgiven your past and future sins?” The Prophet said, “Shall I not be a grateful servant?”
q: Shall I not be a grateful servant?
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Pilgrimage: Successful Hajj completely purifies from sin
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever performs the Hajj pilgrimage to this house, without having intimate relations or committing sin, he will return pure of sin like the day he was born from his mother.”
q: Whoever performs the … pilgrimage to this house, without having intimate relations or committing sin, he will return pure of sin like the day he was born from his mother
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Covenants: A woman’s pledge of protection is honored
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Umm Hani, daughter of Abu Talib, related to me that she granted protection to a man among the idolaters on the day Mecca was liberated. She came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and she mentioned that to him. The Prophet said, “We protect the one you have protected. We grant safety to one whom you have granted safety.”
q: We protect the one you have protected. We grant safety to one whom you have granted safety

title: Hadith on Jihad: The Prophet condemns killing women and children
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: A woman was found killed in one of the battles of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, so the Prophet condemned the killing of women and children.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jihad: The Prophet forbids killing civilians, children
t: Rabah ibn Rabi’ reported: We were with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, during a military expedition. The Prophet saw some people gathered around something, so he sent a man, saying, “Go and see for what they have gathered.” The man returned and said, “It was a woman who was killed.” The Prophet said, “She was not fighting!” Khalid ibn al-Walid was in the advanced guard, so the Prophet sent a man to him, saying, “Do not kill women or workers!”
q: Go and see for what they have gathered … She was not fighting … Do not kill women or workers

title: Hadith on Struggle: Jihad, Hajj among best deeds after faith
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked, “What is the best deed?” The Prophet said, “Faith in Allah and His Messenger.” It was said, “Then what?” The Prophet said, “Jihad in the way of Allah.” It was said, “Then what?” The Prophet said, “A blessed Hajj pilgrimage.”
q: Faith in Allah and His Messenger … Jihad in the way of Allah. … A blessed Hajj pilgrimage
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Muhammad: Prophet of repentance, Prophet of mercy
t: Abu Musa al-Ashari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am the ender of prophecy, I am the gatherer on the Day of Resurrection, I am the Prophet of repentance, and I am the Prophet of mercy.”
q: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am the ender of prophecy, I am the gatherer on the Day of Resurrection, I am the Prophet of repentance, and I am the Prophet of mercy

title: Hadith on Umrah: Two pilgrimages rewarded with forgiveness
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The ‘Umrah pilgrimage to the following ‘Umrah will expiate whatever sins were committed between them, and the blessed Hajj pilgrimage has no reward other than Paradise.”
q: The ‘Umrah pilgrimage to the following ‘Umrah will expiate whatever sins were committed between them, and the blessed Hajj pilgrimage has no reward other than Paradise.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jihad: Best jihad for women is Hajj pilgrimage
