t: Aisha reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, shall we not attend the military expeditions and fight in jihad alongside you?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No, rather the best and most beautiful jihad for you is the Hajj, a blessed pilgrimage.”
q: No, rather the best and most beautiful jihad for you is the Hajj, a blessed pilgrimage

title: Hadith on Umar: The Prophet prays for Umar’s conversion
t:
Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, strengthen Islam with one of two men whom you love more: Abu Jahl or Umar ibn al-Khattab.”

Ibn Umar said, “The most beloved of the two was Umar.”
q: O Allah, strengthen Islam with one of two men whom you love more: Abu Jahl or Umar ibn al-Khattab

title: Hadith on Muhammad: The beautiful names of the Prophet
t: Jubayr ibn Mut’im reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I have many names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am the eraser through whom Allah erases unbelief, I am the gatherer at whose feet the people will be gathered, and I am the last prophet after which there are none.” Jubayr said, “And Allah has named him as kind and merciful.”
q: Verily, I have many names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am the eraser through whom Allah erases unbelief, I am the gatherer at whose feet the people will be gathered, and I am the last prophet after which there are none.

title: Hadith on Tawassul: Not calling on the Prophet after his death
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: If a drought became threatening, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, would ask Al-‘Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib to supplicate for Allah to send rain. Umar would say, “O Allah, we used to ask our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to supplicate for rain and You would bless us with rain. Now we ask the uncle of our Prophet to supplicate for rain, so bless us with rain.” And so it would rain.

title: Hadith on Dua: Allah will forgive him, even if he fled from battle
t: Zayd ibn Harithah reported:  The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever says this supplication, ‘I seek forgiveness from Allah Almighty, besides whom there is no God, the Living, the Sustainer, and I repent to him,’ then Allah will forgive him, even if he fled from battle.”
q: Whoever says this supplication, ‘I seek forgiveness from Allah Almighty, besides whom there is no God, the Living, the Sustainer, and I repent to him,’ then Allah will forgive him, even if he fled from battle.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Uthman on Killing: If you kill one person, you have killed all people
t: Abu Huraira reported:  I entered upon Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, on the day he was under siege in his house, and I said, “O leader of the believers, I have come to give support or fight.” Uthman said, “O Abu Huraira, would it please you to ‘kill the people altogether’ (5:32) including me?” I said no. Uthman said, “By Allah, if you have killed one man, it is as if you have killed all the people.” So I returned and I did not fight.
q: kill the people altogether

title: Hadith on Tyranny: Be patient, even if he strikes your back
t: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman reported: I asked, “O Messenger of Allah, we were living in an evil time and Allah brought us good in which we live now. Will there be evil after this good?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Yes.” I said, “And any good after this evil?” The Prophet said, “Yes.” I said, “And any evil after this good?” The Prophet said, “Yes.” I said, “How will it be?” The Prophet said, “After me, leaders will come who do not follow my guidance or my Sunnah. Some of their men will have the hearts of devils in a human body.” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what should I do if I live to see that time?” The Prophet said, “You should listen and obey the ruler, even if he strikes your back and takes your wealth, even still listen and obey.”
q: Yes … Yes … Yes … After me, leaders will come who do not follow my guidance or my Sunnah … Some of their men will have the hearts of devils in a human body … You should listen and obey the ruler, even if he strikes your back and takes your wealth, even still listen and obey.

title: Hadith on Customs: Follow the Prophet’s revelation, not personal opinions
t: Rafi’ ibn Khadij reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, arrived in Medina, and they were pollinating and grafting palm trees. The Prophet said, “Perhaps it would be better if you did not do so.” They abandoned the practice, but the trees yielded less fruit. It was mentioned to the Prophet, and he said, “Verily, I am only a human being. If I command you with something in the religion, adhere to it. If I command you with something from my opinion, I am only a human being.”
q: Perhaps it would be better if you did not do so … Verily, I am only a human being. If I command you with something in the religion, adhere to it. If I command you with something from my opinion, I am only a human being.

title: Hadith on Rahmah: None enters Paradise but by Allah’s mercy
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Follow the right course, be devoted, and give glad tidings. Verily, none of you will enter Paradise by his deeds alone.” They said, “Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Not even myself, unless Allah grants me His mercy. Know that the most beloved deed to Allah is done regularly, even if it is small.”
q: Follow the right course, be devoted, and give glad tidings. Verily, none of you will enter Paradise by his deeds alone … Not even myself, unless Allah grants me His mercy. Know that the most beloved deed to Allah is done regularly, even if it is small.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tyranny: Hating oppression of Muslim tyrants, but not rebelling
t: Umm Salamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will be rulers from whom you will see both goodness and corruption. One who recognizes their evil and hates it will maintain his innocence, but one who is pleased with it and follows them will be sinful.” It was said, “Shall we not fight them?” The Prophet said, “No, as long as they pray.”
q: There will be rulers from whom you will see both goodness and corruption. One who recognizes their evil and hates it will maintain his innocence, but one who is pleased with it and follows them will be sinful … No, as long as they pray

title: Hadith on Tyranny: Hate a ruler’s actions, but do not rebel
t: Awf ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of your rulers are those whom you love and they love you, who pray for you and you pray for them. The worst of your rulers are those whom you hate and they hate you, whom you curse and they curse you.” It was said, “Shall we confront them with swords?” The Prophet said, “No, as long as they establish prayer among you. If you find something hateful in them, you should hate their actions but not withdraw your hand from obedience.”
q: The best of your rulers are those whom you love and they love you, who pray for you and you pray for them. The worst of your rulers are those whom you hate and they hate you, whom you curse and they curse you … No, as long as they establish prayer among you. If you find something hateful in them, you should hate their actions but not withdraw your hand from obedience

title: Hadith on Marriage: Wife must consent to her Nikah
t: Aisha reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, should women be asked for their consent before marriage?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Yes.” I said, “A virgin might be shy to speak when asked.” The Prophet said, “Her silence is her consent.”
q: Yes … Her silence is her consent
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Nikah: If a woman married without consent
t: Khansa’ bint Khidam reported: Her father married her off after her previous marriage ended, but she disliked it. She came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he annulled their marriage.

title: Hadith on Patience: Believers in past faced great persecution
t: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt reported: We complained to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was leaning upon his rolled up cloak in the shade of the Ka’bah. We said, “Will you ask Allah to help us? Will you supplicate to Allah for us?” The Prophet said, “Among those before you, a believer would be seized, a ditch would be dug for him, and he would be thrown into it. Then, they would bring a saw that would be put on top of his head to split him into two halves, and his flesh would be torn from the bone with iron combs. Yet, all of this did not cause them to abandon their religion. By Allah, this religion will prevail until a rider travels from Yemen to Hadhramaut, fearing no one but Allah and the wolf, lest it trouble his sheep. Rather, you are impatient!”
q: Among those before you, a believer would be seized, a ditch would be dug for him, and he would be thrown into it. Then, they would bring a saw that would be put on top of his head to split him into two halves, and his flesh would be torn from the bone with iron combs. Yet, all of this did not cause them to abandon their religion. By Allah, this religion will prevail until a rider travels from Yemen to Hadhramaut, fearing no one but Allah and the wolf, lest it trouble his sheep. Rather, you are impatient … ”

title: Hadith on Wisdom: Believers prepare for death with good deed
t: Ibn Umar reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, which of the believers is best?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Those with the best character.” The man said, “Which of the believers is the wisest?” The Prophet said, “Those who remember death often and have best prepared for it with good deeds; such are the wisest.”
q: Those with the best character … Those who remember death often and have best prepared for it with good deeds; such are the wisest

title: Hadith on Mawt: Remember death, destroyer of pleasures
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Remember often the destroyer of pleasures: death.”
q: Remember often the destroyer of pleasures: death.

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Regret is part of sound repentance
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Regret is part of repentance.”
q: Regret is part of repentance

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Even if your sins piled to the heavens
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If your sins were to reach to the heavens and then you repented, Allah would still accept your repentance.”
q: If your sins were to reach to the heavens and then you repented, Allah would still accept your repentance.

title: Hadith on Sin: Allah scatters good deeds of transgressors
t: Thawban reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I certainly know people from my nation who will come on the Day of Resurrection with good deeds like the mountains of Tihamah, but Allah will ‘scatter them like dust,’” (25:23). Thawban said, “O Messenger of Allah, describe them to us and tell us more, that we will not become like them.” The Prophet said, “They are your brothers and from your ethnicity, taking up worship at night as you do, but they will be people who transgress the sacred limits of Allah when they are alone.”
q: I certainly know people from my nation who will come on the Day of Resurrection with good deeds like the mountains of Tihamah, but Allah will ‘scatter them like dust,’ … They are your brothers and from your ethnicity, taking up worship at night as you do, but they will be people who transgress the sacred limits of Allah when they are alone.

title: Hadith on Sin: Beware of committing many minor sins
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “O Aisha, beware of seemingly insignificant bad deeds. Verily, they have a pursuer from Allah.”
q: O Aisha, beware of seemingly insignificant bad deeds. Verily, they have a pursuer from Allah.

title: Hadith on Sin: Black spot on his heart until he repents
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when the servant commits a sin, a black mark appears upon his heart. If he abandons the sin, seeks forgiveness, and repents, then his heart will be polished. If he returns to the sin, the blackness will be increased until it overcomes his heart. It is the covering that Allah has mentioned: No, rather a covering is over their hearts from what they have earned.” (83:14)
q: Verily, when the servant commits a sin, a black mark appears upon his heart. If he abandons the sin, seeks forgiveness, and repents, then his heart will be polished. If he returns to the sin, the blackness will be increased until it overcomes his heart. It is the covering that Allah has mentioned: No, rather a covering is over their hearts from what they have earned

title: Hadith on ‘Ashura: Recommendation to fast day of ‘Ashura
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, ‘Ashura is one of the days of Allah. Whoever wants to fast may do so, and whoever does not want to fast may do so.”
q: Verily, ‘Ashura is one of the days of Allah. Whoever wants to fast may do so, and whoever does not want to fast may do so

title: Abu Bakr on Khilafah: Inaugural address of Abu Bakr as Caliph
t: Ibn Hisham reported: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, began to speak at his inauguration, praising Allah as He deserves and saying, “To proceed: O people, I have been put in authority over you, but I am not the best of you. If I do the right thing, then help me. If I do wrong, then correct me. Truthfulness is a sacred trust, and lying is a betrayal. The weak among you are strong in my sight so I will relieve their suffering as is their right, if Allah wills. The strong among you are weak in my sight so I will take what is due from them, if Allah wills. No people abandon jihad in the way of Allah but that Allah strikes them with disgrace. Obscenity never spreads among people but that Allah afflicts them with trials. Obey me as long as I obey Allah and His Messenger, but If I disobey Allah and His Messenger, then you are not obligated to obey me. Now, stand for your prayer, and may Allah have mercy upon you.”

title: Hadith on Faith: Love and hate for Allah is perfection of faith
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever loves for the sake of Allah, hates for the sake of Allah, gives for the sake of Allah, and withholds for the sake of Allah has perfected the faith.”
q: Whoever loves for the sake of Allah, hates for the sake of Allah, gives for the sake of Allah, and withholds for the sake of Allah has perfected the faith

title: Hadith on Faith: Islam has sixty branches, including modesty
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Faith has sixty to seventy branches, the best of which is to declare there is no God but Allah, the least of which is to remove something harmful from the road, and modesty is a branch of faith.”
q: Faith has sixty to seventy branches, the best of which is to declare there is no God but Allah, the least of which is to remove something harmful from the road, and modesty is a branch of faith.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Ibn Rawahah on Iman: Parable of faith is that of a garment
t: Ibn Hajar reported: Abdullah ibn Rawahah, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The parable of faith is that of a shirt. You may not be wearing it and then you put it on, or you may be wearing it and then you take it off.”

title: Hadith on Faith: Or maybe he is merely a Muslim?
t: Sa’d reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was distributing charity, so I said, “O Messenger of Allah, give it to this man for he is a believer.” The Prophet said, “Or merely a Muslim.” I said it three times and the Prophet repeated it three times, “Or merely a Muslim.” Then the Prophet said, “Verily, I may give a man something, although another is more beloved to me, fearing that Allah may throw him down into the Hellfire.”
q: Or merely a Muslim … Or merely a Muslim … Verily, I may give a man something, although another is more beloved to me, fearing that Allah may throw him down into the Hellfire
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Makkah: The Prophet loves his hometown of Mecca
t: Abdullah ibn ‘Adi reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was standing near Mecca and saying, “By Allah, you are the best and most beloved land to Allah. Had I not been driven away from you, I would not have left you.”
q: By Allah, you are the best and most beloved land to Allah. Had I not been driven away from you, I would not have left you

title: Hadith on Satan: Devil will come with doubts, seek refuge in Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Satan will come to one of you and he will say, ‘Who created this and that?’ until he says to him, ‘Who created your Lord?’ When it comes to this, let him seek refuge in Allah and stop such thoughts.”
q: Satan will come to one of you and he will say, ‘Who created this and that?’ until he says to him, ‘Who created your Lord?’ When it comes to this, let him seek refuge in Allah and stop such thoughts
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Satan: Devil runs through people like blood
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Satan flows through the human being like the flowing of blood.”
q: Verily, Satan flows through the human being like the flowing of blood

title: Hadith on Vanity: Dragging one’s clothes out of pride
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever trails his garment in vanity, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection.” Abu Bakr said, “One of my robes slides down unless I am cautious about it.” The Prophet said, “You are not doing it in vanity.”
q: Whoever trails his garment in vanity, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection … You are not doing it in vanity.

title: Hadith on Sahaba: Most beloved companions to the Prophet
t: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As reported: I said, “Which person is most beloved to you?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Aisha.” I said, “I mean among men.” The Prophet said, “Her father.” I said, “Then who?” The Prophet said, “Umar ibn al-Khattab,” and the Prophet mentioned other men.
q: Aisha … Her father … Umar ibn al-Khattab
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authentic) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Islam: Greet strangers with peace
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man asked the Prophet, “Which Islam is best?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “That you feed the hungry and you greet with peace those you know and those you do not know.”
q: That you feed the hungry and you greet with peace those you know and those you do not know
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hasad: Beware envy destroying good deeds
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of envy, for it devours good deeds just as fire devours wood or grass.”
q: Beware of envy, for it devours good deeds just as fire devours wood or grass.

title: Hadith on Independence: Best food to eat earned by hard work
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most wholesome food a man can eat is that which he has earned.”
q: Verily, the most wholesome food a man can eat is that which he has earned.

title: Hadith on Islah: Reporting good information to reconcile people
t: Umm Kulthum reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He is not a liar who reconciles people by spreading good, or saying something good.”
q: He is not a liar who reconciles people by spreading good, or saying something good
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Success in refusing to fight unjust wars
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Woe to the Arabs from an evil approaching! He has succeeded who restrains his hand from fighting.”
q: Woe to the Arabs from an evil approaching! He has succeeded who restrains his hand from fighting

title: Hadith on Tajdid: Righteous people will renew the religion
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah will raise up in this nation at the beginning of every century someone who will renew their religion.”
q: Verily, Allah will raise up in this nation at the beginning of every century someone who will renew their religion

title: Hadith on Habil: Be the son of Adam who did not kill
t:
Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you advise if someone invades my home and stretches forth his hand to kill me?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be like the son of Adam.”

Yazid recited the verse, “If you raise your hand to kill me, I will not raise mine to kill you, because I fear Allah—the Lord of all worlds,” (5:28).
q: Be like the son of Adam. … If you raise your hand to kill me, I will not raise mine to kill you, because I fear Allah—the Lord of all worlds

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Blessed are those saved from trials
t: Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, blessed is one kept away from tribulations, blessed is one kept away from tribulations, blessed is one kept away from tribulations, yet excellent is one who is afflicted and bears it patiently.”
q: Verily, blessed is one kept away from tribulations, blessed is one kept away from tribulations, blessed is one kept away from tribulations, yet excellent is one who is afflicted and bears it patiently.

title: Hadith on Fitnah: This Ummah punished in the world with trials
t: Abu Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “This nation of mine has been granted mercy. Their punishment is not in the Hereafter. Their punishment is in the world through persecution, earthquakes, and slaughter.”
q: This nation of mine has been granted mercy. Their punishment is not in the Hereafter. Their punishment is in the world through persecution, earthquakes, and slaughter.

title: Hadith on Tajdid: Reward for reviving a forgotten Sunnah
t: ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Know that whoever revives a tradition from my Sunnah if it has died out after me, he will have a reward like those who act upon it without diminishing any of their rewards. Whoever innovates a misguided heresy not pleasing to Allah and His messenger, he will have a sin like those who act upon it without diminishing any of the people’s burdens.”
q: Know that whoever revives a tradition from my Sunnah if it has died out after me, he will have a reward like those who act upon it without diminishing any of their rewards. Whoever innovates a misguided heresy not pleasing to Allah and His messenger, he will have a sin like those who act upon it without diminishing any of the people’s burdens

title: Hadith on Dhul-Hijjah: These ten days are greatest to Allah
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are no days greater and more beloved to Allah than these ten days of Dhul Hijjah, so increase in them your declaration of the oneness of Allah, your exaltation of Him, and your praise of Him.”
q: There are no days greater and more beloved to Allah than these ten days of Dhul Hijjah, so increase in them your declaration of the oneness of Allah … your exaltation of Him … and your praise of Him

title: Hadith on Companions: First Muslims were slaves, women, Abu Bakr
t: ‘Ammar reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while there was no one with him but fives slaves, two women, and Abu Bakr.

title: Hadith on Sahaba: If the Prophet is gone, go to Abu Bakr
t: Jubayr ibn Mut’im reported: A woman came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he ordered her to return another time. She said, “What if I come and I do not find you?” It was as if she wanted to say, “What if I find you dead?” The Prophet said, “If you do not find me, go to Abu Bakr.”
q: If you do not find me, go to Abu Bakr
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sunnah: Abdullah ibn Amr writes down the Hadith
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: I would write down everything I heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, wanting to memorize it, but the Quraysh told me not to do it. They said, “Do you write down everything you hear from him? The Prophet is a human being! He speaks when he is angry and pleased.” So, I stopped writing things down. I mentioned it to the Prophet, and he pointed to his mouth and said, “Write, for by the One in whose hand is my soul, nothing comes out of it but the truth.”
q: Write, for by the One in whose hand is my soul, nothing comes out of it but the truth.

title: Hadith on Brothers: If you love your brother, let him know
t: Al-Miqdam ibn Ma’dikarib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you loves his brother, let him know.”
q: When one of you loves his brother, let him know.

title: Hadith on Boycott: Forsaking brother a year like killing him
t: Abu Khirash al-Sulami reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever boycotts his brother for a year, it is as if he has shed his blood.”
q: Whoever boycotts his brother for a year, it is as if he has shed his blood.

title: Hadith on Reconciliation: Good relations better than voluntary worship
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you of what is better in degree than extra fasts, prayers, and charity?” They said, “Of course!” The Prophet said, “Reconciliation between people, for ruined relations between people is the razor.”
q: Shall I not tell you of what is better in degree than extra fasts, prayers, and charity? … Reconciliation between people, for ruined relations between people is the razor

title: Umar on Brothers: Assume good from your brother, give excuses
t: Ibn Abi Mulaykah reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “It is not allowed for a Muslim who hears a word from his brother to assume evil of him if he can find something good about it.”

title: Hadith on Dua: The Prophet teaches Sayyid al-Istighfar
t: Shaddad ibn Aws reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him, “The best way to seek forgiveness is that you say: O Allah, You are my Lord. There is no God but You. You created me and I am Your servant, I am committed to You and Your promise, as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil I have done. I acknowledge Your favors and I acknowledge my sins, so forgive me. Verily, no one forgives sins but You.” The Prophet said, “Whoever says this in the day with conviction and dies before evening, he will be among the people of Paradise. Whoever says this in the night with conviction and dies before morning, he will be among the people of Paradise.”
q: Whoever says this in the day with conviction and dies before evening, he will be among the people of Paradise. Whoever says this in the night with conviction and dies before morning, he will be among the people of Paradise

title: Ja’far on Islam: Companions meet the Christian King of Abyssinia
t:
Umm Salamah reported: When Ja’far ibn Abu Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, was in Abyssinia, he addressed the Negus, saying, “O king! We were plunged in the depths of ignorance and barbarism. We adored idols, lived in immorality, ate dead bodies, and spoke abominations. We severed family ties and neglected the duties of hospitality and neighborliness. We knew no law but that of the strong, but Allah raised among us a man of whose birth, truthfulness, honesty, and purity we were acknowledged, and he called us to the oneness of Allah and taught us not to associate anything with Allah. He forbade us from the worship of idols, he enjoined us to speak the truth, to be faithful to our trusts, to be merciful, and to regard the rights of our neighbors and family members. He forbade us from speaking evil of women or consuming the wealth of orphans. He ordered us to avoid vices, refrain from evil, offer prayers, give charity, and observe fasting. We have faith in him, we have accepted his teachings, his command to worship Allah, and to not to associate anything with Him. We have allowed what he has allowed and prohibited what he has prohibited. For this reason, our people have risen against us. They have persecuted us to make us abandon the worship of Allah and return to the worship of idols and other abominations. They have tortured and harmed us until we found no safety among them, so we have come to your country in hope you will protect us from oppression.”

The Negus said to them, “Do you have anything with you from Allah?” Ja’far said yes. The Negus said, “Then recite it to us.” Ja’far recited from memory the verses of Surat Maryam. The Negus and the bishops in his realm were moved to tears due to what was recited to them until their beards became wet. The Negus said, “Verily, this recitation and what has come from Moses have emerged from the same lamp. You are released. By Allah, I will never surrender them to the Quraysh.”

title: Ibn Qayyim on Akhlaq: Entire religion is good character, manners
t:
Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “The religion itself is entirely good character, so whoever surpasses you in character has surpassed you in religion. Likewise, it is such with spirituality (al-tasawwuf). Al-Kanani said: Spirituality is itself good character, so whoever surpasses you in character has surpassed you in spirituality.”

And he said, “Good manners itself is the religion in its entirety.”

title: Hadith on Salat: Sincere prayer should prevent major sins
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “This person prays in the night but he steals in the morning!” The Prophet said, “Verily, prayer should stop him from doing that if what you say is true.”
q: Verily, prayer should stop him from doing that if what you say is true

title: Hadith on Fiqh: Deadly result to give verdicts without knowledge
t: Ibn Abbas reported: A man was wounded during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. The man had a nocturnal emission, so he was ordered to perform a ritual bath without a concession. The water seeped into his wound causing his death. When this news reached the Prophet, he said, “They killed him! May Allah curse them! Is not the cure for ignorance to ask questions?”
q: They killed him! May Allah curse them! Is not the cure for ignorance to ask questions?

title: Hadith on Neighbors: Worship is no good without manners
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, a woman prays in the night, fasts in the day, does many deeds and gives charity, yet she harms her neighbors with her tongue.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no good in her. She is among the people of Hellfire.” The man said, “O Messenger of Allah, another woman prays the obligatory prayers and gives bits of food in charity, yet she does not harm anyone.” The Prophet said, “She is among the people of Paradise.”
q: There is no good in her. … She is among the people of Hellfire … She is among the people of Paradise

title: Hadith on Wudu: Key to Paradise is prayer, ablution
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The key to Paradise is prayer, and the key to prayer is ablution.”
q: The key to Paradise is prayer, and the key to prayer is ablution.

title: Hadith on Parables: The Prophet is like warning of an enemy
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the parable of what Allah has sent to me is that of a man who came to his people and he said, ‘O people! I have seen an army with my own eyes, and I give you a clear warning that you should flee to safety!’ A group among his people obeyed and fled to a place of safety. A group among them denied him and remained in their place. When morning came, the army attacked and destroyed them. That is the parable of one who obeys me and follows what I have been sent with, and one who disobeys me and denies the truth I have been sent with.”
q: Verily, the parable of what Allah has sent to me is that of a man who came to his people and he said, ‘O people! I have seen an army with my own eyes, and I give you a clear warning that you should flee to safety!’ A group among his people obeyed and fled to a place of safety. A group among them denied him and remained in their place. When morning came, the army attacked and destroyed them. That is the parable of one who obeys me and follows what I have been sent with, and one who disobeys me and denies the truth I have been sent with.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hidayah: Parable of the Prophet’s guidance is rainfall
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the parable of the guidance and knowledge that Allah Almighty sent with me is the likeness of rain falling upon the earth. Among them is a good group which receives the water and thus there is abundant growth of herbage and grass. Among them is a barren land which retains the water and thus Allah benefits people from it; they drink from it and graze their animals. And it falls upon another group which is only abysmal; it does not retain water, nor does herbage grow. Such is the parable of one who understands the religion of Allah and benefits from what Allah sent with me; he learns and he teaches. Such is the parable of one who does not raise his head and does not accept the guidance Allah sent with me.”
q: Verily, t
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Akhirah: The Prophet leads children of Adam on Judgment Day
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I will be the leader of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection. I will be the first intercessor and the first whose intercession will be accepted.”
q: I will be the leader of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection. I will be the first intercessor and the first whose intercession will be accepted.

title: Hadith on Dajjal: The Prophet sees a vision of Jesus and False Messiah
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I saw a vision last night by the Ka’bah in my sleep. There was a brown-skinned man, as beautiful as I had ever seen. His hair fell between his shoulders, a man whose head was dripping with water. He placed his hands on the shoulders of two men as he circled the House. I said: Who is this? They said: It is the Messiah, son of Mary. Then I saw a man behind him, with very curly hair and blindness in his right eye, resembling the look of Ibn Qatan. He placed his hands on the shoulders of a man as he circled the House. I said: Who is this? They said: It is the False Messiah.”
q: I saw a vision last night by the Ka’bah in my sleep. There was a brown-skinned man, as beautiful as I had ever seen. His hair fell between his shoulders, a man whose head was dripping with water. He placed his hands on the shoulders of two men as he circled the House. I said: Who is this? They said: It is the Messiah, son of Mary. Then I saw a man behind him, with very curly hair and blindness in his right eye, resembling the look of Ibn Qatan. He placed his hands on the shoulders of a man as he circled the House. I said: Who is this? They said: It is the False Messiah.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Night Journey: The Prophet meet John, Jesus in heaven
t: Malik ibn Sa’sa’ah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, told them about his Night Journey, saying, “We ascended until we reached the second heaven where Gabriel asked for the gate to be opened, but it was said: Who is it? Gabriel said: I am Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? Gabriel said: It is Muhammad. It was said: Has he been called? Gabriel said yes. When we reached beyond the second heaven, I saw John and Jesus who are cousins. Gabriel said: These are John and Jesus, so greet them with peace. I greeted them with peace and they returned my greeting, saying: Welcome, O righteous brother and prophet.”
q: We ascended until we reached the second heaven where Gabriel asked for the gate to be opened, but it was said: Who is it? Gabriel said: I am Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? Gabriel said: It is Muhammad. It was said: Has he been called? Gabriel said yes. When we reached beyond the second heaven, I saw John and Jesus who are cousins. Gabriel said: These are John and Jesus, so greet them with peace. I greeted them with peace and they returned my greeting, saying: Welcome, O righteous brother and prophet
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Luqman on Life: Knowledge gives life to hearts, like rain on earth
t: Malik reported: Luqman al-Hakim, upon him be peace, instructed his son, saying, “O my son, sit with the scholars and keep close to them. Allah gives life to the hearts with the light of wisdom, just as he gives life to the dead earth with rain from the sky.”
q: O my son, sit with the scholars and keep close to them. Allah gives life to the hearts with the light of wisdom, just as he gives life to the dead earth with rain from the sky.

title: Hadith on Tafsir: The Prophet explains the Quran with the Quran
t: Abdullah reported: When the verse was revealed, “Those who have faith and do not mix their faith with wrong,” (6:82), we said, “O Messenger of Allah, who among us has not mixed his faith with wrong?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is not as you said. They do not mix their faith with the injustice of idolatry. Have you not heard the saying of Luqman to his son: O my son, do not associate anything with Allah, for idolatry is a great injustice?” (31:13)
q: Those who have faith and do not mix their faith with wrong … It is not as you said. They do not mix their faith with the injustice of idolatry. Have you not heard the saying of Luqman to his son: O my son, do not associate anything with Allah, for idolatry is a great injustice?
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sulayman: Wisdom of Solomon, son of David
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There were two women each of whom had a child. A wolf came and took one of their children, so one woman said, ‘It has taken your child!’ The other woman said, ‘No, rather it has taken your child!’ They took their case to David who judged in favor of the older woman. Then, both of them went to Solomon, son of David, and told him about the matter. Solomon said, ‘Bring me a knife. I will cut him into two pieces.’ The younger woman, ‘Do not do it, may Allah have mercy on you! It is her child!’ Thus, Solomon judged in favor of the younger woman.”
q: There were two women each of whom had a child. A wolf came and took one of their children, so one woman said, ‘It has taken your child!’ The other woman said, ‘No, rather it has taken your child!’ They took their case to David who judged in favor of the older woman. Then, both of them went to Solomon, son of David, and told him about the matter. Solomon said, ‘Bring me a knife. I will cut him into two pieces.’ The younger woman, ‘Do not do it, may Allah have mercy on you! It is her child!’ Thus, Solomon judged in favor of the younger woman.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dawud: David only ate what he earned by work
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The recitation of scripture was made easy for David. He would order that his mount be saddled, and he would finish his recitation before they were saddled. He would never eat but from the work of his own hands.”
q: The recitation of scripture was made easy for David. He would order that his mount be saddled, and he would finish his recitation before they were saddled. He would never eat but from the work of his own hands

title: Hadith on Yunus: None should say Muhammad better than Jonah
t:
Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No servant should say that I am better than Jonah son of Mata.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “Whoever says that I am better than Jonah son of Mata has told a lie.”
q: No servant should say that I am better than Jonah son of Mata. … Whoever says that I am better than Jonah son of Mata has told a lie
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ibrahim: First clothed on Judgement Day is Abraham
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The first to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection will be Abraham. Some people among my companions will be taken towards the left side and I will say, ‘My companions! My companions!’ It will be said, ‘They were renegades, turning back on their heels since you left them.’ Then I will say as the righteous servant said, ‘I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them. But when You took me, You were the Witness over them, and You are a Witness over all things. If You punish them, they belong to You after all. But if You forgive them, You are surely the Almighty, All-Wise.’” (5:117-118)
q: The first to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection will be Abraham. Some people among my companions will be taken towards the left side and I will say, ‘My companions! My companions!’ It will be said, ‘They were renegades, turning back on their heels since you left them.’ Then I will say as the righteous servant said, ‘I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them. But when You took me, You were the Witness over them, and You are a Witness over all things. If You punish them, they belong to You after all. But if You forgive them, You are surely the Almighty, All-Wise.’
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Believers’ private conversation with Allah
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A believer will be brought to his Almighty Lord on the Day of Resurrection until He places His veil over him and makes him confess to his sins, saying: Do you acknowledge your sins? The believer will say: My Lord, I do acknowledge them. Allah will say: I concealed them for you in the world and today I forgive you for them. Then, he will be given the record of his good deeds. As for the unbelievers and hypocrites, there will be an announcement before all creation declaring that these people had lied about Allah.”
q: A believer will be brought to his Almighty Lord on the Day of Resurrection until He places His veil over him and makes him confess to his sins, saying: Do you acknowledge your sins? The believer will say: My Lord, I do acknowledge them. Allah will say: I concealed them for you in the world and today I forgive you for them. Then, he will be given the record of his good deeds. As for the unbelievers and hypocrites, there will be an announcement before all creation declaring that these people had lied about Allah.

title: Hadith on Judgment: Allah asks about five things on Judgment Day
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The son of Adam will not be dismissed from his Lord on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about five matters: his life and how he lived it, his youth and how he expended it, his wealth and how he earned it and he spent it, and how he acted upon his knowledge.”
q: The son of Adam will not be dismissed from his Lord on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about five matters: his life and how he lived it, his youth and how he expended it, his wealth and how he earned it and he spent it, and how he acted upon his knowledge.

title: Hadith on Arrogance: Worst Muslims brag, boast, speak too much
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The worst of my nation are the garrulous, the braggarts, and the pompous. The best of my nation are those with the best character.”
q: The worst of my nation are the garrulous, the braggarts, and the pompous. The best of my nation are those with the best character

title: Ibn Umar on Iman: Faith and modesty go together
t: Sa’id ibn Jubary reported: Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, modesty and faith come together. If one of the two is missing, so is the other.”

title: Hadith on Hawd: The Prophet meets believers at the Fountain
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to a graveyard and he said, “Peace be upon you, the abode of a people who had faith. We, if Allah wills, will join you. I love to see our brothers.” They said, “Are we not your brothers, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “You are my companions, but our brothers are those who have yet to come.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize those people from your nation who have not yet been born?” The Prophet said, “Suppose a man had horses with white blazes on their foreheads and legs, among horses that are all black. Tell me, would he not recognize his own horses?” They said, “Of course.” The Prophet said, “They will come with radiant faces, arms, and legs due to the traces of ablution. I will arrive at the fountain before them. Some people will be driven away from my fountain, just as a stray camel is driven away. I will call out: Come! Come! But then it will be said to me: These people changed themselves after you, and I will say: Be off! Be off!”
q: Peace be upon you, the abode of a people who had faith. We, if Allah wills, will join you. I love to see our brothers … You are my companions, but our brothers are those who have yet to come. … Suppose a man had horses with white blazes on their foreheads and legs, among horses that are all black. Tell me, would he not recognize his own horses? … They will come with radiant faces, arms, and legs due to the traces of ablution. I will arrive at the fountain before them. Some people will be driven away from my fountain, just as a stray camel is driven away. I will call out: Come! Come! But then it will be said to me: These people changed themselves after you, and I will say: Be off! Be off!

title: Hadith on Manners: Teach others, do not speak while angry
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Teach others, make things easy, and do not make things difficult. When one of you is angry, he should remain silent.”
q: Teach others, make things easy, and do not make things difficult. When one of you is angry, he should remain silent

title: Hadith on Haya: The Prophet more modest than a young maiden
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was more modest than a virgin in seclusion. If he saw something that he disliked, we would see it on his face.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Anger: Great virtue of controlling, swallowing anger
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is nothing swallowed with a greater reward from Allah than a servant who swallows his rage, seeking thereby the countenance of Allah.”
q: There is nothing swallowed with a greater reward from Allah than a servant who swallows his rage, seeking thereby the countenance of Allah.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Umar on Moderation: Be moderate in your love and hatred
t: Aslam reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Let not your love be infatuation and let not your hatred be destruction.” It was said, “How is this?” Umar said, “When you love someone, you become infatuated like a child. When you hate someone, you love destruction for your companion.”

title: Hadith on Siwak: Using a toothstick before prayer, ablution
t:
Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Were it not a burden upon my nation, I would have ordered them to use the toothstick before every prayer.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “I would have ordered them to use the toothstick with every ablution.”
q: Were it not a burden upon my nation, I would have ordered them to use the toothstick before every prayer … I would have ordered them to use the toothstick with every ablution.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Rape: The Prophet punishes a man who raped a woman
t: Abu Alqama reported: A woman went out to pray during the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and she was met by a man who attacked her and raped her. She screamed and he ran away. Then another man passed by and she said, “This man has molested me!” A group of emigrants were passing by and again she said, “This man has molested me!” They caught the man whom she thought was her attacker and brought him to her and she said, “Yes, this is the one.” They brought him to the Prophet and he issued orders concerning him but the one who had attacked her stood up and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, I am the one who attacked her.” The Prophet said to her, “Go now, for Allah has forgiven you,” and the Prophet said kind words to the man who had been mistakenly arrested. The Prophet said to the man who had attacked her, “Stone him,” and the Prophet said, “Verily, he has repented in such a manner that if the people of Medina were to repent in this way, it would be accepted from them.”
q: Go now, for Allah has forgiven you … Stone … him … Verily, he has repented in such a manner that if the people of Medina were to repent in this way, it would be accepted from them

title: Hadith on Muhammad: Anas describes the appearance of the Prophet
t: Rabi’ah ibn Abdur Rahman reported: I heard Anas ibn Malik describing the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “He was of medium height among people, neither tall nor short. He had a rosy color, neither fully white nor deep brown. His hair was neither completely curly, nor quite lank. Divine inspiration was revealed to him when he was forty years old. He stayed for ten years in Mecca receiving inspiration, and he stayed ten years in Medina. When he passed away, he had less than twenty white hairs on his head and beard.”

title: Hadith on Begging: If you knew how bad it is to beg, no one would do it
t: ‘A’idh ibn ‘Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you knew what it meant to beg, no one would go to anyone else and ask him for anything.”
q: If you knew what it meant to beg, no one would go to anyone else and ask him for anything.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Men and women boast over who is majority in Paradise
t: Muhammad ibn Sirin reported: Some people were boasting, mentioning whether there would be more men or women in Paradise. Abu Huraira said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the first group to enter Paradise will have faces as bright as the full moon at night; the next group will have faces as bright as shining stars in the sky. Every person will have two wives and the marrow of their shanks would glimmer beneath their skin; there will be no one in Paradise without a wife.”
q: Verily, the first group to enter Paradise will have faces as bright as the full moon at night; the next group will have faces as bright as shining stars in the sky. Every person will have two wives and the marrow of their shanks would glimmer beneath their skin; there will be no one in Paradise without a wife
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Work: Earning yourself better than begging
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to carry a bundle of firewood on his back and sell it, that would be better for him than begging a man who may or may not give him anything.”
q: By the One in whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to carry a bundle of firewood on his back and sell it, that would be better for him than begging a man who may or may not give him anything
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Mosques: Virtue of praying at two sacred mosques
t: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except the Sacred Mosque. Prayer in the Sacred Mosque is one hundred times better than prayer in this mosque of mine.”

title: Hadith on Family: Charity given to family has two rewards
t: Salman ibn ‘Amir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Charity given to the poor has one reward, and charity given to family has two rewards: one for charity and one for upholding family ties.”
q: Charity given to the poor has one reward, and charity given to family has two rewards: one for charity and one for upholding family ties.

title: Hadith on Da’wah: The Prophet invites world leaders to Islam
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: Before the passing away of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, he had written to Khosrau, to Casear, to Negus, and to every tyrant, inviting them to Allah. This was not the same Negus for whom the Prophet had performed the funeral prayer.

title: Hadith on Customs: The Prophet’s seal for letters to world leaders
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, intended to write to the Romans, it was said to him, “Indeed, foreigners will not read a letter unless it has a seal.” The Prophet took silver a ring for himself. I remember it as if I were looking at it in the Prophet’s hand, on it was engraved: Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah.

title: Hadith on Manners: Companions shake each other’s hands
t: Qatadah reported: I said to Anas, “Did the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, shake hands?” Anas said, “Yes.”

title: Hadith on Manners: Muslims rewarded for shaking hands
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No two Muslims meet each other and shake hands but that Allah forgives them before they part.”
q: No two Muslims meet each other and shake hands but that Allah forgives them before they part.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Meals: Recommendation to lick fingers, clean plates
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would lick what he ate with his three fingers during a meal, saying, “When one of you drops a mouthful, he should remove any filth from it and then eat it. He should not leave it for the devil.” The Prophet commanded us to wipe clean our dishes, saying, “Verily, you do not know in which portion of your food is the blessing.”
q: When one of you drops a mouthful, he should remove any filth from it and then eat it. He should not leave it for the devil. … Verily, you do not know in which portion of your food is the blessing.

title: Hadith on Charity: Support needy travelers in your group
t: Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, decided to embark on an expedition, saying, “O Muhajirun and Ansar, there are people among you who have no property or family. Let every one of you take along with him two or three men.” There was none of us who had a spare animal, so we took rides by turn. I took two or three men with me, and I rode my camel by with them by turns.
q: O Muhajirun and Ansar, there are people among you who have no property or family. Let every one of you take along with him two or three men.

title: Hadith on Charity: Donate extras to needy travelers
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: While we were traveling with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, he said, “Whoever has a spare mount should give it to one who has no mount. Whoever has spare provisions should give them to one without provision,” and the Prophet mentioned so many kinds of wealth until we thought that none of us had the right to a surplus.
q: Whoever has a spare mount should give it to one who has no mount. Whoever has spare provisions should give them to one without provision,

title: Hadith on Learning: Seeking knowledge an obligation on every Muslim
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim.”
q: Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim.

title: Hadith on Animals: Cutting animals while alive is forbidden
t:
Abu Waqid al-Layth reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whatever is cut from an animal while it is alive is unlawful carrion.”

Al-Tirmidhi said, “This is acted upon by the people of knowledge.”
q: Whatever is cut from an animal while it is alive is unlawful carrion.

title: Hadith on Animals: Fear Allah regarding rights of animals
t: Sahl ibn al-Hanzala reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by a camel whose back had fallen to its stomach. The Prophet said, “Fear Allah regarding these beasts. Ride them while they are healthy, and eat them while they are healthy.”
q: Fear Allah regarding these beasts. Ride them while they are healthy, and eat them while they are healthy.

title: Hadith on Animals: Prohibition of mutilating, torturing animals
t: Abdullah ibn Ja’far reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by some people who were shooting arrows at a ram for target practice. The Prophet disapproved of it, saying, “Do not mutilate your animals.”
q: Do not mutilate your animals

title: Hadith on Carrion: Unlawful to eat an animal used for target practice
t: Abu Tha’labah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “An animal used as a target is not lawful.”
q: An animal used as a target is not lawful.

title: Hadith on Meat: Assume meat of the believers is Halal
t: Aisha reported: Some people among the bedouins would bring us meat and we did not know if the name of Allah was mentioned over it or not. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Mention the name of Allah over it and eat.”
q: Mention the name of Allah over it and eat.

title: Hadith on Animals: Oppressed animals testify on Judgment Day
t: Al-Sharid ibn Suwayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever kills so much as a sparrow unjustly, it will plead to Allah on the Day of Resurrection, saying: O Lord, he killed me unjustly, and he did not kill me for any beneficial purpose!”
q: Whoever kills so much as a sparrow unjustly, it will plead to Allah on the Day of Resurrection, saying: O Lord, he killed me unjustly, and he did not kill me for any beneficial purpose!

title: Hadith on Animals: Whoever kills so much as a small bird
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If someone kills so much as a sparrow, or anything larger, without a just cause, Allah Almighty will ask him about it on the Day of Resurrection.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, what is a just cause?” The Prophet said, “A just cause is that you slaughter it for food, but you should not cut off its head and cast it aside carelessly.”
q: If someone kills so much as a sparrow, or anything larger, without a just cause, Allah Almighty will ask him about it on the Day of Resurrection. … A just cause is that you slaughter it for food, but you should not cut off its head and cast it aside carelessly.

title: Hadith on Animals: The Prophet protects sparrows, ants
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: We were on a journey with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he went out to relieve himself. We saw a red sparrow that had two chicks with her and we took her chicks, so the sparrow started to flap her wings. The Prophet came to us, saying, “Who has upset her by taking her children? Give her children back to her!” The Prophet also saw an ant colony which we had burned, saying, “Who burned this?” We said that we did it. The Prophet said, “No one should punish with fire except the Lord of the fire.”
q: Who has upset her by taking her children? Give her children back to her! … Who burned this? … No one should punish with fire except the Lord of the fire.

title: Hadith on Qiblah: Changing direction of prayer from Jerusalem to Mecca
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to pray towards the Sacred House in Jerusalem, then it was revealed to him, “We have certainly seen you turning your face to the heaven. We will surely turn you to a direction of prayer that will please you. Turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque,” (2:144). A man from the tribe of Salimah passed those who were bowing in dawn prayer, having finished one cycle. The man announced, “Indeed, the direction of prayer has been has been changed!” They moved their direction while in that state.
q: We have certainly seen you turning your face to the heaven. We will surely turn you to a direction of prayer that will please you. Turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque,

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet’s supplication in bowing, prostrating
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would say in his bowing and prostrating, “He is glorified and holy, the Lord of the angels and the spirit.”
q: He is glorified and holy, the Lord of the angels and the spirit

title: Hadith on Witr: The Prophet’s supplication in Witr prayer
t: Ubayy ibn Ka’b reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when he finished his Witr prayer with invocations of peace, he would say, “Glory to the King, the Holy.”
q: Glory to the King, the Holy

title: Hadith on Mecca: The Prophet did not remodel the Ka’bah
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to her, “O Aisha, had your nation not recently left ignorance, I would have had the Ka’bah pulled down and rebuilt to include the portion which had been missing. I would have made it level with the ground, with two doors, one towards the east and the other towards the west. By doing so, it would have been upon the foundation laid by Abraham.”
q: O Aisha, had your nation not recently left ignorance, I would have had the Ka’bah pulled down and rebuilt to include the portion which had been missing. I would have made it level with the ground, with two doors, one towards the east and the other towards the west. By doing so, it would have been upon the foundation laid by Abraham
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Quran: Allah raises or humbles by His Book
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah raises the status of people by this Book, and by it He humbles others.”
q: Verily, Allah raises the status of people by this Book, and by it He humbles others.

title: Hadith on Quran: Reciting Ayat al-Kursi after each prayer
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever recites the ‘verse of the Throne’ after every prescribed prayer, there will be nothing standing between him and entry into Paradise but his death.”
q: Whoever recites the ‘verse of the Throne’ … after every prescribed prayer, there will be nothing standing between him and entry into Paradise but his death.

title: Hadith on Faith: Fear Allah, pray your prayers, obey your leaders
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said in his farewell sermon, “Fear Allah your Lord, pray your five prayers, fast your month of Ramadan, give charity from your wealth, and obey those in authority over you. You will enter the Paradise of your Lord.”
q: Fear Allah your Lord, pray your five prayers, fast your month of Ramadan, give charity from your wealth, and obey those in authority over you. You will enter the Paradise of your Lord

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Beware temptations of the worldly life
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The world is sweet and green. Verily, Allah will make you successors in it to see how you will behave. Beware of the world and beware of women. Verily, the first trial of the children of Israel was with women.”
q: The world is sweet and green. Verily, Allah will make you successors in it to see how you will behave. Beware of the world and beware of women. Verily, the first trial of the children of Israel was with women

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Repentance accepted until deathbed
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah accepts the repentance of his servants, as long as they are not on their death bed.”
q: Verily, Allah accepts the repentance of his servants, as long as they are not on their death bed

title: Hadith on Tawbah: Allah accepts repentance night and day
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty stretches out His hand by night to accept the repentance of those who sin by day, and He stretches out His hand by day to accept the repentance of those who sin by night, until the sun rises from the west.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty stretches out His hand by night to accept the repentance of those who sin by day, and He stretches out His hand by day to accept the repentance of those who sin by night, until the sun rises from the west.

title: Hadith on Tawbah: The Prophet repents one hundred times a day
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O people, turn to Allah in repentance. Verily, I repent to Him one hundred times in a day.”
q: O people, turn to Allah in repentance. Verily, I repent to Him one hundred times in a day.

title: Hadith on Parables: The Prophets like bricks of beautiful house
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the parable of myself and the Prophets before me is that of a man who built a house, perfected it, and beautified it, except for the place of one brick at its cornerstone. The people walk around it and are amazed by it, and they say: Why is this brick not placed? Thus, I am the brick. I am the seal of the Prophets.”
q: Verily, the parable of myself and the Prophets before me is that of a man who built a house, perfected it, and beautified it, except for the place of one brick at its cornerstone. The people walk around it and are amazed by it, and they say: Why is this brick not placed? Thus, I am the brick. I am the seal of the Prophets
gf: Sahih (authentic) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Scriptures: Do not believe or disbelieve people of the Book
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not believe the people of the Book, nor disbelieve them. Say: We have faith in Allah, in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes of Israel, in what was given to Moses and Jesus, and in what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims surrendering to Him.” (2:136)
q: Do not believe the people of the Book, nor disbelieve them. Say: We have faith in Allah, in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes of Israel, in what was given to Moses and Jesus, and in what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims surrendering to Him

title: Hadith on Jihad: Do not wish for war, ask Allah for safety
t: Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa reported: On the days the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, faced the enemy in battle, he waited until the sun had set, then he stood in front of the people. The Prophet said, “O people, do not desire to meet the enemy, but rather ask Allah for safety. If you meet your enemy in battle, be patient and know that Paradise is under the shade of swords.” Then, the Prophet said, “O Allah, the Revealer of the Book, the Mover of the clouds, the Defeater of the confederates! Defeat the unbelievers and grant us victory.”
q: O people, do not desire to meet the enemy, but rather ask Allah for safety. If you meet your enemy in battle, be patient and know that Paradise is under the shade of swords.” … “O Allah, the Revealer of the Book, the Mover of the clouds, the Defeater of the confederates! Defeat the unbelievers and grant us victory
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Health: Best thing after faith is well-being
t: Abu Bakr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You are not given anything after the sincere word of faith like wellness, so ask Allah for wellness.”
q: You are not given anything after the sincere word of faith like wellness, so ask Allah for wellness
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Slaves: Evil masters will not enter Paradise
t: Abu Bakr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The evil custodian will not enter Paradise.”
q: The evil custodian will not enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Injustice: Stop oppressors or be punished altogether
t: Abu Bakr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, if people see an oppressor and they do not seize his hand, Allah will soon send His punishment upon all of them.”
q: Verily, if people see an oppressor and they do not seize his hand, Allah will soon send His punishment upon all of them

title: Hadith on Salat: Virtue of praying in first row of congregation
t: Ubay ibn Ka’b reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the first row of prayer resembles the rows of angels. If you knew its virtue, you would compete for it. The prayer of a man with another man is more purifying than his prayer alone, and his prayer with two men is more purifying than his prayer with one man. The more people there are, the more beloved it is to Allah Almighty.”
q: Verily, the first row of prayer resembles the rows of angels. If you knew its virtue, you would compete for it. The prayer of a man with another man is more purifying than his prayer alone, and his prayer with two men is more purifying than his prayer with one man. The more people there are, the more beloved it is to Allah Almighty

title: Hadith on Qabr: Grave is first stage of the Hereafter
t: Uthman reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the grave is the first stage of the Hereafter. If one is saved from it, whatever comes after will be easier for him. If one is not saved from it, whatever comes after will be harder for him. I have never seen anything more frightening than the grave.”
q: Verily, the grave is the first stage of the Hereafter. If one is saved from it, whatever comes after will be easier for him. If one is not saved from it, whatever comes after will be harder for him … I have never seen anything more frightening than the grave.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Allah keeps believers steadfast in the grave
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The verse, ‘Allah keeps firm those who have faith in the firm word,’ was revealed about the punishment in the grave. It will be said to him: Who is your Lord? He will say: Allah is my Lord and Muhammad is my prophet. That is the meaning of the words of Allah Almighty: Allah keeps firm those who have faith in the firm word, in the worldly life and in the Hereafter.” (14:27)
q: The verse, ‘Allah keeps firm those who have faith in the firm word,’ … was revealed about the punishment in the grave. It will be said to him: Who is your Lord? He will say: Allah is my Lord and Muhammad is my prophet. That is the meaning of the words of Allah Almighty: Allah keeps firm those who have faith in the firm word, in the worldly life and in the Hereafter.”

title: Umar on Justice: Judge Shurayh rules against the Caliph
t: Al-Sha’bi reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, took a horse from a man to test-ride it. The man handed it over and the horse injured its leg while it was with Umar. The man argued with him, so Umar said, “Let a man judge between us.” The man said, “Indeed, I would be satisfied with Shurayh from Iraq.” They went to Shurayh and he said to Umar, “You took it healthy and sound, so you are liable to return it healthy and sound.” Umar was so impressed that he appointed him as a judge.

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Making up missed fasts throughout the year
t: Abu Salamah reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “I had to make up some fasts I missed during the month of Ramadan, but I was unable to do so until the month of Sha’ban as I was busy with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Disease: Infection decreed by Allah, but quarantine needed
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no superstitious infection, but do not mix the sick with the healthy.”
q: do not mix the sick with the healthy

title: Hadith on Honey: The Prophet uses honey to treat upset stomach
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “My brother has diarrhea.” The Prophet said, “Give him honey to drink.” The man gave him honey to drink and he said, “I gave it to him but his diarrhea only got worse.” The Prophet said, “Allah has told the truth and your brother’s stomach is mistaken.” He gave him more honey and he was cured.
q: Give him honey to drink … Allah has told the truth and your brother’s stomach is mistaken
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Smiling: The Prophet would always smile at Jarir
t: Jarir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, never avoided me ever since I embraced Islam. I would never see him but with a smile on his face.

title: Hadith on Smiling: No one smiled more than the Prophet
t: Abdullah ibn al-Harith reported: I have not seen anyone smile more often than the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.

title: Hadith on Manners: Respectful to elders, merciful to children
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever does not show mercy to our young ones, or acknowledge the rights of our elders, he is not one of us.”
q: Whoever does not show mercy to our young ones, or acknowledge the rights of our elders, he is not one of us.

title: Hadith on Vinegar: The Prophet loves vinegar, companions love vinegar
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, took hold of my hand one day and led me to his residence. Some pieces of bread were given to him and the Prophet said, “Are there any condiments?” They said, “None but some vinegar.” The Prophet said, “Verily, vinegar is an excellent condiment.” Jabir said, “I have always loved vinegar ever since I heard this from the Prophet.” Talha said, “I have always loved vinegar ever since I heard this from Jabir.”
q: Are there any condiments? … Verily, vinegar is an excellent condiment

title: Hadith on Khall: The Prophet likes to eat food with vinegar
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of condiments or toppings is vinegar.”
q: The best of condiments or toppings is vinegar

title: Hadith on Intoxicants: Every intoxicant is forbidden no matter how it is made
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent myself and Mu’adh ibn Jabal to Yemen. I said, “O Messenger of Allah, there is a wine in our land prepared from barley known as beer and another wine prepared from honey known as mead.” The Prophet said, “Every intoxicant is unlawful.”
q: Every intoxicant is unlawful

title: Hadith on Hawd: The Prophet recognizes believers at the Fountain
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, my fountain is wider than the distance between Aylah and ‘Adan. Its water is whiter than ice, sweeter than honey and milk. Its cups are more numerous than the stars. Verily, I will block some people from it, just as a man blocks camels from his fountain.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, will you recognize us on that Day?” The Prophet said, “Yes, you will have marks which no one among people will have but you. You will come to me with a blazing forehead and bright hands and feet from the traces of ablution.”
q: Verily, my fountain is wider than the distance between Aylah and ‘Adan. Its water is whiter than ice, sweeter than honey and milk. Its cups are more numerous than the stars. Verily, I will block some people from it, just as a man blocks camels from his fountain. … Yes, you will have marks which no one among people will have but you. You will come to me with a blazing forehead and bright hands and feet from the traces of ablution

title: Hadith on Drinks: The Prophet drinks honey, juice, water, milk
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: I have served the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, from this cup of mine with honey, juice, water, and milk.

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Allah made many ways to give charity
t: Abu Dharr reported: Some of the companions came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and they said, “O Messenger of Allah, the rich have taken all the rewards.
