Indeed, this man is ignorant!” By Allah, Umar would not overlook a verse when it was recited to him, for he strictly adhered to the book of Allah.
q: Show forgiveness, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant

title: Abu Darda on Taqwa: One accepted prayer better than entire world
t: Tamim ibn Malik reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “That I was certain Allah accepted even one prayer from me, it would be more beloved to me than the world and everything in it, for Allah says: Verily, Allah only accepts from those who are righteous.” (5:27)
q: Verily, Allah only accepts from those who are righteous

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Expiation by charity for one who breaks fast
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “I am ruined, O Messenger of Allah!” The Prophet said, “What has ruined you?” The man said, “I was intimate with my wife during Ramadan.” The Prophet said, “Can you find a slave to set free?” He said no. The Prophet said, “Are you able to fast two months in a row?” He said no. The Prophet said, “Can you find sixty poor people to feed?” He said no. Then the man sat down and someone came to the Prophet with a basket of dates. The Prophet said, “Give these dates in charity.” The man said, “Is there anyone poorer than us? There is no family between the two plains of Medina that is poorer than mine.” The Prophet laughed until we could see his back teeth and he said, “Go and feed your family.”
q: What has ruined you? … Can you find a slave to set free? … Are you able to fast two months in a row? … Can you find sixty poor people to feed? … Give these dates in charity … Go and feed your family
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ramadan: A blessed month of mercy, salvation
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said when the month of Ramadan arrived, “The month of Ramadan has come, a blessed month in which Allah Almighty has obligated you to fast. In it the gates of the heavens are opened, the gates of Hellfire are closed, the devils are chained, and in it is a night that is better than a thousand months. Thus, whoever is deprived of its good is truly deprived.”
q: The month of Ramadan has come, a blessed month in which Allah Almighty has obligated you to fast. In it the gates of the heavens are opened, the gates of Hellfire are closed, the devils are chained, and in it is a night that is better than a thousand months. Thus, whoever is deprived of its good is truly deprived.

title: Hadith on Fasting: One who accidentally breaks fast completes it
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever eats or drinks forgetfully while he is fasting, let him complete his fast, for Allah has fed him and given him drink.”
q: Whoever eats or drinks forgetfully while he is fasting, let him complete his fast, for Allah has fed him and given him drink.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fasting: A Muslim who fasts will be distant from Hellfire
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever fasts a day in the way of Allah, Allah will move his face away from the Hellfire by a distance of seventy years.”
q: Whoever fasts a day in the way of Allah, Allah will move his face away from the Hellfire by a distance of seventy years
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fasting: A fasting person must give up bad behavior
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you wakes up in the morning for fasting, then he should not use obscene language or behave foolishly. If anyone abuses him or fights with him, he should say twice: Indeed, I am fasting.”
q: When one of you wakes up in the morning for fasting, then he should not use obscene language or behave foolishly. If anyone abuses him or fights with him, he should say twice: Indeed, I am fasting.

title: Hadith on Fasting: Politely refuse an invitation to eat if fasting
t: Zuhayr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If one of you is invited to a meal while he is fasting, then let him say: Indeed, I am fasting.”
q: If one of you is invited to a meal while he is fasting, then let him say: Indeed, I am fasting.

title: Hadith on Sawm: Hasten to break the fast, delay pre-fasting meal
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “My nation will continue in goodness so long as they hasten to break their fast and prolong the pre-fasting meal.”
q: My nation will continue in goodness so long as they hasten to break their fast and prolong the pre-fasting meal

title: Hadith on Fasting: Help break fast, earn same reward
t: Zayd ibn Khalid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever helps break the fast of a fasting person, he will have the same reward as him without decreasing anything from the reward of the fasting person.”
q: Whoever helps break the fast of a fasting person, he will have the same reward as him without decreasing anything from the reward of the fasting person

title: Hadith on Fasting: Permission to kiss, embrace with no lust when fasting
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would kiss and embrace his wives while fasting, and he had more control over his passions than any of you.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fasting: The Prophet continuously fasted, Muslims may not
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would observe continuous fasting during the month of Ramadan and so did the people, but he prohibited them. It was said, “You are continuously fasting.” The Prophet said, “Verily, I am not like you, for I am supplied with food and drink from Allah.”
q: Verily, I am not like you, for I am supplied with food and drink from Allah.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ramadan: New moon begins and ends Ramadan
t:
Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not fast the month of Ramadan until you see the crescent moon, and do not break your fast until you see it. If the sky is cloudy for you, then estimate it.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “If the sky is cloudy for you, then complete the term as thirty days.”
q: Do not fast the month of Ramadan until you see the crescent moon, and do not break your fast until you see it. If the sky is cloudy for you, then estimate it. … If the sky is cloudy for you, then complete the term as thirty days
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Do not fast days before Ramadan, unless a routine
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Let not one of you precede Ramadan with one or two days of fasting, unless it is part of a man’s fasting routine, so let him fast that day.”
q: Let not one of you precede Ramadan with one or two days of fasting, unless it is part of a man’s fasting routine, so let him fast that day
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Abu Darda on Sinners: Hate his sinful deeds, do not abuse him
t: Abu Qilaba reported: Abu Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by a man who was being beaten because of his sin and they were cursing him. Abu Darda said, “What do you think if he had fallen into a well. Would you not try to rescue him?” They said yes. Abu Darda said, “Then do not abuse your brother, and praise Allah who has protected you from sin.” They said, “Do you not hate him?” Abu Darda said, “Verily, I only hate his sinful deed, but if he leaves it then he is still my brother.”

title: Hadith on Sawm: Supplication at breaking fast is never rejected
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the supplication of a fasting person is not turned away at the time of breaking fast .” Abdullah would say when breaking fast, “O Allah, I ask You by You mercy, which encompasses all things, to forgive me.”
q: Verily, the supplication of a fasting person is not turned away at the time of breaking fast .

title: Hadith on Iftar: Breaking fast with dates and water
t: Salman ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you breaks his fast, let him break it with dates for they are blessed. If they are not found, let him break it with water for it is pure.”
q: When one of you breaks his fast, let him break it with dates for they are blessed. If they are not found, let him break it with water for it is pure.

title: Hadith on Fasting: The Prophet’s supplication upon breaking his fast
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would say upon breaking the fast, “Gone is the thirst, quenched are the veins, and assured is the reward if Allah wills.”
q: Gone is the thirst, quenched are the veins, and assured is the reward if Allah wills.

title: Hadith on Mothers: Be good to your mother, Paradise under her feet
t: Mu’awiyah ibn Jahima reported: Jahima came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, I intend to join the military expedition, and I seek your counsel.” The Prophet said, “Do you have a mother?” He said yes. The Prophet said, “Stay with her, for Paradise is beneath her feet.”
q: Do you have a mother? … Stay with her, for Paradise is beneath her feet.

title: Hadith on Hijab: Modest woman only reveal face, hands
t: Aisha reported: Asma’ bint Abi Bakr entered the house of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while she was wearing a thin garment and she showed it to him. The Prophet said, “O Asma, when a woman reaches the age of maturity, it is not proper for her to show anything but this and this,” and the Prophet pointed to his face and hands.
q: O Asma, when a woman reaches the age of maturity, it is not proper for her to show anything but this and this,
gf: Hasan li ghayri (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Zakat al-Fitr at end of Ramadan
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, obligated payment of charity at the end of Ramadan, a portion of dates or barley, upon slave and freeman, male and female, young and old among the Muslims. The Prophet ordered it to be given before people go out for Eid prayer.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Reward of fasting and praying in Ramadan
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever fasts the month of Ramadan due to faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven. Whoever stands in prayer during the Night of Decree due to faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven.”
q: Whoever fasts the month of Ramadan due to faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven. Whoever stands in prayer during the Night of Decree due to faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Save yourself from Hell, even with small charity
t: ‘Adi ibn Hatim reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Guard yourself against the Hellfire, even with half of a date in charity. If one cannot find it, then with a kind word.”
q: Guard
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Leniency: Man rewarded for easy business, relieving debt
t: Abu Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man among those before you was called to account in the Hereafter. Nothing good was found with him but that he was lenient in his dealings with people, and he would order his servant to relieve the debts of those in hardship. Allah Almighty said: We are more worthy of such actions, so overlook his sins.”
q: A man among those before you was called to account in the Hereafter. Nothing good was found with him but that he was lenient in his dealings with people, and he would order his servant to relieve the debts of those in hardship. Allah Almighty said: We are more worthy of such actions, so overlook his sins

title: Hadith on Nifaq: Allah exposes hypocrites on Judgment Day
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the first people to be judged on the Day of Resurrection will be a man who was martyred. He will be brought, the blessings of Allah will be made known, and he will acknowledge them. Allah will say: What did you do with them? The man will say: I fought in Your cause until I was martyred. Allah will say: You have lied, for you fought only that it would be said you were brave, thus it was said. Then, Allah will order him to be dragged upon his face until he is cast into Hellfire. Another man studied religious knowledge, taught others, and recited the Quran. He will be brought, the blessings of Allah will be made known, and he will acknowledge them. Allah will say: What did you do with them? The man will say: I learned religious knowledge, taught others, and I recited the Quran for Your sake. Allah will say: You have lied, for you studied only that it would be said you are a scholar and you recited the Quran only that it would be said you are a reciter, thus it was said. Then, Allah will order him to be dragged upon his face until he is cast into Hellfire. Another man was given an abundance of blessings from Allah and every kind of wealth. He will be brought, the blessings of Allah will be made known, and he will acknowledge them. Allah will say: What did you do with them? The man will say: I did not leave any good cause beloved to You but that I spent on it for Your sake. Allah will say: You have lied, for you spent only that it would be said you are generous, thus it was said. Then, Allah will order him to be dragged upon his face until he is cast into Hellfire.”
q: Verily, the first people to be judged on the Day of Resurrection will be a man who was martyred. He will be brought, the blessings of Allah will be made known, and he will acknowledge them. Allah will say: What did you do with them? The man will say: I fought in Your cause until I was martyred. Allah will say: You have lied, for you fought only that it would be said you were brave, thus it was said. Then, Allah will order him to be dragged upon his face until he is cast into Hellfire. Another man studied religious knowledge, taught others, and recited the Quran. He will be brought, the blessings of Allah will be made known, and he will acknowledge them. Allah will say: What did you do with them? The man will say: I learned religious knowledge, taught others, and I recited the Quran for Your sake. Allah will say: You have lied, for you studied only that it would be said you are a scholar and you recited the Quran only that it would be said you are a reciter, thus it was said. Then, Allah will order him to be dragged upon his face until he is cast into Hellfire. Another man was given an abundance of blessings from Allah and every kind of wealth. He will be brought, the blessings of Allah will be made known, and he will acknowledge them. Allah will say: What did you do with them? The man will say: I did not leave any good cause beloved to You but that I spent on it for Your sake. Allah will say: You have lied, for you spent only that it would be said you are generous, thus it was said. Then, Allah will order him to be dragged upon his face until he is cast into Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Astrology: Whoever has faith in stars, disbelieves in Allah
t: Zayd ibn Khalid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: Among My servants are those who awaken with faith in Me and disbelief in Me. Whoever said we have been given rain due to the favor and mercy of Allah, he is a believer in Me and an unbeliever in the stars. Whoever said we have been given rain due to the rising of this star, he has disbelieved in Me and has put his faith in the stars.”
q: Allah Almighty said: Among My servants are those who awaken with faith in Me and disbelief in Me. Whoever said we have been given rain due to the favor and mercy of Allah, he is a believer in Me and an unbeliever in the stars. Whoever said we have been given rain due to the rising of this star, he has disbelieved in Me and has put his faith in the stars
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Son of Adam tells a lie against Me
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: The son of Adam has lied against me and he has no right to do so, he has insulted me and he has no right to do so. As for his lie, it is his saying that I cannot recreate him as I did before. As for his insult, it is his saying that I have a son; I am glorified above taking a wife or a son.”
q: Allah Almighty said: The son of Adam has lied against me and he has no right to do so, he has insulted me and he has no right to do so. As for his lie, it is his saying that I cannot recreate him as I did before. As for his insult, it is his saying that I have a son; I am glorified above taking a wife or a son

title: Umar II on Faith: Islam is fulfilled by duties, limits, traditions
t: Al-Bukhari reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, faith consists of obligations, laws, limits, and traditions. Whoever perfects them has perfected faith, and whoever does not perfect them will not have perfect faith.”

title: Umar II on Da’wah: The Prophet is caller to Allah, not tax collector
t: Ibn Kathir reported: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Verily, Allah has only sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, as a preacher. He did not send him as a tax collector.”

title: Hadith on Sunnah: Trimming moustache, letting beard grow
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be different from the idolaters. Let the beard grow and trim the moustache.” Whenever Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, performed the Hajj or Umrah pilgrimage, he would grab hold of his beard and cut what was beyond his grasp.
q: Be different from the idolaters. Let the beard grow and trim the moustache
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hatim on Debate: I have good will towards my opponents
t: Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi reported: Hatim al-Asamm, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “I have three traits that give me an advantage over my adversary. I rejoice when he is correct, I am saddened when he is wrong, and I guard myself from insulting him.”

title: Nasafi on Ikhtilaf: Our way is correct, but could be wrong
t: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami reported: Imam al-Nasafi, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “When we are asked about our way and the way of those who disagree with us in the branches of the religion, it obligatory for us to answer that our way is correct but could be mistaken, and their way is mistaken but could be correct.”

title: Shafi’i on Provisions: Best provision is fear of Allah, worst is aggression
t: Al-Bayhaqi reported: Al-Shafi’i, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “The most beneficial of provisions is the fear of Allah, and the most harmful of provisions is aggression.”

title: Hadith on Salat: First deed to be judged is prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The first action for which a servant of Allah will be held accountable on the Day of Resurrection will be his prayers. If they are in order, he will have prospered and succeeded. If they are lacking, he will have failed and lost. If there is something defective in his obligatory prayers, then the Almighty Lord will say: See if My servant has any voluntary prayers that can complete what is insufficient in his obligatory prayers. The rest of his deeds will be judged the same way.”
q: The first action for which a servant of Allah will be held accountable on the Day of Resurrection will be his prayers. If they are in order, he will have prospered and succeeded. If they are lacking, he will have failed and lost. If there is something defective in his obligatory prayers, then the Almighty Lord will say: See if My servant has any voluntary prayers that can complete what is insufficient in his obligatory prayers. The rest of his deeds will be judged the same way

title: Hadith on Salat: Allah delights in one who prays, fears Him
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Your Lord delights in a shepherd who announces the call to prayer on the peak of a mountain and he prays. Allah Almighty says: Behold My servant who calls to prayer, performs prayer, and fears Me. I have forgiven My servant and admitted him into Paradise.”
q: Your Lord delights in a shepherd who announces the call to prayer on the peak of a mountain and he prays. Allah Almighty says: Behold My servant who calls to prayer, performs prayer, and fears Me. I have forgiven My servant and admitted him into Paradise.

title: Hadith on Prayer: Allah responds to Surat al-Fatihah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: I have divided prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves, and My servant shall have what he has asked for. When the servant says, ‘All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds,’ Allah says, ‘My servant has praised Me.’ When he says, ‘The Gracious, the Merciful,’ Allah says, ‘My servant has exalted Me.’ When he says, ‘The Master of the Day of Judgment,’ Allah says, ‘My servant has glorified Me, and My servant has submitted to Me.’ When he says, ‘You alone we worship, You alone we ask for help,’ Allah says, ‘This is between Me and My servant, and My servant will have what he has asked for.’ When he says, ‘Guide us to the straight path, the path of those whom you have favored, not those who earned wrath and went astray,’ Allah says, This is for My servant, and My servant will have what he has asked for.’”
q: Allah Almighty said: I have divided prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves, and My servant shall have what he has asked for. When the servant says, ‘All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds,’ Allah says, ‘My servant has praised Me.’ When he says, ‘The Gracious, the Merciful,’ Allah says, ‘My servant has exalted Me.’ When he says, ‘The Master of the Day of Judgment,’ Allah says, ‘My servant has glorified Me, and My servant has submitted to Me.’ When he says, ‘You alone we worship, You alone we ask for help,’ Allah says, ‘This is between Me and My servant, and My servant will have what he has asked for.’ When he says, ‘Guide us to the straight path, the path of those whom you have favored, not those who earned wrath and went astray,’ Allah says, This is for My servant, and My servant will have what he has asked for.’

title: Hadith on Charity: Feed hungry, visit sick, emancipate slaves
t: Abu Musa al-Asha’ri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Feed the hungry, visit the sick, and set the captives free.”
q: Feed the hungry, visit the sick, and set the captives free.

title: Ibrahim on Love: Hate the sin, compassion for sinners
t: Ibrahim ibn Adham reported: We were passing through some cities and I saw two people among the ascetics on a journey. One of them said to the other, “O brother, what do the people who love Allah inherit from their beloved?” The other said, “They inherit insight from the light of Allah the Exalted and compassion for those who disobey Allah.” I said, “How can he have compassion for people who contradict their beloved?” He looked to me and said, “They abhor their sinful deeds and have compassion for them that by their admonition they might leave their deeds, and they feel sympathy that their bodies might be burned in Hellfire. The believer is not truly a believer until he is pleased for people to have what he is pleased for himself.” Then they left and I never saw them again.

title: Hasan on Rebellion: Rush to their swords, left to their swords
t: ‘Umar ibn Yazid reported: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “If people had patience when they are afflicted with trials from their ruler, it would not be long before Allah relieves them of it. Yet, they take refuge in their swords, so they are left to their swords. By Allah, not even for a single day did they bring about any good.” Then, he recited the verse, “The good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because they had patiently endured, and We destroyed everything Pharaoh and his people were building and constructing.” (7:137)
q: The good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because they had patiently endured, and We destroyed everything Pharaoh and his people were building and constructing.

title: Ibn Taymiyyah on ‘Adl: Allah helps a just government, even by unbelievers
t: Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “It is said that Allah allows the just state to remain even if it is led by unbelievers, but Allah will not allow the oppressive state to remain even if it is led by Muslims. And it is said that the world will endure with justice and unbelief, but it will not endure with oppression and Islam.”

title: Ibn Qayyim on Sharia: Islam is based on justice, mercy, wisdom
t: Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said, “Verily, the Sharia is founded upon wisdom and welfare for the servants in this life and the afterlife. In its entirety it is justice, mercy, benefit, and wisdom. Every matter which abandons justice for tyranny, mercy for cruelty, benefit for corruption, and wisdom for foolishness is not a part of the Sharia even if it was introduced therein by an interpretation.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Kufr: Contradicting the Sharia is lesser unbelief
t: Al-Tabari reported: A man asked Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, about this verse, “Whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the unbelievers,” (5.44). The man said, “Has one who does this committed unbelief?” Ibn Abbas said, “It is a type of unbelief if he does that, but it is not like one who disbelieves in Allah, the Last Day, and so on.”
q: Whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the unbelievers

title: Ali on Justice: Caliph rules in favor of a Christian
t: Al-Sha’bi reported: Ali ibn Abi Talib saw a Christian man wearing his lost armor and he decided to take up the matter legally, so he brought the dispute to the judge Shurayh. Ali said, “This is my armor and I have not sold it or given it away.” The judge said to the Christian, “What do you say about what the commander of the faithful has said?” The Christian said, “It is my armor, but I do not consider the commander of the faithful to be a liar.” The judge turned to Ali and he said, “O commander of the faithful, do you have proof?” Ali laughed and he said, “Shurayh is correct. I do not have proof.” Thus, the judge ruled in favor of the Christian. The Christian took the armor and began to walk away, but then he returned and he said, “As for me, I testify that this is the wisdom of the prophets. The commander of the faithful himself has taken me to his judge and the judge has ruled against him! I testify that there is no God but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. By Allah, the armor is yours. I followed the army while you were on your way to Siffin and the armor fell from your luggage.” Ali said, “If you have embraced Islam, the armor is yours.”

title: Hadith on Law: Allah has made duties, limits, do not transgress
t: Abu Tha’laba reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has made duties obligatory, do not neglect them. He has set limits, do not transgress them. He has made some things sacred, do no violate them. He has remained silent upon matters as mercy for you, not out of forgetfulness, so do not search them out.”
q: Verily, Allah has made duties obligatory, do not neglect them. He has set limits, do not transgress them. He has made some things sacred, do no violate them. He has remained silent upon matters as mercy for you, not out of forgetfulness, so do not search them out.

title: Hadith on Adam: All people are the children of Adam
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has removed from you the pride of the time of ignorance, with its boasting of ancestors, for one can only be a righteous believer or a miserable evildoer. All of the people are the children of Adam, and Adam was created from dust.”
q: Verily, Allah has removed from you the pride of the time of ignorance, with its boasting of ancestors, for one can only be a righteous believer or a miserable evildoer. All of the people are the children of Adam, and Adam was created from dust.

title: Hadith on Tyranny: Patience with unjust rulers until you meet the Prophet
t: Usayd ibn Hudayr reported: A man among the Ansar took aside the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “Will you not appoint me leader as you have appointed others?” The Prophet said, “Verily, you will see favoritism after me, so be patient until you meet me at the Fountain.”
q: Verily, … you will see favoritism after me, so be patient until you meet me at the Fountain.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tyrants: The Prophet orders patience with unjust rulers
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, after me there will be undue favoritism and matters you will reject.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you order us to do if we reach that time?” The Prophet said, “Fulfill the duties placed over you and ask Allah for what belongs to you.”
q: Verily, after me there will be undue favoritism and matters you will reject. … Fulfill the duties placed over you and ask Allah for what belongs to you
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Love: Marriage best for those who love each other
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “We do not see for those who love one another anything like marriage.”
q: We do not see for those who love one another anything like marriage.

title: Hadith on Conscience: Consult your heart on righteousness, sin
t: Wabisah ibn Ma’bad reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “Have you come to ask about righteousness and sin?” I said yes. The Prophet clenched his fist and struck his chest, saying, “Consult your soul, consult your heart, O Wabisah. Righteousness is what reassures your soul and your heart, and sin is what wavers in your soul and puts tension in your chest, even if people approve it in their judgments again and again.”
q: Have you come to ask about righteousness and sin … Consult your soul, consult your heart, O Wabisah. Righteousness is what reassures your soul and your heart, and sin is what wavers in your soul and puts tension in your chest, even if people approve it in their judgments again and again

title: Hadith on Muhammad: Bless the Prophet once, Allah blesses you ten times
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah will send blessings upon him ten times.”
q: Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah will send blessings upon him ten times.

title: Hadith on Islam: Embrace Islam, even if you dislike it
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to a man, “Embrace Islam.” The man said, “I find that I dislike it.” The Prophet said, “Embrace Islam, even if you dislike it.”
q: Embrace Islam … Embrace Islam, even if you dislike it

title: Hadith on Rights: All people have a right to basic life-needs
t: Uthman ibn Affan reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no right for the son of Adam other than these things: a house in which he lives, a garment to cover his nakedness, a piece of bread, and water.”
q: There is no right for the son of Adam other than these things: a house in which he lives, a garment to cover his nakedness, a piece of bread, and water.

title: Hadith on Reliance: Must work for provision like the birds
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you were to rely upon Allah with reliance due to Him, He would provide for you just as He provides for the birds. They go out in the morning with empty stomachs and return full.”
q: If you were to rely upon Allah with reliance due to Him, He would provide for you just as He provides for the birds. They go out in the morning with empty stomachs and return full.

title: Hadith on Trust: People with hearts like birds enter Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “People whose hearts are like the hearts of birds will enter Paradise.”
q: People whose hearts are like the hearts of birds will enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Trust: Abraham and Muhammad rely upon Allah
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Abraham, upon him be peace, said when he was thrown into the fire, “Allah is enough for us, and excellent is he as the guardian,” and it was likewise said by Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, when they said, “Verily, the people have gathered against you, so fear them. It only increased their faith and they said: Allah is enough for us, and excellent is he as the guardian.” (3:173)
q: Allah is enough for us, and excellent is he as the guardian … Verily, the people have gathered against you, so fear them. It only increased their faith and they said: Allah is enough for us, and excellent is he as the guardian

title: Hadith on Recitation: Quran should not be recited too quickly
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One has not understood the Quran if he reads it in less than three days.”
q: One has not understood the Quran if he reads it in less than three days

title: Hadith on Humanity: Allah created all people from Adam
t: Abu Musa al-Ashari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty created Adam from a handful which He took from the earth, so the children of Adam come in accordance with the earth. Some come with red skin, white skin, or black skin, and whatever is in between: smooth and rough, bad and good.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty created Adam from a handful which He took from the earth, so the children of Adam come in accordance with the earth. Some come with red skin, white skin, or black skin, and whatever is in between: smooth and rough, bad and good.

title: Hadith on Salat: The Prophet’s first supplication for night prayer
t: Aisha reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would stand for prayer at night, he would begin by saying, “O Allah, the Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Israfel, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You judge between Your servants in that over which they differ. Guide me, by Your will, in what they differ regarding the truth. Verily, You guide whomever You will to the straight path.”
q: O Allah, the Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Israfel, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You judge between Your servants in that over which they differ. Guide me, by Your will, in what they differ regarding the truth. Verily, You guide whomever You will to the straight path

title: Hadith on Janazah: Miscarried fetus is given a funeral prayer
t: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “The rider should travel behind the funeral procession, and those on foot should walk behind it, in front, to the right or to the left, near to it. The funeral prayer should be offered over the miscarried fetus, and supplications for forgiveness and mercy should be made for the parents.”
q: The rider should travel behind the funeral procession, and those on foot should walk behind it, in front, to the right or to the left, near to it. The funeral prayer should be offered over the miscarried fetus, and supplications for forgiveness and mercy should be made for the parents

title: Hadith on Warning: The Prophet sent to warn of divine punishment
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ascended mount Al-Safa one day and he called out, “O people! Come at once!” The Quraysh gathered before him, and the Prophet said, “Verily, I have been sent to warn you of a severe punishment before you. If I told you an enemy was preparing to attack you this morning or evening, would you believe me?” Abu Lahab said, “Is it for this you have called us? May you perish!” Then, Allah revealed the verse, “Perish the hand of Abu Lahab!” (111:1)
q: O people! Come at once! … Verily, I have been sent to warn you of a severe punishment before you. … If I told you an enemy was preparing to attack you this morning or evening, would you believe me? … Perish the hand of Abu Lahab!

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Best of you are best to their families
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of you are the best to their families, and I am the best to my family. When your companion dies, then do not abuse him.”
q: The best of you are the best to their families, and I am the best to my family. When your companion dies, then do not abuse him

title: Hadith on Hijab: Allah reveals verse for women to veil
t: ‘Urwah reported: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “May Allah have mercy on the foremost women of the Muhajirun. When Allah revealed the verse, ‘Let them draw their cloaks over their bodies,’ (24:31) they cut their sheets and veiled themselves with them.”
q: Let them draw their cloaks over their bodies

title: Hadith on Idolatry: Those who made graves into places of worship
t:
Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said during his illness from which he did not recover, “Allah has cursed the Jews and Christians, who have taken the graves of their prophets as places of worship.”

Aisha said, “Were it not for that, his grave would have been in a prominent place, but it was feared that it would be taken as a place of worship.”
q: Allah has cursed the Jews and Christians, who have taken the graves of their prophets as places of worship
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Favor: Good deeds multiplied by the grace of Allah
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has recorded good and evil deeds and He made them clear. Whoever intends to perform a good deed but does not do it, Allah will record it as a complete good deed. If he intends to do it and does so, Allah Almighty will record it as ten good deeds, up to seven hundred times as much or even more. If he intends to do an evil deed and does not do it, Allah will record for him one complete good deed. If he does it, Allah will record for him a single evil deed.”
q: Verily, Allah has recorded good and evil deeds and He made them clear. Whoever intends to perform a good deed but does not do it, Allah will record it as a complete good deed. If he intends to do it and does so, Allah Almighty will record it as ten good deeds, up to seven hundred times as much or even more. If he intends to do an evil deed and does not do it, Allah will record for him one complete good deed. If he does it, Allah will record for him a single evil deed
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Haya: One without shame does whatever he pleases
t: Abu Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among the words people obtained from the Prophets are this: If you feel no shame, do as you wish.”
q: Verily, among the words people obtained from the Prophets are this: If you feel no shame, do as you wish

title: Hadith on Tawheed: Must reject false gods to complete faith
t:
Tariq ibn Ashyam reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever says there is no God but Allah, and disbelieves in what is worshiped besides Allah, his property and his life are sacred and he will be held accountable to Allah.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “Whoever declares Allah is one…”
q: Whoever says there is no God but Allah, and disbelieves in what is worshiped besides Allah, his property and his life are sacred and he will be held accountable to Allah

title: Hadith on Signs: False prophets, idol worship are signs of the Hour
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hour will not be established until tribes from my nation join the idolaters and they worship idols. Verily, there will be thirty liars among my nation, all of them claiming to be a prophet, but I am the seal of the Prophets. There is no prophet after me.”
q: The Hour will not be established until tribes from my nation join the idolaters and they worship idols. Verily, there will be thirty liars

title: Hadith on Islam: Perfection in Islam to mind your own business
t: ‘Ali ibn Husayn reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among excellence in Islam is for a man to leave what does not concern him.”
q: Verily, among excellence in Islam is for a man to leave what does not concern him.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Favor: Allah multiplies good deeds for believers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you practices Islam well, every good deed he does is written as ten good deeds up to seven hundred times as much, and every bad deed he does is written as one bad deed until he meets Allah.”
q: When one of you practices Islam well, every good deed he does is written as ten good deeds up to seven hundred times as much, and every bad deed he does is written as one bad deed until he meets Allah.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Nothing greater than to testify Allah is One
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Moses said: My Lord, teach me something with which I can remember You and call upon You. Allah said: Say ‘there is no God but Allah.’ Moses said: My Lord, all of Your servants say this. Allah said: O Moses, if the seven heavens with their inhabitants, as well as the seven earths, were upon a scale against the statement ‘there is no God but Allah,’ then ‘there is no God but Allah’ would outweigh them.”
q: Moses said: My Lord, teach me something with which I can remember You and call upon You. Allah said: Say ‘there is no God but Allah.’ Moses said: My Lord, all of Your servants say this. Allah said: O Moses, if the seven heavens with their inhabitants, as well as the seven earths, were upon a scale against the statement ‘there is no God but Allah,’ then ‘there is no God but Allah’ would outweigh them.

title: Hadith on Eisa: Whoever testifies that Jesus is the servant of Allah
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever testifies that there is no God but Allah alone without any partners, that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, that Jesus is the servant of Allah and His Messenger, His word which He bestowed upon Mary and a spirit from Him, and that Paradise is the truth and Hellfire is the truth, then Allah will admit him into Paradise by whatever good deeds he had done.”
q: Whoever testifies that there is no God but Allah alone without any partners, that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, that Jesus is the servant of Allah and His Messenger, His word which He bestowed upon Mary and a spirit from Him, and that Paradise is the truth and Hellfire is the truth, then Allah will admit him into Paradise by whatever good deeds he had done.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Justice: No collective punishment, unjust killing
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not return to unbelief after me by striking the necks of each other. No man is to be punished for the crimes of his father or his brother.”
q: Do not return to unbelief after me by striking the necks of each other. No man is to be punished for the crimes of his father or his brother.

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Two Muslims fighting are both in Hell
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If two Muslims confront each other with swords, both the killer and the killed will be in Hellfire.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, we understand for the killer, but why for the one killed?” The Prophet said, “Verily, he intended to kill his companion.”
q: If two Muslims confront each other with swords, both the killer and the killed will be in Hellfire … Verily, he intended to kill his companion.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Shahid: Killed defending from injustice is a martyr
t: Suwayd ibn Muqarrin reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is killed defending himself from injustice is a martyr.”
q: Whoever is killed defending himself from injustice is a martyr

title: Hadith on Dreams: Good dreams of believers part of prophecy
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the end of time approaches, the dream of a believer can hardly be false. The dream of a believer is one of forty-six parts of prophecy, and whatever is from prophecy does not lie.”
q: When the end of time approaches, the dream of a believer can hardly be false. The dream of a believer is one of forty-six parts of prophecy, and whatever is from prophecy does not lie
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Visions: Good dreams from Allah, bad dreams from Satan
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you sees a dream he likes, it is from Allah, so let him praise Allah for it and speak about it. When one of you sees something he dislikes, it is from Satan, so let him seek refuge from its evil and not mention it to anyone. It will not harm him.”
q: When one of you sees a dream he likes, it is from Allah, so let him praise Allah for it and speak about it. When one of you sees something he dislikes, it is from Satan, so let him seek refuge from its evil and not mention it to anyone. It will not harm him.

title: Hadith on Salat: Supplications at end of prayer, never deprived
t: Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are ending statements that never deprive one who said them: glorifying Allah thirty-three times after every prayer, praising Him thirty-three times, and exalting Him thirty four-times.”
q: There are ending statements that never deprive one who said them: glorifying Allah thirty-three times after every prayer, praising Him thirty-three times, and exalting Him thirty four-times.

title: Hadith on Khutbah: Not allowed to speak during Friday Sermon
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you tell your companion to be quiet on Friday while the Imam is speaking, you have spoken improperly.”
q: If you tell your companion to be quiet on Friday while the Imam is speaking, you have spoken improperly.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ghusl: Perform ritual bath before Friday prayer
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Taking a bath on Friday is a duty upon every person who has reached the age of puberty.”
q: Taking a bath on Friday is a duty upon every person who has reached the age of puberty.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jihad: Women participate in defense of Islam
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would go into battle with Umm Sulaym and a group of women with her from the Ansar; they would give water and tend to the wounded.

title: Hadith on Shahid: Killed defending his life is a martyr
t: Sa’id ibn Zayd reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is killed protecting his property is a martyr. Whoever is killed protecting his religion is a martyr. Whoever is killed protecting his life is a martyr. Whoever is killed protecting his family is a martyr.”
q: Whoever is killed protecting his property is a martyr. Whoever is killed protecting his religion is a martyr. Whoever is killed protecting his life is a martyr. Whoever is killed protecting his family is a martyr

title: Hadith on Poetry: Some poetry is truthful, praiseworthy
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most truthful word ever spoken by an Arab poet is the saying of Labid: Everything besides Allah is in vain.”
q: The most truthful word ever spoken by an Arab poet is the saying of Labid: Everything besides Allah is in vain

title: Hadith on Shi’r: Wasting time memorizing vain peotry
t: Sa’d reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “That one of you fills his belly with puss is better than filling it with vain poetry.”
q: hat one of you fills his belly with puss is better than filling it with vain poetry.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Shi’r: The Prophet listens to a hundred verses of poetry
t: Al-Sharid ibn Suwayd reported: I was riding with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, one day and he said, “Do you havee anything of the poetry of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt?” I said yes. The Prophet said, “Carry on.” I recited a couplet and the Prophet said, “Carry on.” Then I recited another couplet and the Prophet said, “Carry on,” until I recited one hundred couplets.
q: Carry on. … Carry on … Carry on,

title: Hadith on Justice: Tremendous responsibility of being a Judge
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever accepts an appointment as a judge, it is as if he has been slaughtered without a knife.”
q: Whoever accepts an appointment as a judge, it is as if he has been slaughtered without a knife

title: Hadith on Justice: Parents must be fair with their children
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be just between your children. Be just between your children.”
q: Be just between your children. Be just between your children

title: Hadith on Fatwa: Sin falls upon one who issued ignorant judgment
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is given an opinion not based on knowledge, his sin falls upon the one who gave him the opinion. Whoever directs his brother to a matter of which he knows good lies elsewhere, he has betrayed him.”
q: Whoever is given an opinion not based on knowledge, his sin falls upon the one who gave him the opinion … Whoever directs his brother to a matter of which he knows good lies elsewhere, he has betrayed him.

title: Hadith on Oaths: Swearing by other than Allah an act of idolatry
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever swears by other than Allah has committed an act of idolatry.”
q: Whoever swears by other than Allah has committed an act of idolatry.

title: Hadith on Habits: Good routines rewarded even if sick or traveling
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a servant falls ill or travels, the likes of what he used to do when he was settled and healthy will be recorded for him.”
q: If a servant falls ill or travels, the likes of what he used to do when he was settled and healthy will be recorded for him.

title: Hadith on Sickness: Fever expiates sins, just as fire purifies gold
t: Umm al-Ala reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, visited me when I was sick, and he said, “Be cheerful, O mother of al-Ala. When a Muslim is sick, Allah takes away his sins just as fire takes away impurities in gold and silver.”
q: Be cheerful, O mother of al-Ala. When a Muslim is sick, Allah takes away his sins just as fire takes away impurities in gold and silver

title: Hadith on Forgiveness: A humble sinner, an arrogant worshiper
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two men among the children of Israel were the opposite of each other. One of them was a sinner and the other would strive in worship. The worshiper would see the sinner and tell him to stop. One day he found him sinning so he said: Stop! The sinner said: Leave me alone, by my Lord, have you been sent to watch over me? The worshiper said: By Allah, Allah will not forgive you or admit you into Paradise! Later their souls were taken and they met in the presence of the Lord of the worlds. Allah said to the worshiper: Did you have knowledge of Me or power over what is in My hand? Allah said to the sinner: Enter Paradise by My mercy. And Allah said to the worshiper: Take him to the Hellfire.” Abu Huraira said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, he spoke a word which ruined him in this world and the Hereafter.”
q: Two men among the children of Israel were the opposite of each other. One of them was a sinner and the other would strive in worship. The worshiper would see the sinner and tell him to stop. One day he found him sinning so he said: Stop! The sinner said: Leave me alone, by my Lord, have you been sent to watch over me? The worshiper said: By Allah, Allah will not forgive you or admit you into Paradise! Later their souls were taken … and they met in the presence of the Lord of the worlds. Allah said to the worshiper: Did you have knowledge of Me or power over what is in My hand? Allah said to the sinner: Enter Paradise by My mercy. And Allah said to the worshiper: Take him to the Hellfire

title: Hadith on Zina: Accusers must bring proof, or be punished
t: Ibn Abbas reported: Hilal ibn Umayyah was with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he accused his wife of adultery with Sharik ibn Sahma. The Prophet said, “Bring proof, otherwise the punishment is on your back.” Hilal said, “O Messenger of Allah, if any one of us saw a man over his wife, would he leave to search for proof?” The Prophet said, “Bring proof, otherwise the punishment is on your back.” Then, the Prophet mentioned the verses of adjudication of adultery allegations without proof. (24:6-9)
q: Bring proof, otherwise the punishment is on your back. … Bring proof, otherwise the punishment is on your back

title: Hadith on Salvation: Allah alone decrees Paradise or Hell
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: On the day of Uhud, the front teeth of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, were broken and his head was wounded. The Prophet said, “How will a people succeed who have wounded their Prophet and broken his teeth, while he calls them to Allah?” Then, Allah Almighty revealed the verse, “You have no say in the matter. It is up to Allah to turn to them in mercy or punish them, for they are surely wrongdoers.” (3:128)
q: How will a people succeed who have wounded their Prophet and broken his teeth, while he calls them to Allah? … You have no say in the matter. It is up to Allah to turn to them in mercy or punish them, for they are surely wrongdoers.

title: Hadith on Harm: Allah forbids alcohol, carrion, pork
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has forbidden wine and its sale. He has forbidden carrion and its sale. He has forbidden swine and its sale.”
q: Verily, Allah has forbidden wine and its sale. He has forbidden carrion and its sale. He has forbidden swine and its sale.

title: Hadith on Society: Muslims must provide for each other’s life-needs
t: Abu Khidash reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Muslims are partners in three things: vegetation, water, and fire.”
q: The Muslims are partners in three things: vegetation, water, and fire.

title: Hadith on Marriage: Warning not to publicize private bedroom secrets
t: Asma’ bint Yazid reported: She was with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while men and women were sitting with him. The Prophet said, “Perhaps a man will say what he did intimately in his home? Perhaps a woman will tell others what she did intimately with her husband?” The people sat in embarrassed silence, so I said, “By Allah, the women say such and the men do such!” The Prophet said, “Do not do this, for it is like a male devil and a female devil fornicating in the street while people watch.”
q: Perhaps a man will say what he did intimately in his home? Perhaps a woman will tell others what she did intimately with her husband? … Do not do this, for it … is like a male devil and a female devil fornicating in the street while people watch
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Marriage: Worst husband spreads their wife’s bedroom secrets
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most evil of people in the presence of Allah on the Day of Resurrection is a man who was intimate with his wife and then spreads her secrets.”
q: Verily, the most evil of people in the presence of Allah on the Day of Resurrection is a man who was intimate with his wife and then spreads her secrets.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: If you could see, you will cry more and laugh little
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, led us in prayer on day. The Prophet turned to us and he said, “O people, I am your leader. Do not precede me in bowing, prostration, standing, and turning. I see you in front of me and behind me.” Then the Prophet said, “By him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if you could see what I see then you would laugh less and weep more.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you see?” The Prophet said, “I see Paradise and Hellfire.”
q: O people, I am your leader. Do not precede me in bowing, prostration, standing, and turning. I see you in front of me and behind me … By him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if you could see what I see then you would laugh less and weep more … I see Paradise and Hellfire

title: Hadith on Salat: Recitation of Surat al-Fatihah in every prayer
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no prayer for one who does not recite the opening of the Book, Surat al-Fatihah.”
q: There is no prayer for one who does not recite the opening of the Book, Surat al-Fatihah
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Adhan: Satan runs away from the call to prayer
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, when Satan hears the call to prayer, he flees to a very distant place.”
q: Verily, when Satan hears the call to prayer, he flees to a very distant place.

title: Hadith on Adhan: Description of call to prayer, its wording
t: Abu Mahdhurah reported: The Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, taught the call to prayer like this, “Allah is the greatest. Allah is greatest. I bear witness there is no God but Allah. I bear witness there is no God but Allah. I bear witness Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. I bear witness Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.” Then, it is repeated, saying, “I bear witness there is no God but Allah. I bear witness there is no God but Allah. I bear witness Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. I bear witness Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Come to prayer, twice. Come to success, twice.” Ishaq added, “Allah is the greatest. Allah is the greatest. There is no God but Allah.”

title: Hadith on Dhikr: Remembering Allah is life, forgetting is death
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of one who remembers his Lord and one who does not remember is that of the living and the dead.”
q: The parable of one who remembers his Lord and one who does not remember is that of the living and the dead
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sabr: No gift better than patience, resilience
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: Some people from the Ansar asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he gave them. Then they asked for charity again and he gave them. Then they asked again and he gave them until all he had was gone. The Prophet said, “If I had anything, I would not withhold it. Whoever refrains from asking others, then Allah will make him content. Whoever would be independent, then Allah will make him independent. Whoever seeks to be patient, then Allah will make him patient. No one is given a gift that is better and more comprehensive than patience.”
q: If I had anything, I would not withhold it. Whoever refrains from asking others, then Allah will make him content. Whoever would be independent, then Allah will make him independent
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Judgment: No faith benefits after sun rises from West
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hour will not be established until the sun rises from the west. When it rises from the west, all people together will believe. Yet on that day, ‘No soul will benefit from his faith if he did not believe earlier, nor earn good from his faith.'” (6:158)
q: The Hour will not be established until the sun rises from the west. When it rises from the west, all people together will believe. Yet on that day, ‘No soul will benefit from his faith if he did not believe earlier, nor earn good from his faith
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Pilgrimage: No religious travel but to Mecca, Medina, Jerusalem
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not undertake a religious journey but to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque in Mecca, the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah, and the Furthest Mosque in Jerusalem.”
q: Do not undertake a religious journey but to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque in Mecca, the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah, and the Furthest Mosque in Jerusalem.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jesus: The Messiah returns to establish law of Islam
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Jesus the son of Mary, peace and blessings be upon him, will descend and the Muslim leader will say: Come lead us in prayer. Jesus will say: No, some of you are leaders over others, as Allah has honored this nation.”
q: Jesus the son of Mary, peace and blessings be upon him, will descend and the Muslim leader will say: Come lead us in prayer. Jesus will say: No, some of you are leaders over others, as Allah has honored this nation

title: Hadith on Hope: Expect good from Allah at time of death
t: Jabir reported: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say three days before his death, “None of you should die unless he expects good from Allah.”
q: None of you should die unless he expects good from Allah

title: Hadith on Hypocrisy: Four signs of a pure hypocrite
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are four signs that make someone a pure hypocrite and whoever has them has a characteristic of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when he speaks he lies, when he makes a covenant he is treacherous, when he makes a promise he breaks it, and when he argues he is wicked.”
q: There are four signs that make someone a pure hypocrite and whoever has them has a characteristic of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when he speaks he lies, when he makes a covenant he is treacherous, when he makes a promise he breaks it, and when he argues he is wicked
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Shukr: Health and free time, two blessings wasted
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There are two blessings which many people waste: health and free time.”
q: There are two blessings which many people waste: health and free time.

title: Hadith on Awliya: Loyal friends and allies of Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah said: Whoever shows hostility to a friend of Mine, I have declared war upon him. My servant does not grow closer to Me with anything more beloved to Me than the duties I have imposed upon him. My servant continues to grow closer to Me with extra good works until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his seeing with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. Were he to ask something from Me, I would surely give it to him. Were he to ask Me for refuge, I would surely grant it to him. I do not hesitate to do anything as I hesitate to take the soul of the believer, for he hates death, and I hate to displease him.”
q: Allah said: Whoever shows hostility to a friend of Mine, I have declared war upon him. My servant does not grow closer to Me with anything more beloved to Me than the duties I have imposed upon him. My servant continues to grow closer to Me with extra good works until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his seeing with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. Were he to ask something from Me, I would surely give it to him. Were he to ask Me for refuge, I would surely grant it to him. … I do not hesitate to do anything as I hesitate to take the soul of the believer, for he hates death, and I hate to displease him.

title: Hadith on Mawt: No Muslim should wish for death
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None of you should wish for death due to a calamity that has afflicted him. Yet if he must do something, let him say: O Allah, keep me alive so long as life is good for me, and cause me to die if death is better for me.”
q: None of you should wish for death due to a calamity that has afflicted him. Yet if he must do something, let him say: O Allah, keep me alive so long as life is good for me, and cause me to die if death is better for me
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jihad: Striving for Allah is better than the world
t:
Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A single endeavor or journey in the way of Allah is better than everything over which the sun rises and sets.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “It is better than the world and everything in it.”
q: A single endeavor or journey in the way of Allah is better than everything over which the sun rises and sets … It is better than the world and everything in it
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fitnah: You will endure five types of trials
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O emigrants, there are five things with which you will be tested, and I seek refuge in Allah that you will live to see them. Promiscuity never becomes widespread among people but that they will be afflicted by plagues and diseases that were unknown to their forefathers. They do not cheat in weights and measures but that they will be stricken with famine, calamity, and the oppression of rulers. They do not withhold charity from their wealth but that rain will be withheld from the sky, and were it not for the animals, there would be no rain at all. They do not break their covenant with Allah and His Messenger but that Allah will enable their enemies to overpower them and take what is in their hands. Their leaders must rule according to the Book of Allah and seek every good from what Allah has revealed, lest Allah place violence among them.”
q: O emigrants, there are five things with which you will be tested, and I seek refuge in Allah that you will live to see them. Promiscuity never becomes widespread among people but that they will be afflicted by plagues and diseases that were unknown to their forefathers. They do not cheat in weights and measures but that they will be stricken with famine, calamity, and the oppression of rulers. They do not withhold charity from their wealth but that rain will be withheld from the sky, and were it not for the animals, there would be no rain at all. They do not break their covenant with Allah and His Messenger but that Allah will enable their enemies to overpower them and take what is in their hands. Their leaders must rule according to the Book of Allah and seek every good from what Allah has revealed, lest Allah place violence among them

title: Hadith on Ghuluw: Nations destroyed by religious extremism
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said on the morning of al-‘Aqabah, “Pick up some pebbles for me.” I picked up seven pebbles, small like those used for flicking. He was turning them in his palm, saying, “Like these, so throw them.” Then, the Prophet said, “O people, beware of excessiveness in religion, for those who came before you were only destroyed by excessiveness in religion.”
q: Pick up some pebbles for me … Like these, so throw them … O people, beware of excessiveness in religion, for those who came before you were only destroyed by excessiveness in religion.

title: Hadith on Faith: Allah loves strong believers, but all good
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The strong believer is more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, but there is goodness in both of them. Be eager for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not be frustrated. If something befalls you, then do not say: If only I had done something else! Rather say: Allah has decreed what He wills. Verily, the phrase ‘if only’ opens the way for the work of Satan.”
q: The strong believer is more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, but there is goodness in both of them. Be eager for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not be frustrated. If something befalls you, then do not say: If only I had done something else! Rather say: Allah has decreed what He wills. Verily, the phrase ‘if only’ opens the way for the work of Satan.

title: Hadith on Islam: Its pillar is prayer, its peak is jihad
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: I was traveling with the Prophet one morning, close to him as we journeyed together, and I said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell me of a deed that will admit me into Paradise and keep me away from the Hellfire.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You have asked about an enormous matter, yet it is easy upon those for whom Allah makes it easy. Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, establish the prayer, give the charity, fast the month of Ramadan, and perform pilgrimage to the House.” Then, the Prophet said, “Shall I not tell you about the gates of goodness? Fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sins as water extinguishes fire, and the prayer of a man in the late night,” and the Prophet recited the verse, “They arise from their beds and supplicate to their Lord in fear and hope. They spend from what We have provided them, for no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort as reward for what they used to do.” (32:16) Then, the Prophet said, “Shall I not tell you about the head of the matter and its peak?” I said, “Of course, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is prayer, and jihad is its peak. Shall I not tell you how to achieve all of this?” I said, “Of course, O Prophet of Allah.” The Prophet pointed to his tongue and he said, “Restrain this.” I said, “O Prophet of Allah, will what we say be held against us?” The Prophet said, “May your mother be bereaved of you, O Mu’adh! Is there anything that topples people onto their faces into the Hellfire but the harvest of their tongues?”
q: You have asked about an enormous matter, yet it is easy upon those for whom Allah makes it easy. Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, establish the prayer, give the charity, fast the month of Ramadan, and perform pilgrimage to the House … Shall I not tell you about the gates of goodness? Fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sins as water extinguishes fire, and the prayer of a man in the late night … They arise from their beds and supplicate to their Lord in fear and hope. They spend from what We have provided them, for no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort as reward for what they used to do … Shall I not tell you about the head of the matter and its peak? … The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is prayer, and jihad … is its peak. … Shall I not tell you how to achieve all of this … Restrain this. … May your mother be bereaved of you, O Mu’adh! Is there anything that topples people onto their faces into the Hellfire but the harvest of their tongues?

title: Hadith on Gender: Those who mimic opposite sex are cursed
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, cursed men who imitate women and women who imitate men.

title: Hadith on Jihad: Did you tear open his heart to see his intention?
t: Usamah ibn Zayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent us on an expedition. In the morning we attacked Al-Huraqat of Juhaynah. I caught hold of a man and he said, “There is no God but Allah!” I stabbed him anyway. Then, it occurred to me that I should mention that to the Prophet. The Prophet said, “Did he say ‘there is no God but Allah’ but you killed him?” I said, “O Messenger of Allah, he only said it because he feared the weapon!” The Prophet said, “Did you tear open his heart to know if he meant it or not?” The Prophet continued repeating it to me until I had wished I had not embraced Islam until that day.
q: Did he say ‘there is no God but Allah’ but you killed him? … Did you tear open his heart to know if he meant it or not?

title: Hadith on Shirk: Whoever dies associating idols with Allah
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever dies while associating partners with Allah will enter Hellfire.” And I said in his presence, “Whoever dies without associating partners with Allah will enter Paradise.”
q: Whoever dies while associating partners with Allah will enter Hellfire. … Whoever dies without associating partners with Allah will enter Paradise.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Major Sins: Worst are idolatry, murder, false witness
t: Anas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said regarding the major sins, “They are associating partners with Allah, disrespect to parents, killing someone, and false testimony.”
q: They are associating partners with Allah, disrespect to parents, killing someone, and false testimony
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Shirk: Allah abandons idolaters to their idols
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: Verily, I am free of the idolatry of any partners. Whoever performs a deed in which he associates another with Me, I will abandon him to his partner.”
q: Allah Almighty said: Verily, I am free of the idolatry of any partners. Whoever performs a deed in which he associates another with Me, I will abandon him to his partner.

title: Hadith on Kids: The Prophet greets children with peace
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would pass by young boys and greet them with peace.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Trials: People wish for death before the Hour
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Hour will not be established until a man passes by the grave of another man and he says: Would that I were in his place!”
q: The Hour will not be established until a man passes by the grave of another man and he says: Would that I were in his place!
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Trials: Worship in turmoil like emigration to Prophet
t: Ma’qil ibn Yassar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Worship in a time of turmoil is like emigrating to me.”
q: Worship in a time of turmoil is like emigrating to me

title: Hadith on Death: After death, only his deeds remain
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Three things follow a deceased person. Two of them return and one remains. His family, his wealth, and his deeds follow him. His family and wealth return, but his deeds remain.”
q: Three things follow a deceased person. Two of them return and one remains. His family, his wealth, and his deeds follow him. His family and wealth return, but his deeds remain
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Humility: Beware of excessively praising people
t: Abu Bakrah reported: A man praised another man in the presence of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet said, “Woe to you! You have cut your companion’s neck! You have cut your companion’s neck! If one of you inevitably praises his companion, let him say: I consider him to be good and Allah will hold him accountable. I cannot testify to anyone’s purity before Allah, but I consider him good as far as is known.”
q: Woe to you! You have cut your companion’s neck! You have cut your companion’s neck!
