If one of you inevitably praises his companion, let him say: I consider him to be good and Allah will hold him accountable. I cannot testify to anyone’s purity before Allah, but I consider him good as far as is known.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Graves: Do not turn homes into graves, or graves into celebrations
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not turn your houses into graves, and do not turn my grave into a place of festivity. Send blessings upon me, for your blessings will reach me wherever you are.”
q: Do not turn your houses into graves, and do not turn my grave into a place of festivity. Send blessings upon me, for your blessings will reach me wherever you are.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Shirk: You asked for a god like people of Moses
t: Abu Waqid al-Laythi reported: When we traveled to Hunayn with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, we passed by a tree that the idolaters called Dhat al-Anwat. They would hang their weapons upon it for blessings. I said, “O Messenger of Allah, make a blessed tree for us, just as they have one.” The Prophet said, “Glory be to Allah! You have said just as the people of Moses said, ‘Make a god for us, just as they have a god’ (7:138). By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will follow the ways of people before you.”
q: Glory be to Allah! You have said just as the people of Moses said, ‘Make a god for us, just as they have a god’ … By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will follow the ways of people before you.

title: Hadith on Tawakkul: The Prophet and Abu Bakr trust Allah in the cave
t: Abu Bakr reported: I saw the feet of the idolaters over our heads while we were hiding in the cave, fleeing to Medina. I said, “O Messenger of Allah, if one of them only looked under his feet, he would see us!” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two for whom Allah is the third?”
q: O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two for whom Allah is the third?

title: Hadith on Tawhid: Some Jews and Christians take their leaders as gods
t: ‘Adi ibn Hatim reported: I came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while I had a crucifix of gold around my neck. The Prophet said, “O ‘Adi! Remove this idol from yourself!” I heard him reciting the verse in Surat al-Tawbah, “They have taken their priests and rabbis as lords besides Allah.” (9:31) The Prophet said, “As for them, they did not worship them, but rather when they made something lawful for them, they considered it lawful. When they made something unlawful for them, they considered it unlawful.”
q: O ‘Adi! Remove this idol from yourself! … They have taken their priests and rabbis as lords besides Allah. … As for them, they did not worship them, but rather when they made something lawful for them, they considered it lawful. When they made something unlawful for them, they considered it unlawful.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Quran: Why bismillah is missing from Surat al-Tawbah
t: Ibn Abbas reported: I said to Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, “What is your reasoning with Surat al-Anfal, which has less than a hundred verses, and Surat Bara’ah (al-Tawbah), which has more than a hundred verses, yet you put them together without writing ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,’ between them and you placed them with the seven long chapters. Why did you do that?” Uthman said, “A long time might pass with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, without anything being revealed to him, and then sometimes a chapter with numerous verses might be revealed. So when something was revealed he would call for someone who could write and tell them to put these verses in the chapter which mentions this and that. When a verse was revealed, he would tell them to put this verse in the chapter which mentions this and that. Al-Anfal was among the first to be revealed in Medina, and Bara’ah was among the last of those revealed of the Quran and their discussions resemble each other, so we thought that they were part of each other. Then, the Prophet passed away and it was not clear to us if they were part of each other. For this reason, we put them together without writing ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,’ and we included them with the seven long chapters.”

title: Hadith on Jihad: The Prophet’s commandments of just war
t: Buraydah reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, issued orders to a commander of an army or a company, he would personally command him to fear Allah and be good to the Muslims with them. Then, the Prophet would say, “March forward in the name of Allah and in the way of Allah. Fight those who deny Allah. March forward and do not embezzle the spoils, do not be treacherous, do not mutilate, and do not kill children. When you meet your enemy among the idolaters, call them to three options. If they respond to any of these, you must accept it and refrain from harming them. Thus, call them to Islam. If they answer you, accept it from them and refrain from harming them. Then, call them to relocate from their abodes to the abode of the emigrants. Inform them if they do that, they will have the privileges and duties of the emigrants. If they refuse to relocate, inform them they will be like the Bedouin Arabs among the Muslims under the rulings of Allah, the same as the believers, but they will have no share of the spoils unless they fight with the Muslims. If they refuse, ask them to pay tribute. If they answer you, accept it and refrain from harming them. If they refuse everything, then seek help from Allah and fight them.”
q: March forward in the name of Allah and in the way of Allah. Fight those who deny Allah. March forward and do not embezzle the spoils, do not be treacherous, do not mutilate, and do not kill children. When you meet your enemy among the idolaters, call them to three options. If they respond to any of these, you must accept it and refrain from harming them. Thus, call them to Islam. If they answer you, accept it from them and refrain from harming them. Then, call them to relocate from their abodes to the abode of the emigrants. Inform them if they do that, they will have the privileges and duties of the emigrants. If they refuse to relocate, inform them they will be like the Bedouin Arabs among the Muslims under the rulings of Allah, the same as the believers, but they will have no share of the spoils unless they fight with the Muslims. If they refuse, ask them to pay tribute. If they answer you, accept it and refrain from harming them. If they refuse everything, then seek help from Allah and fight them.

title: Hadith on Bid’ah: Muslims make same mistakes as previous nations
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You will surely follow the path of those before you, step by step and inch by inch. If they entered a lizard hole, you would follow.” We said, “O Messenger of Allah, do you mean the Jews and Christians?” The Prophet said, “Who else?”
q: You will surely follow the path of those before you, step by step and inch by inch. If they entered a lizard hole, you would follow. … Who else
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Amulets: Allah will not bless good luck charms
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever hangs an amulet around his neck, Allah will not fulfill his wishes. Whoever hangs a seashell as a charm, Allah will not leave him without penalty. ”
q: Whoever hangs an amulet around his neck, Allah will not fulfill his wishes. Whoever hangs a seashell as a charm, Allah will not leave him without penalty

title: Hadith on Amulets: Good luck charms only bring harm
t: ‘Imran ibn Husayn reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, noticed a man was wearing a brass ring as a charm. The Prophet said, “Woe to you! What is this?” The man said, “It is protection from arthritis.” The Prophet said, “Remove it, for it will only add to your arthritis. If you died while wearing it, you would never succeed.”
q: Woe to you! What is this? … Remove it, for it will only add to your arthritis. If you died while wearing it, you would never succeed.

title: Hadith on Qadr: The Prophet seeks refuge from unfortunate decrees
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the divine decree, from falling into misery, from the gloating of enemies, and from an unbearable trial.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dajjal: False Messiah says evil is good, good is evil
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I surely know what the False Messiah will have with him. He will have two flowing rivers, one that appears to be clear water and another that appears to be blazing fire. If one of you sees that, let him go to the river of fire, lower his gaze, put his head down, and drink from it, for it will be cool water. The False Messiah has one covered eye with thick skin over it. Written between his eyes is the word of unbelief. Every believer will be able to read it, whether he is literate or not.”
q: I surely know what the False Messiah will have with him. He will have two flowing rivers, one that appears to be clear water and another that appears to be blazing fire. If one of you sees that, let him go to the river of fire, lower his gaze, put his head down, and drink from it, for it will be cool water. The False Messiah has one covered eye with thick skin over it. Written between his eyes is the word of unbelief. Every believer will be able to read it, whether he is literate or not.

title: Hadith on Iman: Sinful believers will not stay in Hellfire forever
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah will admit the people of Paradise into Paradise among whomever He wills, due to His mercy, and He will admit the people of Hellfire into Hellfire, then Allah will say: Look for those with faith in their hearts as much as a seed and bring them out! Then, they will be brought out from it as burnt charcoal. They will be cast into the river of life and sprout just as a seed sprouts on the side of the riverbank. Have you not seen that it comes out yellow and entwined?”
q: Allah will admit the people of Paradise into Paradise among whomever He wills, due to His mercy, and He will admit the people of Hellfire into Hellfire, then Allah will say: Look for those with faith in their hearts as much as a seed and bring them out! Then, they will be brought out from it as burnt charcoal. They will be cast into the river of life and sprout just as a seed sprouts on the side of the riverbank. Have you not seen that it comes out yellow and entwined
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Criminals: The Prophet recommends forgiveness
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: I never saw a case involving legal retaliation being referred to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, but that he would encourage pardoning the criminal.

title: Hadith on Jihad: Fighting for freedom to preach, practice Islam
t: Abu Musa reported: A man asked the Prophet, “A man may fight to be courageous, another may fight for zeal, and another may fight to show off. Which of these is fighting in the way of Allah?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He who fights to raise the word of Allah is in the way of Allah.”
q: He who fights to raise the word of Allah is in the way of Allah
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Nikah: Young men who can get married should do so
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O young men, if you are able to support a wife, get married. Verily, it lowers the gaze and guards chastity. Whoever is not able to do so, he must fast as it will restrain his passions.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Mut’ah: Temporary marriage forbidden by consensus
t: Sabrah al-Juhanni reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited temporary marriage, saying, “Behold, it is forbidden from this day of yours until the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Behold, it is forbidden from this day of yours until the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Nikah: Propose to the religious girl for marriage
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A woman is married for four reasons: her property, her status, her beauty, and her religion. Thus, give precedence to one with religion.”
q: A woman is married for four reasons: her property, her status, her beauty, and her religion. Thus, give precedence to one with religion
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Islam: This is the straight path to Allah
t: Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, drew a line in the sand with his hand and he said, “This is the straight path of Allah.” Then, the Prophet drew lines to the right and left, saying, “These are other paths, and there is no path among them but that a devil is upon it calling to its way.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “Verily, this is the straight path, so follow it and do not follow other ways.” (6:153)
q: This is the straight path of Allah. … These are other paths, and there is no path among them but that a devil is upon it calling to its way … Verily, this is the straight path, so follow it and do not follow other ways

title: Hadith on Pardon: Allah forgives honest mistakes, coerced sins
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has pardoned my nation for their mistakes, their forgetfulness, and what they are coerced into doing.”
q: Verily, Allah has pardoned my nation for their mistakes, their forgetfulness, and what they are coerced into doing

title: Hadith on Love: One is with loved ones in the Hereafter
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A bedouin asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “When is the Hour?” The Prophet said, “What have you prepared for it?” The man said, “Love for Allah and his messenger.” The Prophet said, “You will be with those whom you love.”
q: What have you prepared for it? … You will be with those whom you love
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Praise: Believer’s glad tidings are praise in the world
t: Abu Dharr reported: It was said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “What do you think of a man who does good deeds and people praise him?” The Prophet said, “They are early glad tidings for a believer.”
q: They are early … glad tidings for a believer.

title: Hadith on Hellfire: Story of the last man to exit Hell
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I know the last of the people of Paradise to enter it and the last of the people of Hell to come out of it. He is a man who is brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: Present his minor sins to him and withhold his major sins. Then the minor sins will be placed before him and it will be said: On this day you did this, and this day you did this. He will say yes. It is not possible for him to deny it, while he will be afraid that his major sins will be presented before him. It will be said: In place of every evil deed you will receive one good deed. He will say: My Lord, I have done other things I do not see here.”
q: Verily, I know the last of the people of Paradise to enter it and the last of the people of Hell to come out of it. He is a man who is brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: Present his minor sins to him and withhold his major sins. Then the minor sins will be placed before him and it will be said: On this day you did this, and this day you did this. He will say yes. It is not possible for him to deny it, while he will be afraid that his major sins will be presented before him. It will be said: In place of every evil deed you will receive one good deed. He will say: My Lord, I have done other things I do not see here

title: Hadith on Khawatir: Allah forgives Muslims for their involuntary thoughts
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has pardoned my nation for the stray thoughts occurring within themselves, as long as they do not speak of them or act upon them.”
q: Verily, Allah has pardoned my nation for the stray thoughts occurring within themselves, as long as they do not speak of them or act upon them
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jesus: The Messiah returns to lead the believers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “How will you be when the son of Mary descends upon you while your leader is among you?”
q: How will you be when the son of Mary descends upon you while your leader is among you
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Suicide: Whoever kills himself is punished in Hell
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever kills himself with a piece of iron, his piece of iron in his hand will be thrust into his stomach in the fire of Hell forever and ever. Whoever drinks poison and kills himself, he will consume it in the fire of Hell forever and ever. Whoever throws himself off a mountain and kills himself, he will tumble into the fire of Hell forever and ever.”
q: Whoever kills himself with a piece of iron, his piece of iron in his hand will be thrust into his stomach in the fire of Hell forever and ever. Whoever drinks poison and kills himself, he will consume it in the fire of Hell forever and ever. Whoever throws himself off a mountain and kills himself, he will tumble into the fire of Hell forever and ever
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Muslims: Whoever fights us is not one of us
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever takes up arms against us is not one of us.”
q: Whoever takes up arms against us is not one of us
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Miracles: Gabriel takes Satan out of the Prophet’s heart
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: Gabriel came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when he was a child playing with his friends. Gabriel took hold of him and laid him on the ground, then he tore open his chest, took out his heart, and extracted a blood clot from it. Gabriel said, “This was the measure of Satan inside you.” Gabriel washed his heart with Zamzam water in a golden vessel and it was joined together and restored. The boys came running to his mother and said, “Muhammad has been killed!” They rushed to Muhammad and found that he was alive and his color had changed. Anas said, “I myself saw the marks of the needle on his chest.”
q: This was the measure of Satan inside you.

title: Hadith on Jesus: Every person is touched by Satan upon birth
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No person is born but that he is pricked by Satan and he cries from the touch of Satan, except for the son of Mary and his mother.” Abu Huraira said, “Recite the verse if you wish: Verily, I seek refuge for her and her offspring from the cursed Satan.” (3:36)
q: No person is born but that he is pricked by Satan and he cries from the touch of Satan, except for the son of Mary and his mother … Verily, I seek refuge for her and her offspring from the cursed Satan
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Anger: Seek refuge from Satan inciting rage
t: Sulayman ibn Surad reported: Two people insulted each other in the presence of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and the eyes of one of them became red like embers and the veins of his neck were bulging. The Prophet said, “Verily, I know a word he could say to calm himself: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.”
q: Verily, … I know a word he could say to calm himself: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Musa: Do not make Muhammad superior to Moses
t: Abu Huraira reported: Two people, one Jewish and the other Muslim, fell into dispute and began to abuse one another. The Muslim said, “By the one who has chosen Muhammad above the worlds!” And the Jew said, “By the one who has chosen Moses above the worlds!” Then, the Muslim slapped the face of the Jew. The Jew went to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and told him about the incident. The Prophet said, “Do not say I am better than Moses, for humanity will faint on the Day of Resurrection and I will be the first to recover. Moses at that time will be holding the side of the Throne. I do not know if he would faint and recover before me, or if Allah will make an exception for him.”
q: Do not say I am better than Moses, for humanity will faint on the Day of Resurrection and I will be the first to recover. Moses at that time will be holding the side of the Throne. I do not know if he would faint and recover before me, or if Allah will make an exception for him.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ibrahim: Prophet Abraham is best of creation
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O best of creation!” The Prophet said, “That is Abraham, upon him be peace.”
q: That is Abraham, upon him be peace

title: Hadith on Wudu: Description of a perfect ablution
t: Humran reported: Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, requested a vessel of water and he poured water over his hands three times and washed them. Then, he put his right hand in the vessel and rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose. Then, he washed his face three times, and his hands up to the elbow three times. Then, he wiped his head and washed his feet three times. Then, Uthman said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine and performs two cycles of prayer, without allowing his thoughts to stray, his previous sins will be forgiven.”
q: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine and performs two cycles of prayer, without allowing his thoughts to stray, his previous sins will be forgiven
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Najashi: The Prophet prays funeral prayer for King of Abyssinia
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, told us about the Negus, the ruler of Abyssinia, on the day he died. The Prophet said to us, “Seek forgiveness for your brother.”
q: Seek forgiveness for your brother
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Faith: People of the Book who hear of Muhammad
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none from this nation of Jews and Christians hears of me, and then dies without having faith in my message, but that he will be an inhabitant of Hellfire.”
q: By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none from this nation of Jews and Christians hears of me, and then dies without having faith in my message, but that he will be an inhabitant of Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Khawarij: Rebels with good words, foolish dreams
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “In the last days, there will appear young people with foolish dreams. They will say the best of words, but they will go out of Islam just as an arrow goes through its game. Their faith will not go beyond their throats.”
q: In the last days, there will appear young people with foolish dreams. They will say the best of words, but they will go out of Islam just as an arrow goes through its game. Their faith will not go beyond their throats
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Imamah: The Muslim leader is a shield who defends them
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the leader is only a shield behind whom they fight, and he protects them. If he commands the fear of Allah Almighty and justice, he will have a reward. If he commands something else, it will be held against him.”
q: Verily, the leader is only a shield behind whom they fight, and he protects them. If he commands the fear of Allah Almighty and justice, he will have a reward. If he commands something else, it will be held against him

title: Hadith on Customs: The Prophet considers customs of other nations
t: Judamah bint Wahb reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I considered forbidding intercourse with a breastfeeding woman, until it occurred to me that the Romans and Persians do that and it does not harm their children.”
q: I considered forbidding intercourse with a breastfeeding woman, until it occurred to me that the Romans and Persians do that and it does not harm their children.

title: Hadith on Muhammad: Do not exaggerate status of the Prophet
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not exaggerate my status as the Christians have done with the son of Mary. Verily, I am only a servant, so refer to me as the servant of Allah and His Messenger.”
q: Do not exaggerate my status as the Christians have done with the son of Mary. Verily, I am only a servant, so refer to me as the servant of Allah and His Messenger

title: Hadith on Anger: If you are mad, perform ablution with water
t: ‘Atiyyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace be and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, anger comes from Satan, and Satan was created from fire. Fire is extinguished with water, so if you become angry, perform ablution with water.”
q: Verily, anger comes from Satan, and Satan was created from fire. Fire is extinguished with water, so if you become angry, perform ablution with water

title: Hadith on Rage: If you are angry, sit or lie down
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to us, “If one of you is angry while he is standing, let him sit down so his anger will leave him; otherwise, let him lie down.”
q: If one of you is angry while he is standing, let him sit down so his anger will leave him; otherwise, let him lie down.

title: Hadith on Quran: Parable of reciters of Allah’s Book
t: Abu Musa al-Asha’ri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the believer who recites the Quran is that of a citrus fruit, which tastes good and has a pleasant scent. The parable of the believer who does not recite the Quran is that of a date, which has no scent but tastes good. The parable of a hypocrite who recites the Quran is that of basil, which has a pleasant scent but tastes bitter. The parable of the hypocrite who does not recite the Quran is that of a vine, which has no scent and tastes bitter.”
q: The parable of the believer who recites the Quran is that of a citrus fruit, which tastes good and has a pleasant scent. The parable of the believer who does not recite the Quran is that of a date, which has no scent but tastes good. The parable of a hypocrite who recites the Quran is that of basil, which has a pleasant scent but tastes bitter. The parable of the hypocrite who does not recite the Quran is that of a … vine, which has no scent and tastes bitter
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Quran: Best Muslims learn the Quran and teach it
t: Uthman bin Affan reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.”
q: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

title: Hadith on Hikmah: Wisdom is the lost property of believers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The word of wisdom is the lost property of the believer. Wherever he finds it, he is most worthy of it.”
q: The word of wisdom is the lost property of the believer. Wherever he finds it, he is most worthy of it

title: Hadith on ‘Ilm: Virtue of scholars over worshipers
t:
Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The virtue of the scholar over the worshiper is like my virtue over the least of you. Verily, Allah, His angels, the inhabitants of the heavens and earth, even the ant in his hole and the fish, send blessings upon the one who teaches people what is good.”

Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “A scholar who works in teaching has a high status in the domain of the heavens.”
q: The virtue of the scholar over the worshiper is like my virtue over the least of you. V … erily, Allah, His angels, the inhabitants of the heavens and earth, even the ant in his hole and the fish, send blessings upon the one who teaches people what is good

title: Hadith on Joking: The Prophet tells jokes, but only in truth
t: Abu Huraira reported: It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, do you joke with us?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I do not say anything but the truth.”
q: Verily, I do not say anything but the truth

title: Hadith on Masajid: Whoever builds a mosque given Paradise
t: Uthman ibn Affan reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah will build for him a house like it in Paradise.”
q: Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah will build for him a house like it in Paradise.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Cursing: Do not curse time, Allah is Time
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: The son of Adam insults Me. He curses time, but I am time, for in My hand are the night and day.”
q: Allah Almighty said: The son of Adam insults Me. He curses time, but I am time, for in My hand are the night and day
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Kufr: Good deeds no benefit to unbelievers in Hereafter
t: Aisha reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, the son of Jud’an would maintain family ties and feed the poor in the time of ignorance. Will it benefit him?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It will not benefit him, for he never said even for one day: My Lord, forgive my sins on the Day of Judgment.”
q: It will not benefit him, for he never said even for one day: My Lord, forgive my sins on the Day of Judgment

title: Hadith on Expiation: Good deeds erase bad deeds from record
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: A man kissed a woman and he came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and mentioned it to him. The verse was revealed, “Establish prayer at both ends of the day and in the early part of the night. Surely good deeds wipe out evil deeds,” (11:114). The man said, “O Messenger of Allah, is it for me only?” The Prophet said, “It is for all who act upon it from my nation.”
q: Establish prayer at both ends of the day and in the early part of the night. Surely good deeds wipe out evil deeds, … It is for all who act upon it from my nation.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ijtihad: Judge with the Quran, Sunnah, then your opinion
t: Al-Harith ibn ‘Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent Mu’adh to Yemen and he said, “How will you judge?” Mu’adh said, “I will judge according to the Book of Allah.” The Prophet said, “What if it is not in the Book of Allah?” Mu’adh said, “Then, with the Sunnah of the messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “What if it is not in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah?” Mu’adh said, “Then, I will strive to form an opinion.” The Prophet said, “All praise is due to Allah, who has made suitable the messenger of the Messenger of Allah.”
q: How will you judge? … What if it is not in the Book of Allah? … What if it is not in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah? … All praise is due to Allah, who has made suitable the messenger of the Messenger of Allah.
gf: Sahih (authentic) according to Ibn Abdul Barr

title: Hadith on Leniency: May Allah forgive a lenient businessman
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “May Allah have mercy on a man who is lenient when selling, buying, and seeking repayment.”
q: May Allah

title: Hadith on Imam: Muslim leaders must take care of people’s needs
t: ‘Amr ibn Murrah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no leader who closes the door to someone in need, in hardship, and in poverty, but that Allah closes the gates of heaven to him when he is in need, in hardship, and in poverty.”
q: There is no leader who closes the door to someone in need, in hardship, and in poverty, but that Allah closes the gates of heaven to him when he is in need, in hardship, and in poverty.

title: Hadith on Reason: Do not be blind followers of society
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not be blind followers, saying that if the people are good we will be good, and if they are unjust we will be unjust. Rather, decide for yourselves. If the people are good, be good. If they are evil, do not be unjust.”
q: Do not be blind followers, saying that if the people are good we will be good, and if they are unjust we will be unjust. Rather, decide for yourselves. If the people are good, be good. If they are evil, do not be unjust

title: Ibn Mubarak on Akhlaq: Good character is smiling, good deeds
t: Abu Wahb reported: Abdullah ibn Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him, described good character, saying, “It is a cheerful face, offering good deeds, and refraining from harm.”

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Good character is heaviest on the Scale
t: Abu Darda reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Nothing is heavier upon the scale of a believer on the Day of Resurrection than his good character. Verily, Allah hates the vulgar and obscene.”
q: Nothing is heavier upon the scale of a believer on the Day of Resurrection than his good character. Verily, Allah hates the vulgar and obscene.

title: Hadith on Speech: All body parts defer to the tongue
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the son of Adam wakes up in the morning, all of his limbs defer to the tongue, saying: Fear Allah regarding us, for we are only a part of you. If you are upright, we are upright. If you are crooked, we are crooked.”
q: When the son of Adam wakes up in the morning, all of his limbs defer to the tongue, saying: Fear Allah regarding us, for we are only a part of you. If you are upright, we are upright. If you are crooked, we are crooked.

title: Hadith on Anger: Judge should not issue ruling if angry
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The judge should not issue a ruling between two people while he is angry.”
q: The judge should not issue a ruling between two people while he is angry

title: Hadith on Justice: If a judge is unjust, Allah leaves him to Satan
t: Ibn Abi Awfa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is with the judge as long as he is not unjust. If he is unjust, Allah will leave him in the attendance of Satan.”
q: Verily, Allah is with the judge as long as he is not unjust. If he is unjust, Allah will leave him in the attendance of Satan

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication for refuge at the end of prayer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you finishes his testimony at the end of prayer, let him seek refuge in Allah from four trials, saying: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, from the punishment of the grave, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil trial of the False Messiah.”
q: When one of you finishes his testimony at the end of prayer, let him seek refuge in Allah from four trials, saying: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, from the punishment of the grave, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil trial of the False Messiah
gf: Sahih (authentic) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Optimism: Good thoughts about Allah is worship
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, thinking well about Allah Almighty is a part of the excellent worship of Allah.”
q: Verily, thinking well about Allah Almighty is a part of the excellent worship of Allah

title: Hadith on Dua: Let one of you ask Allah for all of his needs
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Let one of you ask his Lord for his needs, all of them, even for a shoestring when his breaks.”
q: Let one of you ask his Lord for his needs, all of them, even for a shoestring when his breaks

title: Hadith on Faith: Example of believers who endure trials
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the believer is a fresh plant, the leaves of which rustle in whatever direction the wind takes them, but when the winds calm down, it returns to its balance. Such is the parable of the believer who endures trials. The parable of the unbeliever is that of a firm pine tree, unbending until Allah shatters it as He wills.”
q: The parable of the believer is a fresh plant, the leaves of which rustle in whatever direction the wind takes them, but when the winds calm down, it returns to its balance. Such is the parable of the believer who endures trials. The parable of the unbeliever is that of a firm pine tree, unbending until Allah shatters it as He wills.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Killing: Son of Adam responsible for every murder
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No soul is wrongfully killed but that some responsibility for its blood is upon the first son of Adam, for he was the first to set the precedent of murder.”
q: No soul is wrongfully killed but that some responsibility for its blood is upon the first son of Adam, for he was the first to set the precedent of murder
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Kufr: Between faith and disbelief is leaving prayer
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, between a man and idolatry and unbelief is abandoning the prayer.”
q: Verily, between a man and idolatry and unbelief is abandoning the prayer

title: Hadith on Sincerity: Three traits to purify oneself of malice
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “May Allah illuminate one who hears my words, such that he understands it, memorizes it, and conveys it. Perhaps he will carry understanding to one who has more understanding than he does. There are three qualities by which malice cannot enter the heart of a Muslim: sincere deeds for Allah, good will to the leaders of the Muslims, and keeping to their community. Verily, the call to Islam is protected behind them.”
q: May Allah illuminate one who hears my words, such that he understands it, memorizes it, and conveys it. Perhaps he will carry understanding to one who has more understanding than he does. There are three qualities by which malice cannot enter the heart of a Muslim: sincere deeds for Allah, good will to the leaders of the Muslims, and keeping to their community. Verily, the call to Islam is protected behind them

title: Hadith on Funerals: Shroud deceased in white garments
t: Samurah ibn Jundab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Clothe yourselves in white, for it is cleaner and purer, and shroud your deceased in it.”
q: Clothe yourselves in white, for it is cleaner and purer, and shroud your deceased in it.

title: Hadith on Loot: Not a believer while he plunders
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The plunderer is not a believer while he is looting such things people look fondly upon.”
q: The plunderer is not a believer while he is looting such things people look fondly upon
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Moderation: Love and hatred in balance
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Love whom you love mildly, perhaps he will become hateful to you someday. Hate whom you hate mildly, perhaps he will become your beloved someday.”
q: Love whom you love mildly, perhaps he will become hateful to you someday. Hate whom you hate mildly, perhaps he will become your beloved someday

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: The Prophet teaches good character, manners
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was never obscene or immoral. The Prophet would say, “Verily, among the best of you are those with the best character.”
q: Verily, among the best of you are those with the best character.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Qadr: If Allah intends good, He puts him to action
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If Allah wills goodness for a servant, He puts him into action.” It was said, “How is he put into action, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “He is guided to righteous deeds before death.”
q: If Allah wills goodness for a servant, He puts him into action. … He is guided to righteous deeds before death

title: Hadith on Dishonesty: Most hated behavior to the Prophet was lying
t: Aisha reported: There was no behavior more hateful to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, than dishonesty. A man would tell a lie when speaking in the presence of the Prophet, and he would not be satisfied until he knew that he had repented from it.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Every good deed is charity, even smiling
t: Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Every good deed is charity. Verily, it is a good deed to meet your brother with a smiling face, and to pour what is left from your bucket into your brother’s vessel.”
q: Every good deed is charity. Verily, it is a good deed to meet your brother with a smiling face, and to pour what is left from your bucket into your brother’s vessel

title: Hadith on Hereafter: If people knew what was with Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If the believer knew what was with Allah of punishment, no one would hope for Paradise. If the disbeliever knew what was with Allah of mercy, no one would despair of attaining Paradise.”
q: , … If the believer knew what was with Allah of punishment, no one would hope for Paradise. If the disbeliever knew what was with Allah of mercy, no one would despair of attaining Paradise

title: Hadith on Muhammad: The Prophet’s face was like the Moon
t: Abu Ishaq reported: A man asked Al-Bara’, may Allah be pleased with him, “Was the face of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, like a sword?” Al-Bara’ said, “No, it was like the moon.”

title: Hadith on ‘Ijaz: The Quran is greatest miracle of the Prophet
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There were none among the prophets but that he was given unique signs to instill faith in humanity. Verily, I have been given the revelation that Allah has inspired in me, so I hope to have the most followers on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: There were none among the prophets but that he was given unique signs to instill faith in humanity. … Verily, I have been given the revelation that Allah has inspired in me, so I hope to have the most followers on the Day of Resurrection
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Character: Reasons people go to Paradise or Hell
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked, “What admits most people into Paradise?” The Prophet said, “Fear of Allah and good character.” It was asked, “What condemns most people to Hellfire?” The Prophet said, “The mouth and the genitals.”
q: Fear of Allah and good character … The mouth and the genitals

title: Hadith on Jihad: Helping the poor is jihad in the way of Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One who lends effort to the widows and the poor is like one waging jihad in the way of Allah, or one who regularly prays at night and fasts during the day.”
q: One who lends effort to the widows and the poor is like one waging jihad in the way of Allah, or one who regularly prays at night and fasts during the day
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tazkiyyah: Pure hearts have no aggression, malice, envy
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: We said, “O Messenger of Allah, who are the best of people?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One with a heart swept clean and truthful in speech.” We said, “O Messenger of Allah, we recognize truthful speech, but what is a heart swept clean?” The Prophet said, “One that is Godfearing and pure, in which there is neither sin, nor transgression, nor envy.” We said, “Who shows a sign of it?” The Prophet said, “One who despises worldliness and loves the Hereafter.” They said, “And who shows a sign of it?” The Prophet said, “A believer with good character.”
q: One with a heart swept clean and truthful in speech … One that is Godfearing and pure, in which there is neither sin, nor transgression, nor envy. … A believer with good character

title: Hadith on Oppression: Tribalism is to support your people in injustice
t: Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ reported: I asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, is it part of tribalism that a man loves his people?” The Prophet said, “No, rather it is tribalism that he supports his people in wrongdoing.”
q: No, rather it is tribalism that he supports his people in wrongdoing

title: Hadith on Obedience: No obeying creation if disobeying the Creator
t: Ali reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no obedience to anyone if it is disobedience to Allah. Verily, obedience is only in good conduct.”
q: There is no obedience to anyone if it is disobedience to Allah. Verily, obedience is only in good conduct
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Islam: Religion of Islam is built on five pillars
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Islam is built upon five: to worship Allah and to disbelieve in what is worshiped besides Him, to establish prayer, to give charity, to perform the Hajj pilgrimage to the house, and to fast the month of Ramadan.”
q: Islam is built upon five: to worship Allah and to disbelieve in what is worshiped besides Him, to establish prayer, to give charity, to perform the Hajj pilgrimage to the house, and to fast the month of Ramadan
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Faith: Spread peace and love each other
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You will not enter Paradise until you have faith, and you will not have faith until you love each other. Shall I tell you something that, if you did, you would love each other? Spread peace between yourselves.”
q: You will not enter Paradise until you have faith, and you will not have faith until you love each other. Shall I tell you something that, if you did, you would love each other? Spread peace between yourselves.

title: Hadith on Iqtisas: Oppressor’s good deeds given to victims
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever wrongs his brother in his honor or anything else should resolve the matter today before it cannot be resolved with gold and silver coins. If he has good deeds to his credit, they will be taken from him according to the measure of his injustice. If he has no good deeds left, he will bear the evil deeds of the one he has oppressed.”
q: Whoever wrongs his brother in his honor or anything else should resolve the matter today before it cannot be resolved with gold and silver coins. If he has good deeds to his credit, they will be taken from him according to the measure of his injustice. If he has no good deeds left, he will bear the evil deeds of the one he has oppressed

title: Hadith on Tribalism: The Prophet rejects tribalism, terrorism
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever withdraws from lawful obedience to the leader and divides the community and dies in this state, he will have died upon ignorance. Whoever fights under a banner of blindness, raging for the sake of tribalism, or calling to tribalism, or supporting tribalism and he is killed in this state, he will have died upon ignorance. Whoever rebels against my nation, striking the righteous and wicked alike, sparing not even their believers and he does not fulfill the pledge of security to whom it is due, he has nothing to do with me and I have nothing to do with him.”
q: Whoever withdraws from lawful obedience to the leader and divides the community and dies in this state, he will have died upon ignorance. Whoever fights under a banner of blindness, raging for the sake of tribalism, or calling to tribalism, or supporting tribalism and he is killed in this state, he will have died upon ignorance. Whoever rebels against my nation, striking the righteous and wicked alike, sparing not even their believers and he does not fulfill the pledge of security to whom it is due, he has nothing to do with me and I have nothing to do with him

title: Hadith on Generosity: The Prophet gives charity without fear of poverty
t:
Anas ibn Malik reported:  The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was never asked anything for the sake of Islam but that he would give it. A man came to the Prophet and he gave him many sheep, so the man returned to his people and he said, “O my people! Embrace Islam, for Muhammad gives in charity as if he has no fear of poverty!”

In another narration, Anas said, “Indeed, a man would embrace Islam desiring worldly gains. He would not practice Islam but for a while, until Islam became more beloved to him than the world and everything in it.”

title: Hadith on Tashahhud: What to say when sitting in prayer
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: While praying behind the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, we were saying, “Peace be upon Allah, peace be upon this person.” The Prophet told us one day, “Verily, Allah Himself is Peace. When one of you sits in prayer, let him say, ‘Greetings, prayers, and good things are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah.’ If you say that, it will reach every righteous servant in the heavens and the earth. Then, say, ‘I bear witness there is no God but Allah, and I bear witness Muhammad is His servant and His messenger.’ Then, you may ask for whatever you wish.”
q: Verily, Allah Himself is Peace. When one of you sits in prayer, let him say, ‘Greetings, prayers, and good things are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah.’ If you say that, it will reach every righteous servant in the heavens and the earth. Then, say, ‘I bear witness there is no God but Allah, and I bear witness Muhammad is His servant and His messenger.’ Then, you may ask for whatever you wish.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Huquq: Guarding rights of women and orphans
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, I have issued a warning regarding the rights of two vulnerable groups: orphans and women.”
q: O Allah, I have issued a warning regarding the rights of two vulnerable groups: orphans and women.

title: Hadith on Rahmah: Allah’s mercy surpasses His wrath
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Allah completed the creation, He wrote in His book with Him upon the Throne: Verily, My mercy prevails over My wrath.”
q: When Allah completed the creation, He wrote in His book with Him upon the Throne: Verily, My mercy prevails over My wrath.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ihsan: Allah has prescribed excellence in all things
t: Shaddad ibn Aws reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has prescribed excellence in everything. If you have to kill, kill in the best manner. If you have to slaughter, slaughter in the best manner. Let one of you sharpen his knife, so his animal is spared of suffering.”
q: Verily, Allah has prescribed excellence in everything. If you have to kill, kill in the best manner. If you have to slaughter, slaughter in the best manner. Let one of you sharpen his knife, so his animal is spared of suffering.

title: Hadith on Anger: Do not get angry, do not get angry
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man came to the Prophet and he said, “Advise me.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not be angry.” The man repeated his request and the Prophet said, “Do not be angry.”
q: Do not be angry … Do not be angry

title: Hadith on Sunnah: Follow the Prophet, beware of innovation
t: Al-‘Irbad ibn Sariyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed with us one day. Then, he faced us and delivered an eloquent sermon that brought tears to our eyes and hearts were shaken by it. It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, it is as if this is a farewell address. What do you instruct for us?” The Prophet said, “I advise you to fear Allah, listen, and obey, even if an Abyssinian slave is put in charge of you. Whoever lives after me will see many conflicts. You must adhere to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the righteous, guided successors. Hold firmly to it as if biting with your molar teeth. Beware of newly invented matters in religion, for every new matter is an innovation, and every innovation is misguidance.”
q: I advise you to fear Allah, listen, and obey, even if an Abyssinian slave is put in charge of you. Whoever lives after me will see many conflicts. You must adhere to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the righteous, guided successors. Hold firmly to it as if biting with your molar teeth. Beware of newly invented matters in religion, for every new matter is an innovation, and every innovation is misguidance.

title: Hadith on Qunut: Supplication for performing Witr prayer
t: Hasan ibn Ali reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, taught me some words to say in the Witr prayer, “O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, secure me among those You have secured, protect me among those You have protected, bless me in what You have given me, and save me from the evil You have decreed. Verily, You alone decree and none can issue decree over You. Verily, he cannot be humiliated whoever is protected by You. Blessed are You, our Lord, the Almighty.”
q: O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, secure me among those You have secured, protect me among those You have protected, bless me in what You have given me, and save me from the evil You have decreed. Verily, You alone decree and none can issue decree over You. Verily, he cannot be humiliated whoever is protected by You. Blessed are You, our Lord, the Almighty

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: Believers are one body in compassion
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The parable of the believers in their affection, mercy, and compassion for each other is that of a body. When any limb aches, the whole body reacts with sleeplessness and fever.”
q: The parable of the believers in their affection, mercy, and compassion for each other is that of a body. When any limb aches, the whole body reacts with sleeplessness and fever.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Peace: True wealth is contentment of the soul
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Wealth is not in having many possessions. Rather, true wealth is the richness of the soul.”
q: Wealth … is not in having many possessions. Rather, true wealth is the richness of the soul.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Rahmah: The Prophet’s forbearance with a bedouin
t: Abu Huraira reported: A bedouin entered the mosque of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while the Prophet was sitting. The man prayed, and when finished, he said, “O Allah, have mercy upon me and Muhammad and no one else.” The Prophet turned to him and he said, “You have restricted something vast.” It was not long before he was urinating in the mosque, so the people rushed to him, but the Prophet said, “Pour a bucket or a tumbler of water over it. You have only been sent to make things easy, and you were not sent to make things difficult.”
q: You have restricted something vast … Pour a bucket or a tumbler of water over it. … You have only been sent to make things easy, and you were not sent to make things difficult.

title: Hadith on Qadr: Be mindful of Allah, He will protect you
t: Ibn Abbas reported: I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when he said to me, “Young man, I will teach you some words. Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. If you ask, ask from Allah. If you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the nations gathered together to benefit you, they could not benefit you unless Allah has decreed it for you. And if the nations gathered together to harm you, they could not harm you unless Allah has decreed it for you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.”
q: Young man, I will teach you some words. Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. If you ask, ask from Allah. If you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the nations gathered together to benefit you, they could not benefit you unless Allah has decreed it for you. And if the nations gathered together to harm you, they could not harm you unless Allah has decreed it for you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried

title: Hadith on Slavery: No servant should be called a ‘slave’
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not refer to anyone as ‘my slave,’ for all of you are the slaves of Allah. Rather, you should refer to him as ‘my young man.’ The servant should not refer to anyone as ‘my lord,’ but rather he should refer to him as ‘my master.’”
q: Do not refer to anyone as ‘my slave,’ for all of you are the slaves of Allah. Rather, you should refer to him as ‘my young man.’ The servant should not refer to anyone as ‘my lord,’ but rather he should refer to him as ‘my master

title: Hadith on Akhirah: Whoever has faith eventually enters Paradise
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Gabriel, upon him be peace, came to me to give the good news that anyone from my nation who dies without associating partners with Allah will eventually enter Paradise.” I said, “Even if he commits adultery and theft?” The Prophet said, “Even if he commits adultery and theft.” And the Prophet said, “Even if he drinks wine.”
q: Even if he drinks wine.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Praise Allah in all situations after sneezing
t: Nafi’ reported: A man sneezed beside Ibn Umar, saying, “All praise is due to Allah and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah!” Ibn Umar said, “I also say all praise is due to Allah and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah, but this is not what the Messenger of Allah taught us, peace and blessings be upon him. Rather, the Prophet taught us to say: All praise is due to Allah in every circumstance.”
q: All praise is due to Allah in every circumstance.

title: Hadith on Munkar: Whoever sees evil should change it if possible
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever among you sees evil, let him change it with his hand. If he cannot do so, then with his tongue. If he cannot do so, then with his heart, which is the weakest level of faith.”
q: Whoever among you sees evil, let him change it with his hand. If he cannot do so, then with his tongue. If he cannot do so, then with his heart, which is the weakest level of faith

title: Hadith on Curses: Do not invoke the Hellfire
t: Samurah ibn Jundab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not curse each other with the curse of Allah, nor invoke His wrath, nor invoke the Hellfire.”
q: Do not curse each other with the curse of Allah, nor invoke His wrath, nor invoke the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Shaytan: Do not curse Satan, rather mention Allah
t: Abu al-Malih reported: A man said, “I was riding on a mount behind the Prophet, and it stumbled, so I said: May Satan perish!” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not say: May Satan perish! If you say that, he will swell with pride until he becomes as big as a house, and he says: By my might! Rather, you should say: In the name of Allah. If you say that, he will shrink until he becomes as small as a fly.”
q: Do not say: May Satan perish! If you say that, he will swell with pride until he becomes as big as a house, and he says: By my might! Rather, you should say: In the name of Allah. If you say that, he will shrink until he becomes as small as a fly

title: Hadith on Neighbors: The best neighbor is best to his neighbors
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best companion to Allah is the best to his companions, and the best neighbor to Allah is the best to his neighbors.”
q: The best companion to Allah is the best to his companions, and the best neighbor to Allah is the best to his neighbors

title: Hadith on Treachery: Betrayal exposed to all on Judgment Day
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Allah gathers the earlier and later generations on the Day of Resurrection, He will raise a banner for every treacherous liar. It will be announced that this is the betrayal of this person, the son of this person.”
q: When Allah gathers the earlier and later generations on the Day of Resurrection, He will raise a banner for every treacherous liar. It will be announced that this is the betrayal of this person, the son of this person
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Covenants: Whoever betrays peace treaty not enter Paradise
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever kills a person protected by a treaty without a just cause, Allah has forbidden Paradise for him.”
q: Whoever kills a person protected by a treaty without a just cause, Allah has forbidden Paradise for him

title: Hadith on Covenants: Believers do not commit assassination
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Faith has restrained assassination. A believer does not assassinate.”
q: Faith has restrained assassination. A believer does not assassinate
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Muhammad: I knew his was not the face of a liar
t: Abdullah ibn Salaam reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to Medina, the people rushed toward him and it was said, “The Messenger of Allah has come!” I came along with the people to see him and when I looked at the face of the Prophet, I realized that his face was not the face of a liar. The first thing the Prophet said was this, “O people, spread peace, feed the hungry, and pray at night when people are sleeping. You will enter Paradise in peace.”
q: O people, spread peace, feed the hungry, and pray at night when people are sleeping. You will enter Paradise in peace

title: Hadith on Akhlaq: Fear Allah everywhere, have good character
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Fear Allah wherever you are, follow a bad deed with a good deed and it will erase it, and behave with good character towards people.”
q: Fear … Allah wherever you are, follow a bad deed with a good deed and it will erase it, and behave with good character towards people

title: Hadith on Sabr: Ahead are days of persecution and trial
t: Abu Tha’labah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Rather, you must enjoin good and forbid evil until you see greed being obeyed, desires being followed, worldly life being preferred, and everyone is impressed by their own opinion. Then you must take care of yourself and leave the common people. Verily, ahead of you are days of patience in which patience will be like grasping a hot coal. The one who does good deeds in that time will have the reward of fifty men who do likewise.”
q: Rather, you must enjoin good and forbid evil until you see greed being obeyed, desires being followed, worldly life being preferred, and everyone is impressed by their own opinion. Then you must take care of yourself and leave the common people. Verily, ahead of you are days of patience in which patience will be like grasping a hot coal. The one who does good deeds in that time will have the reward of fifty men who do likewise

title: Hadith on Salat: Allah forgives whoever prays the five prayers
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty has made the five prayers an obligation. Whoever performs their ablution well, prays them at their proper time, and completes their bowing with the reverence due to them, then Allah has promised to forgive him. Whoever does not do so has no promise from Allah. If He wills, He will forgive him, and if He wills, He will punish Him.”
q: Allah Almighty has made the five prayers an obligation. Whoever performs their ablution well, prays them at their proper time, and completes their bowing with the reverence due to them, then Allah has promised to forgive him. Whoever does not do so has no promise from Allah. If He wills, He will forgive him, and if He wills, He will punish Him.

title: Hadith on ‘Asabiyyah: Whoever supports tribalism is like a dead camel
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever supports his own people in their oppression is like a camel that falls dead into a well and is pulled out by its tail.”
q: Whoever supports his own people in their oppression is like a camel that falls dead into a well and is pulled out by its tail

title: Hadith on Ijtihad: Sincere judge is rewarded, even if wrong
t: Amr ibn al-‘As reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a judge makes a ruling, striving to apply his reasoning and he is correct, he will have two rewards. If a judge makes a ruling, striving to apply his reasoning and he is mistaken, he will have one reward.”
q: If a judge makes a ruling, striving to apply his reasoning … and he is correct, he will have two rewards. If a judge makes a ruling, striving to apply his reasoning and he is mistaken, he will have one reward
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ikhtilaf: Companions interpret the Prophet’s order differently
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, made an announcement on the day he returned from the Confederates, saying, “No one will pray his noon prayer unless he is among the tribe of Qurayzah.” Some people feared that the time for prayer would expire, so they performed their prayers before reaching Qurayzah. Others said, “We will only perform our prayer where the Prophet has ordered us to pray, even if the time expires.” When the Prophet heard this, he did not rebuke anyone from the two groups.
q: No one will pray his noon prayer unless he is among the tribe of Qurayzah
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salat: Unmindful prayers only partially rewarded
t: ‘Ammar ibn Yasir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, a man may return from his prayer and nothing good is written for him but a tenth of his prayer, or a ninth, or an eighth, or a seventh, or a sixth, or a fifth, or a fourth, or a third, or a half.”
q: Verily, a man may return from his prayer and nothing good is written for him but a tenth of his prayer, or a ninth, or an eighth, or a seventh, or a sixth, or a fifth, or a fourth, or a third, or a half

title: Hadith on Refutation: The Prophet criticizes without shaming
t: Aisha reported: If the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, heard something bad about a man, he would not name him by saying, “What is the matter with this person that he says this?” Rather, the Prophet would say, “What is the matter with some people who say this?”
q: “What is the matter with some people who say this

title: Hadith on Hijrah: No obligatory emigration after end of persecution
t: ‘Ata bin Abi Rabah reported: I visited Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, with ‘Ubayd bin ‘Umayr to ask her about emigration. Aisha said, “There is no emigration today. One of the believers would flee with his religion to Allah Almighty and to his messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, fearing persecution for it. Today, Allah has made Islam prevail and a believer may worship his Lord wherever he wishes. Rather, there is only jihad and good intentions.”

title: Hadith on Hijrah: Allah accepts good deeds wherever you are
t: Abu Sa’id reported: A bedouin came to the Prophet and asked him about emigration. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Woe to you! The matter of emigration is difficult. Have you got some camels?” The man said yes. The Prophet said, “Do you pay its charity?” The man said yes. The Prophet said, “Do you let them be used by others?” The man said yes. The Prophet said, “Do you milk them on the proper day?” The man said yes. The Prophet said, “Then do good deeds beyond the sea, for Allah will never disregard any of your deeds.”
q: Woe to you! The matter of emigration is difficult. Have you got some camels? … Do you pay its charity? … Do you let them be used by others? … Do you milk them on the proper day? … Then do good deeds beyond the sea, for Allah will never disregard any of your deeds
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Justice: Allah treats you as you treat others
t: Abu Sirmah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever harms others, Allah will harm him. Whoever is harsh with others, Allah will be harsh with him.”
q: Whoever harms others, Allah will harm him. Whoever is harsh with others, Allah will be harsh with him

title: Hadith on Kindness: The Prophet visits his Jewish servant
t: Anas reported: A young Jewish boy used to serve the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he became sick, so the Prophet went to visit him. The Prophet sat near his head and asked him to accept Islam. The boy looked at his father, who was sitting next to him, and he told him, “Obey Abu al-Qasim,” and so the boy embraced Islam. The Prophet came out saying, “All praise is due to Allah, who has saved him from the Hellfire.”
q: All praise is due to Allah, who has saved him from the Hellfire

title: Hadith on Justice: Applying legal punishments with due process
t: Abu Huraira reported: Sa’d ibn ‘Ubadah said, “O Messenger of Allah, if I find another man with my wife, should I leave him alone until I bring four witnesses?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Yes.” Sa’d said, “Never! By the One who sent you with the truth, if that happened to me I would quickly grab the sword!” The Prophet said, “Listen to what your leader is saying. Verily, he has a sense of honor, and I have a greater sense of honor than him, and Allah has a greater sense of honor than me.”
q: Yes … Listen to what your leader is saying … Verily, he has a sense of honor, … and I have a greater sense of honor than him, and Allah has a greater sense of honor than me

title: Hadith on Forbearance: Reconcile, forgive your wrongdoers
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amr reported: I met the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said to me, “O ‘Uqbah, reconcile with whoever cuts you off, give to whoever deprives you, and forgive whoever wrongs you.”
q: O ‘Uqbah, reconcile with whoever cuts you off, give to whoever deprives you, and forgive whoever wrongs you.

title: Hadith on Shaytan: Satan incites hatred among believers
t: Jabir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Satan has given up that those who pray will ever worship him, so rather he incites discord between them.”
q: Verily, Satan has given up that those who pray will ever worship him, so rather he incites discord between them.

title: Hadith on Adab: Paradise guaranteed for those with good character
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I guarantee a house on the outskirts of Paradise for one who leaves arguments even if he is right, and a house in the middle of Paradise for one who abandons lies even when joking, and a house in the highest part of Paradise for one who makes his character excellent.”
q: “I guarantee a house on the outskirts of Paradise for one who leaves arguments even if he is right, and a house in the middle of Paradise for one who abandons lies even when joking, and a house in the highest part of Paradise for one who makes his character excellent.”

title: Hadith on Rifq: Deprived of kindness, deprived of goodness
t: Jarir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is deprived of the characteristic of gentleness is deprived of all goodness.”
q: Whoever is deprived of the characteristic of gentleness is deprived of all goodness.

title: Hadith on Medina: The Prophet’s city expels impurity like a furnace
t: Jabir reported: A bedouin came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and gave the pledge of allegiance for embracing Islam. The next day he came with a fever and he said, “Cancel my pledge.” The Prophet refused three times and he said, “Medina is like a furnace. It expels its impurities and makes use of what is pure.”
q: Medina is like a furnace. It expels its impurities and makes use of what is pure
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jihad: March forward with the best behavior
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to his army, “Depart in the name of Allah, and with Allah, upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah. Do not kill elders, nor children, nor young ones, nor women. Do not plunder, but rather collect your spoils. Behave righteously and in the best manner. Verily, Allah loves those who behave in the best manner.”
q: Depart in the name of Allah, and with Allah, upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah. Do not kill elders, nor children, nor young ones, nor women. Do not plunder, but rather collect your spoils. Behave righteously and in the best manner. Verily, Allah loves those who behave in the best manner.
gf: Hasan li ghayrihi (fair due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Charity: Upper hand that gives is better than receiving
t: Abu Umamah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O son of Adam, to offer your surplus in charity is better for you, and to withhold it is evil for you, yet there is no blame to keep what is needed. Start by giving to your dependents, for the upper hand is better than the lower hand.”
q: O son of Adam, to offer your surplus in charity is better for you, and to withhold it is evil for you, yet there is no blame to keep what is needed. Start by giving to your dependents, for the upper hand is better than the lower hand

title: Hadith on Mercy: Angel offers to destroy a town, but the Prophet relents
t: Aisha reported: She asked the Prophet, “Have you encountered a harder day than the battle of Uhud?” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have met your people as they are, and the worst of it was the day of ‘Aqabah as I had an audience with Ibn ‘Abd Yalil ibn ‘Abd Kulal. He did not respond as I had hoped, so I departed with grief upon my face. I could not recover until I reached Qarn al-Tha’alib, then I raised my head to behold a cloud shading me. I looked again to behold the Angel Gabriel within it, calling out to me, ‘Verily, Allah has heard what your people said to you and their response. He has sent the Angel of the Mountains for you to command as you wish regarding them.’ The Angel of the Mountains called out to greet me with peace, then he said, ‘O Muhammad, speak as you wish.
