I will crush them under two mountains if that is your desire.’ I said, ‘No, rather I hope Allah will bring out from their progeny those who would worship Allah alone without associating any partners with Him.”
q: I have met your people as they are, and the worst of it was the day of ‘Aqabah as I had an audience with Ibn ‘Abd Yalil ibn ‘Abd Kulal. He did not respond as I had hoped, so I departed with grief upon my face. I could not recover until I reached Qarn al-Tha’alib, then I raised my head to behold a cloud shading me. I looked again to behold the Angel Gabriel within it, calling out to me, ‘Verily, Allah has heard what your people said to you and their response. He has sent the Angel of the Mountains for you to command as you wish regarding them.’ The Angel of the Mountains called out to greet me with peace, then he said, ‘O Muhammad, speak as you wish. I will crush them under two mountains if that is your desire.’ I said, ‘No, rather I hope Allah will bring out from their progeny those who would worship Allah alone without associating any partners with Him.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tawbah: If you did not sin, Allah would replace you
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you did not sin, Allah would replace you with people who would sin, and they would seek forgiveness from Allah and He would forgive them.”
q: By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you did not sin, Allah would replace you with people who would sin, and they would seek forgiveness from Allah and He would forgive them

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: Allah helps him as long as he helps his brother
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever relieves the hardship of a believer in this world, Allah will relieve his hardship on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever helps ease one in difficulty, Allah will make it easy for him in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever conceals the faults of a Muslim, Allah will conceal his faults in this world and the Hereafter. Allah helps the servant as long as he helps his brother. Whoever travels a path in search of knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise. People do not gather in the houses of Allah, reciting the Book of Allah and studying it together, but that tranquility will descend upon them, mercy will cover them, angels will surround them, and Allah will mention them to those near Him. Whoever is slow to good deeds will not be hastened by his lineage.”
q: Whoever relieves the hardship of a believer in this world, Allah will relieve his hardship on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever helps ease one in difficulty, Allah will make it easy for him in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever conceals the faults of a Muslim, Allah will conceal his faults in this world and the Hereafter. Allah helps the servant as long as he helps his brother. Whoever travels a path in search of knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise. People do not gather in the houses of Allah, reciting the Book of Allah and studying it together, but that tranquility will descend upon them, mercy will cover them, angels will surround them, and Allah will mention them to those near Him. Whoever is slow to good deeds will not be hastened by his lineage

title: Hadith on Jihad: Greatest jihad a word of justice to a tyrant
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among the greatest acts of jihad is a word of justice before a tyrannical ruler.”
q: Verily, among the greatest acts of jihad is a word of justice before a tyrannical ruler

title: Hadith on Servants: A slave who is beaten is set free
t: Suwayd ibn Muqarrin reported: He had a slave girl and someone slapped her, so he said to him, “Did you not know that it is forbidden to strike the face? I was the seventh of my brothers during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessing be upon him, and we had only one servant. One of us became enraged and slapped him, so the Prophet commanded us to set him free.”

title: Hadith on Women: Criticism of men who beat their wives
t: Abdullah bin Zam’ah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “How does one of you beat his wife as he beats a stallion or a slave and then embrace her?”
q: How does one of you beat his wife as he beats a stallion or a slave and then embrace her

title: Hadith on Torture: Allah will punish those who torture people
t: Hisham ibn Hakim reported: He passed by some people in Syria who had been forced to stand in the sun, and oil was poured over their heads. Hisham said, “What is this?” It was said, “They are being punished for not paying taxes.” Hisham said, “I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: Verily, Allah will torture those who tortured people in this world.”
q: Verily, … Allah will torture those who tortured people in this world

title: Hadith on Women: Best of you are kind to their women
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most complete of believers in faith are those with the best character, and the best of you are the best in behavior to their women.”
q: The most complete of believers in faith are those with the best character, and the best of you are the best in behavior to their women

title: Hadith on Zina: Allah decreed for everyone a portion of adultery
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has decreed upon the son of Adam his portion of adultery that he will inevitably commit: the adultery of the two eyes is a lustful look, the adultery of the tongue is obscene speech. The soul yearns and craves for what the passions will indulge or deny.”
q: Verily, Allah has decreed upon the son of Adam his portion of adultery that he will inevitably commit: the adultery of the two eyes is a lustful look, the adultery of the tongue is obscene speech. The soul yearns and craves for what … the passions will indulge or deny
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Killing: The Prophet warns bloodshed leads to unbelief
t: Jarir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, asked me to make the people quiet on the occasion of the farewell pilgrimage. Then, the Prophet said, “Do not return to unbelief after me by striking the necks of one another.”
q: Do not return to unbelief after me by striking the necks of one another
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Two phrases are easy, highly rewarded
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Two words are beloved to the Most Merciful. They are light on the tongue but heavy on the scale: Glory and praise to Allah, and glory to Allah the Almighty.”
q: Two words are beloved to the Most Merciful. They are light on the tongue but heavy on the scale: Glory and praise to Allah, and glory to Allah the Almighty
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity greed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Mercy: I will forgive you without reservation
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: O son of Adam, if you call upon Me and place your hope in Me, I will forgive you despite what is within you and I will not hesitate. O son of Adam, if you have sins piling up to the clouds and then ask for My forgiveness, I will forgive you without hesitation. O son of Adam, if you come to Me with enough sins to fill the earth and then you meet Me without associating anything with Me, I will come to you with enough forgiveness to fill the earth.”

title: Farewell Sermon: Your Lord is one, your father is one
t: Abu Nadrah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said during the days after the pilgrimage, “O people, your Lord is one and your father Adam is one. There is no favor of an Arab over a foreigner, nor a foreigner over an Arab, and neither white skin over black skin, nor black skin over white skin, except by righteousness. Have I not delivered the message?” They said, “The Messenger of Allah has delivered the message.”
q: O people, your Lord is one and your father Adam is one. There is no favor of an Arab over a foreigner, nor a foreigner over an Arab, and neither white skin over black skin, nor black skin over white skin, except by righteousness. Have I not delivered the message

title: Khutbah al-Hajah: How to begin a Khutbah Sermon in Arabic and English
t:
In the name of Allah, the Gracious, the Merciful

Click here for ready-made printable instructions in PDF format

When the preacher (khatib) begins his sermon, he should say the following words in Arabic, along with the English translation if the audience primarily speaks English.

Note: This is not the only permissible formula that can be used, but it is popular and in accordance with the authentic Sunnah as recorded in Sunan Ibn Mājah 1892 and Sunan al-Nasā’ī 1578. Allah knows best.

The preacher should begin, saying:

In the name of Allah, the Gracious, the Merciful

All praise is due to Allah. We praise him, we seek His help, we seek His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Allah from the evil within ourselves and our evil deeds. Whoever Allah guides, there is none to misguide him. Whoever Allah leads astray, there is none to guide him. I testify there is no God but Allah alone, without any partners, and that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, is His servant and His messenger.

Allah Almighty said, “O you who have faith, fear Allah as it is His right to be feared and do not die unless you are Muslims,” (3:102)

And Allah Almighty said, “Fear Allah, from whom you ask each other, and in your family ties, for Allah is ever watchful over you,” (4:1)

And Allah Almighty said, “Fear Allah and speak words as befitting. He will amend your deeds for you and forgive your sins. Whoever obeys Allah and His messenger has achieved a great triumph.” (33:70-71)

The truest word is the Book of Allah and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad. The most evil matters are those that are newly invented, for every newly invented matter is an innovation. Every innovation is misguidance, and every misguidance is in the Hellfire.

To proceed (and then begin the sermon)…
q: Click here for ready-made printable instructions in PDF format

title: Hadith on Tahajjud: Allah descends in the last third of the night
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Our Lord Almighty descends to the lowest heaven in the last third of every night, saying: Who is calling upon Me that I may answer him? Who is asking from Me that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness that I may forgive him?”
q: Our Lord Almighty descends to the lowest heaven in the last third of every night, saying: Who is calling upon Me that I may answer him? Who is asking from Me that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness that I may forgive him?
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Charity: Every tree a Muslim plants is rewarded as charity
t: Anas bin Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No Muslim plants a tree or sows a seed and then a bird, or a human, or an animal eats from it but that it is charity for him.”
q: No Muslim plants a tree or sows a seed and then a bird, or a human, or an animal eats from it but that it is charity for him.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Treachery: Strict prohibition on betraying peace treaties
t: Sulaym ibn Amir reported: There was a peace treaty between Mu’awiyah and the Romans. He was marching towards their country, and when the treaty ended, he would surprise attack them. A man came on a horse, saying, “Allah is the Greatest! Let there be faithfulness and not treachery!” They found that he was ‘Amr ibn ‘Abasah. Mu’awiyah sent for him and questioned him about that. ‘Amr said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say, “If one has a covenant with people, he must not strengthen or loosen it until its term comes to an end, or he brings it to an end in agreement with them.” Thus, Mu’awiyah returned with the people.
q: If one has a covenant with people, he must not strengthen or loosen it until its term comes to an end, or he brings it to an end in agreement with them

title: Hadith on Hijrah: Live anywhere as long as you practice Islam
t: Salih ibn Bashir reported: Fudayk came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, they argue that whomever does not make emigration will be ruined.” The Prophet said, “O Fudayk, establish prayer, avoid sins, and live in the land with your people wherever you wish.”
q: O Fud … ayk, establish prayer, avoid sins, and live in the land with your people wherever you wish
gf: Sahih (authentic) according to Ibn Abdul Barr

title: Hadith on Ghuraba: Righteous strangers among many evil people
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “We are in such a time when the strangers are blessed.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, who are the strangers?” The Prophet said, “Righteous people among many evil people. Those who disobey them are more numerous than those who obey them.”
q: We are in such a time when the strangers are blessed … Righteous people among many evil people. Those who disobey them are more numerous than those who obey them

title: Hadith on Hamd: O Allah, You are as You praised Yourself
t: Aisha reported: One night in bed, I missed the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, so I looked for him and my hand touched his feet while he was in prostration. They were raised, and the Prophet was saying, “O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger and in Your forgiveness from Your punishment. I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot fully praise You, for You are as You have praised Yourself.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger and in Your forgiveness from Your punishment. I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot fully praise You, for You are as You have praised Yourself

title: Hadith on Faith: Until he loves goodness for his brother
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, a servant does not have faith until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself of goodness.”
q: By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, a servant does not have faith until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself of goodness

title: Hadith on Distress: Dua to say when anxious or depressed
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A servant is not struck by worry or grief but let him say, ‘O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant, the son of Your maidservant. My forelock is in Your hand, Your decision over me has passed, and Your decree upon me is in justice. I ask You by every name with which You have named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to one of Your creatures, or kept hidden in the Unseen with You, that You make the Quran the spring of my heart, the light within me, the banisher of my depression, and the expeller of my anxiety,’ then Allah will expel his worry and replace his grief with joy.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, shall we not study these words?” The Prophet said, “Of course, whoever hears them should study them.”
q: A servant is not struck by worry or grief but let him say, ‘O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant, the son of Your maidservant. My forelock is in Your hand, Your decision over me has passed, and Your decree upon me is in justice. I ask You by every name with which You have named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to one of Your creatures, or kept hidden in the Unseen with You, that You make the Quran the spring of my heart, the light within me, the banisher of my depression, and the expeller of my anxiety,’ then Allah will expel his worry and replace his grief with joy. … Of course, whoever hears them should study them

title: Hadith on Creation: Were they created by nothing?
t: Jubayr bin Mut’im reported: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, reciting Surat al-Tur in the evening prayer. When the Prophet reached this verse, “Were they created by nothing, or were they creators of themselves? Did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain!” (52:35-36), I felt my heart was about to fly.
q: Were they created by nothing, or were they creators of themselves? Did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain!

title: Hadith on Ghuraba: Islam began as strange, blessed are strangers
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Islam began as something strange and it will return to being strange, so blessed are the strangers.”
q: Islam began as something strange and it will return to being strange, so blessed are the strangers

title: Hadith on Law: No harming yourself or harming others
t: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, issued a decree, “Do not cause harm or return harm.”
q: Do not cause harm or return harm

title: Hadith on Allah: Glory of Allah revealed would consume all creation
t: Abu Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah Almighty does not sleep, nor is it befitting that He sleeps. He lowers and raises the balance of justice. Deeds ascend to him by night before the work of the day, and deeds ascend to him by day before the work of the night. His veil is light. If He were to reveal Himself, the splendor of His countenance would consume His creation as far as the eye can see.”
q: Verily, Allah Almighty does not sleep, nor is it befitting that He sleeps. He lowers and raises the balance of justice. Deeds ascend to him by night before the work of the day, and deeds ascend to him by day before the work of the night. His veil is light. If He were to reveal Himself, the splendor of His countenance would consume His creation as far as the eye can see

title: Hadith on Fear: Man who cremated himself, afraid of Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man had indulged himself in sin. When death approached, he enjoined his sons, saying: When I die, you should burn me, pulverize me, and scatter me to the winds over the sea. By Allah, if Allah is capable, He will punish me in such a way as He has not punished anyone else. They did that to him, and when he stood before his Lord, Allah said to him: What made you do what you did? The man said: Fear and awe of You, O Lord. Thus, Allah forgave him due to that.”
q: A man had indulged himself in sin. When death approached, he enjoined his sons, saying: When I die, you should burn me, pulverize me, and scatter me to the winds over the sea. By Allah, if Allah is capable, He will punish me in such a way as He has not punished anyone else. … They did that to him, and when he stood before his Lord, Allah said to him: What made you do what you did? The man said: Fear and awe of You, O Lord. Thus, Allah forgave him due to that.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authentic) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Angels supplicate for you as you do for others
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No Muslim servant supplicates for his brother behind his back but that the angel says: And for you the same.”
q: No Muslim servant supplicates for his brother behind his back but that the angel says: And for you the same

title: Hadith on Salaam: If you can end conflicts in peace, do so
t: Ali ibn Abi Talib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, after me there will be conflicts or affairs, so if you can end them in peace, then do so.”
q: Verily, after me there will be conflicts or affairs, so if you can end them in peace, then do so

title: Hadith on Dua: Your final supplication before sleep
t: Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When you go to sleep, perform ablution as for your prayer, then lie down on your right side and say: O Allah, I submit my face to You, I entrust my affair to You, and I commit myself to You, in hope and in fear of You. There is no refuge or place of safety but with You. I believe in the Book You have revealed, and in the Prophet You have sent.“ Then, the Prophet said, “Make these your last words. If you died in this night of yours, you will have died upon pure nature.”
q: When you go to sleep, perform ablution as for your prayer, then lie down on your right side and say: O Allah, I submit my face to You, I entrust my affair to You, and I commit myself to You, in hope and in fear of You. There is no refuge or place of safety but with You. I believe in the Book You have revealed, and in the Prophet You have sent. …  … Make these your last words. If you died in this night of yours, you will have died upon pure nature
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fasting: Best fast after Ramadan is Muharram
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best prayer after the prescribed prayers is a prayer offered in the middle of the night. The best fast after the month of Ramadan is fasting in the month of Allah, al-Muharram.”
q: The best prayer after the prescribed prayers is … a … prayer offered in the middle of the night. The best fast after the month of Ramadan is fasting in the month of Allah, al-Muharram.

title: Hadith on Faith: Until he loves people as he loves himself
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None of you has faith until he loves for people what he loves for himself, and until he loves a person only for the sake of Allah Almighty.”
q: None of you has faith until he loves for people what he loves for himself, and until he loves a person only for the sake of Allah Almighty.

title: Hadith on Tazkiyyah: Man in Paradise for purifying his heart
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “A man from the people of Paradise is coming to you.” A man from the Ansar came, his beard disheveled by the water of ablution, and he was carrying both of his shoes with his left hand. The next day, the Prophet repeated the same words, and the man came in the same condition. On the third day, the Prophet repeated the same words again, and the man came in the same condition again. When the Prophet stood up to leave, Abdullah ibn Amr followed the man and said to him, “I am in an argument with my father, and I have sworn not to enter my home for three days. May I stay with you?” The man said yes. Abdullah stayed three nights with the man, but he never saw him praying at night. Whenever he went to bed, the man would remember Allah and rest until he woke up for morning prayer. Abdullah said that he had never heard anything but good words coming from his mouth. When three nights had passed, and he did not see anything special about his actions, Abdullah asked him, “O servant of Allah, I have not been in an argument with my father, nor have I cut off relations with him. I heard the Prophet say three times that a man from the people of Paradise was coming to us, and then you came. I thought I would stay with you to see what you are doing that I could follow, but I did not see you do many good deeds. Why did the Prophet convey this about you?” The man said, “There is nothing else but what you see here, except that I find no malevolence within myself towards the Muslims, nor do I envy anyone for the good that Allah has given them.” Abdullah said, “This is what was conveyed about you, but it is something we have been unable to do.”
q: A man from the people of Paradise is coming to you

title: Hadith on Jihad: Do not desire to fight, war a last resort
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not wish to meet the enemy in battle, but if you meet them, be steadfast.”
q: Do not wish to meet the enemy in battle, but if you meet them, be steadfast.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Destiny: People seal their fate with deeds at end of life
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, a man may act with the deeds of the people of Paradise for a long time, then he ends his life acting with the deeds of the people of Hellfire. And a man may act with the deeds of the people of Hellfire for a long time, then he ends his life acting with the deeds of the people of Paradise.”
q: Verily, a man may act with the deeds of the people of Paradise for a long time, then he ends his life acting with the deeds of the people of Hellfire. And a man may act with the deeds of the people of Hellfire for a long time, then he ends his life acting with the deeds of the people of Paradise

title: Hadith on 99 Names: Whoever acts upon them enters Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah has ninety-nine names. Whoever preserves them will enter Paradise.”
q: Allah has ninety-nine names. Whoever preserves them will enter Paradise
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Eid: Let them play and sing on Eid
t: Aisha reported: Abu Bakr came to her on the day of Eid while the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was with her and there were two girls singing songs of the Ansar on the day of Bu’ath. Abu Bakr said twice, “Musical instruments of Satan!” The Prophet said, “Leave them Abu Bakr. Verily, every community has a celebration and this day is our celebration.”
q: Leave them Abu Bakr. Verily, every community has a celebration and this day is our celebration.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Zuhd: The Prophet supplicates only for basic needs
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Allah, make provision for the family of Muhammad sufficiently nourishing.”
q: O Allah, make provision for the family of Muhammad sufficiently nourishing.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Women: The Prophet ensures education for women
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and she said, “O Messenger of Allah, only the men benefit from your speeches. Set a day for us when we can come to you and you will teach us what Allah has taught you.” The Prophet said, “Gather on an upcoming day at this place.” They gathered and the Prophet came and taught them what Allah had taught him. The Prophet said, “No woman among you will lose three children but that they will shield her from the Hellfire.” A woman said, “O Messenger of Allah, what if she only lost two children?” She repeated her question. The Prophet said three times, “Even two.”
q: Gather on an upcoming day at this place … No woman among you will lose three children but that they will shield her from the Hellfire … Even two.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hudhayfah on Balance: Straight path does not swerve right or left
t: Hammam reported: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O townspeople, remain upright and you will have taken a great lead, but if you swerve right or left, you will have been led far astray.”

title: Hadith on Dhul-Hijjah: Virtue of ten days of Dhul-Hijjah
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No good deeds are better than what is done in these first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah.” Some companions of the Prophet said, “Not even jihad in the way of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Not even jihad in the way of Allah, except for a man who goes out with his life and wealth at risk and he returns with nothing.”
q: No good deeds are better than what is done in these first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah … Not even jihad in the way of Allah, except for a man who goes out with his life and wealth at risk and he returns with nothing

title: Hadith on Sunnah: All Muslims enter Paradise but those who refuse
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Everyone from my nation will enter Paradise but those who refuse.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, who will refuse?” The Prophet said, “Whoever obeys me enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys me has refused.”
q: Everyone from my nation will enter Paradise but those who refuse. … Whoever obeys me enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys me has refused.

title: Hadith on Death: His deeds end except knowledge, charity, offspring
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the human being dies, his deeds end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for him.”
q: When the human being dies, his deeds end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for him

title: Hadith on Dua: Grant my soul righteousness and purify it
t: Zayd ibn Arqam reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would supplicate, “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disability, sloth, cowardice, miserliness, senility, and the punishment of the grave. O Allah, grant my soul a sense of righteousness and purify it, for You are the best to purify it. You are its Protector and its Guardian. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit, from a heart that is not reverent, from a soul that is not content, and from a supplication that is not answered.”
q: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disability, sloth, cowardice, miserliness, senility, and the punishment of the grave. O Allah, grant my soul a sense of righteousness and purify it, for You are the best to purify it. You are its Protector and its Guardian. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit, from a heart that is not reverent, from a soul that is not content, and from a supplication that is not answered

title: Hadith on Work: The Prophet helps a man earn a living
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A man from the Ansar came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and begged from him. The Prophet said, “Have you nothing in your house?” The man said, “Yes, a piece of cloth, a part of which we wear and a part of which we spread on the ground, and a wooden bowl from which we drink water.” The Prophet said, “Bring them to me.” The man brought these articles to him and the Prophet took them in his hands and he said, “Who will buy these?” Someone said, “I will buy them for one coin.” The Prophet said twice or thrice, “Who will offer more than one coin?” Someone said, “I will buy them for two coins.” He sold them for two coins and the Prophet said, “Buy food with one of them and give it to your family. Buy an axe and bring it to me.” The man brought it to him. The Prophet fixed a handle on it with his own hands and he said, “Go gather firewood and sell it, and do not let me see you for a fortnight.” The man went away and gathered firewood and sold it. When he had earned ten coins, he came and bought a garment and food. The Prophet said, “This is better for you than for begging to come as a blemish on your face on the Day of Resurrection. Begging is only appropriate for three people: one in grinding poverty, one in serious debt, and one who must pay a difficult compensation.”
q: Have you nothing in your house? … Bring them to me … Who will buy these? … Who will offer more than one coin? … Buy food with one of them and give it to your family. Buy an axe and bring it to me … Go gather firewood and sell it, and do not let me see you for a fortnight. … This is better for you than for begging to come as a blemish on your face on the Day of Resurrection. Begging is only appropriate for three people: one in grinding poverty, one in serious debt, and one who must pay a difficult compensation.
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Albani

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: Do not hate others, righteousness in the heart
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not envy each other, do not outbid each other, do not hate each other, do not turn away from each other, and do not outsell each other. Rather, be servants of Allah as brothers. The Muslim is the brother of another Muslim. He does not wrong him, nor humiliate him, nor look down upon him. Righteousness is here,” and he pointed to his chest three times. The Prophet said, “It is enough evil for a man to look down upon his Muslim brother. The entirety of the Muslim is sacred to another Muslim: his life, his wealth, and his reputation.”
q: Do not envy each other, do not outbid each other, do not hate each other, do not turn away from each other, and do not outsell each other. Rather, be servants of Allah as brothers. The Muslim is the brother of another Muslim. He does not wrong him, nor humiliate him, nor look down upon him. Righteousness is here, … It is enough evil for a man to look down upon his Muslim brother. The entirety of the Muslim is sacred to another Muslim: his life, his wealth, and his reputation.

title: Hadith on Suspicion: Assumption, speculation are biggest lies
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of tales. Do not seek out faults, do not spy on each other, do not contend with each other, do not envy each other, do not hate each other, and do not turn away from each other. Rather, be servants of Allah as brothers.”
q: Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of tales. Do not seek out faults, do not spy on each other, do not contend with each other, do not envy each other, do not hate each other, and do not turn away from each other. Rather, be servants of Allah as brothers.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ikhwah: Be servants of Allah as brothers and sisters
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not hate each other, do not envy each other, do not turn away from each other, but rather be servants of Allah as brothers. It is not lawful for a Muslim to boycott his brother for more than three days.”
q: Do not hate each other, do not envy each other, do not turn away from each other, but rather be servants of Allah as brothers. It is not lawful for a Muslim to boycott his brother for more than three days.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Rahim: Whoever cuts off family will not enter Paradise
t: Jubayr ibn Mut’im reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The one who severs his family ties will not enter Paradise.”
q: The one who severs his family ties will not enter Paradise
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Rahim: Be good to family, even if they are not
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have relatives with whom I try to relate but they cut me off. I treat them well, but they treat me badly. I am forbearing with them, but they are harsh with me.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If it is as you say, then it is as if you threw hot ashes at them. Allah will be with you as a supporter as long as you remain like so.”
q: If it is as you say, then it is as if you threw hot ashes at them. Allah will be with you as a supporter as long as you remain like so.

title: Hadith on Rahim: Will you spread corruption, cut off your family?
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah made the creation and when He finished, the womb said: In this place, I seek refuge in you from those who sever me. Allah said: Are you not pleased that I keep good relations with those who are good to you and I will cut off whoever severs relations with you? The womb said: Yes, my Lord. Allah said: Thus, you will have it.” Then, the Prophet said, “Recite the verse if you wish: Will you then, if you were given authority, spread corruption in the land and sever your family ties?” (47:22)
q: Verily, Allah made the creation and when He finished, the womb said: In this place, I seek refuge in you from those who sever me. Allah said: Are you not pleased that I keep good relations with those who are good to you and I will cut off whoever severs relations with you? The womb said: Yes, my Lord. Allah said: Thus, you will have it … Recite the verse if you wish: Will you then, if you were given authority, spread corruption in the land and sever your family ties
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Character: Righteousness is good character and conscience
t: Al-Nawwas ibn Sam’an reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Righteousness is good character, and sin is what disturbs your heart and you hate for people to find out about it.”
q: Righteousness is good character, and sin is what disturbs your heart and you hate for people to find out about it

title: Hadith on Parents: Good relations with friends of parents
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among the best acts of righteousness is to keep relations with a man who was loved by one’s father.”
q: Among the best acts of righteousness is to keep relations with a man who was loved by one’s father

title: Hadith on Walidayn: Woe to one not dutiful to his parents
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Let him be humbled! Again, let him be humbled! Again, let him be humbled!” It was said, “Who is it, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “One whose parents reach old age, one or both of them, and he does not enter Paradise by them.”
q: Let him be humbled! Again, let him be humbled! Again, let him be humbled! … One whose parents reach old age, one or both of them, and he does not enter Paradise by them.

title: Hadith on Jihad: Are your parents alive? Strive in their service
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, asking permission to wage jihad. The Prophet said, “Are your parents alive?” The man said yes. The Prophet said, “Then strive in the service of them both.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Niyyah: Deeds only rewarded by their intentions
t: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, deeds are only with intentions, and every person will have only what they intended. Whoever emigrated to Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is for Allah and His Messenger. Whoever emigrated to get something in the world or to marry a woman, his emigration is for that to which he emigrated.”
q: Verily, deeds are only with intentions, and every person will have only what they intended. Whoever emigrated to Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is for Allah and His Messenger. Whoever emigrated to get something in the world or to marry a woman, his emigration is for that to which he emigrated
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on War: Kindness to non-combatant unbelievers
t: Asma’ bint Abi Bakr reported: My mother, who was an idolater, came to me hoping for good treatment during the truce of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, so I asked him, “Shall I keep relations with her?” The Prophet said, “Yes.” Then, Allah Almighty revealed the verse, “Allah does not forbid you from dealing kindly and fairly with those who have neither fought nor driven you out of your homes. Surely, Allah loves those who are fair. Allah only forbids you from befriending those who have fought you for your faith, driven you out of your homes, or supported others in doing so. And whoever takes them as friends, then it is they who are the true wrongdoers.” (60:8-9)
q: Yes … Allah does not forbid you from dealing kindly and fairly with those who have neither fought nor driven you out of your homes. Surely, Allah loves those who are fair. Allah only forbids you from befriending those who have fought you for your faith, driven you out of your homes, or supported others in doing so. And whoever takes them as friends, then it is they who are the true wrongdoers.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fiqh: Allah gives understanding of Islam to the Ummah
t: Mu’awiyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “To whomever Allah wills goodness, He grants him understanding of the religion. Verily, I am only a distributor, but Allah is the giver. Those within this nation will continue to establish the commandments of Allah. They will not be harmed by anyone who opposes them until the decree of Allah has come.”
q: To whomever Allah wills goodness, He grants him understanding of the religion. Verily, I am only a distributor, but Allah is the giver. Those within this nation will continue to establish the commandments of Allah. They will not be harmed by anyone who opposes them until the decree of Allah has come.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Pride: Worst to Allah are the arrogant ‘king of kings’
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most vile man to Allah on the Day of Resurrection, the most filthy and the most wretched, is a man who was named ‘king of kings,’ yet there is no king but Allah.”
q: The most vile man to Allah on the Day of Resurrection, the most filthy and the most wretched, is a man who was named ‘king of kings,’ yet there is no king but Allah

title: Hadith on Fasting: Companions fasted and broke fast during travel
t:
Anas bin Malik reported: We would travel with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and those who fasted did not blame those who broke their fast, and those who broke their fast did not blame those who fasted.

In another narration, Abu Sa’id al-Khudri said: Their view is that whoever found strength to fast, he fasted and that was good. Whoever found himself too weak to fast, he broke his fast and that was good.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Travel: Not righteousness to fast on a journey
t: Jabir bin Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was on a journey and he saw a crowd of people over a man being shaded by them. The Prophet said, “What is this?” They said, “He is fasting.” The Prophet said, “It is not righteousness to fast while traveling.”
q: What is this? … It is not righteousness to fast while traveling
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Siyam: Many virtues of fasting for Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah said, ‘Every deed of the son of Adam is for him, except for fasting. It is for Me and I will reward it.’ Fasting is a shield, so when one of you fasts, he may not be obscene or boisterous. If someone insults him or fights him, let him say: Indeed, I am fasting. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the breath coming from the mouth of a fasting person is more pleasant to Allah than the scent of musk. The fasting person has two moments of relief he enjoys: when he breaks his fast he is joyful, and when he meets his Lord he is joyful for his fasting.”
q: Allah said, ‘Every deed of the son of Adam is for him, except for fasting. It is for Me and I will reward it.’ Fasting is a shield, so when one of you fasts, he may not be obscene or boisterous. If someone insults him or fights him, let him say: Indeed, I am fasting. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the breath coming from the mouth of a fasting person is more pleasant to Allah than the scent of musk. The fasting person has two moments of relief he enjoys: when he breaks his fast he is joyful, and when he meets his Lord he is joyful for his fasting.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sawm: True fasting is leaving sins, bad words
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever does not leave evil words and deeds while fasting, Allah does not need him to leave food and drink.”
q: Whoever does not leave evil words and deeds while fasting, Allah does not need him to leave food and drink

title: Hadith on Ramadan: The Prophet was most generous in Ramadan
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was the most generous of people and he was even more generous in Ramadan when Gabriel would meet him. He would meet him every night of Ramadan to study the Quran. Thus, the Prophet would be more generous than a refreshing wind.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jannah: Many gates through which to enter Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Anyone who spends a pair in the way of Allah will be called from all the gates of Paradise: O servant of Allah, this is good! The people of prayer will be called from the gate of prayer, the people of jihad will be called from the gate of jihad, the people of fasting will be called from the gate of al-Rayyan, and the people of charity will be called from the gate of charity.” Abu Bakr said, “One who is called from all those gates would need nothing. Will anyone be called from all those gates, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Yes, and I hope you will be among them, O Abu Bakr.”
q: al-Rayyan … Yes, and I hope you will be among them, O Abu Bakr
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Heaven opened, devils chained for Ramadan
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the month of Ramadan begins, the gates of the heaven are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are chained.”
q: When the month of Ramadan begins, the gates of the heaven are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are chained
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sawm: Special gate in Paradise for those who fast
t: Sahl ibn Sa’d reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, there is a gate in Paradise called ‘al-Rayyan,’ through which only those who fasted will enter on the Day of Resurrection. No one else will enter it along with them. It will be said: Where are those who fasted? They will stand and no one will enter it along with them. When they enter it, it will be closed and no one else will go through it.”
q: Verily, there is a gate in Paradise called ‘al-Rayyan,’ through which only those who fasted will enter on the Day of Resurrection. No one else will enter it along with them. It will be said: Where are those who fasted? They will stand and no one will enter it along with them. … When they enter it, it will be closed and no one else will go through it
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Ramadan: Forgiveness for night prayer in Ramadan
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, encouraged standing for night prayer in the month of Ramadan, without imposing it on them. The Prophet would say, “Whoever stands in prayer during Ramadan due to faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven.” After the Prophet passed away the matter continued like that, then continued like that during the Caliphate of Abu Bakr and in the early part of the Caliphate of Umar.
q: Whoever stands in prayer during Ramadan due to faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Islam: Muslims do not harm others, and abandon sins
t: Abdullah bin Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand Muslims are safe. The emigrant is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden.”
q: The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand Muslims are safe … . The emigrant is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Best charity is given when independent, enriched
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best charity is what you give when you are independent; start by spending on your dependents.”
q: The best charity is what you give when you are independent; start by spending on your dependents.

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Spending on your family is an act of charity
t: Abu Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a Muslim spends on his family seeking reward from Allah, it is charity for him.”
q: “If a Muslim spends on his family seeking reward from Allah, it is charity for him.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sadaqa: Spend in charity, Allah spends on you
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah said: Spend in charity, O son of Adam, and I will spend on you.”
q: Allah said: Spend in charity, O son of Adam, and I will spend on you.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Jannah: No one knows the pleasures of Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah said: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, what no ear has heard, and what no human heart has conceived. Recite the verse if you wish: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort.” (32:17)
q: Allah said: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, what no ear has heard, and what no human heart has conceived … Recite the verse if you wish: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fiqh: Excellence in Islam requires understanding
t: Abu Huraira reported: It was said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, “Which people are the most noble?” The Prophet said, “The most noble to Allah are the most righteous.” They said, “That is not what we are asking about.” The Prophet said, “The most noble of people was Joseph, the prophet of Allah, the son of the prophet of Allah, the son of the Prophet of Allah, the son of the friend of Allah.” They said, “That is not what we are asking about.” The Prophet said, “Are you asking about the Arabs?” They said yes. The Prophet said, “The best of you in the time of ignorance are the best of you in Islam, if you have understanding.”
q: The most noble to Allah are the most righteous. … The most noble of people was Joseph, the prophet of Allah, the son of the prophet of Allah, the son of the Prophet of Allah, the son of the friend of Allah. … Are you asking about the Arabs? … The best of you in the time of ignorance are the best of you in Islam, if you have understanding
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Masajid: Do not stop women from attending Mosque
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not prevent women from their share of the mosques if they seek your permission.”
q: Do not prevent women from their share of the mosques if they seek your permission
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Family: Taking care of daughters leads to Paradise
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There is no Muslim with two daughters, caring for them in the best manner as long as he accompanies them, but that they will admit him into Paradise.”
q: There is no Muslim with two daughters, caring for them in the best manner as long as he accompanies them, but that they will admit him into Paradise

title: Hadith on Salaam: Greeting unbelievers with peace
t: Abu Uthman reported: Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to a Persian leader and greeted him with peace in his letter. It was said, “Do you greet him with peace when he is an unbeliever?” Abu Musa said, “Indeed, he wrote to me and greeted me with peace, so I have returned it.”

title: Hadith on Rifq: Cruelty is disgraceful, Allah loves gentleness
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Harshness is not found in anything but that it disgraces it. Verily, Allah is kind and He loves kindness.”
q: Harshness is not found in anything but that it disgraces it. Verily, Allah is kind and He loves kindness

title: Umar on Forgiveness: No mercy for the unmerciful, unforgiving
t: Qabisah ibn Jabir reported: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “Whoever does not show mercy will not receive mercy. Whoever does not forgive others will not be forgiven. Whoever does not pardon others will not be pardoned. Whoever does not protect others will not be protected.”

title: Ibn Abbas on Humanity: Only righteousness makes one better
t: ‘Ata reported: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “I do not see anyone acting upon this verse: O people, We have created you male and female and made you into nations and tribes so that you may know one another, for the most noble of you to Allah is the most righteous of you.” (49:13) Thus, a man says to another man that I am more noble than you, yet no one is made noble but by the fear of Allah.”
q: O people, We have created you male and female and made you into nations and tribes so that you may know one another, for the most noble of you to Allah is the most righteous of you

title: Hadith on Responsibility: Each of you is a shepherd for his flock
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Every one of you is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock. The leader of people is a guardian and is responsible for his subjects. A man is the guardian of his family and he is responsible for them. A woman is the guardian of her husband’s home and his children and she is responsible for them. The servant of a man is a guardian of the property of his master and he is responsible for it. No doubt, every one of you is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock.”
q: Every one of you is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock. The leader of people is a guardian and is responsible for his subjects. A man is the guardian of his family and he is responsible for them. A woman is the guardian of her husband’s home and his children and she is responsible for them. The servant of a man is a guardian of the property of his master and he is responsible for it. No doubt, every one of you is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Chores: The Prophet does chores for his family
t: Al-Aswad reported: I asked Aisha, “What did the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, do in his house?” Aisha said, “The Prophet would do chores for his family and he would go out when it was time for prayer.”

title: Hadith on Neighbors: Gabriel advises the Prophet to treat neighbors well
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Gabriel continued to instruct me to treat neighbors well until I thought he would make them my heirs.”
q: Gabriel continued to instruct me to treat neighbors well until I thought he would make them my heirs.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Sadaqah: Every good deed rewarded as charity
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Every good deed is charity.”
q: Every good deed is charity

title: Hadith on Charity: All good deeds rewarded, even smiling
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face.”
q: Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face.

title: Hadith on Fame: Allah loves righteous, independent, not famous
t: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah loves a servant who is righteous, independent, and obscure.”
q: Verily, Allah loves a servant who is righteous, independent, and obscure

title: Hadith of Akhirah: Give us good in this life, in Hereafter
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would say, “Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter and save us from the punishment of the Hellfire.” (2:201)
q: Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter and save us from the punishment of the Hellfire
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hudud: Best to avoid legal punishments if possible
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have committed an offense, so impose punishment upon me.” The man was present at the prayer and he prayed with the Prophet. When they finished praying, the man repeated his request. The Prophet said, “Were you with us during the prayer?” The man said yes. The Prophet said, “You have been forgiven.”
q: Were you with us during the prayer? … You have been forgiven.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Treachery: Betrayal of treaties forbids entry to Paradise
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever kills a person protected by a treaty will never smell the fragrance of Paradise. Verily, its fragrance can be found from a distance of forty years of travel.”
q: Whoever kills a person protected by a treaty will never smell the fragrance of Paradise. Verily, its fragrance can be found from a distance of forty years of travel

title: Hadith on Jumuah: Best day on which sun has risen is Friday
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. Adam was created on Friday and on it he entered Paradise and on it he was expelled from therein. The Hour will not be established but on Friday.”
q: The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. Adam was created on Friday and on it he entered Paradise and on it he was expelled from therein. The Hour will not be established but on Friday

title: Hadith on Cruelty: Harsh, mean people do not enter Paradise
t: Harithah ibn Wahb reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Neither the haughty, nor the cruel, will enter Paradise.”
q: Neither the haughty, nor the cruel, will enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Whoever enters Paradise enjoys eternal pleasure
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever enters Paradise will enjoy bliss without misery, clothes without wear, and youth without aging.”
q: Whoever enters Paradise will enjoy bliss without misery, clothes without wear, and youth without aging

title: Hadith on Truth: Honesty leads to Paradise, dishonesty to Hell
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “You must be truthful. Verily, truthfulness leads to righteousness and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to be truthful and encourages honesty until he is recorded with Allah as truthful. And beware of falsehood. Verily, falsehood leads to wickedness and wickedness leads to the Hellfire. A man continues to tell lies and encourages falsehood until he is recorded with Allah as a liar.”
q: You must be truthful.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Faith: All is good for a believer by patience, gratitude
t: Suhayb reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Wondrous is the affair of a believer, as there is good for him in every matter; this is not the case for anyone but a believer. If he experiences pleasure, he thanks Allah and it is good for him. If he experiences harm, he shows patience and it is good for him.”
q: Wondrous is the affair of a believer, as there is good for him in every matter; this is not the case for anyone but a believer. If he experiences pleasure, he thanks Allah and it is good for him. If he experiences harm, he shows patience and it is good for him

title: Hadith on Mercy: Forgive my people for they do not know
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: I remember seeing the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, tell the story of a prophet who was beaten by his people, and he wiped the blood from his face, saying, “My Lord, forgive my people for they do not know.”
q: My Lord, forgive my people for they do not know. …
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Destiny: Everyone has two places in Hereafter
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None will enter Paradise but that he will be shown the place he would have occupied in Hellfire if he had done evil, so that he may be more thankful. None will enter the Hellfire but that he will be shown the place he would have occupied in Paradise if he had done good, so that it may be a cause of sorrow for him.”
q: None will enter Paradise but that he will be shown the place he would have occupied in Hellfire if he had done evil, so that he may be more thankful. None will enter the Hellfire but that he will be shown the place he would have occupied in Paradise if he had done good, so that it may be a cause of sorrow for him

title: Hadith on Gratitude: Thanking people is gratefulness to Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah.”
q: Whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah

title: Hadith on Condemning: Overly judgmental Muslims are most astray
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If a man says the people are ruined, he is the most ruined among them.”
q: If a man says the people are ruined, he is the most ruined among them.

title: Hadith on Iqtisas: Perfect justice restored on Day of Resurrection
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The rights of justice will surely be restored to their people on the Day of Resurrection, even the hornless sheep will lay claim to the horned sheep.”
q: The rights of justice will surely be restored to their people on the Day of Resurrection, even the hornless sheep will lay claim to the horned sheep

title: Hadith on Compassion: Mercy only removed from the miserable
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Mercy is only deprived by those who are damned.”
q: Mercy is only deprived by those who are damned.

title: Hadith on Greed: If he had all the gold, he still wants more
t: Anas bin Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If the son of Adam had a valley full of gold, he would want to have two valleys. Nothing fills his mouth but the dust of the grave, yet Allah will relent to whoever repents to Him.”
q: If the son of Adam had a valley full of gold, he would want to have two valleys. Nothing fills his mouth but the dust of the grave, yet Allah will relent to whoever repents to Him
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Trade: The Prophet does business with Jews
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed away while his armor was mortgaged to a Jew for thirty portions of barley.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dunya: You know better the affairs of your world
t: Anas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by some people grafting trees. The Prophet said, “It would be better if you did not do that.” They abandoned the practice, but there was a decline in the yield. The Prophet passed by again, and he said, “What is wrong with your trees?” They said, “You said not to do so.” The Prophet said, “You know better the affairs of your world.”
q: It would be better if you did not do that … You know better the affairs of your world.

title: Hadith on Christ: Muhammad closer to Jesus than anyone else
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I am the closest of the people to Jesus the son of Mary in this life and in the Hereafter.” It was said, “How is that, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “The prophets are like brothers from one father with different mothers. They have one religion and there was no other prophet between us.”
q: “I am the closest of the people to Jesus the son of Mary in this life and in the Hereafter … The prophets are like brothers from one father with different mothers. They have one religion and there was no other prophet between us

title: Hadith on Sabr: Patience over friend’s death leads to Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty says: I have nothing to give to My faithful servant but Paradise if I cause his dear friend to die and he remains patient.”
q: Allah Almighty says: I have nothing to give to My faithful servant but Paradise if I cause his dear friend to die and he remains patient.

title: Hadith on Food: The Prophet’s family rarely ate to their fill
t: Aisha reported: The family of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, never ate to their fill of wheat bread for three consecutive nights, ever since they had come to Medina, until he passed away.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Salaf: Best generations are the companions, successors
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The best people are those of my generation, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. Then, there will come people after them whose testimony precedes their oaths and their oaths precede their testimony.”
q: The best people are those of my generation, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. Then, there will come people after them whose testimony precedes their oaths and their oaths precede their testimony
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Avoiding trials better than rushing into them
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “There will come tribulations in which one sitting will be better than one standing. The one standing will be better than one walking. The one walking will be better than one running. Whoever seeks these tribulations will be destroyed by them. Whoever finds a place of shelter or refuge, let him take refuge in it.”
q: There will come tribulations
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tribalism: Help the oppressed, stop the oppressor
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: Two young men were fighting, one from the Muhajirin and one man from the Ansar. The Muhajir called out, “O Muhajirin!” And the Ansari called out, “O Ansar!” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out and he said, “What is this call of the people of ignorance?” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, it is only two boys fighting and one had kicked the other.” The Prophet said, “No matter, let a man help his brother whether he is wrong or being wronged. If he is oppressing others, then stop him, for that is supporting him. If he is being oppressed, then support him.”
q: What is this call of the people of ignorance? … No matter, let a man help his brother whether he is wrong or being wronged. If he is oppressing others, then stop him, for that is supporting him. If he is being oppressed, then support him

title: Hadith on Neighbors: No Paradise if neighbor unsafe from harm
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He will not enter Paradise whose neighbor is not secure from his evil.”
q: He will not enter Paradise whose neighbor is not secure from his evil

title: Hadith on Healing: Take away the pain by Your healing
t: Aisha reported: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would visit a sick person, he would say, “Take away the pain, O Lord of all people, and give healing for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no trace of illness.”
q: “Take away the pain, O Lord of all people, and give healing for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no trace of illness.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Qulub: Allah directs the hearts as He wills
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the hearts of the children of Adam, all of them, are between the two fingers of the Merciful as one heart. He directs them wherever He wills. O Allah, the Director of the hearts, turn our hearts to Your obedience.”
q: Verily, the hearts of the children of Adam, all of them, are between the two fingers of the Merciful as one heart. He directs them wherever He wills … O Allah, the Director of the hearts, turn our hearts to Your obedience

title: Hadith on Iqtisas: Do you know who the truly bankrupt are?
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do you know who are bankrupt?” They said, “The one without money or goods is bankrupt.” The Prophet said, “Verily, the bankrupt of my nation are those who come on the Day of Resurrection with prayers, fasting, and charity, but also with insults, slander, consuming wealth, shedding blood, and beating others. The oppressed will each be given from his good deeds. If his good deeds run out before justice is fulfilled, then their sins will be cast upon him and he will be thrown into the Hellfire.”
q: Do you know who are bankrupt? … Verily, the bankrupt of my nation are those who come on the Day of Resurrection with prayers, fasting, and charity, but also with insults, slander, consuming wealth, shedding blood, and beating others. The oppressed will each be given from his good deeds. If his good deeds run out before justice is fulfilled, then their sins will be cast upon him and he will be thrown into the Hellfire.

title: Hadith on Arrogance: Never say Allah will not forgive someone
t: Jundab reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man said: By Allah, Allah will not forgive this person! Allah Almighty said: Who is he who swore by Me that I will not forgive someone? I have forgiven him and erased your good deeds.”
q: “A man said: By Allah, Allah will not forgive this person! Allah Almighty said: Who is he who swore by Me that I will not forgive someone? I have forgiven him and erased your good deeds.”

title: Hadith on Scholars: Knowledge disappears with death of ‘Ulama
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah does not withhold knowledge by snatching it away from his servants, but rather he withholds knowledge by taking the souls of scholars, until no scholar remains and people follow ignorant leaders. They are asked and they issue judgments without knowledge. Thus, they are astray and lead others astray.”
q: Verily, Allah does not withhold knowledge by snatching it away from his servants, but rather he withholds knowledge by taking the souls of scholars, until no scholar remains and people follow ignorant leaders. They are asked and they issue judgments without knowledge. Thus, they are astray and lead others astray
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Kibr: Arrogance is looking down on others, rejecting truth
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one who has the weight of a seed of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise.” A man said, “But a man likes to have nice clothes and nice shoes.” The Prophet said, “Verily, Allah is beautiful and He loves beauty. Arrogance is to disregard the truth and to look down upon people.”
q: No one who has the weight of a seed of arrogance in his heart will … enter Paradise. … Verily, … Allah is beautiful and He loves beauty. Arrogance is to disregard the truth and to look down upon people.

title: Hadith on Purification: Five prayers expiate sins like water removes dirt
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If there was a river at your door and he took a bath in it five times a day, would you notice any dirt on him?” They said, “Not a trace of dirt would be left.” The Prophet said, “That is the parable of the five prayers by which Allah removes sins.”
q: If there was a river at your door and he took a bath in it five times a day, would you notice any dirt on him? … That is the parable of the five prayers by which Allah removes sins.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Tribalism: Whoever dies for tribalism dies in ignorance
t: Jundab ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever is killed under the banner of blind following, who calls to tribalism or supports tribalism, then he has died upon ignorance.”
q: Whoever is killed under the banner of blind following, who calls to tribalism or supports tribalism, then he has died upon ignorance

title: Hadith on Threats: Do not point a weapon at Muslims
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None of you should point a weapon at his brother. Verily, he does not know if Satan will cause his hand to slip and thus he falls into a pit of fire.”
q: None of you should point a weapon at his brother. Verily, he does not know if Satan will cause his hand to slip and thus he falls into a pit of fire.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Religion: Islam is easy, extremism will overwhelm you
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the religion is easy and no one burdens himself in religion but that it overwhelms him. Follow the right course, seek closeness to Allah, give glad tidings, and seek help for worship in the morning and evening and a part of the night.”

title: Hadith on Peace: O Allah, you are peace and from you is peace
t: Aisha reported: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, finished his prayer, he would not sit long enough but to say, “O Allah, You are peace and from You is peace. Blessed are You, the Majestic and Noble.”
q: O Allah, You are peace and from You is peace. Blessed are You, the Majestic and Noble

title: Hadith on Ruin: Muslims led astray by young, foolish Quraish
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The destruction of my nation is at the hands of young men from the Quraysh tribe.”
q: The destruction of my nation is at the hands of young men from the Quraysh tribe

title: Hadith on Adhan: Supplication for the Prophet’s intercession
t: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever hears the call to prayer and says, ‘O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and established prayer, give Muhammad the means of nearness and the most excellent reward, and raise him to the praiseworthy station that You have promised him,’ then my intercession will be allowed for him on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Whoever hears the call to prayer and says, ‘O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and established prayer, give Muhammad the means of nearness and the most excellent reward, and raise him to the praiseworthy station that You have promised him,’ then my intercession will be allowed for him on the Day of Resurrection

title: Hadith on Lessons: Believers learn from bad experiences
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The believer is not stung twice from the same hole.”
q: The believer is not stung twice from the same hole
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Treachery: Forbidden to betray, kill peaceful non-Muslims
t: Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah reported: During the period of ignorance, Al-Mughirah accompanied some people, killed them, and took their wealth. Then, he later embraced Islam. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “As for your Islam, we have accepted it. As for the property, it is the wealth of treachery and we have no need for it.”
q: As for your Islam, we have accepted it. As for the property, it is the wealth of treachery and we have no need for it

title: Hadith on Khalil: Allah is the best friend of the Prophet
t: Jundub reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I am innocent before Allah of taking any of you as my best friend. Verily, Allah Almighty has taken me as His best friend, just as he took Abraham as His best friend. If I were to take anyone of my nation as a best friend, it would have been Abu Bakr. Verily, those before you would take the graves of their prophets and righteous as places of prayer. Do not take graves as places of prayer. I forbid you from doing so.”
