q: I am innocent before Allah of taking any of you as my best friend. Verily, Allah Almighty has taken me as His best friend, just as he took Abraham as His best friend. If I were to take anyone of my nation as a best friend, it would have been Abu Bakr. Verily, those before you would take the graves of their prophets and righteous as places of prayer. Do not take graves as places of prayer. I forbid you from doing so.

title: Hadith on Gratitude: Look to the poor, that you may be grateful
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace  and blessings be upon him, said, “Look at those below you and do not look at those above you, lest you belittle the favors of Allah.”

title: Hadith on Takfir: False charges of unbelief backfire
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When a man calls his brother an unbeliever, it turns against at least one of them. Either the accused is as he claimed, or else the charge will turn against him.”
q: When a man calls his brother an unbeliever, it turns against at least one of them. … Either the accused is as he claimed, or else the charge will turn against him
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Injustice: Guard yourself from oppression, greed, violence
t: Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of committing oppression, for oppression will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection. Beware of greed, for greed ruined those before you. It caused them to shed their blood and to make lawful what was unlawful to them.”
q: “Beware of committing oppression, for oppression will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection. Beware of greed, for greed ruined those before you. It caused them to shed their blood and to make lawful what was unlawful to them.”

title: Hadith on Sincerity: Allah judges hearts and deeds, not wealth or looks
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah does not look at your appearance or wealth, but rather He looks at your hearts and actions.”
q: Verily, Allah does not look at your appearance or wealth, but rather He looks at your hearts and actions.

title: Hadith on Bidah: You do not know what they innovated after you
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Some of my companions will come towards me at the Fountain in the Hereafter until I recognize them. They will be taken away from me, then I will say: My companions! It will be said: You do not know what they innovated after you.”
q: Some of my companions will come towards me at the Fountain in the Hereafter until I recognize them. They will be taken away from me, then I will say: My companions! It will be said: You do not know what they innovated after you
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Supplication is worship itself, for Allah alone
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Supplication is worship itself.” Then, the Prophet recited the verse, “Your Lord said: Call upon Me and I will answer you. Verily, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell in humiliation.” (40:60)
q: Supplication is worship itself. … Your Lord said: Call upon Me and I will answer you. Verily, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell in humiliation.

title: Hadith on Manners: The Prophet never even said ‘Uff’
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: I served the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, for ten years. By Allah, he never even said to me, “Uff!” He never said harshly, “Why did you do that?” or, “Why did you not do that?”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Mercy: The Prophet is sent as mercy to the worlds
t: Abu Huraira reported: It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, pray against the idolaters!” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, I was not sent to invoke curses, but rather I was only sent as mercy.”
q: Verily, I was not sent to invoke curses, but rather I was only sent as mercy

title: Hadith on Humility: Allah has revealed that we be humble
t: ‘Iyad ibn Himar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah has revealed to me that you must be humble towards one another, so that no one oppresses another or boasts to another.”
q: Verily, … Allah has revealed to me that you must be humble towards one another, so that no one oppresses another or boasts to another

title: Hadith on Islam: Sweetness of faith is satisfaction with Islam
t: Al-‘Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He has tasted the sweetness of faith who is content with Allah as a Lord, Islam as a religion, and Muhammad as a messenger.”
q: He has tasted the sweetness of faith who is content with Allah as a Lord, Islam as a religion, and Muhammad as a messenger.

title: Hadith on Funerals: The Prophet stands for a Jewish funeral
t:
Qays ibn Sa’d reported: A funeral passed by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he stood up. It was said to him, “It is a Jew.” The Prophet said, “Was he not a soul?”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “Verily, you stand to glorify Allah, who is the receiver of souls.”
q: Was he not a soul … Verily, you stand to glorify Allah, who is the receiver of souls.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Peace: The Prophet commands to spread peace
t: Abu Umamah reported: Our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded us to spread peace.

title: Hadith on Character: Best believers are kind to family
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most complete of believers in faith are those with the best character and who are most kind to their families.”
q: Verily, the most complete of believers in faith are those with the best character and who are most kind to their families.

title: Hadith on Faith: The trust descended from heaven to people
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The covenant of faithfulness descended from the heavens and settled in the hearts of men. The Quran was revealed and they read it in the Quran and learned it from the Sunnah.”
q: The covenant of faithfulness descended from the heavens and settled in the hearts of men. The Quran was revealed and they read it in the Quran and learned it from the Sunnah
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dua: Be determined, certain in your supplications
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When one of you calls upon Allah, let him be determined in the supplication and he should not say, ‘O Allah, give me if You will,’ for there is no one to coerce Allah.”
q: When one of you calls upon Allah, let him be determined in the supplication and he should not say, ‘O Allah, give me if You will,’ for there is no one to coerce Allah.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Faith: Love your brother as yourself
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None of you will have faith until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.”
q: None of you will have faith until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Peacemaking: The Prophet goes to reconcile two groups
t: Sahl bin Sa’d reported: The people of Quba’ were fighting to the point of throwing stones. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was told about that, so he said, “Go with us. We will reconcile between them.”
q: Go with us. We will reconcile between them

title: Hadith on Justice: Support wrongdoers by stopping them
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or is being oppressed.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah, we help the oppressed, but how do we help an oppressor?” The Prophet said, “By seizing his hand.”
q: Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or is being oppressed. … By seizing his hand.

title: Hadith on Paradise: No entrance to Jannah until absolved from sin
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When the believers are saved from Hellfire, they will be held at a bridge between Paradise and Hell. They will requite each other for wrongs done in the world, until they are purified and absolved and they will be called to enter Paradise. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of you will recognize his place in Paradise better than he did his home in the world.”
q: When the believers are saved from Hellfire, they will be held at a bridge between Paradise and Hell. They will requite each other for wrongs done in the world, until they are purified and absolved and they will be called to enter Paradise. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of you will recognize his place in Paradise better than he did his home in the world

title: Hadith on Fitnah: Killing, upheaval, sin before the Hour
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Time will pass rapidly, knowledge will be withdrawn, tribulations will prevail, greed will be cast into hearts, and there will be many upheavals.” They said, “What is upheaval?” The Prophet said, “It is killing.”
q: Time will pass rapidly, knowledge will be withdrawn, tribulations will prevail, greed will be cast into hearts, and there will be many upheavals. … It is killing
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Women: Allah created women different, so be good
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I enjoin you to treat women well, for the woman was created from a rib and the most curved part of the rib is its highest point. If you try to straighten it, you will break it. If you leave it as it is, it will remain bent. Thus, I enjoin you to be good to women.”
q: I enjoin you to treat women well, for the woman was created from a rib and the most curved part of the rib is its highest point. If you try to straighten it, you will break it. If you leave it as it is, it will remain bent. Thus, I enjoin you to be good to women.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Manners: Good form is part of Prophethood
t: Ibn Abbas reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Good form, good composure, and moderation are among the twenty-five parts of prophecy.”
q: Good form, good composure, and moderation are among the twenty-five parts of prophecy

title: Hadith on Imamate: Prohibition of desiring power, authority
t: Abu Musa reported: Two of my cousins and myself entered the home of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. One of them said, “O Messenger of Allah, appoint us as leaders over some lands that Allah Almighty has entrusted to your authority.” The other said something similar to it. The Prophet said, “Verily, by Allah, we do not appoint this work to anyone who asks for it, or is eager for it.”
q: Verily, by Allah, we do not appoint this work to anyone who asks for it, or is eager for it.

title: Hadith on Imam: Obey your leader, regardless of race or status
t: Umm al-Husayn reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, delivered a sermon during the farewell pilgrimage, saying, “Even if an Abyssinian slave were appointed in charge over you and he leads you with the Book of Allah, you must listen and obey.”
q: Even if an Abyssinian slave were appointed in charge over you and he leads you with the Book of Allah, you must listen and obey.

title: Hadith on Zuhd: Be in this world as a stranger, traveler
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Be in this world as if you were a stranger or a traveler along a path.” Ibn Umar would say, “If you make it to the evening, do not wait for the morning. If you make it to the morning, do not wait for the evening. Take from your health for your sickness, and from your life for your death.”
q: Be in this world as if you were a stranger or a traveler along a path.

title: Hadith on Rahmah: Ninety-nine parts of mercy for Judgment Day
t: Salman al-Farisi reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth, He created one hundred parts of mercy. Each part can fill what is between the heavens and the earth. He made one part of mercy for the earth, from which a mother has compassion for her child, animals and birds have compassion for each other. On the Day of Resurrection, He will perfect this mercy.”
q: Verily, on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth, He created one hundred parts of mercy. Each part can fill what is between the heavens and the earth. He made one part of mercy for the earth, from which a mother has compassion for her child, animals and birds have compassion for each other. On the Day of Resurrection, He will perfect this mercy

title: Hadith on Love: Spread love and peace, beware hatred
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you submit to Allah, and you will not submit until you love one another. Spread peace and you will love one another. Beware of hatred, for it is the razor. I do not say that it shaves hair, but rather it shaves away the religion.”
q: By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you submit to Allah, and you will not submit until you love one another. Spread peace and you will love one another. Beware of hatred, for it is the razor. I do not say that it shaves hair, but rather it shaves away the religion

title: Hadith on Debts: Forgive their debt so Allah forgives you
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man would give loans to the people and he would say to his servant: If the debtor is in hardship you should forgive the debt that perhaps Allah will relieve us. So when he met Allah, then Allah relieved him.”
q: A man would give loans to the people and he would say to his servant: If the debtor is in hardship you should forgive the debt that perhaps Allah will relieve us. So when he met Allah, then Allah relieved him.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Kusuf: Great humility of the Prophet proves him true
t: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah reported: The sun eclipsed on the day the Prophet’s son Abraham died, and the people said the eclipse was because of the death of Abraham. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The sun and the moon are two signs of Allah, and they do not eclipse because of the death or birth of anyone. When you see them, call upon Allah and pray until the eclipse is clear.”
q: The sun and the moon are two signs of Allah, and they do not eclipse because of the death or birth of anyone. When you see them, call upon Allah and pray until the eclipse is clear.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Neighbors: Be kind to neighbors, regardless of religion
t: Mujahid reported: We were with Abdullah ibn Amr while his servant prepared to distribute a sheep. Abdullah said, “Young man, when you are finished, then begin with our Jewish neighbor.” A man said, “Jewish? May Allah correct you!” Abdullah said, “I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, enjoining good treatment of our neighbors so often that we feared he would make them our heirs.”

title: Hadith on Jumuah: Reward goood manners at Friday
t: Salman al-Farisi reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No one takes a bath on Friday, purifies himself as much as he can, uses oil or perfume in his house, then proceeds for prayer and does not separate two persons sitting together, then prays as much as is written for him and remains silent while the Imam is delivering the sermon, except that his sins between this Friday and the previous will be forgiven.”
q: No one takes a bath on Friday, purifies himself as much as he can, uses oil or perfume in his house, then proceeds for prayer and does not separate two persons sitting together, then prays as much as is written for him and remains silent while the Imam is delivering the sermon, except that his sins between this Friday and the previous will be forgiven.

title: Hadith on Sanctity: Your lives, property, and honor are sacred
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said during his last pilgrimage, “What is the day today?” We kept quiet, thinking he might give the day another name. The Prophet said, “Is it not the day of sacrificing?” We said yes. The Prophet said, “Which month is this?” We again kept quiet, thinking he might give it another name. The Prophet said, “Is it not the month of Dhul Hijja?” We said yes. The Prophet said, “Verily, your lives, your property, and your honor are sacred to one another like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this city of yours. Let one present inform those who are absent; perhaps one present will inform another who understands better than him.”
q: What is the day today … Is it not the day of sacrificing … Which month is this … Is it not the month of Dhul Hijja … Verily, your lives, your property, and your honor are sacred to one another like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this city of yours. Let one present inform those who are absent; perhaps one present will inform another who understands better than him

title: Hadith on Trials: If Allah loves someone, He tests him
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If Allah wills good for someone, He afflicts him with trials.”
q: If Allah wills good for someone, He afflicts him with trials.

title: Hadith on Tribalism: He is not one of us who fights for tribalism
t: Jubayr ibn Mut’im reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “He is not one of us who calls to tribalism. He is not one of us who fights for the sake of tribalism. He is not one of us who dies following the way of tribalism.”
q: He is not one of us who calls to tribalism. He is not one of us who fights for the sake of tribalism. He is not one of us who dies following the way of tribalism
gf: Sahih li ghayrihi (authentic due to external evidence) according to Al-Arna’ut

title: Hadith on Law: Lawful and unlawful clear, avoid doubts
t: Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between the two of them are doubtful matters about which many people do not know. Thus, he who avoids doubtful matters clears himself in regard to his religion and his honor, and he who falls into doubtful matters will fall into the unlawful as the shepherd who pastures near a sanctuary, all but grazing therein. Verily, every king has a sanctum and the sanctum of Allah is His prohibitions. Verily, in the body is a piece of flesh which, if sound, the entire body is sound, and if corrupt, the entire body is corrupt. Truly, it is the heart.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Allah: Gabriel announces if Allah loves or hates someone
t:
Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Allah loves a servant, he calls Gabriel and he says: Verily, I love this person so you should love him. Then Gabriel loves him and makes an announcement in the heavens, saying: Allah loves this person and you should love him. Thus, the dwellers of the heavens love him and he is honored on the earth.”

In another narration, the Prophet said, “When Allah is angry with a servant, he calls Gabriel and he says: I resent this person, so you should resent him. Then Gabriel resents him and makes an announcement in the heavens, saying: Verily, Allah resents this person, so you should resent him. Thus, they become resentful with him and he is hated on the earth.”
q: When Allah loves a servant, he calls Gabriel and he says: Verily, I love this person so you should love him. Then Gabriel loves him and makes an announcement in the heavens, saying: Allah loves this person and you should love him. Thus, the dwellers of the heavens love him and he is honored on the earth … When Allah is angry with a servant, he calls Gabriel and he says: I resent this person, so you should resent him. Then Gabriel resents him and makes an announcement in the heavens, saying: Verily, Allah resents this person, so you should resent him. Thus, they become resentful with him and he is hated on the earth.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Words: Descent into Hell by a sinful tongue
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the servant may speak a single word for which he plummets into the Hellfire farther than the distance between East and West.”
q: Verily, the servant may speak a single word for which he plummets into the Hellfire farther than the distance between East and West
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Most privileged, most miserable on Judgment Day
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The most privileged people in the world among the people of Hellfire will come on the Day of Resurrection to be dipped in Hellfire, then it will be said: O son of Adam, did you see any good? Did you get any blessing? He will say: No, by Allah, my Lord! Then, the most miserable people in the world among the people of Paradise will come on the Day of Resurrection to be dipped in Paradise, then it will be said: O son of Adam, did you see any hardship? Did you have any distress? He will say: No, by Allah, my Lord! I did not once see hardship or distress.”
q: The most privileged people in the world among the people of Hellfire will come on the Day of Resurrection to be dipped in Hellfire, then it will be said: O son of Adam, did you see any good? Did you get any blessing? He will say: No, by Allah, my Lord! Then, the most miserable people in the world among the people of Paradise will come on the Day of Resurrection to be dipped in Paradise, then it will be said: O son of Adam, did you see any hardship? Did you have any distress? He will say: No, by Allah, my Lord! I did not once see hardship or distress.

title: Hadith on Salvation: None enters Paradise by deeds alone
t: Jabir reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None of you will enter Paradise by his good deeds alone, nor would you be rescued from the Hellfire, not even myself, but for the mercy of Allah.”
q: None of you will enter Paradise by his good deeds alone, nor would you be rescued from the Hellfire, not even myself, but for the mercy of Allah

title: Hadith on Iman: Purity is half of faith, prayer is light
t: Abu Malik al-Ashari reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Purity is half of the faith. The praise of Allah fills the Scale, as the glorification and praise of Allah fill everything between the heavens and the earth. Prayer is a light, charity is a proof, and patience is luminous. The Quran is a decisive proof for you or against you. All people begin the day by trading for their soul, either setting it free or ensuring its ruin.”
q: Purity is half of the faith. The praise of Allah fills the Scale, as the glorification and praise of Allah fill everything between the heavens and the earth. Prayer is a light, charity is a proof … and patience is luminous. The Quran is a decisive proof for you or against you. All people begin the day by trading for their soul, either setting it free or ensuring its ruin.

title: Hadith on Oppression: Allah has forbidden injustice for Himself
t: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah Almighty said: O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and I have forbidden it among you, so do not oppress one another. O My servants, all of you are astray except for those I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I shall guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except for those I have fed, so seek food from Me and I shall feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except for those I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I shall clothe you. O My servants, you sin by night and day and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me and I shall forgive you. O My servants, you are unable to harm Me and you are unable to bring benefit to Me. O My servants, were the first of you and the last of you, the human of you and the jinn of you, to be as pious as the most pious heart of anyone of you, that would not increase My dominion at all. O My servants, were the first of you and the last of you, the human of you and the jinn of you, to be as wicked as the most wicked heart of anyone of you, that would not decrease My dominion at all. O My servants, were the first of you and the last of you, the human of you and the jinn of you, to rise up in one place and make a request of Me, and were I to give everyone what he requested, that would not diminish what I have any more than a needle would diminish the sea if put into it. O My servants, it is only your deeds that I record and then recompense for you. Let him who finds good praise Allah, and let him who finds something else blame no one but himself.”
q: Allah Almighty said: O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and I have forbidden it among you, so do not oppress one another. … O My servants, all of you are astray except for those I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I shall guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except for those I have fed, so seek food from Me and I shall feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except for those I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I shall clothe you. O My servants, you sin by night and day and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me and I shall forgive you. O My servants, you are unable to harm Me and you are unable to bring benefit to Me … . O My servants, were the first of you and the last of you, the human of you and the jinn of you, to be as pious as the most pious heart of anyone of you, that would not increase My dominion at all. O My servants, were the first of you and the last of you, the human of you and the jinn of you, to be as wicked as the most wicked heart of anyone of you, that would not decrease My dominion at all. O My servants, were the first of you and the last of you, the human of you and the jinn of you, to rise up in one place and make a request of Me, and were I to give everyone what he requested, that would not diminish what I have any more than a needle would diminish the sea if put into it. … O My servants, it is only your deeds that I record and then recompense for you. Let him who finds good praise Allah, and let him who finds something else blame no one but himself …

title: Hadith on Love: Where are those who love for the sake of Allah?
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: Where are those who love each other for the sake of My majesty? Today, I will shelter them in My shade on a day when there is no shade but Mine.”
q: Verily, Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: Where are those who love each other for the sake of My majesty? Today, I will shelter them in My shade on a day when there is no shade but Mine

title: Hadith on Character: The Prophet was sent to perfect good character
t: Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have been sent to perfect good character.”
q: I have been sent to perfect good character
gf: Sahih (authentic) according to Ibn Abdul Barr

title: Hadith on Self-Bullying: Do not condemn yourself as evil
t: Aisha reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None of you should say: My soul has been wicked. Rather, let him say: My soul has faulted.”
q: None of you should say: My soul has been wicked. Rather, let him say: My soul has faulted.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Manners: How the Prophet criticized people
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would not insult others, he would not use profanity, and he would not curse others. If he wanted to criticize one of us, he would say, “What is the matter with him? His forehead be dusted!”
q: What is the matter with him? His forehead be dusted!

title: Hadith on Daughters: Treating daughters well protects from the Fire
t: Aisha reported: A woman came to me along with her two daughters asking for charity, but she found nothing with me except one date. I gave it to her and she divided it between her two daughters. She did not eat anything herself, then she got up and left. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came in and I told him what happened. The Prophet said, “Whoever is tested with daughters in any way and treats them well, they will be their shield from Hellfire.”
q: Whoever is tested with daughters in any way and treats them well, they will be their shield from Hellfire
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Rahim: The womb is derived from mercy of Allah
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the womb derives its name from the Merciful. Allah said: I will keep good relations with one who keeps good relations with your relatives, and I will sever relations with one who severs relations with your relatives.”
q: Verily, the womb derives its name from the Merciful. Allah said: I will keep good relations with one who keeps good relations with your relatives, and I will sever relations with one who severs relations with your relatives

title: Hadith on Islam: Essentials of salvation are pillars of Islam
t: Abu Huraira reported: A bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, “O Messenger of Allah, show me a deed by which I may enter Paradise.” The Prophet said, “Worship Allah and never associate anything with Him, establish the prescribed prayers, give the obligatory charity, and fast of the month of Ramadan.” The man said, “By Him in whose hand is my soul, I will never add anything to it, nor will I lessen anything from it.” When the man turned his back, the Prophet said, “Whoever is pleased to see a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this one.”
q: Worship Allah and never associate anything with Him, establish the prescribed prayers, give the obligatory charity, and fast of the month of Ramadan. … Whoever is pleased to see a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this one.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Istighfar: The Prophet teaches Abu Bakr to seek forgiveness
t: Abu Bakr reported: He said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication to say in my prayers.” The Prophet said, “Say: O Allah, I have wronged myself with great injustices and none forgives sin but You, so forgive me and have mercy upon me. Verily, You alone are the Forgiving, the Merciful.”
q: Say: O Allah, I have wronged myself with great injustices and none forgives sin but You, so forgive me and have mercy upon me. Verily, You alone are the Forgiving, the Merciful.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Unseen: None knows five keys of the Unseen but Allah
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The keys of the Unseen are five and no one knows them but Allah: no one knows what is in the womb but Allah, no one knows what will happen tomorrow but Allah, no one knows when it will rain but Allah, no one knows where he will die but Allah, and no one knows when the Hour will be established but Allah.”
q: The keys of the Unseen are five and no one knows them but Allah: no one knows what is in the womb but Allah, no one knows what will happen tomorrow but Allah, no one knows when it will rain but Allah, no one knows where he will die but Allah, and no one knows when the Hour will be established but Allah

title: Hadith on Monotheism: Rights of Allah upon His servants
t: Mu’adh bin Jabal reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Mu’adh, do you know what the right of Allah is upon His servants?” I said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Prophet said, “To worship Him alone and to associate none in worship with Him. And do you know what their right is upon Him?” I said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Prophet said, “Not to punish them if they do so.”
q: O Mu’adh, do you know what the right of Allah is upon His servants? … To worship Him alone and to associate none in worship with Him. And do you know what their right is upon Him? … Not to punish them if they do so.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Mercy: Allah is not merciful to the unmerciful
t: Jarir ibn ‘Abdillah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Allah will not be merciful to those who are not merciful to people.”
q: Allah will not be merciful to those who are not merciful to people.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Medina: Virtue of the Prophet’s City, al-Madinah
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Medina is a sanctuary from this place to its borders. Its trees should not be cut. No heresy should be innovated or any sin should be committed in it. Whoever innovates a heresy within it or commits sins, he will invoke the curse of Allah, the angels, and the people altogether.”
q: Medina is a sanctuary from this place to its borders. Its trees should not be cut. No heresy should be innovated or any sin should be committed in it. Whoever innovates a heresy within it or commits sins, he will invoke the curse of Allah, the angels, and the people altogether

title: Hadith on Rifq: Allah loves gentleness, even with wrongdoers
t: Aisha reported: A group of Jews asked permission to visit the Prophet and when they were admitted, they said, “Death be upon you!” I said to them, “Rather, death and the curse of Allah be upon you!” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Aisha, Allah is gentle and He loves gentleness in all matters.” I said, “Have you not heard what they said?” The Prophet said, “I said to them: And upon you.”
q: O Aisha, Allah is gentle and He loves gentleness in all matters. … I said to them: And upon you.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dawah: Priorities of Islam are faith, prayer, charity
t: Mu’adh ibn Jabal reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sent me to Yemen and he said, “Verily, you are going to people among the people of the Book, so call them to testify there is no God but Allah and I am the Messenger of Allah. If they accept that, then teach them that Allah has obligated five prayers in each day and night. If they accept that, then teach them that Allah has obligated charity to be taken from the rich and given to the poor. If they accept that, then beware not to take from the best of their wealth. Beware the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no veil between it and Allah.”
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Dhikr: If he comes to Me walking, I come running
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace be and blessings on him, said, “Allah Almighty says: I am as My servant expects of Me and I am with him as he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I will remember him in Myself. If he mentions Me in a gathering, I will mention him in a greater gathering. When he draws near Me by the span of his hand, I draw near him by the length of a cubit. When he draws near Me by the length of a cubit, I draw near him by the length of a fathom. When he comes to Me walking, I come to him running.”
q: Allah Almighty says: I am as My servant expects of Me and I am with him as he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I will remember him in Myself. If he mentions Me in a gathering, I will mention him in a greater gathering. When he draws near Me by the span of his hand, I draw near him by the length of a cubit. When he draws near Me by the length of a cubit, I draw near him by the length of a fathom. When he comes to Me walking, I come to him running
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Adhan: How the Prophet instituted call to prayer
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: When the Muslims came to Medina, they gathered and sought to know the time of prayer, but no one announced it to them. They discussed the matter one day, and some of them said, “Use something like the bell of the Christians,” and some of them said, “Use a horn like that of the Jews.” Umar said, “Why not send a man to call people to prayer?” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O Bilal, stand and announce the prayer.”
q: O Bilal, stand and announce the prayer
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Wudu: Ablution is radiance on Judgment Day
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, my nation will be called on the Day of Resurrection as brightly radiant from the traces of ablution. Whoever among you is able to extend his radiance, let him do so.”
q: Verily, my nation will be called … on the Day of Resurrection as brightly radiant from the traces of ablution. Whoever among you is able to extend his radiance, let him do so
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Preaching: Wisdom in preaching at right time, not boring
t:
Ibn Mas’ud reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would take care in preaching to us on certain days, disliking it to become boring for us.

In another narration, Ibn Mas’ud said: Fearing it would become boring for us.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Miracles: The Prophet’s miracle of providing water
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, during the afternoon prayer and people were asking for water to perform ablution, but they could not find it. Some water was brought to the Prophet and he placed his hand in the vessel and ordered people to perform ablution. I saw water sprouting from his fingers and people performed ablution until even the last of them could do it.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Famine: Patience of the Prophet, companions with famine
t: ‘Utbah ibn Ghazwan reported: I found myself as the seventh among seven who had been with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. We had nothing to eat but the leaves of a wild tree until the corners of our mouths were wounded.

title: Hadith on Hereafter: Worldly life is a prison for the believer
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the unbeliever.”
q: The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the unbeliever.

title: Hadith on Theft: Allah will punish the usurper of land
t: Sa’id ibn Zayd reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever wrongly seizes a plot of land, Allah will make him carry seven earths around his neck.”
q: Whoever wrongly seizes a plot of land, Allah will make him carry seven earths around his neck.

title: Hadith on Muhammad: Until he loves me more than all people
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “None of you have faith until I am more beloved to him than his children, his father, and all of the people.”
q: None of you have faith until I am more beloved to him than his children, his father, and all of the people.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Faith: Whoever truly knows Allah enters Paradise
t: Uthman reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever died truly knowing that there is no God but Allah will enter Paradise.”
q: Whoever died truly knowing that there is no God but Allah will enter Paradise.

title: Hadith on Integrity: Say I believe in Allah, remain upright
t: Sufyan ibn Abdullah reported: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell me of a word in Islam I will not need to ask of anyone after you.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Say, ‘I have faith in Allah,’ and then remain steadfast.”
q: Say, ‘I have faith in Allah,’ and then remain steadfast

title: Hadith on Killing: Believers have room for error unless they murder
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A believer continues to have room for error in his religion as long as he does not shed sacred blood.”
q: A believer continues to have room for error in his religion as long as he does not shed sacred blood

title: Hadith on Spying: Do not seek faults, lest you corrupt them
t: Mu’awiyah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, if you seek out the faults of people, you will corrupt them or nearly corrupt them.”
q: Verily, if you seek out the faults of people, you will corrupt them or … nearly corrupt them.

title: Hadith on Clarity: The Prophet speaks so they understand him
t: Aisha reported: The discourse of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was clear such that he was understood by everyone who heard him.

title: Hadith on Backbiting: If Allah seeks his faults, he will be exposed
t: Abu Barzah al-Aslami reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “O you who have faith with their tongues but faith has not entered their hearts! Do not backbite the Muslims or seek their faults. Whoever seeks their faults, Allah will seek his faults. And if Allah seeks his faults, He will expose him even in the privacy of his own house.”
q: O you who have faith with their tongues but faith has not entered their hearts! Do not backbite the Muslims or seek their faults. Whoever seeks their faults, Allah will seek his faults. And if Allah seeks his faults, He will expose him even in the privacy of his own house.

title: Hadith on Roads: Public highways have rights, so fulfill their rights
t: Abu Sa’id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Beware of loitering in the roads.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, we have nowhere else to sit and talk.” The Prophet said, “If you insist, then give the road its rights.” They said, “What are its rights, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Lower the gaze, refrain from harm, return greetings of peace, enjoin good and forbid evil.”
q: Beware of loitering in the roads … If you insist, then give the road its rights … Lower the gaze, refrain from harm, return greetings of peace, enjoin good and forbid evil
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Friendship: A person follows religion of his best friend
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A man is upon the religion of his best friend, so let one of you look at whom he befriends.”
q: A man is upon the religion of his best friend, so let one of you look at whom he befriends.

title: Hadith on Transgression: No sin more worthy of fast punishment
t: Abu Bakrah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No sin deserves quicker punishment from Allah Almighty for one who commits it in this world, along with what is prepared for him in the Hereafter, other than injustice or severing family ties.”
q: No sin deserves quicker punishment from Allah Almighty for one who commits it in this world, along with what is prepared for him in the Hereafter, other than injustice or severing family ties.

title: Hadith on Desire: Miserable is the worshiper of money, wealth
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Wretched is the slave of gold, silver, fine clothes and garments. If he is given, he is pleased, but if he is not given, he is displeased.”
q: Wretched is the slave of gold, silver, fine clothes and garments. If he is given, he is pleased, but if he is not given, he is displeased

title: Hadith on Killing: First cases on Judgment Day will be murders
t: Abdullah ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The first of matters to be judged between people will be cases of murder.”
q: The first of matters to be judged between people will be cases of murder.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Najwa: Do not exclude believers from conversation
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “If you are three, let not two privately converse to the exclusion of their companion, for that will sadden him.”
q: If you are three, let not two privately converse to the exclusion of their companion, for that will sadden him.

title: Hadith on Manners: Good character equals many fasts and prayers
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the believer may reach by his good character the rank of one who regularly fasts and stands for prayer at night.”
q: Verily, the believer may reach by his good character the rank of one who regularly fasts and stands for prayer at night.

title: Hadith on Truth: Do not lie by repeating everything you hear
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is enough falsehood for someone to speak of everything he hears.”
q: It is enough falsehood for someone to speak of everything he hears.

title: Hadith on Mercy: Show compassion to those on the earth
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on the earth, and the One in the heavens will have mercy upon you.”
q: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on the earth, and the One in the heavens will have mercy upon you

title: Hadith on Sincerity: I pledged to the Prophet sincerity to all Muslims
t: Jarir ibn Abdullah reported: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, to establish prayer, to give charity, and to be sincere to every Muslim.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Qadr: What Allah wills, then what so-and-so wills
t: Hudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do not say: What Allah wills and this person wills. Rather you should say: What Allah wills, then what this person wills.”
q: Do not say: What Allah wills and this person wills. Rather you should say: What Allah wills, then what this person wills

title: Hadith on Pranks: Not allowed to scare another Muslim on purpose
t: Ibn Abi Layla reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “It is not lawful for a Muslim to frighten another Muslim.”
q: It is not lawful for a Muslim to frighten another Muslim

title: Hadith on Modesty: Do not admonish him, modesty is part of faith
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by a man from the Ansar who was warning his brother about modesty, but the Prophet said, “Let him be, for modesty is part of faith.”
q: Let him be, for modesty is part of faith
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Joking: Warning not to tell a lie, even as a joke
t: Mu’awiyyah ibn Haydah reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Woe to one who tells lies to make people laugh. Woe to him! Woe to him!”
q: Woe to one who tells lies to make people laugh. Woe to him! Woe to him!

title: Hadith on Pardon: The Prophet ordered to forgive bad character
t: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr reported: Allah commanded our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to keep forgiving the bad character of people.

title: Hadith on Islam: Muslim does no harm, can be trusted
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand people are safe, and the believer is the one people trust with their lives and wealth.”
q: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand people are safe, and the believer is the one people trust with their lives and wealth.

title: Hadith on Jannah: Amazing rewards for righteous in Paradise
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for one hundred years. Recite the verse if you wish, ‘And shade extended,’ (56:30). The space of one of your bows in Paradise is better than everything over which the sun rises and sets.”
q: Verily, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for one hundred years. Recite the verse if you wish, ‘And shade extended,’ … The space of one of your bows in Paradise is better than everything over which the sun rises and sets.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Women: Virtue of caring for daughters, young girls
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever cares for two girls until they reach maturity, then he and I will come together on the Day of Resurrection,” and the Prophet held up his two fingers together.
q: Whoever cares for two girls until they reach maturity, then he and I will come together on the Day of Resurrection

title: Hadith on Friends: Parable of a good and bad companion
t: Abu Musa reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the parable of good and bad company is that of a seller of musk and a blacksmith. The seller of musk will give you perfume, you will buy some, or you will notice a pleasant smell. As for the blacksmith, he will burn your clothes, or you will notice a bad smell.”
q: Verily, … the parable of good and bad company is that of a seller of musk and a blacksmith. The seller of musk will give you perfume, you will buy some, or you will notice a pleasant smell. As for the blacksmith, he will burn your clothes, or you will notice a bad smell.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Humility: Allah supports the weak and downtrodden
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “An impoverished man might be turned away by people at the gates, but Allah would fulfill his oath if he made it.”
q: An impoverished man might be turned away by people at the gates, but Allah would fulfill his oath if he made it

title: Hadith on Cruelty: Severe punishment for torturing animals
t: Ibn Umar reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “A woman was punished due to a cat she had imprisoned until it died, so she entered the Hellfire. She did not give it food or water while it was imprisoned, nor did she set it free to eat vermin of the earth.”
q: A woman was punished due to a cat she had imprisoned until it died, so she entered the Hellfire. She did not give it food or water while it was imprisoned, nor did she set it free to eat vermin of the earth
gf: Muttafaqun alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Charity: Man enjoys Paradise for cleaning road
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “I have seen a man enjoying himself in Paradise due to a tree in the road he cut down that used to harm people.”
q: I have seen … a man enjoying himself in Paradise due to a tree in the road he cut down that used to harm people

title: Hadith on Akhirah: Worldly life is nothing compared to Hereafter
t: Al-Mustawrid reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “What is the parable of this worldly life, in comparison to the Hereafter, but one of you dipping his finger in the sea? Let him see what he brings forth.”
q: What is the parable of this worldly life, in comparison to the Hereafter, but one of you dipping his finger in the sea? Let him see what he brings forth.

title: Hadith on Desire: Humankind was created vulnerable to Satan
t: Anas ibn Malik reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “When Allah formed Adam in Paradise, He left him as long as He willed. Satan walked around him, looking at him. When he saw what was within mankind, he knew they were created with a disposition they would struggle to control.”
q: When Allah formed Adam in Paradise, He left him as long as He willed. Satan … walked around him, looking at him. When he saw what was within mankind, he knew they were created with a disposition they would struggle to control.

title: Hadith on Anger: Truly strong control themselves when enraged
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The strongest are not the best wrestlers. Verily, the strongest are those who control themselves when angry.”
q: The strongest are not the best wrestlers. Verily, the strongest are those who control themselves when angry.
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Truth: Avoid gossip, scandal, and fake news
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Shall I not tell you about calumny? It is gossip spreading between people.”
q: Shall I not tell you about calumny? It is gossip spreading between people.

title: Hadith on Hypocrisy: Worst people are hypocrites with two faces
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, among the worst of people is one with two faces, coming with one face to these and another to those.”
q: Verily, among the worst of people is one with two faces, coming with one face to these and another to those
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Kindness: Allah loves gentleness, gives it a special reward
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, Allah is gentle, and He loves gentleness. He rewards for gentleness what is not granted for harshness, and He does not reward anything else like it.”
q: Verily, Allah is gentle, and He loves gentleness. He rewards for gentleness what is not granted for harshness, and He does not reward anything else like it

title: Hadith on Trials: Believer rewarded for any pain endured
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No believer is pricked by a thorn or more but that Allah will raise him one degree in status or erase a sin.”
q: No believer is pricked by a thorn or more but that Allah will raise him one degree in status or erase a sin
gf: Mutaffaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Brotherhood: Believers are bricks supporting each other
t: Abu Musa reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the believers are like bricks of a building, each part strengthening the other,” and the Prophet clasped his fingers together.
q: Verily, the believers are like bricks of a building, each part strengthening the other
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Charity: Virtue of visiting the sick for Allah
t: Thawban reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever visits a sick person will remain in an orchard of Paradise until he returns.”
q: Whoever visits a sick person will remain in an orchard of Paradise until he returns.

title: Hadith on Virtues: Honor in charity, forgiveness, humility
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Charity does not decrease wealth, no one forgives another but that Allah increases his honor, and no one humbles himself for the sake of Allah but that Allah raises his status.”
q: Charity does not decrease wealth, no one forgives another but that Allah increases his honor, and no one humbles himself for the sake of Allah but that Allah raises his status.

title: Hadith on Cruelty: Most hated man to Allah argues harshly
t: Aisha reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Verily, the most hated man to Allah is the one who is fiercest in an argument.” (2:204)
q: Verily, the most hated man to Allah is the one who is fiercest in an argument

title: Hadith on Redemption: Prayer and fasting expiate minor sins
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The five prayers, Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan will expiate the sins committed between them, as long as major sins are avoided.”
q: The five prayers, Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan will expiate the … sins committed between them, as long as major sins are avoided

title: Hadith on Faults: Concealing character faults like saving baby girls
t: ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “One who sees a character flaw and conceals it is like one who revives a baby girl buried alive.”
q: One who sees a character flaw and conceals it is like one who revives a baby girl buried alive.

title: Hadith on Curses: Habitual cursers will not be intercessors
t: Abu Darda reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Those in the habit of cursing others will not be intercessors or witnesses on the Day of Resurrection.”
q: Those in the habit of cursing others will not be intercessors or witnesses on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Hadith on Enormities: Worst sins are usury, slander, cutting off family
t: Sa’id ibn Zayd reported: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Among the worst acts of usury is to disparage the reputation of a Muslim without right. Verily, this womb derives its name from the Most Merciful. Whoever severs its family ties, Allah will forbid him from entering Paradise.”
q: Among the worst acts of usury is to disparage the reputation of a Muslim without right. Verily, this womb derives its name from the Most Merciful. Whoever severs its family ties, Allah will forbid him from entering Paradise.

title: Hadith on Parents: No child can truly repay his father
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “No child can repay his father unless he finds him as a slave, purchases him, and emancipates him.”
q: No child can repay his father unless he finds him as a slave, purchases him, and emancipates him.

title: Hadith on Backbiting: Speaking badly in their absence is backbiting
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Do you know what backbiting is?” They said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Prophet said, “To mention your brother in a way he dislikes.” It was said, “What if it is true about him?” The Prophet said, “If what you say about him is true, it is backbiting. If it is not true, it is slander.”
q: Do you know what backbiting is? … To mention your brother in a way he dislikes … If what you say about him is true, it is backbiting. If it is not true, it is slander

title: Hadith on Parents: Honoring your mother, then your father
t: Abu Huraira reported: A man asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, “Who is most deserving of my good company?” The Prophet said, “Your mother.” The man asked, “Then who?” The Prophet said “Your mother.” The man asked again, “Then who?” The Prophet said, “Your mother.” The man asked again, “Then who?” The Prophet said, “Your father.”
q: Your mother … Your mother … Your mother … Your father
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Mercy: The Prophet is merciful to his children
t: Abu Huraira reported: Al-Aqra’ ibn Habis saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, kissing his grandson Al-Hasan. He said, “I have ten children and I do not kiss any of them.” The Prophet said, “Verily, whoever does not show mercy will not receive mercy.”
q: Verily, whoever does not show mercy will not receive mercy
gf: Muttafaqun Alayhi (authenticity agreed upon) according to Al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Hadith on Excess: Nitpicking, extremism ruinous to religion
t: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “The hairsplitters have been ruined.” The Prophet said it three times.
q: The hairsplitters have been ruined.

title: Hadith on Guidance: Whoever calls others to righteousness or sin
t: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward similar to those who follow him, without detracting from their rewards at all. Whoever calls to misguidance will have sin upon him similar to those who follow him, without detracting from their sins at all.”
q: Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward similar to those who follow him, without detracting from their rewards at all. Whoever calls to misguidance will have sin upon him similar to those who follow him, without detracting from their sins at all

title: Hadith on Salaam: Worship the Merciful, feed the poor, spread peace
t: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Worship the Most Merciful, feed the poor, and spread peace. You will enter Paradise in peace.”
q: Worship the Most Merciful, feed the poor, and spread peace. You will enter Paradise in peace.

title: Hadith on Animals: In every living being a reward for charity
t: Suraqah ibn Ju’shum reported: I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about a lost camel who comes to drink from my cisterns that I have prepared for my own camels, “Will I be rewarded if I give it some water to drink?” The Prophet said, “Yes, in every living being with a warm liver is a reward for charity.”
q: Yes, in every living being with a warm liver is a reward for charity
